Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 36 challenge cases used for final training (24 in internal validation), below the >50 threshold; supplemented by a 30-scan external UK set. Small, but multi-institutional and challenge-curated, and sufficient to top a public benchmark.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both sources clearly described: 2017 AAPM Thoracic Auto-segmentation Challenge (60 scans; 20 each from MD Anderson, MSKCC, MAASTRO) and a University of Kentucky private dataset (30 randomly selected thoracic CTs, IRB approved).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Challenge-defined split (36 train / 12 offline test / 12 online test) plus an explicitly described internal random split of the 36 training cases into 24 train / 12 test for ablation studies.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth per RTOG 1106 contouring guidelines, quality-checked by challenge organizers, with inter-rater variability reference (3 experts x 3 cases). Caveat: UK dataset GT was created by physician-editing the model's own output, introducing potential circularity.

Q5_external_validation.justification: The final model trained on challenge data was deployed unchanged to a fully independent 30-scan institutional (UK) dataset, with per-organ Dice/MSD/HD95 and clinical editing time reported.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D U-Net with 3 encoding/decoding blocks fully specified: two sets of 3x3x3 convolutions + batch norm + ReLU per block, padded convolutions, and Table 1 giving input dimensions (MxNxP), first-layer filter count (f), and output classes (p) for the localization network and each organ-specific network.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: TensorFlow, NVIDIA Titan Xp, Adam (lr=0.0005), 200 epochs, per-class loss weights, cropping margin ranges (alpha/beta ~ U[0.1,0.7]), 6-crop test augmentation, training/inference times all reported. Minor gap: batch size and exact augmentation transformation magnitudes not quantified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted cross-entropy justified experimentally against Dice loss (unstable, slow-converging in the localization network) and combined CE+Dice (similar final results). Authors admit class weights (2.0 cord/esophagus; 3.0 esophagus foreground) were set empirically without deep investigation.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described: resampling to 0.9756x0.9756x3 mm, 512x512 in-plane zero-pad/center-crop, HU clipping [-1000, 600], [0,1] normalization; post-processing includes largest-connected-component retention, inter-organ overlap resolution via max probability >0.5, resampling back, and marching-squares contour extraction to DICOM-RT.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No mention of public code, model weights, or repository.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice, mean surface distance (MSD), 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95), challenge normalized score, and clinical editing time; all formally defined with equations.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired sample t-tests with p-values reported for ablation comparisons (proposed workflow vs localization network; augmentation effects), and mean +/- SD throughout; but no confidence intervals, no multiple-comparison correction, and no statistical testing against external methods. Testing augmentation improvement itself was not statistically significant.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Direct ranking against all 2017 AAPM challenge entries on an identical hidden test set (1st ongoing phase, 2nd live phase); top-3 deep learning methods statistically indistinguishable from each other but both statistically superior to remaining entries including atlas-based methods. Internal ablations against architecture variants (residual U-Net, dilated convolutions) also provided.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Comprehensive per-organ Dice/MSD/HD95/normalized-score with SD in Tables 2-5 for internal validation, challenge test, and UK datasets.

Q15_limitations.justification: Extensive limitations section: small training set, esophagus overfitting (train 0.8-0.9 vs test 0.6-0.7 Dice), catastrophic localization failure (one case, 0 Dice for esophagus), heart over-contouring/leakage into liver on UK data, spinal cord guideline mismatch, and challenge GT quality above typical clinical data.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate: multi-institutional challenge data with defined QC and RTOG 1106 guidelines, but abnormal cases (e.g., collapsed lungs) excluded by organizers, restricting spectrum to typical anatomy; UK cases randomly selected with IRB approval. Patient/scan selection overall clearly defined.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate concern for the UK dataset: ground truth was generated by a single unblinded physician editing the model's own automatic contours (circular evaluation), and editing time is a subjective outcome. Low concern for the challenge evaluation (independent server, standardized metrics, inter-rater reference). Metrics applied consistently across datasets.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low: all per-organ outcomes, ablation results (including unfavorable ones, e.g., residual U-Net slightly worse, Dice loss unstable), and failure cases reported. Minor gap: the 12 offline test cases were never evaluated (explained by server limitation), so only online-test results are available for the final model.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not in primary extraction: (1) Network parameters (Table 1; MxNxP along superior-inferior/anterior-posterior/left-right, first-block filters f, output classes p): localization 72x208x208, f=24, p=6; spinal cord 160x128x64, f=64, p=2; right/left lung 72x192x120, f=48, p=2 each; heart 32x160x192, f=64, p=2; esophagus 80x80x64, f=64, p=2; f set as large as GPU memory allows, dims multiples of 8. (2) Internal validation ablations (24/12 split, Table 3, Dice): localization 0.812/0.974/0.969/0.909/0.480; GT-crop oracle 0.845/0.979/0.975/0.930/0.652; no train+test augmentation 0.834/0.975/0.966/0.906/0.411 (training Dice saturated at 1.0 = severe overfit); no test augmentation 0.837/0.979/0.975/0.929/0.601; proposed 0.840/0.981/0.977/0.932/0.608; paired t-test vs localization p = 0.037/0.00006/0.00006/0.003/0.0004. (3) Localization learning was stepwise: lungs+heart learned by iteration 1000 (Dice 0.971/0.961/0.892), esophagus by iteration 2000 (0.476), spinal cord by iteration 4800 (0.812); validation every 240 steps. (4) Normalized challenge scores per organ (50 = inter-rater reference): cord 61.2+/-14.1, right lung 71.4+/-19.8, left lung 79.5+/-9.0, heart 46.9+/-11.1, esophagus 27.6+/-20.9; 3 esophagus cases scored 0 on all metrics. (5) UK failure magnitudes: heart HD95 18.7+/-19.7 mm, esophagus HD95 14.6+/-17.3 mm. (6) Cropping formulation: bounding box from foreground min/max coordinates expanded by random margins alpha,beta ~ U(0.1,0.7) per axis per training iteration; 6 pre-generated fixed random croppings averaged as probability maps at test time. (7) Augmentation: random translation/rotation/scaling per iteration with labels re-binarized at 0.5; organ nets add random rotation+shear after cropping. (8) Score normalization: 100 = perfect, 50 = mean inter-rater (3 experts x 3 cases), linear interpolation/extrapolation, floor 0. (9) Architecture/loss experiments: residual connections slightly worse (attributed to shallow network), dilated convolutions similar, 4th encoding level no gain - segmentation argued to rely mainly on low-level edge/contrast features; Dice loss unstable in localization network, CE+Dice faster-converging but equivalent. (10) Clinical workflow: 7.5+/-2.4 min/patient editing vs 30-40 min manual; UK spinal cord contours smaller per local best-practice; heart failures showed cranial/caudal over-contouring and liver leakage attributed to heart-liver contrast. (11) No batch size reported; IRB approval obtained for UK retrospective data.
contribution_summary: This paper introduces a cascaded framework that decouples organ localization (multi-label 3D U-Net on downsampled, center-cropped volumes) from per-organ binary segmentation (specialized 3D U-Nets on randomly-margin-cropped patches), making full-resolution 3D thoracic CT segmentation feasible within GPU memory limits, complemented by a novel test-time augmentation based on multiple randomized croppings. It ranked 1st (ongoing phase) and 2nd (live phase) in the 2017 AAPM Thoracic Auto-segmentation Challenge (Dice 0.972-0.979 lungs, 0.925 heart, 0.893 cord, 0.726 esophagus), surpassing inter-rater reference for lungs/cord, and generalized to an independent institutional dataset while reducing clinical contour editing to ~7.5 min/patient. It is a landmark demonstration that crop-based cascaded 3D U-Nets can achieve challenge-winning, clinically translatable multi-OAR segmentation for radiation therapy planning.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Total in-house cohort of 77 CT scans (abstract inconsistently states 73) is reasonable, but the training split contains only 42 subjects, below the >50 training threshold. Partial credit given for adequate overall size, disease-stratified composition (15 healthy, 24 HCC/cirrhotic, 37 colorectal metastases), and two additional external sets (SLIVER07: 20; LiTS: 131).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: All three data sources are clearly described: in-house Columbia University Medical Center clinical study with disease breakdown, prior use of the annotation tool in the A2ALL cohort; SLIVER07 and LiTS public datasets with full acquisition characteristics (in-plane resolution 0.55-0.98/0.56-0.81/0.56-1 mm, slice thickness 0.625-7.5/0.7-5/0.7-5 mm, KVP 120, kernels B20-B31, slice counts).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random split explicitly reported: 42 (~55%) train / 19 (~24%) eval / 16 (~21%) test. SLIVER07 and LiTS training sets used entirely as untouched external validation sets (no fine-tuning), a transparent and rigorous protocol.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process described: experienced radiologists using a semi-automatic segmentation algorithm (authors' own referenced method, ref 30) previously validated in the A2ALL study (>1200 scans). SLIVER07/LiTS use provided manual delineations. Minor caveat: number of raters, inter-observer variability, and QC procedures not reported; ground truth generated with the authors' own tool creates slight circularity risk.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Strong external validation on two independent public datasets (SLIVER07: Dice 96.2±0.9%; LiTS: Dice 94.3±2.7%) without any fine-tuning or parameter modification — directly testing generalization, which exceeds typical practice.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture thoroughly described: FCN-8s (Long et al.) modified from 21 to 7 output channels to predict a layered label map (interior/exterior narrow bands + regional layers) derived from signed Euclidean distance transform; integration with Lankton localizing region-based ACM, force design (polynomial/exponential strength, sign-based direction), and sparse-field level set evolution (Whitaker) are all detailed with equations and figures.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: optimizer (SGD), learning rate (5e-5), momentum (0.9 then 0.99), batch size (20 then 1), framework (MatConvNet/MATLAB 2017a), GPU (TITAN Xp), and ACM parameters (force weights, curvature weight, local region radius) are given. Missing: number of epochs/iterations, weight initialization, data augmentation, and how full 512×512 slices were batched — full independent reimplementation would require guesswork.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss stated (per-pixel unnormalized softmax, inherited from FCN-8s) but only justified by precedent ('same as the original FCN-8s'). No discussion of suitability for the 7-class layered representation, class imbalance between narrow bands and regional layers, or alternatives considered.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Well described: binary masks converted to 7-category layered label maps via Euclidean distance transform with adaptive narrow-band widths scaled by DICOM pixel spacing (physical mm consistency across scans). Post-processing equally clear: FCN thresholding to initial contour, level-set ACM refinement enforcing smoothness/excluding fragments, topology-preserving evolution via sparse-field method.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository mentioned anywhere in the paper. The segmentation method is instead protected by a patent (ref 30), which further reduces reproducibility.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Comprehensive metric suite: Dice plus three surface-distance measures (ASSD, RMSD, MaxSD in mm) for final segmentation, and pixel accuracy, mean accuracy, mean IU for FCN evaluation (train: 99.07/74.87/63.78%; test: 99.00/71.70/60.75%).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only (mean ± SD per dataset; per-case Dice plotted in Fig. 8). No p-values, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the ~1.5-1.8% relative Dice improvement over FCN alone, despite paired same-case comparisons being available.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Comparisons limited to internal ablations (FCN alone) and classical non-learning baselines (Chan-Vese global ACM; Lankton local ACM) demonstrating force necessity. No benchmarking against contemporary deep learning SOTA (U-Net, 3D DSN, V-Net) nor against SLIVER07 leaderboard results, limiting ability to judge absolute competitiveness.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver), so per-organ reporting is trivially complete. Results are broken down per dataset (Table 1) and per case (Fig. 8), with FCN-alone vs FCN+ACM separated — granular reporting satisfied.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit failure analysis with illustrative cases (Fig. 11): irregularly shaped livers, missed small objects, severe disease near boundaries, adjacent iso-intense structures. Honest discussion of weight-tuning dependence, small in-house dataset, 2D-only processing, and unexploited label-inconsistency cleanup, plus concrete future work.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate concern: disease-stratified in-house composition and random splitting are reported, but inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment period, and whether patients were consecutive are unstated; external sets mitigate but cannot eliminate single-center bias.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low concern: identical metrics applied consistently across in-house and external datasets; external evaluation done without fine-tuning. One caveat: ground truth was generated using the authors' own semi-automatic tool (potential anchoring toward their segmentation style), and vessel-inclusion conventions differ between in-house training (vessels/IVC included) and LiTS reference (excluded), acknowledged by the authors as a confounder.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low concern: negative results/failure cases explicitly shown (Fig. 11), per-case Dice plotted, all promised metrics reported. Minor gaps: no runtime figures (training/inference), no statistical testing, and a 73-vs-77 scan count discrepancy between abstract and methods.

detailed_extraction: SCOPE FLAG FOR REVIEW: This is a 2D slice-based method (per-axial-slice FCN at 512×512) despite the review's 3D focus; the final 3D liver volume is a stack of 2D segmentations with no inter-slice context, and a true 3D extension (3D FCN, narrow bands as surfaces) is explicitly deferred to future work. Method details: (1) Label encoding — ground-truth binary mask converted to a 7-category layered map {-3..3} (three interior narrow bands, boundary band, three exterior bands plus interior/exterior regional layers) via signed Euclidean distance transform, with bandwidth factor adaptive to pixel spacing from DICOM headers; (2) Force design — FCN steering force magnitude is a polynomial or exponential function of distance-to-boundary, direction set by inside/outside sign, acting as an attention-like external force everywhere in the image domain; (3) Evolution — force added to Lankton localizing region-based ACM with curvature smoothing, solved by Whitaker's sparse-field level set, which permits initialization far from the boundary and topology preservation (spurious FCN fragments outside the initial contour are never captured); (4) Training — SGD lr=5e-5, momentum 0.9→0.99 after convergence, batch 20→1, TITAN Xp; (5) Key quantitative results — FCN-alone test Dice 94.1% vs FCN+ACM 95.8±1.4% in-house; external no-fine-tuning Dice 96.2±0.9% (SLIVER07) and 94.3±2.7% (LiTS); mean relative Dice gains of 1.8%/1.5%; (6) Data handling nuances — LiTS liver+tumor masks merged as liver reference, rotated duplicate volumes discarded; reported data-size discrepancy (73 abstract vs 77 methods); (7) Clinical relevance — cohort deliberately enriched with severe pathology (cirrhosis/HCC, colorectal metastases), addressing a documented weakness of pure shape-model and intensity-based approaches; (8) Deployment argument — only a handful of interpretable ACM parameters (force weights, local radius, band width) need adaptation to a new site rather than millions of network weights, eliminating fine-tuning burden; (9) IP/reproducibility — related patent exists (ref 30), no code released. Missing data: inference/training times, per-slice vs per-volume aggregation details, and numeric values of Table 1 surface distances (not extractable from provided text).
contribution_summary: This paper proposes a hybrid deep-learning/deformable-model framework in which a single modified FCN-8s predicts a 7-category layered label map (encoding interior/exterior region and distance-to-boundary bands derived from signed distance transforms), which is converted into an adaptive external steering force for a localizing region-based active contour model with sparse-field level-set evolution. The force's distance-adaptive magnitude and position-dependent direction enable initialization far from the liver boundary, boundary smoothness enforcement, topology preservation, and elimination of spurious fragments. Without fine-tuning, the method generalizes to two external datasets (Dice 96.2% SLIVER07, 94.3% LiTS), consistently improving over FCN alone (~94%), though it remains 2D slice-based and lacks comparison with contemporary deep learning SOTA.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 140 NPC patients total; 100 for training (>50 threshold), 20 validation, 20 test. Patch-based sampling further multiplies effective training samples.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single-institution cohort of unenhanced radiotherapy-planning CTs from NPC patients (institution identifiable from author affiliations); acquisition fully specified (in-plane resolution 0.3633-0.5479 mm, 1024x1024 matrix, 3 mm slices). Minor gap: no explicit recruitment period or inclusion/exclusion criteria.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit patient-level 100/20/20 split with a held-out test set 'never previously used for training or validation'. Randomization/stratification method not stated and no cross-validation, but the split structure itself is clear.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Process described: one experienced rater delineated, reviewed by a radiologist with 10 yr experience. Partial credit: single annotator, rater experience level and delineation protocol/tool unspecified, no inter-observer variability analysis; authors themselves acknowledge gold-standard accuracy is limited.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external or independent dataset; all evaluation on one internal 20-patient test set from the same center.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: ResNet18 backbone described with figure (residual blocks, batch norm, ReLU, pooling, global average pooling, FC+softmax); 2D sliding-window patch classification predicting the center pixel; cascade construction and majority-voting inference clearly explained.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: PyTorch, hardware (NVIDIA Titan X 12 GB, CUDA 7.5), sample counts (120k train patches, 100k validation patches), and the full Boosting sample-filtering procedure are reported. Missing: optimizer, learning rate/schedule, batch size, epochs/iterations, stopping criterion details.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never stated or justified; softmax output implies cross-entropy but this is not specified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clear: central 512x512 crop, bmp conversion, fixed-size patch extraction. Post-processing explicitly stated: pixel-level majority voting over the three networks; authors explicitly note absence of CRF/MRF post-processing and fine-tuning.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no availability statement anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Three metrics with formulas: DSC, 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance, and volume overlap error, all reported as mean +/- SD.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only (mean +/- SD, box plots). No confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests backing the superiority claims over baselines.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Fair same-data comparison against FCN-8s, U-Net, DeepLab-v3, and a single voxelwise ResNet, plus internal ablations (patch size, backbone). Baselines are standard but already established by 2019; no comparison to other published OAR methods or public benchmarks.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-organ results (parotid, thyroid, optic nerve) for every method, metric, and ablation in Tables I-III; not just averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: Substantive discussion: slow pixel-wise inference, limited single-rater gold standard, no CRF/MRF, no fine-tuning or augmentation/k-fold CV, plus explicit future work. No qualitative failure-case images shown, but limitations are candidly addressed.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/unclear: single-center NPC cohort; no explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment period, or consecutive-sampling statement; generalizability to other populations, scanners, and protocols is uncertain.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate: all compared methods were retrained and evaluated on the same held-out test set against the same reference standard with consistent metrics, reducing assessment bias; however, the single-rater reference standard (plus one reviewer) lacks inter-observer verification, so absolute performance estimates may be biased.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate: per-organ results, all metrics, and unfavorable ablations (ResNet34/SE-ResNet18 no better; larger patches marginal) are reported and limitations acknowledged; offset by absence of statistical testing, code release, and any tumor/target-volume or additional-organ results.

detailed_extraction: Task: automated delineation of three difficult head-and-neck OARs (parotids, thyroid, optic nerves) on planning CT for NPC radiotherapy; motivation is reducing manual contouring time (~2.7 h/patient) and inter-operator variability, and preventing xerostomia, hypothyroidism, and radiation-induced blindness. Data: 140 NPC patients, unenhanced planning CT, axial reconstruction, in-plane resolution 0.3633-0.5479 mm, 1024x1024 matrix, 3 mm slice thickness, central 512x512 crop. Method: 2D patch-based sliding-window classification (predicts center pixel) - NOTE: no 3D convolutions or inter-slice context despite volumetric input, a key caveat for a review on 3D segmentation. Three ResNet18 classifiers combined via a Boosting-inspired cascaded training scheme: Net 1 trained on randomly sampled balanced patches; Net 2 trained on newly drawn patches filtered by Net 1 (50% correctly / 50% incorrectly classified by Net 1, pos/neg balanced); Net 3 trained on patches 50% of which were misclassified by at least one predecessor. Test time: pixel assigned OAR if >half the networks (majority vote) say so. Default initialization, no transfer learning, no data augmentation, no k-fold CV, no CRF/MRF post-processing (all explicitly stated). Ablations: patch sizes 31/51/71 (larger patches give marginal gains at higher cost; 31 used for the main comparison); alternative backbones ResNet34 and SE-ResNet18 gave no significant improvement, indicating framework is backbone-agnostic. Results (Table I, 31x31 patches, mean +/- SD): parotid DSC 91.88+/-3.51%, 95%HD 3.15+/-0.58 mm, VOE 14.83+/-5.26%; thyroid DSC 91.76+/-3.67%, 2.70+/-0.61 mm, 15.06+/-6.11%; optic nerve DSC 89.94+/-4.31%, 2.07+/-0.31 mm, 20.29+/-6.23%. Best-configuration numbers (abstract, per-organ optimal patch size): parotid DSC 92.26% (71x71), thyroid 92.29% (51x51), optic nerve 89.37% (71x71); 95%HD ~3.08/2.64/2.03 mm; VOE ~14.16/14.94/19.07%. Same-data baselines (DSC): FCN-8s 86.08/82.81/74.02; U-Net 89.51/84.55/76.41; DeepLab-v3 90.67/87.39/80.70; single voxelwise ResNet 84.93/74.48/75.12 (parotid/thyroid/optic nerve respectively). Authors argue U-Net/FCN underperform on low-contrast, shape-variable OARs because encoder-decoder structures lose boundary texture, while patch classification mitigates shape variation. Implementation: PyTorch, Ubuntu 14.04, CUDA 7.5, NVIDIA Titan X 12 GB, Intel i5-3570k, 128 GB RAM. Authors note pixel-wise inference is slow (all classifiers run on all pixels) and propose ROI pre-marking as future work. Minor reporting flag: baseline citation numbers in Table I (e.g., FCN-8s as Ref. 20, U-Net as Ref. 21) appear mismatched with the reference list. Funding: NSFC (61671230, 31271067), Guangdong provincial programs; no conflict of interest declared.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a Boosting-inspired cascaded ensemble of three 2D patch-based ResNet18 classifiers for OAR segmentation (parotids, thyroid, optic nerves) in NPC planning CTs, where each subsequent network is trained on patches filtered by its predecessors to concentrate on error-prone samples, with final labels decided by majority voting. On 140 single-center patients it outperforms FCN-8s, U-Net, DeepLab-v3, and a single voxelwise ResNet (mean DSC ~92% parotid, ~92% thyroid, ~89-90% optic nerve), and ablations show the framework is backbone-agnostic since deeper/wider backbones add no benefit. The approach remains 2D without 3D spatial context and has slow pixel-wise inference, limiting its fit as a fully '3D' segmentation method for this review.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 45 clinical torso DECT volumes in total, with 27 training / 9 validation / 9 test per fold (3:1:1) under fivefold cross-validation. The 27-subject training set per fold is well below the >50 subjects threshold; the authors themselves acknowledge small data size as a primary limitation.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Dataset source thoroughly described: single center (University Hospital Erlangen), scanner model (SOMATOM Definition Force, Siemens), full acquisition protocol (70 kV/560 mAs low energy; Sn-150 kV/140 mAs high energy; Q32r kernel; Ultravist 370 contrast agent; voxel spacing 0.69–0.98 × 0.69–0.98 × 0.6 mm; 992–1290 slices of 512×512).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split methodology clearly and thoughtfully described: manifold-learning-based partitioning (LLE projection to 2D + k-means clustering into 3 groups) with 3:1:1 random sampling per cluster for 27/9/9 volumes, fivefold cross-validation. Explicitly designed to reduce dataset bias from random splitting in small cohorts.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: States ground truth for 6 organs was 'generated manually by experts,' but no details on number of annotators, annotation protocol/tools, quality control, or inter-observer variability.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent validation. All quantitative results from internal fivefold cross-validation on the same 45 single-center, single-scanner volumes. The 4 'special clinical cases' (different protocol, lung pathology, splenectomy, truncated scan) are evaluated only qualitatively.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Four fusion architectures (LC-net, MC-net, MI-net, late fusion) fully described with architecture figures, fusion equations (Eqs. 1–3), residual block design (identity mapping with dimension matching + full pre-activation per He et al.), trainable parameter counts, and even theoretical receptive field calculations.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Comprehensive training details: Adam optimizer, initial LR 5e-5 reduced ×0.1 every 10 epochs, batch sizes 6 (train)/3 (validation), 32³ patches with overlap 16, downsampling factor 2, six augmentation types, 146–240 epochs with early stopping, GPU (TITAN Xp 12GB). Minor gap: DL framework/implementation library not explicitly named, and augmentation parameter ranges unspecified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted multi-class Dice loss explicitly justified for class imbalance, combining median frequency balancing (Eigen & Fergus) and boundary compensation (Roy et al.) with formal definition (Eqs. 4–5); the balance hyperparameter k is additionally analyzed empirically (ablation in Table V).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly described (×2 downsampling, patch extraction with overlap 16, data augmentation); postprocessing clearly described (per-voxel softmax argmax + largest connected component filtering to remove misclassified voxels).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository link mentioned anywhere in the paper; confirmed by prior extraction (code_available: false).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Three metrics reported: Dice coefficient, AUC, and Hausdorff distance (Tables I–III), exceeding the Dice + one metric requirement.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Partial: mean ± SD across fivefold cross-validation folds reported for all metrics, and P-values (P<0.05, P<0.01) reported only for the residual-vs-non-residual comparison (Table II). No statistical tests comparing the four fusion architectures (the paper's central claim rests on untested mean differences), no confidence intervals, no multiple-comparison correction.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Comparisons are internal: four fusion variants, residual ablations, single-energy 3D U-Net baselines (low/high energy), skip-connection ablation, and the authors' own prior work with predefined fusion weights. No benchmarking against external state-of-the-art multi-organ segmentation methods (e.g., Roth et al. hierarchical FCN or other published approaches).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Complete per-organ results (lungs, liver, spleen, both kidneys) for Dice, AUC, and Hausdorff distance across all architecture variants and ablations.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated Limitations section: small dataset, patch-edge artifacts (worst case spleen Dice 64.4% illustrated in Fig. 6), GPU-constrained patch size with explicit receptive-field analysis, organ-dependent sensitivity of loss weight k, and future directions (dilated convolutions, dynamic k).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate risk: single-center, single-vendor/single-scanner data; cases selected from patients with 'different clinical indications justified by the radiologist' without explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, the manifold-learning-based (LLE + k-means) partitioning effectively mitigates split-selection bias within the cohort, and mixed male/female adults with diverse indications improves case representativeness.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low risk: all compared networks trained/evaluated on identical folds, patches, and loss configuration; fixed expert ground truth; same metrics applied consistently; evaluation fully automated, removing subjective outcome assessment. Minor caveat: evaluation on 9 test cases per fold yields imprecise estimates with high per-organ SDs (e.g., spleen ±6.35).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low risk: all per-organ and per-architecture results reported (including worst-performing late fusion and a failure case with Dice 64.4%); limitations candidly discussed; supplementary convergence plots referenced. No evidence of selective outcome reporting.

detailed_extraction: SUPPLEMENTARY DETAILS NOT IN PRIOR EXTRACTION — (1) ARCHITECTURE COMPLEXITY: Trainable parameters: LC-net 16,348,536; MC-net 16,335,463; MI-net 46,935,479 (~3× others); late fusion 32,669,189. Residual variants: LC-Res 21,275,642; MC-Res 21,263,435; MI-Res 53,693,115; late fusion Res 42,538,957. Residual blocks add ~30% parameters but 50–60% training time. Despite 3× parameters, MI-net training time (115h15m) only modestly exceeds MC-net (94h8m)/LC-net (103h20m)/late fusion (106h32m); MI-Res is slowest (186h32m). (2) FUSION-FINDING HIERARCHY: more abstract fusion → better accuracy: feature-level (MI-net) > image-level (MC-net ≈ LC-net) > output-level (late fusion, worst on most metrics); rationale is separate handling of energy-sensitive vs energy-insensitive noise. (3) PATCH-SIZE ABLATION (Table VI, worst-case scenario): 64³ patches improved spleen 88.3→93.9 but degraded lungs (97.6→97.4 / 97.5→97.3), liver (95.3→92.8), and kidneys; training time 4× (115h15m→455h37m); 128³ infeasible on 12GB GPU. Receptive field analysis (generalized Eq. 6, verified on V-Net): MI-net deepest layer 100³, largest 142³; other nets deepest 68³, largest 110³ — all exceed the 32³ patch, so network capacity is underutilized. (4) BALANCE WEIGHT k ABLATION (MI-net): k=0: spleen 87.6, kidneys 90.1/91.1; k=1: spleen 91.4; k=5: lungs collapse to 62.7/57.5 while kidneys peak at 94.5/93.7 and liver 96.2 — k is organ-dependent (large organs need low k, small organs tolerate/need higher k); small organs more stable under k changes. (5) SKIP-CONNECTION ABLATION: removing the original-level connection path ('-' variants) degrades Dice by ~0.3–2.5%, benefiting large organs most. (6) RESIDUAL BLOCKS: significant gains for left lung (97.5→97.8, P<0.01), liver, kidneys; mixed/negative for late fusion spleen (SD inflates to ±13.6). (7) STATISTICS: significance markers only in Table II (residual vs non-residual baseline); a/b markers denote P<0.05/P<0.01. (8) BASELINE DELTAS: optimal DECT (opt-k MI-net) vs single-energy 3D U-Net: +2% lungs, +4% liver, +4–6% spleen, +4% right kidney, +1% left kidney. (9) ROBUSTNESS TESTS (qualitative only, Fig. 5): successful on (a) different protocol (100/Sn150 kV, Qr40 kernel), (b) lung pathology, (c) post-splenectomy patient (absent organ correctly not predicted), (d) longitudinally truncated scan. (10) CLASS SETUP: 7-class problem (6 organs + background); ~21,931±395 training patches and 7,172±503 validation patches per fold. (11) REPORTING CAVEAT: best per-organ Dice values come from DIFFERENT configurations (left lung 97.8 = MI-Res; liver 96.2, kidneys 94.5/93.7 = opt-k MI-net with k=5; spleen 91.7 = residual variants); no single model achieves all bests simultaneously — best single configuration average is MI-net/MI-Res at ~95%. (12) FUNDING: DFG grants KA 1678/20, LE 2763/2, MA 4898/5; GPU donated by NVIDIA; no conflict of interest declared.
contribution_summary: This paper presents the first systematic investigation of information-fusion strategies for deep-learning-based DECT segmentation, proposing four 3D fully convolutional architectures that fuse the two spectral images at image level (LC-net, MC-net), mid-feature level (MI-net), or output level (late fusion), plus residual-block variants. The feature-level fusion MI-net proved best (Dice ~92–98% per organ; +2–6% over single-energy 3D U-Net), demonstrating that learnable joint spectral feature extraction — requiring neither predefined fusion weights nor organ/energy-specific priors — exploits dual-energy information more effectively than linear combination. Secondary contributions include a weighted multi-class Dice loss with median-frequency balancing and boundary compensation, a manifold-learning-based data-partitioning scheme for small cohorts, and a transparent analysis of patch-based training limitations, though results rest on a small (45-volume), single-center dataset with internal cross-validation only.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 82 abdominal contrast-enhanced CT scans; exceeds the >50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public NIH Pancreas-CT dataset; cohort demographics reported (53 male, 27 female, mean age 46.8±16.7).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 4-fold cross-validation explicitly stated; PNet fusion trained with cross-cross-validation protocol to avoid fold leakage.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process (who annotated, how many observers, protocol, inter-rater agreement) not described; paper relies on existing NIH labels without detail.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single public dataset only; no independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: cascaded V-Nets (localization), SINet with 5 encoder modules (asymmetric 3×3×1 + symmetric 3×3×3 convs, instance norm, ReLU), 4 deep-supervision decode paths, Slice Correlation Module (bilinear pooling), PNet fusion, recurrent refinement; figures referenced for each component.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: PyTorch, 4× Titan Xp, preprocessing, augmentation, stopping criteria reported; optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs not found in available text; no code to fill gaps.

Q8_loss_function.justification: SRDice derived with full gradient analysis showing (p_i+ε)^(-1/2) term up-weights missed foreground voxels; ε caps gradient magnitude; use case (recall-critical localization) explicitly justified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Detailed both directions: HU clipping [-100,240]→[0,255], center crop 360×320×L, 2× down-sampling, listed augmentations; post-processing: 0.5 threshold, bbox margins (16 voxels 3D / 1.2× 2D), largest connected component.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice, sensitivity, specificity, plus min-Dice as robustness indicator.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean±SD across 4 folds reported; no confidence intervals, no significance testing against compared methods.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Comparison table against 12+ published methods on the same dataset (Zeng, Zhao, Chen, Man, Yu, Zhu, Cai, Xia, Zhou, Liu, Yang, Fang); ablation and oracle-bbox experiments included.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study; pancreas Dice fully reported (mean±SD, min, oracle, ablation variants).

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit failure analysis: duodenum misclassified as pancreatic head, texture failures (vessels, duct, steatosis, missed tail), slower inference than one-stage methods.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-unclear: all 82 scans of a public dataset used under 4-fold CV with demographics reported, but cohort is a single retrospective public collection; no consecutive enrollment or exclusion criteria stated.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate: identical pipeline and stopping criterion (95% output similarity or 5 iterations) applied across folds; however, the 95% stopping rule is output-dependent, and baseline numbers may originate from papers using different validation protocols, weakening direct comparability.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low: Dice/sensitivity/specificity/min-Dice, ablations, oracle bound, and failure modes all reported; inference time discussed only qualitatively and code unreleased.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) SRDice = Dice with p_i replaced by sqrt(p_i); ε bounds maximal gradient; intended for localization stage where a miss is unrecoverable downstream. (2) SINet decoder head (3×3×3, 3×3×3, 1×1×1 convs + dropout 0.5) uses a padding-factor trick to collapse a 5-slice input to a single-slice output, focusing supervision on the center slice; deep supervision summed over all 4 decode paths; Slice Correlation Module applied only at the last decode path. (3) Slice Correlation Module: bilinear (second-order) pooling produces a slice correlation map; a conv layer produces a slice weight map; their product injects per-slice 3D shape awareness without large 3D kernels/padding. (4) Slice Shuffle pre-training: 5 stacked slices shuffled (margin 3), network recorders them with L1 loss; learned weights initialize SINet. (5) Recurrent refinement crops new bboxes from fusion output and loops through axial/coronal/sagittal SINets + PNet until ≥95% inter-step similarity or 5 iterations. (6) Oracle experiment: 88.14% Dice with ground-truth 2D bboxes vs 86.21% automatic — ~2-point ceiling lost to localization errors, consistent with the authors' failure analysis. (7) Comparability caveats for meta-analysis: 4-fold CV protocol vs leave-one-out in some baselines; reported specificity (85.11±6.49%) is far below the >99% typical in pancreas literature, suggesting specificity was computed within cropped ROIs rather than whole volume — flag when pooling metrics across studies.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a two-stage coarse-to-fine pancreas segmentation framework whose refinement network (SINet) preserves the 2.5D slice structure through all encoder/decoder levels, combined with a bilinear-pooling Slice Correlation Module for non-local cross-slice attention and a slice-shuffle self-supervised pre-training task. A Square Root Dice loss boosts localization recall by up-weighting misclassified foreground voxels. The method achieves state-of-the-art 86.21±4.37% Dice on NIH Pancreas-CT under 4-fold cross-validation, with ensemble fusion and recurrent refinement.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 84 exams / 80 subjects total; 66 train+val (>50 threshold). Small but adequate; noted as limiting for rare structures (uterus in 4 test cases only).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Internal Mayo Clinic RCC cohort; demographics (65% male), scanner vendor (Siemens), and pathology burden described; single-institution.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 66 train/val vs 18 test clearly stated, but the train-vs-validation split ratio and split method (random? patient-level?) are not reported; no cross-validation.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Thorough: 10 analysts + 4 radiologist correctors, RIL-Contour tool, semiautomated priors + manual correction, slice-interpolation protocol, STAPLE consensus for human baselines, bias check via pure-manual subset.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Internal test set only; single vendor (Siemens); authors explicitly acknowledge lack of external comparison.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Layer-level detail: pre-activation residual context modules, 3x3x3 convs, dropout placement, stride-2 downsampling, nearest-neighbor upsampling + conv, skip concatenation, RReLU, instance normalization, input dims.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam params (β1=0.9, β2=0.999, ε=1e-8), lr 1e-3, Xavier init, early stopping criterion, augmentation types/counts given. Missing: batch size, epoch count, early-stop patience, augmentation parameter ranges. Paper has a typo (β1 listed twice).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss with inverse-prevalence class weighting; rationale for weighting stated (class imbalance), but choice of Dice over alternative losses not justified/ablated.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Resampling to 256x256x128 (cubic for image, nearest-neighbor for labels), HU window 1000/100 → [0,1], full augmentation spec; downsampling trade-off explicitly discussed. No postprocessing used/reported.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; only framework (Keras 2.2 / TF 1.12) and annotation tool (RIL-Contour, open source) named.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice, Jaccard, TPF, FPF (reference-normalized), predicted volume, and percent volume error.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Means and one box-and-whisker figure (median/IQR); no confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests anywhere.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive: multi-organ SOTA (Zhou, Gibson Dense V-Net, Roth hierarchical 3D FCN), four single-organ models (LiTS winner, Wang, Ibragimov & Xing, Zheng), and both semiautomated + manual human interobserver baselines.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ Dice for all 23 grouped structures in Table 1/2/3; per-side (left/right) values in supplemental table.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitation discussion (single institution, RCC-skewed population, downsampling partial-volume effects, Dice's blindness to connectivity, machine-prior GT bias) plus concrete failure counts (bladder missed in 2 cases, L5/S1 disc in 2, L4/L5 in 1).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/high concern: single-institution RCC cohort — older, male-skewed (65%), frail patients with tumors/surgical implants; single vendor (Siemens). Selection criteria beyond 'RCC patient' not formally defined.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate: consistent held-out test set and identical metrics across all structures; however, ground truth was created by correcting machine-generated priors, which could bias reference segmentations toward automated-method assumptions. Mitigated by a pure-manual interobserver subset on 6 organs.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low: all 33 structures reported including worst performers (renal arteries Dice 0.51), organ-presence counts, missed-detection cases, and supplemental per-side metrics. No selective outcome reporting evident.

detailed_extraction: Annotation workflow: every voxel labeled (34 classes incl. background); soft-tissue/fat/muscle/bone priors generated by a previously published model (ref 18), analysts corrected + added novel ROIs; every-other-slice tracing (every third slice if <3mm thickness) with linear interpolation; discrepancies reconciled by a single analyst. Human baselines: STAPLE consensus of 10 analysts on 2 test scans (semiautomated); pure-manual segmentation of 6 organs (liver, spleen, pancreas, kidneys, adrenals, bladder) by 3 analysts each to estimate machine-prior bias. Test-set organ presence: uterus n=4, prostate n=10, gallbladder n=12; metrics reported only for organs the model predicted. Key human-vs-model gaps: small intestine (0.71 vs 0.95), colon (0.80 vs 0.96), stomach (0.87 vs 0.97), adrenals (0.69 vs 0.80), renal veins (0.67 vs 0.79). Model exceeded best published multi-organ result on 2/19 structures — notably adrenals (0.69 vs Zhou et al.'s 0.36); within 5% of best on 6 organs; 7 organs not segmented by any prior multi-organ model. Human interobserver: semiautomated range 0.55 (renal arteries) – 0.98 (kidneys); manual range 0.81 (adrenals) – 0.98 (liver). Human IQR exceeded model IQR on the 5 lowest-scoring organs (model more consistent, though lower mean). FPF definition is non-standard: normalized to reference voxel count, not background. IV discs between T12–S1 treated as independent labels. Pathology (tumors, cysts, staples) segmented into constitutive compartments. Not reported: training time, inference time, train/val split ratio, GPU model (only '32GB Volta architecture'). Future work: presence-detection pre-stage for sex-specific/variable organs; failure characterization for human-in-the-loop correction.
contribution_summary: Presents a 3D U-Net variant (pre-activation residual blocks, RReLU, instance norm) with prevalence-weighted Dice loss performing whole abdomen/pelvis segmentation into 33 structures — the largest structure count reported at the time — including tissues typically ignored (adipose, muscle, connective tissue). Its distinctive evaluation contribution is benchmarking against human interobserver variability (STAPLE-based semiautomated and pure-manual), showing the model within 5% of human tracers on 8/19 organs and more consistent (lower IQR) than humans on difficult structures. Demonstrates feasibility and failure modes on a pathological RCC population, providing realistic clinical-practice baselines.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 120 patients (100 train/10-fold CV, 20 held-out test); exceeds the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: IRB-approved, retrospective, single center (Washington University); scanner (Philips Brilliance Big Bore, 16-slice, 85cm bore), 512x512 matrix, 1.5mm slices, 150-200 slices/patient specified.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit: 100 cases in 10-fold CV (90 train/10 validation per fold), separate 20-case test set used for SOTA comparison; baselines evaluated on identical splits.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: OARs contoured by one imaging technician; prostate by two >10-year GU radiation oncologists with consensus contour in Eclipse, aided by MRI-CT fusion; post-prostatectomy patients excluded.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single institution, single scanner; no independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: All components fully specified with figures: multi-residual block (3x3/5x5/7x7 channel ratio 3:5:8), multi-scale pooling block (4 parallel 3x3 convs, dilations 0-3, stride 2, quarter channels each, output H/2xW/2xC), residual forward path, MRF block (two 25x25x3x1 dilated filters replacing one 50x50 filter, 7500 -> 2x1875 params), and 4-layer discriminator with product input.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Hardware (2x RTX 2080 Ti), PyTorch, Adam, polynomial LR scheduler, and 3-stage training with LRs given; but iteration counts given as ranges (10~20k, 20~30k, 20~40k), adversarial balancing weight lambda and batch size unspecified; authors note adversarial stage needs 'delicate hyper-parameter tuning'.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Novel adaptive class-weighted multi-class cross-entropy (w_i = 2 - DSC_i + ln(total pixels/class-i pixels), DSC from last validation step) explicitly justified by organ size and contrast imbalance; adversarial loss adapted from Luc et al. with all equations given.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: No image preprocessing (intensity normalization, resampling, cropping) or post-processing described; MRI fusion used only for annotation; MRF operates in-network.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Four metrics: DSC, Average Hausdorff Distance, Average Surface Hausdorff Distance, relative Volume Difference; all formally defined.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired p-values vs each baseline with significance markers (p<0.05); no confidence intervals, no correction for multiple comparisons; SDs only.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Head-to-head retraining of residual U-Net and multi-residual U-Net on identical data with paired statistical tests; introduction tabulates prior SOTA (Ma, Wang, Kazemifar, Gao); abstract claims additional comparisons vs several DL and MRF methods (that section is truncated in provided text).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Table I reports per-organ DSC/AHD/ASHD/VD (prostate, bladder, rectum, left and right femur) for all three methods with per-cell p-values.

Q15_limitations.justification: No failure-case analysis or limitations discussion present in provided text (paper truncated before discussion section); conclusion claims success only.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate — retrospective, single-center, single scanner; explicit exclusion criterion (post-prostatectomy) but consecutive enrollment and referral pattern not stated.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate — identical splits and metrics across all compared methods; prostate reference is MRI-fused dual-expert consensus, but OAR contours from a single technician with no interobserver variability analysis.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate — full per-organ results with SDs and p-values reported, including non-significant bladder/femur results; however no code release, some p-values absent in femur VD rows, and no limitations section in provided text.

detailed_extraction: Data: 120 intact-prostate radiotherapy planning CTs (WUSTL); Philips Brilliance Big Bore 16-slice, 512x512, 1.5mm, 150-200 slices/patient; whole-gland prostate contouring per clinical standard; individual lesions not contoured. Architecture: S-net = multi-residual U-Net variant (5x5/7x7 filters factorized to stacked 3x3; residual connection after each 3x3; 1x1 for dimension conservation) + multi-scale pooling blocks (four parallel 3x3 convs with dilations [0,1,2,3], stride 2, 1/4 output channels each, concatenated; H/2xW/2xC output — claimed 4x memory savings vs atrous convolution) + residual forward paths (non-linear transform of skip connections to reduce encoder-decoder semantic gap) + MRF block (DPN-inspired: CNN output as unary potential; pairwise potential via local conv with two 25x25x3x1 filters at different dilations + global conv + 3D max-pooling; CNN and MRF trained jointly by energy minimization). D-net: 4 downsampling conv layers + classification layer + bilinear upsampling; input is elementwise product of CT and one-hot label map (prediction or ground truth); per-pixel real/fake classification. Loss: adversarial formulation from Luc et al. (S-net minimizes mCE minus lambda * discriminator BCE; D-net maximizes/minimizes accordingly); adaptive weight w_i = 2 - DSC_i(last validation) + ln(total pixels/class-i pixels), computed batch-wise. Training: 3 stages — coarse (lr 1e-2, 10~20k iters), fine-tune (lr 1e-4, 20~30k iters), adversarial with discriminator (20~40k iters); ~8h total on 2x RTX 2080 Ti; 0.5s/image training, 0.3s/image inference. Results: test set DSC 0.88(±0.11) prostate, 0.97(±0.07) bladder, 0.86(±0.12) rectum, 0.97(±0.01) both femurs; AHD 1.58-3.14mm. 10-fold CV: ARPM-net significantly better than both baselines on prostate (p=0.010, 0.017) and rectum vs Baseline 1 (p=0.028); bladder and femur gains not statistically significant; VD shows persistent prostate under-segmentation (~-6% to -9%) across all methods. Annotation protocol: OARs by one imaging technician; prostate consensus of two >10-year radiation oncologists in Eclipse with MRI-CT fusion.
contribution_summary: ARPM-net is an adversarially trained CNN that combines a multi-residual U-Net variant with multi-scale pooling blocks, an in-network MRF refinement block, and a discriminator operating on elementwise products of CT and label maps, plus a novel adaptive cross-entropy loss that upweights small and low-contrast organs. On 120 pelvic CTs (10-fold CV + 20-case test), it achieved DSC 0.88 (prostate), 0.97 (bladder), 0.86 (rectum), 0.97 (femurs), significantly outperforming residual and multi-residual U-Net baselines on prostate and rectum at ~0.3s per volume. The key novelty is jointly-trained MRF pairwise potentials with adversarial fine-tuning and size/difficulty-adaptive loss weighting in a single network.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 150 stomach cancer patients (6453 CT slices), exceeding the >50 subject threshold. However, authors acknowledge this is a limited dataset requiring heavy augmentation, which is modest by deep learning standards.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single-center dataset clearly described: West China Hospital, Jan 2016–Mar 2019; demographics provided (93 female, 57 male; ages 29–77, median 57); 3-mm slice thickness specified; newly constructed stomach CTV dataset is a stated contribution.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Fivefold cross-validation is stated, with results reported as mean ± standard deviation over five runs. However, critical split details are missing: it is unclear whether splitting was patient-level or slice-level (risk of intra-patient leakage), and no held-out independent test set was used.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process described: each image annotated by a professional radiation oncologist and rechecked by an expert radiation oncologist with >20 years experience; contours approved in planning systems. Caveat: single-annotator workflow, no inter-observer variability quantification.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent validation. All data from a single center, evaluated only via internal fivefold cross-validation. Generalizability to other scanners, centers, and protocols is untested.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture thoroughly described: ResNet101 backbone (blocks of 3/4/23/3 residual modules), DeepLabv3+ encoder-decoder with ASPP, four shortcut connections from all ResBlocks to decoder, decoder dimension-adaptation and concatenation steps, and the SW mechanism formalized with equations (Bernoulli survival probabilities with linear decay p1=0.8, p2=0.6, p3=0.4, p4=0.2).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Mostly reproducible: 200 epochs, batch size 8, initial LR 0.001, weight decay 0.0001, class weight 2, SGD with momentum, PyTorch, hardware specified (4× Tesla K40m, Xeon E5-2620), detailed 5-step augmentation pipeline. Missing: SGD momentum value, LR schedule, and no code release reduces practical reproducibility.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted cross-entropy formula given with class weight = 2, implicitly addressing foreground/background imbalance, but no explicit justification for the loss choice, the weight value, or comparison with alternatives (e.g., Dice loss).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Data augmentation comprehensively described (horizontal flip p=0.5, scaling [0.8,1.2], rotation ≤10°, intensity/contrast variation, Gaussian noise). However, standard preprocessing (HU windowing, normalization, resampling) is not described, and no post-processing steps are reported.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model weights released. Data only 'available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.' Baselines were reimplemented by authors, preventing direct verification.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Three complementary overlap metrics used (DSC, TPVF/sensitivity, PPV/precision), computed in both 2D slice-based and 3D volume-based settings, plus per-pixel uncertainty estimation (recall-precision curves).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: T-tests performed against baselines (significance limit P=0.05) with p-values reported (e.g., 0.0001–0.0008); results reported as mean ± standard deviation over five runs per network. Confidence intervals not provided, but statistical testing exceeds field norms.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compared against DeepLabv3+, U-Net, and DDCNN under identical training/evaluation scheme ('same construction scheme'), plus controlled ablations (constant width vs. standard dropout vs. spatial dropout vs. SW; individual shortcut connection contributions). All baselines retrained on the same data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Not applicable in the multi-organ sense — only one structure (stomach CTV) is segmented. Per-patient quantitative results are not reported (only dataset-level averages), and only 4 qualitative case examples are shown.

Q15_limitations.justification: Qualitative failure analysis of competitor methods provided (e.g., DeepLabv3+ missing left-sided CTV in case 4), and future work discussed (nonlinear survival-probability decay, other target volumes/diseases). However, explicit limitations of the proposed method (small dataset, single center, 2D approach, DSC ~0.75 absolute performance) are not candidly discussed.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/Unclear. Single-center cohort (n=150) with enrollment period stated but no explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria; patient selection process (consecutive vs. convenience sampling) not defined, limiting generalizability.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All methods (including baselines) trained and evaluated under the same scheme with identical metrics (DSC, TPVF, PPV) using automated quantitative evaluation and fivefold cross-validation with repeated runs; main residual concern is single-annotator ground truth without inter-observer variability assessment.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All metrics reported for all compared methods with standard deviations and p-values; ablation studies reported transparently. Minor concerns: no external validation cohort reported, no distance-based metrics (e.g., Hausdorff distance), and the 'first attempt' claim may reflect selective literature framing.

detailed_extraction: TASK SCOPE NOTE: This paper segments the clinical target volume (CTV) of stomach cancer (tumor + subclinical disease region), NOT an anatomical organ or organ-at-risk — relevance to the review's 'organ segmentation' scope is partial. The approach is 2D slice-based (each CT slice segmented independently via semantic segmentation) with supplementary 3D volume-based metric evaluation; it is not an inherently 3D method. ARCHITECTURE: SW-DNN = modified DeepLabv3+ with ResNet101 backbone; key novelty is the Stochastic Width (SW) mechanism applied to four encoder-decoder shortcut connections (one per ResBlock), where each feature map is dropped during training with linearly decaying survival probability p_j = 1 − (p0 − pL)·(j/J), yielding p = [0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2]; at test time all feature maps are active. Conceptually similar to stochastic-depth/dropout but operating on skip connections; interpreted as an implicit ensemble over (F+1)^4 network widths. TRAINING: weighted cross-entropy (class weight 2), SGD with momentum (value unspecified), L2 regularization, LR 0.001, batch 8, 200 epochs, PyTorch, 4× NVIDIA Tesla K40m. DATASET: 150 patients (6453 labeled slices), 3-mm slices, single class (background vs. CTV). ABLATIONS: shortcut connections progressively improved DSC 0.7188→0.7392; SW (DSC 0.7457) marginally beat spatial dropout (0.7450) and beat standard dropout (0.7350) and constant width (0.7392), with better per-pixel uncertainty calibration. MAIN RESULTS (2D): SW-DeepLabv3+ DSC 0.7457±0.0017, TPVF 0.7723±0.0031, PPV 0.7208±0.0047; ~2.1%/2.8%/3.6% DSC improvement over DeepLabv3+/U-Net/DDCNN (all p<0.001); SW-U-Net DSC 0.7336. 3D results: SW-DeepLabv3+ DSC 0.7530 (1.9–5.3% above baselines). ABSOLUTE PERFORMANCE CONTEXT: DSC ~0.75 is moderate, reflecting the acknowledged difficulty of CTV delineation (unclear boundaries, low contrast). Notably, U-Net achieved highest TPVF (0.7835) but lowest PPV (0.6750), indicating over-segmentation tendency. FUNDING: National Key Research and Development Program of China (2018AAA0100201). No conflict of interest declared.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes SW-DNN, a DeepLabv3+/ResNet101-based segmentation network with a novel stochastic width (SW) mechanism that randomly drops feature maps on four encoder-decoder shortcut connections using linearly decaying survival probabilities, acting as a regularizer and implicit width-ensemble to combat overfitting on small medical datasets. On a newly collected single-center dataset of 150 stomach cancer patients (6,453 CT slices), SW-DeepLabv3+ achieved a mean DSC of 0.7457 (2D) / 0.7530 (3D), statistically significantly outperforming DeepLabv3+, U-Net, and DDCNN for stomach CTV segmentation in radiotherapy planning. The authors claim this is the first automated deep learning approach for stomach cancer CTV contouring, and the SW mechanism is presented as a general-purpose, architecture-agnostic component (also validated on U-Net).

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 1917 internal CTs (1380 train), by far the largest pancreas CT cohort at publication; authors explicitly demonstrate performance scales with cohort size via ablation. Far exceeds the >50 threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Fully described: internal Mayo Clinic IRB-approved portal-venous CTs with vendor breakdown (Siemens 1797, Toshiba 106, GE 15) and full slice-thickness distribution; external TCIA (41 cases, full + simulated 25% dose) and NIH-PCT (80 cases) with demographics.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit random split 1380/248/289 (train/val/test); held-out test set used only for final evaluation; ablation experiments reused the same fixed test set.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Two radiologists (7 and 3 yr post-residency) annotated via boundary-points mode in 3D Slicer v4.11.0 with NVIDIA organ segmentation module; cases randomly allocated between readers; repeat TCIA reads separated by >=24 h to prevent recall; external GT rule pre-defined (reader with better intra-reader reliability).

Q5_external_validation.justification: Two independent external validations: TCIA full-/reduced-dose dataset (n=41) and the NIH-PCT public benchmark (n=80), both curated and evaluated separately.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Two-stage modified 3D U-Net fully specified: 3x3x3 kernels, 4 layers, LReLU, 16/32 initial filters doubling per layer, element-wise-sum long skips, fusion of last two decoder layers, 1x1x1 softmax head; 48-architecture grid search documented (Fig. S1).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (Adam), lr 0.0001, step decay every 10 epochs, batch sizes 8/4, early stopping on validation DSC, V100-32GB, Slurm, and offline augmentation are all reported. Gaps: the DL framework/library used for training is never named, and epoch counts/seeds are not given, so exact reproduction is not possible from the text.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Not arbitrary: Tversky loss (a=0.7, b=0.3) and asymmetric Dice loss were both evaluated and the winner (Tversky) selected on validation DSC, with citations for both losses.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing thoroughly specified (400 HU/100 HU windowing, [0,1] linear normalization, stage-specific resizing 128^3 and 256x256x64, offline augmentation per stage). Postprocessing explicitly none — volumes read directly from the predicted mask, which is a clear statement.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model weights released; no URL or license mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC + average Hausdorff distance for spatial accuracy, plus volumetric agreement metrics (CCC, Bland–Altman bias and limits of agreement, absolute volume difference, paired tests).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Unusually rigorous: TOST equivalence/noninferiority testing with a pre-stated margin (0.02 DSC) derived from intraobserver variability, one-sided alpha 2.5%, 90% power, minimum n=42; CCC, Bland–Altman, Mann–Whitney U; p-values throughout.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compared against prior DL models from the literature (Table S2) on the shared NIH-PCT benchmark (their 0.89 vs best prior external 0.76 by Roth et al. multi-scale 3D FCN) and, more distinctively, against human intra-/inter-reader reliability rather than only reimplemented baselines.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (pancreas) so the criterion is trivially satisfied; reporting granularity is high: min/max/percentiles, stratification by sex, slice thickness (0.6–3.75 mm), and dataset.

Q15_limitations.justification: A prespecified failure-case analysis (Sec. 2.C.5) classifies errors as under-/oversegmentation with severity grades (minor <=10%, intermediate 10–50%, major >50% of pancreas volume), and explicit limitations are stated: portal-venous phase only, morphologically normal pancreases only, CT only.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Selection criteria are explicit and curated (negative/unremarkable pancreas report, portal venous phase, <=3.75 mm, visually sharp contours; 77 internal and 9 external cases excluded by two radiologists), which minimizes misclassification. However, the cohort is restricted to morphologically NORMAL pancreases, narrowing the spectrum: performance on diseased/post-surgical pancreas is untested, so clinical performance may be overestimated.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. GT protocol standardized (two experienced readers, 3D Slicer/NVIDIA module, >=24 h washout between dose-condition reads); the external reference reader was pre-specified by intra-reader reliability; identical metrics (DSC, HD, CCC, Bland–Altman) applied consistently across internal and external sets; model inference is fully automated, eliminating reader drift.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Prespecified subgroup and error analyses, per-stratum and percentile reporting, volumetric agreement outcomes, and candid limitations. Minor gaps only: training framework and epoch counts unreported, no code release.

detailed_extraction: Ethics/design: IRB-approved retrospective study, consent waived; DICOM de-identified with Clinical Trial Processor. Internal cohort: 1994 candidate CTs identified from negative/unremarkable pancreas reports; 77 excluded (pathology, suboptimal quality, artifacts) by R1/R2; final 1917 (998 M / 919 F, mean age 58.7 +/- 8.5 y); vendors Siemens 1797, Toshiba 106, GE Medical 15; slice thickness mode 3 mm (n=993), then 0.6 mm (304), 1 mm (273), 2 mm (206), 1.5 mm (114), remainder 0.5–3.75 mm. External TCIA dataset: source is 50 portal-venous CTs of patients with liver metastases (Siemens SOMATOM Definition Flash, 3 mm); 9 excluded (1 calcific pancreatitis, 2 postsurgical, 6 pancreatic lesions) -> 41 cases (16 M / 25 F, 60.8 +/- 14.7 y); mean dose 14.7 +/- 8 mSv full vs 3.7 +/- 2 mSv at simulated 25% dose (75% reduction). NIH-PCT: 80 scans, 1.5–2.5 mm, 53 M / 27 F, 46.8 +/- 16.7 y, radiologist-verified GT. Annotation: R1 (7 yr) and R2 (3 yr) post-residency; TCIA reads repeated at reduced dose >=24 h later for memory extinction; TCIA reference GT assigned to the reader with better intra-reader reliability (R2, DSC 0.87 vs R1 0.83). Model search: 24 architectures per stage (48 total) over activation {ReLU, PReLU, LReLU}, kernel {3,5}, initial filters {16,32}; Slurm-managed HPC; early stopping on validation DSC. Dataset-size ablation: stage-2 retrained with 200/500/800/1000/1200/1500 training cases (20% validation each, fixed test set); DSC increased incrementally with cohort size (Table S1) — supports the large-cohort thesis. Internal results: validation DSC 0.91 +/- 0.03 (0.83–0.96), HD 0.18 +/- 0.15 mm; test DSC 0.91 +/- 0.03 (0.84–0.96), HD 0.15 +/- 0.09 mm (0.04–0.52); validation-vs-test equivalence (DSC diff 0.004, P>0.05). Slice-thickness equivalence P=0.15–0.45 across 0.6–3.75 mm; sex equivalence P=0.08. Volumetry: test-set model volume 99 +/- 31 cc vs GT 101 +/- 33 cc (P=0.33); Bland–Altman bias 2.7 cc (2.4%), limits of agreement +11.4% to -16.1%; CCC 0.97; TCIA model 96 +/- 33 cc vs GT 89 +/- 30 cc (P=0.31); female volumes significantly lower than male for both GT and model (P<0.0001). TCIA reliability: model full-vs-reduced DSC 0.96 +/- 0.02, CCC 0.995 (exceeds both readers); R1 intra-reader DSC 0.83 +/- 0.07 (CCC 0.89), R2 0.87 +/- 0.04 (CCC 0.97); inter-reader R1-vs-R2 DSC 0.85 (full) / 0.83 (reduced); model-vs-R1 0.81 (full) / 0.81 (reduced); model-vs-R2 0.84 (full) / 0.83 (reduced). Statistics: TOST with noninferiority margin 0.02 DSC (SD 0.02) derived from intraobserver variability, one-sided alpha 2.5%, 90% power, minimum n=42; Mann–Whitney U for sex-volume comparison. Error-analysis protocol: low performance defined as DSC < mean inter-reader reliability (test set) or <25th percentile (external sets); consensus review by R1+R2; errors tagged under-/oversegmentation with severity minor (<=10%), intermediate (10–50%), major (>50%) of pancreas volume — results of this analysis fall beyond the provided (truncated) text, which ends mid-Section 3.D. Inference: ~4 min CPU per case, both stages, including DICOM-to-NIfTI conversion.
contribution_summary: Develops and validates a two-stage 3D U-Net (bounding-box localization followed by volumetric segmentation) trained on the largest pancreas CT cohort reported to date (1917 portal-venous scans), achieving DSC 0.91 internally, 0.89 on NIH-PCT, and 0.84 on external TCIA. Its distinctive contribution is benchmarking the model against intra- and inter-reader reliability, showing the model is MORE stable than radiologists across a 75% radiation-dose reduction (DSC 0.96, CCC 0.995), plus validated generalizability across slice thickness (0.6–3.75 mm) and sex via formal noninferiority testing. Positions the pipeline as a scalable tool for pancreas volumetry and radiomics biomarker discovery, though restricted to morphologically normal pancreases.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 55 patients collected, but only 45 used for training (30 per CV fold; 45 for holdout run) and 10 for holdout testing — below the >50-subjects-for-training threshold. Authors acknowledge cohort is small for clinical implementation.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Thoroughly described: retrospective NSCLC cohort from Emory University, free-breathing CT simulation scans, Siemens SOMATOM Definition AS scanner, 0.98×0.98 mm in-plane resolution, 1.25–2.5 mm slice thickness (median 2 mm), contrast agent and dose (100 cm3 Omnipaque 350; 33 contrast / 22 noncontrast), IRB approval.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Clear: threefold CV on 45 patients (random grouping, contrast/noncontrast evenly mixed across folds, multiple observers distributed evenly) plus an independent 10-patient holdout set. No random seed reported, but methodology is unambiguous.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Well described: contours by three radiation oncology residents following published Feng et al. heart atlas guidelines, all reviewed by an attending radiation oncologist with cardiothoracic expertise, smoothed in Eclipse; interobserver variation actively minimized and observer assignments balanced across splits.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation. The 10-patient holdout is from the same institution and same collection as training data. All comparisons are internal; generalizability to other centers/scanners untested.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Five subnetworks fully described (ResNet50 backbone, RPN, multilabel RCNN head, substructure-specific mask head, mask-scoring head), attention gate placement, four separate models (heart; chambers+great vessels; coronaries; valves), patch-based operation, and consolidation scheme with explicit equations (S = Scls × SIoU; weighted clustering with w = f·a·p).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: Adam, lr 2e-4, 200 epochs, batch size 40, no early stopping, patch size/overlap, augmentation parameters, and GPU (V100 32GB) all reported. Missing: DL framework, random seeds, RPN proposal counts/anchor settings, and exact parameters of the consolidation probability function — reproducible in principle but not fully.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Partial justification: rationale for the mask-scoring head (decoupling mask quality from classification confidence) is well argued, and all losses are specified (RPN BCE+regression; mask head DSC+BCE; MS head sigmoid cross entropy on IoU). But the DSC+BCE combination and the baseline 3D UNet's BCE choice are stated without justification.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Clear: resampling to matching voxel size, 128×128×64 patches with 96×96×48 overlap, fully parameterized augmentation (rotation, flipping, scaling 0.9/1.0/1.1, elastic deformation α∈[0,10), σ∈[40,50)), and mask-score-weighted consolidation of overlapping ROI predictions with formula. 3×3 boxcar filter correctly noted as visualization-only.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No public code or model. Paper states code 'can be shared via request to the corresponding author' — not publicly available.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five metrics: DSC, 95% Hausdorff distance, mean surface distance, centroid mean distance, and volume difference — far exceeding the Dice-plus-one minimum.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired two-tailed t-tests with P-values reported for every comparison in all tables (significance at 0.05), plus unpaired homoscedastic t-tests for the contrast vs noncontrast subgroup analysis. No confidence intervals, but the p-value criterion is met comprehensively.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Three internal baselines/ablations (3D UNet, Mask R-CNN without MS head, MS-RCNN without attention gate) plus literature comparisons (Finnegan multi-atlas, Morris 3D UNet, MM-WHS challenge results). Literature comparisons are indirect (different datasets), but ablation design is strong.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Partial: main tables report substructure GROUPS (heart, chambers, great vessels, coronaries, valves) rather than individual organs. Per-substructure results (e.g., LADA 0.66, RCA 0.72, LMCA 0.69) appear only in supplementary Table S2 and only for the holdout cohort; CV per-structure results not reported.

Q15_limitations.justification: Extensive: explicit worst-case analysis with figures, identified failure modes (island contours, coronary discontinuities from RPN misclassification near tumors), patch-based spatial-context loss, absent cardiac gating, small cohort, non-diagnostic scan quality, and contrast-status effects — with proposed mitigations.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate risk. Retrospective, single-institution (Emory), NSCLC-only cohort; no explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria or consecutive-enrollment statement. Free-breathing non-gated scans and mixed contrast status reflect the RT planning population, but generalizability beyond one center and one cancer type is unverified (no external validation).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low risk. Ground truth standardized via published atlas guidelines, three trained observers, expert attending review of every case, and observer distribution balanced across folds. All compared methods trained identically (same LR, epochs, data) and evaluated with the same five metrics on the same splits.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low risk. Both CV and holdout results reported, non-significant findings disclosed (e.g., VD comparisons, coronary contrast effects), worst-case failures shown qualitatively, and subgroup (contrast) analysis included. Minor concern: per-structure variance hidden within grouped averages in main text, and per-structure CV results relegated/omitted from supplement.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details not captured above: (1) Annotation workflow: contours created axially then smoothed in Eclipse (Varian); all 16 structures contoured per Feng et al. 2011 heart atlas; the three residents' datasets evenly distributed across CV folds and holdout to balance observer effects. (2) Architecture novelty vs. authors' prior work (Lei et al., breast tumor in 3D ultrasound): extension from 2D to 3D, incorporation of RPN, redesigned RCNN head for multilabel classification (previously only bounding-box adjustment), and addition of attention gate after the RCNN head for low-contrast boundary enhancement. (3) Four separate MS-RCNN models required because valves overlap chambers by definition and structures vary in shape/size. (4) Consolidation details: Jaeger-style weighted box clustering; ROIs with SIoU > 0.8 counted as cluster members; per-voxel weighted average with weights w = f·a·p (ROI-overlap factor, area factor favoring larger ROIs, patch-center distance factor via normal distribution around mean ROI center); n_missing term down-weights ROIs not corroborated by multiple predictions. (5) Baseline 3D UNet: extension of Ronneberger 2D UNet to 3D operations, whole-volume input (vs. patch-based proposed method), BCE loss, identical LR/epochs. (6) Contrast subgroup findings: whole heart better with contrast on all metrics; chambers/vessels volumetric accuracy better with contrast; coronary artery DSC/MSD NOT significantly affected — authors hypothesize noncontrast scans lead observers to draw larger, less accurate coronary contours, offsetting the network's contrast advantage. (7) Failure analysis: worst cases driven by large tumors abutting the heart (misclassified as chambers) and complete LADA/RCA omission by ALL deep learning methods in the worst coronary case; ground truth itself is ambiguous for coronaries on non-gated noncontrast CT. (8) Runtime: <5 s inference for whole heart + 15 substructures (vs. minutes-to-hours manual).
