(9) Indirect literature benchmarks: Finnegan multi-atlas heart DSC 0.94, coronaries 0.04–0.12; Morris 3D UNet chambers 0.88 / great vessels 0.85 / LADA 0.53 / RCA 0.50 / LMCA 0.50 (proposed holdout: 0.93 / 0.94 / 0.66 / 0.72 / 0.69); MM-WHS comparisons on cardiac-gated/imaging cohorts. (10) FBCT used instead of 4DCT because pixel averaging degrades small-substructure visibility; cardiac motion consequently ignored. (11) Funding: NCI R01-CA215718 and Winship CI pilot grant; declared COI (K. Higgins: AstraZeneca, Varian, Genentech advisory board, RefleXion research funding). (12) Unreported: DL framework, release version, license, benchmark reproduction artifacts.
contribution_summary: First adaptation of mask-scoring R-CNN to simultaneous multi-structure cardiac segmentation, delineating the whole heart plus 15 substructures (chambers, great vessels, coronary arteries, valves) on free-breathing radiotherapy CT in a single framework, with a redesigned multilabel RCNN head and an added attention gate as the two key modifications. The mask-scoring head enables probabilistic consolidation of multiple ROI proposals, yielding statistically significant improvements over 3D UNet and Mask R-CNN ablations across DSC, 95% HD, MSD, CMD, and VD (whole heart 0.96; coronaries 0.66 vs 0.48 for UNet), with <5 s inference. The work targets the clinical need for substructure-specific dose-toxicity studies and cardiac-sparing RT planning, though single-institution training (n=45), lack of external validation, and degraded small-structure performance (coronaries/valves) limit current clinical readiness.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Four public datasets (LCTSC ~60, NSCLC-Radiomics Lung1 ~422, HN1 ~101, MSD) collectively far exceed 50 subjects; per-structure slice totals (e.g., liver 27,449) confirm scale, though exact patient counts per structure are not tabulated.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Four openly available TCIA/MSD datasets named and individually referenced in Table I.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random patient-level 60:20:20 train/val/test split with per-structure counts for each split reported (Table I); no stratification, but methodology is explicit.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Reference contours inherited from public datasets via citation; annotation process (who, protocol, inter-observer) not described in this paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Test sets are held-out splits from the same public datasets; no independent institution/site validation. 'Unseen structure' (spleen) tests structural generalization, not external data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: R2U-Net with attention gates fully described with per-layer feature counts (Fig. 1b), 3-channel input scheme, and sigmoid output.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (Adam, lr 1e-5), batch size 4, augmentation, and a novel 8-initialization survival-selection scheme are given; but epoch schedule is ambiguous, context-slice distance sampling distribution unspecified, framework unreported, no code.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Pixelwise BCE stated and cited, but not justified against alternatives (e.g., Dice/compound losses) despite class imbalance being inherent.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: HU clamping [-1000, 2000], 512→256 rescale, on-the-fly affine augmentation, and bilinear upsampling for evaluation all described with explicit rationale.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model weights released.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC, Hausdorff distance, and relative APL; APL (2 mm tolerance) is well-argued as clinically relevant for correction effort.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Boxplots and mean±SD reported (e.g., spleen APL 0.35±0.21), but paper explicitly states no significance testing of incremental model changes due to small test sets.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Contextual references to nnU-Net, Feng 2019, Hossain 2019; acknowledges below nnU-Net for unseen spleen, but no head-to-head comparison on identical data/splits.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure train/val/test counts (Table I), per-structure boxplots (Fig. 4), and full per-structure results in supplement; seen and unseen structures both reported.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations: absent significance testing, below-SOTA performance on unseen structures, arbitrary model-order choice; quantified failure case (model A on spleen: DSC 0.33).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low/unclear — public datasets with defined inclusion rules and random patient-level split, but structures with sparse or small (<10 slices) annotations were excluded, biasing toward well-annotated, larger structures.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low — identical evaluation protocol across all 6 models and all 19 structures; metrics consistently computed after upsampling to original 512×512 resolution.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low/moderate — all structures including unseen ones reported with distributions (boxplots, supplement); however, no formal uncertainty quantification and detailed per-structure tables deferred to supplement rather than main text.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond prior extraction: (1) Model selection via 'survival of the fittest' — 8 randomly initialized models trained; worst 50% discarded after 5 epochs, halving repeated each time epochs double until one remains, then trained 20 further epochs. (2) Two inference modes: 'direct' (initial contour reused as context for all slices) vs 'iterative' (each prediction becomes next context); iterative superior for unseen structures, comparable for seen. (3) Context-slice distance d sampled relative to each structure's size to prevent the shortcut of copying adjacent contours; target slices may fall outside the structure so the model learns when to stop. (4) Ablation (Suppl. Mat. 3) shows all three input channels (target slice, previous slice, previous mask) are essential. (5) Structures <10 slices or sparsely delineated excluded. (6) Model order for training-set expansion (A→ABCDEF, Fig. 2) chosen arbitrarily, no combinatorial study. (7) Single GTX 1080; ~0.1 s inference per slice. (8) Scope note for review: network is 2D slice-wise; 3D segmentation achieved only via slice propagation — consistent with is_3d=false in prior extraction.
contribution_summary: Proposes a semi-automatic 'contextual deep learning' contouring method: an attention-gated R2U-Net takes a target slice plus a previously contoured slice and its mask as a 3-channel input, propagating a single user-drawn contour through a volume without structure-specific class labels. The key finding is that training-set diversity — not structure-specific features — drives generalization: models trained on more structures segment never-seen structures (spleen DSC 0.33→0.80, HD 44→13 mm), enabling de-novo contouring of arbitrary anatomy. Iterative prediction is shown superior to direct propagation for unseen structures.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 359 pediatric CT scans total; 299 for training, 60 withheld for testing — well above the >50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source fully described: public TCIA collection Pediatric-CT-SEG (doi:10.7937/tcia.x0h0-1706), 3 named scanners at Children's Wisconsin, IRB-approved retrospective acquisition, ages 5 days–16 years, ~1:1 sex ratio, random sample of routine indications, with a companion dataset paper.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split methodology explicit and repeated across experiments: 60-patient test set withheld entirely from training and hyperparameter tuning; additional 10% of the 299 training scans withheld for validation/tuning; controlled splits by scanner and age group documented with per-subgroup sizes and demographics.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth = 'expert manual contours of up to 29 organs', but per-case annotation protocol (annotator count, training, arbitration) is deferred to the companion dataset paper. Interobserver variability quantified (5 experts vs STAPLE), but only on 2 scans / 15 structures.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Independent 60-patient held-out test set exists, but all data come from one institution and the same 3 scanners; no truly external validation at another site. Generalizability to an unseen scanner (Scanner B) is internal, not external.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Modified FCN 3D V-Net fully specified: 3 resolution levels, group normalization, asymmetric encoder–decoder, long+short skip connections, ~300k parameters, 3x3x3 kernels, He init, input 192x192x168, with figure.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Good: TensorFlow 2.0/Keras 2.1.4, Adam lr=0.0001, batch size 7, Dice loss, explicit convergence rule (validation loss <1% improvement over 5 epochs), augmentation ranges, GPU specified. Not fully reproducible: no code release, filter counts per layer unspecified, hyperparameters admittedly empirically chosen.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss stated and used consistently with convergence rationale, but the choice itself is not explicitly justified and no alternative losses are discussed or ablated.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thorough: resample to 2x2x2 mm, crop/pad to 256x256x192 FOV centered on label (two-pass coarse→fine inference for localization), HU clamping [-900,4096], zero-mean/unit-variance normalization, online augmentation; postprocessing (marching cubes → smoothed RTSS) described with note that metrics are computed on 3D masks directly.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or trained model weights released. Data are public (TCIA) and results stated to be reproducible via Plastimatch replication of postprocessing, but the model/code itself is not available (models deployed only via proprietary Varian Research Portal).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Three metrics: DSC, mean surface distance (MSD), and application-specific CT dose % error — all reported per structure.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mann–Whitney U tests (alpha=0.05) for every generalizability comparison with mean±SD reported; per-structure significance called out. Minor gap: no confidence intervals on headline segmentation metrics.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: No head-to-head against competing segmentation architectures (e.g., U-Net variants, nnU-Net). Comparisons are indirect: expert interobserver variability (STAPLE), published numbers from one prior adult CNN dose study, and internal ablations (scanner-/age-specific vs combined models).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Table 1 reports median/mean/SD of DSC, MSD, and dose error separately for all 19 structures; generalizability figures also per-structure.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit and candid: small test sets limit statistical power (false negatives possible); only 3 scanners from one institution; empirical hyperparameters may be sub-optimal; 6 structures dropped after training non-convergence; noisy ground truth in youngest patients; pancreas fails cross-age generalization; independent validation on unseen scanners required.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Retrospective single-institution cohort; described as a random sample of routine clinical indications with ~1:1 sex ratio, but explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria appear only in the companion dataset paper. Subgroup exclusions (Scanner C removed from scanner experiments for age confounding) are justified and disclosed, not ad hoc.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All predictions generated by the same deployed two-pass models and evaluated with identical metrics (DSC, MSD) computed directly on 3D masks, uniformly across all experiments and test sets. Caveat: dose evaluation used a surrogate scanner model (GE Discovery 750 HD) rather than the acquisition scanners — a systematic measurement offset, but applied identically to ground-truth and predicted contours so the segmentation-vs-dose comparison remains internally valid.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate, mitigated by transparency. Per-organ results are fully reported for all structures (no averaging away of failures — duodenum DSC 0.52 is prominently reported). However, 6 difficult ICRP-recommended structures (gonads, prostate, uterocervix, thymus, adrenals) were excluded after training failed to converge — a post-hoc exclusion of the hardest organs from headline results, openly disclosed. Small test sets without CIs limit precision of reported differences.

detailed_extraction: Model input 192x192x168 voxels, deliberately smaller than the 256x256x192 preprocessed FOV to leave room for online scale/translation/rotation augmentation before cropping; ~300k parameters. Single-structure-per-model design (not multi-label) chosen to optimize each organ independently and to keep FOV/parameter budget; consequence is possible inter-structure overlap, removable via postprocessing if needed. Convergence rule (validation loss <1% improvement over 5 epochs) ensures dataset-size comparisons are not biased by extra optimization steps. Group normalization chosen specifically because batch size 7 is memory-limited on the Tesla P40 (24 GB); training orchestrated on in-house Kubeflow/Kubernetes platform. Generalizability experiments restricted to 7 representative structures (easy: liver, kidneys; hard: pancreas, stomach) to limit compute. Scanner study: trained on 138 Scanner A scans, tested on 20 Scanner A + 20 Scanner B (age-matched, mean ~13 y); Scanner C excluded from scanner tests due to much younger age distribution. Age study: 182 younger (mean 4.04±2.11 y) vs 177 older (mean 12.41±2.36 y), 30-case test sets each; combined model on all 299. Key ablation findings: scanner generalization holds (no significant DSC drop on unseen Scanner B); left kidney the only significant scanner-model comparison, favoring the combined model (0.968 vs 0.972); pancreas fails cross-age generalization (younger model on older test set DSC 0.531 vs 0.383, and vice versa); age-/scanner-specific models offer no advantage over combined models, and adding out-of-distribution data neither helps nor hurts performance. Dose pipeline: deterministic LBTE solver (Acuros CTD) with proprietary GE Discovery 750 HD scanner model rather than the acquisition scanners — justified as isolating segmentation-induced error (scanner-modeling error studied elsewhere); organ dose = summed energy deposition within contour divided by organ mass, partial organs normalized by in-FOV mass. Interobserver benchmark: 3 dosimetrists + 1 radiation oncologist + 1 medical analyst independently delineated 15 structures in 2 scans; STAPLE consensus; model reaches human-level agreement (within 1 SD of expert-vs-consensus DSC) in 13/15 structures, and 12/15 in MSD. Structure exclusions: gonads, prostate, uterocervix, thymus, adrenals (training non-convergence, attributed to small size, positional variability, low contrast); skin, bones, breasts not yet contoured at study time; bone model confounded by contrast material. Pediatric vs adult cross-study comparison: comparable or better median DSC on most shared organs vs prior adult CNN study (e.g., heart 0.95 vs 0.92, stomach 0.92 vs 0.90, liver 0.97 vs 0.96; worse: duodenum 0.52 vs 0.61, pancreas 0.74 vs 0.80), with the caveat of a larger training set here. Dose–segmentation decoupling observed: bony interfaces (spinal canal, femoral heads) show dose errors disproportionate to DSC, soft tissue robust to contouring error. Deployment: TensorFlow Serving on cloud GPU via Varian Research Portal; ~60 s end-to-end for all 19 structures on a typical full-body CT. Test set composition: 60 patients evenly distributed across the 3 scanners, 1:1 male:female. Conflict of interest: 4 authors were Varian employees; NIH-funded (U01EB023822).
contribution_summary: This technical note provides the first systematic evaluation of 3D FCN (V-Net) autosegmentation on pediatric CT, using a public 359-scan dataset (Pediatric-CT-SEG) across 19 structures, and quantifies generalizability across scanner protocols and patient age — showing models transfer to unseen scanners but not fully across age groups (pancreas), and that combined heterogeneous training matches or beats scanner-/age-specific models. It links segmentation error to clinical consequence via patient-specific CT dose estimation, achieving mean dose error within 5% for 18/19 organs and human-level (interobserver-equivalent) agreement in 13/15 benchmarked structures. The work establishes a reproducible public benchmark and practical deployment pipeline for pediatric organ segmentation in dosimetry.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 70 CT scans with patient-level five-fold CV (56 train+val, 14 test per fold), exceeding the >50 subjects threshold; however, authors themselves acknowledge this is a modest cohort for deep learning.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Scanner specified (Philips Big Bore 16-slice) and target structures defined (entire duodenum, partial small intestine/colon above kidneys), but no patient demographics, image acquisition parameters (slice thickness, spacing), collection period, ethics approval, or inclusion/exclusion criteria reported. Single-center data implied.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Five-fold cross-validation at the patient level clearly stated, preventing patient-level data leakage; per-fold sizes reported (56 train+val, 14 test). Within-fold train/val partitioning not detailed.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Structures described as 'manually contoured,' but no details on observer number, expertise, contouring protocol, consensus process, or inter-/intra-observer variability. Authors note that partial small intestine/colon coverage creates potential annotation consistency issues.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation; all evaluation performed via internal cross-validation on the same 70-scan single-center dataset.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: SANet thoroughly described: HRNet-w18 encoder, neck (feature merging via bilinear resize + concatenation, convolution-based specialization/fusion with C=64, channel-wise splitting), and SAM decoder (GAP+GMP scale representations, 2-layer 4x4 MLP with sigmoid, element-wise recalibration, pixel-wise summation fusion). Formal equations and figures provided.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Highly detailed: mmsegmentation framework, SGD (momentum 0.9), batch size 8, initial LR 0.01, polynomial decay (power 0.9, min LR 1e-4), 40,000 iterations, loss weights (0.4/0.6/1e-4), augmentation settings, NVIDIA 2080Ti GPU, and slice-by-slice inference with 3D volume stacking for evaluation.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted CE + Dice loss with L2 regularization defined and fully specified, but choice justified only by reference to prior works (Swin-Unet, TransUNet); no task-specific rationale or weighting sensitivity analysis.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing explicit: 3D-to-2D slice conversion, HU clamping (-125 to 275), min-max normalization; augmentation detailed (random resize 0.5-2.0, 512x512 center crop, random flip); post-hoc 3D volume reconstruction for evaluation described. No complex post-processing employed, consistent with 2D design.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or trained model availability statement; only the underlying public framework (mmsegmentation) is cited.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Four complementary metrics: DSC, HD95, RVD (absolute values), and center-of-mass distance (CD).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± SD across five folds reported for all metrics, but no confidence intervals, paired statistical tests, or p-values to establish significance of improvements (many differences vs. baselines are small, e.g., 74.18 vs. 73.97 mean DSC).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Rigorous controlled comparison against UNet, UNet++ (NestedUNet), AttentionUNet, DeepLabV3p, and CascadedUNet all using the identical HRNet-w18 backbone; additionally compared against channel/spatial attention modules and four multi-scale feature exploitation strategies (Final, RC, DSN-S, DSN-NS).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ results (colon, small intestine, duodenum) reported for every experiment, plus per-organ means; parameter counts also disclosed.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated Limitations section covering small sample size (70 scans), partial target annotations (consistency concerns), and loss of z-direction spatial information from 2D input; failure cases explicitly illustrated (blue boxes, Figure 3) showing under-segmentation at ambiguous boundaries.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High/Unclear — single-center retrospective data with no reported inclusion/exclusion criteria, patient demographics, or recruitment process; generalizability to other scanners/centers unverified.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low — uniform training and evaluation protocol applied identically to all compared models (same backbone, hyperparameters, five-fold CV, and volume-level metric computation), minimizing differential assessment.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low/Moderate — all organs, metrics, ablations, and negative findings (e.g., residual connections not helping, limited colon/small bowel gains) transparently reported, and limitations disclosed; however, lack of code release precludes independent verification.

detailed_extraction: NOTE: Although indexed under 3D organ segmentation, this is a 2D slice-based method; 3D evaluation is achieved only by stacking per-slice predictions into volumes. Task: segmentation of colon, small intestine (partial), and duodenum for radiotherapy planning. Data: 70 upper abdominal CT scans (Philips Big Bore 16-slice), contours covering entire duodenum but only partial small intestine/colon above the kidneys. Method: SANet = HRNet-w18 encoder + custom neck (resize→concatenate→1x conv fusion→split into 4 scales, C=64) + Scale Attention Module (per-scale GAP+GMP representation → 2-layer MLP (4x4) with sigmoid → element-wise recalibration → pixel-wise summation). Key design decisions from ablations (single-fold): encoder HRNet-w18 (69.64% mean DSC vs. ResNet34-d8 67.12%, SwinTiny 67.53%, UNet_s5-d16 63.11%); GAP-GMP > GAP or GMP; 2 FC layers optimal; residual connections in SAM harmful (70.22 vs. 69.82); C=64 optimal; sigmoid > softmax. Loss: 0.4·CE + 0.6·Dice + 1e-4·L2. Final 5-fold CV results (mean±SD): DSC — colon 84.06±3.66%, small intestine 76.79±5.12%, duodenum 61.68±4.32%, mean 74.18±3.72%; HD95 — 7.51±2.45, 11.08±2.45, 12.21±1.95 mm; RVD — 3.4±0.8%, 11.6±11.81%, 6.2±3.71%; CD — 7.85±2.82, 9.89±2.70, 9.94±1.58. SANet (10.19M params) ranked best on mean DSC, HD95, CD and second on RVD (CascadedUNet best RVD, attributed to its multi-stage correction); gains concentrated in small-structure duodenum segmentation (61.68% vs. 56.91–60.63% for baselines) while improvements on colon/small intestine were marginal. SAM vs. channel/spatial attention: 70.88% vs. 69.47%/69.39% mean DSC; SAM vs. other multi-scale exploitation: 70.88% vs. DSN-NS 70.05%, RC 69.31%, DSN-S 69.27%, Final 68.17% (reported improvement range 0.83–2.71 DSC points). Interpretation offered: spatial attention favors large organs (colon), whereas channel/scale attention better preserves small-structure information. No external cohort testing; no statistical significance testing; code not released.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes the Scale Attention Module (SAM), a lightweight channel-style attention that adaptively recalibrates multi-scale features by scoring each scale's importance (GAP+GMP representations fed to a 2-layer MLP), embedded into a HRNet-w18 encoder–neck–decoder network (SANet) for 2D slice-based segmentation of colon, small intestine, and duodenum. Under patient-level five-fold cross-validation on 70 CT scans, SANet achieved 74.18±3.72% mean DSC with a comparable/lower parameter count (10.19M) than UNet, UNet++, AttentionUNet, DeepLabV3p, and CascadedUNet, with its largest gains on the small duodenum (61.68% DSC) and a reported 0.83–2.71 DSC-point advantage over alternative attention and multi-scale feature exploitation strategies. The work demonstrates that efficient exploitation—rather than richer extraction—of multi-scale features can address scale-variability in abdominal OAR segmentation, though validation remains limited to a modest single-center cohort with a 2D approach and no statistical significance testing.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: KiTS21 dataset includes 300 patients (240 for training/val, 60 for internal test), well above the >50 subject threshold. Additional independent testing on 60 KiTS23 cases and 24 Qubiq cases. Training used 16,151 2D slices.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Three public datasets clearly described with URLs: KiTS21 (300 nephrectomy patients, contrast-enhanced CT), KiTS23 (60 additional cases with consensus expert annotations), and Qubiq challenge (24 out-of-distribution cases with 3-expert annotations). Clinical context fully justified.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split methodology explicitly described: 80% patients (240 volumes) for training process, with 2D slices randomly split 80/20 into training (16,151) and validation (4,038); remaining 20% of patients (60 volumes) held out for testing. Patient-level splits avoid data leakage.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process thoroughly described: each KiTS21 image segmented by three independent operators for kidney, tumor, and cyst; one annotation randomly selected as GT per patient to avoid operator-dependent bias. KiTS23 uses consensus expert delineation; Qubiq has 3-expert annotations used for inter-observer variability analysis.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Strong external validation: internal test on KiTS21, independent test on KiTS23 (same distribution, later data release), and out-of-distribution external evaluation on Qubiq dataset.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Reference U-Net (Ronneberger et al.) with VGG16 encoder and skip-connection decoder described, with details in supplementary Figure S1. Four uncertainty variants (MC Dropout, MC DropConnect, Ensemble, TTA) clearly specified, including where regularization is applied and how T=10 replications are generated.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Comprehensive training details: 100 epochs (125 for BDC), batch size 16, Adam optimizer with lr=10^-4, dropout rates 30% (BDR) and 50% (BDC), T=10 samplings, model selection criterion (best cyst Dice), and full data augmentation parameter ranges.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Multi-class weighted Dice (mc.wDice) loss explicitly defined with equation, justified by class imbalance (cysts present in only ~7% of training images), with class weights proportional to inverse volume.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing fully described: resampling to 128×128 pixels, CT intensity bounding [-79, 304] HU following Heller et al., mean/std normalization. Post-processing described: per-voxel argmax class assignment and uncertainty map thresholding.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No statement regarding public release of code or trained models. Datasets are public, but implementation details would need to be re-implemented from the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Multiple metrics: Dice coefficient, Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASD), plus uncertainty-specific metrics (RCC, RIU, UA at two thresholds), predictive uncertainty values, and inter-observer variability Dice.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: ANOVA tests with p-values reported for all comparisons across the four approaches, followed by Tukey's post-hoc tests. Mean and standard deviation reported for all metrics. (Confidence intervals not explicitly reported.)

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Indirect comparison only: results contextualized against the KiTS21 challenge leaderboard ('in line with competitors positioned in the middle of the leaderboard') and benchmark results, but no direct head-to-head implementation of SOTA methods (e.g., nnU-Net); acknowledged that advanced architectures could improve accuracy.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Detailed per-structure results (kidney, tumor, cyst) plus derived 'mass' and 'total' metrics for all approaches and both test sets, including Dice distributions (cdf plots) and uncertainty metrics per structure.

Q15_limitations.justification: Thorough limitations discussion: 2D vs 3D architecture choice and its justification, failure on small/under-represented cysts (Dice ~0.21, >50% of patients with Dice ≈ 0), overconfidence on wrong classifications, poor RIU for tumor/cyst, and illustrative failure cases (Figure 6).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low. Patients from public challenge datasets with predefined inclusion (nephrectomy for suspected renal cancer); random, patient-level splits and random GT annotator selection explicitly used to avoid operator-dependent bias. Population is disease-specific (renal cancer patients), which is appropriate for the research question.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All four approaches trained and evaluated identically on the same internal/independent/external test sets with the same metrics, thresholds, and statistical testing; evaluation protocol aligned with challenge recommendations.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All outcomes reported including unfavorable results (poor cyst segmentation, Dice 0.18-0.23; BDR failure modes; lower accuracy of BDC on tumors). Standard deviations and p-values provided. Uncertainty metrics reported at two thresholds with rationale.

detailed_extraction: TASK: Multi-class segmentation of kidney, renal tumor, and cyst from contrast-enhanced abdominal CT, with primary focus on comparing uncertainty quantification (UQ) approaches rather than maximizing segmentation accuracy. ARCHITECTURE: 2D U-Net with VGG16 encoder and skip-connection decoder (note: 2D approach despite review focus on 3D segmentation; Dice/ASD computed over full 3D volumes; authors justify 2D choice for clinical transferability and anisotropic voxel limitations of 3D CNNs). FOUR COMPARED METHODS: (1) BDR = Bayesian CNN via Monte Carlo Dropout (rate 30%) applied to every last convolution operation, active at train and test; (2) BDC = Bayesian CNN via Monte Carlo DropConnect (rate 50%) dropping weights instead of neurons; (3) Ens = ensemble of T=10 deterministic U-Nets with variety induced by random initialization and training/validation reshuffling; (4) TTA = single deterministic U-Net with T=10 test-time augmentations (rotations, translations, flips matching training augmentation ranges). T=10 selected for stable uncertainty estimation following Roy et al. TRAINING: 100 epochs (125 for BDC), batch 16, Adam (lr=1e-4), multi-class weighted Dice loss, model checkpoint selected on cyst Dice due to late learning curve for this class. PREPROCESSING: resampling to 128×128, HU clipping [-79, 304], z-score normalization. UNCERTAINTY DEFINITION: predictive variance decomposed into aleatoric (mean of p̂(1-p̂) over samples) and epistemic (variance of mean probability) components; evaluation via correctness/uncertainty binary maps at threshold IT (0.01 chosen as optimal from UA-vs-IT analysis; also reported at 0.001), yielding RCC, RIU, and UA metrics. KEY QUANTITATIVE RESULTS (KiTS21 test): kidney Dice 0.92-0.93 (ASD ~1.3-1.7 mm), tumor Dice 0.48-0.65 (Ens best, BDC worst; p=0.01), cyst Dice 0.18-0.23 (no significant difference; >50% of patients had Dice ≈ 0, cysts absent in 28/60 test patients). Uncertainty magnitude ranking: TTA > Ens > BDC > BDR (p<0.0001). BDR = most risk-taking (highest UA, lowest RIU; misses flagging some errors); TTA = most conservative (largest uncertainty regions, flags errors but also correct areas); BDC and Ens intermediate (BDC lower accuracy than Ens with similar uncertainty behavior, but Ens more computationally expensive). INTER-OBSERVER ANALYSIS: on KiTS21 differences driven by structure not method; on out-of-distribution Qubiq (kidney only), significant differences (p<0.0001): TTA 0.94, BDC 0.93, Ens 0.88, BDR 0.82 — BDR showed poorer generalization of its uncertainty under distribution shift. PRACTICAL GUIDANCE: uncertainty confined to boundaries suggests trustworthy segmentation; whole-structure uncertainty suggests missed/misclassified structure; per-class (tumor vs cyst) uncertainty maps aid misclassification detection. CLINICAL CONTEXT: renal cancer affects >400,000 individuals/year; CT is preferred diagnostic modality. FUNDING: Italian MUR PRIN 2022 (grant 2022B23JT5), EU NextGenerationEU. RELEVANCE TO REVIEW: included as a multi-class organ (kidney) + lesion segmentation study on CT; relevant caveat — architecture is 2D slice-based, so should be tagged accordingly if the review strictly requires 3D networks; its UQ comparison framework is transferable to 3D pipelines.
contribution_summary: This study provides a controlled, clinically-oriented comparison of four uncertainty quantification approaches (Monte Carlo Dropout, Monte Carlo DropConnect, deep ensembles, and test-time augmentation) built on the same 2D VGG16 U-Net for multi-class kidney/tumor/cyst segmentation on CT. It shows that accuracy is comparable across approaches but uncertainty behavior differs significantly, enabling a risk-propensity-based selection framework: BDR is risk-taking with compact uncertainty regions, while TTA is conservative with large alert regions, and BDR generalizes worst on out-of-distribution data (Qubiq Dice 0.82 vs TTA 0.94). The work also demonstrates current UQ limitations for small, under-represented structures (cysts), where models remain overconfident in wrong predictions.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Partial. Subregion training set = 62 scans (>50, adequate); duct training set = only 22 scans (<50). One of two datasets meets the threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both sources fully described: public NIH Pancreas-CT (TCIA) and private Innopolis-ethics-approved set, with scanner vendors, matrix sizes, slice thickness, sex/age distributions, and clinical characteristics (kidney donors vs. pancreatitis/PDAC symptoms).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Numeric splits reported (62:10:10 and 22:5:10) but split methodology (randomization, patient-level vs. slice-level, stratification) not described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Single radiologist annotated all structures; no annotation software/protocol/boundary-definition details. Intraobserver DSC reported (subregions 0.53-0.68, duct 0.58), which partially offsets the absence of interobserver checks/consensus.

Q5_external_validation.justification: None. Each dataset serves only its own task (NIH -> subregions, private -> duct); no model tested on an independent external cohort, and cross-dataset comparison explicitly acknowledged as not viable.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: DQN fully specified (3 conv + max-pool, 3 FC layers; shared conv / independent FC across agents; Qm/Qe communication), agent start/stop conditions, landmark-guided registration, probability-map generation, and fusion S = P^lambda * R all described; U-Net variants are standard cited architectures.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam lr 1e-4, weight decay 1e-5, cyclical LR schedule, 30,000 iterations, 64^3 patches, augmentation probabilities, PyTorch 1.9.0+cu111, RTX 3080, training time 5-12 h, plus public code. Only batch size unreported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: RL loss formally defined (Bellman/DQN, Eq. 3) but cited rather than justified; the segmentation network's training loss is never specified - notable reproducibility gap.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Augmentation with explicit probabilities (flip/rotation 10%, intensity shift 50%), fixed patch size, and both fusion weighting lambda and binarization threshold tuned on validation set.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Public: https://github.com/sepidehamiri/Segmentation-of-the-pancreatic-anatomy (license/release version not stated).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC plus landmark localization error in mm (3.41-8.54 mm) and intraobserver DSC as an agreement reference.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired t-tests with exact p-values (e.g., duct DSC 0.50 -> 0.68, p=5.36e-13; most model/subregion pairs significant). No confidence intervals or multiple-comparison correction.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Nine comparators: three same-data retrained baselines (3D U-Net, Attention U-Net, Swin U-Netr) plus published methods (Shen et al., Xia et al., Zhou et al.). Caveat: published-method comparisons are cross-dataset and acknowledged as indirect.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-subregion DSC (head 0.53, neck 0.40, body 0.66, tail 0.47, duct 0.71) for each architecture, not just averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid: multiagent landmark error worse than single-agent (8.54 vs 3.41 mm), low intraobserver agreement/no expert consensus on boundaries, neck hardest (0.40), duct datasets not comparable to PDAC-focused prior work.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. NIH cohort well characterized (public, defined inclusion: kidney donors/subjects without abdominal pathology). Private duct dataset is single-center with patients selected for pancreatic abnormalities; explicit selection criteria not reported.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. Evaluation protocol (DSC, fixed splits, tuned-on-validation postprocessing) applied consistently across all compared methods; however the reference standard is a single radiologist (intraobserver repeat only, no consensus panel), and comparisons against published duct methods use different datasets/populations.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Per-structure results, significance tests, and limitations reported transparently; minor omission of the segmentation loss function.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond prior extraction: (1) RL formulation - reward r_t = d(p_{t-1}, p_hat) - d(p_t, p_hat) (Euclidean distance to target); agent terminates within 1 mm of target or at max steps; single-agent starts from ROI center of a fixed-size ROI; multiagent modified from Vlontzos et al. so agents start from the predefined pancreas center rather than random locations; formulated as a concurrent partially observable MDP; duct modeled via 3 landmarks (start/center/end), subregions via centers. (2) Probability map generation - landmark-based nonrigid registration of every training atlas to the target using Euclidean landmark distance as cost; propagated labels merged into P_s (4 channels: background/head/neck/body/tail context) and P_d (1 channel, duct). (3) Cohort specifics - NIH: 82 contrast-enhanced scans, 27F/53M, mean age 46.8 (18-76), 17 healthy kidney donors, Philips/Siemens, 512x512, 181-466 slices, 1.5-2.5 mm thickness. Duct set: 37 scans, 16F/21M, mean age 64.0 (40-88), symptomatic (pancreatitis/cancer), five scanner vendors, 1.0 mm slices, Innopolis ethics approval 2021-10-30. (4) Other - funding: Novo Nordisk Foundation NNF20OC0062056 and ARRS P2-0232/J2-50067; open access CC-BY. (5) Caveat: the supplied full text is truncated mid-Section 2.4 (probability map definition cut off); the segmentation loss, batch size, and test-time details could not be verified from the provided text and rely on the prior extraction.
contribution_summary: First framework to jointly segment the four pancreatic subregions and the pancreatic duct from 3D CT by coupling multiagent DQN landmark detection with landmark-guided nonrigid atlas registration, whose anatomical probability maps augment standard 3D U-Net variants (3D U-Net, Attention U-Net, Swin U-Netr). Improves mean subregion DSC from 0.38-0.44 (vanilla U-Nets) to 0.47-0.51 and achieves 0.71 duct DSC, with statistical testing and public code/annotations. Clinically significant because even experts disagree on subregion boundaries, which the authors handle transparently via intraobserver agreement baselines.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 270 LIDC training cases (243 train / 27 val after 10% holdout) plus 154 LTRC cases; far exceeds the >50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Three named public datasets (LIDC, LTRC, LOLA11) with case counts and characteristics; LIDC subset selection criteria stated (both challenging and clearly visible fissures represented); LTRC described as pathological (COPD/ILD, emphysema, fibrosis).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Splits explicitly stated: LIDC 270 train / 84 test, with 10% of training held out for validation; LTRC (154) and LOLA11 (55) used purely as test sets. Mechanism (randomization/seed, patient-level splitting) not specified, but proportions and roles are unambiguous.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: LIDC GT: semi-automatic annotation by multiple observers in 3D Slicer, refined and validated by an expert radiologist to mitigate bias — process clearly described. LTRC masks come pre-annotated with the database; LOLA11 reference standard held by challenge organizers.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Strong external validation: LOLA11 challenge (55 unseen cases scored by independent organizers, 0.9345) plus fully independent pathological cohort (LTRC, 154 cases, 0.950).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: input strided 5x5x5 conv (24 kernels); three dense blocks of 5/10/10 layers with growth rates 4/8/16; 3x3x3 convs with BN and PReLU; three-resolution pathways via downsampling and skip connections; progressive supervision at each pathway; batch-wise spatial dropout; architecture figure provided.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: Adam (LR 0.01, weight decay 1e-7), input rescaling to 512x512x64, normalization, GPU model (Titan XP), and gradient-checkpointing repo referenced. Missing: batch size, epochs/iterations, LR schedule, data augmentation (none mentioned).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice-based loss (V-Net, Milletari et al.) applied at each progressive stage — stated and cited but not explicitly justified; no discussion of alternatives or class-imbalance rationale.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly stated (volume normalization, rescaling to 512x512x64); postprocessing explicitly none — single forward pass with no atlases, priors, or post-hoc heuristics, which is itself a claimed contribution.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or trained model released; only third-party gradient-checkpointing repo cited.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Beyond Dice: LOLA11 Jaccard from organizers (converted via Dice = 2J/(1+J)), Bland-Altman volume agreement, Pearson correlation (p<0.001), one-way ANOVA robustness tests, quartile/distribution reporting, and runtime (2s/case).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± SD throughout, medians and Q1/Q3 on LOLA11, Pearson correlations with p-values, one-way ANOVA across z-spacing, vendor, and kernel groupings. Caveat: 'significantly outperformed' claims for baseline comparisons lack explicit significance tests.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Retrained 2D U-Net and 3D Dense V-Net baselines; comparison with George et al. (progressive HNN + random walker) on LTRC; LOLA11 leaderboard comparison against Bragman et al. (0.9384), Giuliani et al. (0.9282), van Rikxoort et al. (0.9195).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-lobe (RUL/RML/RLL/LUL/LLL) mean Dice ± SD reported for all three datasets and all models, plus distributional statistics on LOLA11.

Q15_limitations.justification: No dedicated limitations section and no future work. Challenges partially acknowledged: incomplete/distorted fissures under pathology, RML as weakest lobe (0.862 on LOLA11, SD 0.415), semi-automatic LIDC ground truth. No failure-case analysis or discussion of the marginal LTRC gain over Dense V-Net (0.950 vs 0.946).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. All datasets are public and inclusion counts are given, but the LIDC subset was purposively sampled (challenging and visible fissures both represented) rather than randomly — a criterion-based, non-random selection that may not reflect routine clinical case mix.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Fixed test sets with consistent Dice evaluation; LOLA11 scored by independent challenge organizers, removing evaluator subjectivity. Baselines retrained by the same authors; the 2D U-Net used different hyperparameters (LR 5e-5, batch 10) than the 3D models, so baseline tuning parity is not fully verifiable.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate. All lobe-wise results, SDs, and LOLA11 distribution statistics reported, including unfavorable ones (RML 0.862). Offsets: no limitations section, no p-values for the headline baseline comparisons despite 'significantly' language, and the small LTRC improvement over Dense V-Net (+0.004) is presented as an improvement without statistical testing.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond prior extraction: (1) Validation split = 10% of the 270 LIDC training cases (~27), yielding ~243/27/84 train/val/test. (2) Baseline settings: 2D U-Net trained on axial slices containing at least one lobe (512x512, normalized 0-1, Adam LR 5e-5, batch size 10, background-class overfitting mitigation via slice filtering); Dense V-Net trained with same preprocessing as PDV-Net. (3) Reproducibility gaps: batch size, epoch count, LR schedule, and data augmentation (none mentioned) unreported; training time not stated; hardware = 1x Titan XP + Intel Xeon E5-2697 v4. (4) LOLA11 variability is high: RML SD 0.415 and LLL SD 0.373 imply intermittent near-total failures on individual challenge cases despite high medians (0.928, 0.955). (5) George et al. LTRC comparison reported as 0.941 ± 0.255 — the SD magnitude suggests a likely decimal typo in the paper (possibly 0.0255), but the gap (vs 0.950 ± 0.007) and the 4-8 min vs 2 s runtime difference are the substantive points. (6) Framework inference: gradient check-pointing citation is the OpenAI PyTorch repo, implying PyTorch; not confirmed by authors. (7) 'Significantly outperformed' claims are not backed by reported p-values or paired tests for model-vs-model comparisons. (8) First reported fully-3D convolutional approach for lung lobe segmentation per authors; robustness ANOVA covered z-spacing (<=1, 1-2, >=2 mm), four vendors (GE, Philips, Siemens, Toshiba), three kernel types (soft, lung, bone), plus null correlation of Dice with nodule volume and emphysema index.
contribution_summary: PDV-Net combines Dense V-Net feature blocks with progressive holistically nested supervision to segment all five lung lobes end-to-end in a single 3D forward pass (~2 s/CT on a Titan XP), eliminating reliance on prior airway/vessel segmentation, atlases, random-walker post-processing, or user interaction. It achieves Dice 0.939 (LIDC), 0.950 (pathological LTRC), and 0.934 (LOLA11, within 0.004 of the best challenge entry) while being orders of magnitude faster than competing methods. Extensive robustness analyses (vendor, reconstruction kernel, z-spacing, nodule burden, emphysema index) support reliability on both healthy and pathological lungs.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 20 unique subjects, below the >50 threshold. The x200 elastic-deformation augmentation inflates to 4,000 samples but adds no subject-level diversity.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public dataset identified by citation (Zhuang & Shen, ref [15]) with subject count stated. Minor oddity: ref [15] title says MRI while the paper calls it a CT dataset; the cited multi-modality atlas work does include CT.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 4-fold cross-validation is stated and used for all headline results, but fold composition (patient-level vs slice-level), validation set usage, and the data used for the lambda grid search are unspecified. No held-out test set.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: GT point-cloud derivation from masks is well described (mesh -> vertices -> downsample to N=4096, centered at origin), but the original mask annotation process (who/how labeled, inter-rater) is inherited from the source dataset and not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single dataset, 4-fold CV only; no independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: image encoder (3D convs, channels shown), PointNet MLP 32/128/512 + global max-pool + FC, mask decoder with voxel-wise-multiplied skip connections; architecture figure with all channel counts and operation types.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, lr 1e-4, single NVIDIA Tesla K40, fixed input size (128,128,64), N=4096 points are given. Missing: framework, batch size, epochs/iterations, elastic deformation parameters, and grid-search range for lambda.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Standard cited choices (Chamfer [12], soft Dice [7]) with empirically grid-searched weight lambda=0.001, but no substantive justification of why these losses suit the thin-structure problem.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Complete pipeline: LV ROI crop, 1.0 mm isotropic resampling, resize to (128,128,64), intensity /2048 clamped to [-1,1], x200 elastic deformation, GT point-cloud centering/downsampling. No postprocessing needed or used.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice + Hausdorff distance for segmentation, plus Chamfer distance for point-cloud reconstruction.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean +/- SD across 4 folds reported, but no confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests despite claims of 'slightly better'/'significantly smaller' differences.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: U-Net (cited SOTA segmentation baseline) and PointOutNet (baseline for reconstruction), each in 2D-conv and 3D-conv variants, plus two ablations. Fair given no prior joint method exists.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single structure (LV MYO); its Dice, HD, and CD are fully reported with per-fold variance for every variant.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section and no discussion of the proposed method's own failure modes. Qualitative error analysis exists for baselines and ablation variants (holes, outliers, thin regions) via Figs. 4-6.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High concern: single public dataset of 20 subjects with no description of patient selection criteria, demographics, or acquisition protocol; results may not generalize beyond this cohort.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate concern: all models evaluated identically under 4-fold CV with the same metrics; however, the lambda hyperparameter grid search lacks a stated tuning split, and the ablation study used only 1 fold, so it is not directly comparable to the 4-fold table.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low concern: all metrics (CD, Dice, HD) reported for every variant including unfavorable ones (e.g., PC-Unet-2DConv Dice below UNet-volume-2DConv); no selective outcome reporting evident, though no formal limitations disclosure.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond prior extraction: (1) GT point-cloud pipeline — marching-cubes-style mesh from volumetric mask, vertices form dense cloud, downsampled to N=4096 and centered at origin; label GT masks exist from the source dataset, point clouds are derived. (2) Skip connections fuse encoder features via voxel-wise multiplication (not concatenation), reported to reduce segmentation outliers. (3) The mask decoder learns an implicit function f(PF, IF) -> {0,1}; this is claimed as the first work to reconstruct a dense mask from a sparse point cloud via CNNs (validated by PC-Mask-Decoder ablation, Dice 0.725 with GT points). (4) Scope note for the review: single cardiac structure (LV myocardium), not multi-organ; dataset citation [15] is titled as an MRI atlas paper though the CT subset is used. (5) Key quantitative finding is a ~33% HD reduction (10.446 -> 7.050 mm) vs U-Net 3D with marginal Dice gain (+0.008); HD gain attributed to eliminating isolated outliers. (6) Ablations (PC-Mask-Decoder, PC-Unet-no-skip) run on 1 fold only — CD 1.149 / Dice 0.884 / HD 5.862 for PC-Unet on that fold, not comparable to the 4-fold headline numbers. (7) PointOutNet-single-slice has no segmentation output, so it appears only in the CD column. (8) No postprocessing at inference; no inference/training time reported despite GPU being named.
contribution_summary: PC-U Net jointly reconstructs a 4096-point 3D point cloud of the LV myocardium wall and its voxel segmentation from 3D CT volumes, using the point cloud as an explicit shape prior fused into a U-Net-style decoder via voxel-wise-multiplied skip connections. Trained end-to-end with Chamfer + soft Dice loss, it matches U-Net Dice (0.885 vs 0.877) while substantially reducing Hausdorff distance (7.05 vs 10.45 mm) on a 20-subject public CT dataset, and yields hole-free 3D surface reconstructions. The work's novelty is the reverse direction as much as the forward one: demonstrating dense masks can be decoded from a sparse point-cloud representation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 3,643 CT scans (602,708 slices) for SSL pre-training far exceeds 50 subjects. Fine-tuning sets are small by design (BTCV: 21 train; MRI: 92 scans, ~74/fold in 5-fold CV), which is the paper's stated point (low fine-tuning data requirement), but the overall training corpus is large.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources fully enumerated with references: internal MSKCC head/neck (N=837) and lung (N=1,455), kidney cancer (N=710, TCGA-KIRC via TCIA), COVID-19 CT (N=650, Harmon et al.), public BTCV, and internal 92 3D T2w MRI pancreatic-cancer scans with acquisition parameters (TR/TE 1300/87 ms, voxel size, FOV).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: BTCV: random 21 train / remainder validation / 20 blinded test via grand-challenge website. MRI: 5-fold cross-validation with validation-fold results reported. Split seeds/stratification not stated, but methodology is unambiguous and identical across compared methods.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Partial. BTCV ground truth is the established public benchmark annotation, but the annotation process for the internal MRI dataset (rater expertise, number of raters, inter-rater agreement, correction protocol) is not described. Pre-training data are unlabeled by design.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Blinded testing of 20 CECTs through the BTCV grand-challenge website provides independent evaluation. Additionally, cross-domain generalization is demonstrated by pre-training exclusively on CT (no MRI, no pancreatic cancer cases) and fine-tuning on internal MRI.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: SWIN-small backbone, 768 embedding dim, 4x4x4 window, patch size 2, 28.19M parameters, 1-layer linear projection decoder, EMA teacher with momentum 0.996->1 (cosine), student-only network retained for fine-tuning.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Pre-training is well specified (ADAMw, cosine LR 0.0002, 30-epoch warmup, 400 epochs, mask ratio 0.7, lambda_MPD=lambda_ITD=0.1, tau_s=0.1, tau_t 0.04->0.07, 4x V100). Missing: batch size, fine-tuning hyperparameters/schedule for SMIT itself, and code not yet released at review time.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Strongly justified. MIP is motivated by dense pixel dependencies needed for segmentation; ablations (Fig.4) show MIP+distillation beats full-image reconstruction, MPD-only, ITD-only, and multi-layer-decoder MIP, with per-organ-group analysis of where the gains come from.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Explicit: resample to 1.5x1.5x2 mm, crop to 128^3 enclosing body region, random 96^3 crops (6x6x6 patch tokens) for SSL views; sliding-window inference with half-window overlap. No post-processing (none reported, stated implicitly).

Q10_code_availability.justification: Partial only: authors commit to releasing code 'upon acceptance for publication'; no public repository or URL exists at time of review (code_available=false in extracted data).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Segmentation evaluated with Dice only. MSE is reported (0.061 CT / 0.062 MRI reconstruction) but measures pretext-task image reconstruction, not segmentation quality. No HD95/ASSD or volume error for segmentations.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, standard deviations, or significance tests anywhere. With a 20-case blinded test set and 92 MRI scans (5-fold), differences of ~0.01-0.03 DSC are reported without uncertainty quantification.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive: 4 published segmentation architectures (ASPP, nnU-Net, TransUNet, CoTr, UNETR) on the BTCV test set plus ~10 SSL pretext-task baselines (Model Genesis, 3D CPC, Rubik's Cube+, PRCL, DINO, iBOT, SSIM/SimMIM, PCRL, random init on CNN and SWIN backbones) under identical splits.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-organ Dice tables for all 13 BTCV CT structures (Table 1) and all 6 MRI structures (Table 2), plus organ-group ablation analysis (large vs. low-contrast vs. small organs vs. vessels, Fig. 4).

Q15_limitations.justification: No explicit limitations section and the conclusion is one line. Partial credit: small-bowel is acknowledged as least accurate, adrenal glands score lowest (0.754), and the 21-scan BTCV fine-tuning / 20-case test size is visible in the text, but constraints (single institution, small test set, no statistical testing) are not frankly discussed.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. BTCV split is from a standard public benchmark (low concern), but internal data come from a single cancer center (MSKCC) with no inclusion/exclusion criteria stated; pre-training corpus is curated across disease sites, so the representation may not generalize to general-population CT.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. Identical train/test splits used for all compared SSL methods and BTCV test evaluation is blinded via challenge website. Mitigating concern: baseline hyperparameters were 'adopted from their default implementation' rather than tuned per method, which could under-tune competitors; single-run results (no repeated seeds).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. All organs are reported per-organ (low selective-reporting concern), but no uncertainty measures are given, the blinded test set is small (n=20), and the strongest claims (beats all SSL baselines) rest on small absolute DSC gaps (0.002-0.018 over iBOT/SSIM) without significance testing.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details: (1) Pre-training corpus composition: H&N 837 + lung 1,455 (internal + external public) + kidney 710 (TCGA-KIRC) + COVID-19 650, reported total 3,643 scans / 602,708 slices; no MRI or abdominal-pancreatic data included in pre-training, making the MRI result (avg DSC 0.875) a cross-modality, cross-disease transfer result. (2) Decoder ablation: 1-layer linear projection decoder for MIP outperforms a 5-layer transposed-convolution decoder (reconstruction MSE 0.061 vs 0.32 on 10 CT cases; 0.062 vs 0.34 on 92 MRI), and is faster; SMIT's gains over SimMIM-style masked reconstruction (0.848 vs 0.830 BTCV avg) are attributed to this dense pixel regression plus self-distillation. (3) Mask ratio ablation: segmentation DSC rises then plateaus with increasing mask ratio; reconstruction MSE rises slightly; 0.7 chosen as default. (4) Fine-tuning data-efficiency: SMIT dominates all SSL baselines at every fine-tuning set size tested and converges faster (Fig. 3a,c). (5) Organ-group findings: pretext-task choice barely matters for large high-contrast organs (liver, spleen, kidneys); largest gains for low-contrast/high-variability organs (stomach, pancreas, esophagus), small organs (gallbladder, adrenals), and vessels. MIP alone with 1-layer decoder is nearly as accurate as full SMIT (MIP+MPD+ITD). (6) Anti-collapse measures from DINO carried over: centering/sharpening to avoid degenerate solutions. (7) Known weaknesses visible in tables: adrenal glands hardest (0.669-0.754 CT), small bowel hardest on MRI (0.775), and PRCL beats SMIT on gallbladder (0.797 vs 0.787) — the only per-organ loss to a baseline explicitly acknowledged. (8) MRI acquisition detail: 3D T2w with pneumatic compression belt for breath-hold; only validation-fold results reported. (9) Study is single-institution for fine-tuning data (MSKCC); MICCAI 2022 early-accept; arXiv 2205.10342.
contribution_summary: SMIT introduces a self-supervised pre-training scheme for 3D vision transformers combining masked image prediction (dense L1 pixel regression inside masked patches via a 1-layer linear decoder) with masked patch-token and global CLS-token self-distillation from an EMA teacher. Pre-trained on 3,643 heterogeneous CT scans spanning four disease sites, it sets the best reported average Dice on the BTCV 13-organ benchmark (0.878, blinded test) among both supervised transformer baselines and ten SSL pretext tasks, and transfers to MRI abdominal organ segmentation (0.875) without any MRI pre-training data. It further shows reduced fine-tuning data requirements and faster convergence relative to prior medical SSL methods.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: PROSTATEx exceeds threshold (193/200 patients) but is MRI, not CT. The only CT arm (BTCV) uses 23 training + 6 validation volumes — far below 50 subjects. For a CT-focused review, dataset size is inadequate.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both public datasets named and cited (PROSTATEx Challenge [28]; BTCV). Explicit exclusion criteria for PROSTATEx (11 patients removed for T2WI/GT inconsistencies; 4 without contoured lesions).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Clearly described: ten-fold cross-validation for PROSTATEx; 23/6 train/validation split for BTCV. Caveat: no held-out test set; BTCV evaluated on validation set only.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Partial. Prostatic lesions defined via expert radiologist PI-RADS readings (≥2). Whole-prostate and BTCV organ annotation processes not described (BTCV multi-atlas reference not mentioned). GT inconsistencies only surfaced via exclusions.

Q5_external_validation.justification: None. PROSTATEx evaluated via internal ten-fold CV; BTCV evaluated on its own 6-volume validation set. No independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: DeepEdit's contribution (Gaussian-smoothed click-map input channels, mixed click-free/simulated-click training, multi-label support) is well described. But backbones are cited prior architectures (nnU-Net, UNETR) without configuration details; click-map Gaussian parameters not specified.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: LR 1e-4, batch size 1, Adam, 200 epochs (BTCV), augmentation transforms, and exact library versions (MONAI Core 0.8.1, MONAI Label 0.3.1) reported; code public. Minor gaps: loss, prostate-task epochs, clicks-per-iteration during training.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function not reported anywhere in the paper.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing thorough for all tasks (resampling, whitening/interquartile normalization, ADC/Cb2000 registration, prostate-region cropping with margin, fixed output sizes). No post-processing reported.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Fully public and maintained within the Project-MONAI/MONAILabel repository, integrated with 3D Slicer and OHIF front-ends.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice coefficient only. No HD95, ASSD, or volumetric metrics.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive only: mean ± std over ten-fold CV, and three repetitions averaged to account for simulated-click placement variability. No significance tests or confidence intervals.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Strong comparisons: nnU-Net (prostate), UNETR (BTCV), DeepGrow. BTCV baselines retrained with identical images, transforms, and epochs — a genuinely fair comparison.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-task results reported, but the multilabel BTCV run (spleen, liver, both kidneys) is reported only as an aggregate Dice; no per-organ breakdown for the CT experiments.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section, no failure-case analysis. Key weaknesses (simulated clicks instead of user studies, 6-volume CT evaluation) are not acknowledged.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. PROSTATEx exclusions explicitly stated with reasons. BTCV is a fixed public benchmark used as-is; no patient selection criteria discussed. Only 6 CT volumes available for evaluation.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. All interactive evaluation uses simulated inference clicks — applied consistently across models (fair), but never validated against real user interaction, so reported gains may not transfer to clinical use. Baseline retraining under identical conditions mitigates tuning bias.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Dice-only reporting; per-organ breakdown withheld for multilabel BTCV; loss function unreported; no limitations section despite evident ones (small CT set, no human study). Active-learning workflow claimed but not quantitatively evaluated (no annotation-time results).

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Evaluation protocol — interactive performance assessed at 0/1/5/10 simulated inference clicks (not real users); prostate results are averages of three click-placement repetitions; BTCV results from the 6-volume validation set only. (2) Training regime — fraction of click-free iterations p ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5} sampled from uniform distribution; DeepEdit-0 is explicitly equivalent to DeepGrow; number of simulated clicks per training iteration is user-configurable and not disclosed for the reported experiments. (3) Key trade-off — higher click-free fraction improves 0-click Dice but degrades with-click Dice relative to DeepEdit-0 (e.g., BTCV multilabel: DeepEdit-0.25 = 0.901 at 0 clicks vs 0.906 at 10; DeepEdit-0 = 0.892 at 0 vs 0.926 at 10). DeepEdit never exceeds dedicated automatic baselines at 0 clicks (spleen: 0.874 best vs UNETR 0.919). (4) Scope flag for CT-focused review — only BTCV experiments use CT (spleen single-label; spleen/liver/left kidney/right kidney multilabel, aggregate Dice only); all prostate work is T2WI MRI (lesion task adds ADC + computed b2000 DWI), so MRI evidence should be excluded or flagged in CT-specific synthesis. (5) Unreported items — loss function, GPU hardware, training/inference times, click-map Gaussian sigma, PROSTATEx epoch count. (6) Active learning (aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty ranking) is implemented and integrated but evaluated only qualitatively/design-level; claimed annotation-time savings are not measured. (7) Additional applications (metastatic spine, teeth) shown qualitatively in supplementary material only. (8) Venue note: MICCAI 2022 paper; arXiv v1 posted May 2023. (9) Provenance: King's College London + NVIDIA collaboration; part of the MONAI ecosystem.
contribution_summary: DeepEdit unifies automatic and click-based interactive 3D segmentation in a single network: Gaussian-smoothed label/background click maps occupy extra input channels, and mixed click-free/simulated-click training enables one model to serve fully automatic, semi-automatic, and refinement modes with multi-label support and pluggable backbones. Against retrained nnU-Net (prostate MRI) and UNETR (BTCV abdominal CT) baselines, simulated clicks substantially improve Dice (prostatic lesion 0.27→0.72 at 10 clicks) while click-free performance stays near automatic-baseline level. Released in MONAI Label with 3D Slicer/OHIF integration, it operationalizes uncertainty-driven active-learning annotation — though with Dice-only evaluation and no real-user or annotation-time validation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 20 CT volumes total, 15 with tumors actually used, in 2-fold CV. Far below the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: 3DIRCADb clearly described: 20 venous-phase contrast-enhanced CT volumes from multiple European hospitals/scanners, publicly available with URL, cited (Soler et al. 2012), and justified over grand-challenge data for heterogeneity.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split stated (2-fold cross-validation on the 15 tumor volumes) but fold composition, existence of any validation set for model selection/early stopping, and per-fold results are not reported.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process never described. No mention of who annotated liver/lesions, how many observers, inter-observer agreement, or reference standard provenance beyond the dataset citation.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort. All experiments on the single public 3DIRCADb dataset.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Identified as two cascaded 2D U-Nets (19 conv layers) with liver-ROI cropping/resampling between stages, but relies on the Ronneberger citation for layer specifics; input sizes, filter counts, and step-2 input resolution are not given.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: LR (0.001), momentum (0.8), weight decay (0.0005), framework (Caffe), and GPU (Titan X) reported; missing batch size, iteration/epoch count, optimizer name (SGD implied), and the actual tuned CRF parameter values (only 'random search' stated).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted cross-entropy explicitly justified: class balancing via ω_class = 1/|pixels of class| is motivated by extreme lesion class imbalance, with the observation that small-structure segmentation fails without it. Formula provided (Eq. 1).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing fully specified (HU window [-100,400], histogram equalization, augmentation by translation/rotation/Gaussian noise → 22,693 slices); post-processing (dense 3D CRF) given with full energy/pairwise-potential formulation (Eqs. 2-3) and mean-field inference, though exact kernel values are unreported.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Trained models released under open-source license at https://github.com/IBBM/Cascaded-FCN; explicitly intended for fine-tuning to other CT applications.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five metrics: Dice, VOE, RVD, ASD, MSD — the standard grand-challenge (SLIVER) metric set.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: One paired two-sided t-test reported (p < 4·10⁻¹⁹ for CRF improvement), but no confidence intervals, no correction for multiple comparisons, and no significance testing for the CFCN-vs-UNet or vs-competing-methods comparisons.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compares against U-Net baseline (ablation) and three published methods (Li 2015 graph cut, Chartrand 2014 semi-automatic, Li 2013 level set). Caveat: competitor numbers are copied from original papers, not re-run on identical splits.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver Dice reported per-method, but lesion segmentation — half the paper's stated aim — has no aggregate quantitative result; 82.3% appears only as a single qualitative example in Fig. 1.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations or failure-case discussion anywhere in the paper. Small dataset, 2D-only design, and qualitative-only lesion results are never acknowledged.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Inclusion rule is explicit and exhaustive within the source (all 15/20 tumor-bearing 3DIRCADb volumes used), but a single public dataset with no consecutive clinical cohort limits generalizability and inflates apparent robustness.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. Own ablations (UNet → CFCN → +CRF) are evaluated consistently with identical metrics, but all external comparisons quote numbers from original publications under potentially different evaluation protocols and splits, favoring the proposed method.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate-high. Lesion segmentation results are selectively reported (one cherry-picked 82.3% example, no mean/median lesion Dice, no per-lesion-size breakdown) despite lesions being central to the title and abstract; no failure cases shown.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Evaluation protocol is 2-fold cross-validation on 15 tumor-bearing volumes of 3DIRCADb (5 volumes excluded for having no tumors); lesion burden ranges 1-42 lesions per volume with heterogeneous contrast enhancement. (2) Metrics are those of the SLIVER/grand-challenge benchmarks [9,4]; voxel spacing is anisotropic (0.57-0.8mm xy, 1.25-4mm z), which the authors give as the explicit reason for 2D slice-wise FCNs + 3D CRF instead of volumetric 3D convolutions (VRAM limits). (3) Labels L={0,1,2} = background/liver/lesion; the loss (Eq. 1) is a per-voxel weighted binary cross-entropy form with ω_class = 1/|pixels of class xi=k|. (4) CRF: fully-connected graph over all voxels, Potts pairwise terms with spatial (w_pos, σ_pos) and bilateral appearance (w_bil, σ_bil, σ_int) kernels, unaries = −log FCN softmax, MAP via Krähenbühl & Koltun mean-field; hyperparameters tuned by random search (values unreported). (5) Runtime: 0.2s per slice per U-Net (0.4s CFCN, 0.8s with CRF), <100s per volume on Titan X. (6) Ablation ladder on liver Dice: 72.9% (single U-Net) → 93.1% (CFCN) → 94.3% (+3D CRF); VOE 39% → 12.8% → 10.7%. The cascade's main documented effect is eliminating false-positive lesions outside the liver ROI (Fig. 1A-B vs C). (7) The t-test (p < 4·10⁻¹⁹) covers only the CRF refinement step. (8) Competitor rows in Table 1 are transcribed from the cited papers, not re-evaluated; Chartrand et al. is semi-automatic, so not a like-for-like comparison. (9) License type unspecified beyond 'open-source'; release version and benchmark (e.g., SLIVER leaderboard) submission not documented.
contribution_summary: First application of fully convolutional networks to liver CT segmentation via a two-stage cascade of 2D U-Nets, where the first network segments the liver and the second segments lesions within the cropped liver ROI, drastically reducing lesion false positives. A dense 3D conditional random field (mean-field inference) is added as a volumetric post-processing step to enforce spatial coherence across slice-wise 2D predictions, raising liver Dice from 93.1% to 94.3% at <100s per volume. Trained models are open-sourced, and the authors position multi-organ extension via multiple cascaded FCNs as future work.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Partial: abdominal model trained on 85 scans (>50), but chest model trained on only 40 (<50); external sets also small (55 and 10).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Clearly described: single-center SNUH; abdominal CT from emergency department (Jun-Nov 2020, Canon Aquilion ONE); chest CT from health checkups (Jan-Feb 2021) on 3 named scanners with counts; external sets from different named scanners; acquisition params in supplementary tables.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit random splits 85/10/10 (abdominal) and 40/10/10 (chest) for train/tuning/internal test, plus fully separate external test sets from different scanners.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Thorough: preliminary labels via MEDIP PRO v2.0.0, manually corrected slice-by-slice by a board-certified radiologist (6 y body CT experience) with explicit annotation rules (exclude hepatic fissures/IVC/portal veins; kidney cortex+medulla only; focal lesions included). Caveat: single annotator, no inter-rater agreement.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Yes: 55 abdominal + 10 chest CT external tests on scanners different from development. Caveat: same institution (single-center), chest external n=10.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D nnU-Net with self-configuration; Figure 1 details Leaky ReLU, instance norm, softmax; final patch sizes given (56x192x160, 96x160x160); residual details deferred to Isensee et al. (ref 20), appropriate for nnU-Net.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Key hyperparameters reported: SGD Nesterov 0.99, polynomial LR (init 0.01), 1000 epochs, Dice+CE loss, patch sizes, batch>=2 memory constraint; nnU-Net auto-configuration makes remaining settings deterministic. Minor gaps: nnU-Net version, GPU hardware, seeds not stated.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice + cross-entropy sum, explicitly justified via nnU-Net's published ablations (convergence speed, class-imbalance handling, stability) in the Discussion; no own ablation, but the choice is reasoned and cited.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly described: nnU-Net auto-configured pipeline (patch size, pooling, kernel); MEDIP PRO for label preparation; novel input conditioning on organ-area masks from a body-composition segmentation algorithm. Postprocessing: none applied/none reported (stated implicitly).

Q10_code_availability.justification: Partial only: no public repo; algorithm available as commercial product (MEDIP PRO, MEDICAL IP) and code 'on reasonable request' from corresponding author. Not independently verifiable.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC + sensitivity + precision, plus ICC, Bland-Altman (95% LoA), and volume/radiomics agreement metrics.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: ICCs with 95% CIs, paired t-tests with exact p-values, mean +/- SD for DSC, Bland-Altman with 95% LoA, pre-defined <5% volume-error threshold, R 4.2.0.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Narrative comparison only (refs 27-30: contrast-enhanced DSC 0.94-0.97; fine-tuned non-contrast model 0.96 liver/0.94 spleen; KiTS19). No head-to-head benchmark or re-implementation on shared data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-organ tables (Table 1: DSC/sensitivity/precision per organ, internal and external, both models; Table 2: ICC per feature per organ).

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit 4-point limitations section (small external set, normal organs only, incomplete chest CT coverage, feature-dependent radiomics reliability) plus a concrete failure-case analysis (Fig. 3: calyceal stone distorts skewness/kurtosis).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (age >=18, no organ resection/intervention, no contour-distorting masses, excluded large cysts/ADPKD); but single-center, abdominal cases from emergency department, chest cases from health checkups, and normal/near-normal organs only (diseased anatomy untested); not stated whether sampling was consecutive.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low for segmentation evaluation (model vs GT on identical images, identical metrics internal/external). Concerns: GT created by a single radiologist using commercial software with no inter-rater reliability check; conflict of interest — one author is a MEDICAL IP employee and another is MEDICAL IP founder/CEO, and the model ships in their commercial product (MEDIP PRO).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All planned outcomes reported per organ and per feature, including unfavorable results (skewness ICC 0.210-0.831, kurtosis 0.053-0.933, sphericity 0.368-0.819; significant volume biases for liver/kidneys). Some results relegated to supplementary material; no protocol registration mentioned.

detailed_extraction: Ethics: SNUH IRB approval, informed consent waived (retrospective). Cohorts: abdominal development set = non-enhanced ED CT, Jun-Nov 2020, single scanner (Canon Aquilion ONE); chest development set = health-checkup low-dose CT, Jan-Feb 2021, three scanners (Somatom Force n=25, Somatom Definition n=20, Philips iCT 256 n=15); chest external set on GE Discovery CT750 HD; full acquisition/reconstruction parameters in supplementary tables 1-2. Inclusion: age >=18, no surgical/interventional treatment of target organs, no mass-like lesions altering organ contours; excluded large/extensive cysts (e.g., ADPKD); organ size not an exclusion criterion; incomplete chest-CT coverage of liver/spleen included (evaluation restricted to scanned portion).
