Annotation rules: exclude hepatic fissures, intrahepatic IVC, main/lobar portal veins from liver; kidney = cortex + medulla only (renal sinus excluded); focal lesions included in masks. Training: patch size initialized to median image shape, iteratively reduced until batch >=2 fits GPU memory; final patches 56x192x160 (abdominal), 96x160x160 (chest); input conditioned on internal-organ-area masks from a published body-composition model (Lee et al. 2021, ref 24). Volumetry: <5% volume error achieved in 98.2%/90.9%/83.6%/94.5% of external cases (liver/spleen/RK/LK) and 9/10 chest cases per organ; paired t-tests significant for liver/RK/LK abdominal (p<0.001, 0.004, <0.001) and chest liver (p=0.006); spleen non-significant (p=0.674, p=0.401); mean volume differences -0.7% to 2.2%. Radiomics: 3 shape + 7 first-order features; mean HU difference <1 HU (abdominal), 0.3/1.2 HU (chest); SD ICCs moderate-good (0.728-0.883 abdominal, 0.793-0.877 chest); failure example: left-kidney calyceal stone changes skewness -1.907 vs -3.344 and kurtosis 10.210 vs 197.886 between GT and model masks (Fig. 3). Statistics: R 4.2.0; ICC bands per Koo & Li (poor <0.5, moderate 0.5-0.75, good 0.75-0.9, excellent >0.9); <5% volume difference pre-defined as accurate. Code/model: algorithm deployed in commercial MEDIP PRO (MEDICAL IP Co. Ltd.); code 'on reasonable request' from corresponding author; no public repo, version, or license — nuance vs previously recorded code_available=false. Conflicts/funding: J.-M. Kim is a MEDICAL IP employee; S.J. Park is MEDICAL IP founder/CEO; supported by SNU New Faculty Startup Fund and NRF-2021R1F1A1059901. Not reported: GPU hardware, nnU-Net version, training/inference time, seeds, augmentation details.
contribution_summary: Two self-configured 3D nnU-Net models segment liver, spleen, and both kidneys on non-enhanced abdominal CT and liver/spleen on low-dose chest CT, achieving external-test DSCs of 0.952-0.969 — matching contrast-enhanced-CT SOTA despite the harder non-contrast input. The main novelty is the downstream reliability analysis rather than the segmentation itself: automated volumetry is trustworthy (ICC >=0.986, <5% error in most cases), and a defined subset of radiomics features (HU statistics, uniformity, entropy, elongation, flatness) is reliably automatable while skewness, kurtosis, and sphericity are not. This enables opportunistic volumetry and fatty-liver assessment from already-acquired non-contrast and low-dose chest CTs, with the model commercialized via MEDIP PRO.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Well above the >50 subject threshold: 193 CTs (D-CT) and 120 MRIs (D-MRI) for segment models under 5-fold CV; 750 lesion-model training studies (429 CT, 321 MRI; 722 manually segmented) with 80 held-out test studies (153 CT lesions, 118 MRI lesions); plus a 172-study TACE cohort and LiTS external test set.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources comprehensively described: single-center institutional clinical data warehouse (University Hospital Basel) with SQL-based report retrieval and GPT-4o report screening; public Couinaud CT dataset (Tian et al.); TotalSegmentator MRI subset; public LiTS benchmark. Flowcharts (Figs. 1-2) document cohort derivation with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (poor image quality, missing sequences, incomplete data).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Splits are clearly described (5-fold CV for segment models; 750/80 train-test for lesion model; random 40-study blinded inter-rater subset), but splitting was performed at study level rather than patient level — acknowledged by the authors as a possible source of data leakage that could inflate metrics, hence not 'good' despite being clearly reported.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process thoroughly described: junior physician (reader 1) performed voxel-wise Couinaud and lesion segmentation under supervision of a radiologist with 3 years' experience (reader 2) on the NORA platform; supervisor corrections documented (12 CTs, 19 MRIs corrected; 4 complex postoperative cases excluded); D-CT used public expert annotations; blinded dual reading on 40 studies quantified reference-standard ambiguity.

Q5_external_validation.justification: External validation performed by applying the lesion model directly, without fine-tuning, to the public LiTS test set (131 lesions; sensitivity 65.7%, FP/c 0.73, Dice 0.593, PPV 80.17%). Caveat: external validation covered the lesion model only; segment models were evaluated via internal cross-validation on public data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: nnU-Net (Isensee et al., Nature Methods) used unmodified — the architecture is fully specified in the cited framework publication; the paper clearly defines the four trained variants (SMCT, SMMRI, joint CT+MRI Lesion Model, LM-onlyCT ablation) and their data allocations.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partially reproducible: nnU-Net's self-configuration determines most hyperparameters and all training/evaluation code is open-source, but the paper omits explicit hyperparameters, GPU hardware, training time, and inference time; the 'iterative optimization process' for the lesion model is described only by reference to prior work (TotalSegmentator).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never explicitly stated — implicitly defined by nnU-Net defaults. The discussion partially addresses loss design by noting nnU-Net's adaptive loss weighting (Dice or focal loss) and patch-based sampling to counter class imbalance in small Couinaud segments (I, IVa), but no explicit statement or justification of the chosen loss is provided.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly attributed to nnU-Net's automatic self-configuring pipeline (resampling, normalization, cropping); post-processing/detection decision rules explicitly specified: >=20% volume overlap with reference, minimum absolute lesion volume 0.06 ml, and a 15-lesion-per-scan cap for disseminated disease.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Models, training code, and evaluation pipelines openly released via the TotalSegmentator GitHub repository; partially integrated into TotalSegmentator with full incorporation planned; article is Open Access (CC BY 4.0); authors explicitly state 'Data Availability: Our model is publicly available on GitHub'.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Rich metric set beyond Dice: lesion-wise sensitivity, false positives per case, PPV, precision, F1, Cohen's kappa for detection, volume difference, and HU attenuation change (TACE analysis), reported separately per modality and model variant.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: 95% CIs via non-parametric bootstrapping (1000 iterations); Shapiro-Wilk normality testing; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with p<0.05 threshold; Cohen's kappa for inter-rater agreement; non-significant results explicitly reported (TACE volume p=0.32; LM vs LM-onlyCT p=0.05).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive comparisons: Hu et al. (0.9725 whole-liver CT), Tian et al. (0.882 Couinaud CT vs their 0.897), Han et al. (0.920 MRI segments vs their 0.847), Vorontsov et al. (CRLM FCN), Dai et al. (MRI detection), Araujo et al. RetinaNet+U-Net (LiTS Dice 0.83 vs their 0.593), and LiTS challenge leaders (Dice 0.67-0.74), plus direct zero-shot benchmarking on LiTS; the generalizability-vs-specialization trade-off is candidly discussed.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure results reported: boxplots of Dice for each Couinaud segment for both CT (Fig. 5a) and MRI (Fig. 5b), with discussion of variability in small segments (I, IVa); lesion results broken down per modality and per model variant (Tables 1-2).

Q15_limitations.justification: Thorough limitations discussion: single-center design, study-level (not patient-level) splitting/data-leakage risk, class imbalance in small segments, MRI protocol/field-strength/contrast-agent variability, inherent lesion-identification ambiguity (inter-reader kappa 0.244), computational efficiency unaddressed, TACE analysis framed as qualitative only. Concrete failure examples illustrated (vessels and a renal tumor segmented as false positives, Fig. 7).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Retrospective single-center design; cases identified via keyword ('liver'/'TACE') screening of radiology reports (GPT-4o-assisted), which may introduce spectrum/collider bias toward lesion-bearing or treated patients; explicit exclusion of poor-quality/incomplete studies; study-level split risks train-test patient overlap. Mitigating factors: prespecified TACE time windows (+/-6/12 months), inclusion of lesion-negative cohorts, and deliberately heterogeneous real-world sampling with minimal exclusions, all transparently reported.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Outcomes assessed with prespecified, standardized metrics and detection thresholds applied uniformly across all cohorts; blinded independent dual reading for the inter-rater subset. Caveat: the primary reference standard was created by a single junior reader under senior supervision, and the fair inter-rater kappa (0.244) indicates an inherently ambiguous reference standard against which the model was judged.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All preplanned metrics reported with 95% CIs, including unfavorable outcomes (MRI lesion Dice 0.337; LiTS Dice below challenge leaders; non-significant TACE volumetric change; non-significant LM vs LM-onlyCT difference); failure cases illustrated. Minor gaps: per-segment results presented graphically (boxplots) rather than as numeric tables; segment models lack external validation; no ablation beyond LM-onlyCT.

detailed_extraction:
PUBLICATION & ETHICS: J Imaging Inform Med 2026;39:3508-3523 (online 24 Oct 2025; received 23 Jun 2025, accepted 30 Sep 2025); Open Access CC BY 4.0; ethics waiver EKNZ BASEC 2023-00446 (retrospective, fully anonymized data); CLAIM checklist followed; corresponding author A.J. Wilder-Smith, University Hospital Basel; all authors affiliated with Clinic of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine, USB.
IMAGING PROTOCOLS: CT — Siemens (Somatom Force/Edge/Definition Flash/Definition AS+/go.top), Philips iCT 256, GE Revolution CT; late arterial + portal venous phases with iodinated contrast; kVp min/median/max 70/100/512; slice thickness 0.6/1.5/3.0 mm; tube current 0/191/2595 mA. MRI — Siemens scanners, T1 VIBE with Dixon fat suppression (GRE predominant); TE 1.23/2.39/90 ms; TR 3.95/6.64/1100 ms; slice thickness 1.5/3/6 mm; contrast agents Primovist, Dotarem, Gadovist at variable dosages; no phase/protocol selection prior — heterogeneity deliberately embraced.
NLP COHORT-CONSTRUCTION PIPELINE: SQL retrieval of reports containing keyword 'liver' (or 'TACE' for D-TC); text truncated to +/-200 characters around keyword; PHI de-identification; GPT-4o (OpenAI) screening for 16 lesion entities: HCC, cholangiocarcinoma, abscess, cyst, haemangioma, metastasis/metastases, adenoma, FNH, cystadenoma, angiosarcoma, fibrolamellar carcinoma, hamartoma, Meyenburg complex, regenerative nodule, angiomyolipoma, echinococcosis.
COHORT FLOW ARITHMETIC: Lesion pipeline: 905 initial studies -> 71 unavailable -> 4 excluded (2 CT, 2 MRI, poor quality) -> 830 -> 750 training (429 CT/321 MRI; 722 manually segmented; 28 lesion-negative used to refine detection thresholds) + 80 test (46 CT/153 lesions; 34 MRI/118 lesions). TACE (D-TC): 232 retrieved -> 172 valid; inclusion window <=6 months pre to <=12 months post-TACE; late-arterial phase preferred, portal-venous substituted when unavailable; serial-TACE chaining permitted (post-procedural scan of one TACE may serve as pre-TACE baseline for the next). Segment cohorts: D-CT = 193 public CTs with public Couinaud annotations (Tian et al. GLC-UNet dataset); D-MRI = 120 TotalSegmentator MRI subset ('abdomen'+'liver' criteria; 59 manually segmented, 2014-2022; 61 liver-negative).
ANNOTATION WORKFLOW: Reader 1 (junior physician) primary annotator, reader 2 (radiologist, 3 yrs experience) supervisor on NORA web platform; Couinaud landmarks: hepatic veins as vertical dividers (S7,8,4,2 clockwise from superior through IVC), portal vein bifurcation for horizontal division (turnover to S6,5,4,3), S1 anteromedial to IVC; supervisor corrected 12 CTs and 19 MRIs; 4 complex postoperative cases excluded; inter-rater subset = 40 studies (20 CT, 20 MRI) randomly selected from training data, independently and blindly segmented.
STATISTICAL METHODS: bootstrap (1000 iterations) for 95% CIs; Shapiro-Wilk normality test; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p<0.05 significance; volume-difference sign convention: positive = ground truth > prediction.
MODEL-SELECTION RATIONALE: LM-onlyCT vs joint LM difference non-significant (p=0.05) but joint CT+MRI LM retained for higher sensitivity and training-data diversity/generalizability philosophy; separate modality-specific segment models retained because joint training offered no benefit for anatomy.
EVALUATION RULES: detection = >=20% predicted/reference volume overlap AND >=0.06 ml absolute volume; scans with >15 lesions counted as fully detected (sensitivity=1) to prevent metric distortion in disseminated disease; LiTS applied zero-shot (no fine-tuning).
REVIEW-SCOPE RELEVANCE: Single-organ (liver) 3D segmentation subdivided into 8 Couinaud sub-structures on CT (plus MRI); no architectural novelty (off-the-shelf nnU-Net) — value lies in multimodal generalist modeling, Couinaud-level anatomical localization, open-source release into the TotalSegmentator ecosystem, and clinical workflow demonstration (TACE response: median HU 51.33->38.50, p=0.021; median volume 2.41->4.07 ml, p=0.32 NS). Suitable for inclusion as a representative open-source, multi-modality single-organ segmentation study; flag study-level split when pooling Dice estimates.
contribution_summary: This study delivers open-source nnU-Net models, contributed to the TotalSegmentator ecosystem, for Couinaud liver segment segmentation on CT (mean Dice 0.897) and MRI (0.847) and a modality-agnostic liver lesion detection/segmentation model trained jointly on CT+MRI (CT: 75.8% sensitivity, Dice 0.658; MRI: 62.7%, 0.337), externally validated zero-shot on LiTS. Its key novelty is a deliberately heterogeneous, generalist multimodal design with Couinaud-level anatomical localization, demonstrated clinically through automated HCC attenuation/volumetry tracking after TACE (median HU 51.33->38.50, p=0.021). The work prioritizes accessibility and broad real-world applicability over peak task-specific performance, candidly documenting the generalizability-specialization trade-off against specialized pipelines such as RetinaNet+U-Net on LiTS.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 82 public CT scans; 65-66 used for training per fold in 5-fold CV, exceeding the >50 threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public NIH Pancreas dataset (NIH Clinical Center), explicitly cited (Roth et al. [25]), with 82 high-resolution scans described.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 5-fold cross-validation clearly specified: 65-66 train / 16-17 test per fold; same folds reused for all 7 compared variants enabling paired testing. (No separate external held-out set, covered under Q5.)

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth described only as 'accurate manual segmentations' inherited from the dataset citation; annotation protocol (annotators, consensus, inter-rater agreement) not described in this paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single dataset only (NIH); no independent external cohort. BCV data appears only via literature comparison.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Exemplary: full layer-by-layer table (Table 1) with kernel sizes, channels, MFLOPs, skip connections; 4-level 2D U-Net, 2.6M parameters, 36-voxel receptive field, 15-slice input stacks, 1x1 convs at lowest level, batch norm placement.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam lr 0.0025, batch size 10, 40 epochs x 150 iterations, beta continuation schedule (3.0->8.0 linearly), class weights, shadow-weight quantisation trick, PyTorch framework, GPU model stated, plus public code and pre-trained models.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted cross-entropy with rationale given: ~2% foreground voxels cause severe class imbalance, motivating 0.5/2.5 background/organ weights. Individual weight values not ablated, but justification is explicit.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Fully specified: resample to 1.0 mm isotropic, ROI cropping to fixed 194x122x138 bounding boxes, zero-mean unit-variance normalisation; post-processing explicitly stated as none (deliberate, for fair method comparison).

Q10_code_availability.justification: PyTorch implementation and pre-trained models released at https://github.com/mattiaspaul/TernaryNet.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice is the only segmentation accuracy metric (no HD/Jaccard/sensitivity). Supplemented with efficiency metrics central to the contribution (weight memory, per-layer MFLOPs, CPU inference time, weight sparsity), which earns partial credit.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired t-tests against TernaryNet across all 82 cases reported per variant (Table 2), with std deviations; establishes equivalence to full precision (p=0.54) and inferiority of binary variants (p<=0.01).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Seven internal variants (2 binary XNORnet, 3 ternary ablations, 2 full-precision baselines) plus literature comparison: Roth 71%/78%, Zhou 82%, Dense V-Net 66%, multi-atlas 74%. Literature numbers are not re-run head-to-head, but context is thorough.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (pancreas), so average = per-organ; additionally per-case ranked Dice distribution shown across all 82 cases (Fig. 4) plus qualitative case #12 analysis.

Q15_limitations.justification: Multiple limitations acknowledged: does not target SOTA accuracy (71% vs 82%), assumes ROI bounding box is given (localisation out of scope), no post-processing could add accuracy, binary variants' failure modes analysed, 2D convolutions instead of full 3D.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low. All 82 scans of a public dataset entered 5-fold CV with no exclusions or case cherry-picking. Caveat: patient selection criteria/demographics are inherited from the dataset publication and not restated, so dataset-level selection cannot be verified from this paper alone.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Automated Dice evaluation applied identically to all seven variants on identical folds, with post-processing deliberately disabled to avoid differential benefit; equivalence claims backed by paired t-tests. Qualitative review limited to one case, but quantitative evaluation is consistent.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All variants reported including strongly negative results (binary continuation 48.4% Dice), full ablations, sparsity curves, and per-case ranked Dice. Minor caveats: no external validation attempted, and the 5-7 s CPU inference time is an 'estimated' figure from a custom OpenCL implementation rather than a benchmarked release.

detailed_extraction: Original scans: 512x512 axial, 181-466 slices, 0.5-1.0 mm slice thickness before resampling. Memory: >5 GB GPU during training (batch 10), ~1 GB full-precision inference. Ternary encoding: 2 bits/entry via separate sign (Is) and value (Iv) planes, one float scaling factor alpha per channel; inner product computed as masked XOR/XNOR + two popcounts (Eq. 9); theoretical throughput up to 16x fewer ops, 8x vs AVX2 FMA at 0.5 cycles/popcount. Training trick: full-precision shadow weights quantised before forward pass and restored before optimiser step; gradients at full precision. Key empirical findings beyond Dice: (1) tanh-continuation is critical - fixed beta=3 collapses to 56.3% vs 71.0%; (2) binary XNORnet with analytic tanh continuation fails badly (48.4%), showing ternary sparsity (zeros) is essential, not just quantisation; (3) full-precision ReLU baseline reaches 75.7%, but symmetric activations remain viable due to U-Net skip-connection gradient flow; (4) learned ternary weight sparsity increases with depth and training epochs, acting as implicit regularisation, concentrated in layers with most parameters. Inference: ~80 s full-precision CPU vs estimated 5-7 s ternary on dual-core mobile CPU via custom OpenCL Hamming-distance kernel (abstract claims a path to sub-second). Funding: DFG grant 320997906; NVIDIA Titan Xp donation; preprocessing assistance by N. Bouteldja. Code (with pre-trained models) released post-submission.
contribution_summary: First semantic segmentation network to quantise both weights and activations to ternary values {-1,0,+1}, enabled by a novel fully differentiable ternary hyperbolic tangent (ternTanh) trained via tanh-continuation (beta linearly 3->8), replacing floating-point convolutions with masked XOR/XNOR + popcount operations. On NIH pancreas CT (82 scans, 5-fold CV) it is statistically equivalent to its full-precision U-Net (71.0% vs 71.9% Dice, p=0.54) while reducing model memory >15x (0.66 MB) and achieving >10x faster CPU inference, targeting GPU-free clinical and mobile deployment. It also demonstrates that ternary sparsity, not binarisation alone, is the key to avoiding quantisation loss.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: CHD (110 volumes) and WRAMC (116) exceed 50 subjects, but flagship BTCV benchmark has only 30 annotated volumes (20 train) with labeled subsets as small as 2 cases (10% split); only 10 WRAMC cases annotated.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: All three datasets cited with references [9,15,16] and case counts; public datasets named (BTCV, CHD, WRAMC). Minor gap: no scanner, acquisition, or demographic details.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit: BTCV 4 val/6 test/rest train; CHD 11 test/11 val/rest train; WRAMC 3-fold CV on 10 annotated cases; labeled fractions stated (10/20/40% BTCV, 5/10/20% CHD). Split randomization method not described (minor).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: BTCV/CHD public annotations reused without describing annotation provenance or QC; WRAMC 10 cases self-annotated by authors with no annotator expertise, tooling, protocol, or inter-rater agreement reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Three datasets spanning abdomen/cardiac/colon show domain breadth, but all are used in training (SSL unlabeled portions) — no truly independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: dual 5-layer 3D V-Nets, kernels [32,64,128,256,512], CPS co-training with EMA teachers, Kaiming-normal init for heterogeneity.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: SGD (momentum 0.9), poly LR decay (init 0.03), patch (128,128,64), α=0.5, β=0.99, γ=0.2, θ=0.1, early stopping 30 epochs, 3 seeds. Missing: batch size, total epochs, EMA momentum μ value, GPU hardware.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted Dice + 0.5·weighted CE (supervised), weighted CE (unsupervised), Gaussian ramp-up cited; the core category-wise weighting (CDifW/DisW) is extensively motivated (Figs. 1–2, small-structure instability analysis).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Random flip/crop, patch extraction, sliding-window inference (stride 32,32,16), dual-model logit averaging + argmax all described; CT intensity normalization/windowing and resampling not mentioned.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Public repo stated in abstract and conclusion: https://github.com/MoriLabNU/Double-Mix

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice + Average Surface Distance (ASD) both reported.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean±std over 3 random-seed trials; Wilcoxon signed-rank tests vs second-best method, all p<0.05 (Fig. 8).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: 10 baselines (SS-Net, DST, Depl, CPS, CReST, CLD, DHC, CutMix, CutOut, ClassMix) re-implemented on identical splits and data; plus component ablation ('ours w/o DMP').

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-structure Dice tables for all 13 BTCV abdominal organs and all 7 CHD cardiac structures, not just averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly acknowledged: DMP module introduces segmentation noise and degrades performance on balanced/simpler data (WRAMC colon); future work stated; qualitative failure regions highlighted.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Public datasets with reported split sizes, but case-to-split assignment and labeled-subset selection procedures are not described; WRAMC annotated subset is very small (10 cases, self-annotated).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All baselines re-implemented on identical data, splits, seeds, and metrics with repeated trials and significance testing. Caveat: author-run re-implementations without stated hyperparameter-tuning parity could favor the proposed method.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Per-class results include unfavorable values (0.0 Dice classes for baselines) and the method's own weakness on WRAMC; limitations and code reported. Contents of ablation Tables 3–4 fall in a truncated section of the provided text.

detailed_extraction: Training details not in prior extraction: dual models fA/fB differ by random init (Kaiming normal) for heterogeneity; EMA teachers updated as μE_t + (1−μ)E_(t−1) (μ value not reported); CDifW fuses (a) an information score from EMA-smoothed (β=0.99) category confidence, normalized as (1−c_k)/max(1−c), with (b) Dice-based learning-speed difficulty computed via Population Stability Index (τ=50 iterations, smoothing ∂=max(t−τ,0), exponent α=0.5); DisW from log voxel-count ratios, also EMA-smoothed; DMP samples category sets Z from the weight distribution to build binary pseudo-label masks — model A mixes via DisW, model B via CDifW; total loss L = L_sseg + θ·L_su (θ=0.1) with epoch-dependent Gaussian ramp-up; inference averages both models' logits then per-voxel argmax. Absolute labeled-case counts: BTCV 2/4/8 of 20 training cases at 10/20/40%; CHD ≈4/9/18 of 88 at 5/10/20%; WRAMC 3-fold CV on 10 annotated cases (air-area vs solid-material). Ablation: DMP adds +1.2 avg Dice on BTCV-40% (60.0→61.2) and +2.2 on CHD-5% (64.3→66.5); baselines collapse to 0.0 Dice on gallbladder/PSV/adrenals at BTCV-40% under CPS/DST/Depl. Not reported anywhere in the paper: batch size, total epochs, EMA momentum μ, GPU hardware, DL framework, HU windowing/resampling, license, release version. Provided full text is truncated mid-Results (Tables 3–4 headers visible, contents and WRAMC results table unavailable).
contribution_summary: Proposes DMPF, a semi-supervised co-training framework on CPS with two differently-initialized 3D V-Nets and EMA teachers, whose Double-Mix pseudo-label module selects categories for mixing augmentation using a novel confidence-difficulty weight (confidence-based information score fused with Dice learning-speed via PSI) plus a voxel-count distribution weight, targeting class-imbalanced CT segmentation. It improves average Dice on difficult categories by +7.0% (BTCV, 40% labeled) and +5.1% (CHD, 5% labeled) over the best of 10 SSL baselines with Wilcoxon significance (p<0.05), and releases code. Main weakness: the mixing module injects noise and underperforms on balanced/simpler datasets.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 82 CT scans exceed 50 images, but only 37 subjects (animals) are available; with subject-wise 10-fold CV, ~33 animals (~66-74 scans) per training fold — below the >50-subject threshold. Partial credit for adequate scan-level volume in a rare, hard-to-acquire NHP imaging domain.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Excellent source description: 37 rhesus/cynomolgus macaques exposed to EBOV/MARV/LASV; two Philips 16-slice scanners specified (Gemini/Precedence), 140 kVp, 250-300 mAs/slice, 1-mm slices/0.5-mm increments; full breakdown by virus, species, pre/post scans, weight (3.06-14.52 kg) and liver volume (61.78-279.49 mL) in Table 1. Dataset publicly released on Synapse.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Subject-wise 10-fold cross-validation clearly described: images randomized before splitting, and ALL pre/post scans of test animals held out from training, preventing intra-subject leakage. Minor caveat: no separate validation set (for early stopping/hyperparameter tuning) and no held-out external test set are described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation protocol thoroughly described: contours drawn in axial plane by a trained imaging fellow and monitored by a CT body radiologist using MIM Maestro v6.9 (2D brush, Contour Copilot, interpolation); explicit rules for breathing artifact (contour drawn halfway through artifact extents) and gallbladder exclusion. Limitation: single annotator; no inter-rater variability quantified.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation on an independent dataset; all evaluation is internal 10-fold cross-validation on the single in-house NHP cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: FPN adaptation reasonably described: ResNet50 bottom-up encoder limited to 4 levels (justified by 64³ patch size), top-down pathway with lateral connections and 1×1 convolutions before fusion, semantic segmentation overhead following Kirillov et al. (Panoptic FPN), with Figure 2 schematic. However, exact filter configurations are not specified ('adjusted the filter parameters for our application'), and V-Net/U-Net implementations rely solely on citations — partially limiting reproducibility.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Training highly specified: 64×64×64 patches randomly sampled with equal liver/non-liver counts (class by center voxel), mini-batch 90, Adam (lr 5e-5, decay 5e-5), 30 epochs with reshuffling, mask Gaussian smoothing (σ=1×1×1 mm³), focal loss parameters (α=0.3, γ=2), hardware (3× TitanX 12GB), training time (~8 h/fold) and inference time (~1.5 min/scan). Missing only: framework name and any augmentation details.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Focal loss explicitly justified by class-imbalance variation across subjects and hard-to-detect boundaries with adjacent iso-dense organs; α=0.3 and γ=2 empirically selected and reported; rationale of modulating factor for hard samples explained.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Both pipelines fully specified: preprocessing (1 mm³ isotropic resampling with cubic interpolation, HU thresholding [-40, 160], rescaling to [0,1], anisotropic diffusion filtering with citation) and postprocessing (probability map resampling to native resolution, Gaussian smoothing, 0.5 thresholding).

Q10_code_availability.justification: Code and trained models not made publicly available (the public Synapse release covers only the dataset and masks, credited under Q2).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Four complementary metrics with formal definitions: Dice, sensitivity, relative absolute volume difference (RAVD), and average surface distance (ASD).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests between models with p<0.05 significance reported (FPN significantly better Dice); full descriptive statistics (mean, std, median, max, min) for all metrics, pre/post stratified. No confidence intervals, but significance testing and outlier visualization (Figure 5) are present.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Two CNN baselines (V-Net, 3D U-Net) retrained on identical data/folds, plus external comparison to an atlas-based NHP method (Solomon et al.: mean Dice 89.0%, median 91.0%) and contextual benchmarking against LiTS challenge results.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver), so per-organ breakdown is trivially satisfied; additionally, results are usefully stratified by pre-/post-exposure scans with complete statistical distributions rather than only averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations candidly discussed: post-exposure outliers from severely infected animals under-represented in training (min Dice 62.34%), difficulty segmenting iso-dense boundaries (gallbladder, muscles, kidney, stomach), breathing motion blur, small dataset; concrete future work proposed (spatial deformation augmentation, cascaded CNNs, human translation).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Dataset composition is transparently reported (species, virus, pre/post, weight/volume ranges) and folds are randomized at subject level, but all animals come from a single BSL-4 preclinical program (NIH/NIAID) — a narrow, virus-exposed population with no healthy controls and no explicit scan inclusion/exclusion criteria, limiting generalizability.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All three networks were trained and evaluated with identical preprocessing, patch sampling, and metric pipelines against the same reference standard. Residual concern: reference masks from a single trained fellow (radiologist-supervised) without inter-rater reliability assessment.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All four metrics reported with full descriptive statistics, pre/post stratification, and boxplots showing outliers; unfavorable results (post-exposure Dice minimum of 62.34%) are openly discussed; limitations and future work clearly stated. Minor note: abstract cites 3.6% RAVD (the pre-exposure value) while the overall FPN RAVD is 4.01%.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond prior extraction: (1) Annotation workflow — MIM Maestro v6.9 (Cleveland, OH) with 2D brush, Contour Copilot, and interpolation tools; contours drawn axially; for breathing motion, contour placed halfway through artifact extents; gallbladder excluded when clearly visible. (2) Full dataset composition (Table 1): EBOV — 25 rhesus, 25 pre/21 post scans, 3.06–14.52 kg, liver 61.78–253.14 mL; LASV — 6 cynomolgus, 9 pre/9 post scans, 3–10 kg, liver 99.14–122.88 mL; MARV — 6 rhesus, 12 pre/6 post scans, 4.8–10 kg, liver 128.65–279.49 mL; FOV head-to-pelvis or head-to-knee. (3) Patch strategy — equal numbers of liver/non-liver 64³ patches, patch class assigned by center voxel, reshuffled each epoch; soft targets generated by blurring masks with 3D Gaussian (σ=1×1×1 mm³). (4) Compute — 16-core Intel Xeon E5 3.2 GHz CPU + 3× NVIDIA GeForce TitanX 12 GB; ~8 h training per 10-fold CV fold per network; ~1.5 min inference per 1 mm³ whole-body CT. (5) Results detail — FPN overall Dice 94.08±3.93% (median 94.63), pre 94.77±1.43%, post 93.19±5.71% (min 62.34%); V-Net overall 92.23±2.74%, UNet 92.03±3.20%; FPN sensitivity 93.57±6.12%, RAVD 4.01%, ASD 0.67 mm; Wilcoxon signed-rank p<0.05 for FPN vs both baselines on Dice. (6) Mechanistic explanation offered: FPN's 1×1 convolutions before lateral fusion (vs UNet's copy-append) and ResNet50 encoder semantics yield better generalizability across liver size/density variability; multiple predictions per upsampling level. (7) Implementation stack — not named explicitly, but the cited Mask R-CNN Keras/TensorFlow implementation (Abdulla 2017) as the FPN overhead basis implies Keras/TF; metrics computed with MedPy; statistics in Python SciPy/NumPy. (8) Ethics/funding — BSL-4 facility imaging under AAALAC accreditation; funded by NIH CIDI, IRF-NIAID, NCI contract HHSN261200800001E, and LGS/Battelle contracts. (9) Minor abstract/body inconsistency: abstract reports 3.6% RAVD (pre-exposure figure) vs 4.01% overall in Table 2. (10) Quality note: total score 24/30 sits exactly at the High/Medium threshold (High per rubric ≥24), driven down by absent external validation, no code release, sub-50 subject count, and incomplete architectural specifications.
contribution_summary: This is the first CNN-based automated liver segmentation study in nonhuman primates with viral hemorrhagic fever infections (EBOV, MARV, LASV), addressing a domain with extreme liver size/morphology variability and infection-induced density heterogeneity. It demonstrates that an FPN with a ResNet50 encoder (focal loss, 10-fold subject-wise CV) significantly outperforms V-Net, 3D U-Net (overall Dice 94.08% vs ~92.2%) and an atlas-based baseline (89.0%), while releasing a publicly available dataset of 82 annotated whole-body NHP CTs on Synapse. The work establishes a reproducible baseline for automated organ volumetry to support pathogenesis tracking and medical countermeasure evaluation in preclinical infectious disease research.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 82 subjects from NIH Pancreas-82; ~61-62 per training fold under 4-fold CV, exceeding the >50 threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public NIH Pancreas-82 (Roth 2015) with acquisition details: 82 contrast-enhanced abdominal CTs, 181-466 slices, 0.5-1.0 mm slice thickness.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 4-fold cross-validation stated, but fold construction, validation-set use for hyperparameter tuning, and whether the standard NIH-82 split convention was followed are not detailed.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Uses the public dataset's manually segmented expert labels (Fig. 1 shows green ground truth); authors describe no annotation protocol (rater count, adjudication, inter-rater agreement).

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single-dataset study; evaluation confined to NIH-82. JHMI appears only as the benchmark of other published methods.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Layer-level description of both phases: Mask R-CNN (ResNet-101 head with C1-C5 dims, FPN P2-P6, RPN anchor scheme, ROI Align to 7x7x256, mask head) and custom 3D U-Net (3x3x3 kernels, BN+ReLU, first-section 2x2x2 vs. later 1x2x2 pooling, initial 1x4x4 input conv).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Keras/TensorFlow, public Mask R-CNN base repo, 100,000 iterations, 4-fold CV, hardware and training times stated; but optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and augmentation strategy are not reported in the available text.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Binary cross-entropy with 0.5 threshold stated but not justified; no discussion against region-overlap losses (Dice/Tversky) that are standard for small, class-imbalanced organs like pancreas.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Explicit pipeline: grayscale reconfiguration of Mask R-CNN input, crop to 256x256x2N/3, resize to 64x64x2N/3 for GPU memory, sigmoid threshold at 0.5, resize back, decrop/montage into zero-filled 512x512xN.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no repository URL or license.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Seven metrics: DSC, Jaccard, Precision, Recall, Pixel Accuracy, Specificity, plus ROC/AUC.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Point estimates only; no SD, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the proposed method (SDs shown in Table 1 belong to the compared studies).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compares against 16 deep-learning methods on the same NIH-82 benchmark (Roth 2015 through Zheng 2020), a thorough and current SOTA table for 2021.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study, so organ-level reporting is inherently complete (pancreas DSC 86.15%). Caveat: no per-case distribution or variance reported, so consistency across patients cannot be judged.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations: 6 GB GPU forced 64x64 downsampling in phase 2, 3D U-Net-only baseline (78.86%) trails full-resolution literature, evaluation limited to one dataset; concrete future work listed.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Uses the standard public NIH-82 cohort with no author-controlled enrollment, minimizing cherry-picking; however patient inclusion/exclusion criteria and demographics are inherited from the dataset and not restated.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. A uniform 4-fold CV protocol with consistent metrics is applied to the proposed method, but cross-study comparisons rely on previously published numbers obtained under differing preprocessing and split conventions, not on reimplementation under a single protocol. Single manual reference standard, no inter-rater verification.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate. All headline metrics and an ablation of both phases are reported; however results are means without dispersion, no failed-case analysis beyond qualitative figures, and no external dataset outcomes.

detailed_extraction: Ablation: Mask R-CNN localization alone achieves 81.00% DSC, 3D U-Net alone 78.86%, combined pipeline 86.15%, supporting the two-phase design claim. Efficiency: ~20 s inference per CT and ~8 days total training per fold (7 d Mask R-CNN + 1 d 3D U-Net) on a consumer RTX 2060 6 GB, the paper's central efficiency argument versus competitors needing high-end GPUs. Phase-1 output sub-volumes span 2N/3 slices at 256x256; phase-2 operates at 64x64x2N/3 due to memory limits. Data inconsistency: abstract lists four metric names for five values (DSC, JI, REC, ACC = 86.15, 75.93, 86.27, 86.27, 99.95); extracted PRE is 86.23 and REC 86.27, suggesting an abstract typo. Missing for full reproducibility: optimizer, learning rate schedule, batch size, augmentation, anchor scales/ratios, and per-fold variance. The claimed SOTA margin over Zhao 2019 (86.15 vs 85.99) is 0.16 DSC points, within typical reported SD (~4.5), and without significance testing the 'best on NIH-82' claim is weakly supported.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a two-phase pancreas segmentation pipeline combining 2D Mask R-CNN (rough localization and cropping) with a custom 3D U-Net (refinement), achieving 86.15% mean DSC on NIH-82 — nominally the best among 16 compared methods — while running on a modest 6 GB consumer GPU. Its main practical contribution is demonstrating that crop-then-segment reduces memory demands enough to make 3D refinement feasible on low-end hardware (~20 s/scan). Ablation confirms both phases contribute, though the margin over prior SOTA (0.16 DSC) is not statistically supported.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Partial. LiTS (~65 train) and MSD8 (~96 train) exceed 50 training subjects, but the primary annotated 3Dircadb cohort has only ~10 training subjects (20 volumes, 10:3:7 split).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Three public datasets (3Dircadb, LiTS, MSD8) with slice thickness, volume dimensions, and label types specified; institutional overlap between 3Dircadb/LiTS vs MSD8 explicitly disclosed.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 10:3:7 train/val/test ratio reported per dataset, but randomization procedure, seeding, and whether splits are patient-level are not described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Authors annotated 20 3Dircadb + 131 LiTS subjects (publicly released); MSD8 Couinaud labels reused from Tian et al. However, annotation protocol (raters, expertise level, software, inter-rater agreement) is not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: OOD cross-dataset experiments including 3Dircadb→MSD8, where MSD8 is from a different institution (though 3Dircadb→LiTS is compromised by same-institution overlap).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully described with figure: dual-branch point-voxel design (PVCNN-inspired), 4-scale re-voxelization from 64³, local attention module per scale, MLP decoder, upstream 3D UXNet liver masker, semi-supervised MixMatch vessel-attention generator.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: 600 epochs, SGD lr 0.01, augmentation ranges, 50k points/epoch, voxel resolutions, binarization threshold, dilation kernel reported; Section 5 dedicated to hyperparameters; public code fills remaining gaps (training/inference times and batch size absent).

Q8_loss_function.justification: CE + Dice + novel feature-level distance loss, each component motivated (intra-segment feature compactness, CE concentrated on top-10% uncertain inter-segment points) to address the two stated challenges (no intensity contrast, vessel-defined boundary uncertainty).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing exhaustively described: HU windowing [-100,300], z-score normalization, liver masking, vessel attention map construction (erode/dilate combine, 0.5 binarization, morphological dilation), image-to-world transform, per-baseline resizing; post-processing explicitly none.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Public GitHub repo (code) plus release of two manually Couinaud-annotated datasets.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice + Accuracy + Average Surface Distance (ASD), reported for both in-distribution and OOD settings.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests reported for any comparison.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Five baselines spanning voxel (3D UNet, 3D UXNet, Swin UNetR) and point-based (PointNet2Plus, Jia et al.) families under common protocol.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Only dataset-level average Dice/Acc/ASD evidenced in extracted results; no per-segment (Couinaud I–VIII) Dice breakdown captured.

Q15_limitations.justification: No dedicated limitations section, but failure modes are candidly discussed inline: OOD Dice drop to 81.3 (slice-thickness mismatch 4.6mm vs 1.78mm), coarse vessel attention maps interfering as baseline inputs, small 3Dircadb training set.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Public cohorts without stated inclusion/exclusion criteria; rationale for LiTS subset (131/200) and MSD8 subset (193/443) unreported; 3Dircadb–LiTS same-institution overlap weakens the independence of cross-dataset claims between them.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. All methods evaluated on identical splits and metrics with common preprocessing (baselines resized to 256×256×64); no statistical significance testing; outcome assessment is automated/metric-based (blinding not applicable).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Primary metrics and OOD results fully reported; however, no per-segment breakdown, no runtimes, no hyperparameter ablation values in extracted text, and no dedicated limitations section. Negative findings (OOD degradation) are disclosed.

detailed_extraction: Journal extension of a prior conference paper with five stated additions: expanded related work; semi-supervised MixMatch vessel-attention generation (enables training on LiTS/MSD8 lacking vessel labels by fusing eroded+dilated regions, binarizing at 0.5, and dilating with kernel (1,1,1) within the liver mask); local attention module (LAM) for adaptive per-scale branch fusion; feature-level distance loss with R_intra center-loss and R_inter CE terms on top-10% uncertain points (weights lambda, alpha); expanded experiments incl. OOD. Pipeline: 3D UXNet liver mask (Dice 94.05–96.84% across datasets) → image-to-world coordinate transform → 50,000 points/epoch sampled within liver, each as (x,y,z,intensity)+vessel-attention channel → 4-scale re-voxelization/de-voxelization starting at 64³ → point branch (MLP, spatial topology) + voxel branch (3D conv, semantics) → LAM fusion → multi-scale concat → point-wise MLP decoder over 8 classes ({0..7} ↔ segments I–VIII) → voxelized back to full 3D Couinaud mask. Training: 600 epochs, SGD lr 0.01, augmentation (scale 0.9–1.1, axis flip, ≤5° rotation), PyTorch, single RTX A6000. Claimed margins: +3–25% Dice over best voxel methods, +5–15% over best point methods. Key caveats for synthesis: (a) 3Dircadb/LiTS institution overlap inflates apparent cross-dataset robustness between those two; MSD8 is the only truly external transfer target; (b) OOD drop (91.05→81.30) attributed to slice-thickness mismatch (1.78mm vs 4.6mm), relevant for thick-slice clinical CT applicability; (c) not reported: training/inference time, batch size, statistical tests, per-segment Dice; (d) only ~10 training subjects on 3Dircadb. Releases: code (github.com/xukun-zhang/Couinaud-Segmentation) + manual Couinaud annotations for 20 3Dircadb and 131 LiTS volumes (license: paper CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; code license unstated).
contribution_summary: Proposes a multi-scale point-voxel fusion network for automatic Couinaud liver segmentation that embeds vessel-structure attention priors into densely sampled 3D point clouds, fuses point-spatial and voxel-semantic branches via a local attention module, and adds a feature-level distance loss to compact intra-segment features and sharpen uncertain inter-segment boundaries — achieving SOTA Dice (~89–91% in-distribution) on 3Dircadb, LiTS, and MSD8 with demonstrated OOD robustness on thick-slice CT. Secondarily contributes the first publicly released manual Couinaud annotations for 20 3Dircadb and 131 LiTS subjects alongside open code. It is an extended journal version of a prior conference paper.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Far exceeds threshold: 331 scans for train/validation (281/50), 150 external test scans, plus 82 TCIA and 240-scan 18-structure sets.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources explicit: Nagoya University portal-venous-phase gastric-surgery CTs for training; independent hospital/scanners for testing; TCIA and Visceral public sets. Voxel spacings and slice counts reported per cohort.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 281/50 train/validation split stated; test set is a completely unseen collection from a different hospital, scanners, and study population — the strongest possible split design.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Test-set annotation described (semi-automatic delineation by 3 trained researchers, clinician-confirmed), but the annotation protocol for the 331 training scans is only stated as 'manually labeled' — no annotator, tool, or QC details in the text.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Excellent: 150-scan external test set from a different hospital, plus TCIA Pancreas-CT, Visceral fine-tuning, and a 240-scan 18-structure comparison set.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: Çiçek 3D U-Net, 4 resolution levels, 3×3×3 valid convs, ReLU, BatchNorm, 2×2×2 pooling/up-convs, skip connections with cropping, 1×1×1 output conv, >19M parameters, exact input/output tile sizes (Fig. 2).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: SGD, BatchNorm, iteration counts (200k/115k), full augmentation parameters, fixed sub-volume sizes, Caffe framework, GPU model all given; minor gaps (learning rate schedule, batch size) offset by released code and trained models.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted voxel-wise cross-entropy with per-class weights λk = (1 − Nk/NC)/(K−1), Σλk = 1 (Eq. 3-4); explicitly motivated by foreground/background imbalance and small-structure under-weighting.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (×2 downsampling, body mask via thresholding + morphology, dilation r=3 for C2) and testing (tiling, overlapping-tile probability averaging) fully described; postprocessing explicitly stated as none.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Code and trained models publicly released: github.com/holgerroth/3Dunet_abdomen_cascade.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice (mean/std/median/min/max) plus sensitivity and false-positive rate (Fig. 6 candidate-region analysis); sensitivity/FPR serve cascade tuning rather than final segmentation scoring, but multiple metrics are reported.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests vs 2D FCN baseline (p<0.05 for most organs) per prior extraction; full distributional statistics (std, median, min, max) per organ per stage.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Seven baselines spanning multi-atlas (Wolz 2013), dictionary learning (Tong 2015), graph cuts (Oda 2016), and 2D FCN variants (Roth 2017, Zhou 2016a/b); claims highest reported pancreas score on the external dataset.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Complete per-organ tables with distribution statistics across all stages, all four datasets, and stage-over-stage deltas (e.g., artery 59.0→79.6, pancreas 54.8→63.1 on validation).

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit discussion: pancreas outliers from contrast/shape variability, large organs sometimes better served by 2D FCNs, 12 GB GPU memory forcing half-resolution and fixed input size, loss-weighting-only imbalance handling.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Inclusion criteria are explicit (contrast-enhanced portal-venous-phase abdominal CT; gastric surgery training cohort, gastric cancer test cohort), and the random split plus external-hospital test minimizes selection effects. Caveat: all cohorts are Japanese gastric-surgery/cancer populations, so anatomic/pathologic spectrum is narrow and generalizability to other populations is untested.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. One fixed model and identical tiling protocol applied to all test data; no test-time augmentation; test annotations independently created (3 researchers) and clinician-confirmed; Dice computed consistently across stages and datasets.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Per-organ results include weak outcomes (pancreas 33.0 on fine-tuned torso test, gallbladder ~70-76), min/max/std reported, unfavorable findings acknowledged (2D FCNs competitive on large organs), and code/models released for verification.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not in prior extraction — (1) Annotation: test-set liver/spleen/pancreas were SEMI-automatically delineated by 3 trained researchers with clinician confirmation; training-set annotation protocol not detailed in provided text. (2) Baseline context: external-test pancreas improved from 68.5 (prior best reported) to 82.2. (3) Candidate-region economics: stage 1 sees ~40% of voxels (body mask C1), stage 2 ~10% (C2); dilation radius r=3 chosen from sensitivity/FPR trade-off curves (>99% sensitivity, ~10% FPR on train and validation, Fig. 6). (4) Overlapping tiles use 4× per-voxel sampling with probability averaging (Eq. 5); stage 1 tested non-overlapping only. (5) Class weights: λk = (1 − Nk/NC)/(K−1) normalized to sum 1. (6) Architecture specifics: valid (unpadded) convolutions shrink output relative to input (132×132×116 → 44×44×28), skip connections require cropping; base implementation from LMB Freiburg open-source 3D U-Net in Caffe. (7) Resampling: ×2 downsampling; predictions resampled to full resolution via nearest-neighbor (labels) or linear (probability maps); no deformation at test time. (8) Stage-2 gains on validation: mean +7.5 Dice points/organ; artery +20.6, vein +8.4, pancreas +8.3, liver only +3.6 (large organs benefit least). (9) Scan specifications: training 460–1177 slices, voxel [0.59–0.98, 0.59–0.98, 0.5–1.0] mm; test 263–1061 slices, [0.55–0.82, 0.55–0.82, 0.4–0.80] mm. (10) MINOR INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: §2.3 states elastic deformations sampled from a UNIFORM distribution (max displacement ±4); §3.1 states a NORMAL distribution (std 4) — same grid spacing 32 voxels, but the sampling distribution is contradictory. (11) Gaps not stated in text: learning rate schedule, batch size, momentum/weight decay, training-set annotation workflow, inter-observer variability. (12) Note: provided manuscript text is an accepted-manuscript version truncated mid-§3.2 (ends at Figure 8 reference); Q12 and Q15 assessments partly rely on the previously extracted data fields (Wilcoxon tests, limitations discussion).
contribution_summary: This paper introduces a two-stage coarse-to-fine cascade of multi-class 3D U-Nets for multi-organ and vessel CT segmentation: a first network operating on an automatically generated body-mask candidate region (~40% of voxels) produces dilated foreground predictions (~10% of voxels) that narrow the search space for a second, boundary-focused network. The single shared model — avoiding per-organ models and handcrafted features — achieves state-of-the-art results at the time, including raising external-test pancreas Dice from 68.5 to 82.2% on 150 unseen scans and significantly outperforming 2D FCN baselines on small organs and vessels across 18 structures in 240 scans. Code and trained models are publicly released, making it one of the more reproducible early 3D FCN multi-organ baselines.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: BraTS2021: 1,251 MRI scans (adequate). BTCV: only 30 CT scans — below the >50 threshold for the organ CT task central to this review (~24 train subjects per fold in 5-fold CV).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both public benchmarks cited and described: BraTS2021 (multi-institutional, 4 modalities, 240×240×155, 1mm³ isotropic, label groups WT/TC/ET) and BTCV (30 subjects, 13 organs, resolution and voxel spacing ranges given).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 5-fold cross-validation stated for both datasets, but fold composition, seeds, and patient-level splitting not detailed. No held-out test set; best-DSC checkpoint on validation used for reporting — risk of optimistic estimates.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Relies on pre-annotated public benchmark masks. Label definitions described, but no annotation protocol, annotator expertise, or inter-rater agreement reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort. All results from internal cross-validation on the same two benchmarks.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully described: DACB (depth-wise 3×3×3 dilated convs, rates 1/2/3, 1×1×1 fusion, residual + instance norm), Swin bottleneck (2×2×2 patch partition, 7×7×7 windows, M/2 shift, depths 2/6/2, dim 768, Eq. 1), CSAB (dual max/avg-pool channel+spatial branches, sigmoid, multiplicative refinement), DMSU, deep supervision. Architecture ablations (Table 3) and depth/dilation ablations (Table 4) included.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: PyTorch 2.0.1, MONAI 1.2.0, AdamW, lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-5, cosine annealing, 1000 epochs, batch 2, 96³ patches, sliding-window 0.8 overlap, GPU specified, plus public code. Minor gap: augmentation list not enumerated, training time not reported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Equal-weight Dice+CE (Eq. 2) with deep-supervision weighting 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 (Eq. 3). Choice empirically justified via ablation: Dice-only loses 1.32%; Dice-CE ≈ Focal-Dice.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Training preprocessing described (random 96³ patch sampling, 1×1×1 pointwise conv to 24 channels, instance norm in DACB) and inference (sliding window 0.8). Augmentation referenced as 'identical across models' but never specified; no postprocessing reported.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Code publicly available: https://github.com/yaziciz/GLIMS (stated in abstract and contributions).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice (Eq. 4) + HD95 (Eq. 5), plus efficiency metrics (params, FLOPs, inference time).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests. 5-fold means reported without standard deviations.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Six strong baselines retrained under identical settings: UNETR, nnU-Net, TransBTS, nnFormer, Swin UNETR, SegResNet, with complexity comparison (Table 5).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ Dice for all 13 BTCV structures (Table 1); per-region ET/TC/WT for BraTS (Table 2). HD95 per-class only in BraTS ablations; BTCV HD95 not reported.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section. One failure case discussed (stomach missed due to air). Slower inference (36.63 s, slowest of all compared) reported in Table 5 but not acknowledged; no BTCV HD95.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate: patient selection defined by public benchmark inclusion (BraTS multi-institutional; BTCV 30 pre-surgical abdomen CT subjects). Small BTCV cohort and no external validation limit generalizability to broader CT populations.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate: fair comparison setup (identical preprocessing/augmentation/hyperparameters across models) reduces bias, but reporting best-validation-DSC checkpoints without a held-out test set risks optimistic performance estimates.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate: most outcomes reported thoroughly (per-organ Dice, complexity), but no limitations section, no fold variance, HD95 omitted for BTCV, and the unfavorable inference-time result is reported but not discussed. Minor inconsistency: Swin UNETR params 61.98M (abstract) vs 62.83M (Table 5).

detailed_extraction: Additional methodological details: (1) Transformer design — tokens from 2×2×2 partitioning with learnable positional embeddings of shape (H/2, W/2, D/2, C); windowed (W-MSA) and shifted-window (SW-MSA, shift M/2) attention; transformer spans last two encoder layers and first two decoder layers plus bottleneck; patch-merging (2×2 concat, C→2C) in encoder, patch-expanding in decoder. (2) CSAB — parallel spatial branch (max+avg pooling → weight-shared MLP → sum → sigmoid) and channel branch (pooled concat → 1×1×1 conv → sigmoid); attention maps multiplied with input feature map; Grad-CAM (Fig. 12) shows CSAB concentrates attention on tumor ROI. (3) Ablations (single fold, BraTS2021): baseline conv enc/dec 89.72 DSC / 8.92 HD95 → +deep supervision 90.64/7.59 → +DMSF/DMSU 91.04/5.54 → +CSAB 91.41/5.44 → +transformer bottleneck (full GLIMS) 92.14/4.34. Depth ablation: T1/T2/Tb = 2/6/2 optimal; larger Tb inflates params with diminishing returns; T2 depth matters most. Dilation ablation: combined rates 1/2/3 > 1/2 > 1. (4) Hyperparameter sensitivity (100-epoch runs): lr 1e-3 best; weight decay insensitive; AdamW ≈ Adam > SGD (0.72% gap); Dice-CE ≈ Focal-Dice > Dice-only (1.32% gap). (5) Data efficiency: at 25% training data GLIMS drops 1.16% mean Dice vs Swin UNETR's 1.32%, with fewer edema over-segmentation errors. (6) External benchmark standing: top-5 in BraTS2023 Adult Glioblastoma validation challenge. (7) Efficiency trade-off: fewest FLOPs among compared hybrids (72.30G vs 384.2G Swin UNETR) but slowest wall-clock inference (36.63 s). (8) BTCV voxel spacing anisotropic 0.54×0.98×[2.5–5.0] mm³; scan sizes 512×512×85–198. (9) Not reported anywhere: augmentation specification, per-fold std, training wall-clock time, BTCV HD95, license of released code.
contribution_summary: GLIMS is a lightweight hybrid CNN–Swin Transformer U-shaped network for 3D volumetric segmentation that combines depth-wise dilated multi-scale convolution blocks (DACB), a Swin Transformer bottleneck, and attention-guided skip connections (CSAB) with deep supervision. It achieves state-of-the-art mean Dice of 92.14% (BraTS2021) and 84.50% (BTCV multi-organ CT), surpassing nnU-Net and Swin UNETR with fewer parameters (47.16M) and FLOPs (72.30G) than Swin UNETR, at the cost of the slowest inference time among compared models. Within this review's scope, it is a multi-organ CT segmentation method validated only on the 30-scan BTCV benchmark under cross-validation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 210 CT scans from KiTS19 with 134/34/42 train/val/test split; training set well above the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public KiTS19 challenge dataset fully characterized (Table 1): preoperative abdominal CT, late-arterial phase, NIfTI format, voxel-size ranges, affine; interpolated variant used to unify voxel spacing.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split clearly specified: random 20% independent test (42 scans), remaining 80/20 into train (134) and validation (34); additional evaluation on the official KiTS19 challenge test set (90 patients). Minor gap: no seed/stratification reported.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process not described by the authors; paper only asserts 'unambiguous definition of kidney tumor voxels' and defers to KiTS19 references. No annotator count, protocol, or inter-observer agreement reported in this paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Evaluated on the held-out KiTS19 challenge test set (90 patients), but this derives from the same source cohort as training data. Authors explicitly acknowledge train/test are identically distributed and that multi-vendor/multi-center generalization is untested.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully described: 6-layer 3D U-Net (incl. bottleneck) built on nnU-Net, strided-conv downsampling, transposed-conv upsampling, instance normalization (chosen due to GPU memory limits), 30 base kernels, deepest feature map ≥8×8×8, skip connections, deep supervision on decoder layers (Fig. 3).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, initial LR 3e-4, ×0.2 decay after 30 epochs without loss improvement, early stop at 50 epochs without improvement, patch 192×192×48, batch 8, 250 iterations/epoch, 2× Tesla 32GB, PyTorch, batchgenerators augmentation, plus public code.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Thoroughly justified: CE alone suffers background dominance; exponential logarithmic loss on Soft Dice (exponent 0.3, weights 0.4 kidney / 0.6 tumor; CE weights 0.28/0.28/0.44) chosen to address sample imbalance and heterogeneous tumor difficulty, with rationale per training phase (Fig. 4) and citation of Wong et al.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing explicit (0.5th–99.5th percentile clipping, foreground mean/std normalization, resampling via KiTS19 interpolated dataset); augmentation enumerated and visualized (rotations, scaling, elastic deformation, gamma, mirroring); postprocessing described with example (TTA mirroring, half-patch overlap aggregation with center weighting, connected-components-3d to keep ≤2 kidney components and attached tumors).

Q10_code_availability.justification: Code publicly released at https://github.com/LINGYUNFDU/MSSU-Net, including the loss modification details.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Six metrics per structure: Dice, Jaccard, Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Hausdorff distance (mm), reported for both internal and challenge test sets.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Only descriptive statistics (box plots of per-patient metric distributions, Fig. 8); no confidence intervals, no significance tests, no variance over seeds reported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Three-tier comparison: controlled ablation vs identical classic 3D U-Net; comparison with Yang et al. ROI-based methods (PSPNet, 3D U-Net, FCN-PPM) with explicit caveat that datasets/task complexity differ; and head-to-head KiTS19 challenge leaderboard results vs top-5 teams.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Kidney and tumor reported separately in every table (Tables 2–5) and both evaluation sets, not averaged.

Q15_limitations.justification: Failure case explicitly analyzed (Fig. 9: missed small tumor, Dice = 0, attributed to fixed receptive field of classic convolutions); sensitivity of results to undetected small tumors noted; single-dataset identical-distribution generalization limitation acknowledged; deformable convolutions and multi-center data proposed as remedies.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate: all cases come from the single public KiTS19 cohort with random splitting; authors define no inclusion/exclusion criteria and report no demographics; single-source data limits generalizability (acknowledged by authors).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: identical unified preprocessing applied to training and testing data; the same six metrics computed consistently per structure; challenge evaluation performed against official held-out labels not available to participants.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low: reports all six metrics, per-structure results, ablation results, honest challenge rank (7th of 106), and a complete failure case; minor omissions only (inference time, random seeds, annotation details).

detailed_extraction: Training regime: Adam with initial LR 3e-4, LR multiplied by 0.2 when training loss plateaus for 30 epochs, training terminated after 50 epochs without improvement; patch-based training with patch size 192x192x48, batch size 8, 250 iterations per epoch (= 250x8 randomly sampled patches). Loss composition: per-layer loss = exponential-logarithmic Soft Dice (exponent 0.3; kidney/tumor weights 0.4/0.6) + weighted CE (background/kidney/tumor 0.28/0.28/0.44); layer losses weighted 0.4/0.2/0.2/0.1/0.1 across the 5 decoder layers (bottleneck excluded, Eq. 1). Inference: half-patch overlap with center-weighted aggregation, TTA by mirroring along valid axes (paper also mentions adding Gaussian noise), up to 64 aggregated predictions per voxel in patient interior; postprocessing keeps the two largest kidney 3D connected components and tumors attached to kidneys, using connected-components-3d (accommodates post-nephrectomy single-kidney patients). Ablation deltas vs identical classic 3D U-Net: kidney Dice 0.962→0.969, Hausdorff 38.945→19.188 mm; tumor Dice 0.781→0.805, Hausdorff 50.808→33.469 mm — largest gains on tumor boundary accuracy. Challenge test ground-truth labels were not public (server-side evaluation only). Table 4 comparison with Yang et al. is cross-dataset (ROI-cropped vs raw images), explicitly flagged by authors as not directly comparable. Dataset statistics (Table 1): voxel dims ranging [434,434,69] to [639,639,182], median [523,523,116], anisotropic affine handled via the challenge's interpolated dataset. License: paper CC BY-NC-ND; code license not stated. No random seeds or repeated runs reported; ~5 days training on 2x Tesla 32GB; inference time not reported. Ethics: public data only, no additional approval required.
contribution_summary: The paper presents MSS U-Net, a 6-layer 3D U-Net built on the nnU-Net framework that combines multi-scale deep supervision across decoder layers with exponential logarithmic Soft Dice loss plus weighted cross-entropy, and a connected-component postprocessing rule, to segment kidneys and tumors end-to-end from raw full-scale CT without ROI cropping. It achieves Dice 0.969 (kidney) / 0.805 (tumor) on an internal KiTS19 split and 0.974 / 0.818 on the official KiTS19 challenge test set (7th of 106 teams), demonstrating that training-strategy enhancements to the plain 3D U-Net rival more complex architectures while retaining simplicity and reproducibility. Code is publicly released.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 53 total scans across two benchmarks, but per-experiment training sets are small: 9 scans (VISCERAL leave-one-out) and 32-33 scans (TCIA four-fold). No single experiment trains on >50 subjects; authors themselves identify dataset size as the main accuracy limiter.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Two established public benchmarks (VISCERAL; TCIA abdominal CT following Gibson et al. 2018) clearly named with references; preprocessing specifics (3mm³ isotropic resampling, 156x115x160 crop; manual bbox + 144³) fully specified. Patient demographics/scanner details not reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit: leave-one-out CV on VISCERAL (10 folds x 7 labels); four-fold CV on TCIA43 with exact fold sizes (32/33 train, 10/11 test). Standard, reproducible protocols.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Reference annotations inherited from the public benchmarks via prior work (Gibson et al. 2018; VISCERAL); no description of annotator expertise, annotation protocol, or inter-rater agreement in the paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Both datasets are evaluated with internal cross-validation only (train and test within the same dataset). No independent external cohort tested.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Thorough: OBELISK sparse deformable kernel (learned offsets + coefficients via differentiable interpolation/gridsample), 1x1 Dense-Net classifier, hybrid OBELISK+CNN variant with high/mid-res encoder-decoder, architecture figures, parameter count (~230k).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Detailed training recipe: Adam, LR 0.002, 300 epochs, batch sizes (1 hybrid / 3 U-Net; 192 samples x 64 iterations for original OBELISK), OHEM 75% quantile, affine augmentation, leaky ReLU, GPU hardware and training time (~90 min/model). Minor gap: framework only implied (PyTorch via gridsample), no code release.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Class-frequency-weighted cross-entropy with OHEM; choice empirically justified by ablating Dice loss and hinge Dice loss (negligible difference after 300 epochs), and OHEM's marginal contribution is honestly reported.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Fully specified per dataset; post-processing explicitly stated as none, with the no-postprocessing evaluation framed as a deliberate, uniform condition.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No public code or model release; no URL or license reported.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice is the only segmentation accuracy metric reported (per organ and average). Secondary metrics are computational only (parameters, memory 700MB vs 2500+MB, 87ms inference) — no boundary/overlap metric such as Hausdorff distance or ASSD.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests; only fold-averaged Dice. With 10- and 43-scan cohorts, variance across folds is not characterized.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive: parameter-matched lean U-Net, all-conv and global-FCN U-Nets, dense V-Net (Gibson 2018), MALF, keypoint transfer (Wachinger 2015), Roth 2018, BRIEFnet, and deformable conv nets (Dai 2017), including ablation of deformable offsets vs fixed kernels.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure Dice reported for all organs on both datasets (e.g., TCIA liver 95.39%, spleen 94.35%, pancreas 70.2%), not just averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit and substantive: small-data Dice gap (>9% avg TCIA vs VISCERAL for large organs), rough whole-abdomen crop harder than two-stage pipelines, anisotropic spacing unhandled by OBELISK layer, and confounded comparison vs Gibson et al. (their larger training set + post-processing).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate: fixed public benchmarks with cited, standardized protocols avoid cherry-picking, but cohorts are small (10 and 43 scans) and no patient inclusion/exclusion criteria or demographics are reported, limiting generalizability to broader populations.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: identical splits, preprocessing, and training budgets (300 epochs) applied uniformly to all compared architectures; evaluation performed without post-processing for all methods; Dice computed consistently across folds.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low: per-organ results, null findings (Dice/hinge-Dice losses no better than weighted CE; OHEM marginal with augmentation), and unfavorable comparison confounds (competitor's larger training set and post-processing) are all transparently disclosed. No protocol registration, but no evidence of selective outcome reporting.

detailed_extraction: Precursor: extended from MIDL 2018 conference paper (Heinrich et al. 2018); this journal version adds multi-layer OBELISK, grid-regular sampling enabling subsequent grid convolutions, and the encoder-decoder hybrid — explicitly addressing three stated limitations of the original (single kernel only; random non-grid sample locations; no encoder-decoder path). Implementation: filter offsets and coefficients jointly learned in continuous space via differentiable image interpolation (gridsample, from spatial transformer networks); per-voxel outputs computed independently ('sparsely sampling prediction'), so memory (~700MB) is independent of image dimensions. Training sampling: original OBELISK trained on 512 random voxels/image (192 spatial samples x 64 random minibatch iterations x 50 epochs); hybrid and U-Nets trained fully-convolutionally on whole images (batch 3 for U-Nets, 1 for hybrid). Baseline: original single-layer OBELISK without augmentation reached 76.7% mean Dice on VISCERAL (7 labels). Ablations: Dice loss and hinge Dice loss vs sqrt-inverse-frequency-weighted CE with OHEM (75% quantile) — negligible difference after 300 epochs; OHEM's influence marginal once affine augmentation used; U-Nets used leaky ReLU. TCIA pipeline inherits Gibson et al. 2018 manual bounding-box cropping to 144³ (irregular voxel spacings), which the authors note is an important initialization dependency for single-pass U-Nets without attention gates. Hardware: GTX 1080 Ti (training, ~90 min/model); Titan Xp (Nvidia-donated). Limitations with direct bearing on synthesis: anisotropic spacings unhandled, gains over dense V-Net partially confounded by unequal training data and post-processing, dataset-size correlation with Dice explicitly demonstrated (>9% gap for liver/spleen/kidney between 43-scan and 10-scan cohorts).
contribution_summary: OBELISK-Net replaces stacks of conventional 3D convolutions with a learnable sparse deformable kernel that jointly learns filter coefficients and continuous spatial offsets via differentiable interpolation, followed by a 1x1 Dense-Net classifier, with an optional hybrid combining a shallow U-Net-like CNN for small-organ refinement. Using only ~230k parameters, ~700MB memory, and 87 ms/volume inference, it matches or exceeds parameter-matched and larger U-Net variants on two multi-organ CT benchmarks (82.27% mean Dice on VISCERAL 7 structures; 79.03% mean on TCIA43), demonstrating that deep encoder-decoder stacks are not always necessary when labeled data is scarce. The flexible sparse sampling also enables per-voxel prediction with potential for time-sensitive image-guided interventions.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Total of 399 CT volumes across three datasets. Training sets exceed 50 subjects for the two main experiments: NIH (82 volumes; ~61 training per fold in 4-fold CV) and MSD (281 volumes; ~210 training per fold). Only the ISICDM sub-experiment is small (20 training / 16 testing), but this does not drive the main conclusions.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: All three sources explicitly identified with references/URLs: ISICDM 2018 Pancreas Segmentation Challenge, NIH Pancreas-CT (TCIA), and MSD pancreas challenge (Fang et al. 2019). Table 2 additionally reports image sizes, intensity ranges (e.g., -1024 to 3071 for ISICDM, -2048 to 4009 for MSD), and voxel spacings for each dataset.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Splits clearly specified: ISICDM 20 train / 16 held-out test; NIH 4-fold CV with fold sizes 21/21/20/20 (matching Roth et al. and Cai et al. for fair comparison); MSD 4-fold CV with an explicitly stated index-based partition ({1,5,9,...}, etc.). Minor caveat: no distinct validation set or random seed is described; hyperparameters were 'determined based on cross-validation using the training dataset.'

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth described only at a high level: annotations are stated to be manual/expert ('The training set has manual annotations'; 'all datasets with expert annotations are available'), and the introduction generically notes gold standards come from experienced radiologists. No details on who annotated, number of raters, protocol, quality control, or inter-/intra-rater variability for any of the three datasets.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Partial credit: the framework is evaluated on three independent datasets from different sources/scanners with substantially different intensity ranges, demonstrating cross-domain robustness (including tumor-bearing MSD cases). However, each dataset is used for its own training (4-fold CV, or same-challenge train/test for ISICDM); there is no strict external validation where a model trained on one cohort is tested, untouched, on a fully independent cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture well documented: U-Net-based 3D CNN (3x3x3 kernels, 2x2x2 pooling, 4 down/up-sampling levels, 16 first-layer channels, 49x49x49 patches, 15x15x15 sliding window) and three 2-channel 2D U-Nets (3x3 kernels, 5 down/up-sampling levels, 32 first-layer channels, per-plane input sizes 256x160x2 / 256x256x2), plus full specification of the multi-atlas (affine + fast LDDMM-image, 5 atlases) and DRLSE level-set refine stage. Key parameters tabulated in Table 1 and pipeline illustrated in Figs. 1-3.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: epochs (30 x 20 subepochs for 3D CNN; 10 for 2D CNNs), samples per subepoch (500), patch/window sizes, atlas count, registration downsampling (1/4 resolution), and augmentation (random sampling; random margin padding per Zhou et al. 2017) are given, and the 3D training strategy follows LiviaNET.
