However, optimizer, learning rate, learning-rate schedule, batch size, deep learning framework, and GPU hardware are not reported, preventing full independent reproduction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Losses are stated (cross-entropy for the 3D CNN; Dice loss for the 2D CNNs, Table 1) but no rationale is provided for choosing them, for mixing CE (3D) with Dice (2D), or for alternatives considered.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre- and post-processing thoroughly described: CT intensity normalization to zero mean/unit variance; 1/4-resolution downsampling for registration; intensity truncation at 99th percentile within the CNN mask with linear normalization for the edge indicator; fuzzy c-means masking of high-intensity structures (e.g., aorta); LCCD on 3D CNN output; majority-vote fusion of the three planes; 3D DRLSE with fine segmentation as initialization and constraint. Worked examples in Figs. 3, 8, and 9.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or trained model publicly available at publication (pre-proof stage). The paper only promises that 'source code and all dataset with ground truth segmentations will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the manuscript'; no URL or repository is provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Three complementary metrics reported with formal definitions: Dice (DSC), Jaccard index (JI), and volume difference (VD), reported as mean +/- std and [worst, best] for every pipeline stage (Tables 3 and 5).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests quantify every ablation step: coarse->fine p<0.01 (all metrics); fine->refine p=0.0004 (Dice and JI) and p=0.0229 (VD); LCCD p<0.05; adding each 2D plane p<0.01 (Dice/JI) and p<0.05 (VD); 2.5D fusion vs. individual planes p<0.001 (Dice/JI). Mean +/- std reported throughout (no confidence intervals, but significance testing is substantive).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Direct comparison on NIH against four recognized baselines under the same 4-fold partition: Roth 2015 (71.42), Roth 2016 (78.01), Zhou 2017 (82.37), Cai 2017 (82.40) vs. proposed 84.61 Dice; also wins ISICDM 2018 challenge (highest Dice/JI, lowest VD). Caveat: competitor numbers are quoted from prior publications rather than re-implemented; no published head-to-head on MSD.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ (pancreas) study, so per-organ breakdown is not applicable; the intent of the criterion (granular, non-average-only reporting) is fully met via per-case Dice distributions per fold (Fig. 10), per-stage results with worst/best bounds (Tables 3, 5), per-plane (coronal/sagittal/axial) results, and min/max Dice on NIH (91.46 / 70.36).

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid and specific: 6/281 MSD cases fall below 50% Dice (tumor-related; worst case 16.31% with a large hole, shown in Fig. 11 with a manual-correction recovery path to 85%); explicitly states no manual intervention was used in reported results; discussion identifies multi-atlas runtime (~2 min), independent (non-joint) 3D/2D training, non-adaptive plane fusion, and level-set dependence on edge quality, with concrete future work.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate concern. All evaluations use established public benchmarks (NIH-TCIA, MSD, ISICDM), limiting arbitrary case selection, and standard splits matching prior work are reused. However, no patient-level inclusion/exclusion criteria (demographics, disease status, contrast phase) are reported, and the 5 multi-atlas templates were 'pre-selected' from the training set without stated selection criteria, leaving room for favorable template choice.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low concern for internal validity: a single fixed pipeline with identical metrics is applied across all cases/datasets, and ablations are statistically tested. Moderate concern for comparative validity: state-of-the-art numbers are taken directly from previous publications rather than re-executed, and no published competitor results exist for the MSD/ISICDM evaluations (challenge ranking only), so cross-method comparability rests on the NIH dataset alone.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low concern. All three predefined metrics are reported for every stage with dispersion and extremes; failure cases (6/281 MSD, Dice<50%) and their tumor-related cause are explicitly disclosed, and authors affirm no manual correction was applied to reported numbers. Minor gap: only average/min/max Dice are compared against SOTA on NIH, while JI/VD comparisons against prior methods are not tabulated.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details not captured in prior extraction: (1) Coarse stage mechanics: 5 atlases are pre-selected from the training set; each is affinely registered then fast LDDMM-image registered (Wu & Tang 2019) to the test image at 1/4 resolution; transformed labels are combined by UNION (not majority STAPLE-style fusion) followed by dilation; smallest enclosing cuboid defines the CNN ROI. Atlas-count ablation (Fig. 6): 1 atlas gives FVF ~2% but sensitivity only ~70%; 5 atlases chosen as the FVF/sensitivity operating point. (2) Fine-stage training details: dense-training sampling (Kamnitsas et al. 2017) restricted to a pancreas-containing cubic bounding box, with uniform pancreas/background patch sampling to counter class imbalance; 49x49x49 patches; training protocol replicates LiviaNET (Dolz et al. 2018); 3D CNN: 30 epochs x 20 subepochs x 500 samples; test-time 15x15x15 sliding window. 2D CNNs: 10 epochs each, trained independently per plane. Augmentation: random sampling (3D) and random margin padding (2D), following Zhou et al. 2017. (3) Two-channel mechanism: 3D CNN probability maps are sliced along each plane and concatenated as a second input channel with the CT; feature-map visualization (Fig. 7) shows activation concentrated on pancreas vs. single-channel inputs. Per-plane ablation (Table 5): 3D CNN 75.0 Dice -> +LCCD 79.3 -> +coronal/sagittal/axial 2D 82.4/82.9/83.0 -> fused 2.5D 83.7; coronal weakest (2D annotations disconnected in that plane), axial best (attributed to axial labeling of GT). (4) Refine stage: DRLSE (Li et al. 2010) with external energy terms from Ngo et al. 2017; phi0 set to -c0 where RF>0.5 and used as both initialization and constraint; edge indicator g=1/(1+|grad(G_sigma*I)|^2) computed after 99th-percentile truncation/normalization within the CNN mask and FCM masking of high-intensity tissues; evolution performed volumetrically (3D), shown to remove residuals and recover missing parts vs. 2D slice-wise level-set (Fig. 9). (5) Quantitative stage contributions (Table 3): coarse 24.4 Dice / 14.1 JI / 288.0 VD; fine 83.7 / 72.3 / 13.8; refine 85.7 / 75.4 / 7.9 (avg across the three datasets). (6) NIH head-to-head (Table 6) includes runtime: Roth 2015 71.42 (6-8 min), Roth 2016 78.01 (2-3 min), Zhou 2017 82.37, Cai 2017 82.40 vs. proposed 84.61 +/- 5.21, max 91.46, min 70.36, 3-5 min (multi-atlas fusion ~2 min of this). (7) MSD protocol: pancreas and tumor masks merged into a single foreground class (binary-segmentation design); folds assigned by case-index modulo 4; most cases >70% Dice, average 82.74. (8) Failure analysis: worst MSD case (Dice 16.31%, large hole due to tumor) is recoverable by placing a sphere with ITK-SNAP then re-running level-set (85% Dice), but no manual correction was used in any reported result. (9) Implementation environment (framework, GPU) unreported; ISICDM challenge outcome (best Dice/JI, lowest VD) cited without publishing the comparison table of rival challenge entries.
contribution_summary: The paper introduces a fully automated cascaded coarse-fine-refine framework for pancreas CT segmentation that fuses classical and learned components: multi-atlas fast-LDDMM registration for ROI localization, a joint 3D patch-based CNN plus two-channel 2.5D U-Net ensemble (with 3D probability maps fed as a second input channel to capture both local context and global shape), and a 3D distance-regularized level-set refinement with fuzzy-c-means-enhanced edge indicators. Validated on three public datasets with different intensity ranges (ISICDM n=36, NIH n=82, MSD n=281 including tumor cases), it achieves >82% average Dice on all three (84.61% on NIH), surpassing Roth 2015/2016, Zhou 2017, and Cai 2017 under the same 4-fold protocol, and improves worst-case Dice on NIH by ~8 points (70.36%). Its distinctive contribution is explicitly integrating global location, contextual, shape, and edge information - via registration, 3D+2.5D CNNs, and level-sets, respectively - to address the pancreas's small size, shape variability, and ambiguous boundaries.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Both cohorts below 50 subjects: MSD Spleen 41 CT volumes (~35 train after 6 val), MSD Cardiac 20 CMR (16 train/4 val). Adequate for framework demonstration, not for validating segmentation performance.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public benchmark data (MSD Spleen CT, MSD Cardiac CMR) clearly identified with modality and volume counts; additional qualitative use cases (brain hemorrhage CT, brain tumor MRI) named.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Splits stated (41 w/ 6 val; 16/4) but no held-out independent test set — final performance is reported as validation Dice during active-learning stages, inflating optimism.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation workflow is the paper's subject and described in depth (clicks, scribbles, GUIs), but the provenance, annotator expertise, and protocol for the evaluation ground truth itself are not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: All quantitative results are on MSD subsets. Telestroke and Neurosurgical Atlas use cases are demonstrations without controlled external validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: DeepGrow/DeepEdit/scribbles mechanisms well described with input/output tensor structure (Figs. 2-4), but the specific experimental backbone (UNet variant, depth, filter counts) is deferred to prior work (Sakinis 2019, Diaz-Pinto 2022) rather than specified.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Per-stage training times reported (90/135/250/360 min), but optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and epochs are absent from the text. Open-source code partially compensates for the paper-level gaps.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Not reported anywhere in the text; only the scribbles pipeline's GraphCut energy optimization is named.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Random affine augmentation and heuristic planner deriving transforms from intensity/spatial metadata are described; no postprocessing reported.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Fully open source: GitHub repo, Apache-2.0, pip-installable (PyPI), release v0.3.0, with SDK and template apps.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice plus annotation time (min/volume, % reduction) — the time metric is arguably the paper's primary endpoint and is reported against paintbrush and contouring baselines.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or variance estimates; results presented as point values and learning curves.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Quantitative comparison is only against manual alternatives (paintbrush, contouring). Interactive DL methods discussed in related work (DeepIGeoS, ilastik, BioMedisa, Clara) are not compared experimentally.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single organ per dataset, so no cross-organ averaging: spleen reported per model and active-learning stage (0.967 DeepGrow 2D, 0.959 3D), left atrium as a separate DeepEdit experiment (final value only as Fig. 7 curve).

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section, no failure cases. Future work only mentions adding more interaction types. DeepGrow's one-label-at-a-time constraint is stated as a design fact, not analyzed as a limitation.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Public MSD data avoids clinical selection bias, but only two small single-organ subsets were picked from a multi-organ benchmark — convenience selection favoring demonstration success.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Outcomes are objective (Dice, annotation time) and recorded consistently across active-learning stages; manual baselines compared under the same conditions. No assessor blinding, but metrics are not subjective.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Annotation-time savings and best Dice are emphasized; left atrium final Dice appears only as a figure; no failure cases, negative results, or statistical testing reported.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details: DeepEdit trains in two alternating modes — half the iterations with zero click-channels (automatic) and half with simulated positive/negative clicks per Sakinis et al. — enabling both click-free inference and click-guided editing from one model. Scribbles support two workflows: (1) online likelihood segmentation where user scribbles seed a GraphCut energy optimization directly, and (2) CNN segmentation refinement where scribbles refine a pretrained model's output. Active learning offers in-sequence, random, TTA (aleatoric), and MC-dropout (epistemic) acquisition; acquisition functions and uncertainty estimators are user-extensible; uncertainty ranking requires the non-interactive DeepEdit path (DeepGrow needs clicks before uncertainty is computable). Server stack: REST API with DICOMWeb (WADO-RS/STOW-RS/QIDO-RS) for PACS/XNAT/IDC integration, datastore layer for local files or DICOM, any GUI may integrate via REST. Annotation-time results: DeepGrow ~1-2.5 min/volume at stage 4 (~10x faster than contouring); scribbles ~2 min/sample (12.5x faster than paintbrush, 6.25x faster than contouring); Neurosurgical Atlas use case reports 50-80% time reduction. Hardware/GPU used for experiments not specified; heuristic planner auto-selects GPU-aware configurations. Release v0.3.0, Apache-2.0.
contribution_summary: MONAI Label is an open-source (Apache-2.0) client-server framework for AI-assisted interactive 3D medical image annotation, coupling click- and scribble-guided models (DeepGrow, DeepEdit) with active learning and DICOMWeb-based deployment into 3D Slicer and OHIF. On MSD Spleen it reaches Dice 0.967 while reducing annotation time ~10x versus manual contouring. It addresses the annotation bottleneck upstream of segmentation rather than proposing a new segmentation architecture, so its relevance to organ-segmentation accuracy benchmarks is as enabling infrastructure.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 241 CT scans (193 train / 24 val / 24 test + 25 qualitative), far above the >50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Clearly described: MSKCC thoracic RT planning CTs of NSCLC patients, IRB 16-142 with written informed consent, mixed contrast/non-contrast, kVp 120-140, avg resolution 1x1x2.5 mm, artifact types noted.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit 80/10/10 split (193/24/24) with defined roles plus separate 25-scan qualitative set; only gap is that the assignment method (random vs. other) is not stated.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Gold-standard contours drawn by 'an expert radiation oncologist or a physicist'; no inter-observer variability assessment, annotator count, delineation protocol, or disagreement-resolution process described. Note: pericardium label also includes thymus.

Q5_external_validation.justification: All data (including the 25 qualitative scans and 283 downstream outcome scans) from a single institution; no independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: DeepLab encoder-decoder with atrous separable convolutions, spatial pyramid pooling, ResNet-101 backbone, output stride 16, x4 bilinear decoder upsampling fully specified.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: lr=0.01, 'policy' scheduler, crop 513x513, batch 8, 50 epochs, PyTorch, GTX 1080Ti, augmentation listed; but optimizer is never named and training time is unreported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Strongest point of the paper: formal definitions of CE, M-DSC, G-DSC, and combined loss, plus a 4-way ablation with explicit rationale for selecting CE (tubular structures, class imbalance).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing fully described (lung auto-crop in SI/AP directions, 512x512 resize, 0-255 normalization, deliberate omission of spatial resampling to avoid interpolation bias, augmentation); postprocessing explicitly none.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Models integrated into the open-source CERR platform, but no repository link for training code; license and release version unspecified.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC + HD95 + 8 dosimetric DVH metrics + expert qualitative clinical-acceptability rating; segmentation time also reported.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on DVH metrics (p 0.69-0.98, alpha=0.05); medians reported with IQR (heart DSC 0.96 (0.95-0.97)). No confidence intervals on DSC itself.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Indirect, cross-dataset literature comparison only (Dormer 2018 ~0.87, Morris 2020 ~0.88, multi-atlas Luo/Zhuo); no baseline retrained on the same data, so comparison is not like-for-like.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure DSC (Fig. 2b) and HD95 (Fig. S1) for all 12 structures; per-structure DVH comparisons (Fig. 4); per-structure slice-adjustment counts in supplement.

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid discussion: domain-adaptation sensitivity, IVC contoured beyond heart boundary contrary to guidelines, no contour-continuity constraints, contours not clinically approved, small structures harder due to low boundary contrast and calcification/motion artifacts.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Single-institution NSCLC radiotherapy cohort limits generalizability; inclusion was by prior treatment rather than a stated consecutive/enrollment protocol, and the method of assigning patients to train/val/test is not reported.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. All 24 hold-out scans were scored against the same expert reference contours with consistent metrics; however, the radiation oncologist rating the 25 qualitative scans was not blinded to the auto-generated origin of the contours.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All 12 structures, all four loss variants (including unfavorable results), and worst-case examples (Fig. S2) are reported; minor issue that exact per-organ values are partly confined to figures/supplementary material rather than tables.

detailed_extraction: Training used 10,284 2D axial slices derived from the 193 training volumes. Pipeline comprises five models total: one multi-label model for 8 non-overlapping structures (aorta, LA, RA, LV, RV, IVC, SVC, PA) plus four separate models for overlapping structures (heart, atria, pericardium, ventricles); the best loss was selected on the 8-structure model then reused for all. Model selection per loss = minimal validation loss per epoch ('steady state') on the 24-scan validation set. Dosimetric validation: 8 DVH metrics on 6 structures associated with heart toxicity (atria, LA, pericardium, SVC, ventricles; plus heart/LA dose-volume thresholds), Wilcoxon signed-rank at alpha=0.05. LV achieved highest agreement (least cardiac motion artifact); aorta had lowest HD95 accuracy. Downstream deployment: auto-segmentation applied to 283 additional planning CTs for heart-toxicity outcomes analysis; inference ~10 s/patient on a GTX 1080Ti. Unreported items: optimizer, training time, license, code release version, exact per-organ DSC numeric values (in Fig. 2b only), and any inter-observer contour variability data.
contribution_summary: A multi-label 2D DeepLab (ResNet-101) system segmenting 12 cardio-pulmonary substructures from contrast and non-contrast thoracic planning CTs, with a loss-function ablation showing cross-entropy outperforms Dice-based losses for long tubular structures (aorta 0.81 to 0.93 DSC). Validation goes beyond geometric overlap to dosimetric equivalence (DVH metrics, p>=0.69) and expert-judged clinical acceptability (85% of contours acceptable without adjustment), cutting contouring time from ~1 h to ~10 s per patient. Models were released via the open-source CERR platform and applied to 283 scans for cardiac toxicity outcomes analysis.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 755 CT scans total with 505 for training — far exceeding the >50 threshold. Substantial per-site cohorts (H&N 320, thorax 110, abdomen 200, pelvis 125) plus 40 cases for time evaluation and 20 patients for dose-accuracy evaluation.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both sources explicitly identified: in-house data from Shanghai General Hospital with full acquisition protocol (GE Discovery 590RT, 120 kV, 300 mA, 2.5 mm slices, 512×512, iohexol contrast 90 mL @ 2 mL/s, 50 s delay); public data from TCIA (215 cases). IRB approval stated. Public acquisition protocol admittedly unknown, but this was transparently reported and exploited as a generalization test.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split sizes and per-site/per-source distribution clearly tabulated (505 train / 250 test, Table 1). However, the split methodology (random vs. stratified, patient overlap checks) is not described; a validation set is implied ('same dataset for training, validation, and evaluation' for all DL methods) but never characterized. No cross-validation.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process well documented: all OARs delineated by a single expert (>10 years RT experience) following published consensus guidelines (DAHANCA/EORTC/GORTEC H&N, RTOG thoracic/upper-abdominal/pelvic atlases), with review by a committee of three experts (>30 years experience). Limitation of single-expert subjectivity is acknowledged; no inter-observer variability quantified.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Genuine independent evaluation on 215 public TCIA cases (thorax/abdomen/pelvis public cases used only for testing), with different acquisition protocols. Consistent performance (avg DSC 0.81 public vs 0.84 in-house; no significant difference for 25 OARs) demonstrates generalization. Not multi-center/prospective, but a valid external test set.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: System-level architecture well described with design rationale: AlexNet-based site detector dividing the volume via lung-based cutoffs with boundary offsets; Ua-Net (region-proposal-based, from authors' prior work) for H&N, 2.5D U-Net for thorax, patch-based 3D U-Net for abdomen/pelvis, and contour merging logic. However, layer-level specifications and model hyperparameters are deferred to supplementary materials and cannot be verified from the main text.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No training details in the main text: optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, patch size, and loss configuration are absent (relegated to supplementary materials). Source code and weights are not released. Only a hosted web platform (DV.Target) is offered, which does not enable independent retraining or rigorous reproduction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function not reported in the provided text; no justification of the loss choice is available in the main paper (stated to be in supplementary materials).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre/post-processing logic described at a conceptual level: automatic site detection with region offsets around lung-based cutoffs, custom histogram-based data augmentation designed from cross-modality intensity differences, and boundary-region merging of site-specific contours. Exact parameters (offset sizes, augmentation specifics, intensity normalization) are in supplementary materials.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Partial availability: source code and model weights are NOT open-source, but a free web-based research platform (https://irvine.deep-voxel.com/) allows inference use. This supports practical accessibility but not methodological reproducibility. Potential commercial conflict (DeepVoxel employees as co-authors) is declared.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Two complementary geometric metrics: volumetric DSC and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (with sound justification for 95% over max HD). Beyond geometry, clinically meaningful metrics: delineation time savings and dosimetric differences in treatment plans — a strength rare among DL segmentation papers.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Per-organ results reported as mean ± SD; two-sided paired Student's t-tests with explicit p-values for time savings (all p<0.0001) and dose differences (e.g., left eye p=0.015, larynx p=0.005, right parotid p=0.00042); group t-test for in-house vs. public comparisons. The use of t-tests on non-normal data is explicitly justified via the central limit theorem. Minor gaps: no formal statistical tests comparing DSC between methods, and no confidence intervals.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Strong comparison against three baselines under identical train/val/test data: commercial multi-atlas ABAS, AnatomyNet, and the highly competitive nnU-Net. WBNet best in 34/50 OARs (in-house DSC) vs. nnU-Net 18, AnatomyNet 3. Honest acknowledgment of where baselines win (e.g., nnU-Net superior on esophagus). Additional literature-level comparison in supplementary tables.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Complete per-organ tables for all 50 OARs (DSC with SD in Table 2, 95%HD in Table 3 for in-house; corresponding public-dataset tables in supplementary), not merely averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: Thorough limitations discussion: (1) training data predominantly 'normal' anatomy — caution for tumor-involved/resected anatomy; (2) single-expert annotation bias; (3) limited direct methodological comparisons due to dataset differences. Failure modes explicitly identified with reasons: small/low-contrast OARs (brachial plexus DSC 0.61, hypophysis 0.59, optic chiasm 0.64, sublingual gland 0.43) and digestive organs (esophagus 0.76, duodenum 0.77); 11/560 OARs with >1000 cGy dose differences flagged.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/Unclear. No explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, patient demographics, or disease characteristics reported; single-institution in-house cohort plus TCIA. Training data predominantly 'normal' anatomy (tumor invasion/resection effectively excluded), which plausibly inflates reported performance relative to the clinical population requiring auto-segmentation.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-Moderate. Outcome assessment largely consistent: all DL baselines used identical data splits and metrics; dose plans standardized (Varian Eclipse v13.6, RapidArc). However, the same expert who trained the model reviewed WBNet outputs unblinded in the time-saving experiment (potential bias toward favorable revision times), and single-expert ground truth introduces subjectivity despite committee review.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-Moderate. All 50 OARs reported per-organ for both datasets, including frankly poor results (sublingual gland DSC 0.43), which argues against selective reporting. Gaps: no statistical significance testing of DSC differences between methods, key training details (loss, hyperparameters) hidden in supplementary materials, and declared commercial interests (DeepVoxel employees; platform promotion) constitute a potential source of favorable reporting, though transparently disclosed.

detailed_extraction: Additional methodological details not captured in prior extraction: (1) STUDY DESIGN: retrospective development + clinical validation study; IRB approved in-house data use; open access under CC BY-NC-ND. (2) ANNOTATION GUIDELINES: H&N per DAHANCA/EORTC/GORTEC/HKNPCSG/NCIC CTG/NCRI/NRG/TROG consensus; thorax per Kong et al. RTOG atlas; upper abdomen per Jabbour et al. RTOG consensus; pelvis per Gay et al. RTOG consensus atlas — 50 OARs total (28 H&N, 6 thorax, 16 abdomen/pelvis; note spinal cord and trachea counted at multiple sites). (3) SITE DETECTION LOGIC: lung-position-based cutoffs with offsets to broaden regions (e.g., liver may extend above lung cutoff; offsets prevent truncation); boundary merging between site models. (4) MODEL SELECTION RATIONALE: Ua-Net's region-proposal approach confines segmentation to ~26% of total voxels, enabling high-resolution prediction, reduced GPU memory, and fewer false positives for small H&N OARs, but requires large data and is inefficient for large OARs — hence 2.5D U-Net for thorax (axial features sufficient; higher prediction resolution and larger feature depth outweigh 3D context) and patch-based 3D U-Net for abdomen/pelvis (3D spatial context needed where axial appearance is non-distinctive). Design constraints: extensibility (model compression compatibility), low cost (must fit NVIDIA GTX 1080 Ti at inference), generalization (fewer domain-specific hyperparameters). (5) DATA AUGMENTATION: handcrafted augmentation derived from histogram differences across imaging modalities (rather than random augmentation as in nnU-Net) to scale/diversify training data — credited for good generalization to public data. (6) EVALUATION DETAIL: WBNet best DSC on 34/50 OARs (in-house) and 33/50 (public); best 95%HD on 37/50 (in-house) and 40/50 (public); nnU-Net best DSC on 18 (in-house)/15 (public); AnatomyNet 3/4. Literature-level comparison (supplementary Tables 6-9): WBNet highest DSC in 22/36 common OARs vs. previously published methods. (7) CLINICAL EVALUATION PROTOCOL: time study — 40 cases (10/site), Method 1 = full manual delineation by the training expert vs Method 2 = WBNet output + expert revision; dose study — 20 nasopharyngeal cancer patients, AD-based plans transferred to MD for comparison; max-dose metric for serial organs (brachial plexus, brainstem, spinal cord, lenses, optic chiasm/nerves, temporal lobes), mean-dose for others; significant but clinically acceptable mean dose differences found for left eye (Δ~20 cGy), larynx (Δ~50 cGy), right parotid (Δ~207 cGy), right TMJ; 11/560 OAR dose differences >1000 cGy, concentrated in small/low-DSC OARs. Some low-DSC OARs (brachial plexus, hypophysis, optic chiasm/nerves, sublingual gland) occasionally required MRI assistance during review. (8) BASELINE SETUP: ABAS used the 505-case training set as atlas library; AnatomyNet and nnU-Net trained/validated/tested on identical data as WBNet. (9) FUNDING: Shanghai General Hospital Clinical Research Innovation Plan (CTCCR-2019D06) and Shanghai Municipal Education Commission Gaofeng Clinical Medicine Grant (20181713). (10) COMPETING INTERESTS: five co-authors DeepVoxel employees; one advisor to DeepVoxel. (11) REPORTING GAPS: framework/library, optimizer, learning rate schedule, training time, and inference time not reported in main text (some in supplementary); validation set composition unspecified; no DSC p-values between competing methods.
contribution_summary: This paper presents WBNet, a divide-and-conquer whole-body auto-segmentation system that couples an AlexNet-based anatomic site detector with three site-specific deep segmentation models (Ua-Net for 28 head/neck OARs, 2.5D U-Net for 6 thoracic OARs, patch-based 3D U-Net for 16 abdominal/pelvic OARs), enabling fully automated delineation of 50 OARs across the entire body without manual site or organ selection. Trained/tested on 755 CT scans (505/250 split) with external TCIA validation, it achieved average DSC of 0.84 (in-house) and 0.81 (public) with 6.39 mm/13.71 mm mean 95%HD, outperforming commercial ABAS, AnatomyNet, and nnU-Net on most OARs. Its key clinical contributions are demonstrated delineation time reductions of 61-86% across body sites and clinically acceptable dosimetric agreement in treatment plans of 20 nasopharyngeal cancer patients, establishing practical feasibility for radiation therapy workflows while honestly flagging weaknesses on small/low-contrast and digestive OARs.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 101 CECT cases for training (>50 threshold met); 136 total scans.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: In-house RT-planning CTs from Osaka International Cancer Institute; ethics approval; full scanner/protocol specs (GE LightSpeed 16-slice, 120 kVp, 2.5 mm slices, contrast injection parameters).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split clearly stated (101 CECT train, 20 CECT + 15 nCECT validation, random selection), but no separate test set — 'validation' data is the final test set, and the data used for grid-search hyperparameter tuning is unspecified (leakage risk).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Contours drawn by one of seven radiation oncologists (>5 years experience), randomly allocated to cases; contour-to-mask conversion described. No consensus reading or interobserver variability quantification of GT.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single institution, in-house data only; no external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Only described as 'a structure similar to U-Net' — no depth, channel counts, patch/tile strategy, or 2D vs 3D specification; the U-Net citation (#16) points to Su et al. cell-detection paper, not Ronneberger's original.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Framework named (Sony Neural Network Console), grid search stated, but resulting hyperparameter values, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and epochs all unreported — not reproducible.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never specified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Fully described: 16→8-bit compression, contour fill to binary masks, rotation augmentation (-30/-15/+15/+30°) in ImageJ; post-processing: binarization at 128 + largest 3D connected component.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or license released.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice + Hausdorff distance, both defined formally; runtime comparison as secondary outcome.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Appropriate paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (CNN vs MIM) and Mann-Whitney U (CECT vs nCECT) tests; p-values reported; R 3.5.1. No confidence intervals.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Head-to-head vs MIM Maestro commercial auto-segmentation on identical data — a valid clinical baseline, but no head-to-head vs published DL methods (prior CNN results only cited with the caveat they are not comparable).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single organ (liver); results fully reported, stratified by contrast status and method, with SDs and box plots.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit failure examples (Fig. 6: gallbladder/kidney/intestine included in lower liver) and limitations section: no cysts/tumors in validation, insufficient nCECT training data, single institution/organ.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate: selection rules clear (pancreatic RT-planning cases, retrospective, random case-to-annotator allocation), but single institution and all-pancreatic-cancer population limit generalizability; livers presumably largely disease-free (confirmed as a limitation).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low for evaluation consistency: identical GT, metrics, and paired statistics applied to both CNN and MIM Maestro. Moderate reference-standard bias: GT from a single annotator per case with no consensus or interobserver reliability check.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low: all planned outcomes (Dice, HD, both contrast groups, both methods, timing) reported; failure cases shown; no signs of selective outcome reporting.

detailed_extraction: Retrospective study, ethics-board approved. CT protocol: GE LightSpeed 16-detector, 120 kVp, 250–440 mA (noise index 13), 12×1.25 mm collimation, pitch 0.938, 0.5 s rotation, 512×512 matrix, 50 cm FOV, 2.5 mm axial reconstruction, standard kernel; oral water-soluble contrast (3 mL in 30 mL water); IV nonionic iodine 450 mgI/kg at 3 mL/s with 45 s delay (CECT only); exhalation breath-hold. GT: binary contour images delineated by 1 of 7 radiation oncologists (>5 yrs), random allocation, filled to masks. Pipeline: 16→8-bit intensity compression; rotations added as extra training copies (not on-the-fly augmentation); CNN trained in Sony Neural Network Console with grid-searched (unreported) hyperparameters. Inference: 8-bit probability output, threshold 128, largest 3D connected component retained. Comparator: MIM Maestro with user-specified liver superior/inferior extents, atlas-style matching against several dozen registered cases. Results: Dice 0.961±0.01 (CECT) / 0.949±0.02 (nCECT) for CNN vs 0.844±0.06 / 0.841±0.08 for MIM; HD 7.87±4.28 / 8.59±4.97 mm vs 24.5±7.9 / 29.9±21.98 mm; all CNN-vs-MIM differences p<0.001. CECT-vs-nCECT: CNN Dice p=0.003 (CECT higher) but HD p=0.82 (NS); MIM Dice p=0.95. Mean liver CT attenuation 182 HU (CECT) vs 160 HU (nCECT); authors attribute nCECT robustness to shape/position cues rather than intensity alone. Timing: ~10 min manual, several min MIM, seconds per case CNN. Statistical software R 3.5.1. nCECT training data unavailable at institution (contrast protocols standard of care in Japan); diagnostic CTs excluded due to geometric mismatch with RT-simulation CT. Not 3D architecture per se ('U-Net-like'); 3D appears only in post-processing connectivity.
contribution_summary: The key contribution is clinical evidence that a U-Net-like CNN trained exclusively on contrast-enhanced planning CTs (101 cases) generalizes to non-contrast CT (Dice 0.949 vs 0.961 on CECT), with no significant HD difference — the first reported demonstration of this cross-contrast liver transfer, addressing a practical RT-planning gap for contrast-contraindicated patients. The CNN significantly outperformed commercial MIM Maestro auto-segmentation on both Dice and Hausdorff distance (p<0.001) while reducing delineation time from ~10 min to seconds. Its value is as a single-center clinical validation study rather than a methodological advance; the architecture and training details are too under-specified for reproduction or benchmark use.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Far exceeds threshold: 500 patients prospectively enrolled (497 analyzed) across 5 centers, yielding 2,483 delineation sets covering 27,043 individual OARs (993 manual, 497 AI, 993 AI-assisted). Model was trained on 827 retrospective planning CTs (SYSUCC n=518, SDCIH n=309).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Exceptionally well described: prospective trial (NCT05787522, Sept 2022–Feb 2023) at 5 named Chinese hospitals with site-specific IRB approvals; full baseline table (age, sex, diagnosis, 4 scanner platforms, kV/mA, contrast, detector slices, slice thickness, pixel spacing); training data sources (2 institutions) also explicitly named with no center/patient/delineator overlap.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split methodology is unambiguous: entire evaluation cohort is prospective and fully external (5 institutions disjoint from the 2 training institutions, with no overlap in centers, patients, or delineators). Crossover randomization of images (1:1, SAS block size 10, concealed allocation) is clearly reported. Minor caveat: internal train/validation split of the 827 training CTs is deferred to Supplementary Tables 6–7, not visible in main text.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Rigorous consensus protocol: three senior radiation oncologists (>10 yrs experience); Experts A and B independently delineated each image, Expert C adjudicated/selected the best structures with mandatory consensus before finalization; GT experts were excluded from trial delineations and training-set creation. Contouring followed published atlases (RTOG 1106 for thoracic OARs, RTOG upper-abdominal consensus for liver, standard radiological anatomy for humeral heads).

Q5_external_validation.justification: The core design IS external validation: 497 analyzed patients from 5 centers fully independent of the 827-image development set (different institutions, patients, and delineators). Additionally benchmarked against nnU-Net retrained on identical development data and open-source TotalSegmentator.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Partial: main text identifies iCurveE as a 2D U-Net backbone with Res-SE (squeeze-and-excitation) blocks (Supplementary Fig. 23) and notes NMPA Class III approval. Layer-level details, depth, and channels are deferred entirely to Supplementary Table 6 and are not verifiable in the main text.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: training workflow (preprocessing, augmentation, training, morphological post-processing) is described at a high level, with hyperparameters claimed to be 'comprehensively listed' in Supplementary Table 6 and training performance in Table 7. However, the model is proprietary commercial software and imaging data are only available under restricted access, preventing independent reproduction even with supplementary hyperparameters. Sample-size calculation and randomization (SAS 9.4) are well documented.

Q8_loss_function.justification: No loss function is named or justified anywhere in the main text. It may appear in Supplementary Table 6, but it is neither stated nor justified in the accessible text.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: A 'standardized preprocessing pipeline, data augmentation, model training, and morphological post-processing' are mentioned, with parameters deferred to Supplementary Table 6. CT acquisition/positioning/scan-range standardization is well described, but image-level pre/post-processing specifics are not provided in the main text.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Explicitly not available: 'The iCurveE auto-segmentation model... is a commercial software product developed by Perception Vision Medical Technology (PVmed), and its source code is proprietary and not publicly available.' CT data available only on restricted request (protocol + ethics approval, 6-month availability window). Source data files for figures are provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Extensive multi-metric evaluation: primary endpoints vDSC and contouring time; secondary HD95, surface DSC, and volumetric revision index (VRI); supplementary precision, recall, and relative volume difference; plus a dosimetric arm computing absolute deviations across 38 DVH parameters (QUANTEC/Timmerman-guided) on a 40-patient subset.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Comprehensive: a priori non-inferiority sample-size calculation (one-sided α=0.025, 90% power, margin −0.05, SD 0.225, n=426→500), Friedman+Dunn, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann–Whitney U, Welch's ANOVA+Games–Howell, linear regression with 95% CIs, exact p-values throughout, and Source Data file with exact values.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Strong benchmarking: iCurveE (vDSC 0.896, HD95 5.62 mm) significantly outperformed nnU-Net trained from scratch on identical development images (0.850, 12.05 mm; p<0.0001) and open-source TotalSegmentator (0.781, 19.07 mm; p<0.0001), winning in 6/11 and 4/8 comparable OARs respectively.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ results reported for all 11 OARs (e.g., AI-assisted beat manual for 11/11 OARs except aorta HD95, p=0.461; AI-assisted beat AI for 6/11 OARs), with extensive subgroup analyses by center, cancer type, slice thickness, contrast, physician experience, and attitude (Supplementary Figs. 2–17, Supplementary Tables 1–3).

Q15_limitations.justification: Thorough limitations section: 75.6% of scans at 5-mm thickness (partial-volume effects, humeral heads), dosimetric confounders (plan optimization, fractionation, respiratory motion) and single-center dosimetric subset, 2D architecture, and absence of validation on cardiac substructures/brachial plexus. Specific failure instances are reported (no AI-assisted advantage for trachea in Center 4/EC patients, aorta in Center 5); one model generation failure caused an exclusion.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: LOW. Prospective registered trial with explicit inclusion criteria (age ≥18, lung/esophageal/breast cancer, thoracic radiotherapy candidate, planning CT slices ≤5 mm, informed consent) and exclusion criteria (non-tumoral thoracic deformity, artifact/implant-obscured anatomy, non-DICOM, investigator-determined unsuitability); defined consecutive enrollment window. Minor caveats: 'investigator-determined unsuitability' is subjective; all 5 centers are in China; case mix is skewed (64% breast cancer, 72.6% female), limiting generalizability to other populations.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: LOW-TO-MODERATE. Blinding of physicians to contouring method was impossible and investigators were unblinded (open-label by design, acknowledged). Mitigated by crossover design with >4-week washout, randomized 1:1 image allocation with concealed sequencing (opaque sealed cards), objective geometric metrics computed against independent 3-expert consensus ground truth (experts uninvolved in trial delineations and training data), standardized contouring atlases, and identical AI outputs for paired comparisons. AI satisfaction ratings were subjective and one assessment was inadvertently omitted (transparently reported as a protocol deviation); attitude effects were analyzed rather than hidden.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: LOW. Prospective registration (NCT05787522) with pre-specified primary/secondary endpoints; Source Data file provided; patient exclusions and protocol deviation disclosed; unfavorable/null findings reported (aorta HD95 exception; trachea and aorta subgroups where AI-assisted did not outperform manual; non-significant attitude subgroup results); Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary included. Restricted data access and proprietary code limit independent verification, but no evidence of selective outcome reporting.

detailed_extraction:
TRIAL & DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, observational trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05787522), enrollment Sept 30, 2022–Feb 14, 2023; 5 centers in China (TMUCIH, WHUH, SXCH, FHSU, NXSH), all with IRB approval. Crossover design: anonymized CTs randomized 1:1 (SAS 9.4, block size 10, opaque sealed cards by independent statistician) to Cohort 1 (manual → AI-assisted after >4-week washout) or Cohort 2 (reverse sequence). Images circulated to adjacent centers (Center 1→2 ... Center 5→1) creating paired shared-image sets enabling intra-physician (manual vs AI-assisted) and inter-center/inter-physician comparisons. One Center 05 image failed to transfer and was delineated only locally. Research CTs also used for clinical planning at treating physician's discretion.

COHORT: 500 enrolled, 497 analyzed (3 excluded: 2 insufficient inferior scan coverage, 1 model generation failure); 137 M / 363 F; median age 54 (range 20–88); LC n=146, EC n=35, BC n=320 (1 concurrent LC+BC counted in both). Scanners: GE Revolution/Discovery RT, Philips Brilliance CT Big Bore, Siemens SOMATOM Confidence; 49.2% non-contrast; 75.6% 5-mm slices; 512×512 matrix; scan range cricoid cartilage to lower liver edge.

MODEL: iCurveE (commercial, PVmed; NMPA Class III medical device approval, Reg. No. 20253210066); 2D U-Net backbone with Res-SE blocks (Suppl. Fig. 23); trained on 827 retrospective planning chest CTs (SYSUCC n=518, SDCIH n=309) with explicit no-overlap in centers/patients/delineators vs. trial cohort; GT for training by independent expert panel using same consensus process; standardized preprocessing, data augmentation, morphological post-processing (Suppl. Tables 5–7).

TASK & ANNOTATION PROTOCOL: 11 OARs — left/right lung, trachea, bronchial tree, aorta, heart, esophagus, liver, left/right humeral head, spinal cord. Standards: RTOG 1106 atlas (thoracic OARs), RTOG upper-abdominal consensus (liver), humeral heads = apex to surgical neck under bone window. 37 physicians (≥1 yr experience) performed manual and AI-assisted delineations; 'experienced' = >3 yrs radiotherapy + >50 thoracic/breast cases annually. Ground truth: Experts A & B (>10 yrs) delineated independently, Expert C selected best structures/minor edits, mandatory consensus; all excluded from trial delineation and training data. Annotation volume: 2,483 sets / 27,043 OARs = 993 manual (10,803 OARs), 497 AI (5,403), 993 AI-assisted (10,837). Per-center delineation sets: 261/317/160/138/117 (Centers 1–5).

KEY QUANTITATIVE RESULTS: Standalone iCurveE: vDSC 0.896, HD95 5.62 mm vs. nnU-Net 0.850/12.05 mm and TotalSegmentator 0.781/19.07 mm (both p<0.0001); superior to nnU-Net in 6/11 OARs, TotalSegmentator in 4/8 (TotalSegmentator lacks humeral heads + bronchial tree). Manual vs AI vs AI-assisted: vDSC 0.857 (SD 0.102) / 0.896 (0.072) / 0.902 (0.067); HD95 8.01 / 5.62 / 5.20 mm; all pairwise p<0.0001. AI-assisted > manual for 11/11 OARs (exception: aorta HD95 p=0.461); AI-assisted > AI for 6/11 OARs (heart, aorta, liver, trachea, spinal cord, esophagus). Time: median 10.0 vs 55.0 min (−81.63%, p<0.0001), significant in all subgroups; AI-assisted time less dependent on slice number/thickness (p<0.0001). VRI: 0.168 (Aa) vs 0.221 (M) vs 0.181 (AI), p<0.0001. Inter-center variability reduced: F-values vDSC 54.50→7.53, HD95 25.83→2.07 (p=0.081, non-significant), sDSC 153.2→11.30; paired inter-center |Δ|: vDSC 0.032→0.003, HD95 1.88→0 mm, time 22.0→5.0 min (all p<0.0001). Experience gap (276 paired sets): vDSC |Δ| 0.034→0.003, HD95 1.957→0 mm, time 26.0→5.0 min; OARs with significant experience differences reduced from 9 to 6–8 depending on metric. Attitude analysis: positive (n=897) vs neutral (n=95) — positive group higher AI-vDSC (p=0.0044) and lower AI-VRI (p=0.0009) but longer times; AI assistance narrowed positive-vs-neutral gap in all metrics (p<0.0001). Lower manual accuracy OARs gained most from AI (p<0.0001); model excelled at lobar bronchus, esophagus-azygos boundary, dural sac, humeral surgical neck, cricoid cartilage. Longitudinal analysis (25 less-experienced physicians): 19/25 stable manual vDSC, 3 improved, 3 declined (over/under-segmentation, OAR overlap). Dosimetric validation (n=40 from Center 1: 19 LC/18 BC/3 EC; fixed clinical dose distribution; 38 DVH parameters per QUANTEC/Timmerman): mean absolute deviations 11.1% (manual) / 5.8% (AI) / 4.2% (AI-assisted); significant reduction vs manual in 13/38 (34.2%) and 23/38 (60.5%) parameters; vDSC and HD95 linearly correlated with dosimetric deviation across LC/EC and BC plans (p<0.0001). Heterogeneity: LC/EC lowered AI accuracy for adjacent structures (heart, trachea, esophagus); physician revision eliminated EC-related trachea differences; CE-CT improved heart/aorta/liver accuracy; 5-mm slices hurt only humeral heads.

METRICS & STATISTICS: Primary: vDSC, contouring time; secondary: HD95, sDSC, VRI (optimized RVD estimating expert revision workload); supplementary: precision, recall, RVD (formulas in Suppl. Table 8). Tests: Friedman+Dunn, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann–Whitney U, Welch's ANOVA+Games–Howell, linear regression; GraphPad Prism 10.5.0; two-tailed p<0.05. Safety: no method-related adverse events anticipated; only CT-interruption incidents documented (Suppl. Table 9).

AVAILABILITY: Source data files provided; CT images/delineations restricted-access (request to corresponding author with protocol + ethics approval; 15-working-day response; 6-month availability); model code proprietary/unavailable.

AUTHOR-REPORTED LIMITATIONS: 75.6% 5-mm slices (partial-volume effects, humeral heads); dosimetric confounders and single-center dosimetric subset; 2D architecture; no validation of cardiac substructures/brachial plexus; observational (non-interventional) design without patient-outcome follow-up; unclear whether manual-skill changes stem from AI learning or atlas reference.
contribution_summary: This prospective, multicenter observational trial (NCT05787522; 500 patients, 5 centers, 37 physicians, 2,483 delineation sets across 11 thoracic OARs) delivers the largest end-user validation to date of deep-learning-assisted OAR auto-segmentation in thoracic radiotherapy, showing that AI-assisted delineation with the commercial 2D U-Net/Res-SE model iCurveE significantly outperforms both manual contouring (vDSC 0.902 vs 0.857; HD95 5.20 vs 8.01 mm; 81.6% contouring-time reduction) and standalone state-of-the-art models (nnU-Net, TotalSegmentator). Beyond accuracy, it uniquely demonstrates that AI assistance narrows inter-center and inter-physician-expertise performance gaps—supporting healthcare equity—characterizes physician–AI interaction dynamics (including attitude effects and longitudinal skill changes), and links improved contouring accuracy to reduced dosimetric (DVH) deviations. For a systematic review on 3D organ segmentation, it is a high-evidence clinical validation study, though its methodology-scoring weakness is the proprietary, non-reproducible model and the fact that the architecture is 2D rather than a fully described 3D network.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 50 kidneys from 36 patients total; only 40 kidneys used for training at stage III — below the >50-subject threshold. Very small even for a feasibility study.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Thoroughly described: Asan Medical Center, Siemens Sensation 16, slice thickness 1-1.25 mm, renal cortical (arterial) phase selected, exclusion criteria (cysts/stones), IRB approval with consent waiver, HIPAA de-identification.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split sizes given for stage III (40 train / 10 test), but split method (randomization, stratification) never stated, and a validation set is referenced only via the 6.17 val/test DSC gap without ever defining its size or composition.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Process described (manual delineation at stage I; CNN-corrected labels via Mimics thereafter), but annotators' number, expertise, and any inter-rater agreement are not reported — notable given RCC/ureter have high anatomical variability.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation. Single-center, single-scanner in-house data only.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Cascade described (U-Net 1 → cuboidal ROI bounding box replacing RPN; U-Net 2 → 5-subclass segmentation), with schematic figure, 3×3×3 max pooling, and skip concatenations. Missing: filter counts, depth, patch/crop sizes, first-stage training details.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Strong on stated parameters: Keras 2.2.4/TF 1.14.0, GTX 1080 Ti, Adam (lr 1e-5, weight decay 0.0005, momentum 0.9), batch size 1, epochs per stage (150/300), Gaussian-noise augmentation. Minor gaps: patch size, learning-rate schedule, validation-split construction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss (1 − DSC) defined with equations, but no justification for the choice versus alternatives; no ablation.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Partial: contrast-phase selection, ROI cropping by first U-Net, Gaussian-noise augmentation, slice-thickness range described. No intensity normalization/resampling details; 'postprocessing' is a manual correction workflow (Mimics), not an automated output step.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model released. Data only 'available from the corresponding author on reasonable request'.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC plus RMS surface distance (mm) on 3D models plus annotation time (manual vs CNN-corrected) plus inference time.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired t-tests between stages (SPSS v25) with p-values and mean±SD throughout. Caveats: no confidence intervals, and all stage comparisons were non-significant (stage 1 vs 3 p=0.252; stage 2 vs 3 p=0.330), which weakens the central active-learning claim.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: nnU-Net (KiTS19 winner) comparison claimed as inferior to their method, but the actual nnU-Net numbers are not traceable in the paper — the text cites 'Table 2', which is the labeling-time table. Authors attribute nnU-Net underperformance to their own insufficient preprocessing/tuning, further limiting the comparison's value.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-subclass DSC with SD reported for all stages (artery, vein, ureter, parenchyma, RCC), revealing the clinically important spread (parenchyma 96.27 vs RCC 52.55).

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit and honest: >2 mm error unsuitable for 3D printing/VR/AR without correction, small dataset, low and highly variable RCC Dice, need for more data and further network comparisons.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Retrospective, single-center (36 patients), RCC-enriched (30/50 kidneys); kidneys with cysts/stones excluded, but no consecutive-sampling or enrollment flow described.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate-to-high. Ground truth for stages II-III is partly CNN-generated ('CNN-corrected'), creating circularity between labels, training, and evaluation; corrector identity/blinding not reported. DSC/RMS applied consistently once labels exist.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate-to-high. nnU-Net quantitative results cited but not locatable (table cross-reference error); abstract vs methods conflict on stage II composition (20 reused + 20 new vs 16 reused + 16 new); all stage-improvement p-values non-significant yet the conclusion presents monotonic DSC gains as success; no confidence intervals.

detailed_extraction: Ethics: AMC IRB approval, informed-consent waiver, HIPAA de-identification. Tools: Mimics (Materialise) for manual/CNN-corrected labeling, 3-matic (Materialise) for RMS surface comparison, SPSS v25 for paired t-tests. RMS computed over 17,650 surface points (manual-vs-CNN, manual-vs-CNN-corrected) and 26,471 points (CNN-vs-CNN-corrected). Internal inconsistencies: abstract states stage II = 20 reused + 20 new kidneys; methods state 16 reused + 8 RCC + 8 normal (=32); training section says stages II-III used N=40/50. Authors interpret a 6.17-point validation-vs-test DSC gap as 'not overfit' — questionable given the undefined validation set. Stage-wise DSC gains (54.45 → 70.65 → 71.07 total average) are monotonic but statistically non-significant. Labeling-time savings: 149m6s → 73m6s (~51%); largest per-structure savings on artery (19m8s) and ureter (19m23s). nnU-Net comparison underpowered by authors' own admission (insufficient preprocessing/tuning on their data). Only renal cortical contrast phase used; non-contrast, parenchymal, and excretory phases discarded. Single scanner model (Sensation 16) limits scanner-generalizability. RCC is the worst class (stage III: 52.55 ± 34.57) — very high variance suggests near-failure cases. Data not public; available only on request.
contribution_summary: Proposes an active-learning framework built on a cascaded 3D U-Net (ROI-localizing U-Net followed by a fine-segmentation U-Net for kidney parenchyma, artery, vein, ureter, and RCC) in which new training labels are produced by manually correcting CNN outputs rather than annotating from scratch. This 'CNN-corrected' labeling halves annotation time (149 to 73 min per case) while average DSC improves monotonically across active-learning stages (54.45 to 71.07) on a small single-center CT dataset. Claims superiority over nnU-Net, but the comparison numbers are not verifiable in the paper and stage-wise gains are not statistically significant.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 120 CT simulation scans total; 80 training subjects exceeds the >50 threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Clearly described: Asan Medical Center (Seoul, Korea), HCC patients treated Jul 2017–Mar 2018, IRB approval with waived consent, contrast-enhanced free-breathing 4D-CT (GE LightSpeed RT 16, 2.5 mm slices, end-expiratory phase), full demographics in Table 1.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split explicitly stated (80/20/20, test set independent of training/validation, no cross-validation), but the allocation method (random vs. chronological) is not described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Well described: two professional radiographers (>500 abdominal cases/year) delineated; two radiation oncologists (>10 yrs HCC experience) confirmed each structure; contouring in Eclipse v13.6 on end-expiratory phase.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single-institution, in-house data only; no independent external dataset, site, or scanner tested.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D-patch-based U-Net with 64x64x64 input and multi-label 3D output, illustrated in Fig. 4a, but layer-level specification (depth, filter counts) is deferred to the original 3D U-Net references rather than fully stated.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (RMSprop), LR (1e-5), 1e5 iterations, mini-batch of 8 patches, TensorFlow 1.14, hardware, and training time (3–4 days) reported; missing intensity-normalization scheme, data augmentation (none mentioned), and inference patch-stitching/overlap details.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Cross-entropy loss is stated with no rationale given (e.g., vs. Dice/compound losses for class imbalance between small organs).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (interpolation to 2 mm isotropic + intensity normalization, ITK) and postprocessing (graph-cut with data-penalty term for regional label preference and boundary term penalizing intensity discontinuity, Fig. 4b) are clearly described; only exact graph-cut parameters omitted.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC plus Hausdorff distance and mean surface distance, plus a clinical time-efficiency outcome.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean (SD) per structure with p-values for all U-Net vs. atlas and U-Net vs. inter-observer comparisons (Table 2); time comparison p<0.001. Confidence intervals not reported, but p-values satisfy the criterion.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Quantitative head-to-head against commercial atlas-based autosegmentation (Mirada Medical, 20-scan atlas) and inter-observer contours; competing deep learning methods only discussed qualitatively via literature DSC ranges (0.94–0.98 liver), never tested directly.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ DSC, HD, and MSD for all five structures in Table 2 (liver 0.959, stomach 0.813, duodenum 0.595, Rt kidney 0.900, Lt kidney 0.911), plus per-organ refinement times.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit failure analysis (patient 3: insufficient kidney enhancement — DSC rises to 0.937/0.947 when excluded; patient 11: left lateral segment hypertrophy) and five stated limitations (weak stomach/duodenum, upper abdomen only, radiographer ground truth, fast local manual baseline, time-only efficiency metric).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate: inclusion window and population explicitly defined (radiotherapy-treated HCC, one center, Jul 2017–Mar 2018), but cohort is skewed (81.7% male, 73.3% advanced stage with vascular invasion, mostly multi-treated) and consecutive enrollment is not stated — limits generalizability rather than internal validity.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: all 20 test cases scored against the same ground truth with identical metrics; atlas and inter-observer comparisons run on identical data. Residual concern: ground truth is radiographer contours, not a definitive reference (acknowledged by authors).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low: per-organ results reported including the worst performer (duodenum DSC 0.595) and individual outlier cases; limitations candidly discussed. Minor omissions (inference time, loss curves) do not indicate selective reporting.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details: (1) Imaging protocol — patients immobilized supine with vacuum cushion; free-breathing 4D-CT with RPM respiratory gating; IV contrast injected; data sorted into 10 respiratory phases; all contouring on end-expiratory phase. (2) Atlas baseline — Mirada Medical commercial system with a 20-scan liver atlas library; notably, in discussion the authors report atlas-based refinement took LONGER than manual contouring and was deemed inapplicable (not shown in results tables). (3) Inter-observer arm — a radiation oncology resident uninvolved in ground-truth contouring re-delineated the 5 structures on all 20 test cases. (4) Per-organ manual refinement times after U-Net: 2.0 min (liver), 2.0 min (stomach), 2.5 min (duodenum, longest due to worst accuracy), 1.0 min (each kidney). (5) Training details — patches randomly sampled, no data augmentation described; single RTX Titan 24GB, i9-7960X CPU; pre/post-processing via ITK. (6) Metric observations — authors note DSC was the most stable metric while HD/MSD were 'noisy and fluctuating'; interestingly U-Net duodenum MSD was statistically better than inter-observer (P=0.679, i.e., not significantly different) despite lower DSC. (7) Translation status — framework reportedly in routine clinical use at Asan Medical Center for liver-cancer patients; manually refined contours stored on intranet server for iterative retraining. (8) Caveat — provided paper text is truncated mid-sentence in the evaluation-metrics section, but complete per-organ values are available from Table 2. (9) Cohort complexity — most livers contained treatment artifacts (iodized oil, post-ablation cavities, post-resection volume loss), making this a harder-than-typical liver segmentation cohort; claimed liver DSC 0.959 should be interpreted in that context.
contribution_summary: This paper presents a 3D-patch-based U-Net (64x64x64 voxel inputs, multi-label output) combined with graph-cut post-processing for auto-segmenting five upper-abdominal organs at risk (liver, stomach, duodenum, bilateral kidneys) on contrast-enhanced 4D-CT from 120 hepatocellular carcinoma patients. The framework significantly outperformed commercial atlas-based autosegmentation on all structures (e.g., liver DSC 0.959 vs 0.808) and was statistically comparable to inter-observer segmentation for liver and kidneys, while reducing segmentation time from 22.6 to 7.1 minutes. Its key significance is clinical validation: it was deployed in routine radiotherapy practice at the authors' institution, an early demonstration of clinically operational DL-based multi-organ autosegmentation for abdominal radiation oncology.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: KiTS19 provides 300 kidney tumor CT cases (cited from Heller et al.), well above the 50-subject threshold. CHAOS CT subset size is not stated in the text, but KiTS19 alone satisfies the criterion.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both datasets are public challenge datasets (KiTS19, CHAOS) with citations and explicit rationale for their use. CHAOS CT subset size is not reported, but the sources themselves are clearly identified.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 5-fold cross-validation with deliberately non-random fold assignment: samples sorted by slice count and thickness so test volumes are dissimilar to training data, explicitly framed as a worst-case clinical simulation. Clear and well-reasoned.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth is inherited from the challenge datasets. No description of annotation procedures, annotator expertise, or inter-rater agreement anywhere in the paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort. All evaluation is internal 5-fold CV on the same two public datasets; the stratified folds simulate out-of-distribution data but do not constitute external validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Modifications are precisely stated (nnU-Net: instance norm, LeakyReLU slope 1e-2; MS-D Net: dilated multi-scale convolutions, same activation change) and ensemble construction (top-5 per architecture by validation score) is described, but full specifications (depth, filter counts, level configuration) are deferred to the cited nnU-Net and MS-D papers.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Strong: ADAM (defaults per Kingma & Ba), loss weights (0.6/0.4, smooth=1e-5), batch sizes (28 for 2D, 1 for 3D), augmentation application rates (80-90% of batches, 20% CWVRS), 16-slice input, 128x128 downsampling, TensorFlow 1.14, hardware specified, plus Algorithm 1. Missing: number of epochs and learning-rate schedule.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Tanimoto loss explicitly justified for class imbalance (treats classes independently), formula given, smooth factor (1e-5) discussed with citation; combined with categorical crossentropy at stated weights (0.6/0.4).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described: percentile-based HU windowing (0.6-0.99, radiologist organ window), z-score normalization from a random data subset (with clinical rationale), 16-slice random sampling, downsampling, and CTIA augmentations (CWVRS, rotation <=16 deg, Gaussian noising, slice skipping/interpolation) with base windows in Supplementary Table S1. Postprocessing: none reported.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release. Data Availability section only points to the arXiv preprint (1907.10132).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice score only. No IoU, Hausdorff distance, ASSD, or any other segmentation metric; mean +/- std of Dice is the sole reported outcome.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests. Mean +/- std across folds is reported and std-reduction claims are made descriptively ('order of magnitude'), but no formal statistical comparison of CTIA vs MIA is performed.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Systematic internal comparison across 2 architectures x 2 dimensionalities x 2 augmentation schemes plus ensemble (10 configurations), using the DeepMind multidimensional augmentation as a SOTA baseline. However, no comparison against published external SOTA results on KiTS19 or CHAOS (challenge leaderboards, original nnU-Net results).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Separate result tables for kidney (kidney, tumor, and total Dice) and liver, broken down per architecture, dimensionality, and augmentation scheme, each with mean +/- std.

Q15_limitations.justification: Failure modes are well discussed with figures (Fig. 4, Fig. 5): errors on first/last ROI slices, small ROIs, and small/disconnected tumors; percentile adjustment per task acknowledged. But no dedicated limitations section; dataset size, lack of external validation, and single-metric evaluation are not acknowledged as limitations.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate: public challenge data avoids single-center recruitment bias, but patient selection criteria and demographics are not described (inherited from challenges), and folds are intentionally stratified by slice count/thickness rather than randomized - a deliberate worst-case design, but non-standard and makes comparison to randomized-split baselines imperfect.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: identical preprocessing, training procedure, and Dice-based evaluation applied uniformly across all 10 configurations; windowing-vs-no-windowing comparability explicitly addressed via matched crops (Supplementary Tables S2-S3).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate: all configurations reported with mean +/- std, but only one metric (Dice) is reported, inference/training times are absent, CHAOS CT subset size is unspecified, and no external benchmark numbers are reported for context.

detailed_extraction: Training details not in main extraction: batch size 28 (2D) vs 1, i.e. SGD-style (3D); augmentation applied to 80% of 3D batches and 90% of 2D batches, with cluster-wise voxel intensity range shift (CWVRS) on 20% of data in both cases; random rotation max 16 degrees; Gaussian image noising; slice skipping and slice interpolation; CWVRS shifts pre-defined radiological intensity windows (Supplementary Table S1). Z-score statistics computed from a random data subset rather than the full set, deliberately mimicking clinical conditions where only a subset precedes training. Volume reduction to 16 randomly sampled non-background slices doubles as augmentation via resampling; authors report no gain from more slices, consistent with limited semantic context usage in CNNs. 512x512->128x128 downsampling for GPU memory; larger inputs gave no performance benefit. Ensemble construction: kidney task stacks 3D MS-D Nets trained binary (kidney vs background, no tissue/tumor distinction) with 2D nnU-Nets trained 3-class (healthy/tumor/background); liver task stacks two binary models; top-5 per set selected by validation score. Ablations: no-windowing experiment with matched crops (Supplementary Tables S2-S3); qualitative finding that windowing reduces epochs to convergence by suppressing irrelevant anatomy. Error analysis: 3D MS-D Net has fewer background errors but poor fine foreground (kidney vs tumor) discrimination; MS-D errors are complementary to nnU-Net errors, motivating the stack; 2D vs 3D results confirm 3D offers no advantage on anisotropic data (citing Baumgartner 2017, Isensee 2017). CTIA baseline is DeepMind Health's multidimensional image augmentation for TensorFlow (ref 27). Clinical motivation: existing nephometry scores have poor predictive power; robustness (low std) prioritized over peak accuracy because errors go undetected in (semi-)automated downstream workflows. Manuscript received 5 Feb 2020, accepted 4 June 2020; CC BY 4.0 license.
contribution_summary: The paper introduces a domain-specific CT preprocessing and augmentation framework (radiologist-oriented HU windowing plus CT-specific augmentation: cluster-wise intensity range shift, slice skipping/interpolation, Gaussian noising, bounded rotation) that plugs into existing CNN pipelines and improves robustness rather than raw accuracy: it matches the Dice of general-purpose multidimensional augmentation while reducing Dice standard deviation by roughly an order of magnitude across samples. Validated architecture-independently on modified nnU-Net and MS-D Net in 2D and 3D on KiTS19 (kidney/tumor) and CHAOS (liver), with a stacked ensemble of 3D MS-D + 2D nnU-Net (top-5 selection per family) achieving the best results (liver 0.980, kidney total 0.947, tumor 0.845). The central message is that encoding radiological workflow priors into data handling - not architecture changes - is the key lever for clinically reliable, low-variance segmentation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 1006 internal patients (530 men, 476 women) — 12x larger than the commonly used NIH-82 benchmark and far exceeding the >50 subject threshold; one of the largest pancreas CT segmentation cohorts reported to date, plus 82 external scans.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Internal dataset thoroughly characterized: Gil Medical Center, retrospective 2016–2019 health check-up cohort, SOMATOM Definition Edge (Siemens) scanner, 80–150 kVp, 52–641 mA, 3–5 mm slice thickness, 0.58–0.97 mm pixel spacing, IRB number (GDIRB2020-121), explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, and full demographics table (age, sex, BMI, comorbidities, pancreas volume). External NIH TCIA pancreas-CT dataset properly cited.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Fourfold cross-validation is stated for the internal data (folds with 'almost identical numbers of participants', Fig. 1b), but fold construction details are vague. The external TCIA split is described as 'ratio of 10:5:5 for fourfold cross validation', which is internally ambiguous/contradictory (10:5:5 sums to 20, inconsistent with fourfold logic). No held-out test set distinct from CV.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Gold standard generated by manual 2D axial-plane delineation in ImageJ v1.52a, with the caveat that delineation preceded volume reconstruction (CT and mask co-registered). However, annotator expertise, number of raters, consensus procedure, and inter-/intra-rater reliability are not reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Genuine external validation on the independent NIH Clinical Center TCIA pancreas-CT dataset (n=82), a different institution and scanner profile, with separately reported precision/recall/DSC and volumetry metrics.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Good architectural overview: 3D U-Net backbone, skip connections, batch norm, 4 resolution steps, 3x3x3 kernels, dilation (1,1,1), ReLU, 3D upsample (not transposed conv) decoder, parameter counts per variant (e.g., 47,074,657 for Residual Dense U-Net), and architecture figure. However, per-stage filter/channel widths, dense-block growth rates, and block-internal layer counts are not specified, preventing exact reimplementation from text alone.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Key settings reported (Adam, lr=0.001, batch size 2, 500 epochs, Keras 2.2.5/TF-GPU 1.15.4, Python 3.6.12, Tesla V100 32GB). Missing: learning-rate schedule, early-stopping criteria, data augmentation policy (none mentioned), random seeds, per-fold results, and no code release.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss is named but never justified; no discussion of why it was chosen over cross-entropy, combined losses, or alternatives suited to the extreme class imbalance of a small organ like the pancreas.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Unusually detailed pipeline: voxel-spacing unification to (3,1,1) mm, simultaneous CT+mask reconstruction, ROI cropping with pancreas-shape-adaptive margin ratio z:y:x=1:2:3, bilinear resizing to (64,128,256,1), windowing (center 60 / width 400), CLAHE contrast enhancement; postprocessing described (spacing restoration, 0.5 probability thresholding).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model repository provided; data availability statement explicitly declines public release of the internal dataset (IRB restriction).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Segmentation: DSC, precision, recall (with SDs). Volumetry: Bland–Altman agreement, regression R², Pearson R, ICC, and mean volume differences (1.67 cm³ internal; 2.34 cm³ external) — clinically relevant evaluation beyond overlap metrics.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired t-tests (α=0.05) between the proposed network and all three baselines (all p<0.05), ICC, correlation/regression analyses with p<0.001, Bland–Altman with ±1.96 SD coefficient of repeatability, MedCalc 14.8.1 used. Minor gap: no confidence intervals and some assessments performed in 2D axial plane rather than 3D.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Internal comparison covers four U-Net variants, but external SOTA comparison is only indirect: cited published NIH-82 DSC values (0.866, 0.854, 0.859) without head-to-head re-evaluation under matched conditions; notably their external DSC (0.735) falls below these cited baselines, and the discrepancy (their models trained on 3mm-thick internal data vs. external 1.5–2.5mm) is not experimentally resolved.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ (pancreas) study, so organ-level reporting is complete by construction; additionally provides volume-stratified DSC (four PV subgroups with n=54/361/441/150), separate internal vs. external results, and per-network breakdowns — above-average granularity.

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid, thorough limitations: manual ROI cropping (semi-automated only, due to GPU/RAM limits), external performance drop attributed to slice-thickness mismatch, single-center healthy-Korean cohort lacking racial/age/volume diversity, and failure analysis of 36 outliers (32 underestimations vs. 4 overestimations, mostly in >90 cm³ pancreata with blurred boundaries/low soft-tissue density).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Inclusion/exclusion criteria explicit (no prior pancreatectomy, no benign/malignant pancreatic tumor); consecutive retrospective single-center cohort 2016–2019. However, restricting to healthy health-checkup participants limits the anatomical/pathological spectrum, and all participants are Korean, limiting generalizability to diseased or ethnically diverse populations.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All four networks trained and evaluated under identical preprocessing, fourfold CV, and the same gold standard with a fixed 0.5 threshold; standardized volumetric statistics applied uniformly.
