Caveats: the ROI is cropped using the ground-truth mask (a manual step applied uniformly, but one that would not exist in deployment), and some statistical assessment was performed on 2D axial slices rather than 3D volumes.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate. All four network results reported, including unfavorable external validation (DSC 0.735) and outlier analysis — indicating selective-outcome resistance. However, no per-fold variance, no confidence intervals, code/data unavailable for verification, and minor numeric inconsistencies exist between text and tables (528/475 men/women in text vs. 530/476 in Table 1; mean pancreas volume 66.5 cm³ in text vs. 62.6±19.0 in Table 1), suggesting imperfect reporting rigor.

detailed_extraction: ETHICS/PROVENANCE: IRB-approved (GDIRB2020-121), Declaration of Helsinki compliant, written informed consent obtained; single-center retrospective cohort. ACQUISITION: SOMATOM Definition Edge (Siemens, Germany); 80–150 kVp; 52–641 mA; internal slice thickness 3–5 mm; pixel spacing 0.58–0.97 mm; external NIH-TCIA slice thickness 1.5–2.5 mm (identified as the primary domain-shift factor). SPLIT DETAILS: Internal 4-fold CV with approximately equal participant counts per fold; external TCIA split stated as 10:5:5 for 'fourfold' cross-validation (specification ambiguous). FULL MODEL COMPARISON (internal): Basic U-Net — 11,003,073 params, DSC 0.822±0.143; Dense U-Net — 35,261,601 params, DSC 0.831±0.134; Residual U-Net — 2,350,857 params, DSC 0.808±0.146; Residual Dense U-Net — 47,074,657 params, DSC 0.842±0.128; all paired t-test differences vs. best model significant (p<0.05). External Residual Dense U-Net: precision 0.779±0.204, recall 0.749±0.226, DSC 0.735±0.197 (high per-case variance). PARAMETER–PERFORMANCE OBSERVATION: authors claim segmentation performance scales with trainable parameter count (Residual Dense > Dense > Basic > Residual). VOLUMETRY: internal R²=0.954, R=0.977, ICC=0.987, mean diff 1.67 cm³; external R²=0.667, R=0.817, ICC=0.894, mean diff 2.34 cm³; 32 under-/4 over-estimation outliers out of 1006, concentrated in PV>90 cm³ (blurred boundaries, low soft-tissue density); agreement within ±1.96 SD coefficient of repeatability. VOLUME SUBGROUP n: <30 cm³=54, 30–60=361, 60–90=441, ≥90=150. TOOLS: ImageJ 1.52a (annotation, 2D axial), 3D Slicer 4.11.20200930 (visualization), MedCalc 14.8.1 (statistics). TRAINING: Adam lr=0.001, batch 2, 500 epochs, dice loss; no augmentation, no LR schedule, no early stopping reported. KEY METHODOLOGICAL CAVEAT: semi-automated — the ROI crop derives from the gold-standard manual delineation, meaning the network never localizes the pancreas; clinical deployment would require an additional detection/localization stage. REPORTING INCONSISTENCIES: text vs. Table 1 discrepancies in sex counts (528/475 vs. 530/476) and mean pancreas volume (66.5 vs. 62.6 cm³); 'statistical assessment was performed on 2D axial plane' while volumetry used 3D — evaluation plane inconsistency. FUNDING: Gachon University College of Medicine, Gil Medical Center, GRRC Gyeonggi (GRRC Gachon 2017-B01), Gachon Program; no competing interests; article CC-BY 4.0. NOTABLE FOR REVIEW CONTEXT: this is a single-organ (pancreas) study; the 1006-patient scale is exceptional relative to typical pancreas DL studies (NIH-82), but architectural novelty is limited to standard block substitution within the 3D U-Net family.
contribution_summary: This study delivers one of the largest-scale clinical validations of deep-learning pancreas segmentation (1,006 abdominal CTs vs. the de facto standard NIH-82), systematically comparing four 3D U-Net variants and identifying the residual dense U-Net as the best performer (DSC 0.842 internal; 0.735 external on NIH TCIA) with clinically reliable volumetry (ICC 0.987 internal). Its principal contributions are large-cohort evidence that segmentation quality and volumetric agreement are achievable on healthy populations, volume-stratified performance analysis, and explicit demonstration of the internal–external generalization gap driven by slice-thickness domain shift. The approach remains semi-automated (manual ROI cropping) and the contribution is validation/methodological rather than a novel architecture.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Pipeline trained on >220 abdominal CT scans total (>90 for V-net from Cancer Imaging Archive Pancreas-CT + BTCV; >130 for H-DenseUnet from LiTS), exceeding the >50 subject threshold. Caveat: authors assembled pretrained components from prior works rather than curating/training a new dataset.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: All data sources explicitly named with citations (SLIVER07, 3DIRCADb, Pancreas-TCIA, BTCV, LiTS) and access URLs provided for test sets (sliver07.grand-challenge.org; ircad.fr). Test cohort demographics partially described (3DIRCADb: 20 scans, 10M/10F, 75% with hepatic tumors; SLIVER07: 20 scans, mostly diseased livers, contrast-enhanced).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No own train/validation/test split is described — authors evaluate pretrained components on two public benchmarks. Test sets are clearly identified with reference segmentations, but there is no explicit statement that benchmark data was excluded from component training, no validation set for the ascites-threshold ROC tuning, and no internal split methodology.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth consists of official challenge reference/'gold standard' manual segmentations (SLIVER07, 3DIRCADb), which are well-established, but the annotation process itself (annotator expertise, protocol, inter-rater agreement) is not described. Institutional multiphase scan ground truth not described at all.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Validated on two external public benchmarks (SLIVER07, 3DIRCADb) whose sources (grand challenge/IRCAD) are distinct from component training data (BTCV, TCIA Pancreas-CT, LiTS), plus 3 institutional multiphase CT scans for ascites testing. Independence is inferable from the original component papers' training sets, though never explicitly declared by the authors.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Both architectures summarized in detail (V-net: 144³ input, dense feature stacks, spatial prior, 9 classes; H-DenseUnet: 224×224×12 input, 2D+3D DenseUnet with Hybrid Fusion, ~80M params) with full layer-level details deferred to Supplementary Tables S1–S2. Cascade logic and inter-network data flow clearly specified.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Training hardware/duration reported (V-net: 6h Titan X Pascal; H-DenseUnet: 30h on 2×Titan Xp) and full code + Docker image released, but key hyperparameters absent: optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, augmentation policy, and data used for ascites-threshold ROC optimization are unspecified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Both loss functions given as equations (probabilistic Dice with L2 regularization + spatial prior for V-net, Eq. 1; weighted cross-entropy over background/lesion/liver for H-DenseUnet, Eq. 3), but the choices are inherited from the original component papers and not independently justified (e.g., class-imbalance rationale for weighting not discussed).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Exceptionally detailed: orientation standardization (90° rotation + vertical reflection), DICOM/MHD→NIfTI conversion, bounding-box cropping/resizing, ROC-optimized 15 HU ascites threshold, morphological opening (disk r=2, Eq. 2), 1500-px area filter; post-processing chain (slice truncation, <0 HU exclusion, largest-component filter, closing disk r=2 and sphere r=3, hole filling) fully parameterized.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Full code base on GitHub (github.com/neemajamshidi/PADLLS) plus ready-to-run Docker image (Docker Hub: jaysen20/siml-liver-net); explicitly released as a free tool. License terms not stated.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Six metrics with formulas: Dice, VOE, RVD, ASD, RMSD, and Hausdorff distance (Eqs. 5–10), all reported with mean ± SD on both benchmarks.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Welch's t-tests with explicit p-values for all head-to-head comparisons (e.g., vs H-DenseUnet: p=0.0219 SLIVER07, p=0.0014 3DIRCADb), pre-defined significance criterion (p<0.05), mean ± SD dispersion, boxplots (Fig. 6), and an ablation of the ascites correction with significance testing (p=0.0008 3DIRCADb; p=0.170 NS SLIVER07). Confidence intervals not reported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Direct re-evaluation of constituent SOTA models (V-net, H-DenseUnet) on identical test data with paired statistics, plus a comparison table against ~14 published methods on 3DIRCADb/LiTS (U-Net+GAN, Dial-3DResUNet, DFS U-Net, MSN-Net, DALU-Net, mU-Net etc.). Caveat: literature comparisons are cross-study with heterogeneous protocols and some rows lack SDs, precluding significance testing.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver only), so per-organ breakdown is trivially inapplicable; per-benchmark means with per-case SDs and boxplots are given, and intermediate component-wise (V-net vs pipeline stage) results are provided, but no subgroup analysis by pathology (tumor vs cyst vs ascites burden) or organ-adjacent structure breakdown.

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid limitations section: degraded performance with significant pathology/post-operative anatomy (cirrhotic contours, fatty liver, mass detection), heavy computational cost of cascading (~80M params, 64.3 min/case on 8GB GPU vs 8.4M-param Dial-3DResUNet), unverified clinical/radiomics utility. Qualitative failure examples (ascites/spleen oversegmentation by components) illustrated in Figs. 3–4.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate concern. Test cohorts are well-defined public benchmarks, but all data are contrast-enhanced CT from limited cohorts (n=20 per benchmark; n=3 institutional multiphase scans with selection criteria not described); disease spectrum narrow — cirrhosis, fatty liver, and post-surgical anatomy explicitly acknowledged as underrepresented/challenging.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low concern. All methods (V-net, H-DenseUnet, PADLLS) evaluated on identical test sets against the same reference segmentations using standardized metric definitions. Minor concerns: dataset used for ROC optimization of the 15 HU ascites threshold is unspecified (possible tuning optimism), and literature comparisons in Table 4 use non-uniform protocols.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low concern. All planned metrics reported with dispersion for every benchmark; inability to compute significance for some literature rows transparently flagged with dashes. Minor internal inconsistencies noted (ROC threshold sweep described as 0–30 HU in text vs 0–50 HU in Fig. 2 caption; WW/WL labels in figure captions appear swapped); no evidence of selective outcome reporting.

detailed_extraction: STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective, fully automated single-center methodological study; no novel architecture — contribution is a cascade (PADLLS) composing pretrained Dense V-net (Gibson et al.) and H-DenseUNet (Li et al.) with knowledge-based heuristics. ETHICS: UCLA IRB #10-001869 with waiver of informed consent; Declaration of Helsinki compliance stated. PIPELINE DETAILS: (1) Standardization: 90° clockwise rotation + vertical-axis reflection; DICOM/MHD→NIfTI conversion (SLIVER07 RAW/MHD first converted to DICOM). (2) Stage 1 Dense V-net: 144×144×144 input; 9 classes (background + pancreas, esophagus, duodenum, stomach, liver, spleen, left kidney, gallbladder); probabilistic Dice L2 loss (Eq. 1) with explicit spatial prior from Gibson's prior work; ~12M params; V-net liver mask defines the H-DenseUNet bounding box (resized to 224×224×12); stomach and spleen voxels overwritten to −100 HU to block downstream oversegmentation. (3) Ascites correction: binary mask of voxels <15 HU (threshold ROC-optimized; selected at curve peak, consistent with simple-fluid attenuation 5–15 HU); morphological opening with disk r=2 (Eq. 2); area filter retaining objects >1500 px; masked voxels set to −100 HU. NOTE: text states sweep 0–30 HU with 1-HU steps between 10–20 HU; Fig. 2 caption states 0–50 HU in 5-HU steps — internal inconsistency. (4) Stage 2 H-DenseUNet: 224×224×12 input; 2D DenseUNet on 224×224×3 stacks; 2D outputs concatenated with 3D volume into 3D DenseUNet; Hybrid Fusion layer; weighted cross-entropy (Eq. 3) over background/lesion/liver; ~80M params. (5) Post-processing: truncate to liver-containing slices; remove <0 HU voxels (lung at hepatic dome); largest-connected-component volume filter; image closing disk r=2 then sphere r=3 (Eq. 4); hole filling; liver+tumor masks unioned. ABLATION: ascites correction improves 3DIRCADb Dice 0.926→0.965 (p=0.0008) and SLIVER07 0.940→0.957 (p=0.170, NS) — attributed to higher ascites prevalence in 3DIRCADb. EFFICIENCY: PADLLS 64.30 min/case on 8GB Quadro RTX4000 vs 162 s/case on Hoffman2 cluster V100 (32GB); V-net alone 4.44 s/case; parameter asymmetry H-DenseUNet ~80M vs V-net ~12M vs Dial-3DResUNet ~8.4M highlighted as accuracy-vs-cost trade-off. EVALUATION CORPUS: 2823 slices (3DIRCADb) and 4159 slices (SLIVER07); display settings per figure: Fig.3 WW/WL 30/150, Fig.4 350/40, Fig.5 400/50. FUNDING: NIH NCATS/NIBIB UCLA CTSI KL2TR001882; CC BY 4.0 open access. GAPS/CAVEATS FOR REVIEW: no internal train/val/test split or cross-validation; no confidence intervals; no independent ablation isolating stomach/spleen-removal from ascites-correction contributions; institutional ascites test set very small (n=3) without described ground truth; component training sets inferred from prior papers — possible (unstated) train-test overlap not formally excluded; code license unspecified. Cross-study Table 4 comparisons (e.g., Dial-3DResUNet 0.958, mU-Net, MSN-Net 0.942) are not head-to-head re-runs.
contribution_summary: This paper introduces PADLLS, a fully automated cascading pipeline that chains a Dense V-net and an H-DenseUNet with knowledge-based heuristics — V-net-derived stomach/spleen mask removal (voxels set to −100 HU), a ROC-optimized 15 HU ascites threshold with morphological filtering, and an extensive post-processing chain — specifically to combat oversegmentation, the dominant failure mode of its constituent networks. On public benchmarks it achieves Dice 0.957 ± 0.033 (SLIVER07) and 0.965 ± 0.016 (3DIRCADb), statistically significantly outperforming both H-DenseUNet and V-net, and reduces ascites-case VOE from 22.99%/51.01% (V-net/H-DenseUNet) to 12.45%. The main trade-offs are high computational cost (~80M parameters, ~64 min/case on an 8GB GPU) and unvalidated performance on pathological livers, but the method is notable for its open-source release (GitHub + Docker) targeting radiomics/radiogenomics workflows.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 75 training patients (>50 threshold); 155 examinations total across development (95 DECT) and two external test sets (30 DECT + 30 SECT); 20,020 annotated PVP slices. Modest by nnU-Net standards but adequate for 5 organs.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Exemplary detail: two DECT scanners with patient counts (SOMATOM Force n=49, IQon n=46), acquisition window (Apr–Sep 2020), explicit inclusion criteria (healthy asymptomatic adults, no focal lesions except small cysts), three SECT scanners for external testing, acquisition parameters in Supplementary Table 1, scan coverage specified (dome to ASIS/upper thigh).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit random assignment 75/10/10 (train/val/internal test) plus two temporally independent external test sets (Jan–Feb 2021) from different scanners. No k-fold CV, but split methodology fully transparent.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Clear pipeline: commercial MEDIP PRO v2.4.0 pre-segmentation, then voxel-wise manual correction by board-certified abdominal radiologist (9 years experience). VNC labels transferred via spatiotemporal matching from DE-PVP; TNC labels generated referencing same patient's PVP. Minor gap: single annotator, no inter-rater reliability reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Two independent external test sets: 30 temporally separate DECT exams (different time period) and 30 SECT exams from three different vendors (GE, Siemens, Philips) — the SECT set tests both scanner and reconstruction-type generalization (DECT-trained → SECT inference).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D nnU-Net (standard self-configuring framework, cited) with clearly described novel modification: body-composition algorithm output (7-class internal organ areas) as input, 5 organ classes as output; patch size, target spacing, and Fig. 1 provided. Internal U-Net stage details inherited from nnU-Net auto-configuration.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (SGD, Nesterov momentum 0.99), LR schedule (polynomial, init 0.01), epochs (1000), batch size (2), patch size (160×160×64), spacing, and augmentation list all stated. Minor gaps: DL framework and GPU hardware not reported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice + cross-entropy loss stated but no rationale given; it is the nnU-Net default rather than a justified choice. Strict reading of 'justified' would score 0.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing fully described (resampling to 0.668×0.668×2 mm, patching, augmentation). Postprocessing entirely unaddressed — unclear whether none was performed or simply omitted; nnU-Net normally applies automatic postprocessing, so this is a reproducibility gap.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code/model availability statement; depends on commercial MEDIP PRO software for both annotation and the upstream body-composition algorithm. Not reproducible without commercial licenses.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC plus organ-volume ICC (with 95% CIs), Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman bias/LOA, and % of cases within 10% volume deviation. Segmentation quality linked to clinical endpoint (volumetry).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Thorough: paired t-tests (phase comparison), Mann-Whitney U/Kruskal-Wallis (scanner comparison), 95% CIs on ICCs, Bland-Altman LOAs, predefined accuracy thresholds, MedCalc 19.4.0. Wide CIs on some ICCs (n=30) are honestly reported, e.g., LK TNC ICC 0.970 (0.454–0.993).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Discussion-only comparison against published DSC ranges (liver 0.93–0.97, spleen 0.92–0.96, kidney 0.86–0.97) claiming parity with best prior work. No head-to-head experimental baseline on their own data — notably, vanilla nnU-Net without the body-composition-input modification is absent, so the claimed efficiency/FP-reduction benefit is unvalidated.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-organ × per-phase × per-dataset DSC table (Table 1), per-organ ICC table with CIs (Table 2), per-organ Bland-Altman plots and volumetry accuracy counts. Pancreas weak spots reported with exact numbers.

Q15_limitations.justification: Pancreas failure mode quantified candidly: DSC 0.81–0.87 externally, ICC 0.792–0.890, only 56.7–73.3% of cases within 10% volume accuracy, systematic overestimation bias. Harder non-contrast task acknowledged. Dedicated limitations section likely in truncated text portion.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low risk for internal validity — inclusion/exclusion criteria explicit and random split assignment. However, restricted spectrum: only healthy asymptomatic adults without focal lesions (except small cysts), single institution. Generalizability to pathological abdomens (large tumors, post-surgical anatomy, organ deformation) is untested and is a spectrum limitation rather than selection bias per se.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low risk — identical ground-truth correction process applied to all datasets, same metrics computed uniformly across phases/scanners by blinded comparison of algorithm masks vs. GT masks. The upstream body-composition algorithm introduces a fixed, deterministic input dependency applied identically to all cases.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low risk — all organs, all phases, all three datasets reported including unfavorable pancreas results with exact failure rates; scanner-level comparisons reported in supplement. Residual concern: no protocol registration, truncated text prevents full verification, and no code release to verify reported numbers.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details not in primary extraction: (1) Volumetry precision — DECT test set mean biases (95% LOA): liver −0.4% (−1.9,1.1), spleen 0% (−4.3,4.3), RK −1.6% (−5.3,2.1), LK −2.0% (−6.2,2.2), pancreas +6.8% (−14.7,28.4) in DE-PVP; 100% of liver/spleen/RK/LK cases within 10% deviation in DECT test set (both phases), >90% in SECT test set, but pancreas only 56.7% (DE-PVP), 60.0% (VNC), 56.7% (SE-PVP), 73.3% (TNC). Pancreas volume systematically overestimated in PVP images (+6.8% to +11.3% bias). (2) Internal training test set DSCs: 0.976/0.963/0.954/0.954/0.879 (DE-PVP) and 0.974/0.959/0.945/0.950/0.849 (VNC). (3) Phase effect: post-contrast DSC significantly higher than non-contrast for all organs in external sets (p<0.001) but NOT significant in the internal training test set — suggesting VNC-label transfer introduces minimal phase penalty. (4) Ethics: IRB-approved retrospective study, informed consent waived. (5) Label-efficiency claim: 20,020 training slices derive from 85 exams because each DECT exam yields two training images (DE-PVP + VNC) sharing one annotation. (6) Upstream dependency: body-composition algorithm (ref 14) itself achieves DSC>0.94 on 7 body components; downstream performance is conditional on it, and no ablation isolates its contribution. (7) External DECT test set balanced across vendors (Force n=15, IQon n=15); no significant scanner effect (p>0.05). (8) Wide ICC confidence intervals in SECT TNC set (n=30) — e.g., liver 0.985 (0.772–0.996), LK 0.970 (0.454–0.993) — indicate volumetry agreement estimates are imprecise at this sample size. (9) Fixed inference-time-reduction and false-positive-reduction rationale for the two-stage input design is asserted but never measured (no inference time or FP counts reported). (10) Literature positioning: prior non-contrast CT results were substantially lower (spleen DSC 0.62 in ref 22; liver 0.86–0.95), making the 0.944–0.965 TNC performance the main differentiator.
contribution_summary: The key contribution is a phase-agnostic 3D nnU-Net multi-organ segmenter (liver, spleen, both kidneys, pancreas) trained efficiently by exploiting DECT: ground-truth masks annotated on portal-venous-phase images are reused on spatiotemporally matched virtual non-contrast images, yielding one algorithm valid on both contrast-enhanced and true non-contrast CT. The architecture feeds predicted internal-organ regions from a body-composition model into nnU-Net to cut inference cost and false positives, and achieves DSC >0.94 for four organs and reliable volumetry (ICC >0.95, >90% within 10% error) across external DECT and cross-vendor SECT test sets — though the pancreas lags (DSC ~0.81–0.87, ~57–73% volumetric accuracy). Main evidence gaps: no code release, no ablation against vanilla nnU-Net, and the dual-input design's claimed efficiency gains are asserted rather than measured.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 3031 internal CTs (2579 train/val, 452 test) plus 585 external AbdomenCT-1K and 80 NIH-PCT; largest single-institution pancreas CT dataset reported, far exceeding the >50 threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources fully described: Mayo Clinic RIS portal venous CTs with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (artifact, contrast quality), demographics (mean age 56.8±16.8, 46% M/54% F), vendor/thickness breakdown (Table 1); AbdomenCT-1K composition (12 centers, 5 constituent subsets) detailed.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random split into 2579 train/validation and 452 test; 5-fold CV within training; Table 1 confirms no significant demographic/acquisition differences between subsets (p>0.05).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process well described: five fellowship-trained abdominal radiologists (3-5 yrs experience), standardized protocol, 3D Slicer v4.11 with NVIDIA boundary-points segmentation module; single-reader workflow choice explicitly justified against multi-reader alternatives.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Two independent external validations: multi-institutional AbdomenCT-1K (n=585, newly created expert ground truth, to be released publicly) and NIH-PCT (n=80, independent pre-existing annotations).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D nnU-Net v2 with dynamic self-configuration clearly described, including underlying 3D U-Net encoder-decoder structure with skip connections; exact auto-configured instance (patch size, filter counts) inherited deterministically from the public package rather than enumerated.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partially reproducible: nnunet-V2 package, 5-fold × 1000 epochs, SGD with Nesterov momentum, polynomial LR decay, augmentation suite, and hardware (GV100 32GB) stated; but initial LR, batch size, patch size, random seeds not enumerated and no code or model weights released. Reproduction relies entirely on unmodified public nnU-Net defaults.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Combined Dice + cross-entropy (nnU-Net default) with explicit justification: trade-off between volumetric overlap and voxel-level classification accuracy.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Clearly described: DICOM de-identification (Clinical Trial Processor), NIfTI conversion, portal venous phase verification by radiologists, artifact-based exclusion, nnU-Net automatic preprocessing; postprocessing via nnU-Net built-in steps plus 5-fold ensemble soft voting (voxel-wise probability averaging) fully specified.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or trained model weights released; only AbdomenCT-1K ground-truth segmentations promised publicly. Internal data available only on request with IRB approval.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC, Hausdorff Distance, Concordance Correlation Coefficient, and Bland-Altman volume agreement (mean difference, limits of agreement) — exceeds the Dice+1 minimum.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: SDs reported for all metrics; Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, and Fisher exact tests; significance vs TotalSegmentator (p<0.001); stratified analyses by vendor, slice thickness, gender (p=0.06-0.72). No explicit confidence intervals, but statistical software and tests named (R 4.0.4, scipy 1.8.0).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Head-to-head comparison against TotalSegmentator on both internal and external test sets (DSC 0.89 vs 0.94/0.96, p<0.001), ablation against best individual fold model, and contextual comparison against published DSC range (0.65-0.91).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study; organ-level DSC reported per dataset (0.94 internal, 0.96 AbdomenCT-1K, 0.87 NIH-PCT) with additional stratified subgroup results (Table 2). Per-organ reporting is trivially satisfied; no aggregation obscures results.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated failure analysis of bottom 5th-percentile DSC cases (23 internal, 30 external) categorized as under/over-segmentation with anatomical causes (head-duodenum interface, fatty atrophy, poor fat planes); explicit limitations section covering selection bias, normal-pancreas-only scope, vendor skew, single-reader ground truth.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate concern, disclosed. Retrospective single-institution design; 'normal pancreas' determined from radiology reports (minor incidental findings inconsistently documented); exclusions for motion/streak artifact and poor contrast; heavy vendor skew (75% Siemens). Authors acknowledge and partially mitigate via external validation on multi-vendor, multi-institution data.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low concern. Standardized annotation protocol, identical evaluation pipeline and metrics applied consistently across internal test, AbdomenCT-1K, and NIH-PCT; reference standard weakness (single-reader annotations, no inter-reader variability quantified) is acknowledged but applies uniformly to all compared methods.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low concern. All outcomes reported including unfavorable ones (NIH-PCT DSC 0.87 with attribution to reference quality, failure-case analyses, ablation showing only modest ensemble gain p=0.58-0.67). Minor gap: training/inference times not reported and no model release, limiting independent verification.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond prior extraction: (1) Cohort: 3031 patients, one CT per individual, mean age 56.8±16.8 yrs; train/val vs test subsets statistically balanced (Table 1). Vendors: Siemens 2266 (75%), Toshiba 469, GE 155, Philips 11, Canon 1. (2) Annotation: 3D Slicer v4.11.0, NVIDIA organ segmentation module boundary-points mode; five radiologists randomly assigned scans; single-reader workflow explicitly defended over STAPLE/multi-reader consensus as impractical at this scale. (3) Ensemble/ablation: five-fold CV, 1000 epochs/fold, soft voting via voxel-wise probability averaging; best single fold achieved DSC 0.94±0.06 (internal) and 0.96±0.05 (AbdomenCT-1K), statistically comparable to ensemble (p=0.58-0.67). (4) Failure analysis: internal test 23 cases below 5th percentile (DSC<0.89), 61% mixed over/under-segmentation; AbdomenCT-1K 30 cases (DSC<0.91), 60% under-segmentation; recurring error sites: pancreatic head-duodenum interface, tail vs jejunum/splenic vessels/stomach; worst illustrated case DSC=0.36 (atrophic pancreas, paucity of peripancreatic fat). (5) Volume agreement: internal predicted 75.8±23.6 cc vs GT 78.2±23.7 cc (p=0.15), mean difference 2.41 cc, LoA -11.5 to 16.3 cc; AbdomenCT-1K 77.7±24.1 vs 79.6±24.4 cc (p=0.22), mean difference 1.85 cc, LoA -6.2 to 9.8 cc. (6) TotalSegmentator HDs: 2.8±4.4 mm (internal), 3.1±5.4 mm (AbdomenCT-1K), both p<0.001 vs proposed. (7) NIH-PCT low performance (0.87) attributed to medical-student-annotated reference quality; authors show cases where model outperforms provided GT. (8) Statistical software R 4.0.4, scipy 1.8.0; IRB protocol 19-003018, HIPAA-compliant, consent waived; funding NIH R01CA272628/R01CA256969 plus foundation grants. (9) Scope restriction: morphologically normal pancreas only, portal venous phase only — deliberate design choice for radiomics-based early PDA detection, not a general pathology segmentation tool.
contribution_summary: Trains a 3D nnU-Net v2 ensemble on the largest single-institution pancreas CT dataset to date (n=3031, radiologist-annotated) and achieves state-of-the-art fully automated pancreas segmentation (DSC 0.94 internal, 0.96 on curated AbdomenCT-1K external set with newly created expert ground truth to be released publicly, significantly outperforming TotalSegmentator). Key contributions are scale, rigorous multi-dataset external validation including clinically oriented volume-agreement analysis (CCC, Bland-Altman), a novel expert-annotated external ground-truth resource, and a systematic failure-mode analysis. The contribution is dataset- and validation-driven rather than architectural novelty; no code or model weights are released.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: ACDC (150) and MMWHS (60 CT + 60 MRI) exceed 50 subjects, but MSD cardiac subset has only 30 cases. Mixed adequacy.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: All three public benchmarks named with providers (King's College London/MSD, ACDC, MMWHS) and access URLs.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 5-fold patient-level cross-validation, each patient in test set exactly once; validation fold used for early stopping and temperature scaling. Ablation variants trained on identical splits.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual annotation stated and 'standard MRI imaging protocols' cited, but no annotator count, expertise, or inter-rater agreement reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No independent external cohort. All evaluation is internal 5-fold CV within the same three benchmarks; CycleGAN synthetic CT is not external validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: per-modality 3D U-Net encoders (16-256 channels), Swin blocks for global context, deformable MHCA (K=4 sampling points, H=8 heads, 3x3x3 offset conv, trilinear interpolation), uncertainty head (ensemble M=3, MC-Dropout T=20, dropout 0.2).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, lr 1e-4, cosine annealing, batch 2, augmentation list, 3 seeds, PyTorch 2.1/CUDA 12.1, T4 GPU all given. Epoch count, early-stopping patience, and training time not reported; code not released.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice + CE with heteroscedastic NLL uncertainty term; brief rationale given for the uncertainty term (penalizes overconfidence) but the Dice+CE choice itself is not justified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Detailed pipeline: 1.25mm3 isotropic resampling (B-spline images, NN labels), z-score, 0.5th-99.5th percentile MRI clipping, 128x128x64 crops, full augmentation list; postprocessing (largest connected component, morphological closing, 0.5 threshold, resample back) also specified.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Code 'obtained by contacting the corresponding author' — not publicly available.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice, IoU, HD95, ASSD, precision, recall, ECE, AURC, EAURC, plus inference time and GPU memory.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired t-tests vs U-Net and Swin on DSC and ASSD for all datasets (p=0.0001-0.028); confidence intervals shown in Fig. 8; 3-seed averaging.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compares against U-Net, nnU-Net, Swin Transformer, TransUNet, SegFormer, Attention U-Net. Caveat: unclear if baselines were retrained under identical conditions.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Only per-dataset averages. No per-structure Dice despite MMWHS annotating 7 structures; per-organ table explicitly absent.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations section: computational overhead (8.5 GB / 190 ms), residual false positives after calibration, limited generalization needing broader validation.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Public benchmark datasets with patient-level 5-fold CV and fixed seeds reduce selection bias; however, only three cardiac benchmarks, one with just 30 cases, and no consecutive clinical cohort.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. Same splits used across variants and consistent metric definitions, but unclear whether the six baselines were retrained under identical conditions. Suspicious result: nnU-Net scores below plain U-Net on all datasets, suggesting potentially unfair/under-tuned baseline comparisons.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Per-organ results omitted despite 7-class MMWHS annotations; code not released, preventing independent verification; some tables internally inconsistent (Table 3 text claims 1.25mm3 optimal while the table shows 1.5mm3 with highest DSC; Table 2 row labels ambiguous).

detailed_extraction: Uncertainty pipeline: ensemble of M=3 models (seeds 42/2023/777), T=20 MC-Dropout passes each (dropout 0.2), predictions averaged over M x T passes; epistemic = inter-model variance, aleatoric = learned heteroscedastic variance exp(s(x)); temperature scaling fitted on validation fold to minimize NLL; uncertainty-based rejection of top 20% uncertain voxels sharply reduces risk (AURC 0.125, EAURC 0.02). Explainability: DeepSHAP with 50 randomly selected normalized training patches as background, computed relative to pre-softmax class logits, patch-wise on 3D volumes then aggregated to full resolution. Synthetic CT: unpaired CycleGAN (cycle-consistency + perceptual loss) generates CT from MRI for ACDC/MSD so all experiments run in a CT+MRI setting; cited SSIM ~0.94 / PSNR ~32 dB figures are from prior literature, not validated in-house for this study. Complexity: full model adds <5M parameters over 3D U-Net (~25M) + Swin encoder (~28M, ~4.5 GFLOPs); inference 185-190 ms FP32 batch-1 (mean of 100 runs), peak 7.8-8.5 GB. Resolution ablation: 1.25mm3 chosen as accuracy/compute trade-off. Only ablation (Table 1) run on MM-WHS; Swin-alone reaches 89.0-89.4 Dice vs 93.2 full system, so part of the gain is attributable to multimodal fusion rather than the deformable MHCA itself. Received 20 Aug 2025, accepted 25 Apr 2026. Reviewer cautions: reference list garbled in places (Attention U-Net mis-cited, SHAP attribution irregular); comparison table values for published baselines may be reimplementations or transcriptions from other papers (unverified); UK Biobank discussed as resource but unused.
contribution_summary: Proposes a multimodal 3D cardiac segmentation framework combining a 3D U-Net backbone, Swin Transformer context encoding, and a novel deformable multi-head cross-attention (learnable 3D voxel offsets, K=4 samples/head) for CT/MRI feature fusion, unified with MC-Dropout + heteroscedastic uncertainty maps and DeepSHAP explainability. Achieves Dice 91.8% (MSD-LA), 92.3% (ACDC), 93.2% (MMWHS), with paired t-test significance over U-Net and Swin baselines, at the cost of ~190 ms inference and 8.5 GB GPU memory. Main gap relative to clinical review standards: no per-organ reporting, no external validation, and no released code.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 489 CT scans used for training/validation via 5-fold CV, far exceeding the >50-subject threshold. Authors note it is still 'small' for deep learning, but it is adequate by this criterion and among the larger single-center renal CT cohorts available.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source fully described: public KiTS23 challenge dataset; patients undergoing cryoablation, partial nephrectomy or radical nephrectomy for suspected renal malignancy (2010-2022) at a single M Health Fairview center; contrast-enhanced preoperative scans in corticomedullary or nephrogenic phase; 599 total scans (489 train / 110 test); ethics waived per dataset license; data link provided.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 5-fold cross-validation explicitly described (shuffle, split into 5 equal parts, 4 train / 1 validation-test, repeated 5 times, new network instance per fold). The challenge-held-out 110-scan test set was inaccessible (no labels), which is transparently disclosed. Metrics computed per fold and averaged.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth is inherited from KiTS23: 'majority vote amongst several readers' for kidney and masses (tumours/cysts) annotations. This is a high-level description only; annotator numbers, expertise, and annotation protocol details reside in challenge publications, not this paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent validation. Only the KiTS23 training subset was used with internal 5-fold CV. Test-set labels were unavailable (analysis done outside the challenge), preventing any held-out validation; authors acknowledge a ~5% performance drop observed by challenge top teams on the true test set.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture exhaustively described and illustrated (Fig. 3): custom sparse 3D U-Net with ConvNeXtV2 blocks, stem layer, 6 encoder stages (features 16-512, depths 2,4,4,8,8,8), 5 decoder stages, 3x3x3 kernels, strided 2x2x2 down/upsampling, element-wise-summation skips, per-stage classification heads (3 sigmoid channels, multi-label), deep supervision on last 3 decoder stages, total 27,473,696 parameters.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Highly reproducible: AdamW (lr 5e-4, wd 1e-5, betas 0.9/0.95), batch size 1 + gradient accumulation 8, 500 epochs/fold (1 warmup + 99 fixed LR + 400 cosine annealing), truncated-normal weight init, deep-supervision weights (1/2^i), Optuna-tuned, exact software versions (PyTorch 2.0.0, MinkowskiEngine v0.5.4 custom fork, MONAI, Python 3.10.5), augmentation pipeline (details in Appendix), and public code repository.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss explicitly justified: target structures (tumours) occupy a small volume fraction causing strong voxel-level class imbalance; Dice loss mitigates background dominance and improves small-lesion sensitivity. Weighted deep-supervision scheme justified for multi-scale gradient propagation. Lack of systematic comparison to alternative losses is acknowledged and deferred to future work.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre/post-processing fully specified: resampling to isotropic 1.99 mm (Stage 1) and 0.78 mm (Stage 2); data-driven HU sparsification via 0.5th/99.5th percentiles of segmentation voxels (-53.4 to 283.2 HU, retaining ~99% of foreground, removing 76.8% of background); ROI probability threshold 0.1, elliptical dilation (11 voxels), removal of components <50 voxels, connected-component splitting into K independently processed crops (>99% of non-background voxels retained); MONAI augmentation suite; explicitly no post-processing on final masks. MONAI-based augmentations listed in Appendix.

Q10_code_availability.justification: All study code publicly available (https://github.com/saulam/ai_cancer_research), including the custom MinkowskiEngine fork with CUDA depth-wise convolution kernels (https://github.com/shwoo93/MinkowskiEngine); data availability via KiTS23 GitHub repo also stated.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Partial. Dice (DSC) is the only segmentation-accuracy metric — notably, no HD95 or other surface-distance metric despite KiTS23 challenges using it. However, the paper adds extensive computational metrics (per-volume inference time and peak VRAM with SDs across CPU and 3 GPU types), and an error analysis by lesion burden. No second segmentation-quality metric (e.g., IoU, sensitivity) is reported.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Partial. Per-fold Dice values for every model and output are tabulated (Table 1) with macro-averages, and timing/VRAM results include standard deviations. However, no confidence intervals on Dice, no paired significance tests (e.g., Wilcoxon/t-test) comparing sparse model vs nnU-Net, and differences (e.g., 85.7% vs 83.7% tumour+cyst) are described only as 'numerically higher'.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Strong comparison design: nnU-Net v2 (retrained on identical 5-fold splits, auto-configured, comparable parameter count 31.2M vs 27.5M), SegVol foundation model (zero-shot, standardized prompts), an architecture-matched dense U-Net implementation, and indirect benchmarking against KiTS23 challenge top teams (their 87.3% 'All' vs reported 87-89% training-set range of top teams).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: All three outputs (kidneys+masses, tumour+cyst, tumour) reported separately, per fold and averaged, for every method (Tables 1-2), plus low- vs high-resolution stage results and a case-level error analysis stratified by lesion volume with per-bin case counts. Kidneys are not split left/right, but all annotated structure categories are individually reported.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated, candid limitations section: small dataset (489 patients); no test-set access preventing leaderboard comparison/generalisability assessment; no post-processing used; no systematic loss-function comparison; single-stage sparse variant not compared; results taken from final (not best-validation) epoch. Complemented by a quantitative failure-mode analysis showing degraded and more variable Dice for small lesion burdens.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low risk. Patient selection is clearly defined by the KiTS23 protocol (single center, 2010-2022, specific treatment cohort, contrast-enhanced phases specified); only the public training subset was used with no ad-hoc exclusions reported. Caveat: single-center origin and the challenge-defined cohort (surgical/cryoablation patients) limit generalisability to broader populations, and no external cohort was tested.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low risk. All methods were evaluated on identical 5-fold CV splits with metrics computed in the same reference space (native KiTS23 voxel grid after mapping predictions back), a consistent metric definition across models, no test-time augmentation, and no best-epoch cherry-picking (final-epoch results reported transparently). Baselines were properly retrained (nnU-Net) or evaluated with documented standardized settings (SegVol zero-shot).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate risk. Unfavorable results are reported openly (kidney+masses below nnU-Net; SegVol's near-failure on lesions; dense-baseline OOM events) and limitations are thoroughly discussed. Minor concerns: the Optuna search space and selected augmentation hyperparameters are not fully enumerated, no statistical significance testing is reported, and the assessment is based on an unedited article-in-press manuscript whose Appendix (augmentation details) was not fully available.

detailed_extraction:
SUPPLEMENTARY DETAILS (not captured in prior extraction):

DATASET: Annotations are the KiTS23 majority-vote-of-several-readers version; ethics approval waived per the open-access dataset license; data at github.com/neheller/kits23. Only the 489-scan training subset accessible; 110-scan test set unavailable.

SPARSIFICATION RATIONALE: HU thresholds (-53.4, 283.2) derived empirically from 0.5th/99.5th percentiles of all kidney+mass voxels (Fig. 2 cumulative distributions); Stage 2 uses ROI cropping rather than HU sparsification. Critically, removing/widening HU filtering makes Stage-1 input nearly dense at full FOV and exceeded memory limits — hence dense ablation is represented by the external architecture-matched dense U-Net, not an ablated sparse variant.

PIPELINE DETAILS: Stage-1 probability threshold 0.1 for any class; MONAI elliptical dilation (11 voxels); Stage-2 removal of components <50 voxels; connected-component analysis splits each scan into K independently processed components; >99% of original non-background voxels retained in crops; final masks mapped back to original scan space. ALL metrics for ALL methods computed in native KiTS23 image space (fair-resolution comparison). Deep-supervision auxiliary targets generated via MinkowskiAvgPooling. On CPU, the custom fork's CUDA depth-wise convs fall back to ME built-in channel-wise convs (identical predictions, less GPU-efficient).

BASELINES (exact configs): nnU-Net v2 3d_fullres PlainConvUNet, 31.2M params, patch 128x128x128, batch 2, spacing (1.0, 0.78, 0.78) mm, 1000 epochs/fold, SGD+Nesterov momentum, sliding-window inference without TTA. SegVol: ViT, 180.9M params, pre-trained on >90,000 CT volumes / 200 categories, zero-shot text prompts 'kidney'/'kidney tumor'/'kidney cyst', zoom-out/zoom-in with 32x256x256 sliding windows, batch size 1 by design.

PER-FOLD RESULTS (Table 1, DSC): Ours high-res: kidneys+masses 0.9526-0.9676 (avg 0.9581); tumour+cyst 0.8313-0.8671 (avg 0.8568); tumour 0.7734-0.8143 (avg 0.8033); macro-avg 0.8728. nnU-Net: 0.9669 / 0.8366 / 0.7965 (avg 0.8666). SegVol zero-shot: 0.9140 / 0.2184 / 0.1953 (avg 0.4426). Ours low-res Stage-1: 0.9487 / 0.7508 / 0.6974 (avg 0.7989).

COMPUTATIONAL RESULTS (Table 2): CPU (Xeon E5-2698 v4): nnU-Net 592.5 s, SegVol 305.9 s, sparse low-res 29-34 s, sparse high-res 33-54 s, dense low-res 48-67 s. GPU: nnU-Net 7.85-7.88 s on A100s but OOM on V100 16GB; SegVol ~1.22-1.24 s on all GPUs at ~2 GB VRAM; sparse high-res 0.29-0.44 s at ~3.3-6.7 GB. Dense U-Net frequently OOMs (V100 all configs; A100 40GB at high-res batch 2). Sparse advantage: 33-60% inference-time reduction, 2-4x lower VRAM (up to 75% reduction).

ERROR ANALYSIS: Dice vs tumour+cyst burden pooled across folds (8 log-sized bins, n=16/69/98/126/96/64/13/7); both sparse model and nnU-Net show lower, more variable Dice for small lesions; sparse model broadly comparable to nnU-Net across size range.

INDIRECT BENCHMARK: Their macro-avg 87.3% lies within top KiTS23 teams' training-set range 87-89%; second-place team ranges 86.5-88.7% (all), 97.3-97.9% (kidney+masses), 84.0-85.8% (tumour+cyst), 77.1-82.6% (tumour) — their results fall within all ranges. Top teams' test-set drop ~5% noted as untestable generalisability gap.

TRANSPARENCY/PROVENANCE NOTES: Results strictly from final training epoch (no best-epoch selection); no post-processing on final masks (unlike top challenge teams); no funding; no conflicts declared; paper is an unedited 'Article in Press' (Accepted 29 Apr 2026) — Appendix with augmentation implementation details referenced but truncated in provided text. Prior extraction gaps: license not stated for code (dataset is open-access licensed); release_version not specified; components/benchmark_reproduction not applicable — baselines retrained/evaluated on identical splits constitutes internal benchmark reproduction.
contribution_summary: This paper reports the first application of submanifold sparse convolutional networks (SSCNs) to 3D CT organ/tumour segmentation, combining Hounsfield-unit-based voxel sparsification with a two-stage sparse U-Net pipeline (low-resolution ROI detection followed by high-resolution segmentation within cropped components). On KiTS23 (5-fold CV), it achieves accuracy competitive with retrained nnU-Net and top KiTS23 challenge teams (Dice 95.8% kidneys+masses, 85.7% tumour+cyst, 80.3% tumour) while reducing inference time by up to 60% and VRAM by up to 75% versus an architecture-matched dense U-Net, enabling full-resolution native 3D inference on 16 GB GPUs. The principal contribution is a resource-efficiency-oriented methodology demonstrating sparse convolutions as a viable alternative to dense/patch-based pipelines in medical imaging, rather than a new state-of-the-art in accuracy.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 60 training volumes per fold technically exceeds the >50 threshold, but this is minimally adequate for a 103M-parameter deep network; the authors themselves identify limited annotated data as a core limitation. Only 80 total volumes, single-center public dataset.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Excellent description: public NIH pancreas dataset (Roth et al./TCIA) of 80 contrast-enhanced abdominal CTs; full demographics (53M/27F, age 18-76, mean 46.8±16.7), clinical composition (17 healthy kidney donors, 63 diseased incl. pancreatic cancer), scanner/vendor (Philips, Siemens MDCT, 120 kVp), and slice thickness (1.5-2.5 mm) all reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Four-fold cross-validation with 60/20 train/test random splits is clearly stated and used consistently for all comparisons. However, no separate validation set is described (unclear how hyperparameters like λ=1, dilation rates, and candidate region size were tuned, creating potential test-set leakage), and no fixed splits/seeds are provided for reproducibility.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process stated: all 80 volumes manually annotated by a medical student and verified by a radiologist. Lacks finer detail (annotation tool, protocol, inter-observer agreement), but the essential annotator/verification chain is described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort validation. All evaluation is internal four-fold CV on a single public dataset.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Comprehensive: DCAE encoder-decoder with adaptive dilated blocks (dilation rates 4 and 8, justified by pancreas size statistics of 10-15 px at layer 5), separable 1x3/3x1 convolutions (~30% memory saving); Local-LSTM with Hilbert-curve patch serialisation (26x26 space, downsampling factor 4) with full LSTM gate equations; discriminator fully specified (three 5x5 conv layers, batch norm, average pooling, two dense layers with dropout). Parameter counts reported (103M vs 296M U-Net, 158M FCN); architecture figures provided.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Mostly reproducible: framework (TensorFlow 1.8.0, Python 2.7), hardware (Titan X, CUDA 9.0, cuDNN 7.0), batch size 5, 200 epochs, optimizers per subnetwork (RMSProp: decay 0.9, momentum 0.9; Adam: β1 0.9, β2 0.999, ε 1e-8), soft-label threshold T=0.01, adversarial weight λ=1. Critical omissions: learning rate not reported, the stated RMSProp ε of 1e-1 appears anomalous/likely typographical, no random seeds, and training/inference times unreported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Choices are explicitly motivated: Laplacian-smoothed log-DSC loss for numerical stability; hybrid discriminative loss (BCE + perceptual loss on hidden layers) to improve training stability and quantitative performance; adversarial loss to enforce inter-slice spatial smoothness as a global distribution constraint; non-saturating GAN form adopted for stronger gradients; label smoothing (T=0.01) justified as preventing the discriminator from trivially separating real/fake. Minor gap: λ=1 not ablated.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly described: area-sensitive candidate region generation via modified RPN labeling (Equation 1 for label expansion targeting ~1:3 positive:negative ratio, ~100% recall), resize to 224x160, per-CT normalization formula given; explicitly states no denoising and no data augmentation. Post-processing explicitly none (adversarial module positioned as a replacement for post-processing).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned anywhere in the paper; no repository URL provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five metrics reported with formulas: DSC (89.87±3.17%), pixel-wise accuracy (95.85±3.04%), per-class accuracy (89.91±2.31%), mean IoU (82.37±3.30%), and mean surface distance (1.30±0.41). Well exceeds the Dice-plus-one requirement.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only: mean±SD across four folds, plus min/max DSC (77.12-91.96%). No confidence intervals, no paired significance tests against baselines, no correction for CV dependence; min/max spread of ~15 DSC points suggests high variance across cases that is not statistically explored.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Thorough comparisons: (i) general segmentation baselines (FCN, SegNet, U-Net, DeepLab v3+) re-implemented in TensorFlow on identical data for fairness; (ii) pancreas-specific SOTA (Roth 2015: 71.80%, Roth 2016: 78.01%, Roth 2018: 81.27%, authors' Pancreas-GAN: 88.72%) under the same 4-fold protocol; (iii) module ablations (DCAE 82.43 → +Local-LSTM 84.47 → +adversarial 86.81 → full DRAN 89.87) and candidate-region ratio ablation (1:3 optimal).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (pancreas), so per-organ reporting is trivially satisfied; case-level distribution reported (mean, SD, min 77.12%, max 91.96%), and per-slice qualitative expert grading shown. No per-case table is provided, however.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations discussed: dependence on costly pixel-wise annotations, typically small annotated datasets, and candidate region generation left for future work; brief acknowledgment of 'a few false-positive samples'. However, no dedicated failure-case analysis (e.g., examination of the worst-performing cases near min DSC 77.12%), and limitations section is brief.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Well-characterized public cohort with demographics and clinical composition reported; however, the entire sample derives from a single external dataset (NIH/TCIA), splits are random without fixed seeds, and the small sample (80) plus dominance of healthy-kidney-donor/diseased mix may limit generalizability. No external validation compounds this.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. Consistent evaluation protocol: all baselines re-implemented in the same framework on identical folds with identical metrics; expert qualitative scoring used a defined external rubric (Litjens et al. criteria). Concerns: no independent validation set for hyperparameter tuning, no inter-observer ground truth variability assessment, and single expert grader for subjective evaluation.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. All planned metrics appear reported (five metrics + ablations), but key details are withheld: learning rate, training/inference runtimes, code availability, per-case results, and no significance testing despite wide per-fold variance (DSC min 77.12 vs max 91.96). Extended-journal relationship to the authors' own BIBM 2018 paper means favorable self-comparison (Pancreas-GAN as baseline).

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not captured in prior extraction: (1) COHORT/IMAGING: 17 of 80 subjects are healthy kidney donors, 63 have diseases (incl. pancreatic cancer); 512x512 in-plane resolution with varying pixel size; 120 kVp tube voltage. (2) ARCHITECTURE: pancreas size at DCAE layer 5 statistically characterized as 10-15 px (height/width max), motivating dilation rates 4 and 8; Hilbert curve constructed over a 26x26 grid (feature map itself is not power-of-2, handled via Algorithm 1); Local-LSTM downsamples DCAE features by factor 4, serializes to ((m x n)/16) sequences of c channels, then upsamples via two deconvolutions; discriminator trained with soft labels (ground truth = 1-T, prediction = T, T=0.01) and non-saturating generator loss for stronger gradients and faster convergence. (3) TRAINING: adversarial optimization alternates between discriminator update (Eq. 12) and segmentation network update (Eq. 14) with fixed discriminator; discriminator not needed at inference. (4) ABLATIONS: candidate region positive:negative ratio sweep — 1:1.5→74.37, 1:2→81.07, 1:2.5→85.31, 1:3→89.87 (best), 1:3.5→86.25, 1:4→84.37 DSC; module ablation confirms each component contributes (adversarial module adds +2.34 DSC over DCAE alone... see Table 1: DCAE 82.43, +Local-LSTM 84.47, +adversarial 86.81, full 89.87). (5) EVALUATION NUANCES: MSD unit (mm vs pixels) not specified in text; baselines 'strictly following the original papers' but re-implemented by authors; qualitative assessment by one expert using Litjens et al. 2017 grading criteria; feature-map visualizations before/after Local-LSTM and 3D renderings provided as qualitative evidence. (6) PUBLICATION CONTEXT: journal extension of authors' BIBM 2018 Pancreas-GAN paper with six enumerated incremental additions (ADB blocks, Hilbert-curve serialisation replacing x/y-direction serialisation, Laplacian-smoothed DSC loss, hybrid perceptual discriminative loss, additional visualizations, larger candidate-region ablation). (7) SCOPE NOTE: method is fundamentally 2D slice-wise processing with intra-slice patch-sequence LSTM modeling and inter-slice smoothness enforced only implicitly via the adversarial distribution constraint — not true 3D volumetric segmentation, which is relevant for review categorization. (8) EFFICIENCY CLAIM: 103M parameters vs 296M (U-Net) and 158M (FCN), claimed to reduce convergence time and aid clinical deployment, though no runtime measurements substantiate this.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes DRAN, an end-to-end adversarial framework combining (i) a dilated convolution autoencoder with adaptive dilated blocks for resolution-preserving multi-scale context, (ii) a novel Local-LSTM module operating on patches serialized via a Hilbert space-filling curve to model intra-slice spatial context for boundary refinement, and (iii) a discriminator with hybrid BCE+perceptual loss and Laplacian-smoothed DSC loss to enforce inter-slice smoothness. It achieves state-of-the-art pancreas segmentation on the standard 80-volume NIH benchmark (DSC 89.87±3.17% via 4-fold CV), outperforming U-Net/FCN/SegNet/DeepLab v3+ and prior pancreas-specific methods, with a parameter-efficient design (103M parameters). For the systematic review, this represents a medium-quality single-organ, effectively-2D methodological contribution notable for its GAN-LSTM hybrid design but lacking external validation, code release, and inferential statistical analysis.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 90 training scans (D1) exceed the >50-subject training threshold, supported by ~1000-fold augmentation. Caveats: total cohort is only 100 scans (modest for deep learning), the external validation set comprises just 10 scans, and the authors themselves acknowledge the small training set limits generalization. Meets the stated criterion but only marginally above it.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources fully documented: D1 = 90 late venous-phase abdominal CTs from the public Gibson et al. (2018) multi-organ reference standard (TCIA Pancreas-CT + BTCV, noted to contain non-pancreatic pathologies); D2 = 10 scans randomly sampled from 1905 late venous-phase CTs (2015, Radboud UMC oncology department) with demographics (941 M/964 F, age 58.4±13.3), voxel spacing, and explicit exclusion criteria (pancreas-related pathologies). IRB approval (IRB2017-3976) and GDPR de-identification reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Experiment 1: clearly described random 5-fold cross-validation on D1 (4 folds train / 1 fold development, repeated 5×, averaged). Experiment 2: independent 10-scan validation set split into two 5-scan subsets alternated across readers and methods to minimize learning effects. No separate held-out test set beyond the 10 external cases, but the split strategy is explicit and justified.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: D1 ground truth is a published, publicly available reference standard (Gibson et al. 2018). For D2, a consensus reference standard was produced by two readers at full resolution; three radiological experts performed segmentations (ITK-SNAP), and annotation reliability was quantified (mean intra-observer DSC 0.86, 95% CI 0.85–0.87; pairwise kappa 0.85–0.87).

Q5_external_validation.justification: Interactive validation performed on a genuinely independent external dataset (D2, Radboud UMC) distinct from the public training data (D1). Notably, automatic iUnet performance was higher on D2 (86%) than in D1 cross-validation (78.1%), which the authors attribute to greater visceral fat in D2 patients — an honest discussion of cross-dataset behavior.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture is based on the known U-Net/Çiçek 3D U-Net extended with 3D convolutions and padding (1,1,1); Figure 1 shows feature-map counts per block and highlights the retrained layers (final layer + one layer in the deepest encoder–decoder/latent section, chosen for largest receptive field). However, kernel sizes, strides, and activation functions are not stated in the text, so the description is not fully self-contained.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Baseline training is well specified: Keras/TensorFlow 1.12, Adam, lr 1×10⁻⁴, 2000 iterations, batch size 8, ~12 h on Nvidia RTX 2070 (CUDA 10.0); interactive retraining on GTX 1080; augmentation parameters (±3 voxel translations, ±10° rotations, Gaussian noise σ 0–3 HU) fully given. However, key interactive-training details are missing: the volume-penalty weight λ in Eq. (3) is not reported, the number of interactive fine-tuning iterations is described only as 'a few iterations', and no code is released.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Soft Dice loss is adopted from Milletari et al. (2016) and directly matches the DSC evaluation metric (reasonable, cited). The interactive loss components have qualitative rationale (scribble voxels weighted 3; zero weight within a geodesic-distance threshold 0.2 as an uncertainty region), but the numeric choices appear heuristic, are not ablated, and the volume-difference penalty λ is introduced without value or justification.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Fully described: Gaussian smoothing (σ=0.75), HU windowing [−160, 240]→[−1,1] with clipping (justified soft-tissue window, cited), automatic bounding-box crop around the reference segmentation with 5% margin, trilinear resampling to 64×64×24 (resulting spacings reported: x 1.7–2.7, y 0.79–1.8, z 3.34–4.7 mm). Absence of post-processing for iUnet is explicitly stated and motivated (organ-specific post-processing inadequate for pancreas).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or trained model released; no code URL. Data availability statement states the Radboud UMC clinical data are not publicly available due to restrictions.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Beyond DSC: segmentation time (a primary interactive outcome; median 48.4% reduction), inter-/intra-observer agreement (DSC + kappa), and distribution plots (box/violin). No surface-distance metrics (HD/ASSD), but the criterion (Dice + at least one other metric) is clearly met.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests reported for all key comparisons: architecture differences (p<0.001), manual vs interactive DSC (p=0.017), manual vs interactive time (p<0.001), initial vs interactively refined segmentation (p<0.001); 95% CI for observer agreement; means±SD for cross-validation results. Minor gaps: no CIs on headline DSC values and no multiple-comparison correction.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compares against a re-implemented, similarly optimized iFCN (the directly relevant interactive predecessor), the canonical Çiçek 3D U-Net, and manual expert segmentation, with literature context (Wolz 2013: 70%; Gibson 2018: 78%). Limitations: baselines are dated relative to 2019–2020 automatic pancreas SOTA, and the human-user validation did not include iFCN as an interactive comparator — only automatic baselines were compared head-to-head.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (pancreas), so organ-level reporting is inherently satisfied; results are reported per experiment (5-fold CV, external validation) with full distributions (box/violin plots) and a per-observer-pair agreement matrix, not just pooled averages. Per-case results are not tabulated, however.

Q15_limitations.justification: Extensive, candid limitations: failure at the uncinate process (low contrast, high anatomical variability); BMI/visceral-fat dependence; coarse 64×64×24 resolution; bounding-box dependency on a reference segmentation; initial DSC drop/under-segmentation after the first interactive iteration; divergence risk if too many layers are retrained; inter-observer variability drivers (partial-volume artifacts; outer edge = 25.1% of segmentation volume); small training set.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Selection is transparent: D2 randomly sampled from 1905 scans with explicit exclusion criteria; D1 provenance public and documented. Concerns: single-center data; D2 drawn from an oncology patient population; pancreas-pathology cases excluded from validation despite the stated clinical target (pancreatic cancer diagnosis/interventional guidance); very small validation sample (n=10).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. Standardized validation protocol (reader/method alternation across two 5-scan subsets, two practice cases per reader, defined timing start/stop, consensus reference at full resolution). Concerns: the consensus reference standard was produced by two readers apparently drawn from the same observer pool (potential circularity); observers could not be blinded to method (inherent to interactive designs); only iUnet — not iFCN — was evaluated with human users; no inference latency reported.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Main outcomes match the analysis plan and negative findings are openly discussed (initial DSC drop, divergence risk, small dataset). Minor inconsistencies: an observer 'satisfaction score' is mentioned in the analysis plan but never reported; the first Wilcoxon statement in the Results appears mislabeled (text says 'manual versus interactive' but references Figure 4, the automatic architecture comparison); abstract reports manual DSC 87% while the Discussion cites 87.5%; no per-case results table.

detailed_extraction: Ethics/governance: national research ethics approval (Radboud UMC IRB2017-3976), local data collection on implied consent, de-identification per GDPR (EU 2016/679). Problem framing: pancreas is hard to segment due to poor parenchyma–bowel contrast (especially duodenum), large volume/shape variation, variable peripancreatic fat; prior multi-atlas (Wolz 2013) ~70% DSC and best deep learning (Gibson 2018) ~78% DSC. Key methodological details not fully captured elsewhere: (1) Classification setup uses K=1 foreground class (background + pancreas). (2) Baseline loss = differentiable soft Dice per class (Eq. 1, Milletari V-Net formulation), total loss = mean over classes (Eq. 2). (3) Interactive loss (Eq. 3) = voxel-weight-map-weighted soft Dice between the updated prediction Ŷ′ and the current prediction Ŷ (second term acts as a volume-difference penalty scaled by unreported λ), with weight map initialized uniformly, scribble voxels weighted 3, and voxels within geodesic-distance threshold 0.2 (map computed from image, scribbles, voxel indices) weighted 0 as an uncertainty region; total loss again class-averaged (Eq. 4). (4) Rationale for retraining layer selection: early layers encode generic image features, deeper layers encode segmentation-specific features, and the deepest latent layers have the largest receptive field (citing Esser et al. 2018); no general freezing rules exist, so last layer + one latent layer chosen. (5) Experiment 1 protocol: random 5-fold CV on D1, mean development-set DSC across folds, Wilcoxon signed-rank for significance; intro separately reports 68% DSC for iFCN when using its original organ-specific post-processing (inadequate for pancreas), vs 72.3±11.4% without in CV — a minor internal inconsistency worth noting. (6) Experiment 2 protocol: 3 radiological experts ('readers'); 10 D2 cases split into two 5-scan subsets alternated across readers and methods to reduce learning effects; manual segmentation in ITK-SNAP with full feature access; interactive segmentation in a custom VTK/QT5 GUI served via X-server; two practice cases per reader before validation; observers instructed to correct only global features (voxel-level edits counter to the tool's purpose); timing measured from first annotation placement (manual) / initial segmentation generation (interactive) until save; consensus reference standard created by two readers on full-resolution images, then cropped to validation dimensions; pairwise observer agreement matrix reported (DSC 0.85–0.87; kappa 0.85–0.87). (7) Results: 5-fold CV DSC on D1 — iUnet 78.1±8.7%, Çiçek 3D U-Net 75.3±8.1%, dilated iFCN 72.3±11.4%; external D2 — interactive iUnet 86.0 DSC in median 8 min vs manual 87% in 15 min (Discussion cites 87.5), median 48.4% time reduction (p<0.001). (8) Notable finding: automatic iUnet performed better on the external set than in internal CV, attributed to D2 patients having more visceral fat (better delineated boundaries), consistent with Roth et al. (2015) on BMI effects. (9) Failure behavior: first interactive iteration often causes a DSC drop/under-segmentation, correctable with further scribbles; opening too many layers for retraining risks divergence; uncinate process is the weakest region. (10) Gaps: no human-user comparison against interactive iFCN; no per-case results table; no surface-distance metrics; λ and interactive iteration count unreported; no per-update inference latency; resolution cap (64×64×24) and bounding-box dependency on reference standard limit clinical deployment. (11) Overall quality is borderline High (24/30, exactly at threshold), primarily dragged down by no code release, partially unspecified interactive hyperparameters, and dated/limited baselines.
contribution_summary: This paper introduces iUnet, an interactive 3D U-Net in which only the final layer and one deep latent layer are per-case fine-tuned on user scribbles via a weighted soft-Dice loss with a volume-penalty term, removing the organ-specific post-processing that the earlier iFCN interactive framework required and that fails for the pancreas. iUnet achieved a stronger automatic baseline than iFCN and the canonical Çiçek 3D U-Net (78.1% vs 72.3% and 75.3% DSC, 5-fold CV on 90 public CTs), and in a three-observer study on an external 10-scan Radboud UMC cohort reached near-interobserver-expert accuracy (86.0% DSC) in a median 8 minutes versus 15 minutes for manual segmentation (48.4% time reduction, p<0.001). Its key contribution is demonstrating that scribble-based interactive deep-learning refinement can attain expert-level pancreas segmentation roughly twice as fast as manual annotation, with a design the authors claim is organ- and modality-agnostic.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: NIH Pancreas-CT: 82 CT scans (~61-62 training cases per fold in 4-fold CV, >50 threshold met); MSD pancreas: 281 scans with 211 for training. Both clearly exceed the 50-subject threshold, though absolute sizes are modest and typical for the difficult pancreas segmentation task.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both datasets are well-known public benchmarks with explicit citations (Roth et al. 2015b for NIH; Simpson et al. 2019 for MSD), with image dimensions reported (512×512×L, L∈[181,466] for NIH; L∈[37,751] for MSD) and the MSD label convention (pancreas+tumor merged as foreground) clearly stated.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: NIH: 4-fold cross-validation with fixed folds, reporting the average across folds; MSD: 211 train / 70 test split explicitly following Zhang et al. 2021 to ensure comparability. Caveat: no dedicated validation set is described for hyperparameter selection (settings were transferred from NIH to MSD and taken from prior literature).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: The paper relies entirely on the annotations shipped with the public benchmarks and does not describe the annotation protocol (annotator expertise, inter-rater agreement, verification procedures) within this paper. Partial credit given because community-standard datasets with externally documented annotation quality are used.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Evaluation on two independent public datasets (NIH and MSD) with identical hyperparameters demonstrates some transferability, but this is not true external validation: within each dataset, training and testing share the same source/scanner distribution, and no cross-dataset (train NIH → test MSD) or multi-center/institutional test is performed.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture is thoroughly described with mathematical formulation (Eqs. 1-13, Algorithm 1) and figures: Stage 1 M-FCN with three per-view FCNs fused by averaging; Stage 2 2.5D UNet with 4 residual-conv encoder blocks and 4 ordinary-conv decoder blocks, pooling/deconvolution, and skip connections. Hybrid channel construction (guidance depth 2 → 5 channels, boundary slices duplicated) and the bi-directional recurrent update rule (λ_new=λ_ori=0.5) are fully specified. Minor gaps: exact filter counts/kernel sizes and the FCN variant are not given.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Reported: PyTorch, GTX 2080Ti, SGD optimizer, learning rates (1e-5 M-FCN, 1e-4 UNet), batch size 1, DSC loss, termination thresholds (τ=0.95, P=5 iterations). Missing: number of epochs/iterations, data augmentation strategy, learning-rate schedule, filter counts, and critically whether the bi-directional recurrent iterations are trained end-to-end or applied only at inference — a key ambiguity for reimplementation.

Q8_loss_function.justification: DSC loss (Eq. 14) is formally defined and is a reasonable/standard choice for the small, class-imbalanced pancreas, but the paper provides no explicit justification or discussion of the choice versus alternatives (e.g., combined CE+Dice); hyperparameters are justified only as 'empirical values widely used in pancreas segmentation tasks'.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly specified: HU windowing to [-100, 240], zero-mean/unit-variance normalization, ROI cropping of image and probabilistic maps using binarization threshold 0.5 with padding margin 20. Postprocessing equally clear: binarization, de-cropping, bi-directional recurrent refinement with explicit termination criterion (DSC between consecutive predictions > 0.95 or max 5 iterations).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository link mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Rich metric set: DSC, ASD, 95% Hausdorff distance, plus localization recall/precision/IOU, DSC distribution histograms, reliability curves, slice-wise DSC interval analysis, volume correlation and Bland-Altman agreement tests, and per-slice inference time — far exceeding the Dice-plus-one minimum.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics (mean ± std over 4 folds, min/max), Bland-Altman agreement analysis, and linear regression correlation of segmented vs. reference volumes are provided. However, no confidence intervals, no p-values, and no formal statistical significance tests against competing methods are reported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive comparison against 13 state-of-the-art methods on NIH (Table VII) spanning 2D, 2.5D, 3D, P3D, and projection-based approaches, with CV protocol annotated per method; additional comparison on MSD (Table VIII). Comparisons rely on published numbers rather than reimplementation, but the authors acknowledge protocol differences (e.g., hold-out vs. 4-CV). Parameter/complexity comparison (75M vs. 239M params vs. Chen et al. 2019) adds value.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (pancreas), so per-organ results are inherently reported; the paper goes well beyond a single average by reporting min/max/std, DSC distribution over all 82 cases, slice-wise DSC intervals, head/body/tail regional results, small-target slice breakdowns, and per-stage ablation results.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated limitations section (4.4) identifying that some initial-estimation ROIs fail to cover the entire pancreas, degrading primary segmentation — a fundamental weakness of stage-wise methods. Failure cases are explicitly visualized (Fig. 10 failed initial segmentations; Table IV small-target slices), and future work on reasonable ROI estimation is outlined.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low risk. Patient selection is defined by established public benchmarks (NIH Pancreas-CT, MSD pancreas) with fixed 4-fold CV splits and all cases evaluated (full DSC distribution over 82 cases shown), reducing cherry-picking concerns. However, no patient demographics, scanner, or contrast-phase details are provided, so generalizability across populations cannot be judged; both benchmarks are single-source collections.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low risk. Outcomes assessed with standardized, clearly defined metrics (DSC, ASD, HD95, localization recall/precision/IOU) applied consistently across ablations; timing comparisons conducted on identical hardware; ablation experiments run under identical settings. Minor concern: SOTA comparisons use quoted numbers from studies with different CV/hold-out protocols (acknowledged by authors), and the bi-directional recurrent mechanism's training procedure is not fully specified, which could affect measured inference behavior.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate risk. Reporting is unusually transparent (min/max/std, distributions, reliability curves, Bland-Altman, failure cases, limitations). Caveats: MSD evaluation reports only DSC (no surface-distance metrics), the MSD SOTA comparison includes only two methods, no significance testing is performed, and no code release prevents independent verification.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details not captured in the primary extraction: (1) Problem formulation: segmentation as composition of E (initial estimation → pixel-wise probabilistic maps) and F (primary bi-directional segmentation), optimized via DSC loss (Eq. 14: 1 − 2ΣYŶ/(ΣY+ΣŶ)).
