(2) Hybrid data construction (Eq. 7): center slice + probabilistic maps of adjacent slices; guidance depth d yields 2d+1 channels (3/5/7 tested; 5 used, i.e., depth 2); first/last slices duplicated for boundary handling; ROI cropping threshold ε=0.5, padding margin m=20. (3) Recurrent update rule (Eq. 10): linear blend of new and initial probabilistic maps with λ_new=λ_ori=0.5; forward pass processes slices 1→n, then inverted backward pass n→1 (Algorithm 1); final predictions from the three views are again fused by arithmetic averaging before binarization/de-cropping. (4) Termination criterion: iteration stops when DSC(Y_t, Y_{t+1}) > τ=0.95 or at max P=5 iterations. (5) Design rationale: FCN chosen over UNet for Stage 1 due to lower GPU memory at 512×512 inputs; UNet with skip connections chosen for Stage 2 once background is removed. (6) Training: SGD; LR 1e-5 (M-FCN) and 1e-4 (2.5D UNet); batch size 1; hyperparameters adopted from prior pancreas literature; number of epochs and augmentation strategy NOT reported; whether recurrent iterations are trained end-to-end or inference-only is NOT clarified. (7) Parameter selection (Table V, NIH): guidance depth 1/2/3 → DSC 84.90/85.35/85.38%, ASD 1.11/1.10/1.10 mm, HD 3.66/3.68/3.69 mm; depth 2 chosen as accuracy/compute trade-off despite depth 3 being marginally best. (8) Ablation results: PBR-UNet places 71.34% of slices in DSC [0.8,1.0) vs. 65.04% (C2F) and 44.65% (M-FCN); slices with DSC<0.5 reduced to 7.58% (vs. 9.52% C2F, 17.73% M-FCN). Small-target slices: head/tail (480 cases) DSC 59.93% with 53 failed slices (vs. M-FCN 36.23%, 128 failed; C2F 50.53%, 75 failed); size≤300 px (496 cases) DSC 55.53%, 68 failed (vs. 33.25%, 165 failed; 45.65%, 98 failed); DSC=0 slices more than halved vs. M-FCN. (9) Volume-level agreement: M-FCN volume correlation only 0.59 (averaging discards uncertain pixels); PBR-UNet shows strongest regression slope≈1 and Bland-Altman agreement mostly within ±1.96 SD. (10) Localization (Table II): recall 82.76±8.21% (54.06-94.41), precision 83.45±7.19% (59.24-94.39), IOU 75.03±7.46% (53.33-86.58). (11) NIH full metrics (Table I): DSC 85.35±4.13% (71.36-91.05), ASD 1.10±0.40 mm (0.66-2.95), HD 3.68±2.30 mm (1.83-17.78). (12) MSD: 85.65% DSC (69.33-93.98) vs. Fang 2019 84.71% and Zhang 2021 85.56% (same 211/70 split); all hyperparameters unchanged from NIH. (13) Efficiency: inference 0.57±0.11 s/slice (full pipeline; range 0.36-1.21), vs. 0.38±0.06 (C2F) and 0.17±0.01 (M-FCN); Stage-2 UNet has 75M parameters vs. 239M for closest competitor Chen et al. 2019 (3D UNet 90M + VGG16 138M + ResNet18 11M). (14) Not reported anywhere: epochs/training duration, augmentation, filter counts, kernel sizes, validation-set usage, license, release version. (15) Relevance note for the review: despite the review topic (3D organ segmentation), this is a 2.5D single-organ (pancreas) method that explicitly trades global 3D context for local 3D (inter-slice) context to reduce computational cost.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes PBR-UNet, a two-stage 2.5D framework in which multi-view FCN probabilistic maps are combined with the center-slice image into a local 3D hybrid multi-channel input, which is iteratively refined by a novel bi-directional recurrent update scheme inside a 2.5D UNet — balancing 2D efficiency against 3D context exploitation. Achieving 85.35±4.13% DSC on NIH (4-fold CV) and 85.65% on MSD with only 75M parameters (~0.57 s/slice), it matches or exceeds heavier 3D competitors while particularly improving poorly-segmented, small-target slices. The bi-directional recurrent guidance paradigm is presented as a plug-in alternative to costly 3D convolutions for context modeling in medical image segmentation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 10 patients (361 slices, augmented to 24,052). Well below the >50 subject threshold; slice augmentation inflates volume but does not add subject diversity.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Cardiac CT from clinical patients stated, but no details on scanner, acquisition protocol, image phase, number of institutions, or inclusion criteria.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No split described. Best-IoU checkpoint was saved, implying an internal validation set, but its size and method are unstated. The 2 HOCM cases are demo cases, not a formal test set.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual segmentation is implied as the target, but no annotation protocol, annotator expertise, tooling, or quality control is described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No independent external cohort. Evaluation on 2 cases from the same clinical environment as training data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Described only as 'our original CNN program based on the latest artificial intelligence techniques' — no architecture type, depth, or input/output specification.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No hyperparameters, optimizer, learning rate, epochs, batch size, or framework named. Not reproducible from the text.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function not mentioned. IoU is reported only as an evaluation/selection metric, not a justified training loss.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Partial: slice-level data augmentation (361 to 24,052 slices) and 3D polygon construction are mentioned; augmentation type, resampling, intensity normalization, and post-correction details are absent.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Single metric only (IoU). No Dice, Hausdorff distance, or volumetric error.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals or significance tests for model performance. The median 30h (IQR 23-50) manual timing is descriptive lab-record data from 8 unrelated models, not a controlled comparison.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: No comparison against any baseline or published segmentation method (e.g., nnU-Net, atlas-based).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Whole-heart IoU only. No per-structure results (chambers, valves, papillary muscles) despite these being the stated surgical targets.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly acknowledged: IoU 0.85 called 'insufficient for fully automatic segmentation'; manual correction requirement for one case discussed; authors note prior application to other structures.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High — 10 patients with no stated selection criteria; unknown whether cases were consecutive or hand-picked.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: High — outcomes assessed on only 2 demonstration cases with no standardized protocol; the time-saving claim compares CNN cases against historical lab records of 8 different models (confounded, non-contemporaneous).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: High — conference abstract only; only the best IoU checkpoint reported, no test-set results, per-structure breakdown, or negative case details beyond one correction anecdote.

detailed_extraction: Conference abstract (EHJ-CV Imaging supplement, Hybrid and Fusion Imaging), not a peer-reviewed full paper. Task: whole-heart segmentation from cardiac CT to accelerate patient-specific 3D-printed/surgical planning models for cardiac surgery (2 HOCM preoperative cases). Approach: slice-based 2D CNN, custom-built, trained on 361 slices from 10 patients, expanded ~66x to 24,052 slices via unspecified data augmentation; best-IoU checkpoint retained (IoU = 0.85). Deployment workflow: 5 min CNN inference + optional manual correction (Case 1: 3 h correction; Case 2: none) versus reported fully-manual median of 30 h (IQR 23-50 h) from 8 prior models in lab records — an uncontrolled historical comparison. Same group previously applied the CNN to aorta, aortic stenosis valves, and atheromatous plaque. Funding: Japan Organization of Occupational Health and Safety on behalf of J3D. Note for review scope: this targets the heart as a single structure from cardiac (not whole-body) CT, has no per-organ segmentation benchmarks, and reports no Dice/HD metrics — flag accordingly when pooling with other studies.
contribution_summary: Presents a custom CNN for whole-heart segmentation from cardiac CT aimed at speeding up 3D surgical planning models, achieving IoU 0.85 and reducing segmentation time from a reported ~30 h manual median to 5 min automated (+ up to 3 h human correction). Contribution is primarily a workflow/feasibility demonstration on 2 HOCM cases rather than a methodological advance; no architecture, loss, or comparative evaluation details are provided, so it serves as a low-evidence clinical-translation data point in this review.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 28 training patients (560 volumes) — below the >50-subject threshold; partially offset by 20 cardiac phases/patient. Authors themselves note the effective test set is only 10 patients.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single-center routine ECG-gated coronary CTA (Linköping University); scanner, resolution, slice count, and pixel spacing all reported (Siemens Somatom Force, 0.5 mm slices, pixel 0.27–0.41 mm).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Patient-level split fixed prior to analysis (28 train / 6 val / 11 test), kept consistent across all three methods; nnU-Net used its internal 5-fold CV. No external split, penalized under Q5.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Detailed pipeline: ITK-Snap active contour + multi-atlas propagation; only ED/ES frames manually corrected; visual spot-checks with corrections for 2 patients. Caveat: 18 of 20 phases per patient are atlas-derived, not manually verified.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external cohort; all data from one scanner at one site. Data not publicly shareable per ethics approval.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: All three are published architectures with public implementations: nnU-Net ('3D low-res' config), MONAI UNETR, and the authors' 2D→3D TransUNet modification with released code. Exact ViT hyperparameters live in the repo rather than the paper — acceptable for standard architectures.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: PyTorch 1.9, Adam, LR 0.01 with poly decay (power 0.9), batch 2, augmentation specified — but training terminated by a 72 h wall-clock cap rather than fixed epochs, and nnU-Net config is delegated to auto-configuration. Wall-clock termination harms exact reproducibility.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Mean Dice + cross-entropy (background excluded) stated but not justified; nnU-Net loss is automatic. Standard choice, no rationale given.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (224³ resampling, rotation/flip augmentation with probabilities), postprocessing (largest connected component; PV multi-cluster exception), and per-method ED/ES identification via max/min LV volume all explicitly described.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Authors' 3D TransUNet at github.com/ljollans/TRUNet; nnU-Net and MONAI UNETR are publicly available off-the-shelf, so all three models are reproducible. Data available only on reasonable request.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice plus ICC, Bland–Altman (bias, limits of agreement), Wilcoxon signed-rank, and downstream functional metrics (EDV/ESV/SV/EF) — well beyond the Dice+1 threshold.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: ICC 95% CIs, Benjamini–Hochberg-corrected Wilcoxon p-values, Shapiro–Wilk normality checks, Bland–Altman LoA. Rigorous and fully tabulated.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Head-to-head comparison of three current SOTA baselines (nnU-Net, TransUNet, UNETR). No comparison to prior cardiac-specific published models, but architecture-level SOTA comparison is the stated aim.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Table 1 reports per-ROI Dice for all five structures per method; functional metrics (SV/EF/EDV/ESV) also reported per chamber, not just averaged.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations section: n=10 effective test patients, wall-clock training cap (UNETR possibly undertrained), architecture effect confounded with nnU-Net's preprocessing/ensembling, data non-shareable. One concrete failure case documented (UNETR failed to segment LAA in 1 patient).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Retrospective single-center routine CTA; exclusions reported (1 patient fully excluded, 13 patients partially excluded for poor image quality) but 'poor image quality' criteria are not operationalized and the clinical spectrum of included patients is not described.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. Identical patient-level splits, test protocol, and automated evaluation across methods; however, unequal training budgets (72 h wall-clock cap) and nnU-Net's proprietary auto-preprocessing plus cross-validation ensembling confound the architecture comparison — authors acknowledge this. UNETR may be undertrained rather than fundamentally inferior.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Negative results fully reported (UNETR failure to estimate SV/EF, TransUNet's non-significant LAAEF, per-ROI and per-metric tables with CIs); per-case best/median/worst segmentations shown; open access CC BY.

detailed_extraction: Ground truth: semi-automatic ITK-Snap active contour + multi-atlas segmentation (method of Bustamante et al.); atlases built only from manually corrected end-diastolic/end-systolic frames; remaining 18 phases per patient label-propagated automatically; visual spot-checks led to manual correction of 2 patients × 2 time instances — i.e., Dice on non-peak phases is measured against unverified propagated labels. Exclusions: 1 patient fully excluded, 13 patients partially (poor image quality); functional analysis restricted to N=10 test patients with all 20 phases; UNETR analyses exclude 1 further patient (LAA segmentation failure at peak diastole). Scanner: dual-source 192×192-slice Siemens Somatom Force, 0.5 mm slices with 0.25 mm overlap, pixel 0.27–0.41 mm (mean 0.33 ± 0.034). Training: batch size 2 (A100 80GB-limited), best-validation-DSS checkpoint selected; nnU-Net converged ~48 h, 3D TransUNet peaked ~36 h. Systematic error pattern: both top methods underestimate LAA EDV/ESV and overestimate LAA SV/EF (consistent with incomplete contrast opacification of the LAA apex). Robustness: per-case mean DSS best/median/worst = 0.9392/0.9132/0.8826 (nnU-Net), 0.9226/0.8988/0.8713 (3D TransUNet). Models segment single volumes with no temporal input; ED/ES inferred post-hoc from LV volume extremes per method. License: article CC BY; dataset available on reasonable request subject to ethics.
contribution_summary: First study to show that stroke volume and ejection fraction of the LV, LA, and LAA can be simultaneously estimated from time-resolved CT using fully automatic 3D deep learning. nnU-Net outperformed two ViT-based architectures (mean DSS 0.91 vs 0.89 for 3D TransUNet vs 0.69 for UNETR) and was the only method to reliably predict LAA ejection fraction (ICC 0.68), supporting the conclusion that convolutional encoders with multi-scale skip connections remain superior to transformer encoders for this task, while 3D TransUNet offers ~7× faster inference (41 s vs 276 s/volume).

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 170 patients (120 train / 30 val / 20 test); training set well above the 50-subject threshold; all 12 OARs annotated per patient.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single institution (Peking University Third Hospital) with IRB approval (LM2018118); scanner (Philips Brilliance Big Bore), 512x512 matrix, resolution 0.69-1.34 mm, slice thickness 1.5-3.0 mm, disease breakdown (46 brain mets, 40 NPC, 18 lymphoma, etc.), mask immobilization, and mixed contrast protocol all reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit patient-level split 120/30/20; held-out validation used for early stopping and model selection; test set untouched. Randomization/stratification mechanism not stated, but split itself is fully clear with no evident leakage.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: OARs delineated by experienced radiation oncologists per published guidelines [16], with MRI acquired to assist segmentation; slice-category labels defined by explicit anatomical landmark boundaries. No inter-observer agreement analysis, but the process is described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent institutional dataset; single-center internal test set only.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Both networks fully specified with figures: classifier (depth-wise separable convs, max-pool, global average pooling); segmentation net (7 down/7 up dilated stacks, dilation rates 1-4, SELU, extra inter-stack skip concatenations, 16x256x256 input with 3-slice z-overlay, 1x2x2 max-pooling preserving z resolution).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (Adam), lr (0.001), losses, augmentation, input handling, and early stopping reported; missing batch size, epoch count, training duration, and early-stopping patience prevent exact reproduction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss and categorical cross-entropy are standard, formula-given, and cited; choice is implicitly motivated by the class-imbalance framing but never explicitly justified or ablated against alternatives.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Fully described: bilinear resampling to 1x1 mm, rotation (<=20 deg) and translation (<=20 px) augmentation, 0.5 threshold binarization, morphological erosion+dilation (r=2 px, 1 iteration), anatomical-consistency correction of slice categories, and 5-slice boundary padding.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC plus 95% Hausdorff distance (with rationale for using 95HD over HD), plus classification accuracy and runtime metrics.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Per-organ paired tests (Student's t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank selected via Shapiro-Wilk normality test), mean +/- SD for all results, alpha=0.05, SPSS v24. Confidence intervals not reported, but p-values are comprehensive.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Direct quantitative comparison only against internal ablation (same net without classifier). Prior methods (Ibragimov & Xing, Tong, Liang, AnatomyNet) compared narratively using published numbers on different datasets; no re-implementation or shared-data benchmarking.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Complete per-organ DSC and 95HD tables (all 12 OARs) with SDs and p-values, for both model variants; slice-classification accuracy also broken down per category.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations explicitly discussed: per-OAR independent networks ignore inter-OAR spatial relationships and can produce overlapping edges; single-institution data; small OARs (optic nerves, TMJs, left parotid) remain weak (Dice 0.70-0.73); parotid 95HD high (7.3-8.4 mm). Future work stated.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Retrospective single-center cohort with explicit inclusion criteria (all 12 OARs intact and not invaded by tumor/nodes), which excludes anatomically distorted cases and may inflate performance versus the general radiotherapy population. Scanner/disease mix is heterogeneous within the cohort, which mitigates this partially.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Uniform automated pipeline applied to a fixed patient-level test set; evaluation metrics and postprocessing identical across all patients and both model variants. Caveat: ground truth from a single annotation team with no reported inter-observer variability assessment.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All 12 OAR outcomes reported for both DSC and 95HD, including non-significant comparisons (e.g., right eye DSC p=0.111, right optic nerve 95HD p=0.063); ablation results fully disclosed. Minor gaps (no epochs/batch size, no code) affect reproducibility rather than selective reporting.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not in the primary extraction: (1) Study design: retrospective, IRB-approved (LM2018118), anonymized; CT cranium-to-clavicle in supine position with thermoplastic mask; both enhanced and unenhanced scans included; MRI co-acquired to assist manual delineation. (2) Statistical significance: two-step model significantly better than segmentation-only on DSC for 8/12 OARs and on 95HD for 11/12 OARs (only right optic nerve 95HD non-significant, p=0.063); largest 95HD gains on temporal lobes (right 14.49->3.28 mm, left 16.59->3.73 mm) and brainstem (5.50->2.28 mm). (3) Slice classification: per-category accuracy I=99.12%, II=97.26%, III=92.53%, IV=89.78% (lowest), V=98.21%, VI=99.01%; maximum boundary misclassification 3 slices (2 patients); <=2 misclassified slices in 90% of test patients; anatomical-consistency postprocessing collapses non-monotonic category sequences (e.g., I-I-II-I -> I-I-I-I). (4) Slice exclusion: average 127 slices/patient; category means II=20, III=10, IV=14, V=19; excluded fraction per OAR: eyes 84.25%, TMJ 81.10%, parotids/mandible 66.14%, brainstem/temporal lobes 57.48%; mean 70.98% across OARs. (5) Inference breakdown (GTX 1080, i7-7700, 64 GB RAM): classification 4.47 s + segmentation 7.55 s + postprocessing 28.11 s = 40.13 s total vs 50.90 s segmentation-only (21.16% reduction); postprocessing dominates runtime. (6) Architecture nuance: z-axis kept at native resolution (1x2x2 max-pooling) to handle anisotropic slice thickness (1.5-3.0 mm); one dedicated segmentation network per OAR (12 networks total); 5 extra slices appended at category boundaries to buffer classifier errors. (7) Missing for reproduction: batch size, epoch count, early-stopping patience, training wall-clock time. (8) Funding/industry co-authorship: Beijing Linking Medical Technology Co. employees among authors; no conflict-of-interest or funding statement captured in provided text.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a two-step pipeline for H&N OAR auto-segmentation in which a lightweight slice classifier (six craniocaudal categories, 95.99% accuracy) first excludes irrelevant slices (~71% on average) before a refined 3D dilated encoder-decoder with SELU activations and inter-stack skip concatenations segments each of 12 OARs. This class-imbalance-targeting design cuts false positives on irrelevant slices and reduces total inference time by 21.16% (40.13 s vs 50.90 s) while significantly improving DSC for 8/12 OARs and 95HD for 11/12 versus the same network without the classifier. Its main limitation is the per-OAR independent network design, which ignores inter-organ spatial context and yields 12 separate models requiring retraining per organ.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 151 CT scans total, 104 for training — exceeds the >50-subject threshold, though modest by deep learning standards (authors acknowledge this as a limitation).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Two established public datasets (LiTS, 3D-IRCADb) with original citations, download URLs, and access date (May 31, 2021) explicitly stated.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Clear split: random 80/20 of LiTS into train (104)/validation (27); all 20 IRCAD scans held out entirely as test set. No source overlap between training and test data.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth by board-certified radiologists (3 for LiTS); annotation harmonization to liver-only contours described in detail; full annotation protocols referenced to prior publications (refs 29, 30).

Q5_external_validation.justification: IRCAD test set (n=20, 10M/10F) is a fully independent external database from the training source (LiTS). Not prospective/multi-center, but satisfies independent-dataset validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D U-Net fully specified: 3x3x3 convolutions (BN+ReLU), 2x2x2 max pooling, 2x2x2 transposed convolutions, skip concatenation, 1x1x1 final conv, 19,069,955 parameters; nnU-Net auto-configuration cited.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Package version pinned (nnunet v1.6.6) makes unlisted defaults (optimizer, LR, batch/patch size) deterministic; epochs (4000), early-stop rule, loss, and hardware (8x V100, AWS) all stated. Rerunnable as-is.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice+cross-entropy is used as the nnU-Net package default; composition is described but the choice is never justified and no alternatives or ablations are considered.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (DICOM-to-NIfTI via dicom2nifti, harmonization excluding vasculature/gallbladder/biliary structures, voxel-spacing standardization from headers) and postprocessing (parenchyma voxel selection, header-scaled volume summation, ITK-SNAP 2D/3D rendering) both clearly described.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or trained model released. Only links to the pre-existing public datasets are provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Four metrics: Dice, Hausdorff distance, 95th-percentile HD, and volume percent error, with per-case values tabulated (Table 1).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only (mean/median +/- SD, ranges, sex-stratified breakdowns). No confidence intervals, no significance tests, no comparison of variance between subgroups.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Indirect literature comparison only (H-DenseUNet 0.965, RA-UNet 0.961 Dice on different data); no baseline re-implemented or evaluated on their own test set.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study, so per-organ reporting reduces to liver — which is fully tabulated per case (Dice, HD, HD95, volume error for all 20 test scans) plus sex-stratified statistics, exceeding the requirement.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations explicitly discussed (CT-only, small sample, parenchyma-only without vasculature/lobar anatomy). However, no failure-case analysis — worst cases (Dice 0.965, HD 32.8 mm, 5.56% volume error) are visible in Table 1 but never examined.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low risk. All scans from two public databases were used, split randomly, with the test set drawn from a wholly separate database. Caveat: LiTS demographics (sex/age) unavailable, and no scanner/vendor or protocol diversity documented.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Unclear-to-moderate risk. Global Dice was computed on the test set at every training step, and the early-stop criterion (<1% Dice gain within 2000 epochs) does not specify whether validation or test Dice triggered stopping. Authors state no test feedback entered training, but the monitoring protocol creates a leakage pathway.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low risk. All outcomes reported per case and in aggregate, including unfavorable spread (HD up to 32.8 mm); training curves in supplementary material; no evidence of selective outcome reporting.

detailed_extraction: Image geometry: all scans 512x512 in-plane; z-slice count avg 142 +/- 43 (SD); slice thickness 0.5-2.0 mm; voxel spacing standardized from NIfTI headers during nnU-Net internal preprocessing. Annotation exclusions: gallbladder, intrahepatic vasculature, external biliary system, portal vein, hepatic artery, hepatic veins all excluded from liver contour; LiTS contours harmonized to a single reference standard by 3 radiologists. Training: Dice milestones 0.956 at 1000 epochs, 0.959 at 2000; final training loss -0.7805, validation loss -0.6785, evaluation metric 0.966 at conclusion; stopped at 4000 epochs via early-stop check-in threshold. Hardware: 64 CPUs, 488 GB RAM, 8x NVIDIA V100 (AWS). Inference timing discrepancy: 143.4 +/- 76 s per test CT for mask prediction (Results) vs. <20 s full-pipeline claim (Discussion) — unresolved in paper. Sex-stratified test results: male median Dice 0.975 (SD 0.006, range 0.965-0.985), median volume error 2.055% (max 5.560%); female median Dice 0.975 (SD 0.004, range 0.968-0.980), median volume error 0.911% (max 3.127%). Conflicts/funding: NSF STTR Phase I Award 2014827 with InformAI as recipient; two co-authors (Marlatt, Havelka) salaried by InformAI — industry involvement in a surgical-translation study should be noted in the review. Tooling: dicom2nifti, nnunet v1.6.6 (backend unspecified), ITK-SNAP for visualization. Data openly accessible (LiTS via Kaggle mirror, IRCAD via IRCAD/Dropbox); article CC BY-NC-ND.
contribution_summary: Demonstrates that the self-configuring nnU-Net (3D U-Net, ~19M parameters) achieves near-radiologist liver segmentation (Dice 0.974, HD95 2.46 mm) and clinically actionable volume estimation (1.92% mean error) on an external 20-scan IRCAD test set, exceeding published Dice of liver-specialist architectures (H-DenseUNet 0.965, RA-UNet 0.961) without task-specific tuning. The translational contribution is the complete segmentation-to-volume-to-3D-rendering pipeline aimed at pre-transplant donor/recipient size matching, with high per-case consistency (Dice SD 0.005). Credibility is limited by the single-organ scope, small external test set, absence of released code, and test-set monitoring during training.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Partial. LiTS training set (131 volumes) exceeds 50 subjects, but the primary validation experiments (3-fold CV, all statistical ablations) were performed on the small ISICDM dataset with only 24 training volumes.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Two clearly identified public challenge datasets (ISICDM 2019 and MICCAI 2017 LiTS) with URLs, volume counts, and resolution information. Clinical metadata (demographics, contrast phase, scanner details) not characterized.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit 3-fold cross-validation on ISICDM training data and separate blind testing on hidden-label test sets (ISICDM 36 cases; LiTS 70 cases via official leaderboard). Minor gap: fold stratification and dedicated hyperparameter validation set not described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual annotations confirmed ('the training data have manual annotations', provided by the challenges), but annotation protocol, number of raters, and inter-rater agreement are not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Validated on two independent datasets with blind test evaluation (hidden ground truth; LiTS results from official challenge leaderboard). Caveat: models were trained separately per dataset; no cross-dataset generalization test (e.g., ISICDM-trained model on LiTS).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Layer-by-layer tables provided for both 2D U-Net (9 conv blocks, feature channels 64-1024) and 3D FCN (7 conv blocks, 48x48x48 patches), including kernel sizes, pooling/upsampling placement, concatenation points, and sigmoid output.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: batch sizes (8/16), training schedule (30 epochs x 20 sub-epochs, 100 patches/sub-epoch), patch size, GPU (GTX 1080 Ti), FCM parameters (C=2, T=10, δ=0.001) and level-set weights given. Missing: optimizer, learning rate, DL framework, and loss function.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never stated. Both networks end in 1x1(x1) conv + sigmoid, implying binary cross-entropy, but this is not confirmed or justified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described with quantitative justification: [0,200] HU truncation derived from mean±3std fitting of liver intensities (means 80.23-128.20, std 13.85-26.47 → [18.04, 201.76]); resampling to 1x1x1 mm³; 256x256 resizing; liver-ROI cropping; tumor-specific 99th-percentile piecewise normalization; post-processing includes erosion + median filter for level-set initialization and convexity-based fallback.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No pipeline code or trained models released. Only links to third-party resources: Li's DRLSE code, a MATLAB File Exchange FCM implementation, and DeepMind's surface-distance evaluation code.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five metrics: DSC, VOE, RVD, ASD, and RMSD, with formal definitions and equations for each.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with exact p-values reported for all ablation comparisons (liver fine vs. coarse: DSC p=0.0001, ASD p=0.0195; tumor FCN+LS vs. FCN: DSC p=0.0276, ASD p=0.0035). Mean±std reported. No confidence intervals.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compared against H-DenseUNet, Vorontsov, Yuan, Chen, Bi, and LiTS leaderboard methods on the same test set, plus internal ablations (2D U-Net alone, 3D FCN alone). Comparisons rely on published/leaderboard numbers rather than reimplementations.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver and liver tumor results reported separately with full metric panels on both datasets, with per-case vs. global Dice distinguished. Only aggregate means; no per-case distributions or histograms provided.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly discussed with visualized failure cases (Fig. 11): dependency of tumor segmentation on liver mask quality, 3D segmentation holes requiring 2D fallback, and false positives/negatives on fuzzy tumor boundaries caused by CT noise. Future fixes (atlas-based methods, edge-enhancing diffusion) proposed.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/Unclear. Patient selection criteria, demographics, disease spectrum, and scanner/protocol heterogeneity are not described; dataset composition is dictated by external challenge organizers. ISICDM (24 cases) is small and may not be representative.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. Standard metrics applied consistently; blind evaluation on hidden test sets mitigates assessment bias. However, LiTS comparisons use leaderboard figures computed under potentially different conditions, and ISICDM testing results are presented only qualitatively (no quantitative test-set numbers).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Unfavorable results transparently reported (tumor Dice per case 71.8% slightly below H-DenseUNet's 72.2%); multiple metrics and ablations reported. Minor inconsistency: tumor Dice global stated as 84.1% (Table 4) vs. 84.2% (Discussion text).

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details: (1) Statistical testing: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on 3-fold CV results; liver fine vs. coarse: DSC p=0.0001, VOE p=0.0024, RVD p=0.0056, ASD p=0.0195, RMSD p=0.0005; tumor FCN+LS vs. FCN: DSC p=0.0276, VOE p=0.0113, RVD p=0.0087, ASD p=0.0035, RMSD p=0.0073. (2) Loss function unreported; both networks output 1x1(x1) conv + sigmoid, implying but not confirming binary cross-entropy; optimizer/learning rate/DL framework unreported. (3) Level-set: DRLSE energy E(φ)=Rp(φ)+λLg(φ)+αAg(φ) with weights adopted from Li et al. (λ=1.5, α=1.5, step-related term 0.1); evolution stops at steady state of gradient flow; balloon force in 'expand' mode; refinement performed slice-by-slice in 2D. (4) FCM edge enhancement: C=2 clusters (tumor vs. healthy liver), max 10 iterations, convergence threshold δ=0.001; tumor membership row reshaped to image, Canny edge detection applied → prior gp; final edge indicator gmax = max(gi, gp) combining normalized image gradient with FCM prior. (5) Automatic initialization: coarse tumor mask eroded then median-filtered (SES); binary φ0 with constant c0 inside SES — removes manual ROI requirement of prior LSMs. (6) Tumor ROI: coarse tumor mask enlarged by 20 pixels per direction; non-liver tissue removed via fine liver mask before refinement. (7) Training details: dense training strategy for 3D FCN (30 epochs x 20 sub-epochs x 100 random 48³ patches/sub-epoch, batch 16); 2D U-Net batch 8; 2D stage treats tumor as liver (binary); 3D FCN trained with tumor labels to jointly produce fine liver + coarse tumor; data augmentation and early stopping mentioned in Discussion without specifics. (8) Robustness mechanism: convexity analysis detects 3D liver segmentation failures (holes) on several LiTS cases → automatic fallback to 2D U-Net result. (9) Efficiency: ~90 s/volume (367x367x45): 10 s 2D U-Net + 50 s 3D FCN + 30 s FCM+level-set; cascade reduces DL stage from 400 s (whole-volume 3D FCN) to 60 s. (10) LiTS leaderboard team name: 'Zpark'. Evaluation code: DeepMind surface-distance (GitHub). (11) ISICDM resolution fixed at 1x1x5 mm³; LiTS variable; slope=0/intercept=1 for all used datasets. (12) Minor inconsistency: tumor Dice global 84.1% (Table 4) vs. 84.2% (text). (13) Funding: National Key R&D Program of China (2017YFC0112404), NSFC (81501546). (14) Scope note for review synthesis: two-structure problem (liver + intrahepatic tumor), not multi-organ; retrospective, no prospective/clinical validation.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes a hybrid data-driven/model-driven pipeline for liver and liver tumor CT segmentation: a 2D U-Net and 3D FCN cascade performs coarse-to-fine liver segmentation while automatically initializing a distance-regularized level-set evolution (DRLSE), whose edge indicator is enhanced by unsupervised fuzzy c-means probability maps combined via a max operation with image gradients. The key novelties are eliminating the manual ROI requirement of level-set methods and FCM-based edge enhancement, yielding competitive results on two public benchmarks (liver Dice 96.3-96.7%; tumor Dice 71.8% per-case/84.1% global on LiTS, comparable to H-DenseUNet) at ~90 s/volume. The work demonstrates that coupling CNN initialization with level-set refinement improves tumor boundary accuracy, stability (reduced variance), and topology interpretability relative to pure deep learning baselines.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 139 patients (100 train/39 test) self-collected plus MICCAI 2015 (38/10); well above 50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources fully described: Sun Yat-Sen University Cancer Center (nasopharyngeal cancer patients) and public MICCAI 2015 H&N challenge dataset; CT resolution (0.7-1.2mm transverse, 3mm slices, 90-172 slices) specified.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 100/39 split, 10% inner-validation held out, 5-fold CV for prior-map generation; split is clear though no random seed stated.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual delineation by one experienced oncologist with independent review/adjustment by a second; process described, though inter-observer agreement not quantified.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Validated on MICCAI 2015 public challenge data, independent of the self-collected cohort, with same settings (one output channel swapped).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: IPNet/PANet fully described with figures: justified inception blocks (pooling removed), PAI block (prior attention + learnable spatial attention), three-stage SRSF (OGS/LOS/SOS), OAR grouping defined.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam optimizer, 50 epochs max, early stopping (10), PyTorch/Python 3.5, 2x GTX 1080, augmentation and hyperparameter table referenced; but learning rate/batch size not verifiable in text and no code released.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice + surface-distance loss with explicit rationale (SD more sensitive to boundary shape), weighting alpha=gamma=1 justified by citation [28].

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing fully specified (windowing clip [WL-WW/2, WL+WW/2], normalize to [-1,1], half-res for OGS, translation/rotation/noise augmentation); postprocessing explicitly none - ROI localization is in-pipeline.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no repository URL or license given.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC, HD95 (per organ), plus VCR for ROI localization; all formally defined with citations.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality testing, Wilcoxon rank-sum / paired t-tests (p<0.05) in SPSS 19; mean+/-std reported. No confidence intervals, but significance testing is thorough.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compared against 5 published methods on MICCAI 2015 including the challenge champion (Raudaschl), AnatomyNet, FocusNet, Interleaved 3D-CNN, and hierarchical vertex regression, plus internal ablations (SRSF-UNet, SRSF-IPNet).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-organ DSC and HD95 for all 22 OARs (Table 4) and per-organ MICCAI comparison (Table 5); not averaged away.

Q15_limitations.justification: Five explicit limitations, including candid admission that chiasm/pituitary results are sometimes worse than UNet/IPNet baselines and that training is complex/slow (70h).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate concern: single-center cohort of nasopharyngeal cancer patients only; no statement on consecutive enrollment or exclusion criteria, limiting generalizability to other H&N populations and scanners.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: all methods evaluated with identical, formally defined metrics (DSC/HD95 per patient on 3D basis) on fixed test sets; comparisons against published MICCAI numbers rather than re-training all baselines is a minor caveat (Zhu et al. used extra training data, noted by authors).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low: per-organ results reported for all 22 OARs including unfavorable cases (chiasm, pituitary underperforming baselines); limitations and failure modes stated explicitly.

detailed_extraction: SRSF pipeline: (1) OGS - IPNet on half-resolution CT segments 3 OAR groups as merged classes (A: brainstem+spinal cord; B: mastoids, mandibles, TMJs, parotids, middle ears; C: temporal lobes, eyes + small OARs), producing ROIs and prior probability maps (100% VCR coverage); (2) LOS - PANet per-OAR segmentation of large/easy OARs; (3) SOS - PANet for small OARs (<=1cc: lens, optic nerves, chiasm, pituitary). Prior attention maps at depth i generated by average pooling of previous-stage probability; attention-refined features element-wise added to unrefined features (residual). Inception block: multi-kernel conv paths with 3x3x3 conv + BN + ReLU fusion, pooling path removed. Loss: Dice + SD (alpha=1, gamma=1). Prior maps for training obtained via inner 5-fold CV to avoid leakage. Augmentation yields 360 3D volumes. Training ~70h on 2x GTX 1080 12GB; inference ~30s for all 22 OARs. For MICCAI 2015, TMJ output channels replaced with submandibular; all else identical. Small-OAR stage results: OGS group DSC >83%, HD95 <4.8mm; LOS-C small-OAR DSC 68.3+/-4.7%, HD95 6.3+/-2.6mm. PANet significantly better than UNet on 19/22 OARs and than IPNet on 17/22 (DSC); HD95 superior on 13 and 7 respectively; chiasm/pituitary worse than baselines. Funding: multiple NSFC and provincial grants; industry co-authors from Perception Vision Medical Technology (potential conflict of interest, not declared in text).
contribution_summary: The paper proposes PANet, a pyramidal U-Net variant combining justified inception blocks with a prior attention + learnable spatial attention (PAI) block, embedded in a three-stage Stepwise Refinement Segmentation Framework (OGS -> LOS -> SOS) that segments 22 head-and-neck OARs coarse-to-fine on full-resolution CT. Prior probability maps from earlier stages serve both ROI localization and attention guidance, addressing the large/small organ imbalance without per-organ models. It achieves the best reported small-OAR Dice on MICCAI 2015 (77.6% left optic nerve, 69.2% chiasm) with ~30s inference, though it underperforms baselines on chiasm/pituitary and training requires complex 5-fold cross-validated prior-map generation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 103 training scans from LiTS 2017, exceeding the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: LiTS 2017 challenge data well characterized: 6 clinical sites, mixed scanners/protocols, in-plane 0.55-1.0mm, slice spacing 0.45-6.0mm, 512x512 axial slices.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 103/28 split stated but split methodology (random vs. official LiTS partition) not described; no validation set mentioned; internal inconsistency (Table I text says '30 volumes' but per-case figures show 28).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Stated only as 'manual segmentation results given by experts'; no detail on number of raters, protocol, or inter-rater agreement.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No independent external dataset; all evaluation on LiTS test cases (same challenge distribution).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: 10 residual blocks (20 intra-slice + 4 inter-slice conv layers), factorized pseudo-3D kernels 3x3x1/1x1x3, dilated conv rates 1-3, 2 downsampling layers, PReLU+BN, C0=32, encoder-decoder skip concatenation, 3-scale prediction fusion, receptive field 217x217, patch 256x256x19.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam lr=1e-3, weight decay 1e-7, batch size 1, 20k iterations, patch size, NiftyNet/TensorFlow, GPU (1080 Ti 12GB), and training/inference times all reported; only data augmentation and validation/early-stopping strategy missing.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss used with citation (V-Net) but never justified against alternatives (e.g., class imbalance rationale); stated, not argued.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Explicit: resampling to isotropic 1mm^3 only; authors explicitly assert no other pre- or post-processing, leaving no ambiguity.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; only built on the public NiftyNet platform.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice, VOE, ASD (mm), and MSD (mm), all formally defined.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or standard deviations; only means plus per-case scatter plots.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compared to top-8 LiTS 2017 leaderboard entries plus Christ (FCN+CRF), Yang (DI2IN), Dou (3D DSN); includes internal single-plane ablation. Caveat: leaderboard test set provenance vs. authors' own 28-case split is unclear.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ task (liver); per-case Dice/VOE/ASD/MSD reported for all 28 test cases (Figs. 7-10), exceeding the 'not just averages' requirement.

Q15_limitations.justification: Failure cases identified (axial-only fails on low-slice-count cases 1, 2, 23); acknowledges simple softmax averaging may be suboptimal vs. weighted fusion and that dilated convolution gave no significant gain.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Data from 6 clinical sites via a public challenge reduces site-specific bias, but patient inclusion criteria are not described and the 103/28 split procedure is unspecified, so case allocation could be non-random.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. Standard challenge metrics applied consistently, but it is unclear whether results come from the official LiTS evaluation server or a self-made 28-case holdout; if self-split, direct numerical comparison against the LiTS leaderboard (evaluated on a different test set) is not strictly like-for-like. The 30-vs-28 case-count inconsistency in Table I text adds uncertainty.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All four metrics plus per-case plots reported; negative findings disclosed (dilated convolution no significant benefit, axial-only failure cases); tumor segmentation correctly scoped out as future work rather than selectively omitted.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not in prior extraction: (1) Architecture — each conv layer followed by PReLU and batch normalization; C0=32 output channels, Cl=2 classes; 2D receptive field 217x217 with out-of-plane receptive field of 9; training patch 256x256x19; multi-scale fusion: three 3x3x1 conv heads at different decoder depths, upsampled, then concatenated and fused by a final 3x3x1 conv. (2) Training — converged at ~19k iterations on all three planes (Fig. 4); weight decay 1e-7; total ~97h for three independent plane models on one 1080 Ti. (3) Data — all 131 scans 512x512 in-plane; resampling to 1mm^3 isotropic is the only preprocessing; ground truth manual/expert but protocol unspecified. (4) Evaluation — authors state results were evaluated 'to the LiTS 2017' (likely challenge submission), but test-set count discrepancy: Table I caption says '30 volumes', per-case figures show 28; single-plane axial ablation (Dice 0.685) vs. multi-plane (0.967) is the key internal evidence for the integration scheme. (5) Comparison context — authors emphasize deepX (tied 1st at 96.7) used hierarchical coarse-to-fine pipelines with tiered resampling and post-processing, whereas MPNet is one framework without pre/post-processing; Christ/Yang/Dou characterized as effectively 2D slice-based without 3D context. (6) Funding — NSFC grant 61771056 and BIT interdisciplinary program. (7) Suggested field updates: components='NiftyNet (TensorFlow)', benchmark_reproduction='LiTS 2017 submission vs. leaderboard (test-set provenance unclear)'.
contribution_summary: Proposes MPNet, a pseudo-3D factorized-convolution FCN (3x3x1 intra-slice + 1x1x3 inter-slice kernels) with residual connections, dilated convolutions, encoder-decoder skips, and multi-scale prediction fusion, trained independently in axial, coronal, and sagittal planes and combined by averaging softmax outputs at test time. Achieves 96.7% mean Dice on LiTS 2017 liver segmentation using a single framework with no pre/post-processing beyond 1mm^3 resampling, matching the top leaderboard entry while avoiding the coarse-to-fine pipelines and refinement stages used by competitors. The main empirical evidence is the ablation showing multi-plane integration lifts Dice from 0.685 (axial-only) to 0.967, largely by rescuing low-slice-count volumes where the axial model fails.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 100 LiTS training scans (>50); 31 custom test; 3DIRCADb adds 15 via 2-fold CV. Adequate.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Two public datasets (LiTS [16], 3DIRCADb [17] with URL), scan counts and phase (venous/contrast-enhanced) stated.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split described (100/31 random, 2-fold CV) but non-standard custom LiTS split, no validation set mentioned, CV fold composition unspecified.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process never described; relies on dataset GT without stating who annotated or how (expert review, interpolation, etc.).

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation: 3DIRCADb model was trained on 3DIRCADb itself (2-fold CV); LiTS test set is drawn from its own training pool.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture fully specified: DenseNet-121 encoder (dense blocks 6/12/24/16 per Fig. 1), CCA bottleneck with affinity equations (1)-(2), 2.5D three-slice input, standard components by reference.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (SGD, momentum 0.9, wd 1e-4), poly LR (init 0.01), augmentation, and pretrained init given; but batch size, max iterations, crop/patch size, and loss weights w^c missing.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted cross-entropy fully formulated (Eq. 3) for 3 classes, but no rationale for the choice and class weights unspecified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: HU windows per dataset (LiTS [-200,200]; 3DIRCADb [-100,400]), augmentation detailed, test-time full slice size and 2.5D stacking explicitly stated.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL or statement of availability.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five metrics: DSC, VOE, RAVD, ASD, RMSD for every experiment.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, std devs, or significance tests anywhere; single point estimates per cell.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Five baselines (2D/3D U-Net, Cascaded U-Net, DCNN, H-DenseUNet) on both datasets plus component ablations; though reimplementation protocol for baselines is not stated.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver and tumor reported separately with all five metrics in all four tables.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations or failure-case discussion; qualitative figures show successes only; conclusion is purely promotional.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/high. Authors self-selected a 31-scan 'custom LiTS test set' with no seed, no stratification, and no per-case results; results on this split are not comparable to official LiTS leaderboard numbers, and baseline numbers may mix reimplemented and cited results. 3DIRCADb fold assignment unreported (possible slice-level leakage).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. Same metrics applied uniformly across methods and both datasets; ablation protocol consistent. However, whether baselines were retrained under identical preprocessing is unstated, and some baseline values (e.g., H-DenseUNet liver VOE 3.31% vs. others ~8-11%) look imported from prior papers under different protocols.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. All preplanned metrics reported per organ (good), but no limitations section, no failure analysis, selected qualitative examples only, and an internal inconsistency exists: 2D U-Net tumor DSC is 0.562 in Table I but 0.526 in Table III on the same custom LiTS test set. Gains over H-DenseUNet (+2.1/+1.3% tumor DSC) are presented as superiority without significance testing, and H-DenseUNet actually wins several liver metrics (VOE, RAVD, ASD) in Table I.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Loss: weighted CE over 3 classes (background/liver/tumor); per-class weights w^c not disclosed. (2) Training: poly LR schedule lr = lr0*(1 - iter/max_iter)^0.9, lr0=0.01; SGD momentum 0.9, weight decay 1e-4; batch size and total iterations not reported; GPU 1080Ti 11GB; no wall-clock times. (3) Init: ImageNet-pretrained DenseNet-121 (ImageNet implied, not explicit); paper claims transfer learning speeds convergence and lowers loss (ablation Tables III/IV: pretrained vs not = +9.5% tumor DSC LiTS, +2% 3DIRCADb). (4) CCA: single-module from CCNet [8]; C' channel reduction via 1x1 convs; recursion count not stated. (5) CCA ablation contribution: +0.4% liver / +3.9% tumor DSC on LiTS custom test, +0.2% / +4.3% on 3DIRCADb vs. DenseUNet+pretrained — most benefit on tumor, marginal on liver. (6) Inconsistencies: 2D U-Net tumor DSC differs between Table I (0.562) and Table III (0.526); H-DenseUNet LiTS liver VOE 3.31% is an outlier vs. its own paper's typical range, suggesting cross-paper number mixing. (7) 2.5D: input = 3 adjacent cropped slices, crop size unstated; output volume = stacked center-slice predictions; no CRF or morphological postprocessing. (8) Funding: NSFC 61771056. (9) 3DIRCADb: 15 of 20 volumes used (those with tumors), 2-fold CV, fold definition unreported.
contribution_summary: CC-DenseUNet inserts a criss-cross attention module (from CCNet) into the bottleneck of a DenseNet-121-based densely connected U-Net, processing CT volumes in 2.5D (three adjacent slices) with ImageNet transfer learning. On a custom 100/31 LiTS split it reports liver/tumor Dice of 0.962/0.741 and on 3DIRCADb 2-fold CV 0.943/0.663, edging out H-DenseUNet on tumor Dice by 1-2% while staying competitive on liver. The clinical relevance for multi-organ review is limited: single-organ (liver+tumor) scope, non-benchmark split, no significance testing, and the tumor Dice gain is within plausible run-to-run variance.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Mixed DS training = 54 volumes (barely >50); SLIVER cross-validation used only 20 training scans and produced 3 unusable masks; private DB has 8 scans. Deep-learning training set is marginal by modern standards.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public sources (SLIVER, VISCERAL) cited with basic scan characteristics (slices 64-394, in-plane 0.58-0.81mm, slice 0.7-5.0mm); private DB (8 scans) and the SLIVER/VISCERAL composition of the 60-volume mixed DS are not broken down.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Mixed DS: 6 randomly chosen test volumes (2 SLIVER, 2 VISCERAL, 2 contrast-enhanced VISCERAL), 54 train. No validation set or tuning protocol described. LOO on SLIVER excluded 3 failed cases post hoc, which biases the comparison.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth stated as 'manual segmentations done by experts'; no annotation protocol, rater count, or inter-rater agreement reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Genuine external test on private DB from completely different scanners with different intensity/resolution properties; mixed DS test also includes unseen scan types. Small n=8 is the caveat.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D U-Net used off-the-shelf per Cicek et al. citation; no layer specs, patch size, or input handling described. The traditional pipeline (region growing, Chan-Vese, GrowCut) is described in full detail with equations.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No optimizer, learning rate, epochs, batch size, patch extraction, augmentation, framework, or hardware reported. Training procedure not reproducible.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function not reported at all.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Exceptionally detailed: MIP abdominal extraction, HU rescaling, median filtering, spine-based orientation correction, PDF peak-based thresholding with high/low-contrast handling, cavity filling, morphological opening; postprocessing includes GrowCut labeling scheme, 0.5/0.5 fusion formula, and lung-based liver-heart separation.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: 10 metrics: Precision, TPR, FPR, Accuracy, DSC, VOE, RVD, ASSD, RMSSD, MaxD — well beyond Dice+1.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Only mean values reported; no standard deviations, confidence intervals, or significance tests on any table.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Table IV compares 7 methods spanning pixel-based, shape-based, and learning-based families on SLIVER. Caveats: comparison values partly from original papers (different conditions), and 3 failed LOO cases removed from their own evaluation.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver), so no cross-organ averaging; results are stratified per dataset, per method variant (traditional vs U-Net vs fusion), and per metric, with qualitative failure analysis per case (Fig. 6).

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit failure analysis: undersegmentation at liver tip, boundary vessels, and boundary-adjacent tumors; large MaxD (up to ~50mm); sharp U-Net degradation on unseen data; 3 unusable LOO cases; small private set.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate-high. Evaluation on SLIVER train subset only (20 cases, not full benchmark); 6 test volumes from mixed DS with no breakdown of the 54 training volumes; 3 LOO cases with unusable masks eliminated from evaluation post hoc; private DB (8 scans) has no selection criteria described.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. Same 10 metrics applied consistently across all datasets and method variants against expert ground truth; however, SOTA comparison values are taken from original publications rather than re-run under identical conditions, and their own LOO evaluation excludes 3 failed cases.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Only means reported (no variance/outliers), training details and loss omitted, failed cases dropped without sensitivity analysis, and the result that plain U-Net beats the fusion on the mixed DS (0.95 vs 0.91) is reported but not analyzed.

detailed_extraction: Fusion formula: final mask = 0.5*M + 0.5*PM where M = traditional region-growing mask, PM = GrowCut-refined U-Net mask. Traditional pipeline is training-free: per-axis iterative 2D region growing seeded from maximum of Chan-Vese edge energy on middle slice; threshold tau_1 taken from PDF-based threshold bounds, subsequent tau_{i+1} = 2.5*sigma of previous slice's region; three axis label maps combined by voxelwise OR. GrowCut setup: foreground label = updated U-Net mask eroded with sphere radius 5; background label = largest connected component of preprocessed image within a bounding box; GrowCut run on rescaled image. Liver-heart separation improved over prior lung-delineation method by replacing 3D region growing with binary thresholding [-1024,-300] HU plus connected-component border-connectivity rules. U-Net experiments also mentioned on MRI volumes (passing remark). Key quantitative finding: on the 54-volume mixed DS, updated U-Net alone (DSC 0.95) beats fusion (0.91) and traditional (0.86); fusion wins only in the low-data regime (private DB 0.89 vs U-Net 0.79) and offers scanner-invariant stability without retraining — the core argument for hybrid methods when annotated data is scarce. Comparison methods span van Rikxoort 2007, Zhang 2010, Wu 2016, Dou 2016, Esfandiarkhani 2017, Ajani 2018, Ahmad 2019; their fusion on SLIVER is mid-range (DSC 0.94 traditional, VOE 9.51% fusion) but with poor MaxD (~35-50mm) indicating boundary leakage at vessels/liver tip. Framework, GPU, training and inference times unreported.
contribution_summary: Proposes a hybrid fusion of a training-free traditional pipeline (PDF-based thresholding, Chan-Vese active contour, multi-axis 2D region growing) with a 3D U-Net prediction mask refined by anatomical constraints and GrowCut, weighted 0.5/0.5, plus a fast lung-based liver-heart separation step. The main claim is robustness under data scarcity: fusion remains stable across heterogeneous scanners (DSC 0.89-0.91) where the U-Net alone collapses on unseen data (DSC 0.79-0.81), though the U-Net alone wins when sufficient training data exists. Evaluated on SLIVER, VISCERAL, and a small private DB with 10 overlap/surface metrics; results are comparable to SOTA on SLIVER but with notably large maximum surface distances.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 20 CT volumes total (15 training / 5 validation) from 3D-IRCADb-01, far below the >50 subject threshold. Additionally tested on 1 real patient. Extremely small dataset limits generalizability and statistical power.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: 3D-IRCADb-01 dataset is clearly described: 20 CT scans (10 women, 10 men), hepatic tumors in 75% of cases, 512x512 pixel slices, >120 slices per patient. Additional single real patient CT also mentioned. Dataset is publicly available and well-characterized.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Authors state 15 volumes for training and 5 for validation with 2-fold cross validation. However, details of fold construction are not provided, no separate test set is defined, and the single-patient evaluation protocol is unclear. The split methodology is only partially specified.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: The paper relies on pre-existing annotations from 3D-IRCADb-01 without describing who performed the annotations, how they were created, inter-observer agreement, or quality control. Authors note that 'labeling data must be done by physicians with high expertise' as a general statement but do not describe the actual annotation process for their study.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Partial external validation attempted: the model was tested on a single real patient CT volume achieving 78% Dice for liver. However, this is extremely limited (1 case), lacks systematic protocol, and no external validation was performed for tumor segmentation. The main evaluation remains internal to 3D-IRCADb-01.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: The CFCN architecture is referenced from Christ et al. (MICCAI 2016) and the two-phase cascade concept is described (liver segmentation → liver ROI → tumor segmentation with dense CRF). However, no specific architectural details are provided: number of layers, filter sizes, receptive fields, or any modifications made by the authors are not reported.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial reproducibility: SGD optimizer (lr=0.001, momentum=0.8, weight decay=0.0005), Caffe framework, NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPU are specified. However, critical details are missing: batch size, number of training epochs/iterations, specific augmentation parameters (rotation angles, zoom ranges, noise levels), number of augmented samples generated, and exact 2D/3D transformation parameters.

Q8_loss_function.justification: No loss function is explicitly stated anywhere in the paper. While Caffe's default for segmentation (likely softmax with cross-entropy) could be inferred, this is never confirmed or justified by the authors.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing is thoroughly described and is a major contribution of the paper: intensity normalization to [0, 2047], histogram shrinking and rescaling, elimination of intensity levels with probability <0.0005%, thresholding to remove non-liver tissues using intensity range [700, 1400], and linear slice interpolation for gap filling. Post-processing with dense CRF also clearly described. This is the strongest methodological aspect of the paper.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or augmentation scripts are made publicly available. No GitHub repository or supplementary materials are mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Only Dice score is used as the evaluation metric. No additional metrics such as IoU/Jaccard index, Hausdorff distance, sensitivity, specificity, or volumetric similarity are reported.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No statistical analysis whatsoever: no confidence intervals, no standard deviations, no p-values, no significance testing between augmented and non-augmented conditions. With only 5 validation volumes, statistical robustness cannot be assessed.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Authors compare against Christ et al.'s published results (93.1% liver, 94.3% with CRF) but explicitly acknowledge these are not directly comparable due to different validation sets. Internal comparisons between un-normalized/normalized/augmented variants are provided. No systematic comparison against other state-of-the-art methods.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Results are reported separately for liver (94.58% with CRF) and liver tumor (45.87%) across all experimental conditions. Since these are the two target structures, per-structure reporting is complete and clearly differentiated in Table I.

Q15_limitations.justification: Some limitations acknowledged: authors note results are not comparable to original CFCN paper due to different validation sets, and the low tumor Dice (45.87%) implicitly reveals limitations. The single-patient external result (78%) also demonstrates generalizability issues. However, there is no dedicated limitations section or formal failure case analysis.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate to High - The entire study uses a single small public dataset (3D-IRCADb-01, 20 patients) which is well-curated but does not represent real-world clinical diversity. No patient selection criteria are defined by the authors. The single external patient case appears opportunistic with no selection methodology described. High risk of overfitting to this specific dataset.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate - The same Dice metric is applied consistently across all conditions. However, validation on only 5 patients with unclear 2-fold CV protocol introduces uncertainty. The augmentation strategy is tuned and evaluated on the same dataset, creating potential for information leakage. The dense CRF is applied to some conditions but not consistently across all comparisons.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low to Moderate - Authors transparently report both liver and tumor results including the poor tumor Dice (45.87%), and honestly acknowledge non-comparability with the original CFCN paper. They report the lower external validation result (78%). However, only Dice is reported, no negative findings or failure modes are explicitly discussed, and no per-patient breakdown is provided.

detailed_extraction: The paper proposes three complementary data augmentation strategies for small medical imaging datasets: (1) 2D geometric augmentation (rotation, shift, zoom, noise addition) performed concurrently with training to reduce memory overhead; (2) slice interpolation augmentation using linear interpolation in MATLAB to fill gaps between CT slices and reduce acquisition burden; (3) 3D augmentation combining the volume stack with 3D geometric transformations centered on the target organ's centroid to preserve maximum organ area while generating multi-perspective training samples. The 3D augmentation pipeline involves: detecting organ center point, shifting to origin, applying 3D rotation around multiple vectors/angles, re-shifting, and re-sampling oblique slices at original resolution. The intensity normalization pipeline (contributing 40.01% vs 27.17% tumor Dice improvement) involves: removing intensity levels with probability <0.0005%, histogram shrinking to main intensity scale, rescaling to [0, 2047], then thresholding out non-liver tissues using the empirically determined [700, 1400] range (derived from analyzing labeled liver+tumor voxels across all 20 patients). Authors explicitly note this custom range differs from the Hounsfield Unit scale and better captures liver tumor intensities. The paper identifies that 3D-IRCADb-01 contains labeling errors at liver boundaries, motivating their thresholding approach to eliminate incorrect labels. 3D augmentation alone yielded 93.94%/44.49% (liver/tumor), while targeted tumor-focused 3D augmentation improved tumor Dice to 45.87%. Total augmentation pipeline improved liver Dice from 91.47% to 94.58% and tumor Dice from 27.17% to 45.87%. The augmentation phase took several days of computation. The concurrent augmentation-training approach allows on-the-fly data generation without massive storage requirements. Results demonstrate that even single-patient augmentation can achieve 78% liver Dice, suggesting feasibility for transfer to different CT machine configurations with minimal data.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes a comprehensive data preprocessing and augmentation pipeline for liver and liver tumor segmentation from small CT datasets, combining intensity normalization with custom thresholding, 2D geometric augmentation, slice interpolation, and novel organ-centered 3D augmentation. Using a two-phase cascaded FCN (CFCN) with dense CRF on 3D-IRCADb-01, the pipeline improves liver Dice from 91.47% to 94.58% and tumor Dice from 27.17% to 45.87%. The key novelty is the 3D augmentation strategy that uses the organ's central point as the transformation origin to maximize preserved organ area while generating multi-perspective training samples from oblique slices.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 68 subjects exceeds the >50 threshold; still ≈54 per-fold training set under 5-fold CV, which remains above 50. Respectable for a rare pediatric congenital disease.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Center named (Shanghai Children's Medical Center), population defined (preoperative TAPVC children, Low-Dose CT), de-identification stated, volume dimensions (512×512×112–640) and voxel spacing (0.35×0.35×0.625 mm) reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 5-fold cross-validation stated, but fold construction (random vs. stratified), the validation mechanism behind the LR-on-plateau schedule, and any held-out test set are not described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual slice-by-slice annotation by 'experienced radiologists' stated, but the number of raters, consensus/arbitration procedure, and inter-observer agreement are not reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external or independent dataset; single-center data evaluated only by internal cross-validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Three explicit V-Net modifications (residual removal, Instance Norm, decoder GABs); SCAB and GAB fully specified with equations, kernel shapes (W3: Ci→Ci/2, W4: Ci/2→1, 7×7×7), K=4, and Fig. 1 diagrams.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, lr 0.001 halved on 2-epoch plateau, batch size 2, patch 208×96×208, augmentation (random crop, Gaussian noise), convergence budget (≤25 epochs × 200 iters) all given — but DL framework, GPU hardware, weight initialization, and fold splits are absent.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Generalized Dice Loss with inverse-square class weights (wl = 1/(Σyl)²), justified by class imbalance and cited to V-Net; exact formula with L=3 classes (background/PV/LA) provided.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (OTSU lung extraction to save compute, Z-score normalization) and postprocessing (largest-connected-component retention per class) each clearly described with motivation; pipeline stated to be fully automatic without manual thresholds.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC plus boundary-based ASD and HD, with formal definitions and an explicit rationale (area metrics are insensitive to boundary differences).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± STD over 5-fold CV reported for every metric and method, but no p-values, confidence intervals, or significance tests against baselines.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: V-Net and 3D-UNet retrained and evaluated under the identical protocol, plus a SCAB-only ablation isolating the GAB contribution (~2% DSC gain). Newer methods (e.g., nnU-Net, 2019) not included; acceptable for a 4-page conference paper.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: PV and LA reported separately for DSC, ASD, and HD across all four model variants (GAB, SCAB, V-Net, 3D-UNet).

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section or failure-case analysis. High variance goes unremarked (PV DSC 0.795±0.119; PV HD 12.627±6.724 mm), and 'converges' is asserted without training curves.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/moderate: single-center cohort of preoperative TAPVC patients; no inclusion/exclusion criteria or consecutive-enrollment statement, so referral and case-mix selection effects cannot be ruled out.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low/moderate: all compared methods trained and evaluated under the same 5-fold CV protocol with identical metrics; however, the reference standard lacks rater count and inter-rater reliability, so annotation consistency is unverifiable.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low/moderate: all three metrics reported per structure for every method including ablation; mitigated by absence of a limitations section, no failure cases, and inference time reported only for the proposed model.

detailed_extraction: Loss: GDL over L=3 channels with weights wl=1/(Σyl)². SCAB detail: residual attention Fout = Fin + Fin∘Mc∘Ms (Hadamard, broadcast); channel attention Mc via shared 1×1×1 convs (Ci→Ci/4→Ci) on summed avg+max pool (CBAM-style); spatial attention Ms deviates from CBAM by using two 3D convolutions (W3: Ci→Ci/2; W4: Ci/2→1, 7×7×7 kernels) instead of pooling — stated to be more flexible. GAB: input channels split into K=4 sub-volumes, each processed by an independent SCAB, then concatenated; motivation is that groups learn distinct feature types and reduce parameters. Evaluation equations for DSC/ASD/HD are provided; predictions binarized per class before largest-component filtering. Training: Adam; lr halved when loss plateaus 2 epochs; batch size 2; ≤25 epochs × 200 iterations; augmentation = random crop (208×96×208) + Gaussian noise. 5-fold CV; baselines retrained identically. Inference ~400 ms/volume vs. 2–3 h manual delineation. Qualitative Figs. 2–3 show 2D-plane and 3D render agreement with ground truth. Not reported: framework, GPU, parameter count, fold-generation method, ethics approval (only de-identification noted), inter-rater agreement, statistical significance testing, and per-fold results. Ablation delta: GAB vs. SCAB-only ≈ +0.023 DSC (PV) / +0.020 (LA); margin over V-Net baseline ≈ +0.07 DSC.
contribution_summary: Proposes GAB-V-Net, a modified V-Net (residuals removed, Instance Norm, and a novel Grouped Attention Block combining K=4 CBAM-inspired spatial-and-channel attention blocks with grouped convolution) for the first automatic segmentation (per authors) of pulmonary veins and left atrium in low-dose CT of pediatric TAPVC patients. On 68 single-center scans with 5-fold CV, it reaches DSC 0.795 (PV) and 0.834 (LA), outperforming V-Net and 3D-UNet with fully automatic pre/post-processing and ~400 ms inference versus 2–3 hours of manual delineation. Clinical claim: enables faster preoperative evaluation and surgical planning for TAPVC while reducing radiologist workload.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 82 contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans from the NIH Pancreas Dataset; with 4-fold cross-validation this yields ~61-62 training subjects per fold, exceeding the >50 subject threshold. However, 82 scans is modest by current standards for a small, low-contrast organ like the pancreas.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: The dataset is clearly identified as the public NIH Pancreas Dataset (Roth et al., cited as [7]) with 82 contrast-enhanced CT scans. However, no acquisition details are provided (scanner vendor, slice thickness, reconstruction kernels, contrast phase, patient demographics), so the description is only partially complete.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 4-fold cross-validation with random split of the 82 patients is stated, which is a defensible protocol for this dataset size. However, no separate validation set is described (unclear how hyperparameters such as ROI distance d=16, epochs=16, and LR schedule were selected), no per-fold results are reported, and there is no fixed held-out test set.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground-truth labels are inherited from the NIH dataset but the annotation process is never described: no information on annotator expertise, annotation protocol (2D vs 3D delineation), inter/intra-rater agreement, or quality control. Ground truth is used centrally (to define the training-time contour ROI), making this omission notable.

Q5_external_validation.justification: All experiments are performed exclusively on the NIH Pancreas Dataset. No evaluation on an independent external cohort (e.g., MSD pancreas, clinical data from another institution) is reported.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Topology is described in reasonable detail: 3D U-Net-style encoder (3x3x3 conv + BN + ReLU blocks, 2x2x2 max pooling stride 2), short-range residual shortcuts after the first and second pooling layers, decoder with 4x4x4 stride-2 deconvolutions, and a long-range shortcut summing encoder output with deconvolution output. However, the number of layers, feature channel widths, and per-stage configurations are not specified in the text, and the referenced Fig. 2 details are not verifiable from the text, limiting completeness.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Training is well specified: Adam optimizer, LR 0.001 reduced to 0.0001 after 4 epochs, 16 total epochs, batch size 16, patch size 64x64x64 with stride 8x8x8, contour ROI distance d=16, augmentation scheme, PyTorch, and NVIDIA 1080 Ti. Minor gaps remain (weight decay, random seeds, exact ordering of SeedNet/SegNet training 'two steps'), but the level of hyperparameter detail supports reproduction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Standard voxel-wise cross-entropy is used for both networks without justification or comparison against segmentation-tailored alternatives (Dice loss, compound losses), despite the paper itself identifying extreme class imbalance as the core problem. The restriction of the SegNet loss to the contour ROI is motivated (avoids distant negative voxels), but the choice of CE itself is not defended.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing is clearly described: HU clipping to [-100, 240] and rescaling to [0,1]; augmentation via 90/180/270-degree rotations and flips along all three axes; resolutions unchanged; 64^3 patch sampling. Postprocessing is also explicit: SeedNet output used as seed for region growing/connected-component pickup of SegNet components, and test-time prediction composed from 16^3 output patches at stride 8^3.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository link is mentioned anywhere in the paper; no statement about releasing the SAP framework implementation.
