Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Three complementary metrics are reported: Dice Similarity Coefficient, Jaccard index, and Precision, each with mean +/- standard deviation across the 4 folds (e.g., SAP: DSC 86.96+/-3.85%, Jaccard 74.62+/-4.66%, Precision 88.21+/-4.45%).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean +/- standard deviation over the 4 cross-validation folds is reported, but no confidence intervals, no paired statistical tests against baselines, and no significance analysis. The headline improvement over their own baseline (+0.71% DSC: 86.96 vs 86.25) is smaller than the reported fold-level standard deviation (+/-3.85%), so statistical significance of the gain is uncertain and unexamined. The baseline row in Table II also lacks standard deviations.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Thorough comparative evaluation: Table III compares against 6 published state-of-the-art methods on the same NIH benchmark (Zhu 84.59%, Xue 85.9%, Man 85.93%, Khosravan 84.57%, Chen 85.22%, Li 87.57%); Table II provides an internal framework-controlled comparison (C2F vs SAP on matched architectures); plus ablations of SegNet/SeedNet/SAP components and contour-vs-cube ROI. Caveat: SOTA numbers are taken from literature rather than re-implemented under identical splits.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: This is a single-organ (pancreas) study, so organ-level reporting is trivially complete; all results pertain to the target organ. The paper additionally provides component-level breakdowns (SegNet alone 81.71%, SeedNet alone 83.12%, full SAP 86.96%) and qualitative per-case visualizations (Fig. 3).

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid self-assessment: the authors acknowledge being outperformed by Li et al. (87.57% DSC), state that 'our improvement to the framework is only one aspect of the improvement of the complete pancreas segmentation method', show SegNet's large noise regions (Fig. 3), note the training-time dependence on ground-truth-derived contours, and propose architectural improvement as future work.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. The entire public cohort of 82 scans is used with random 4-fold cross-validation, so there is no cherry-picking of cases; however, no inclusion/exclusion criteria, patient demographics, or acquisition characteristics are reported, and reliance on a single public benchmark limits generalizability assessment.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. Metrics (DSC, Jaccard, Precision) are applied consistently across all framework steps and folds. However, the test-time pickup step depends on SeedNet providing a valid seed (failure mode if the seed misses the pancreas entirely is not quantified), baseline comparisons lack variance reporting, and SOTA comparisons use literature-reported numbers potentially obtained under different splits/protocols.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Per-fold results are not reported (only pooled mean +/- std); many comparison methods lack Jaccard/Precision values; the claimed 'SAP improves 2.1% DSC over C2F' is inconsistent with the Table II delta (86.96 - 86.25 = +0.71%), an unexplained discrepancy; no quantified failure-case analysis; no inference/training time reported.

detailed_extraction: SUPPLEMENTARY EXTRACTION (beyond previously extracted fields): [Framework mechanics] The core novelty is the SAP framework replacing the locate-and-segment (LAS/C2F) paradigm. In LAS/C2F, a first network segments the whole CT to derive a (rectangular/cubic) ROI for a second refinement network; the authors criticize this on two grounds: (1) cubic ROIs contain many distant, low-value voxels (sample imbalance) and (2) predicted ROIs are unreliable for the pancreas specifically. SAP instead uses a ground-truth-defined contour ROI at training time: ROId = {x | D(x) < d}, where D(x) is the Euclidean distance transform to the pancreas (D(x)=0 inside the organ), with d=16. SegNet is trained only on voxels within this ROI (loss masked to ROId); SeedNet is trained on whole-scan patches to produce a coarse but noise-free seed. At inference, no ground truth exists, so SegNet is applied to the entire scan (producing high-precision pancreas voxels plus distant noise), and a region-growing/connected-component procedure seeded by SeedNet's mask selects the correct components. [Ablation details] The contour-vs-cube ROI ablation (on the baseline 3D ResNet) found cube ROI optimal at d=12 (85.22% DSC) and contour ROI optimal at d=16 (86.25% DSC), supporting the contour-ROI design by ~1.03%. Note the contour-ROI optimum (86.25%) equals the Table II baseline figure, implying the Table II baseline is C2F + contour ROI + 3D ResNet. [Reporting discrepancy] The text claims 'SAP framework improves 2.1% DSC over C2F', but Table II shows 86.96% (LS-ResNet+SAP) vs 86.25% (ResNet+C2F baseline), a +0.71% difference that also confounds framework change (C2F->SAP) with architecture change (ResNet->LS-ResNet); the 2.1% figure cannot be traced to any reported table and is flagged as a possible reporting error. [Missing technical details] Number of encoder/decoder stages, channel widths, and total depth are unspecified (Fig. 2 not reconstructable from text); whether SeedNet and SegNet are trained jointly or sequentially is ambiguous ('trained networks in two steps'); no weight decay, momentum, random seed, or early-stopping criterion; learning-rate schedule stated only for the single described schedule. [Statistical concern] The headline gain over baseline (+0.71%) is within one fold-level standard deviation (+/-3.85%), and no significance testing supports superiority over the C2F baseline or over Xue/Man/Chen in Table III (gaps of ~0.2-1.7%). [Compute] Single consumer-grade GPU (1080 Ti) suffices; inference/training wall-clock times not reported despite the two-network cascade implying ~2x inference cost of a single model (not discussed). [Clinical/deployment relevance] Method is pancreas-only, contrast-enhanced CT only, evaluated solely via 4-fold CV on NIH; the training-time use of oracle GT contours means reported gains partly reflect an information advantage unavailable at deployment, partially mitigated by the SeedNet pickup mechanism but never quantified (e.g., performance if SeedNet seed is empty or disconnected).
contribution_summary: This paper proposes the Segment-and-Pickup (SAP) framework as an alternative to coarse-to-fine locate-and-segment pipelines for pancreas CT segmentation: at training time a ground-truth-derived Euclidean-distance contour ROI (d=16) trains a high-precision SegNet free of class imbalance, while at test time a whole-scan SeedNet supplies a clean seed for region-growing pickup of correct components from SegNet's noisy output. Combined with LS-ResNet, a 3D U-Net variant with long- and short-range residual shortcuts, it achieves 86.96% DSC (Jaccard 74.62%) on the NIH pancreas dataset (82 scans, 4-fold CV), surpassing their matched C2F baseline (86.25%) and most compared methods, though trailing Li et al. (87.57%). The contribution is primarily a framework/training-strategy insight (oracle contour ROI + seed-based noise rejection) rather than a novel architecture.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 40 unique volumes total (20 CT + 20 MRI from MM-WHS 2017); per fold, training uses 30 volumes (20 MRI + 10 CT). Well below the >50 subjects threshold, with only 10 CT volumes per fold for the target modality.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public MM-WHS 2017 challenge dataset clearly identified and cited (Zhuang et al.), with composition (20 MRI + 20 CT), 7 cardiac substructures, and the MRI-as-assistant/CT-as-target rationale explicitly described.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Training and test splits are described (two-fold cross-validation on CT with 20 MRI + 10 CT per fold; evaluation on the held-out MM-WHS test set via the challenge test tool). However, the validation set used for Optuna hyperparameter tuning and model selection is never defined, and no random seed is reported.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth for 7 cardiac substructures is referenced through the MM-WHS challenge citation, but the annotation protocol (who annotated, inter-rater agreement, quality control) is not described in this paper. A caveat is noted: GT annotations extend beyond the vessel lengths cut by the test tool, affecting AA/PA scoring.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Evaluation is performed on the official MM-WHS held-out test set with blind online tool scoring (independent of the 40 training volumes), which provides some independence. However, no validation on a dataset from a different source, institution, or distribution; single-challenge cohort only.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Thoroughly described: CIN formulation (Eq. 1), conditional encoder-decoder formalization (Eq. 2), C-ViT encoder with MSA/MLP blocks and residual connections (Eqs. 3-5), Swin variant (W-MSA/SW-MSA), specific configuration (L=8 blocks, K=768, 16x16x16 patches, 96^3 inputs), plus the 3D residual U-Net baseline (Valindria et al.) with figures.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Detailed training protocol: AdamW, cosine-decay LR with warm-up (2/4/6% options), max 2500 epochs, effective batch 16 (4 volumes x 4 crops), systematic Optuna tuning (TPE + ASHA, cyclical LR initialization, log-scale search). Fully reproducible in practice due to public code (PyTorch/MONAI) and released trained weights, although final tuned LR/weight-decay values are not printed in the text.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice + Focal loss (lambda_D = lambda_F = 1) with explicit justification: Dice+Focal chosen over Dice+CE to handle strong background/foreground imbalance, and focal loss down-weights well-classified examples to emphasize hard structures.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Clearly described: N4 bias field correction for MRI, isotropic resampling, [0,1] intensity normalization, random 96^3 crops per volume, augmentation (random intensity shift/scale, 3D flips), and sliding-window inference with 0.5 overlap. Post-processing explicitly absent (none reported).

Q10_code_availability.justification: Code and trained model weights publicly available at https://github.com/matteo-bastico/MI-Seg and in supplementary material.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice similarity coefficient is the only quantitative metric reported throughout; no Hausdorff distance, ASSD, Jaccard/IoU, or runtime/efficiency measurements despite motivating real-time applicability.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Minimal statistics only: two-fold cross-validation mean ± std (C-ViT 91.18 ± 0.68 vs conditional UNet 90.76 ± 0.55). No confidence intervals, significance tests, or p-values; with only 2 folds the std is of limited inferential value.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Strong controlled comparison: fine-tuning, joint training, X-shaped dual-stream (Valindria et al.), cycle/shape-consistent GAN translation (Zhang et al.), online mutual knowledge distillation (Li et al.) — all reimplemented on the same UNet baseline with identical data (20 MRI + 10 CT) and evaluated on the same test set; plus Swin-UNETR baseline, fine-tuning, and joint training for the C-ViT variant.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure Dice reported for all 7 cardiac substructures (MYO, LA, LV, RA, RV, AA, PA) in Tables 1-2, plus Whole Heart in Tables 2-3, with qualitative per-structure slice and 3D render comparisons.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations openly discussed: AA/PA performance decreases attributed to GT annotations extending beyond the test tool's cut vessel lengths; transformer data-hunger (C-ViT better in CV but slightly worse than conditional UNet on the small test set); reliance on a modality flag from metadata; implicitly, single small dataset.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Patient selection is fully defined by the public MM-WHS 2017 challenge protocol (all 20 CT + 20 MRI training volumes used; random but unseeded two-fold split). Concern is generalizability rather than clarity: single challenge, small cohort, cardiac pathology spectrum only, no consecutive/consecutive-clinical sampling described.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All compared methods share the same baseline architecture, training data volumes, tuning effort, and test set; evaluation uses the standardized MM-WHS online test tool, ensuring consistent outcome assessment. No blinded human/clinical evaluation was performed, and Dice-only assessment may not capture clinically relevant errors.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate. All listed outcomes appear reported, but only Dice is reported (no distance-based metrics, no inference times despite real-time motivation); standard deviations are given only for cross-validation; the C-ViT per-structure value for PA is not recoverable from the provided tables (inferable only from the mean); results favoring the method are emphasized while the test-set superiority of the UNet variant over the headline C-ViT is acknowledged but underplayed.

detailed_extraction: SUPPLEMENTARY METHODOLOGICAL DETAILS: (1) Core mechanism — Conditional Instance Normalization (CIN): CIN(z,m) = gamma_m * ((z - mu(z))/sigma(z)) + beta_m, where mu/sigma are computed across spatial dimensions per channel per sample; each modality m has its own learnable affine parameters (gamma_m, beta_m); overhead is negligible (only extra normalization parameters). (2) C-ViT encoder: LayerNorm in each transformer block replaced by CIN before both MSA and MLP sub-layers, with residual connections (Eqs. 3-4); non-overlapping 16x16x16 sub-patches linearly projected to K=768 embedding dims plus learnable positional embeddings (Eq. 5); L=8 blocks following Swin-UNETR; for Swin variant, patch-merging block normalizations are also conditioned; rationale for IN vs LN: LN normalizes across embedding dims within each patch independently, whereas IN normalizes across all patches per embedding dimension, considering the whole volume. (3) Training scheme — 'interleaved mixed training': modalities are randomly mixed within the same batches (unlike joint training's per-batch modality alternation), pushing a shared latent space; single shared decoder D(.) consumes modality-common latent spaces C^1..C^S at all skip connections. (4) Hyperparameter tuning protocol: optimal LR found via cyclical LR technique, then logarithmic search space centered on it; TPE (Tree-structured Parzen Estimator) sampling fitting GMMs to good/bad trials; ASHA early-stopping of poor trials; warm-up epochs in {2%, 4%, 6%}; weight decay tuned; batch size fixed at memory maximum (16 crops = Ns 4 x Nc 4). (5) Controlled comparison design: all Table 1 methods share the identical UNet baseline (Valindria et al., 3D UNet with pre-activation residual blocks) and identical training data (20 MRI + 10 CT per fold), strengthening causal attribution of gains to the cross-modality strategy. (6) Quantified gains: conditional UNet vs best prior method (Li et al. distillation): +0.65% mean Dice, up to +2.71% on RV; C-ViT vs Swin-UNETR baseline: +4.01% mean substructure Dice and +6.87% WH Dice; dramatic RA improvement 77.58 -> 93.39 (baseline -> C-ViT); conditional UNet reaches 90.77% mean Dice on MM-WHS CT test set. (7) Bidirectional capability: unlike assistant-only methods, the model retains/improves MRI (assistant) segmentation — C-ViT on MRI: 85.57 WH / 84.30 mean Dice vs baseline 83.32 / 81.87 (Table 3). (8) Discrepancy noted by authors: C-ViT wins in two-fold CV (91.18±0.68 vs 90.76±0.55) but the conditional UNet wins on the 20-case test set (90.77 vs 89.33), attributed to transformers being data-hungry on small datasets. (9) Practical requirement: input modality flag needed at inference, assumed available from image metadata (e.g., DICOM modality tag) without manual intervention. (10) Compute environment: PyTorch + MONAI, multiple NVIDIA V100 GPUs on IDRIS HPC cluster (GENCI allocation 2022-AD011013902); EU Horizon 2020 Marie Sklodowska-Curie grant No 945304 (AI4theSciences, PSL). (11) REVIEW CONTEXT NOTES: This is a cross-modality paper where CT is the TARGET modality (MRI is assistant), directly relevant to CT organ segmentation under label scarcity; organs covered are cardiac structures only (7 substructures + whole heart); no abdominal/thoracic multi-organ benchmark (e.g., BTCV/AMOS) used; performance figures are challenge-test-set Dice, not directly comparable to single-modality training-set-heavy leaderboards; future work stated as extension to Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (training on single labeled modality, adapting to unlabeled domains).
contribution_summary: This paper proposes a general cross-modality segmentation framework that conditions encoder normalization layers via modality-switched Conditional Instance Normalization (CIN), trained end-to-end with non-registered, interleaved mixed MRI+CT data — eliminating the need for registered image pairs, GAN-based synthetic translation, or dual-stream architectures. Building on it, the authors introduce the Conditional Vision Transformer (C-ViT) encoder (LN replaced by CIN in transformer blocks, applied to Swin-UNETR), which improves whole-heart Dice by up to 6.87% over its baseline and relaxes the data-hunger typical of ViTs. On MM-WHS 2017 with CT as target, the conditional 3D UNet variant achieves state-of-the-art cross-modality performance (90.77% mean Dice), outperforming fine-tuning, joint training, X-shaped architectures, GAN translation, and mutual knowledge distillation, while retaining high-quality bidirectional (MRI) segmentation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: SegTHOR has only 40 training + 20 test scans; the authors train on 32 scans — below the >50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: SegTHOR 2019 named, publicly available via grand-challenge website, with slice counts, in-plane resolution, and slice thickness reported. Patient acquisition criteria/demographics not given, but source is unambiguous.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split sizes given (32/8/20) but selection methodology unspecified (random vs fixed, stratification). Unexplained how metrics on the 20 test scans were computed, since SegTHOR test ground truth is held out by organizers.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process never described — no annotators, protocol, or inter-observer detail; ITK-SNAP is mentioned only for visualization.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single dataset (SegTHOR); no independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Qualitative description of 3D ResNet encoder-decoder, 3D ASPP at bottleneck, PE blocks per stage, 2x2x2 pool/deconv, 1x1x1 sigmoid head. Missing: stage count, channel widths, atrous rates, block depths — not sufficient to redraw the network.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, LR 0.003, batch size 8, 12 GB GPU given. Missing: epochs/iterations, loss, augmentation, patch/crop and inference strategy. Claimed 40-minute total training for 3D volumetric segmentation is implausible and suggests key details are omitted.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function is never stated, therefore cannot be justified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: No preprocessing described (intensity normalization, resampling, cropping all absent). Post-processing merely asserted as 'none required'.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL or repository mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five metrics defined and used: Dice, HD, VOE, ASSD, RVD — though VOE/ASSD/RVD are reported only for the proposed method, not comparators.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, variance, or repeated runs; single point estimates only.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Eight SegTHOR methods compared in Table I, but provenance of comparator values is unclear (likely copied, not re-run), comparators get only DC+HD, and the proposed scores (Dice 98.53, HD 0.24 mm) far exceed published SegTHOR results (~93-94 Dice), undermining comparability.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Only aggregate Dice reported. Paper claims good performance 'for esophagus, heart, trachea and aorta, respectively' but gives no per-organ numbers.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section or failure-case analysis; only a one-sentence future-work remark about small organs.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High — public challenge data with no patient selection criteria described; small cohort (60 scans); split procedure unspecified; evaluation on held-out test labels unexplained.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: High — no statistical testing or variance estimates; results unverifiable without released code; reported Dice (98.53) and HD (0.24 mm) are implausibly superior to all published SegTHOR entries; 40-minute training claim inconsistent with described setup.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: High — per-organ results claimed but not reported; VOE/ASSD/RVD reported only for the proposed method, preventing comparison; no failure cases; Table I is garbled; irrelevant citation [20] (sleep-quality fuzzy logic) appears in the results narrative, indicating weak editorial/reporting rigor.

detailed_extraction: Additional details: output head uses sigmoid activation for multiclass prediction (softmax expected for 4-class segmentation — likely an error or misstatement); 3D ASPP uses four atrous convolutional layers with unspecified dilation rates; PE blocks apply pooling separately along X, Y, Z axes then squeeze; channels double per encoder stage and halve per decoder stage. Missing/unreported: loss function, epochs, data augmentation, patch/sliding-window inference scheme, model parameter count, inference time. Metrics defined per Lalande et al. [10]; symmetric HD used. Visualization via ITK-SNAP. Framework PyTorch; Adam lr=0.003; batch size 8; NVIDIA 12 GB GPU. Red flags for the review: (1) reported Dice 98.53 exceeds all published SegTHOR challenge results by a wide margin; (2) SegTHOR test-set ground truth is organizer-held, yet test metrics are reported without explanation; (3) reference [9] duplicates [6]; (4) reference [20] is off-topic. Recommended for extraction as: architecture = 3D ResNet U-Net + 3D ASPP + PE attention; dataset = SegTHOR 2019 (32/8/20); organs = heart, aorta, trachea, esophagus; quality tier = Low.
contribution_summary: Proposes a hybrid 3D ResNet encoder-decoder U-Net with a 3D-adapted ASPP module at the bottleneck and Project & Excite (PE) recalibration blocks at every encoder/decoder stage, applied to multiclass segmentation of four thoracic organs at risk (heart, aorta, trachea, esophagus) on SegTHOR 2019. The contribution is an incremental combination of existing modules (ResNet, ASPP, PE), reported to achieve Dice 98.53 / HD 0.24 mm without post-processing, outperforming eight published SegTHOR methods. Validity is weak: no loss function or code, aggregate-only results, and reported scores implausibly exceed all published SegTHOR benchmarks.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Trained on 131 LiTS CT volumes (>50); test set only 35 scans, but criterion targets training size.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: LiTS training set well described (131 volumes, multi-institution, expert radiologists); test set vague — 'mixed public and private' with no description of the private portion (no demographics, scanner, ethics).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Train (LiTS) and test (35 mixed scans) stated, but no validation split, no statement of whether public test cases overlap training data, no split rationale.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: LiTS annotation implied via 'experienced radiologists' from 7+ institutes; annotation process for private test scans not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Test set partially external (private institutional scans), but composition undefined and public portion may overlap LiTS training data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Pipeline described at block level (ResNet coarse localization → parallel 2D Dense-UNet + 3D Dense-UNet → feature fusion layer, Figure 1); no layer dimensions, kernel sizes, or fusion-layer specification.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No hyperparameters, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, augmentation, or hardware reported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never mentioned, let alone justified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Histogram equalization (pre) and morphological filtering (post) named; no parameters, kernel settings, or intensity normalization/resampling details.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release stated.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Single metric only: Dice global score. No Hausdorff distance, sensitivity, PPV, or per-case Dice.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, variance, or significance testing; single aggregate 96.2% figure.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Related work contextualizes against LiTS benchmark (24 methods), but superiority claim ('relatively higher than most existing implementations') is unsupported by any quantitative comparison table.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: One global Dice for liver+tumor combined; liver-only and tumor-only Dice never separated — tumor performance unverifiable.

Q15_limitations.justification: Discussion concedes sub-100% accuracy risk in surgery, domain-shift (hospital-specific retraining), and need for clinician validation; but no failure cases shown or failure modes analyzed.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High/unclear — private test-scan selection criteria undefined; no patient demographics, inclusion/exclusion, or pathology spectrum for the 35 test cases.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate — same metric applied to all cases, but ground-truth provenance for private test scans unstated; no per-case results prevent consistency checks; possible train/test leakage via public portion undisclosed.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: High — only a favorable aggregate Dice reported; no per-structure results, no failure cases, no runtime, and an unsupported SOTA-superiority claim; negative or marginal results absent.

detailed_extraction: Task: liver and liver-tumor segmentation from contrast-enhanced abdominal CT. Pipeline: (1) ResNet-based coarse liver localization producing ROI; (2) parallel 2D Dense-UNet (intra-slice features) and 3D Dense-UNet (inter-slice/spatial features); (3) feature-fusion layer producing final segmentation. Architecture is functionally identical to H-DenseUNet (Li et al., KDD 2018) without explicit attribution — treat contribution as application/integration, not novel architecture. Data: training on LiTS (131 CT volumes); testing on 35 mixed public/private CT scans (private source unstated, presumably Hamad Medical Corporation). Preprocessing: histogram equalization on all train/test data. Postprocessing: morphological filtering removing isolated voxels and weakly connected components. Reported result: Dice global score 96.2% on the 35 test scans (liver and tumor not separated). Not reported: loss, optimizer, hyperparameters, validation split, inference time (notable given surgical 'speed' motivation), per-organ results, statistical variability, code. Clinical framing: 3D liver models for hepatic surgical planning (resection, transplant), SIRT dose planning, RECIST staging, post-treatment tracking; authors recommend semi-automatic clinician-verified use. Funding: NPRP 11S-1219-170106, Qatar National Research Fund. Conference paper (4 pages) — limited space partially explains thin methodological detail but does not change extraction verdicts.
contribution_summary: Applies a hybrid 2D+3D densely-connected UNet (with ResNet-based liver localization) to liver and tumor CT segmentation, motivated by surgical planning workflows, reporting a 96.2% global Dice on 35 mixed public/private test scans. The architecture closely mirrors prior H-DenseUNet work, and the contribution is best characterized as a surgical-context application with preprocessing/postprocessing refinements rather than a methodological advance. Evaluation is limited to a single aggregate metric with no statistical analysis, per-structure results, or quantitative SOTA comparison, limiting evidential weight for the reported performance.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 90 training ROIs (one per patient), exceeding the >50 subject threshold; augmented to ~90,000 training images via flipping and random cropping.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Clearly described: single center (First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University), Siemens dual-source 64-slice CT, arterial phase, Jan 2013–Dec 2015, pixel size 0.59–0.74mm², four tumor subtypes, tumor/kidney volume ranges reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 90/50 train/test split stated with one ROI per patient (no patient leakage), but no validation set, no cross-validation, and no description of how patients were randomized/allocated.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Detailed two-reader process: radiologist X. Zhu corrected multi-atlas kidney contours and manually drew tumor contours; radiologist L. Tang performed joint consensus review and amendments.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent dataset. Single-center in-house data only; test set from same institution, scanner, and time period as training data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully described: 13 residual blocks (39 conv layers) from ResNet, only 2 pooling layers (rationale given), dilated convolutions, 4-branch PPM with kernel sizes 2/4/8/16, architecture figure provided.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: PyTorch, SGD (momentum 0.9, weight decay 1e-5), lr 0.001 with multistep schedule [3,5,7] epochs, 14,000 iterations/epoch, batch size 4, augmentation protocol given. Minor gaps: total epochs/stopping criterion, seeds, and dependency on the coarse multi-atlas ROI extraction from the authors' prior work [4] (not reproducible from this paper alone).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted cross entropy justified quantitatively by measured class imbalance (kidney 16.93%, tumor 2.43%, background 80.64%); weights (1.0/2.0/0.2) set via preliminary experiments. Formal equation provided.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Both well specified: HU clamping [-200, 500] with rationale, 0–1 normalization with mean subtraction, ROI cropping (150×150) via multi-atlas alignment, augmentation strategy; post-processing: sub-volume concatenation with majority voting, 3D CRF, 18-connectivity largest-component analysis.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice coefficient plus mean surface-to-surface distance, both computed per patient for both structures.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Only descriptive statistics (mean ± SD, min–max ranges). No confidence intervals, no significance testing, no correction for multiple comparisons.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: 2D_PSPNet and 3D_UNet retrained on the identical training set and evaluated on the identical test set — a fair controlled comparison. Comparison breadth is narrow (no other kidney/tumor methods), but authors state no prior 3D DL attempt existed for this task.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Separate results for kidney and tumor: Dice 0.931 (range 0.871–0.961) vs 0.802 (range 0.440–0.938), surface distances reported per structure, per-patient calculation stated.

Q15_limitations.justification: Failure case explicitly analyzed (lowest tumor Dice 0.440 on ~6ml tumor with under-segmentation shown in Fig. 5), renal hilum prediction bias acknowledged (Fig. 6), GPU memory constraints on input size, and data scarcity discussed in conclusion.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Inclusion criteria are explicit (consecutive LPN patients, 2013–2015, lesioned kidneys only, one ROI per patient), but single-center, arterial-phase-only, tumor-bearing kidneys only — restricts generalizability to healthy kidneys, other phases, and other centers.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. All three networks evaluated on the same held-out test set with consistent per-patient metrics against consensus ground truth. Caveat: ground-truth kidney contours were initialized from the authors' own prior multi-atlas method [4] before correction — a potential circularity favoring their pipeline's ROI stage.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Full metric distributions (ranges, worst case 0.440) and qualitative failure cases reported; no evidence of selective outcome reporting, though no protocol/registration exists (typical for 2018).

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not in prior extraction: (1) Imaging protocol — Siemens dual-source 64-slice scanner, arterial phase only (venous phase deliberately excluded as unnecessary for LPN planning and to limit radiation dose), in-plane pixel size 0.59–0.74mm². (2) Cohort composition — four RCC subtypes (clear cell, chromophobe, papillary, angioleiomyolipoma); tumor volumes 2.11–144.82ml (mean 33.58ml); kidney volumes 85.76–262.78ml (mean 156.37ml). (3) Baseline results (Table I): 2D_PSPNet kidney/tumor Dice 0.902/0.638, surface distance 4.47±1.55/12.08±12.82 px; 3D_UNet 0.927/0.751, 4.28±1.53/2.86±0.94 px; proposed 0.931/0.802, 4.21±1.56/2.65±0.91 px. Note the 2D method's tumor surface-distance SD (±12.82 px) indicates severe outlier failures. (4) Inconsistency: text says 3D_UNet [16] but Table I lists '3D_Net [16]'. (5) Surface distances reported in pixels, not mm — hinders cross-study comparison given variable pixel size. (6) Pipeline is two-stage: coarse multi-atlas localization from prior work [4] (150×150 ROI crop) precedes the CNN, so end-to-end claim applies only to the segmentation stage; coarse-stage failure would propagate. (7) Input constraint: 64-slice sub-volumes with overlap majority-voting fusion. (8) Hardware: i7-5930K, 128GB RAM, TITAN X 12GB; no inference or training time reported. (9) Only tumor-bearing kidneys segmented (one per patient); tumor Dice strongly volume-dependent (0.440 at ~6ml vs 0.938 max). (10) 2D PSPNet produced false-positive tumor classifications; 3D context cited as the key differentiator.
contribution_summary: This paper introduces 3D_FCN_PPM, an end-to-end 3D fully convolutional network combining ResNet residual blocks, reduced pooling, dilated convolutions, and a 4-branch pyramid pooling module for joint kidney and renal tumor segmentation in arterial-phase CT angiography — reportedly the first 3D deep learning attempt for this combined task. Evaluated on 140 single-center patients (90 train / 50 test), it achieved Dice coefficients of 0.931 (kidney) and 0.802 (tumor), outperforming retrained 2D PSPNet and 3D UNet baselines on identical data, with 3D contextual information shown to be critical for discriminating tumors from adjacent tissue. Key open issues are under-segmentation of small tumors (<~10ml), prediction bias near the renal hilum, dependence on a prior multi-atlas ROI localization step, and no code or external validation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 131 LiTS CT volumes; 83 used for training in the main split (and 4-fold CV over 110 cases). Well above the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public MICCAI 2017 LiTS Challenge training set, with competition URL footnoted; 70-volume test set mentioned (excluded only because liver annotations were withheld, stated explicitly).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 83/27 train/test split of the 110 three-organ-complete cases described, plus 4-fold CV for the U-net comparison; but no validation set is described, fold construction is unspecified, and no randomization protocol/seed is given.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Liver masks come from LiTS; spleen and gallbladder manually annotated by the authors and verified by a radiologist. Annotation tool, number of annotators, and inter-rater agreement not reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No independent external cohort. All evaluation is internal to LiTS training data (4-fold CV and held-out split); the LiTS test set was not used.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: 5-level U-Net-style encoder-decoder, 2 conv + pool/deconv per level, kernel sizes and strides given, 4 bi-directional ConvLSTM extractors on top 4 skip connections, 7-slice input chunks, multi-class softmax, plus ConvLSTM equations and architecture figures with channel sizes.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: Adam (lr 1e-4), Gaussian init, batch = 7 consecutive slices, class weights (1/3/3/5) reported. Missing: number of epochs/iterations, LR schedule, data augmentation policy, framework, and code; chunk size of 7 not ablated.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted pixel-wise cross-entropy adopted from prior work [23] to address organ-size imbalance, with stated rationale; but weights are 'empirically set' with no ablation or sensitivity analysis.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly described with a figure: orientation normalization (rotation/flip so liver left, backbone bottom) and HU clipping to [-75, 175]. Post-processing is never addressed, and aggregation of predictions across overlapping 7-slice chunks is not described.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice is the only segmentation metric (per-case mean ± std). FP counts/ratio in the extirpation analysis and inference time add supplementary measures, but no distance-based (HD/ASSD) or volumetric metrics.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± std per case reported across test set and 4-fold CV; no confidence intervals, significance tests, or p-values, despite the CV design enabling them.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Rigorous ablations vs 2D U-net (single/multi-organ). SOTA comparison is limited to a qualitative claim of 'competitive' performance at ~half the inference time of Roth et al.'s hierarchical 3D FCN [25], with no numeric side-by-side results on identical data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ Dice for liver, spleen, gallbladder reported in all tables, with mean, std, max, and min (Tables I–IV).

Q15_limitations.justification: Strong: dedicated gallbladder-extirpation FP analysis (21/131 cases), Fig. 5 challenging cases (adipose infiltration, CT artifacts, lesions, cholelithiasis), acknowledged high gallbladder variance, and concrete future work (organ-detection stage).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate concern: 21 gallbladder-extirpated cases (16.03%) are excluded from the headline 110-case experiments, which mechanically inflates gallbladder Dice; the 83/27 split is random with no described randomization protocol. Partially mitigated by the separate all-131-case extirpation analysis (Tables III–IV).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low concern: all models evaluated on identical splits against the same ground truth with a consistent per-case Dice protocol. Caveat: spleen/gallbladder ground truth is self-annotated with verification by a single radiologist — no independent reference standard.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate concern: per-organ results, variance, extirpation scenario, and runtime are all reported transparently; however, the SOTA comparison is qualitative only (no numbers for Roth et al. on the same data) and no validation-set/tuning results are reported.

detailed_extraction: Network mechanics: contracting-path convolutions are applied independently per slice (authors explicitly distinguish this from a 2.5D network); inter-slice context enters only via the 4 bi-directional ConvLSTM extractors on the top 4 skip-connection levels, while the bottom level passes only the target slice's features to the expanding path. Each 7-feature-map chunk is split into forward/backward subsequences relative to the target slice, ordered farthest-first, and the two ConvLSTM outputs are stacked. Input chunks are overlapping sliding windows of 7 consecutive slices per batch; the chunk size is not ablated. Experimental design: the single-vs-multi-organ comparison uses the random 83/27 split; the U-net-vs-SSN comparison uses 4-fold CV (fold construction unspecified); no validation set, so the hyperparameter tuning procedure is unstated. Annotations: liver masks inherited from LiTS; spleen/gallbladder annotated by authors and verified by a radiologist (tool, annotator count, and inter-rater agreement not reported). Training: from scratch with Gaussian init, Adam lr=1e-4, weighted CE (background 1, liver 3, spleen 3, gallbladder 5); no data augmentation mentioned; framework unspecified. Relevance to review scope (3D segmentation): although the task is volumetric, SSN uses no 3D convolutions — it is effectively a 2D/ConvLSTM hybrid, framed as a memory-cheaper alternative to 3D FCNs (2.39 min/volume on an M40, ~half of Roth et al.'s hierarchical 3D FCN, claimed qualitatively). Extirpation analysis details: 21/131 cases (16.03%) lack a gallbladder; Dice is scored 0%/100% when the model does/does not segment gallbladder in an extirpated case, so single FP volumes dominate the mean; SSN FP ratio 80.95% (17/21) vs U-net 90.48% (19/21), i.e., 9.88% less gallbladder Dice drop for SSN; min gallbladder Dice is 0% for both models in the extirpation-inclusive evaluation.
contribution_summary: SequentialSegNet augments a U-Net-style multi-class FCN with bi-directional ConvLSTM 'sequential feature extractors' on the upper skip connections, capturing inter-slice context from 7-slice chunks while avoiding the memory and training cost of 3D convolutions. On LiTS (plus self-annotated spleen/gallbladder masks verified by a radiologist), it outperforms a multi-organ 2D U-net on all three organs under 4-fold CV (liver 95.91, spleen 91.30, gallbladder 75.57 Dice) with roughly half the inference time of a hierarchical 3D FCN. Its most distinctive contribution is a failure-mode analysis of gallbladder extirpation (~16% of cases), an under-reported scenario in prior multi-organ work, showing the recurrent model yields fewer false positives (FP ratio 80.95% vs 90.48%).

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 30 thoracic CT scans total (25 train / 5 test per fold) — below the >50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Patient population (lung cancer / Hodgkin lymphoma) and voxel resolution described, but dataset is private with no institution, scanner, or enrollment period stated.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 6-fold cross-validation with explicit 25/5 split is stated, but no validation set is described — hyperparameter and fine-tuning choices may have been informed by test folds.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual delineations of the 4 OARs plus body contour are mentioned; annotator expertise, number of raters, consensus protocol, and inter-rater agreement are not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent dataset; all results come from one private 30-scan cohort under cross-validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: 10-layer FCN (5 enc + 5 transposed-conv dec), 7×7 kernels, 5 output channels, SharpMask refinement with conv+ReLU channel equalization on skips, and CRFasRNN module with unary/pairwise formulation and BPTT training.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: SGD (lr 0.1, ×0.1 every 20 epochs), Xavier init, and augmentation are given; missing batch size, total epochs, framework, GPU, and — critically — how full 512×512×(150–284) volumes are fed to the network (patch/slice strategy unstated).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Voxel-wise cross-entropy with class weighting explicitly justified by organ class imbalance; two-step schedule (unweighted pretrain → weighted fine-tune) is specified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Zero-mean/unit-variance normalization, body-contour mask to exclude background from training loss, and augmentation (random affine + B-spline deformation on a 2×2×2 control-point grid) all described; CRF is in-network so no separate post-processing.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL, license, or version.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice Ratio only; no surface-distance metrics (HD/ASSD), sensitivity/specificity, or volumetric error.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired t-tests with per-organ p-values comparing all variants, std across folds reported, and non-significant CRF gains honestly disclosed (p=0.30–0.79).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Systematic ablation (FCN, FCN+CRF, SM, SM+CRF) plus external published baseline (OPAL label fusion); caveat: no comparison to contemporaneous DL methods (e.g., U-Net/V-Net) as published architectures.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ mean Dice ± std for every method in Table 1, with organ-specific discussion (trachea best handled by OPAL, esophagus hardest at 0.67).

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section and the 30-scan dataset size is never acknowledged, but results text candidly reports unfavorable findings (OPAL beats FCN on trachea 0.80 vs 0.72; CRF module mostly non-significant).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/High — 30 patients from a private dataset with conditions stated (lung cancer, Hodgkin lymphoma) but no inclusion/exclusion criteria, institution, scanner, or enrollment period; small sample limits generalizability.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low/Moderate — identical 6-fold CV protocol applied to all compared methods with paired t-tests; residual concerns: no validation set (possible test-informed tuning) and Dice computed against manual delineations of unstated rater provenance.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low/Moderate — per-organ results, std, and p-values reported including unfavorable and non-significant findings; however only Dice is reported, with no runtime, memory, or failure-case gallery beyond two qualitative examples.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Voxel spacing 0.98×0.98×2.5 mm; volumes 512×512×(150–284); anisotropic resolution likely motivates the 2D-style design but is never discussed. (2) CRFasRNN specifics: unary term is the unnormalized FCN output (log-likelihood); pairwise term uses two contrast-sensitive Gaussian kernels (bilateral on intensity+position, intensity-only smoothness) with learnable kernel weights ω_m and learnable compatibility µ — explicitly contrasted with the fixed-penalty Potts model. (3) Two-step training is mandatory for CRF variants: pretrain network without CRF to obtain a usable unary term, then fine-tune jointly via backpropagation-through-time. (4) SharpMask modifications: conv+ReLU on top-down paths instead of copying feature maps (to equalize channel counts with deep layers) and transposed convolutions instead of bilinear upsampling; no unpooling (differs from Noh et al. deconvnet). (5) Body-contour mask is used to exclude background voxels from the training loss — a form of foreground cropping that is a de facto preprocessing step. (6) IMPORTANT FLAG for a '3D segmentation' review: convolution dimensionality is never explicitly stated; the '7×7' kernel notation and per-layer description strongly suggest per-slice 2D convolutions despite volumetric evaluation, 3D B-spline augmentation (2×2×2 control grid), and 3D rendering of outputs. The extracted 'is_3d: true' should be treated as uncertain. (7) Memory-handling of full-resolution volumes (patch vs. full-volume training) is unreported — the main reproducibility gap alongside missing batch size/epoch count/framework. (8) Funding: EU ERDF (HN0002137) and Normandie Regional Council (M2NUM); author affiliations span Normandie Univ/LITIS (France) and UNC-Chapel Hill (USA). (9) Context: among the earliest joint multi-organ thoracic OAR deep learning works (2017), positioned against individually-segmented atlas/patch methods.
contribution_summary: This paper presents one of the first deep learning frameworks for joint segmentation of four thoracic organs at risk (esophagus, heart, trachea, aorta), combining an FCN with SharpMask-style top-down feature fusion and an end-to-end trainable CRFasRNN module that learns spatial relationships between neighboring organs. The SharpMask fusion yields statistically significant gains over plain FCN (p<0.05 for 3/4 organs) and outperforms OPAL label fusion on esophagus, heart, and aorta, while the learned CRF compatibility adds flexibility over the Potts model — though CRF gains themselves are largely non-significant. The work establishes an early baseline for joint thoracic OAR delineation, notable for honest negative results, but is constrained by a 30-scan private dataset, Dice-only evaluation, and unclear 2D vs 3D convolution dimensionality.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 105 training scans (19,608 slices) from 130 total CTs; exceeds the >50 subject threshold, though modest by current standards.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources clearly stated: 72 CTs from LUNA16, 58 from NLST. Explicit enrichment criterion: scans contain nodules/masses attached to chest wall or interstitial disease.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split numbers given per source (Table 1: LUNA16 57/15, NLST 48/10) with difficult cases in both sets, but no description of how the split was performed and no validation set mentioned.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Process described: one experienced radiologist repaired holes in LUNA16 reference masks (nodule regions excluded) and manually segmented NLST lungs. But single rater, no annotation protocol, no inter-rater agreement check.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent validation; single internal test set drawn from the same two sources as training data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: MPN structure shown in Fig. 3 and key innovations described (U-Net backbone reduced to 64 filters, residual blocks, five multi-scale prediction maps averaged, loss on all maps), but full layer-by-layer specification (kernels, strides, depth) not given in text.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Critical training details absent: no optimizer, learning rate, epochs, batch size, augmentation, or patch/slice sampling strategy. Only 2D slice-wise training (3D blocks for V-Net) is stated.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Soft Dice loss chosen to directly optimize the evaluation metric, and an HPM variant (added BCE on positives predicted <0.5) is ablated. Rationale present but brief; no discussion of alternatives (e.g., BCE+Dice, boundary losses).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: No pre- or post-processing steps described; not even stated whether none were used. Only the final-map averaging (an architectural choice) and the efficient HD computation (evaluation) are mentioned.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Four metrics: Dice, Jaccard/IoU, Hausdorff distance (2D slice-wise average), plus a task-specific coverage rate of manually labeled nodule areas.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, variance, or cross-validation; single train/test split with small test set (25 scans, 27 nodules).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Controlled ablations against V-Net and reduced U-Net on identical data (good), but published SOTA (Skourt 0.950, Negahdar 0.983 Dice) is only cited from different datasets, not reproduced for head-to-head comparison.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ task (lungs; no left/right separation). Partial credit for region-specific analysis: slice-wise performance distribution (Fig. 4) and dedicated nodule-area coverage over 27 nodules x 5 slices.

Q15_limitations.justification: Honest reporting of the underperforming HPM variant and the argument that mean Dice alone is insufficient. However, no explicit limitations section and no failure-case visualization.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Enrichment criterion is stated (lesions attached to chest wall/interstitial disease), which is appropriate for the research question, but the sampling procedure from LUNA16/NLST is unspecified and the test set is small (25 scans).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. All models evaluated identically on whole scans ('identical evaluation method' explicitly stated). Main threat: ground truth from a single radiologist with no inter-rater verification.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate. All tested configurations reported, including the one that hurt Dice (HPM) - reduces selective reporting. However, no variance/CI reporting and results derive from one test split.

detailed_extraction: DATA: 130 CTs total; 72 LUNA16 (57 train/15 test) + 58 NLST (48 train/10 test) = 105 train (19,608 slices) / 25 test (6,324 slices). Inclusion criterion: lung lesions attached to chest wall or interstitial disease. LUNA16 reference masks (generated by van Rikxoort 2009 method) rejected as GT because they exclude nodule regions; single radiologist repaired holes (LUNA16) and fully segmented NLST lungs. ARCHITECTURE: U-Net backbone with only 64 filters per conv block (UNet-S; authors report near-identical performance to full-size U-Net), residual blocks (He 2016), and 5 prediction maps at multiple scales; final output = simple average of all 5 maps; loss applied to all 5 maps (deep supervision style). LOSS: soft Dice loss; HPM variant adds BCE on positive pixels predicted with probability <0.5. TRAINING: 2D slice-wise for all models except V-Net (3D blocks); hyperparameters not reported; no validation set mentioned. EVALUATION: all metrics computed per whole scan; HD = 2D slice-wise average using exact efficient algorithm (Taha & Hanbury 2015); nodule coverage computed on 27 nodules x 5 slices (centroid +/- 2) = 135 manually labeled nodule-mask slices. RESULTS (Dice/IoU/HD/coverage): UNet-S+Res+MP 0.9845/0.9697/3.7480/87.54%; UNet-S 0.9830/0.9669/3.9381/85.18%; UNet-S+Res 0.9834/0.9675/3.9073/87.27%; UNet-S+Res+MP+HPM 0.9822/0.9652/3.8375/89.92%; V-Net 0.9783/0.9582/4.4461/52.26%. SCOPE FLAG FOR 3D-SEGMENTATION REVIEW: the best-performing model is 2D slice-wise; the only 3D architecture (V-Net) is a baseline and collapses specifically on nodule coverage (52.26%), i.e., 3D context was not shown to help here.
contribution_summary: Proposes the Multi-scale Prediction Network (MPN): a filter-reduced U-Net with residual blocks that emits five prediction maps at multiple scales, all supervised by Dice loss during training and averaged at inference. On 130 lesion-enriched thoracic CTs (LUNA16+NLST) with radiologist-corrected ground truth, MPN yields marginal gains in Dice (0.9845 vs. 0.9830 baseline) but notable gains in Hausdorff distance and nodule-area coverage (87.54% vs. 52.26% for 3D V-Net). Its main conceptual contribution is demonstrating that mean Dice hides failures on pleura-attached nodules, motivating region-specific coverage metrics for segmentation evaluation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 888 CT scans for training/validation (700/188) far exceeds the >50 threshold; test set small (20 scans) but criterion targets training size.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both public challenges clearly named and cited: LUNA16 (train/val) and VESSEL12 (test), with scan specifications given (512x512, slice thickness 0.6-2.5mm).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 700/188 train/validation split stated; testing done on fully independent VESSEL12 scans, so no test leakage.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Process described for both: training labels semi-automatic (van Rikxoort et al.), explicitly acknowledged as noisy/unvalidated; test labels expert-radiologist-validated, lobes merged into one lung label. Unusually transparent.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Evaluation on VESSEL12, an independent external dataset with expert ground truth, distinct from LUNA16 training data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: All V-Net modifications specified: early max-pooling (512x512x256 to 128x128x64), extra input-to-last-conv skip connection, filters reduced to 2/3, PReLU, batch norm, plus architecture diagram (Fig 2).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, lr=1e-3, 12 epochs, early stopping given; but batch size, framework, GPU, early-stop patience, augmentation magnitudes, and random seed all missing.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Modified Dice loss given with equation (V-Net-style), but choice not argued against alternatives; future work concedes it under-weights boundary errors.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: HU windowing [-1000, 400], depth resampling to 256 voxels, and augmentation types described, but parameter values vague and post-processing not addressed at all.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice plus ASD, with sound reasoning for why ASD is needed (Dice under-penalizes boundary errors on large organs).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Only mean Dice/ASD over 20 scans; no standard deviations, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Only compares against their own retrained standard V-Net (a baseline ablation). Cited lung SOTA (e.g., Harrison et al. PHNN) not numerically compared.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (lung); organ-level Dice and ASD reported, so no cross-organ averaging concern. No per-case distribution given, but criterion is per-organ.

Q15_limitations.justification: No explicit limitations section. Noisy training labels and V-Net stair-casing acknowledged, but no failure-case analysis; limitations must be inferred.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Patients defined entirely by curated public challenge datasets (LUNA16: nodule screening scans; VESSEL12: 20 healthy + pathological scans). No custom inclusion criteria; small test set limits generalizability to broad clinical populations.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Both models evaluated identically on the same external test set against expert ground truth using automated metrics (Dice, ASD); objective protocol. No human reading component to blind.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Only aggregate means reported — no variance, no per-case results, single baseline comparison. Unfavorable or neutral outcomes (e.g., validation curves, per-scan failures) not reported.

detailed_extraction: Test set details: VESSEL12, 20 healthy and pathological chest CTs (512x512 in-plane, max 1mm spacing); ground truth derived from lung-lobe annotations merged into a single lung label, validated by an expert radiologist. Baseline comparison: standard V-Net retrained by the authors on the same LUNA16 data with input downsampled to 128x128x64, isolating the effect of the architecture modification. Loss: Dice-overlap formulation 2*sum(p*g)/(sum(p^2)+sum(g^2)). Training: 12 epochs max, Adam lr=1e-3, early stopping on validation loss (patience value unspecified); augmentation = spatial shifting and depth-axis zooming. Scan geometry: fixed 512 in-plane, slice thickness 0.6-2.5mm, depth resampled to 256 voxels. Core experimental claim: CNNs tolerate noisy pseudo-labels for training as long as evaluation uses clean expert labels (precedent cited: Ghafoorian et al., ventricle segmentation). Key result: proposed 98.7% Dice / 0.576mm ASD vs V-Net 97.2% / 2.627mm — the ASD gap (4.5x) is the meaningful difference, localized to boundary delineation. Funding: NORTE 2020 / ERDF (NanoSTIMA). Note for multi-organ review synthesis: single-organ (lung) study; results not directly comparable to multi-organ benchmarks like V-Net/AMOS/AbdomenAtlas.
contribution_summary: The paper demonstrates that a 3D CNN can be trained on noisy, semi-automatically generated lung labels (LUNA16) and still achieve expert-grade segmentation on externally validated data (VESSEL12: 98.7% Dice, 0.576mm ASD), outperforming standard V-Net especially at lung boundaries. Architecturally, it introduces an early max-pooling layer plus an input-to-output skip connection that lets V-Net ingest full-resolution 512x512x256 CT volumes without downsampling or patching. Its main value to this review is as evidence that pseudo-labels can substitute for costly manual 3D annotation, though it is limited to a single organ and lacks statistical rigor.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 343 chest CT scans total (71 LUNA16, 195 LKDS, 62 Meinian, 15 LOLA11); with five-fold CV, ~274 scans used for training per fold, well above the 50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Four sources clearly named with URLs for LUNA16, LKDS (Tianchi), and LOLA11; slice spacing (0.5–1.5 mm) and pathological/healthy composition stated. Minor caveat: the Meinian subset (62 cases) is a private industrial dataset.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Five-fold cross-validation is stated, but fold construction is not described (random vs. stratified, patient-level vs. slice-level, whether sources were mixed across folds, presence of an internal validation set). No independent held-out test set.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process partially described: all scans manually annotated by 'an experienced radiologist' using 3D Slicer (SlicerCIP). However, no annotation protocol details, no quality control, and no inter-rater/inter-observer agreement reported (single annotator).

Q5_external_validation.justification: All evaluation is internal five-fold cross-validation on the pooled 343 scans. LOLA11 cases are folded into the same CV rather than used as an external challenge test set; no independent external cohort validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: V-net backbone (compression/expansion paths, skip connections, element-wise sums) well described with architecture figure; modifications clearly specified: PReLU instead of ReLU, group normalization instead of BN, dropout 0.5, 3D CoordConv layers (x,y,z channels normalized to [-1,1]) at the last decoding transition, softmax output for 5 lobes + background, and an auxiliary fissure/boundary output head.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: PyTorch 0.4.0, Tesla P100 16GB, input size 256×256×128, dropout 0.5, λ=1, γ=1e-5, and 5-fold CV reported. Missing: optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs/iterations, data augmentation strategy. The exact difference between the '+group norm' and 'Proposed' ablation configurations is also ambiguous.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Losses given mathematically (multi-class Dice excluding background; auxiliary boundary Dice with total loss D_lobes + λD_boundary), and the boundary auxiliary task is motivated (improve lobe distinction). However, the choice of Dice over alternatives is asserted rather than justified, and no ablation isolates the loss components' contribution (ablation covers only coordmap and group norm).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly described: downsampling/resampling to 256×256×128 and 2D U-Net lung segmentation to extract lung ROI and suppress false responses outside the lung. Post-processing explicitly stated as none (fully end-to-end, no heavy post-processing).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no repository URL or license provided (arXiv preprint only).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Despite claiming evaluation 'by several measuring metrics,' only the Dice coefficient (mean ± std) is actually reported. Processing time (12 s/case) is reported but is an efficiency, not an accuracy, metric; no Hausdorff distance, ASSD, sensitivity/specificity, or voxel accuracy.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± std of Dice over five folds reported (overall and per lobe), but no confidence intervals, no p-values, no significance testing against competing methods.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Explicit per-lobe comparison with four prior methods (Watershed, PPLS+RM/random walker, Alpha-Exp, FR-vnet) plus internal ablations (baseline V-net, +coordmap, +group norm). Caveat: it is not stated whether competing methods were re-implemented and re-evaluated on the same folds or whether numbers were taken from original publications.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-lobe Dice with standard deviations reported for all five lobes (RU 0.934, RM 0.919, RL 0.953, LU 0.958, LL 0.973) in both ablation and comparison tables, not just the average.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations briefly acknowledged: dataset contains only thin-slice CTs ('there are only thin slices in our cases'); the introduction notes partially invisible fissures and pathological lobe shape disorders as challenges, and Figure 4 illustrates typical error modes. However, no dedicated limitations section or quantitative failure analysis.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/Unclear. Case selection criteria within public datasets are not defined (e.g., why only 71 of 888 LUNA16 scans were used); the private Meinian subset (62 cases) has undisclosed selection; proportion of pathological vs. healthy cases unspecified.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-Moderate. All scans were annotated by a single experienced radiologist with the same tool (3D Slicer/SlicerCIP) and all ablations used identical hyperparameters, ensuring consistency; however, no blinded second annotator/reference standard exists, and evaluation conditions for compared methods are not confirmed to be identical.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Only Dice is reported despite a claim of 'several measuring metrics'; no per-dataset breakdown of performance; competing-method results may not be reproduced under identical conditions; no significance testing to support superiority claims; limitations discussed only superficially.

detailed_extraction:
SUPPLEMENTARY METHODOLOGICAL DETAILS:
(1) Architecture specifics: V-net compression path progressively downsamples the 256×256×128 input (feature channels doubling per stage); decoding path uses fine-grained feature forwarding (skip concatenations) and element-wise sums; deconvolution layers with 2×2 stride-2 kernels; a 5×5×5 stride-1 convolution appears in the fusion stage; final 1×1 convolution + softmax yields one-hot probability maps for 5 lobe classes + background. The auxiliary fissure/boundary head shares the same trunk network and outputs a boundary probability map supervised with Dice loss (visualized in Fig. 2 as 'Fissure output').
(2) CoordConv design: three extra channels encoding x, y, z voxel coordinates normalized to [-1,1] are concatenated to feature maps and inserted at the LAST transition of the decoding path (not throughout), acting as a 'soft constraint' that anchors lobes to anatomically correct positions to reduce inter-lobe misclassification.
(3) Regularization rationale: group normalization chosen over batch normalization because 3D CNNs are memory-limited to small batches, causing inaccurate BN statistics; PReLU chosen over ReLU to alleviate vanishing gradients; dropout 0.5 during training.
(4) Loss equations: multi-class Dice loss over classes c=1..5 (background excluded), smoothed by γ=1e-5; total loss D_total = D_lobes + λ·D_boundary with λ=1.
(5) Ablation results (average Dice): baseline V-net 0.795 → +coordinate maps 0.916 → +group norm 0.929 → full proposed model 0.947; the largest single gain comes from CoordConv (+0.121). Note: the exact delta between '+group norm' and 'Proposed' (presumably boundary loss and/or lung-ROI preprocessing) is not explicitly enumerated.
(6) SOTA comparison (average Dice): Watershed 0.880; PPLS+RM (George et al.) 0.888; Alpha-Exp (Giuliani et al.) 0.866; FR-vnet (Ferreira et al.) 0.926; Proposed 0.947. Prior methods' two documented failure modes (false response outside lung; inter-lobe misclassification) motivated the U-Net lung-ROI preprocessing and CoordConv additions respectively.
(7) Efficiency: ~12 s total processing time per case on a single NVIDIA Tesla P100.
(8) Annotation: single experienced radiologist using 3D Slicer with SlicerCIP extension; no inter-observer variability data.
(9) Reproducibility gaps: optimizer, learning rate schedule, batch size, epochs, and data augmentation not reported; no code release.
(10) Scope note for review: this paper targets pulmonary LOBES (intra-organ/sub-organ lung substructures) rather than whole organs; relevant to the review as 3D multi-class segmentation of lung anatomy, including both healthy and pathological lungs.
(11) Funding: NSFC grants 81801778 and National Key R&D Program of China 2018YFC0910700.
(12) Reporting quirks: table numbering in the paper is inconsistent (two 'Table 2/3' labels); OCR shows ablation table and SOTA comparison table with overlapping captions.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes an end-to-end 3D pulmonary lobe segmentation network based on V-net, enhanced with 3D CoordConv layers that inject normalized positional coordinates at the final decoding stage to resolve inter-lobe misclassification, combined with U-Net-based lung ROI preprocessing, group normalization, and an auxiliary fissure/boundary Dice loss. Evaluated by five-fold cross-validation on 343 chest CTs from four sources (LUNA16, LKDS, Meinian, LOLA11), it achieves a state-of-the-art mean Dice of 0.947±0.044 versus 0.926 for the best prior method (FR-vnet), with ~12 s processing per case. The main insight—that explicit positional encoding plus boundary-aware auxiliary supervision substantially improves lobe segmentation—is convincingly demonstrated via ablations, though validation is limited to internal cross-validation without external testing, statistical significance testing, or code release.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 210 annotated KiTS19 cases (30 validation, 90 official test, ~180 training) — well above the 50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public KiTS19 challenge data, cited (Heller et al.); contrast-enhanced CT with 3mm inter-plane resolution stated.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 30/210 as validation, remainder training (implied 180), 90 official test cases scored via challenge online server. Random seed not given, but split is clear.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single dataset only. The official test server is held-out KiTS19 cases, not an independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Two-stage pipeline and VP/SSCN concepts well explained, but SSN internals only 'similar architecture and setting as V-Net' — no layer/channel/depth specs.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, LR 1e-4 decayed x0.7 every 50 epochs to 1e-6, PyTorch 1.0.0, GPU models, augmentation given. Missing: batch size, total epochs, CE class weights.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss (V-Net) and weighted CE (SSN) stated with equations, but the choice is never justified and the CE weights are unspecified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Fully described: z-crop to 16, intensity clip [-79, 304], dataset-statistics normalization, 6x z-stretch in VP, rotation/sagittal-stretch (0.9-1.1) augmentation; LCC postprocessing.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/moderate. Fixed public challenge cohort and server-scored test set limit cherry-picking, but no patient inclusion criteria, demographics, or acquisition sites reported in-paper.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. All methods evaluated on the same validation split and official server, but baselines were re-implemented by the authors (Roth et al. run on a different GPU: Tesla V100 vs TITAN Xp) with no blinding or statistical testing.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: High. Tumor-only Dice despite a two-class task (kidney class omitted), no variance or CIs, no failure cases, and best results bolded without discussion of the validation-to-test performance drop.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) SSN label encoding is binary on foreground points: 0=kidney, 1=tumor. (2) SSCN built with 'similar architecture and setting as V-Net' for fairness — exact configs by reference only. (3) 6x z-stretch corresponds to 3mm inter-plane vs 0.5mm in-plane resolution; motivation is avoiding interpolation artifacts on anisotropic CT (resolutions 0.5/1/3mm cited). (4) Table 1 (mangled by PDF extraction) correctly reads: valid/test Dice — V-Net 67.3/62.7, Roth 69.5/63.8, Roth(-) 31.1/26.3, Roth(+) 73.6/67.6, Proposed(-) 69.4/60.4, Proposed 84.9/79.7. Note: prior extraction lists Proposed(-) as '60.4 valid / 60.4 test'; the valid-set value is 69.4 per column order. (5) Coordinates-only ablation (Proposed(-) 69.4/60.4 vs Roth(-) 31.1/26.3) is the paper's key robustness evidence for geometric learning. (6) Efficiency table: Proposed 2.5K MiB, 0.22 s/sample, 2.7M params, 9.3G FLOPs vs Roth(+) 21.6K MiB, 7.17 s, 18.6M params, 558.7G FLOPs (~9x memory, ~33x FLOPs reduction). (7) Whether the two stages are trained jointly or sequentially is not stated; separate losses (Dice / weighted CE) imply separate optimization. (8) Cyst false-positive reduction claimed qualitatively via Fig. 4 visualizations only, no quantitative cyst FP rate. (9) Scope note for review: kidney + tumor only, single dataset, no multi-organ abdominal segmentation despite citing Roth et al. multi-organ work. (10) Reported latency ('Time', s/sample) is not explicitly labeled train vs inference.
contribution_summary: HybridNet is a two-stage model combining a V-Net foreground segmenter with a Submanifold Sparse Convolutional Network (SSCN) that operates on a voxel-to-point-cloud representation of the foreground, enabling whole-ROI context learning, native handling of CT anisotropy via z-axis stretching, and ~9x lower training GPU memory than full-ROI patch-based 3D FCN baselines. It achieves 84.9 (validation) / 79.7 (official test) tumor Dice on KiTS19 with only 2.7M parameters and 0.22 s/sample, and a coordinates-only ablation shows superior geometric robustness versus conventional voxel CNNs. Its main novelty is being the first hybrid voxel + point-cloud pipeline for 3D medical segmentation, though evaluation is limited to a single dataset with tumor-only reporting.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 300 CT scans (210 train / 90 test); well above 50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public KiTS19 MICCAI 2019 challenge dataset, clearly cited (Heller et al.) with cohort description (partial/radical nephrectomy patients).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit: challenge-defined 210/90 test split; internal 168/42 train/validation split; 5-fold cross-validation for training.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Relies on KiTS19 reference labels; annotation process (raters, protocol, inter-rater agreement) not described in this paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single dataset (KiTS19) only; no independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fig. 1 gives full three-stage pipeline, per-stage patch sizes (80x160x160, 48x192x192, 56x160x160), encoder channel progression, DCB specs (3x3x3, dilation 2), Leaky ReLU + instance norm.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (Adam), LR (1e-4), framework (PyTorch), GPU (V100), CV scheme, loss weights given; missing batch size, epochs/iterations, LR schedule, augmentation parameters.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Hybrid dice + distance-map-weighted CE justified by class imbalance; hard-example dice term (IoHem = union minus intersection) justified for stages II/III; formulas and per-stage lambda values (0.5/0.5/0 vs 0.5/0.5/5) provided.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Foreground-only z-score normalization, kidney-region masking for refine net, augmentation list (elastic, rotation, gamma, crop), connected-component postprocessing all described; augmentation parameters unspecified (minor).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice only (kidney/tumor/composite); no surface-based metrics (HD95, ASSD) or others.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or variance across the 5 folds; ablation deltas reported as point estimates.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Table 2 compares against 4 other top KiTS19 teams on the hidden test set; plus 5-condition internal ablation (Stage I -> +II -> +III -> +DCB -> +HL).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Separate kidney, tumor, and composite Dice reported in both ablation (Table 1) and challenge comparison (Table 2).

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section; authors only concede kidney Dice (0.9674) trails most rival teams. No failure-case analysis.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low. Full public KiTS19 cohort (300 nephrectomy patients) with challenge-defined splits; no cherry-picking evident. Internal 168/42 split described as random.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. Test-set scores computed by challenge organizers (results.kits-challenge.org) under identical criteria across teams; however, ablation claims rest on unvalidated point estimates without statistical testing.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Only Dice reported (no surface distances, runtime, or fold variance); qualitative Figure 2 shows 3 selected favorable validation cases; no failure cases presented despite acknowledged weaker kidney performance.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Training used 5-fold cross-validation on the 168-case internal training split; all models trained from scratch. (2) Stage I low-res net operates on 30x80x160x160 downsampled volumes for VOI localization; its upsampled prediction is concatenated with the original CT as input to Stage II (30x48x192x192); Stage III tumor refine net (30x56x160x160) receives Stage II output with intensities outside kidney zeroed. (3) Encoder follows generic 3D U-Net channel doubling (C->2C->4C->8C->16C->32C) but the last two encoder levels replace strided pooling/downsampling with stride-1 dilated convolutions (rate 2), keeping bottleneck at D/4,H/8,W/8 resolution to preserve small-object detail. (4) Loss: L = 0.5*L_dice(all) + 0.5*wd*L_CE + lambda3*L_dice(IoHem), where wd is a distance-transform boundary weight map and IoHem is the symmetric-difference voxel set between ground truth and previous-stage prediction; lambda3 = 0 (stage I) or 5 (stages II/III). (5) Ablation gains on validation set: Stage II +1.6% kidney Dice over Stage I; Stage III +1.5% tumor Dice; DCB +0.8% kidney / +1.1% tumor; hybrid loss +0.9% kidney / +1.0% tumor; final validation composite 0.901. (6) On the KiTS19 test leaderboard the method ranked 2nd overall (composite 0.9064) with the best tumor Dice (0.8454) but the lowest kidney Dice (0.9674) among the five compared teams. (7) Qualitative results: 3 validation cases visualized in coronal view (Fig. 2), including low-contrast and organ-attached tumor scenarios. (8) Equal first-author contribution (Hou, Xie); industrial affiliation Ping An Healthcare Technology; no training/inference times reported; no future work stated.
contribution_summary: Proposes a triple-stage coarse-to-fine self-guided cascade (low-resolution localization net -> full-resolution segmentation net -> tumor refine net) in which each stage consumes the previous stage's prediction as guidance, motivated by nnU-Net. Two technical novelties: dilated convolution blocks replacing deep-layer pooling to retain small-tumor detail, and a dynamic hybrid loss (dice + distance-map-weighted cross-entropy + hard-example dice on the previous stage's error voxels). Achieved 2nd place in KiTS19 with kidney/tumor/composite Dice of 0.9674/0.8454/0.9064, with ablations attributing ~0.8-1.6 Dice points to each component.
