Q1_dataset_size.justification: 60 MRI volumes reported for training/val, but these are CHAOS T1 in-phase/out-of-phase + T2 SPIR sequences, i.e. ~20 unique subjects across 3 sequences each. Meets the >50 threshold only if volumes (not subjects) are counted.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: All sources clearly named and cited: CHAOS challenge (train/val + CT test), TCIA pancreas-CT (43 CT), BTCV (47 CT), with ground truth provenance for TCIA/BTCV attributed to Gibson et al.'s supplementary annotations.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split structure described (60 MRI train/val, 20 CHAOS CT + 43 TCIA + 47 BTCV test; 10 CHAOS CT reserved for fine-tuning and excluded from its evaluation), but the MRI train/validation ratio is never quantified; model selection by best validation loss only.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth provenance is documented (CHAOS-provided annotations; Gibson et al. annotations for TCIA/BTCV), but the annotation process itself (raters, protocol, inter-observer variability) is not described anywhere.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Strong: model trained purely on MRI is evaluated on three independent public CT cohorts (CHAOS CT, TCIA, BTCV) with per-cohort results, which is itself the paper's central claim (zero-shot cross-modality, cross-dataset generalization).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: padded-convolution 3D U-Net (Çiçek et al.), 32 base kernels doubling per encoder level, 3×3×3 convs, 2×2×2 max-pooling, fixed 3D Sobel edge-enhancement branch computing gradient magnitude concatenated to input, and separate convolutional autoencoder whose frozen encoder supplies the shape-prior loss. Architecture figure provided.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Hyperparameters reported: Adam, initial LR 0.001, batch size 1, 200 epochs for both training stages, λ=0.001, resize to 128×128×96, augmentation (translation/rotation/scaling), model selection by validation loss, GTX 1080 Ti. Minor gaps: no random seed, no train/val split ratio, no LR schedule.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Both losses are given as equations and the shape-regularization weight λ is adopted from Oktay et al., but Dice loss is justified only as 'commonly applied' — no discussion of alternatives for the domain-shift setting.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing stated (resize to 128×128×96 for GPU memory, random translation/rotation/scaling augmentation) and postprocessing explicitly stated as none — the absence is deliberate and reported, which satisfies the criterion.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no repository URL or statement of intent to publish code. Framework (TensorFlow; PyTorch for the cycleGAN baseline) is the only implementation detail.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Only Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC, %) is reported. No Hausdorff distance, ASSD, sensitivity/specificity, or volume error.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean±std per test cohort is reported (e.g. 69.2±25 average), giving dispersion, but no confidence intervals, no significance tests, no p-values; ablation differences (e.g. EE vs SP) are not tested statistically despite high BTCV variance (±29).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Internal comparisons are solid — ablations (U-Net, +SP, +EE, +EE+SP), supervised fine-tuning baseline, and a cycleGAN pseudo-CT baseline — but no comparison to published state-of-the-art results on the same benchmarks (e.g. no V-Net/nnU-Net numbers or literature DSCs on BTCV).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver), so per-organ results are trivially complete; additionally, results are broken down per target domain and per ablation variant rather than reported only as an average, and qualitative examples (Fig. 2) accompany the table.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly acknowledged: does not beat supervised fine-tuning; poor BTCV performance (55.1%); cycleGAN baseline failure analyzed (PNG conversion, artifacts, adversarial instability); scope limited to one organ, with multi-class extension deferred to future work.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. All cohorts are well-defined public challenges (CHAOS, TCIA, BTCV) with fixed test sets, and the 10 CT volumes used for fine-tuning were transparently excluded from that baseline's evaluation. However, CHAOS subjects are healthy volunteers, limiting representativeness of clinical patient populations, and patient-level vs volume-level independence (20 subjects yielding 60 MRI volumes) is not discussed.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. A single metric (DSC) was applied identically across all cohorts and ablations, and the same third-party ground truths (Gibson et al.) were used for TCIA/BTCV evaluation, ensuring consistency. But evaluation was performed by the authors with no blinding, no inter-rater reference, and the high per-cohort variance (BTCV ±29) suggests unstable per-case behavior that is not investigated.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All ablation variants and baseline results are reported, including unfavorable ones (the method loses to fine-tuning; the cycleGAN baseline performed worst), and failure modes are discussed. Main reporting gap is the exclusive use of DSC with no secondary metrics or inferential statistics.

detailed_extraction: Two-stage training pipeline: (1) convolutional autoencoder trained 200 epochs on ground-truth masks with Dice loss; (2) segmentation network trained 200 epochs with combined loss L_total = L_unet + λ·||f_enc(y) − f_enc(ŷ)||₁, λ=0.001 taken from Oktay et al.'s ACNN; autoencoder encoder and Sobel kernels frozen during stage 2. Edge enhancement concatenates the 3D Sobel gradient-magnitude volume to the input, giving a 2-channel input. Resizing to 128×128×96 motivated by GPU memory. CycleGAN pseudo-CT baseline used Zhu's and Isola's public PyTorch implementations, with source MRI converted to PNG slices — authors attribute its poor performance (39.1 avg DSC) to this conversion and to abdominal translation being harder than cranial. Key ablation finding: low-level edge enhancement contributes more than the learned shape prior (EE-only 65.0 avg vs SP-only 48.7 avg vs combined 69.2 avg; vanilla 44.6 avg). Zero-shot method approaches the fine-tuned baseline on TCIA (81.7 vs 82.8) but gaps remain on CHAOS CT (75.3 vs 91.6*) and BTCV (55.1 vs 66.2). *Fine-tuned CHAOS figure evaluated on only 10 of 20 CT volumes. No training or inference time reported; hardware limited to a single GTX 1080 Ti. Relevant to the review's CT-segmentation scope only as a cross-modality (MRI-trained) method — no CT training data used at all.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a zero-shot MRI→CT domain adaptation strategy for 3D liver segmentation that requires no target-domain data, combining (a) fixed 3D Sobel-kernel edge enhancement to bias the network toward modality-invariant contour/shape features and (b) an autoencoder-derived latent shape-prior regularization added to the Dice loss. Ablations show edge enhancement is the dominant factor, and the combined model improves vanilla 3D U-Net from 44.6% to 69.2% average DSC across three independent CT cohorts, approaching supervised fine-tuning on TCIA (81.7% vs 82.8%) without seeing any CT during training. It is the first application of contour- and shape-based regularization to zero-shot cross-modality medical segmentation, though results are single-organ and clearly below supervised fine-tuning.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 24 training CT volumes, half the >50-subject threshold; 36 test scans have hidden ground truth and cannot be used for local training/validation.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source identified as the public 2019 ISICDM liver CT segmentation challenge (URL provided) with image counts and fixed 1x1x5 mm3 resolution, but no scanner, contrast phase, patient demographics, or pathology details.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Scheme is clearly stated: 3-fold cross-validation on the 24 annotated training volumes plus evaluation on the fixed 36-volume challenge test set; only fold-construction detail is missing.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual annotations for the training set are confirmed, but no annotator expertise, protocol, consensus procedure, or inter-rater agreement is reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: The 36-volume test set is independent of training data with hidden labels scored by the challenge organizer, but it comes from the same challenge distribution — not a truly external institution/cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: The cascaded pipeline (2D U-Net -> 3D FCN -> level-set) is well described, but network internals and hyperparameters are deferred entirely to prior works [8] (Z-Net, prostate) and [9] (3D FCN, subcortical MRI), borrowed cross-organ and cross-modality.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Training hyperparameters only 'same as [8,9]'; no optimizer, learning rate, epochs, batch size, framework, or GPU stated in this paper. Level-set weights (mu=0.1, lambda=1.5, alpha=-1.5) are given, and key references are named, enabling partial reconstruction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss (2D U-Net) and cross-entropy (3D FCN) are stated with no rationale or justification for either choice.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described: intensity windowing [-200, 250], 256x256 axial resampling for 2D U-Net, 1x1x1 mm3 resampling for 3D FCN, liver-mask tissue removal, +20-pixel ROI crop, erosion + median filter for level-set initialization, slice-by-slice evolution.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice (mean/STD/max/min) is the only quantitative metric; the surface-distance renderings in Fig. 3 are qualitative with no numeric Hausdorff/ASSD values.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Only descriptive mean +/- STD across 3 CV folds; no confidence intervals, significance tests, or p-values supporting the +5.69% improvement claim (n=3 folds).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Comparison is limited to ablation against the authors' own 3D FCN and 2D U-Net components; no external state-of-the-art method is benchmarked (H-DenseUNet is cited but not compared numerically).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Both target structures are reported separately: liver DSC 96.31% and tumor DSC (72.45% CV / 74.26% test) with per-fold max/min for tumor.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section or failure-case analysis; limitations are only implicit — leakage with single indicators (Fig. 4 ablation) and min DSC of 40.04% revealing difficult cases.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High — single public challenge cohort of only 24 training scans; no inclusion/exclusion criteria, demographics, scanner, or contrast-phase information; generalizability beyond this challenge is unknown.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low — DSC was applied uniformly and test-set labels were hidden and scored by the challenge organizer, limiting experimenter discretion; minor residual concern from unreported CV fold composition.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate-to-High — Dice-only reporting, a single 'representative' case visualized (favorable-case selection possible), no limitations or failure-case section, and test-set performance cannot be independently verified beyond the reported organizer score of 74.26%.

detailed_extraction: Level-set formulation: distance-regularized level set (Li et al. 2010) with energy epsilon(phi) = mu*Rp + lambda*Lg + alpha*Ag; weights mu=0.1, lambda=1.5, alpha=-1.5 (expansion/balloon mode); evolution stops at steady state of the gradient flow. Enhanced edge indicator gmax = max(gi, gp): gi is the normalized inverse gradient of Gaussian-smoothed image (Gaussian sigma not stated); gp is derived from unsupervised fuzzy c-means probability estimation followed by Canny edge detection, normalized to [0,1] (FCM cluster count not stated). Automatic initialization: erode 3D FCN tumor mask, apply median filter -> S3D, define binary phi0 = -c0 inside S3D, +c0 outside (c0 value not stated). Networks: 2D U-Net trained on 256x256 axial slices for liver-vs-background with Dice loss; 3D FCN trained at 1x1x1 mm3 with both liver and tumor labels using cross-entropy; architectures/hyperparameters inherited from Zhang 2019 (Z-Net, prostate) and Wu 2019 (multi-atlas-guided 3D FCN, subcortical MRI) — i.e., transferred across organ and modality. Native 1x1x5 mm3 data resampled to isotropic 1 mm3 implies 5x interpolation along z. Quantitative results: liver DSC 94.45% (2D U-Net alone) -> 96.31% (cascaded); tumor DSC (3-fold CV) 66.76 +/- 17.64% (3D FCN) -> 72.45 +/- 13.41% (proposed), max 91.03 vs 89.61, min 40.04 vs 27.85; challenge test DSC 74.26%. Ablation (Fig. 4): level-set using gi-only or gp-only leaks due to inaccurate edges; mixed gmax converges closest to ground truth. Framework, GPU, training/inference time, and number of model parameters are not reported. Funding: National Key R&D Program of China (2017YFC0112404) and NSFC (81501546).
contribution_summary: Proposes a fully automatic coarse-to-fine liver tumor segmentation pipeline in which a cascaded 2D U-Net + 3D FCN localizes and refines the liver and roughly localizes the tumor, and a distance-regularized level-set refines tumor contours. The key novelty is an enhanced edge indicator gmax = max(gi, gp) fusing image gradients with an unsupervised fuzzy c-means probability map, combined with automatic contour initialization from the eroded FCN output — removing the manual ROI initialization required by prior level-set methods. The level-set refinement raises mean tumor DSC from 66.76% to 72.45% (3-fold CV, +5.69%) with the largest gains on challenging cases (min DSC 27.85% -> 40.04%), and achieves 74.26% on the hidden challenge test set.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 519 training CTs from LUNA; far exceeds the >50 threshold. Eval sets: NSCLC 141, LOLA11 55.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: All three public. LUNA/LIDC-IDRI provenance, subset usage, and mask provenance described in detail; NSCLC (radiogenomic, tumor-annotated) and LOLA11 (challenge) cited with sizes.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit: LUNA subsets 0-6 train / 7 val / 8-9 test (519/86/171). NSCLC split into 94 rest + 47 juxtapleural; LOLA11 test-only.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Process described honestly: LUNA masks are algorithm-generated [18] with quantified reliability (IoU 0.95±0.05 vs 0.96±0.04 for second human observer). Weakness is disclosed, not hidden.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Trained on LUNA only; independently evaluated on NSCLC (pathological) and LOLA11.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: V-Net (referenced, Fig. 7) + structure correction CNN fully drawn with per-layer tensor sizes and concatenation skips (Fig. 8); lightweight filter choice criterion stated.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, lr=1e-4 both stages, dice loss (stage 1), BCE (stage 2), max 20 epochs, model selection by val loss, 25x mask augmentation, corruption prob 0.8, 10-50mm corruption sizes, Keras/TF. Batch size not stated in excerpt.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Stage 2 mask-only + BCE justified via shape-prior argument; stage 1 dice loss inherited from V-Net default without discussion. Equations given for both.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Complete: HU rescaling equation, +1024 offset, [0,2000] clip, /2000 normalization, linear interp to 128³; post: NN upsample, 2-voxel dilation bound, parallel flood-fill at -500 HU, Algorithm 1 pseudocode.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL given.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice, IoU (LOLA11), ASD, tumor voxel recall (NSCLC), plus runtime. Well beyond Dice+1.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± std reported (recall 0.869±0.187; ASD 0.41±0.12mm). No CIs, p-values, or significance tests vs baselines.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: 7 baselines: U-Net, V-Net, 3D U-Net, SegNet, Dilated CNN (each with dice and CE variants), P-HNN, multi-instance GAN.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Left lung (0.9975), right lung (0.9974), trachea, and total lung reported separately.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit failure modes: pleural effusion (empty stage-1 mask, unrecoverable), corruption-size range must cover tumor size, lower resolution → worse ASD than full-res 2D SegNet, algorithmic LUNA GT.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low concern: public datasets with predefined subset splits; juxtapleural subset (n=47) selection criterion stated. Caveat: LUNA GT is algorithm-derived, so training labels inherit that method's biases (e.g., handled error cases).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low concern: identical pipeline and metric set applied across all baselines and all three datasets; with/without flood-fill ablation reported.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate: failure cases and limitations disclosed; however, best-performing configuration is highlighted per dataset and absence of released code/weights prevents independent verification.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond existing extraction: (1) Stage 2 takes corrupted masks ONLY as input — no CT intensity — forcing the network to learn lung shape prior; output is S×J with J=3 (left lung, right lung, background), while stage 1 V-Net uses C=4 (adds trachea). (2) Corruption generation pipeline: PyLIDC extracts binary nodule masks from LIDC/IDRI XML; each of the 2-4 radiologist annotations per nodule used as a separate sample; masks enlarged via nearest-neighbour interpolation to 10-50mm (assumption: tumor shape ≈ enlarged nodule); placement at randomly chosen Sobel edge voxels (axial slices); overlapping V-Net mask erased, non-overlapping retained; 25x augmentation; corruption applied with probability 0.8. (3) Training: Adam lr=1e-4, model selection by minimum validation loss, V-Net max 20 epochs. (4) Flood-fill (Algorithm 1): bidirectional sweeps along each axis, bounded by 2-voxel dilation of upsampled mask, cutoff -500 HU, Numba-parallelized. (5) LUNA GT provenance: masks from automated method [18], which handled error cases (small nodules, sarcoidosis, pneumonia); reported IoU 0.95±0.05 vs 0.96±0.04 for a second human observer on LIDC. (6) Motivating constraint: CAD nodule-detection pipeline must finish <5 min; classical shape-prior methods take 189-586s, proposed method 1.47-2.69s. (7) Funding: Siemens Healthineers + NSF IIS-1715985/IIS-1812606; Stony Brook–Siemens collaboration. (8) Future work: pseudo-label pathological CTs with the full pipeline, retrain stage 1 to eliminate stage 2.
contribution_summary: A three-stage lung segmentation pipeline (V-Net → 3D structure-correction CNN → parallel flood-fill) in which the correction stage is trained exclusively on synthetically corrupted masks from normal lungs, eliminating the need for pathological ground-truth annotations. It recovers at least 15% more juxtapleural tumor voxels than CNN state-of-the-art while maintaining accuracy on normal lungs, and runs in ~2.7s per CT versus 189-586s for classical shape-prior methods. The core novelty is the corruption-based augmentation that injects lung shape prior without requiring tumor-segmented training data.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 120 LiTS training volumes (131 labeled in total) clearly exceeds the >50 subject threshold; 3D-IRCADB adds 15 training volumes. Adequate for liver/tumor segmentation.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both public benchmarks clearly identified and cited (LiTS [27]; 3D-IRCADB [28]) with basic characteristics: contrast-enhanced CT, heterogeneity in plane/space resolution, tumors present in 75% of 3D-IRCADB cases. No patient demographics or acquisition-site details reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split sizes explicitly stated: LiTS 120 train / 11 validation plus the 70-volume official challenge test set; 3D-IRCADB 15 train / 5 test. The randomization/selection procedure for the 3D-IRCADB split is not described (minor caveat).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual slice-by-slice labeling described with class encoding (0=background, 1=liver, 2=tumor). However, annotator expertise, number of raters, inter-rater agreement, and quality-control procedures are not reported; LiTS annotation provenance not detailed.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Two datasets are evaluated, but the model is retrained separately on each (3D-IRCADB has its own 15/5 split). There is no cross-dataset generalization test or independent external-cohort (out-of-distribution/multi-center) validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Thorough description: Spatial-Net (2D encoder-decoder, dense connections, 5-stage downsampling to 1/32), Temporal-Net (3D counterpart with two depth-wise downsamplings and anisotropic schedule), SEL mechanics (GlobalAveragePooling3D squeeze, 2 FC + activation excitation), and explicit tensor shapes for all intermediate features (Eqs. 2-10).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (SGD), LR schedule (0.001, x0.1 every 20 epochs), momentum (0.9), 80 epochs x 2000 steps, loss balance (alpha=0.6, beta=0.4), framework (TensorFlow), hardware (GTX 1080Ti), training from scratch/random init all specified. Minor gaps: per-class weight values (w_ic) unspecified, batch size only inferable from input shapes, no data augmentation details.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Explicitly justified: weighted cross-entropy addresses the severe liver/tumor-vs-background class imbalance; Jaccard distance chosen for complementarity with a standard segmentation evaluation metric.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing fully specified: HU truncation to [-200, +250] (standard abdominal window), overlapped slice-based inputs (stack i-1/i/i+1 as RGB, 2-slice overlap, input 224x224x8), and Eq. 1 center-point slice-range selection for redundancy reduction. Post-processing explicitly none beyond converting the 3-class output to binary masks for metrics.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or pre-trained model release mentioned anywhere in the paper; no repository URL provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice (DSC) plus VOE, RVD, MSD, ASD, and tumor-burden RMSE (0.014)/MAE (0.049) reported across both datasets.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests, or p-values reported in the available text or extracted results; single point estimates only.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive benchmarking against 12 published methods (Han, Kaluva, Yuan, Vorontsov, Chlebus, Li, Jin, Tian, Qin, Y. Han, Men, Seo) on both datasets, plus a conceptual taxonomy of context-learning paradigms (Table I).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver and tumor/lesion results reported separately for each dataset (liver DSC 0.968/0.965 vs tumor DSC 0.722-0.824/0.688), not just averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: A dedicated discussion section (Sec. IV) is announced but truncated in the available text; no explicit limitations or failure-case analysis is verifiable. Only an implicit constraint is evident: input restricted to 224x224x8 due to GPU memory.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/Unclear. Public benchmark cohorts used without patient-level inclusion/exclusion criteria, demographics, scanner, or center information. Additionally, the slice-range selection (Eq. 1) depends on ground-truth liver indices, an unrealistic deployment assumption that could bias reported performance favorably.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. Standardized LiTS test set and a uniform metric suite (DSC/VOE/RVD/MSD/ASD) were applied consistently across all compared methods; however, ground-truth-dependent input conditioning and absence of uncertainty quantification weaken confidence in outcome assessment.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate concern. Core quantitative outcomes appear fully reported per organ and per dataset; but no variance/significance testing is given, ablation results and limitations cannot be verified (Sec. IV-V truncated), raising concern about selective reporting of favorable configurations.

detailed_extraction:
CONTEXT TAXONOMY (Table I): Prior work classified into 4 context-learning paradigms - (1) pure 2D CNNs (Han, Y.Han, Kaluva, Qin, Seo); (2) pure 3D CNNs on small voxels (Dou, Deng, Alalwan, Meng, Yuan); (3) cascaded 2D CNNs (Vorontsov, Budak, Albishri, Chlebus, Men); (4) serial 2D-3D without flow/fusion mechanism (Bellver, Li, Zhang, Jin, Tian). The proposed method is presented as the only 'full-context' design with explicit 2D/3D fusion via SEL.

DATA PREPARATION: (a) HU truncation to [-200, +250] following standard abdominal window settings to suppress irrelevant tissues and emphasize hypodense tumors; (b) overlapped slice-based inputs - blocks of s=(224,224,8), each image stacks slices (i-1, i, i+1) as RGB channels so consecutive blocks overlap by 2 slices, preserving inter-slice continuity while retaining full in-plane resolution (contrast to voxel cropping in pure 3D CNNs); (c) redundancy reduction via Eq. 1: center slice drawn from the GT liver range [min_index, max_index] anchored at a random liver/tumor pixel index r - NOTE: this couples input selection to ground truth, an evaluation caveat for real-world deployment.

ARCHITECTURE DATAFLOW: Spatial-Net: 8x224x224x3 input -> dense-connected encoder (1/2...1/32) -> decoder -> r_S (8x224x224x64); 1x1 conv -> m (reshaped to 1x224x224x8x3) serving dual roles: deep-supervision-like signal concatenated with the input for Temporal-Net, and input to SEL. Temporal-Net: t = concat(i, m) (1x224x224x8x4); anisotropic 3D downsampling ((1/2,1/2,1/2), (1/4,1/4,1/4), (1/8,1/8,1/4), (1/16,1/16,1/4), (1/32,1/32,1/4)) -> r_T (1x224x224x8x64). SEL: v = r_S' + r_T -> squeeze (GlobalAveragePooling3D) -> excitation (2 FC + activation) -> channel-reweighted r_SE -> 1x1 conv -> 3-channel output (background/liver/tumor). Trained end-to-end.

LOSS: L = alpha*weighted-CE + beta*Jaccard-distance with alpha=0.6, beta=0.4, M=3 classes; per-class weights w_ic enlarge the minority-class (liver/tumor) penalty, but the actual weight values are not reported.

TRAINING: from scratch with random initialization; SGD, lr 0.001 decayed x0.1 every 20 epochs, momentum 0.9; 80 epochs x 2000 steps; TensorFlow; NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti. Batch size not explicitly stated (tensor dims suggest 8); data augmentation not reported; training and inference runtimes not reported.

EVALUATION NOTES: Separate training runs per dataset (LiTS and 3D-IRCADB); tumor Dice substantially lower and more variable (0.688-0.824) than liver (0.965-0.969); tumor burden additionally quantified via RMSE/MAE. No demographic/clinical subgroup analysis, no reader study, no inference-speed benchmark.

REVIEW CAVEATS: Results tables, ablations, discussion (Sec. IV) and conclusion (Sec. V) are truncated in the available full text; several assessment items rely on the previously extracted data. Funding: NSFC grant 61831014 and Shenzhen S&T projects; no conflict-of-interest statement visible in the provided text.
contribution_summary: Proposes a 'full-context' CNN that jointly learns 2D intra-slice context (Spatial-Net with dense connections) and 3D inter-slice context (Temporal-Net), fused through a squeeze-and-excitation layer to bridge the trade-off between preserving in-plane spatial detail and exploiting volumetric temporal information in CT. This is complemented by a ground-truth-informed overlapped slice-based input scheme and a weighted cross-entropy + Jaccard distance loss to counter extreme class imbalance. Achieves competitive liver segmentation (DSC 0.968 LiTS test; 0.965 3D-IRCADB) and tumor segmentation (DSC up to 0.824 LiTS test) against 12 prior methods, though tumor Dice remains markedly lower than liver Dice and no code is released.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 20 GT subjects (16 training per fold), well below the >50 threshold. Partial mitigation via scaling augmentation to 240 volumes (>5,000 2D slices), but augmentation adds no independent subjects. Authors acknowledge this.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: SLIVER07 public benchmark clearly described: MICCAI challenge, 20 training scans with GT + 10 test cases; challenge context and original evaluation metrics cited.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 5-fold CV explicitly described: five mutually exclusive image groups, each group serves as validation once; partitions made before augmentation so no patient leakage across folds.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: GT used is the SLIVER07-provided annotations; the annotation process itself (who, how, inter-observer) is not described by the authors.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent validation. SLIVER07 evaluation server unavailable, so only internal 5-fold CV on the 20 labeled scans; the 10 test cases were never evaluated.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Described as a standard 2D fully convolutional U-Net: 512x512 input, 5-stage encoder/decoder, 3x3 convs, 20% dropout, with figure. Per-level channel counts not stated in text; relies on figure and 'common one' reference.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: Adam (lr=1e-5, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, zero decay), 10 epochs, 20% dropout, augmentation protocol, and NCDF parameter a=0.25 are given. But framework, GPU, batch size, and the mean-shift bandwidth parameters are unspecified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never stated anywhere in the paper.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described: NCDF enhancement (zero sub-average-HU voxels, Gaussian-erf enhancement of high-HU, a=0.25), isotropic 1.0 mm resampling, 12-resolution scaling augmentation (0.7-1.5 mm), crop/pad to 512x512; post-processing mean-shift histogram algorithm step-by-step.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL or repository mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice plus VOE, RVD, ASSD, MSSD, RMSD — six metrics matching the SLIVER07 challenge protocol.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive only: median Dice across 5 folds and per-fold tables. No confidence intervals, no significance tests, no p-values.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compares against prior methods ([10], [31]-[34]) and internal ablations (Types A-D), but comparison uses literature-reported numbers under a different protocol (challenge server vs internal 5-fold CV); no method re-implemented under matched conditions.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver); per-fold liver Dice and all auxiliary metrics reported in detail (Tables IV-VII).

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly discussed: 80% smaller per-fold training set vs prior work, 3.83 VOE points behind most accurate prior method, and evaluation server unavailability forcing internal CV.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Used the full SLIVER07 labeled training set with fixed pre-augmentation partitioning (no cherry-picking), but n=20 subjects from a single 2007 challenge dataset with no external cohort limits generalizability.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. Same automated metric pipeline applied consistently across all folds; however, all evaluation was performed internally by the authors (no external/blinded assessment), and the median fold was selected as the representative result.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All four configurations (Types A-D) and per-fold results reported; limitations candidly disclosed. Caveat: several exact metric values (RVD/ASSD/MSSD/RMSD) are only in tables, reducing verifiability from text alone.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Pipeline is three stages — NCDF normalization/enhancement, 2D U-Net per-slice segmentation, mean-shift histogram refinement; the two novel components are positioned as plug-ins for any U-Net-based method. (2) Mean-shift histogram mechanics: 2D segmentation stack projected to per-axis 1D frequency histograms (x, y, z), normalized by max bin, mean-shift clustered, largest cluster retained to form a 3D bounding box that prunes over-segmented regions — a cheap pseudo-3D context mechanism compensating for the 2D network's lack of inter-slice awareness. (3) Ablation design: Type A (baseline zero-mean/one-SD), B (NCDF only), C (mean-shift + traditional normalization), D (both); combined configuration improved all five folds, with largest gain on fold 1, reaching median Dice 0.95. Notably, NCDF alone could worsen results by increasing over-segmentation before mean-shift correction. (4) Motivation is clinical speed: liver cancer is the highest-mortality cancer in Thailand (Jaccard index cited), and segmentation is one step in a multi-step diagnostic workflow where total time matters. (5) Speed claim: 0.38 s/slice, ~38 s/CT vs up to 360 s for the most accurate prior method (~9.5x faster) at 3.83 VOE points lower accuracy. (6) Gaps for reproduction: loss function, deep-learning framework, GPU hardware, batch size, and mean-shift bandwidth all unreported; only 10 training epochs stated. (7) The 10 SLIVER07 test scans were never evaluated due to the dead challenge server — reported performance is 5-fold CV only.
contribution_summary: This paper presents a fast liver segmentation pipeline combining a 2D U-Net with two lightweight plug-in components: a CDF-based image enhancement (NCDF) that suppresses unlikely regions during preprocessing, and a mean-shift clustering over per-axis projection histograms that adds compact 3D context post-hoc to remove over-segmentation. On SLIVER07 via 5-fold cross-validation, the full configuration achieves a median Dice of 0.95 at ~38 s per CT volume, deliberately trading modest accuracy against slower prior methods (~9.5x speed advantage) for time-sensitive clinical workflows.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 70 post-hysterectomy patients (~13,000 CT slices), with 62 fully-annotated acquisitions (~11,000 slices) used. Exceeds the >50 subject threshold, though patient-level (not slice-level) sample size is modest.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source institution clearly named (Radiation Center of Hua Xi Hospital, Sichuan University, China) and population defined (post-hysterectomy patients). However, no imaging acquisition details provided (scanner vendor, slice thickness, spacing, kernel, contrast phase) and no patient demographics.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 10-fold cross-validation described (randomly rearranged data, 9 folds train / 1 fold test). Critical ambiguity: unclear whether splitting was performed at patient level or 2D slice level — slice-level splitting would introduce data leakage from adjacent sections of the same patient. No separate validation set described for hyperparameter tuning.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth delineated by a single experienced radiation oncologist at the Radiation Center. No annotation protocol, guidelines, quality control, or inter-observer verification described. The authors themselves acknowledge ground truth inaccuracy in at least one case (over-sized bladder contour in Fig 5), underscoring annotation quality concerns.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent dataset validation. All evaluation performed via internal cross-validation on the same single-center cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Core modification clearly described: dilated convolutions (rates 1,2,4,8; 3x3 kernels; receptive fields 3x3→63x63) replacing standard convolutions in the innermost and penultimate U-Net++ layers; Conv blocks (four 3x3 convs + ReLU + 2x2 max-pooling); Up-models with three upsampling stages; 256x256 input. Missing: filter counts per level, total network depth, and precise placement diagram of dilated blocks.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Framework (Keras/TensorFlow), optimizer (Adam), learning rate (0.0001), batch size (16), iterations (1.5k), batch norm + dropout, and detailed augmentation parameters (rotation 12°, shift 0.1, shear 0.1, zoom 0.02, 0.3 unlabeled-sample abandonment) are reported. However, the loss function and dropout rate are not specified, precluding full reproduction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: The loss function is never mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre-processing well described: CLAHE chosen over HE and AHE with visual comparison (Fig 1) to enhance local contrast while limiting noise amplification; augmentation strategy detailed. Post-processing steps (e.g., connected-component filtering, CRF) are entirely absent.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or data availability statement provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Only Dice Similarity Coefficient is used for segmentation accuracy (plus training time per iteration, which is an efficiency not a quality metric). No Hausdorff distance, ASSD, sensitivity/specificity, or volume agreement.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± SD reported per organ (interpreting the 'r' glyph as ±) and boxplots provided (Fig 6), but no paired significance testing, p-values, or confidence intervals to support the claim that DD-UNet++ significantly outperforms U-Net++.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Comparison limited to an internal ablation (standard U-Net++ vs. DD-UNet++). No benchmarking against external published methods (e.g., vanilla U-Net, FCN, or the DDCNN of Men et al. [26] cited as related state of the art for the same task).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure DSC with SD reported separately for bladder, CTV, and rectum for both networks (Table I), plus per-structure timing (Table II) and qualitative per-organ visual comparisons (Fig 5).

Q15_limitations.justification: Authors candidly discuss ground-truth quality issues (an incorrectly enlarged manual bladder contour), the cost of careful manual delineation, and planned extensions. However, no systematic failure-case analysis (e.g., which patients/organs failed, small-structure behavior, boundary errors) is provided.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate-to-high risk. Single-center cohort (Hua Xi Hospital) with no explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond post-hysterectomy status; acquisitions were excluded for 'lack of manual annotations' without a defined rule, and the mismatch between 70 patients and 62 analyzed acquisitions is not fully explained.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate risk. Outcomes assessed consistently (same DSC definition, smooth coefficient 0.0001, 10-fold CV) for both networks under identical hardware/training configuration; however, ground truth from a single unverified annotator and the possibility of slice-level (rather than patient-level) CV splitting could inflate performance and compromise fair assessment.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate risk. Only favorable headline metric (DSC) reported; no distance-based boundary metrics, no statistical significance testing, no quantified failure analysis; negative or unfavorable per-case results are not reported, though limitations of the ground truth are qualitatively acknowledged.

detailed_extraction: STUDY AIM: Automatic delineation of clinical target volume (CTV) and organs at risk (OARs: bladder, rectum) on post-hysterectomy pelvic CT for adjuvant radiotherapy planning. MODALITY/APPROACH: 2D slice-wise segmentation of 256x256 CT images (NOT volumetric 3D segmentation — relevance caveat for a 3D-segmentation review; no inter-slice context exploited). DATASET: ~13,000 CT images from 70 post-hysterectomy patients; 62 acquisitions with complete annotations (~11,000 slices) retained; collected at Radiation Center of Hua Xi Hospital, Sichuan University; annotations by a single experienced radiation oncologist; some acquisitions excluded due to missing annotations. METHODS: (1) Baseline: standard U-Net++ (nested dense-skip encoder-decoder); (2) Proposed DD-UNet++ ('double-deck dilated U-Net++'): standard convolutions replaced by dilated convolutions with rates (1,2,4,8) in the innermost and penultimate layers, expanding receptive field from 3x3 to 63x63 without resolution loss or added depth; authors argue the penultimate layer benefits most because small-kernel downsampling limits contextual information. Conv block = 4x (3x3 conv + ReLU) + 2x2 max-pooling; Up block = 3 upsampling layers restoring 256x256 output. PRE-PROCESSING: CLAHE (selected over HE/AHE to enhance local contrast and edges while suppressing noise amplification). DATA AUGMENTATION: cropping, scaling, piecewise-affine transform, rotation 12°, translation 0.1 (H/W), shear 0.1, zoom 0.02, random abandonment of unlabeled samples at ratio 0.3 (motivated by class/label imbalance). TRAINING: Keras + TensorFlow backend; Adam optimizer; LR 0.0001; batch size 16; 1.5k iterations; batch normalization + dropout (rates unspecified); loss function NOT reported. EVALUATION PROTOCOL: 10-fold cross-validation (split granularity — patient vs. slice — unspecified; no validation fold for tuning reported); slice-wise inference; DSC with smoothing constant 0.0001. RESULTS (DSC, DD-UNet++ vs U-Net++): bladder 93.2%±4.2 vs 91.2%±3.7; CTV 89%±3.6 vs 85%±2.6; rectum 87.6%±3.6 vs 84.7%±2.1; mean improvement +2.97%. COMPUTATIONAL COST: 204s vs 198s per iteration (+6s); hardware: Intel i7-8700 (3.2 GHz), NVIDIA RTX 2080 Ti. VISUAL ANALYSIS: overlay comparisons (Fig 5) revealing an erroneous oversized manual bladder contour; DSC boxplots per organ (Fig 6). CONTEXT: Positioned against prior pelvic work (DDCNN by Men et al.; multi-task random forests by Gao et al.; U-Net/FCN variants). NOVELTY CLAIM: first application of U-Net++ to CTV+OAR segmentation in post-hysterectomy CT. FUTURE WORK: extend to more pelvic organs, further accuracy gains. NOTE FOR REVIEW: reported SD glyph appears corrupted ('r' likely '±'); conference venue (software quality/security companion) rather than a medical imaging venue; single-center, single-annotator, 2D-only, no external validation, no code release — findings should be treated as preliminary internal evidence.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes DD-UNet++, a modified U-Net++ that replaces standard convolutions with dilated convolutions (rates 1, 2, 4, 8) in the innermost and penultimate layers to enlarge the receptive field and capture global pelvic context without added depth or resolution loss. On a private single-center dataset of ~11,000 CT slices from 62 post-hysterectomy acquisitions, DD-UNet++ modestly outperforms standard U-Net++ in 10-fold cross-validated Dice scores for bladder (93.2% vs 91.2%), CTV (89% vs 85%), and rectum (87.6% vs 84.7%) at negligible additional training cost (+6s/iteration). The authors claim it is the first application of U-Net++ to CTV and OAR segmentation in post-hysterectomy pelvic CT.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 66 patients total, marginally above the >50 threshold; however, no train/test split is reported so the effective training size is unknown and likely falls below 50. Small dataset is acknowledged by the authors as a limitation.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source institution clearly named (West China Hospital of Sichuan University, private dataset) and DICOM format mentioned. However, no patient demographics, scanner parameters, slice thickness, voxel resolution, acquisition protocol, or inclusion/exclusion criteria are reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No split methodology described anywhere. Results are reported on an ambiguously defined 'validation set' (stated in conclusion and shown in Fig. 7 boxplot) with no test set, no split ratios, and no cross-validation scheme; risk of data leakage is unquantifiable.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth implied to be expert manual contours ('expert's manual label' in Fig. 6 discussion), but the annotation process is undescribed: number of raters, expertise level, annotation tool, contouring protocol, and inter-observer handling are all missing.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation. Model evaluated only on the single private West China Hospital dataset; generalizability to other centers/scanners unknown.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Good conceptual description: 3D U-Net encoder-decoder with 3D conv blocks, Instance Normalization, Leaky ReLU, 2x2x2 upconvolutions, concatenation skip connections, and residual elementwise summation ('Add'), plus an architecture figure. Missing quantitative details: number of levels, feature maps per level, kernel sizes, network depth, parameter count. Note an internal inconsistency: text states Instance Normalization while Fig. 5 legend says 'Batch Norm'.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: Keras framework, hardware (RTX 2080 Ti 11GB, i7-8700), batch size 1 (memory-limited), glorot uniform initialization, and Dice loss with backpropagation reported. Missing critical hyperparameters: optimizer type, learning rate, epochs/iterations, LR schedule, negative slope of Leaky ReLU. Without code, full reproduction is not possible.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice coefficient loss is stated but never justified; no discussion of alternatives (e.g., cross-entropy, compound losses) or why Dice loss suits the class-imbalance in pelvic organs.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing is the paper's most thoroughly described element and its claimed novelty: background cropping, DICOM-to-3D conversion, and a four-channel input (original, AHE 8x8 tiles, AHE 100x100 tiles, Laplacian edge map), supported by mathematical formulation (HE/CDF equations) and illustrative figures. No post-processing is used or needed to be described.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository link provided; no statement about availability.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Only DSC for segmentation accuracy; runtime (2.1 s vs 0.9 s for V-Net) is the sole additional metric and measures efficiency, not segmentation quality. No boundary/distance metrics (Hausdorff distance, ASSD), sensitivity, or IoU.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests. Fig. 7 boxplots provide only descriptive distribution of validation Dice per organ; comparative claims are not statistically supported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Three baselines compared (V-Net; Gao et al. 2015; Shao et al. 2015) with per-organ DSC in Table 1. However, it is not stated whether baselines were retrained/reimplemented on the same 66-patient dataset or numbers copied from original papers (which used different data), making cross-study DSC comparisons methodologically questionable; baselines are also dated (2015-2016).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ DSC reported for bladder (91.20%) and rectum (81.84%), including per-organ boxplot distributions (Fig. 7) and per-organ comparison against all baselines (Table 1); rectum underperformance relative to Shao et al. is transparently reported.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations explicitly discussed: small dataset, rectum prediction volatility due to less rectum training data, longer inference time from deeper network (2.1 s vs 0.9 s), and scope restricted to expanding path plus data augmentation; future work directions given.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: HIGH - Single-center, single-vendor private dataset of 66 patients with no stated inclusion/exclusion criteria, no demographics, and unknown recruitment/consecutive-sampling procedure; highly susceptible to selection bias and poor external generalizability.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: HIGH/UNCLEAR - No defined held-out test set; results reported on a 'validation set' with unspecified relationship to training data (possible tuning-on-test leakage). Unclear whether comparison baselines were evaluated on identical data under identical conditions. No blinding of evaluation; only one accuracy metric used.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: MODERATE - Favorable transparency in reporting weaker rectum results and limitations; however, failure cases are not individually analyzed, the claim that accuracy 'basically meets the clinical requirements' is unsubstantiated, no IRB/ethics statement, and potentially unfavorable outcomes (e.g., formal statistical comparison, test-set results) are absent.

detailed_extraction: VENUE/CONTEXT: Published at IEEE QRS-C (Software Quality, Reliability and Security Companion) - a software engineering venue, not a medical imaging venue, which may indicate different peer-review depth than MICCAI/IEEE-TMI-type outlets; should be flagged during review screening. CLINICAL MOTIVATION: Radiotherapy planning for bladder cancer (>80,000 new US cases in 2019); manual contouring takes 20-30 min/patient and suffers inter/intra-operator variability (citing Collier et al. 2003); segmentation supports CTV-to-PTV expansion workflows. ARCHITECTURE DETAIL: Figure 5 legend components: UpConv 2x2x2, MaxPool, 3DConv+Normalization+Leaky ReLU, Add (residual), Concat; residual connections add lower-level outputs to upper-level 3D conv outputs via elementwise summation (ResNet-inspired, He et al. 2016); expanding-path convolutions halve feature-map count; network trained from scratch (no pretrained weights). INCONSISTENCY: body text cites Instance Normalization (Ulyanov et al. 2016) while figure legend reads 'Batch Norm'. FOUR-CHANNEL INPUT (claimed novelty): channels = (1) original cropped CT, (2) AHE 8x8 tile, (3) AHE 100x100 tile, (4) Laplacian edge-enhanced image; authors claim it improves accuracy, convergence, and prevents overfitting (doubles as implicit augmentation), but no ablation isolating each channel's contribution. EVALUATION: DSC formula provided; qualitative overlays in Fig. 6 (bladder green, rectum red/yellow) with claim that network contours are sometimes 'closer to the real shape than the manually delineated outlines' but 'reduces the accuracy in fact' - an unclear/contradictory statement. TIMING: average 2.1 s/case vs 0.9 s for V-Net, attributed to deeper network; acceptable clinically per authors. COMPARISON VALIDITY CAVEAT: Table 1 DSC values for Gao et al. and Shao et al. likely quoted from their publications on different datasets - direct comparability not established. MISSING REPORTING ELEMENTS: no IRB/consent statement, no demographics, no scan parameters (kVp, slice thickness, resolution), no optimizer/LR/epochs, no ablation of residual connections or channels, no failure-case images, no test/validation separation, no code. CLAIMS VS EVIDENCE: superiority claim rests on +0.1% bladder DSC over Gao et al. (91.20% vs 91.10%) without significance testing; rectum result is below one baseline (81.84% vs 84.05%).
contribution_summary: The paper presents a residual-learning-enhanced 3D U-Net combined with a novel four-channel input preprocessing scheme (original CT, two adaptive histogram equalizations with different tile sizes, and a Laplacian edge map) for automatic bladder and rectum segmentation in pelvic CT for radiotherapy planning. On a private 66-patient single-center dataset it achieves mean DSC of 91.2% (bladder) and 81.8% (rectum), marginally outperforming V-Net and two 2015 regression-based methods on bladder at the cost of slower inference (2.1 s vs 0.9 s). The contribution is incremental-combining established components (3D U-Net, residual connections, contrast enhancement)-and the evidence is substantially limited by the small dataset, undefined train/test protocol, absent statistical analysis, and no external validation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 90 abdominal CT scans; with 9-fold cross-validation, ~80 subjects per training fold, comfortably above the >50 subject threshold. Multi-centre (NIH, Vanderbilt, UCL).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources fully characterized: 43 subjects from Cancer Imaging Archive Pancreas-CT (NIH Clinical Center; pre-nephrectomy kidney donors / patients without major abdominal pathology or pancreatic lesions) and 47 from BTCV challenge (Vanderbilt; metastatic liver cancer / ventral hernia patients). Voxel sizes (0.6–0.9 mm AP/LR, 0.5–5.0 mm IS) and cropped field-of-view ranges documented.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 9-fold cross-validation over 90 subjects clearly specified; network architecture fixed a priori to avoid variant-selection bias. Minor caveats: no separate held-out test set and folds share partial training data — both explicitly acknowledged by authors as limitations.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Reference standards: public labels reused where available; remaining organs segmented by an imaging research fellow under supervision of a board-certified radiologist (8 years GI CT/MRI experience) using ITK-SNAP 3.2 and Matlab 2015b under a harmonized protocol. Surgically absent organs (7 gallbladders, 1 left kidney, 1 esophagus) explicitly identified and handled. Released publicly (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1169361).

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation on an independent/disjoint dataset; all evaluation is 9-fold CV on the same 90 scans with overlapping training data across folds. Authors explicitly state an independent disjoint evaluation would be valuable.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Exemplary architectural documentation: dense feature stacks (no 1x1 bottlenecks), V-network downsampling/skip/upsampling design, dilated convolutions, batch-wise spatial dropout with dependent Bernoulli distributions, trainable spatial prior — all defined mathematically plus a full layer-by-layer parameter table (Table II); ~879k trainable parameters; supplementary implementation guidance provided.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (Adam, epsilon/lr=0.001), batch size (10; 8 in ablations), iterations (5000 = 625 epochs), data augmentation, hardware (Titan X Pascal/P100), and training time (~6 h/instance) all reported; trained model in NiftyNet model zoo, reference segmentations on Zenodo.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Label-smoothed probabilistic Dice + L2 regularization; Dice hinge losses (thresholds 0.01 and 0.10 introduced after warm-up at iterations 25 and 100) explicitly justified by extreme class imbalance (esophagus 0.09% vs liver 11.7% of voxels). Loss behavior characterized and empirically ablated (NoHinge variant).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (manual cropping to rib cage/abdominal cavity and liver/spleen-to-kidney extent, resampling to 144^3, affine augmentation with 0–10% skewed subregions) and postprocessing (curvature-flow smoothing, connected-component filtering keeping components >10% of organ volume) fully described with parameter selection rationale; quantitative sensitivity analyses of cropping shifts (+/-5%) and post-processing components provided.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Trained DenseVNet publicly available via NiftyNet model zoo (niftynet.io/model_zoo); completed reference segmentations and subject identifiers released (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1169361); batch-wise spatial dropout implementation identified in NiftyNet codebase.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Three complementary metrics: Dice coefficient, symmetric mean boundary distance, and symmetric 95% Hausdorff distance, each formally defined.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Sign tests for correlated data (chosen for skewed accuracy differences, accounts for within-fold correlation), Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (alpha=0.05) applied separately to primary and secondary analyses, confidence intervals reported (Table VI), missing organs excluded from aggregate statistics with rationale.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Rigorous head-to-head comparison: VNet and VoxResNet retrained with identical loss/optimization/post-processing (fair DL baselines), DEEDS+JLF (top-performing MALF method from BTCV challenge), plus literature-wide comparison table (Table V, 16 prior methods) and an 11-variant architecture ablation.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ median (and mean) Dice, mean boundary distance, and 95% Hausdorff reported for all 8 organs for every comparator and every ablation variant (Tables III-IV); qualitative 25th/50th/75th percentile visual examples provided.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated limitations paragraph (no blinding during development, non-exhaustive hyperparameter optimization, between-fold training overlap, fidelity-vs-clinical-utility gap, cropping variability sensitivity); failure analysis included: gallbladder 13/84 cases with Dice <0.50 (6 cholecystectomy patients affecting training), duodenum hardest organ across all methods.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low. Multi-centre public datasets (NIH, Vanderbilt) plus local data with described clinical populations; however, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and consecutive recruitment are not stated, and the specific populations (kidney donors, metastatic liver cancer, ventral hernia) may limit generalizability to broader pathology spectra rather than introduce selection bias per se.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. Objective automated metrics and identical post-processing applied consistently across all compared methods; reference standard created by a single fellow under radiologist supervision without reported inter-rater reliability; authors were not blinded to manual segmentations during algorithm development (acknowledged, though CV ran only after development froze the design).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Per-organ results for all methods, complete ablation results including null findings (dilated convolutions, spatial prior, hinge loss, batch-wise dropout all non-significant in 46/48 comparisons), missing-organ volumes, and failure statistics transparently reported; supplementary material contains additional outcomes.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not captured in prior extraction: (1) Image properties: voxel size 0.6-0.9 mm AP/LR and 0.5-5.0 mm IS; cropped FOV 172-318 mm AP, 246-367 mm LR, 138-283 mm IS (209-471 x 32-450 voxels), resampled to 144^3 for network input with segmentation output at 72^3. (2) Architecture specifics: 9-class output (8 organs + background); dense feature stacks at 72^3/36^3/18^3 with nf=4/8/16 channels per unit (stack outputs 20/80/160 channels); dilation rates 3 and 9 in the high-resolution stack; spatial prior is a low-resolution trainable 3D map (12^3) bilinearly upsampled and added to V-network logits; total 879k parameters. (3) Baseline adaptations: VNet trained in Caffe with a modified multi-class Dice gradient including epsilon=0.01 stability constant for missing organs; VoxResNet adapted by adding output channels, trained with identical loss/optimization/post-processing as DenseVNet; DEEDS+JLF used deedsRegSSC (published abdominal CT registration parameters) and PICSL MALF tool (default JLF parameters). (4) Ablation findings: removing dense connections is catastrophic (spleen Dice 0.74-0.78 vs 0.96; NoDenseHigh matched parameters, proving connectivity rather than capacity drives gains); V-structure critical (NoVHigh recovered only 38-82% of the gap); 3-resolution ShallowV approximates full DenseVNet, so most multi-scale benefit comes from minimal structure; NoDil, NoPrior, NoHinge, NoBSDO, and Deterministic inference statistically indistinguishable from DenseVNet in 46/48 comparisons - these components are omittable, and inference mode (deterministic vs Monte Carlo, 30 samples) can be chosen by memory/time constraints. (5) Robustness analyses: outward 5% crop shift (outside augmentation range) reduced Dice by 0.03+/-0.06; inward 5% (within augmentation range) changed Dice 0.00+/-0.04; removing connected-component filter or smoothing upsampling changed median Dice <0.005, MAD <0.1 mm, HD <1.1 mm. (6) Runtime comparison: DL inference <1 s deterministic, 8-15 s Monte Carlo; DEEDS+JLF required 60 s per pairwise registration plus 78 min label fusion of 80 atlases. (7) Ablation experiments used batch size 8 (vs 10) for memory-fair comparison with NoBSDO. (8) Statistical methodology: sign test selected for correlated data due to skewed accuracy differences; FDR correction performed separately for primary (algorithm) and secondary (architecture) analyses. (9) Missing organs due to prior surgery: 7 gallbladders, 1 left kidney, 1 esophagus excluded from aggregate metrics; segmented volumes (ideally 0) reported in supplementary Table II.
contribution_summary: This paper introduces DenseVNet, a memory-efficient 3D fully convolutional network combining DenseNet-style dense feature stacks, a shallow multi-scale V-structure, batch-wise spatial dropout, dilated convolutions, and a trainable low-resolution spatial prior, for registration-free segmentation of eight abdominal organs (pancreas, esophagus, stomach, duodenum, liver, spleen, gallbladder, left kidney) from CT. In 9-fold cross-validation on 90 multi-centre scans, it achieved significantly higher Dice than VNet, VoxResNet, and the DEEDS+JLF multi-atlas method for all organs (e.g., pancreas 0.78 vs 0.71-0.74; esophagus 0.76 vs 0.66-0.69; duodenum 0.63 vs 0.56-0.60), with the largest gains on small organs. Ablation studies established dense connectivity and multi-scale structure as the critical accuracy drivers, while showing dilated convolutions, spatial prior, hinge loss, and Monte Carlo inference can be omitted without significant performance loss.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 40 training volumes from FLARE22 labeled set — below the >50 threshold; adequate only for a lightweight proof-of-concept.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: FLARE22 challenge named and labeled/unlabeled subsets distinguished, but no patient demographics, scanner, or acquisition details.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 40/10 split stated; no validation set, no random seed, no cross-validation.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process (who, how many raters, inter-rater agreement) never described; inherited implicitly from challenge data.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single internal split of FLARE22; no independent cohort or comparison to official FLARE22 leaderboard.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Full spec: 4-level encoder/decoder, two 3×3×3 convs + ReLU per level, BN, transposed-conv upsampling, 13 output channels, 1.328M params, 33.263G FLOPs, architecture figure.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (Adam), lr schedule (1e-3, ×0.99/5 epochs → 1e-6), Kaiming init, framework versions, and hardware given; missing batch size, epoch count, augmentation, λ value, and per-stage training details.

Q8_loss_function.justification: WCE + Dice equations provided, but choice is not justified and λ / class weights are unspecified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Both stages precisely specified: coarse spacing 4.4×2.5×2.5mm, cap 128×176, patches 64×128×176; fine ROI resize ≤48×144×192. No post-processing claimed.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL or statement of intent.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC + ASSD + SSD, all with equations, reported per organ for both methods.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, std devs, or significance tests anywhere; single test set of 10 cases.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Only a self-implemented 3D U-Net baseline; no comparison against published FLARE22 entries or nnU-Net itself despite citing it as state of the art.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Complete per-organ DSC/ASSD/SSD tables for baseline and proposed method, plus coarse-stage per-organ figures.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly reports weak small-organ performance (duodenum DSC 0.65, adrenal glands ~0.7) and concedes SSD is worse than the baseline; future work stated.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/moderate — data from FLARE22 challenge with random 40/10 split, but no inclusion/exclusion criteria or population description.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate — both methods evaluated identically on the same 10-case test set with standard metrics; offset by absence of statistical testing and single-run results.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate — no variance reported, and qualitative figures show only successful cases (Figure 11); no failure visualizations despite admitted small-organ weakness.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Pipeline trains one fine-segmentation network per organ (13 dedicated networks) using ROI crops derived from the coarse mask; coarse stage operates on full abdomen at reduced resolution, causing jagged edges the fine stage corrects. (2) Coarse-stage per-organ DSC/ASSD/SSD shown only graphically (Figs. 4-6); exact coarse values not tabulated. (3) Baseline 3D U-Net configured nnU-Net-style: spacing 3.5×2.0×2.0mm, patch 80×128×160, >10× the parameters of Tiny-CED Net, 5.77GB vs 1.91GB GPU memory during inference (<25s). (4) FLARE22's unlabeled set deliberately excluded — strictly fully supervised. (5) Minor inconsistency: loss described as 'weighted cross entropy + Dice' with trade-off λ, but λ value and class weights never given. (6) Reporting gaps vs. extraction fields: no post-processing, no training time, no license, no benchmark reproduction, no release version — all null. (7) Funding: NSFC 62173014, Beijing NSF L192057. (8) Single-run experiments; no evidence of multiple seeds or ensembling.
contribution_summary: Proposes a two-stage coarse-to-fine framework (Tiny-CED Net, a 1.328M-parameter lightweight 3D U-Net variant) that segments 13 abdominal organs from whole CT volumes using <2GB GPU memory and <25s inference, targeting labs without high-end GPUs. On a 40/10 split of FLARE22 it reaches 0.83 average DSC, slightly beating a much larger 3D U-Net baseline (0.81) on DSC and ASSD, at the cost of higher surface distance deviation (SSD) and persistently weak small-organ accuracy (duodenum, adrenal glands). Main novelty is the low-memory coarse-localize-then-fine-segment trade-off rather than architectural innovation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: No dataset of subjects is described. Evaluation consists of one clinical case (hepatocarcinoma patient) and public OsiriX sample volumes (MAGIX/PHENIX/MELANIX) used only to benchmark rendering FPS. Far below any n>50 threshold; no training data exists at all.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources are named but not described: Tongji Hospital (HUST) radiology acknowledged for 'fundamental resources' and OsiriX DICOM sample sets cited for visualization tests. No cohort size, scanner, or acquisition parameters reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Not applicable and not reported — the system uses no learning-based components (Graph-Cut, Hessian filter, region growing), so no train/validation/test split exists.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: No ground truth annotation process described. The only reference standard is postoperative displacement measurement of one resected tumor (512 ml) versus the preoperative estimate (533 ml).

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation. Single internal case demonstration; the authors state a 'comprehensive clinical evaluation' is planned for the future.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: No network architecture — the paper uses classical methods (Graph-Cut interactive segmentation, anatomical-feature-based automatic liver segmentation, improved Hessian filter + adaptive multi-scale region growing for vessels, marching cubes, CUDA ray-casting). These pipelines are described only at a high level with no algorithmic parameters. Paper is out of scope for a DL segmentation review.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No training process exists and no algorithm parameters are given (Graph-Cut settings, filter scales, region-growing thresholds all unreported). Server-side implementation details (Redis, WebSocket, C++ libs) are named but insufficient to reproduce segmentation behavior.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Not applicable — no optimization objective/loss is defined since no learning method is used; Graph-Cut energy and region-growing criteria are not specified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre-processing is partially described: browser-side window level/width adjustment, black/white inversion, zoom (JavaScript), plus noise reduction and Hessian-based vessel enhancement prior to region growing. Details are qualitative.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Source code is not released, but the deployed system is publicly accessible at http://rayplus.life.hust.edu.cn with an open test account — partial availability of the tool, not of the algorithms/code.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: No segmentation accuracy metrics whatsoever (no Dice, no Hausdorff distance, no volumetric error across cases). Reported metrics are rendering throughput (45–51 FPS, loading times 5.24–12.88 s) and one ad-hoc tumor volume comparison.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No statistical analysis: no confidence intervals, p-values, or variability measures; n=1 clinical case.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Prior systems (MeVIS, Graz, DKFZ, INRIA) are cited in the introduction as context, but no quantitative or qualitative comparison of segmentation/visualization performance against any of them is performed.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: No per-structure quantitative results. Liver, vessels, and tumor are segmented and visualized qualitatively (screenshots); only a single tumor volume is numerically reported.

Q15_limitations.justification: Partial: future work (vessel labeling, Couinaud segment classification, resection simulation) is outlined and the need for 'comprehensive clinical evaluation on accuracy and reliability' implicitly concedes current evaluation gaps. No explicit failure cases discussed.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High — no patient selection criteria defined; evidence rests on a single demonstrator case plus public sample images chosen by the developers.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: High — outcomes not assessed consistently or blindly; accuracy inferred from one tumor volume comparison and developer-reported FPS, with no standardized protocol or independent rater.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: High — all quantitative reporting favors system performance (rendering speed, data sizes); segmentation accuracy outcomes are entirely absent and clinical evaluation is deferred to future work.

detailed_extraction: System: RayPlus, a B/S (browser/server) medical image processing platform following MVC with three physical servers — WebServer (UI generation), DataServer (DICOM images, user accounts, pipelines), ProServer (processing applications). Tech stack: Redis for in-memory data exchange, WebSocket for messaging, C++ algorithms packaged as libs, OpenGL for 3D scenes, browser-side JavaScript rendering of streamed 2D frames. Segmentation pipeline: (1) browser-side pre-processing (windowing, inversion, zoom); (2) liver segmentation via interactive Graph-Cut (user-drawn foreground/background lines) or automatic method exploiting anatomical features to separate adjacent organs; Graph-Cut also used for tumors; results can be saved or re-segmented; (3) intrahepatic vessel extraction via improved Hessian filter (handles tubular structures and junctions) followed by adaptive multi-scale region growing. Visualization: marching-cubes surface modeling and CUDA-accelerated ray-casting volume rendering; interaction events (rotate, zoom, transfer function) sent to server, rendered frames returned via Redis/WebSocket with unique keys. Rendering benchmarks (OsiriX datasets): MAGIX 42 MB, 512x512x76, 50.57 FPS, 5.24 s load; PHENIX 191 MB, 512x512x361, 50.89 FPS, 6.36 s; MELANIX 636 MB, 512x512x1203, 45.07 FPS, 12.88 s. Clinical result: one hepatocarcinoma case, preoperative tumor volume estimate 533 ml vs resected volume 512 ml (displacement measurement, ~4% discrepancy, called 'within acceptable error'). Supported browsers: Chrome, Safari, Firefox. Future work: interactive vessel branch labeling for Couinaud segment classification, resection simulation, comprehensive clinical accuracy/reliability evaluation. Funding: NSFC grants #61210003, #61027006, #50905064. Note for review eligibility: publication venue SPIE Medical Imaging 2016; no machine learning of any kind is used, so the paper fails the deep-learning inclusion criterion of the review despite addressing multi-organ/hepatic CT segmentation.
contribution_summary: The paper presents RayPlus, a web-based (B/S) platform delivering liver surgery planning tools — semi-automatic liver/vessel/tumor segmentation, Hessian-filter vessel extraction, marching-cubes surface models, and CUDA ray-casting volume rendering — entirely through a browser with server-side compute and zero installation. Its key claim is architectural rather than algorithmic: classical segmentation and hardware-accelerated visualization wrapped in a Redis/WebSocket server stack to enable ubiquitous, collaborative clinical access. Validation is limited to rendering throughput benchmarks and a single clinical case, with no segmentation accuracy evaluation and no learning-based components.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 228 training CT scans, well above the >50-subject threshold; test set is small (12 cases) but criterion concerns training size.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source clearly identified: Computational Anatomy database (comp-anatomy.org), Tokushima University Hospital; 640 scans/200 patients, 240 with ground truth, breakdown by scan range (89 torso, 17 chest, 114 abdomen, 20 abdomen+pelvis) provided.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split stated (12 random test / 228 train) but scan-level, not patient-level; no validation set; with 640 scans from 200 patients, train/test patient overlap (leakage) is possible and unaddressed.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth is database-provided human annotation of up to 19 labels (cited to ref [24]), but annotation protocol (raters, tools, inter-rater agreement, QC) is not described in this paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single internal dataset, single split; the localization module was trained on a different dataset, but the segmentation system was never evaluated on external data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Described only conceptually (convolution 'coarse recognition' + deconvolution 'fine extraction', compact all-in-one FCN); no layer specifications, filter counts, or receptive field details in this paper — deferred to prior works [18-20].

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Caffe framework and ADAM optimizer named; full 2D sections from 3 orientations without patch sampling stated; but no learning rate, batch size, iterations/epochs, or network dimensions — not reproducible from this paper alone.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss only described as 'sum of pixel-wise losses between network prediction and label map'; exact loss never named and choice never justified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Clearly described: CT values 12→8 bits via linear interpolation, ROI cropping to localization-module bounding box at train and test time, per-slice 2D segmentation followed by 3D majority voting.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or public repository; only the Caffe package is cited.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Two metrics: 3D Jaccard index (IoU) and voxel-level true-positive rate, reported per organ.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or variance of any kind; abstract claims 'significantly' improved accuracy with no statistical testing.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Quantitative comparison only against the authors' own previous method (kidney 80→88, pancreas 31→65 Jaccard); SOTA comparison is qualitative ('comparable') with no external numbers.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Separate results for each target organ (pancreas and left kidney), matching the per-organ network design.

Q15_limitations.justification: Results called 'preliminary' and low baseline pancreas accuracy acknowledged, but no failure-case analysis, no explicit limitations section, and the 12-case test size is never flagged as a limitation.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/unclear. Test cases were 'picked at random' but the split is scan-level on a database with multiple scans per patient (640 scans/200 patients), so training-test patient overlap is possible; single-center Japanese cohort; no external validation.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Evaluation is automated and objective (Jaccard, voxel TPR) with the same test set and metrics as the compared prior method. Caveat: ground-truth annotation quality was never independently verified and no reader study was performed.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate/high. Only 2 of up to 19 annotated organs reported; no per-case results or variance; SOTA comparisons qualitative only; 'significant improvement' claimed without statistical support; no negative results or failure cases shown.

detailed_extraction: Split mechanics: 12 scans picked at random for testing, 228 for training, no validation set; scan-level split on a multi-scan-per-patient database creates possible train/test leakage (unaddressed). Database: 240 of 640 scans annotated with up to 19 organ labels (heart, lungs, aorta, esophagus, liver, gallbladder, stomach/duodenum, spleen, kidneys, IVC, portal/splenic/SMV veins, pancreas, uterus, prostate, bladder); mixed scan ranges and contrast enhancement. Localization module: non-deep, Haar-like + LBP sliding-window likelihood plus group-wise Hough-voting spatial calibration (refs [21,22,27]); trained on a different CT dataset and reused with zero fine-tuning. Training: two separate 2D FCNs, one per organ (pancreas; left kidney) — notably contradicting the single multi-organ network of their prior work; all 2D sections from axial/sagittal/coronal orientations shuffled and fed whole (no patch sampling); ADAM optimizer; Caffe. Inference: 12→8 bit CT-value reduction by linear interpolation, bounding-box crop, per-slice labeling, labels projected back to 3D, majority voting; 'real-time' claimed but no wall-clock timings reported. Results are means over 12 test cases only — no per-case spread: left kidney IU 0.88 / TPR 0.99; pancreas IU 0.65 / TPR 0.84; prior method without localization: kidney 0.80, pancreas 0.31. GPU parallelism mentioned as a property of the approach but no hardware specified. Funding: MEXT Grants-in-Aid 26108005 and 26330134 (Japan).
contribution_summary: The paper adds a non-deep-learning organ localization module (bounding-box detection) in front of the authors' previously published 2D fully convolutional network with 3D majority voting, restricting CNN training and testing to organ ROIs. On 12 test CT scans, this ROI restriction raised mean 3D Jaccard from 31% to 65% for pancreas and 80% to 88% for left kidney over their prior whole-image approach. The key finding — that cheap classical localization substantially boosts deep segmentation of difficult organs — is sound but preliminary, with a tiny test set, no statistical analysis, and no external benchmarks.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 94 CTU cases (79 train / 15 test); exceeds the >50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: In-house CTU dataset, University of Michigan, IRB approval stated. Acquisition parameters and patient demographics not given.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 79/15 split stated and test set explicitly held out of training; but no description of how cases were assigned (randomization), and no validation set for tuning.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Inner and outer walls outlined by 'a radiologist' as reference standard; number of readers, annotation protocol, and inter-/intra-observer agreement not reported.
