Q5_external_validation.justification: Single institutional dataset; no external/independent cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 5-layer topology given (2 conv layers x 64 kernels + pooling, 2 locally connected layers 64/32 kernels, FC output; 16x16 ROI input). Kernel sizes, strides, and intensity normalization not specified.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, or stopping criteria. Framework named (cuda-convnet, Krizhevsky 2012) but training regime absent.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function not reported, let alone justified; binary ROI classification implied but never stated.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: ROI extraction described (240,000 ROIs, 16x16 px, 50/50 balanced in-wall vs not-in-wall). Level sets run twice with two parameter sets, but actual parameters deferred to refs [3,4].

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL or statement of availability.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Single metric: 3D volume intersection. No Dice, Hausdorff distance, ASSD, or boundary metrics. Note: intersection/reference volume is asymmetric — it does not penalize over-segmentation — so values are not comparable to Dice.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± SD per structure plus histograms reported; no confidence intervals, p-values, or significance testing vs the prior method.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Only qualitative claim that outer-wall segmentation 'is improved compared to our previous method' (Cha et al. 2016, same group); no quantitative comparison table, no external methods.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Inner and outer wall reported separately for train and test sets with distributions — appropriate granularity for a single-organ (bladder wall) study.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit failure modes: over-segmentation despite level sets, prostate incorrectly included in outer wall, inner-wall under-segmentation in contrast-enhanced regions; illustrated with failure examples in Fig. 6.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/high. No inclusion/exclusion criteria, no consecutive or randomized sampling statement; case mix (e.g., lesion burden, bladder distension) unreported.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. Consistent reference standard (radiologist outlines) applied to all cases and held-out test set used; mitigated by single reader and no inter-observer variability assessment.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Train and test results with full histograms reported (favors transparency), but the chosen metric (volume intersection / reference volume) rewards enclosing the reference and ignores over-segmentation, flattering results relative to Dice; no quantitative baseline comparison reported.

detailed_extraction: Scope flag for this review: this is NOT a 3D deep-learning segmentation method. The DL-CNN is applied 2D slice-by-slice to 16x16 ROIs (is_3d=false confirmed); the only 3D elements are the level-set contour refinement and the volumetric evaluation metric. Pipeline: (1) extract 240k balanced 16x16 ROIs from training scans (center pixel inside vs outside radiologist-outlined wall); (2) train 5-layer Krizhevsky-style CNN in cuda-convnet to classify pixel-in-wall; (3) apply slice-wise to generate wall likelihood maps; (4) run level sets twice (two parameter sets, from Cha 2016 / Street 2007) on CTU + likelihood map to produce inner and outer wall contours. Framework: cuda-convnet (Krizhevsky, 2012); GPU details, training time, and inference time not reported. Metric definition as printed contains a notation error (VG used for both reference and evaluated volume); the intended formula is |V_reference ∩ V_computer| / |V_reference| — an asymmetric overlap measure, so reported ~87-94% values overstate performance relative to symmetric metrics like Dice and should not be pooled with Dice-based results in meta-analysis. Lineage: direct incremental extension of Cha et al. 2016 (Medical Physics, outer wall only) adding inner-wall segmentation; component of an ongoing bladder cancer CAD system (NIH U01CA179106). No cross-validation; single fixed 79/15 split. Results: train inner 90.0±8.7%, outer 93.7±3.9%; test inner 87.6±7.6%, outer 87.2±9.3% volume intersection. Code, license, benchmark reproduction: none available.
contribution_summary: Extends the authors' prior outer-bladder-wall DL-CNN (Cha et al. 2016) to segment both inner and outer bladder wall in CT urography by generating a per-pixel wall likelihood map with a 5-layer Krizhevsky-style CNN and refining contours via level sets. Achieves 87.6%/87.2% test volume intersection (inner/outer wall) on 15 held-out cases, handling contrast/non-contrast wall appearance variation and prostate overlap imperfectly. Contribution is incremental within an in-house CAD pipeline: 2D patch classification (not volumetric segmentation), single institution, no Dice, no quantitative baseline comparison.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 147 CT scans with 100 training subjects, exceeding the >50 training threshold; adequate though modest for single-organ segmentation.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source described as a research study of gastric cancer patients (contrast-enhanced portal venous CT) with voxel dimensions given, but no institution/trial name, ethics statement, or inclusion/exclusion criteria.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Hard 100/47 train/test split stated, but split procedure undescribed, no separate validation set, and model-configuration comparison (Fig 4) was performed on the test set.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Pancreas delineated by three trained researchers and confirmed by a clinician; process clear, though inter-rater agreement statistics not reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent dataset; single internal cohort, single split.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Full topology given: 4 resolution levels, 3x3x3 convs with ReLU, 2x2x2 pooling/stride-2 up-convolutions (up-sampling + conv), same-size convs via zero padding, two skip-connection variants (concat 25M vs sum 12M params), sigmoid output, batch norm, multi-GPU design.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Keras/TF, Adam (lr 1e-2), 20,000 iterations, augmentation parameters (B-spline displacement 4, grid 24, +/-20 deg rotations, +/-20 voxel translations) and input size (120^3) all given; but exact batch size and RF bounding-box margin unspecified, RF regressor only cited, no code release.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Pseudo-Dice loss adopted from V-Net by citation; class-imbalance rationale implicit but not argued, and no loss ablation performed.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly described (RF bounding-box regression with margin guaranteeing 100% recall, resampling to fixed 120x120x120); postprocessing explicitly limited to thresholding p(x) >= 0.5 with no other steps.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice score only; no volumetric overlap alternatives, boundary distance metrics, or sensitivity/PPV.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only (mean +/- std, min/max range); no confidence intervals or significance testing, and cross-method differences not statistically assessed despite acknowledged validation-scheme differences.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Table 1 compares against four methods including an RF+graph-cut baseline on the identical 147-scan dataset (75.1% Dice), plus cascaded 3D U-Net and two 2D FCN approaches; comparability caveat honestly stated.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study reporting case-level distribution for the pancreas (89.7 +/- 3.8%, range [79.8, 94.8]) rather than only a global average.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations acknowledged (cross-dataset comparison difficulty, single-organ scope, need for topological constraints), but no dedicated failure-case or error-mode analysis of their own results.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/unclear: patients drawn from a single gastric-cancer research cohort (implied single-center, portal venous phase only); no inclusion/exclusion criteria reported and the method of assigning patients to the 100/47 split is undescribed.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate: uniform Dice evaluation on a fixed 47-case test set for all configurations; however, architecture variants were selected by comparing test-set curves (Fig 4) rather than via a held-out validation set, and annotation reliability (inter-rater agreement) is unquantified.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate: only Dice reported with no secondary metrics or per-case analysis of failures; worst-case range is honestly reported, but no protocol registration and emphasis on 'new state-of-the-art' claim without statistical support.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: Cohort/scans — 147 contrast-enhanced portal-venous abdominal CTs from gastric-cancer patients; 263-1061 slices of 512x512; voxel spacing [0.55-0.82, 0.55-0.82, 0.4-0.80] mm. Annotation — pancreas delineated by three trained researchers and confirmed by a clinician; no inter-rater statistics. Localization front-end — random-forest regression bounding box (from authors' prior work, Oda et al. 2016) with an added margin guaranteeing 100% recall; detected boxes resampled to fixed 120x120x120. Key architectural distinction from original 3D U-Net: same-size convolutions via zero padding replace valid convolutions + tiled/cropped inference, enabling single-pass dense whole-pancreas output (<10 s/case) without discontinuity artifacts; multi-GPU (4x Quadro P6000, 24 GB) memory enables mini-batches >1 and batch normalization. Up-convolutions implemented as up-sampling followed by convolution. Ablation findings (Fig 4): summation skip connections (residual-style, 12M params) outperform concatenation (25M params) in testing; without data augmentation the model overfits (training Dice approaches 1.0 while test Dice stagnates). Baseline numbers from Table 1: cascaded 3D U-Net (Roth et al. 2017, 280/150 split) 82.2 +/- 10.2; Oda et al. RF+GC on same 147 scans (LOOV) 75.1 +/- 15.4; Roth et al. 2D FCN (82 pts, 4-fold CV) 81.3 +/- 6.3; Zhou et al. coarse-to-fine 2D FCN (82 pts, 4-fold CV) 82.4 +/- 5.7. No separate validation set exists — both ablation and final comparison use the same 47-case test set. Funding: MEXT KAKENHI grants and JSPS International Bilateral Collaboration Grant.
contribution_summary: The paper presents a custom multi-GPU 3D U-Net using same-size (zero-padded) convolutions to densely segment the whole pancreas in a single pass, eliminating the discontinuity artifacts of tiled subvolume inference. It systematically compares concatenation versus summation skip connections, showing that residual-style summation (12M vs 25M parameters) improves test Dice. Achieving 89.7 +/- 3.8% Dice on 147 gastric-cancer CT scans, it reported the state of the art for pancreas segmentation at the time, with <10-second inference per case.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 377 contrast-enhanced abdominal CT volumes; far exceeds 50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single research study of gastric cancer patients, portal venous phase; slice counts (460-1177), pixel size, and voxel dimensions fully reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random split of 340 train / 37 test stated. No validation set; Table 1 reports results on the training set itself, and the tuning protocol is unspecified.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Arteries, portal vein, liver, spleen, stomach, gallbladder, pancreas delineated by trained researchers and confirmed by a clinician. No annotation tool, protocol, or inter-observer agreement reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No independent external cohort; single-institution single-disease (gastric cancer) data only.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D U-Net-like FCN fully specified: 4 resolution levels, 3x3x3 same-size convolutions, 2x2x2 max pooling, transposed convolutions, concatenation skips, ~19M parameters, voxel-wise softmax, with figure.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Keras/TensorFlow, Adam (lr 1e-2), 50,000 iterations, 64x64x64 subvolumes (batch of 3), batch norm, hardware and training time given. Only random seed missing.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Multi-class differentiable Dice loss (Milletari et al.) with equations given and uniform class weights; rationale cites prior work [39,40] rather than justifying empirically here.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre: x4 downsampling, random 64^3 crops. Augmentation: B-spline deformation (max displacement 4, grid 24 voxels), rotation +/-20 deg, translation +/-20 voxels. Post: overlapping tiling in z, reshaped inference.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice only (mean/std/min/max). No Hausdorff distance, ASSD, or volumetric error.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive stats only; no confidence intervals, no p-values, no significance testing.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Claims performance 'comparable or better' than [25,38,43,44] but no head-to-head numbers; authors themselves note direct comparison is invalid across datasets.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-organ tables (avg/std/min/max Dice) for both training (n=340) and testing (n=37): e.g., test liver 97.1%, spleen 97.7%, pancreas 84.9%, gallbladder 85.1%, vein 80.5%, artery 83.5%.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly discusses absent shape constraints producing disconnected/isolated regions, cross-dataset comparison limits, and proposes anatomical constraints [45] as future work.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate concern. Single-center cohort restricted to gastric cancer patients (uniform portal venous phase); no inclusion/exclusion criteria or consecutive-enrollment statement. Likely unrepresentative of general abdominal CT populations, e.g., non-contrast or other pathologies.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low concern. Single consistent pipeline and Dice metric applied uniformly to a held-out test set; annotations confirmed by a clinician. Mitigating gap: no inter-rater reliability for ground truth.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low concern. Per-organ results reported for both train and test including failure cases (vein min 49.0%, gallbladder min 28.6%). However, no external validation and only qualitative SOTA comparison; the novel contribution is presented as a tutorial example rather than a benchmarked method.

detailed_extraction: Architecture: symmetric encoder/decoder, 4 levels, zero-padded same-size 3x3x3 convolutions, ReLU, 2x2x2 strided max pooling, transposed-conv upsampling, concatenation skips, ~19M params, voxel-wise softmax over 7 foreground classes + background. Training: 64x64x64 random subvolumes, 3 per minibatch (enables batch norm across patients), augmentation = B-spline deform (max displacement 4, grid spacing 24 voxels) + rotation +/-20deg + translation +/-20 voxels per iteration. Loss: per-class differentiable Dice (Milletari V-Net formulation), equal weights wl=1, summed over classes. Optimizer: Adam, lr 1e-2, 50k iterations, ~1 week on 1x NVIDIA Quadro P6000 (24GB); Keras + TensorFlow. Inference: network reshaped to cover full xy extent, overlapping tiles along z; <1 min per case; predictions upsampled to half original resolution. Data: 377 portal-venous CTs, downsampled x4 to 128x128x(slices/4). Results (test, n=37): mean Dice 89.3+/-6.5%; liver 97.1, spleen 97.7, stomach 96.1, gallbladder 85.1 (+/-15.7), pancreas 84.9, artery 83.5, portal vein 80.5. Train (n=340): 89.4+/-6.4%, suggesting no overfitting. Note: Table 1 evaluates on the training set, an unusual choice. Context: paper is a Japanese-language journal special-feature tutorial introducing deep learning for medical segmentation; the experiment serves as a worked example, not a rigorous benchmark. Same group's related work: hierarchical 3D FCNs [44], SPIE pancreas segmentation [38].
contribution_summary: A tutorial-style demonstration that a custom 3D U-Net trained end-to-end with a differentiable multi-class Dice loss achieves state-of-the-art ~89% mean Dice across 7 abdominal structures (liver, spleen, stomach, pancreas, gallbladder, artery, portal vein) on 377 contrast-enhanced gastric-cancer CTs. It shows such 3D FCNs are trainable on a single 24GB GPU using small random subvolumes, batch norm, and aggressive B-spline/rotation/translation augmentation, with sub-minute inference. Key limitations acknowledged: no anatomical/shape constraints, allowing disconnected or isolated segmentation regions.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Patient/subject count never stated; only '960 abdominal CT slices' reported. With source volumes of 89-314 slices and 32-slice z-crops, the data corresponds to at most ~10-30 volumes from an unknown (likely <50) number of patients. The >50 subjects criterion cannot be verified and the slice arithmetic suggests it is not met. Table 1 lists '96 CT Numbers' for this paper, which appears to be test slices (10% of 960), not cases - units inconsistent with competitors' 20/50 volumes.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single hospital named (Sichuan Cancer Hospital & Institute). Missing: scanner vendor/model, contrast phase, patient demographics, pathology spectrum, inclusion/exclusion criteria, ethics approval.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 70/20/10 split reported, but the unit of splitting (patient vs. slice vs. crop) is unspecified. Validation is 'randomly selecting 20% of the data in each epoch' - a non-fixed validation set, raising leakage risk if slices from the same volume land in both train and val. Test-set independence is unverifiable.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process entirely undescribed: no annotator expertise, number of raters, manual/semi-automatic protocol, inter-rater agreement, or reference standard mentioned.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external cohort. All data from one hospital; evaluation only on internal 10% test split.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Thoroughly described: 7 dilated convolution stacks (rates 1,2,4,6), 8 depth-wise separable convolution layers, extra skip concatenations every two encoder conv layers, 3 max-pool (2x2x2, stride 2), 3 transposed conv (2x2x2, stride 2), input 32x256x256, SeLU activation with Lecun_normal init, feature-map counts in Figure 1.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: framework (Keras/TF), optimizer (Adam), LR (0.001), epochs (50), GPU, and 'save best on val loss' model selection are given. Missing: batch size and, critically, the loss function being optimized - the model cannot be reproduced exactly.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never named or justified. Loss values are reported (train 0.0290, val 0.0462) and used for model selection, but what was minimized is unstated; Dice is used only as an evaluation metric.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Detailed pipeline: 2D linear interpolation to 1mm spacing, fixed 256x256x32 crop (center shifted 30px left), HU windowing [20,160] with outside values set to -1000 (motivated by an empirical HU histogram, Fig. 4), 4x rotation/translation augmentation; post-processing includes 0.5 binarization, restoration to 512x512, and HU>0 false-positive removal, all illustrated step-by-step (Figs. 5, 7).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository link provided. First authors are from LinkingMed (commercial entity) with no open-source release.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC is the only evaluation metric. No Hausdorff distance, ASSD, VOE, sensitivity/specificity, or volumetric error. Training/validation loss curves are shown but not a segmentation metric.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only (DSC mean 0.961, std 0.013). No confidence intervals, no p-values, no significance testing against the compared methods, no per-case score distribution.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Two recent liver segmentation methods compared (Lu 2018 graph cut: 0.94; Yang 2017 adversarial network: 0.95). However, comparison is cross-dataset with inconsistent test-set sizes/units ('20/50/96 CT numbers') and no re-implementation on shared data; no ablation against a vanilla 3D U-Net on their own data, so attribution of the gain to the architectural improvements is unsupported. The claim of 'much more test data' conflates slices with volumes.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver only), so the reported result is fully per-organ by construction. (Note: this makes the criterion trivially satisfied rather than a strength; multi-organ generalization is untested.)

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly discussed in the conclusion: the fixed HU range [20,160] and fixed 256x256 crop fail on 'special data', potentially causing false negatives. Honest and specific.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: HIGH - single-center data with no patient selection criteria, inclusion/exclusion rules, or demographics reported; patient count itself unknown, so case-mix and representativeness cannot be judged.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: HIGH - reference standard and annotation protocol unreported; non-fixed per-epoch validation sampling creates possible train/val leakage; outcome measured only by DSC on a small internal test split; unit ambiguity in Table 1 ('CT numbers') prevents fair cross-study comparison.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: MODERATE - headline result (mean/std DSC) is reported, but the optimized loss function, batch size, inference time, per-case variability, and failure-case counts are omitted; comparison table is presented in a way that favors the method despite non-equivalent test data.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond the prior extraction: (1) Validation protocol - 20% of data re-randomized as validation each epoch rather than a fixed split, with model selection via Keras 'save best only' on validation loss (final model = lowest val loss 0.0462; lowest train loss 0.0290, logged via TensorBoard). (2) Activation/initialization rationale - SeLU chosen for self-normalizing behavior (zero mean/unit variance propagation, Klambauer et al. 2017) with Lecun_normal init; the dilated-stack + separable-conv design is justified via multi-scale receptive fields (rates 1,2,4,6) and Xception-style decomposition of 3D correlation into 2D spatial + 1D channel. (3) Spatial config - downsampling 32x256x256 -> 4x32x32; axes ordered (z, x, y); crop center shifted 30 px left of image center to maximize liver coverage. (4) Post-processing geometry - predicted 256x256 mask expanded to 500x500 by background fill, re-interpolated to native 0.9765625 mm spacing yielding 512x512; false-positive removal multiplies mask by original image, thresholding HU>0. (5) Clinical framing - liver treated as radiotherapy organ-at-risk; motivating applications include intraoperative guidance. (6) Conflicts/provenance - industry authors (LinkingMed) plus hospital clinicians; funding acknowledged from Sichuan Cancer Hospital & Institute; no conflict-of-interest or ethics statement; the printed DOI in the PDF header is an invalid ACM placeholder (10.1145/12345.67890) while the actual DOI is 10.1145/3285996.3286014. (7) Missing methods fields: batch size, total parameter count, loss definition, inference runtime, annotation tooling.
contribution_summary: The paper presents an engineering-focused improvement of the 3D U-Net for single-organ (liver) CT segmentation, combining dilated convolution stacks (rates 1-6), depth-wise separable convolutions, denser encoder skip concatenations, and SeLU activation, plus a simple HU-threshold-based post-processing step that removes false positives below 0 HU. On a single-center private dataset it reports DSC 0.961 +/- 0.013, numerically above two prior deep-learning methods, though on non-comparable test data and without ablation isolating each component's contribution. The main value for the review is as an example of efficient 3D architecture modifications (separable/dilated convolutions reduce computation for volumetric processing) and HU-prior post-processing; its evidence quality is low due to undisclosed patient counts, annotation protocol, and loss function, with no external validation or code release.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 131 training 3D CT volumes, well above the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public challenge data used, but inconsistently and incorrectly named ('LiST', 'ISBI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation Challenge' — LiTS was a MICCAI 2017 challenge). No patient demographics, scanner, or acquisition details.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split sizes stated (131 train / 30 test) but no split methodology, no validation set, and unclear whether the 30 test scans are the official LiTS test set (whose labels are non-public) or a held-out subset.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: No description of who annotated the ground truth, the annotation protocol, or quality control; example masks are shown but their provenance is only implicit via the challenge.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single dataset (LiTS) only; no independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Conceptual architecture clearly described (ResNet encoder, atrous convolutions, ASPP, skip connections, bilinear upsampling, figure provided), but exact configuration missing: atrous rates, filter counts, decoder depth, and Figure 1 details are incomplete.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Good hyperparameter coverage: TensorFlow, Adam (lr=0.0001, β1=0.9, β2=0.995), 20 epochs, batch size 4, GTX 1080, ~3 days/model, augmentation specifics, input resolutions per axis. Minor gap: STL stage durations/switching criterion unspecified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Lovász-Softmax loss used with a generic citation-backed claim that it 'is beneficial to improve segmentation performance'; no task-specific rationale and no ablation versus Dice or cross-entropy. Citation in text ([22]) is actually the H-DenseUNet paper; the Lovász paper is [23].

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Axis-wise slice cropping (512×512 sagittal, 512×64 axial/coronal), online augmentation (rotation, zoom, shear, flip), and view-averaging fusion described. Missing: intensity normalization/HU windowing and resampling details, which are standard for CT.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL or repository mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Two complementary overlap metrics reported: Dice and mean IoU, for all experimental conditions.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests, or repeated runs; single-point results throughout Table 1.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Claims of being 'comparable to state-of-the-art' are verbal only. All quantitative comparisons (TTL vs STL, ResNet variants, isotropic vs anisotropic) are internal ablations; no head-to-head numbers against published methods such as H-DenseUNet.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study; liver-specific Dice and mIoU explicitly reported per configuration rather than an opaque average.

Q15_limitations.justification: Only a vague admission that 'model performance' needs improvement and future work is listed. No explicit limitations section and no failure-case analysis or example of segmentation errors.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/high — data drawn from a public challenge without any statement of patient selection criteria, exclusions, or demographics; provenance of the 30-scan test set is ambiguous.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate — Dice and mIoU applied uniformly across all conditions, but single-run results without variance, a not-fully-defined evaluation protocol, and a test set with unclear label availability raise concerns about outcome assessment.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate — the full ablation table is reported, including unfavorable baselines (weak single-axis and TTL results), suggesting no selective omission; however, failure cases and negative findings are not discussed.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Step Transfer Learning (STL) is a two-stage schedule — first freeze ImageNet-pretrained encoder weights and train only the randomly initialized layers (ASPP/decoder), then fine-tune all parameters once loss converges; stage lengths and switch criterion not specified. (2) Input design: each network receives 3 consecutive CT slices stacked as 3 channels, deliberately mimicking ImageNet RGB input to enable ResNet-50/101/152 weight transfer; output is a single-slice mask (2.5D). (3) Three separate networks are trained (axial/coronal/sagittal), so total training cost is ~9 days on one GTX 1080; inference time not reported. (4) Full ablation grid in Table 1 (TTL/STL × ResNet-50/101/152 × axis config): anisotropic fusion improves Dice by ~7-14 points over the best single axis in every setting; STL consistently beats TTL (best: 0.9485 Dice with ResNet-152); deeper encoders monotonically improve results. (5) β2=0.995 is non-standard (Adam default 0.999). (6) Factual errors to flag for the review: dataset misnamed 'LiST' and attributed to 'ISBI 2017' (LiTS = MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation Challenge); official LiTS has 131 train + 70 test volumes, so the '30 testing' scans need clarification; text cites [22] (H-DenseUNet) for the Lovász-Softmax loss, whose actual reference is [23]. (7) Batch Normalization applied before each residual block. (8) Funding: three Chinese provincial/university grants (CXJJ2017045, 201805040YD18CG24(7), 15JK1679).
contribution_summary: Proposes a 2.5D '3D anisotropic' ensemble of three DeepLabV3-style encoder-decoder networks (ResNet backbones with atrous convolutions and ASPP) that segment liver from axial, coronal, and sagittal slice triplets, fused by averaging to exploit between-slice context without full 3D memory cost. Introduces Step Transfer Learning, a staged fine-tuning schedule that first trains randomly initialized layers while freezing ImageNet-pretrained encoder weights, improving over standard transfer learning. Achieves Dice 0.9485 / mIoU 0.9508 on LiTS liver segmentation, with ablations showing each component (anisotropic fusion, STL, deeper ResNet) contributes gains.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 20 CT scans, far below the >50 subject threshold. U-Net explicitly trained on 'a few samples'.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source named (ISICDM2018 challenge) but no scanner, acquisition protocol, contrast phase, or patient demographic details.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No split described. Evaluation uses 20 2D images randomly selected from the same 20 volumes; training/test separation is unclear and likely violated.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual labeling referenced and shown (Fig. 2c), but annotation protocol, annotator count, and inter-observer handling not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No independent external dataset; all evaluation on the single 20-scan challenge set.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: U-Net structure specified (23 conv layers, 3x3 convs + ReLU + 2x2 max pooling, 1x1 output, 64-component features); DRLSE energy given in full with equations (3)-(11).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Level set parameters fixed (mu=0.2, eps=1.5, alpha=5, beta=-3), but U-Net training details entirely absent: no loss, optimizer, learning rate, epochs, augmentation, hardware, or training-set size. Fractional order v and constant z unspecified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: DRLSE energy terms (distance regularization, length, area) are presented and their roles justified; however the U-Net training loss is never stated.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre-processing (fractional differential enhancement, Eq. 1) and post-processing (DRLSE contour evolution, Eqs. 3-11) both clearly described with formulas.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model, or repository released.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Two metrics reported: Dice coefficient (0.82) and volume difference (0.15), both defined formally (Eqs. 12-13).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Box plots only; no p-values, confidence intervals, or variance measures for any comparison.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Four baselines compared (CV, GAC, LBF, IVC), but all are classical active contour models. No comparison against the deep learning pancreas SOTA the paper itself cites (Roth et al., Zhou et al., Cai et al.).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ (pancreas) study; per-case result distributions shown via box plots across the 20 test images.

Q15_limitations.justification: Briefly acknowledged in passing: U-Net trained on few samples extracts only part of the pancreas; conclusion recommends more data. No dedicated limitations section or failure case analysis.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High. 20 challenge CT scans with no inclusion/exclusion criteria, demographics, or acquisition details. Evaluation on 20 randomly selected 2D slices allows slice-level selection bias toward easier images.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: High. Train/test separation unclear (evaluation slices drawn from the same 20 volumes used for development); single unverified ground truth; outcomes assessed only visually/quantitatively on 2D slices without blinding or standardized protocol.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Dice and VD means reported but no per-case table, variance, or runtime figures; 'significantly reduced' computation time claimed without numbers; baseline comparison limited to methods the proposed approach demonstrably beats.

detailed_extraction: Critical caveats not obvious from headline numbers: (1) despite the abstract claiming automatic 3D pancreas segmentation, all quantitative evaluation is 2D slice-level - 20 randomly selected slices from 20 volumes - so Dice 0.82 is not a volumetric 3D Dice; (2) the VD metric as defined (Eq. 13: (S-G)/G) is a relative signed volume difference, not the standard |V_S - V_G|/V_G; (3) the U-Net serves only as contour initializer and the authors concede it captures 'only part of the pancreas' at training sample sizes used, meaning the level set stage performs much of the boundary localization; (4) the signed-distance initialization (Eq. 2) leaves the constant z undefined; (5) the fractional differential order v is described but its value never given; (6) level set parameters fixed across all cases: mu=0.2, eps=1.5, alpha=5, beta=-3; (7) all four baselines (CV, GAC, LBF, IVC) are non-learning active contour variants, so the 0.82 vs 0.37-0.66 margin says little about competitiveness against 2019 CNN methods (typical reported pancreas Dice of that era: ~0.75-0.83 on NIH-TCIA 82 scans); (8) funding: NSFC 61971118, Liaoning provincial funds; data courtesy of ISICDM2018. Update extraction fields: dataset_size confirmed 20 CT scans, is_3d=false confirmed for both method and evaluation, inference/training time and GPU remain unreported.
contribution_summary: Proposes a three-stage pipeline for pancreas CT segmentation: fractional differential enhancement to boost pancreas-to-tissue contrast, a standard 2D U-Net producing a coarse initial region converted to a signed-distance initial contour, and distance regularized level set evolution (DRLSE) for boundary refinement. On 20 ISICDM2018 CT scans (evaluated on 20 2D slices), it reports mean Dice 0.82 and VD 0.15, beating four classical active contour baselines (CV, GAC, LBF, IVC). Its value is a simple demonstration that CNN initialization makes level set evolution viable for pancreas segmentation under very limited data, though the evaluation is too small and baselines too weak to establish clinical or SOTA relevance.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 20 CT volumes, well below the >50 subject threshold. 4-fold CV partially mitigates but cannot compensate for this scale.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source clearly described: private Changhai Hospital dataset, 20 patients with pancreatic endocrine neoplasms, image size 512x512x(36-74), voxel spacing 0.66x0.66x1.5 mm³.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 4-fold cross validation stated with averaged results, but fold construction (patient-level vs. slice-level), fold sizes, and any held-out test set are not described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Stated as 'manually delineated by human experts according to domain knowledge', but no details on number of raters, annotation protocol, or inter-rater agreement.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation; single private single-center dataset only. No public benchmark (e.g., NIH TCIA pancreas) used.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture is only 'motivated by 3D U-net [3]' (Çiçek et al.); no depth, channel configuration, or modifications described. The interactive correction module (ROI 9x9x2, k=8 reference labels, similarity cost) is described in more detail than the network itself.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Interactive-stage parameters are specified (k=8, w_U=0.01, α*=0.375, ROI size, Gaussian correction with coordinate rounding), but network training is unreproducible: no optimizer, learning rate, epochs, batch size, framework, or hardware.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Training loss for the 3D U-Net is never stated anywhere in the paper.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (resize to 256x256, translation and scale augmentation) and postprocessing (shadowed-sets three-way thresholding, Gaussian-modeled interaction label correction) both described with concrete parameters.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no repository or URL mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC, MSE, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 all used (voxel classification framing).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Only 4-fold CV averages reported. No standard deviations, confidence intervals, significance tests, or p-values.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compared only against Otsu thresholding (DSC 0.05, a trivial baseline) and their own retrained 3D U-Net. Cited contemporary pancreas methods (e.g., DeepOrgan) are not compared against numerically.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (pancreas) so per-organ reporting is trivially satisfied. Per-case DSC is given in Figure 7 (82%, 78%, 80%, 72%) and an ablation by interaction round (0.65 → 0.72 → 0.78) is provided.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations or failure-case discussion. Semi-automatic nature, tiny dataset, and below-SOTA Dice are not acknowledged by the authors.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High concern: 20 patients, all with a single pathology (pancreatic endocrine neoplasms), from one center. No inclusion/exclusion criteria defined; private data prevents independent verification of case mix.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate concern: metrics applied consistently across methods via 4-fold CV, but no blinding is possible — the experts who delineated ground truth may have also performed the interactions, and interaction user, skill level, and time cost are unreported. Semi-automatic results are inherently user-dependent.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: High concern: Figure 5(b) accuracy/precision/recall/F1 shown only as plots with no extractable values; no variance reported; no negative or failure results discussed; no limitations section.

detailed_extraction: Pipeline: (1) 3D U-Net produces initial segmentation L0; (2) round-1 clinician interaction (points/scribbles, foreground/background) defines a local ROI of 9x9x2 voxels; (3) top-k=8 reference labels from training data selected via similarity cost S(M,U_t,L_{t-1}) with balancing weight w_U=0.01 (Eq. 1); (4) probability map built by averaging reference labels; (5) shadowed-sets threshold α* found by numerically minimizing the uncertainty-balance objective (no closed form; α*=0.375), partitioning voxels into confident foreground/confident background/uncertain; (6) round-2 interaction restricted to uncertain regions, with interaction points converted to labels via a Gaussian distribution (Eq. 8) and coordinate rounding. Results (4-fold CV averages): Otsu DSC 0.05/MSE 72.3; 3D U-Net DSC 0.65/MSE 6.3; after first interaction DSC 0.72/MSE 4.5; final (second interaction) DSC 0.78/MSE 4.2. Showcased case: DSC 0.82 vs 0.66 for 3D U-Net. Method is semi-automatic: requires two rounds of expert interaction per case; interaction time cost never quantified. Framework, GPU, and training/inference times unreported. Minimum Dice improvement over baseline (+0.13) comes mostly from round 1 (+0.07 from round 2); the shadowed-sets uncertainty detection's specific contribution vs. a second generic interaction round is not isolated in the ablation.
contribution_summary: Proposes a semi-automatic pancreas segmentation framework combining a 3D U-Net initial segmentation with shadowed sets theory (Pedrycz) to explicitly demarcate uncertain boundary regions, which are then targeted for focused two-round expert correction. On a private 20-scan Changhai Hospital CT dataset, this raises mean Dice from 0.65 (3D U-Net baseline) to 0.78. Key novelty is the three-way (confident/uncertain) shadowed-set partitioning of the probability map to reduce interaction scope, rather than a new deep architecture.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 402 CT scans from cancer patients, split 7:1:2, yielding ~281 training scans — well above the >50 subject threshold. Largest public dataset of expert-vetted thoracic cavity segmentations at time of publication.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: PleThora dataset clearly described: publicly available on The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), derived from NSCLC-Radiomics collection, with full curation protocol in companion paper (Kiser et al., Medical Physics 2020).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Ratio (train:val:test = 7:1:2) is explicitly stated, but the allocation mechanism is not described — no mention of randomization, stratification by clinical variables, or patient-level vs. scan-level splitting; no cross-validation.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Process partially described: initial segmentation auto-generated, then manually corrected by human experts; label content comprehensively enumerated (normal/pathologic/atelectatic parenchyma, hilum, effusion, fibrosis, nodules, tumor). However, number of annotators, expertise level, and consensus/quality-control protocol are deferred to the Kiser et al. dataset paper.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation on an independent dataset; all evaluation performed on the internal held-out test split (20%) of PleThora.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: All four architectures described in detail, including exact V-Net modifications (kernel 5→3/stride 1, dropout placement, removal of final 16x compression block), 2D U-Net derivation (3D ops replaced by 2D counterparts), and two-stage coarse-to-fine pipeline mechanics (low-res coarse segmentation → 72×192×120 per-lung crops at original resolution).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partially reproducible: 50 epochs, Adam optimizer, Dice loss, GPU (Quadro RTX 8000, 48GB), parameter counts, and per-epoch training times reported. Missing: learning rate, batch size, data augmentation strategy, early-stopping criterion, random seed, and specifics of the hyperparameter search ('determined by maximizing validation performance').

Q8_loss_function.justification: Differentiable (soft) Dice loss adopted uniformly but with no explicit justification, no discussion of alternatives (cross-entropy, compound losses), and no sensitivity analysis.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly documented two-step pipeline: resample to modal spacing → mask-based cropping → pad to 460×364×130 → resample to (2.5, 2.5, 4.0) mm → pad to 104×208×208 → intensity clipping to [-250, 0] HU. Post-processing (contour cleaning: extract closed contours, count voxels, retain largest per lung) also clearly specified, with before/after ablation.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No author code or trained models released. Reliance on third-party public code (VNet GitHub repo, AAPM 2017 challenge codebase) does not substitute for release of the benchmark pipeline.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Three complementary metrics: Dice coefficient (volume overlap), 95% Hausdorff distance, and average symmetric surface distance (surface-based), all reported as mean (std) before and after post-processing.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Two-sided (Mann-Whitney U) significance tests vs. 2D U-Net baseline (p<0.05 markers in Table 2) and pre- vs. post-processing comparisons per model/lung. No confidence intervals, and one minor text–table inconsistency in HD95 claims, but formal hypothesis testing is clearly performed.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Explicit head-to-head benchmark of four state-of-the-art architectures under identical pipelines (the paper's core contribution), plus human inter-observer agreement as reference ceiling, plus an ablation of an alternative published preprocessing scheme (Yang et al., AAPM 2017).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Left and right lung reported separately for every model and every metric (before/after post-processing), plus Dice distributions (Fig. 3) and per-stratum results across four clinical variables (age, sex, stage, histology).

Q15_limitations.justification: Extensive, candid limitations: failure case on severely collapsed lung (Fig. 2), anatomic outliers under-represented even in largest dataset, left lung consistently worse than right, performance gap to inter-observer agreement, two-stage training/inference inefficiency, 3D GPU memory demands, patch-based methods not evaluated, and potential sex bias.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Source population is well defined (NSCLC patients from public TCIA/NSCLC-Radiomics collections curated into PleThora), but the train/val/test allocation procedure is unspecified (no randomization/stratification detail), preventing assessment of split integrity. Cohort restricted to cancer patients — intentional for the research question but limits generalizability to healthy/emergency chest CTs.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All four models trained and evaluated on identical splits with identical preprocessing, loss, hardware, and three standardized metrics; hyperparameters tuned on a separate validation set; predictions consistently rescaled (nearest-neighbor) before scoring against expert ground truth. Minor internal inconsistency between prose and Table 2 regarding best HD95 model is a small quality blemish, not a systematic bias.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All models reported including relatively underperforming ones (2D U-Net); before- and after-post-processing results both disclosed despite null significance; per-organ and clinical-stratification results reported; limitations and failure cases shown. Minor issues: text–table discrepancy on right-lung HD95, Dice formula notation error (union in denominator instead of sum), and no reporting of inference time.

detailed_extraction:
SUPPLEMENTARY DETAILS (beyond previously extracted data):

GROUND TRUTH & LABEL DEFINITION: Thoracic cavity labels deliberately include normal, pathologic, and atelectatic lung parenchyma, lung hilum, pleural effusion, fibrosis, nodules, tumor, and other anatomic anomalies within a single left/right lung label — i.e., the segmentation target is the diseased lung as a whole, not lesion ROIs. Initial segmentations auto-generated then manually corrected by physician experts (full protocol in Kiser et al. 2020, Med Phys 47(11)).

COHORT: 402 CT scans of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients, derived from NSCLC-Radiomics (Aerts et al.) via TCIA; 7:1:2 split implies ~281/~40/~81 scans. Clinical strata available: age bands (45-85+), sex (61 male / 24 female with data), overall stage (I/II/IIIa/IIIb), histology (adenocarcinoma, large cell, NOS, squamous cell carcinoma).

EVALUATION PROTOCOL: Metrics computed after rescaling predictions to first-step resolution via nearest-neighbor interpolation; evaluation against expert manual segmentation. Human inter-observer agreement provided as ceiling reference (DC 0.983/0.995 left/right; HD95 2.623/1.148 mm; ASSD 0.676/0.191 mm), highlighting a remaining ~0.03-0.04 DC gap for all models.

TWO-STAGE MODEL RATIONALE: Stage 1 coarse low-resolution segmentation of all organs; stage 2 binary 3D U-Net per organ (per lung) on fixed 72×192×120 crops at original resolution — explicitly designed to avoid GPU OOM and to prevent interpolation-mixed voxels at full resolution. Trade-off: requires training up to three models (3.15M + 12.60M params).

2D U-NET FINDING: Achieves near-parity Dice with 3D models (0.942/0.942) but inferior surface metrics (HD95 ~6.0-6.3 mm vs ~5.0-5.5 mm) — attributed to training on shuffled 2D slices without volumetric context.

TRAINING DYNAMICS: All models converge within first few epochs; no validation overfitting observed (authors note medical images have fewer variations than natural images); V-Net validation loss curve flattest/most stable; 3D U-Net stable after ~30 epochs. Parameter counts: 3D U-Net 19.07M (~2.7× 2D U-Net 6.82M), V-Net 9.32M; V-Net more memory-efficient due to stride-2 convolutions replacing pooling.

PREPROCESSING SENSITIVITY: Swapping in Yang et al. (AAPM 2017) preprocessing raised two-stage model DC to 0.950/0.957 (vs 0.947/0.952), demonstrating preprocessing choice materially affects absolute performance — relevant confounder for cross-paper comparisons in this review.

STATISTICAL RESULTS: Only the two-stage 3D U-Net significantly outperformed the 2D U-Net baseline (right-lung DC and HD95, p<0.05); contour cleaning yielded no statistically significant improvements on any metric (Mann-Whitney U).

CLINICAL STRATIFICATION (3D U-Net): Older age associated with better right-lung metrics; male patients outperformed female patients across all metrics (authors flag potential sex bias); stage I disease segmented markedly worse than later stages (HD95/ASSD), attributed to low stage-I representation and possibly distinct early-stage imaging patterns; exception for left lung at stage IIIa.

FAILURE MODE: Severely collapsed left lung case (Fig. 2) failed across models — models did not learn features for this rare anatomic outlier; representative successful case LUNG1-287 (Fig. 1).

SCOPE DECISIONS: Patch-based methods excluded a priori (local patch independence assumption invalid for lungs).

NOT REPORTED: inference time, learning rate, batch size, augmentation, random seeds, split randomization, ethical approval statement.

FUNDING: CPRIT RP170668; NIH 1UL1TR003167, R01AG066749.

DATA QUALITY NOTES FOR REVIEWERS: (1) text asserts 3D U-Net best on right-lung HD95 but Table 2 favors two-stage model (5.088 vs 5.490 mm) — extract table values; (2) Dice equation printed with union in denominator (typographical error); (3) only two structures (lungs) segmented — narrow for 'multi-organ' reviews but valuable as the reference benchmark for segmentation in diseased/pathologic anatomy.
contribution_summary: This paper presents the first head-to-head benchmark of four fully convolutional architectures (3D U-Net, modified V-Net, 2D U-Net, and two-stage 3D U-Net) under identical pre/post-processing pipelines and loss for segmenting lungs containing neoplastic disease, using the 402-scan expert-curated PleThora dataset — the largest public resource of its kind. All models achieved high performance (best Dice 0.947/0.952 left/right with the two-stage 3D U-Net; 3D U-Net best on ASSD bilaterally), with 3D models consistently superior to 2D on surface-distance metrics, though all remained below human inter-observer agreement. Clinical stratification identified systematic failure subgroups — stage I disease, female patients (suggesting potential sex bias), and rare anatomic outliers such as collapsed lungs — and showed that preprocessing choice materially shifts absolute performance, guiding both future data curation and fair benchmarking practice.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Evaluation cohort of 9,552 adults / 11,669 scans (plus 2,117 follow-ups) far exceeds thresholds. Training set (Medical Segmentation Decathlon liver, >100 contrast CTs) is adequate, though its exact size is stated only in the companion technical paper (ref 24), not here.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Thoroughly described: IRB-approved retrospective consecutive cohort, single academic center, noncontrast CT colonography screening, April 2004–Dec 2016, with STARD-style flowchart (Fig 1), exclusion reasons, and demographics (age, sex, BMI).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No train/validation/test split described in this paper; deferred to separate technical publication (ref 24). All 11,669 scans serve as application/evaluation data.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Evaluation ground truth (manual right-lobe ROI, 500–1500 mm², vessel/lesion avoidance, reader experience range, blinding to automated results) is well described. Segmentation training labels (MSD annotations) are only cited, not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Model trained on external MSD data was applied to a fully independent institution/protocol cohort (domain-transferred contrast→noncontrast), so all evaluation data is unseen. However, validation is single-center with no second external site.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Modified 3D U-Net summarized: strided convolution (step 2) + transposed convolution for large volumes, resolution 256×256×192, initial filters 32. Full architecture deferred to ref 24.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: learning rate 1e-4, 10,000 iterations, batch 4, augmentation list, hardware (NIH Biowulf, K80/P100 GPUs) given. Missing: optimizer and loss function.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never mentioned in this paper.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Clear pipeline: fixed 120 kVp acquisition, CycleGAN domain transfer (contrast→noncontrast), defined input resolution, and post-processing (mean/median HU over all segmented liver voxels).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No statement about code or model release.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Multiple metrics: mean HU difference, r², Bland-Altman (proportional bias), 4×4 confusion matrix, per-category sensitivity/specificity with 95% CIs. (No Dice/IoU — segmentation accuracy itself is not reported.)

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Extensive: 95% CIs, two-sided t tests validated by Wilcoxon rank sum, linear and multivariable OLS regression, Sankey longitudinal analysis.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compared against manual ROI (clinical reference method) with per-category sens/spec; no comparison against other automated/DL segmentation or quantification methods; only brief mention of prior smaller automated studies (~100 patients, ref 34).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ (liver) study; results reported at granular subgroup level: sex, age decade, BMI, steatosis category, longitudinal change. Caveat: no direct segmentation quality metrics, only downstream quantification agreement.

Q15_limitations.justification: Failure cases explicitly quantified (7/11,676 = 0.06%, with categorized exclusion flowchart); methodologic differences (volumetric vs areal ROI, hepatic blood pool inclusion) and Bland-Altman proportional bias discussed. Note: full Discussion/Limitations section truncated in provided text.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low within cohort: consecutive screening patients with explicit inclusion/exclusion flowchart. Moderate external validity concern: single-center, asymptomatic, insured screening volunteers are healthier than the general population, inflating generalizability limits.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: standardized protocol (fixed 120 kVp, daily HU calibration across scanners), manual readers blinded to automated results, automated method applied uniformly.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate: comprehensive reporting of prevalence, agreement, and CIs; however, segmentation performance metrics (Dice), comparator algorithms, code availability, and a pre-registered analysis plan are absent; retrospective design.

detailed_extraction: DESIGN: Retrospective, IRB-approved, HIPAA-compliant, single-center (Univ. of Wisconsin), consecutive noncontrast CT colonography screening cohort 04/2004–12/2016. COHORT: 9,552 adults (mean age 57.2±7.9; 4,238 M / 5,314 F; median BMI 27.8); 11,682 eligible scans → 11,669 analyzed. Exclusions: 7 algorithm failure, 4 liver not imaged, 2 severe artifact; failure rate 0.06%. Longitudinal subcohort: 1,862 adults, 2,117 follow-ups, mean interval 5.5 y. Manual comparison subset: results report 4,439 patients / 5,265 scans (methods text cites 5,562 scans — internal inconsistency). SEGMENTATION PIPELINE (per ref 24 companion): modified 3D U-Net; strided conv (step 2) + transposed conv for GPU memory; trained on MSD liver (contrast CT) with CycleGAN domain transfer to noncontrast; augmentation = 3D rotation, crop, elastic deformation, CycleGAN noncontrast images, random flips; batch 4, resolution 256×256×192, initial filters 32, lr 1e-4, 10k iterations; NIH Biowulf (≤48 GPU nodes, K80/P100). POST-PROCESSING: mean/median HU over all segmented liver voxels. QUANTIFICATION (signs OCR-mangled in source; back-calculated consistent with): CT fat fraction (%) = −0.58 × HU + 38.2, valid at 120 kVp, floored at 0% for HU ≥ 65.9. Steatosis classes: normal <5% (>57 HU); mild 5–14% (42–57 HU); moderate 14–28% (18–42 HU); severe >28% (<18 HU). KEY RESULTS: mean 55±10 HU → FF 6.4%; prevalence normal/mild/moderate/severe = 47.9/42.4/8.8/1.0% (≥mild = 52.1%). Male FF 7.4±6.0 vs female 5.8±5.7 (P<.001); age effect <4 HU across decades; BMI r²=0.14; BMI≥30 subgroup: 69.6% any steatosis, 20.5% mod/severe; multivariable model FF = 78.6 − 0.1·age − 2.4·sex − 0.6·BMI (signs per OCR correction). AUTOMATED vs MANUAL: mean difference 2.7 HU (median 3), r² 0.92 (abstract) / 0.93 (results) — minor inconsistency; Bland-Altman proportional bias 2.7 HU attributed to hepatic blood pool inclusion in volumetric measure. Per-category (sens/spec, manual as reference): normal 82.6/96.3; mild 88.7/83.5; moderate 87.5/98.3; severe 74.6/99.9 (all with 95% CIs). LONGITUDINAL: mean change −3±9 HU; 42.0% decreased ≥5 HU, 15.3% increased ≥5 HU, 42.7% stable; 43.3% (806/1861) crossed a steatosis category, predominantly toward more steatosis (Sankey analysis). MANUAL ROI PROTOCOL: right lobe, 500–1500 mm², avoiding vessels/lesions; readers med students (<1 y) to abdominal radiologists (>10 y); blinded; sourced from routine practice + prior steatosis trials. REVIEW-RELEVANCE CAVEAT: this is an application paper — segmentation accuracy (Dice/IoU) is never reported; the primary segmentation methodology lives in the companion paper (ref 24, Sandfort et al.), which should be the extraction target for architecture-level synthesis; CycleGAN contrast→noncontrast domain adaptation is the notable transferable methodological element.
contribution_summary: Demonstrates population-scale clinical deployment of a deep learning liver segmentation tool (3D U-Net trained on MSD with CycleGAN contrast-to-noncontrast domain transfer) for fully automated hepatic fat quantification on noncontrast CT in 9,552 adults, achieving close agreement with manual ROI measurement (mean difference 2.7 HU, r²≈0.92) and a 0.06% algorithm failure rate. Reports >50% prevalence of at least mild steatosis in an asymptomatic screening cohort and quantifies 5.5-year longitudinal steatosis shifts. For this segmentation review its value is evidence of real-world robustness and domain-adaptation practice, not architectural novelty; segmentation performance metrics are deferred to the companion technical paper.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 400 training scans (100 dataset A + 300 corrected from dataset B), far above the 50-subject threshold; 50-scan held-out test set plus 100-patient observer experiment.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single center (Radboud UMC) but exhaustively characterized: oncology referrals 2014-2017, 2 scanner vendors, 5 reconstruction kernels, 4 contrast agents, slice thickness distribution (98.9% 1-2 mm), demographics (mean 58 y, 54.7% women).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit flowchart (datasets A/B/C/D); random selection; per-epoch model evaluation on 30% of training scans; test set C fully held out; observer set D100 disjoint and enriched by design (stated).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Medical-student annotations with peer review, explicit hilum inclusion rule, quality check and corrections by radiologist with >30 y experience; reference standard for observer study by 2 radiologists with consensus meeting.

Q5_external_validation.justification: All data from one institution; no external or multi-center test set.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Standard 3D U-Net cited with patch-based processing and mirroring border handling, but layer/patch configuration deferred to Appendix E2, not in main text.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Reported: epochs (21/43), early stopping (10-epoch patience), Dice-based model selection, 30% validation fraction, resampling scheme. Missing: optimizer, learning rate, batch/patch size, DL framework, GPU.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Training loss never stated anywhere in the paper.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Fully specified: HU clipping, 1-mm isotropic resampling (cubic for scans, nearest-neighbor for masks), patch extraction for memory, stitch -> 0.5 threshold -> largest connected component -> resample back.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No source code released; model testable via grand-challenge.org online demo (model partially available, code not).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five metrics: Dice, relative absolute volume difference, max Hausdorff, 95% Hausdorff, ASSD.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: 95% CIs via 1000-sample bootstrap for every metric; Mann-Whitney U tests for A-vs-B (P=.019), A-vs-observer (P=.011), B-vs-observer (P=.834).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Table 2 compares against 12 published spleen methods plus splenic index and a human observer; literature-based comparison (different datasets/modalities), not re-implemented on shared data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study; full metric set with SD and CI reported for the spleen.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated failure examples (dilated stomach, low contrast enhancement, beavertail liver) with quality ratings (2.5% failure rate) plus explicit limitations: post-splenectomy false positives, single-observer case selection, student observer as comparator, single-center data.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Inclusion criteria explicit (contrast-enhanced thoraco-abdominal oncology CT, 2014-2017) with random dataset allocation, but population restricted to one center and oncology workup; training subset B300 curated by a single observer's relevance judgment; observer set D100 deliberately enriched with volume-change cases, so not representative of routine prevalence.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Reference standard set by two independent radiologists with consensus meeting; independent observer annotated without access to others; identical metrics applied to all methods. Caveats: radiologist ratings of auto-segmentations are inherently unblinded to method, and the human comparator was a medical student, which flatters the human-vs-AI equivalence claim.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low for outcomes, incomplete for methods. All five metrics reported with SDs, CIs, and failure cases (2.5% failures disclosed); however, loss function, optimizer, and hardware are never reported, limiting independent verification of the pipeline.

detailed_extraction: Two-stage training strategy: system A trained from scratch on 100 scans (21 epochs), then used to triage 1000 unlabeled scans so only 300 relevant cases (B300) required manual correction; system B trained from scratch on all 400 (43 epochs) and outperformed system A (Dice 0.962 vs 0.950, P=.019). Both systems evaluated on test set C. Observer experiment: three reading modes (visual, automatic, assisted SVC assessment); +/-25% SVC tolerance defines shrinkage/normal/growth; reference classes 59 normal / 26 growth / 15 shrinkage; readers disagreed on 13 of 100 pairs. Visual accuracy 81% (splenic index used in 20 of 100 cases), automatic 89%, assisted 92%; radiologist changed classification in 15 of 100 cases when shown segmentations, correctly in 11 (73%), with 5 changes near the 25% threshold (25.16%-27.44%). Segmentation quality ratings on 200 scans: 87% excellent, 7% good, 3.5% bad, 2.5% failure (94% deemed reliable). Volume difference between system B and independent observer: 2.37% (5.17 mL). Splenic index equation V = 30 + 0.58*D*L*H performed poorly (16.56% relative volume error). Annotation protocol identical for training, test, and observer datasets; annotations include splenic hilum when surrounded by parenchyma. Note: provided paper text is truncated mid-discussion; extraction above draws on available text plus prior extraction of the full paper.
contribution_summary: A patch-based 3D U-Net segments the spleen on thoraco-abdominal oncology CT with Dice 0.962, statistically indistinguishable from a human observer (P=.834), using a two-stage model-assisted annotation strategy in which a first model (Dice 0.950) triages 1000 unlabeled scans so only 300 need manual correction. Beyond segmentation accuracy, an observer study (n=100) shows radiologist accuracy for splenic volume-change classification rises from 81% (visual) to 92% when algorithm-assisted, demonstrating clinical utility. Main weaknesses are single-center data and unreported training details (loss, optimizer, framework).

Q1_dataset_size.justification: All five training sets exceed 50 subjects (307/170/170/170/492 CT scans); external validation n=146+32. Adequate for each task.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Two named hospitals (Peking University First Hospital for training; Shenzhen Hospital for validation), date ranges, screening totals (2283, 1774), explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, and a STROBE-style flowchart (Fig 1). CT acquisition in Appendix E1.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: External validation on an independent hospital is clear, but no internal test set or within-training split (holdout/cross-validation) is described; unclear how models were tuned or early-stopped.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual annotations for training and manual volumetry as evaluation reference are stated, but annotator expertise, number of raters, annotation protocol, and inter-rater agreement are not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Spatial external validation on 178 patients from a second hospital, deliberately split into diverse-pathology (n=146) and real preoperative candidates (n=32) cohorts.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Standard 3D U-Net (Çiçek et al. 2016) cited and replicated across five tasks; pipeline logic (4 stages) described. But no layer/patch/resolution specifics or per-model configuration in the main text.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No optimizer, learning rate, epochs, augmentation, or hardware in the main text; training details deferred to Appendix E1 (not verifiable from provided text). DL framework unnamed.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never mentioned in the available text; no justification possible.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Image preprocessing deferred to Appendix E1. Post-processing logic is well described in the main text: FLR formulas (Eqs 1–3) and rule-based candidate thresholds (20%/30%/40% for healthy/fatty/cirrhotic). Input restriction to ≤2 mm slices noted.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or availability statement anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Multiple metrics used (Spearman r, Bland-Altman, AUC, sensitivity/specificity, McNemar, DeLong) but zero standard segmentation metrics — no Dice, IoU, or Hausdorff for any of the five segmentation models.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Thorough: 95% CIs on AUCs, DeLong test with Bonferroni correction, McNemar's test, Shapiro-Wilk, Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney with Bonferroni; normality testing justifies metric choice.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Strong clinical baseline comparison (hepatic VCAR + manual volumetry, the actual standard of care) and narrative comparison with prior DL FLR studies (Le, Ruskó, Butdee, Chen), but no head-to-head with modern DL architectures (nnU-Net, transformers) — acknowledged by authors.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: No per-structure segmentation performance reported for any of the five models; only downstream FLR volumes and clinical categorization outcomes. Cannot isolate which segmentation component drives errors.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit and candid: manual reference instead of actual post-resection remnant, no functional (Gd-EOB-DTPA MRI) volumetry, dated architecture, retrospective two-hospital design, Child-Pugh B/C exclusion. One discordant clinical case also reported.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria with flowchart and full screening counts reduce risk; but retrospective, two Chinese tertiary hospitals only, ≤2 mm slice restriction, and exclusion of Child-Pugh B/C limit spectrum generalizability (authors acknowledge).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate/unclear. Reference standard is manual volumetry by 'human doctors' with no detail on rater count, experience, consensus process, or blinding to DL/VCAR outputs. Reference is manual volumetry, not ground-truth post-resection remnant volume.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate. Reports negative/nuanced findings (no binary categorization difference vs VCAR; DL underestimates manual FLR) and a discordant case; however, no segmentation overlap metrics reported despite five segmentation models, and no trial registration/protocol mentioned.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond prior extraction: (1) Ethics: IRB 2019(169) and 2021(071)/(071)-1; consent waived (retrospective, anonymized). (2) Statistical software: MedCalc 19.7, GraphPad Prism 7.00. (3) FLR% definitions differ by method — DL and human doctors use (VLiver − VTumor) as denominator; hepatic VCAR uses VLiver because it cannot measure tumor volume (Eqs 1–3) — a systematic confound in the VCAR comparison. (4) Parenchyma classes: healthy (no clinical/pathologic liver disease), fatty (graded mild/moderate/severe by MRI-PDFF within 2 weeks of CT), cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A only). (5) Mean results: FLR = 493.51±284.77 cm³ (DL), 489.23±286.29 (VCAR), 500.92±284.38 (manual); FLR% = 38.53%, 37.77%, 38.35%. DL and VCAR both slightly underestimate manual FLR; DL slightly overestimates manual FLR%. (6) DATA DISCREPANCY: prior extraction lists sens/spec 0.86/0.75 for DL-FLRVS, but the main text states 'sensitivity and specificity were 0.78 and 0.82' for DL-FLRVS (cutoff 29.21%) and 0.76/0.76 for VCAR (cutoff 30.57%) — verify against Table 4 before locking extraction. (7) DL AUC significantly superior to VCAR in overall cohorts 1+2 (p<0.0001), healthy livers (p=0.0002), and fatty livers (p=0.005); NOT significant in cirrhosis subgroup. Subgroup AUCs >0.91 for both methods. (8) Cohort-2 composition: 19 HCC, 11 cholangiocarcinoma, 2 metastatic adenocarcinoma; hepatectomy types: 21 complete right, 10 complete left, 1 extended right. (9) Training size per task: whole liver 307, Couinaud segments 170, hepatic veins 170, portal veins 170, lesions 492. (10) No Dice/IoU/HD, no GPU/time, no framework reported anywhere — downstream volumetric/clinical evaluation only. (11) Proposed best clinical cutoff for DL-FLRVS (29.21%) is close to but below the standard 30% fatty-liver threshold.
contribution_summary: Develops DL-FLRVS, a five-model 3D U-Net pipeline segmenting whole liver, 8 Couinaud segments, hepatic/portal veins, and lesions on contrast-enhanced CT, with rule-based FLR volumetry and automatic candidate categorization for major hepatectomy. Its key novelty is a full clinical-workflow validation against both the current semi-automated standard (hepatic VCAR) and manual volumetry in real preoperative candidates and diverse pathologies — near-perfect volumetric agreement with humans (Spearman r=0.99), superior discrimination (AUC 0.89 vs 0.86, DeLong p<0.0001), yet identical binary surgical decisions in almost all cases. Unlike prior DL FLR work focused on technical feasibility or living-donor transplant, this targets hepatectomy planning specifically, with explicitly spectrum-broadened external validation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 105 patients (50 train / 20 val / 35 test; 7090 slices). Training alone is exactly 50, borderline vs the >50 threshold, but 70 modeling subjects plus augmentation (70 contours/lobe) clears it in practice.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort (Shanghai Chest Hospital, June 2019–Aug 2020), stage IIIA(N2) NSCLC, imaging specs fully given (512×512, 5 mm slice, supine, MIM 7.0.4 transfer).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit random split 50/20/35 with stated roles (optimize / model selection / final test). Note: test set is skewed toward RML tumors (10/35) vs train-val (4/70), a distribution shift not discussed by authors.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: One 'experienced' radiation oncologist contoured all five lobes, saved as RTSTRUCT DICOM. Single observer, no years-of-experience detail, no second reader, no inter-observer agreement or arbitration described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Internal test set only; single-center data, no independent institution or public-dataset validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Both branches and fusion described in text plus Fig. 5: V-Net 3D branch (PReLU, 2×2×2 stride-2), dense-connected 2D encoder, fusion tensor 256×256×64×32, 3×3×3 refinement, 2-channel softmax output.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam lr=0.001, weight decay 1e-8, batch size 1, 1000 epochs, 2×1080Ti, PyTorch. Gaps: no learning-rate schedule, augmentation parameters unspecified, no wall-clock time.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss with formula given and rationale stated (mitigates class imbalance); applied to both branches.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing fully specified (resample 1×1×3 mm, crop 256×256, 64-slice volumes stride 1, normalization, slice filtering); absence of post-processing explicitly declared rather than left ambiguous.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; data available 'on reasonable request' only.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Six quantitative metrics (DSC, HD95, MSD, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy) plus clinician visual acceptability assessment (164/175 accepted as-is).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± SD reported per lobe per metric; a Statistical Analysis section mentions SPSS 22 and P<0.05 but no actual p-values or confidence intervals for any comparison appear in the paper.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Literature-only comparison (PDV-Net, Park 3D U-Net, Harrison HNN, George) on different, thinner-slice datasets — no retrained baselines, no internal ablation of 2D-only vs 3D-only vs hybrid.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: All five lobes reported individually for all six metrics in Table 2, with SDs.

Q15_limitations.justification: Specific failure analysis: RML hardest (DSC 0.9003) with two stated causes (small volume, fissure onset slices at 5 mm), Fig. 4 shows the consecutive-slice failure mode, 11/175 contours flagged. Limited to post-processing caveat only — single-center/single-observer not framed as limitations.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/high — retrospective single-center convenience sample of stage IIIA(N2) NSCLC only; inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond pathology confirmation not stated; findings may not transfer to other stages, centers, or scanners.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate — same type of expert (single radiation oncologist) produced ground truth and performed visual quality assessment, unblinded; quantitative metrics applied uniformly, but no consensus reading to verify reference standard.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate — all lobes, all metrics, per-lobe SDs reported; visual assessment outcomes fully reported (11 corrections, 0 failures). Offsets: statistical tests announced but not reported, no ablation results, no code to verify.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details beyond the existing extraction: (1) Claimed novelty — first DL lung-lobe segmentation study on 5 mm slice-thickness RT planning CT of locally advanced NSCLC; prior DL work used 0.5–1.5 mm public data (LIDC, COPD cohorts). (2) Acceptance threshold: DSC ≥ 0.75 pre-defined as clinically acceptable; all lobes passed. (3) Test-cohort tumor distribution differs from training (Table 1): RML tumors 10/35 test vs 4/70 train-val — plausible contributor to lower RML DSC, unacknowledged by authors. (4) Clinical deployment metric: 164/175 contours (93.7%) accepted without edit, 11 corrected across 28 slices, 0 failed — a workflow-relevant outcome rarely reported in public-dataset studies. (5) Ground truth: single expert, RTSTRUCT format, imported via MIM 7.0.4; no second observer. (6) Augmentation described only by category (random translation, scaling, rotation), no parameter ranges; augmentation yielded 70 contours per lobe for train+val. (7) Loss applied identically to both branches; softmax over 2 channels; batch size forced to 1 by 11 GB GPU memory. (8) Failure mode characterized: segmentation errors concentrate at superior-inferior slices where fissures first appear (Fig. 4, RUL/RML transition), attributable to partial volume effect at 5 mm. (9) Statistical analysis section names SPSS v22 and P<0.05 but reports no test results — an internal inconsistency. (10) Ethics declared 'not applicable' (retrospective); funded by Shanghai Chest Hospital internal grant 2019YNJCM05; no competing interests. (11) Authors claim no commercial autosegmentation software covers lung lobes on this CT type. (12) Comparative DSCs quoted for context: PDV-Net 0.882–0.966 (thin-slice LIDC), Park 3D U-Net 0.9306–0.9701 (COPD, 0.625–0.8 mm) — not head-to-head.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes a 2D–3D hybrid CNN (a V-Net 3D branch for volumetric context fused with a dense-connected 2D branch for intra-slice edge/texture detail) targeted at the clinically realistic but understudied problem of lung lobe segmentation on 5 mm slice-thickness radiotherapy planning CT of locally advanced NSCLC patients. On a 105-patient single-center cohort it achieves per-lobe DSC of 0.90–0.96, comparable to state-of-the-art results obtained on much thinner-slice data, and demonstrates clinical usability with 93.7% of contours accepted without correction. The main contribution is the anisotropic-data-aware hybrid architecture and the clinical-thickness validation, not a methodological advance validated beyond one center.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 60 patients for training (>50 threshold); 30+30 for ExVal/GenEva. Total N=120. Small by DL standards but meets criterion; authors explicitly position small-data fine-tuning as the point.
