Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single institution (Peking University Cancer Hospital), IRB approved, Stage II/III mid-low rectal cancer, enrollment dates per subset, demographics (71F/49M, median 65), scanner models and full acquisition parameters (kVp, FOV, resolution) in Table 1.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Clear temporal split: training 03/2020–10/2022 (n=60), ExVal 11/2022–05/2023 (n=30, same scanner), GenEva 02–05/2023 (n=30, different scanner). Additionally 5-fold CV within training (48/12). Test sets fully independent of training.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: GT = clinically approved contours delineated in Eclipse and reviewed by an internal panel, unedited real-world data (strength). But: number/identity of observers, delineation guidelines used, and inter-observer variability not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Two held-out external sets: ExVal (same scanner) and GenEva (Philips Big-Bore vs Siemens Sensation Open — a scanner-change generalizability test). All single-institution, so external in temporal/equipment sense, not multi-center.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: DpnUNet (dual-path-network modules in UNet) only 'generally depicted' in Fig. 2; architecture adopted from Wu et al. [19,20] and commercialized (RT-Mind-AI). Full architectural details deferred to prior work.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Hyperparameters stated (Adam, batch 4, LR 1e-4 with 0.9 exponential decay/epoch, 60 epochs, 5-fold CV 48/12, RTX 2080Ti). But fine-tuning ran through a commercial vendor product — third parties cannot reproduce; augmentation, patching, and loss weights unspecified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Class-weighted cross-entropy, with a one-line rationale ('to take into account the overall accuracy in both CTV and OARs'). Class weights not specified; no comparison with alternatives (e.g., Dice loss).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Only 'minimal data preprocessing' is mentioned; no resampling, normalization, or augmentation details. Post-processing entirely undescribed (whether predictions were edited/cleaned before evaluation is unclear).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or data release. Proprietary commercial software (RT-Mind-AI, MedMind Technology Co. Ltd.).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC, 95HD, sensitivity, specificity, plus CTV volume — exceeds Dice+1 requirement; metric definitions given (Eq. 1–5); computed in 3D Slicer 5.4.0.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Wilcoxon paired signed-rank tests with p-values reported for every structure/metric combination (Table 2), mean ± SD throughout, α=0.05, OriginPro 2021a. No confidence intervals, but p-values satisfy the criterion.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Internal ablation (VPM vs LFT) is well done; external comparison is narrative-only in the discussion (cites DSC 0.877–0.90 from Wu, Men, Song, Larsson). No head-to-head benchmark against other methods.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure reporting for CTV, bladder, femoral heads, and small intestine across both test sets and all four metrics (Table 2, Fig. 5), not just averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: Discussion honestly covers failure modes (small intestine variability, VPM over-contouring, some LFT metrics slightly worse than VPM on bladder/femoral heads) and begins a limitations section, but provided text truncates mid-sentence ('we acknowledge several limitations in...'), so breadth of limitations discussion cannot be fully verified.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Retrospective single-center design, but eligibility (Stage II/III mid-low rectal cancer, distance from anal verge) and enrollment windows are explicitly defined per subset with consecutive-style date ranges. No random sampling from a larger pool described.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Both models (VPM and LFT) evaluated against identical GT with automated metric computation in 3D Slicer and paired statistics. Caveat: GT is single-reference (clinical contours, no independent re-annotation or inter-observer check), so 'accuracy' measures agreement with local protocol rather than anatomical truth.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All 4 structures × 4 metrics × 2 test sets reported, including unfavorable results (LFT marginally worse than VPM on some bladder/femoral-head metrics; small intestine still far below other structures). Minor gap: no effect sizes/CIs; conflict-of-interest statement regarding the commercial vendor (MedMind) not visible in the provided text.

detailed_extraction: Task scope: fine-tuning study, not novel architecture. Backbone: DpnUNet (DPN modules embedded in UNet), originating from Wu et al. [19,20], commercialized as RT-Mind-AI (MedMind Technology Co. Ltd., Beijing); vendor pretrained on 122 patients from one institution. Structures segmented: CTV, bladder, femoral heads, small intestine (pelvic 3D CT, planning scans from Eclipse TPS). Fine-tuning: 60 patients via vendor retraining service; 5-fold CV (48 train/12 val per fold); final model = lowest CV loss. GT provenance: clinically approved contours (physician-delineated, internal panel review, no edits for the study). Key results — CTV: LFT DSC 0.879 (ExVal)/0.874 (GenEva) vs VPM; DSC gain +11.4%/+9.3%, 95HD reduced ~47%/42% (both p<0.01); VPM over-contours CTV by +17.9%/+16.9% relative volume error vs −1.3%/−2.8% for LFT (p<0.05). Bladder: DSC ~0.96 both models; femoral heads: DSC ~0.95 both models (some metrics marginally favor VPM — reported honestly); small intestine: hardest structure, LFT DSC 0.853 (ExVal)/0.834 (GenEva) vs VPM 0.838/0.806 (p<0.01 GenEva). Generalizability: no performance degradation on Philips Big-Bore (GenEva) vs Siemens Sensation Open (ExVal), i.e., robust to scanner change; note GenEva FOV 60 cm vs 65 cm, resolution 1.17 vs 1.27 mm. Statistical method: Wilcoxon paired signed-rank, OriginPro 2021a. Metrics computed in 3D Slicer 5.4.0. Training hardware: single RTX 2080Ti. Scope note for review inclusion: this is primarily CTV + OAR radiotherapy auto-contouring; the OAR portion (bladder, femoral heads, small intestine) falls within '3D organ segmentation from CT', the CTV portion is tumor-target segmentation, not an organ. Study design: retrospective, single-center, IRB-approved; text provided truncates mid-limitations section, so the reference list and full limitations/conflict-of-interest disclosures were unavailable for this extraction.
contribution_summary: First study to fine-tune a commercial DLAS product (RT-Mind-AI/DpnUNet) for rectal cancer radiotherapy, showing that institution-specific fine-tuning with only 60 real-world patients significantly improves CTV delineation (DSC +9–11%, eliminating vendor-model over-contouring) and small intestine segmentation while leaving bladder and femoral head performance (already adequate) essentially unchanged. It also provides a clinically relevant generalizability test demonstrating no performance degradation after a CT scanner change (Siemens → Philips), supporting the robustness of locally fine-tuned commercial DLAS in evolving clinical environments.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: LiTS: 170 abdominal CTs (119 train); KiTS19: 200 CTs (120 train); plus internal dataset 3 (60 CTs / 12 patients) and dataset 4 (8 patients, 32 SPECT/CT time points). Training sets far exceed the 50-subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: All sources explicitly named and characterized: public LiTS (7 institutions, 3 radiologists) and KiTS19 (87 F / 123 M); internal data from 6 hospitals in 5 countries under a registered trial (EudraCT 2016-001897-13); resolution and slice-spacing ranges reported per dataset.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit splits: LiTS 70/10/20; KiTS19 60/20/20; dataset 3: 10 CTs fine-tune train / 10 eval / 40 test; dataset 4 fully held out for dosimetry only. Whole procedure repeated 5x with random patient-level re-splits (K-fold).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: LiTS: manually reviewed by 3 independent radiologists; KiTS19: per Santini et al., with stated convention that tumour mask is included as kidney; dataset 3: single medical physicist confirmed by certified radiologist, with explicit exclusion of renal pelvis/artery/vein.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Genuine external validation: trained on public challenge data, tested on independent multi-centre internal CT (6 hospitals, 5 countries; Dice 94.6 after fine-tuning) and on an 8-patient SPECT/CT dosimetry cohort never used in training or testing.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Modified Mask R-CNN fully specified: 2.5D adjacent-slice input, ResNet50-FPN backbone, RoI-pooling enlarged 7x7 to 28x28, mask output reduced to 256x256, P1/C1 excluded from RPN, two-stage RPN + heads; includes ablation (20% memory saving, 4x slower, +15% accuracy vs unmodified).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Epochs, per-phase learning rates (0.001 heads-frozen / 0.0001 full), batch size 2, GPUs (2x Titan XP), ImageNet pretraining (100 epochs), 5-fold repetition, and per-epoch time reported; but optimizer, LR schedule, and data augmentation never stated.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Standard multi-task Mask R-CNN loss (2x classification + 2x box regression + 1x binary CE mask) described but inherited unchanged; only the architectural modifications were empirically justified (including the mask-size/memory tradeoff), not the loss choice itself.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Explicitly minimal and fully described: HU windowing [-100, 200] only, spatial normalization deliberately eliminated. Post-processing: linear interpolation across ~2% failed slices, 256->512 mask resize at inference, 3 mm Gaussian PSF (sigma 3 mm) mask expansion before SPECT activity retrieval.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, weights, or repository released; dosimetry performed in proprietary QDOSE software (ABX-CRO), further limiting reproduction.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Beyond Dice (93.4 liver; 94.1-94.6 kidney): kidney mass difference vs experts (7.5%), kidney self-absorbed dose difference (6.7%), per-slice failure rate (2%), worst-case dose deviation (25%), and DVH-based comparisons.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No CIs, p-values, or dispersion reported despite 5-fold repeated training; expert comparison on n=8 patients given as point estimates only. Caveat: provided text truncates before Tables 1-4; verify full text for variance measures before finalizing.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Tables 1-2 benchmark against multiple published LiTS methods (Yuan 2017, Bi 2017, Chlebus 2018, Delmoral 2019), KiTS19 (Santini 2019), and non-DL baselines (Okada 2007, Lin 2006). Note: comparator scores cited from literature, not re-run under identical conditions.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver (93.4) and kidney reported separately across three datasets (94.1 KiTS19; 94.6 internal post-fine-tune; +1.5% consensus mode). Caveat: left/right kidneys not differentiated; global slice-mean DSC used.

Q15_limitations.justification: Specific and honest: 8-patient dosimetry cohort; automation still needs expert correction due to SPECT-LDCT misregistration; fixed 3 mm spill-out margin caused 25% dose deviation in one patient (6 mm resolves); no true 3D context; no per-patient margin tuning.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low for public challenge data (defined repositories); moderate for internal cohorts — small (12 and 8 patients), all neuroendocrine-tumour patients from a single dosimetry trial, no explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria stated.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate — same QDOSE pipeline applied to automated and expert masks, but the two experts used different reference methodologies (expert 1: CT-based with co-registration plus manual SPECT adaptation; expert 2: SPECT thresholding), workload split non-blinded (5 vs 3 patients), and no blinded reading against a common reference standard.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low — failure rate, worst-case dose deviation, and limitations explicitly reported; residual concern: no dispersion across the 5 K-fold runs and SOTA comparisons rely on literature-reported numbers rather than re-evaluation.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not in prior extraction: (1) Consensus mode trains/predicts in axial, sagittal, coronal planes with voxel-wise majority voting — 3x compute for +1.5% Dice. (2) LDCT/SPECT co-registration verified by two imaging experts, manually corrected when needed; the AI evaluation deliberately skipped manual SPECT adaptation to test full automation (explains residual dose error). (3) Dosimetry pipeline: QDOSE suite, DVHs, kidney density 1.06 g/cc, bi-exponential fit to 4 time points (0.5/6/24/72 h p.i., 7.5 GBq 177Lu-DOTATOC), voxel S-kernel dose convolution. (4) Expert conventions: renal pelvis/artery/vein excluded from parenchyma; filtrate excluded only at 0.5 h p.i. when uptake is high. (5) Dataset 3 excludes renal pelvis/vessels unlike KiTS19 — this discrepancy motivated the fine-tuning stage. (6) Inference: 2.5 s per 2.5D slice on 1.7 GHz i7 CPU; <3 s per liver or both kidneys on GTX 1070 — no dedicated hardware needed, a core design goal. (7) Failure-mode analysis: liver delineation fails preferentially where liver and heart share the plane; kidney failures not generalizable; both patched by linear interpolation. (8) Trial registration EudraCT 2016-001897-13. (9) Future work: add functional SPECT activity as an extra input channel during training.
contribution_summary: Extends Mask R-CNN to a lightweight 2.5D configuration (ResNet50-FPN, 28x28 RoI pooling, 256x256 masks) for automated kidney and liver CT segmentation with near-zero preprocessing, achieving Dice 93.4 (liver, LiTS) and up to 94.6 (kidney, external multi-centre validation) at clinically routine speed on consumer hardware. Its distinctive contribution is closing the loop to clinical outcome: automated 177Lu-DOTATOC kidney dosimetry differed from expert calculations by only 7.5% (mass) and 6.7% (self-absorbed dose), while demonstrating that automation still requires expert oversight due to SPECT-CT misregistration and fixed spill-out margins.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 14 CT scans from 12 patients — far below the 50-subject threshold; authors acknowledge dataset size as the main obstacle due to rarity of pediatric Wilms' tumor.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single center (CHU Besançon) clearly described: contrast-enhanced pediatric CT, all with arterial phase, 5 with late acquisition; patient demographics and segmentation protocol deferred to prior paper [3].

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Leave-one-patient-out cross-validation explicitly stated: for each patient p, U-Net trained on all other patients, tested on p.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual/semi-automatic annotation by two experts (pediatric surgeon + pediatric radiologist, >5 years pediatric oncology experience) in 3D Slicer 4.8.1; inter-expert Dice (0.95 tumor / 0.87 kidney) reported as a reference ceiling.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external or independent validation; all data internal to one center.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Standard U-Net cited [7] with conceptual encoder/decoder description (max-pooling / unpooling), but no depth, filter counts, patch/slice input size, or 2D vs 3D configuration specified.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: 200 epochs, batch size 16, and LOPO CV reported; optimizer, learning rate, data augmentation, framework, and hardware (beyond 'Mesocenter' supercomputer) absent; OV2ASSION training details deferred entirely to refs [9,10].

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: No image preprocessing (normalization, resampling, cropping) or post-processing described; the paper is silent on whether any was applied. Annotation workflow (3D Slicer) is ground-truth creation, not preprocessing.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; datasets only 'available from the corresponding author on reasonable request' due to privacy/IP.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice only. Expert time-saving is reported but is an efficiency outcome, not a segmentation-accuracy metric; no Hausdorff distance, ASSD, Jaccard, or sensitivity/specificity.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Only min–max ranges across patients (e.g., 0.69 [0.01–0.93]); no confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests comparing U-Net vs OV2ASSION vs expert.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Internal comparison across variants (inter-expert vs fully automatic U-Net vs OV2ASSION at gaps 1/5/10) is thorough; KiTS19 winners (kidney 0.97 / tumor 0.85, adults) discussed as context but no head-to-head on shared data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-patient Dice for both structures (Wilms' tumor and neoplastic kidney) in Tables 1–2, each against the inter-expert baseline, plus identification of outlier patients (9, 10).

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid: objective not fully met (semi-automatic, not automatic); tiny single-center dataset; fully automatic U-Net near-failure (kidney Dice 0.27); pediatric CT quality issues (low dose, motion, low fat contrast); patients 9–10 degrade below Dice 0.80 at larger gaps.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High/unclear — single-center series of 12 patients treated at the authors' own institution; no consecutive enrollment or eligibility criteria stated; case mix not characterized beyond Wilms' tumor.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate — evaluation protocol consistent (Dice against expert reference, inter-expert variability as anchor), but the specific expert serving as reference for AI comparison is unspecified, and time-saving assumes uniform per-section annotation time.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low — negative fully-automatic results reported in full; per-patient tables for all 14 cases and all configurations; minor caveat: only gaps 1, 5, and 10 tabulated of the tested gap range.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary notes: (1) SCOPE FLAG for this review — despite '3D reconstruction' motivation, the method is slice-wise 2D U-Net on axial sections; no volumetric/3D-aware architecture (no 3D convolutions, no multi-view fusion). The 3D model is built downstream from per-slice labels. (2) OV2ASSION (overlearning vector for valid sparse segmentations) is a training regime from the authors' prior work [9,10]: train on sparsely, manually annotated slices with a regular 'gap', network infers intervening slices; gap 1 = 1 of 3 slices manual, gap 10 = 1 of ~6 manual. (3) Although healthy kidneys, vessels, and urinary cavities were annotated, only Wilms' tumor and neoplastic kidney were segmented by AI. (4) Expert-equivalence achieved at gap 7 (tumor) and gap 8 (kidney), i.e., ~80% expert time reduction — this, not the fully automatic Dice, is the paper's operative result; the headline Dice 0.97/0.94 requires gap-1 expert input. (5) Dice defined via explicit pixel-count formula in Methods. (6) Ethics: IRB approval CHU Besançon; consent waived (non-identifying data). (7) Funded by EU Interreg V France-Switzerland (SAIAD/SAIAD 2); computation on Franche-Comté Mesocenter. (8) Data not public, on reasonable request only. (9) No framework, GPU, optimizer, or timing figures reported anywhere.
contribution_summary: The paper shows that a standard U-Net fails at fully automatic segmentation of Wilms' tumor and neoplastic kidney in pediatric CT on a very small single-center dataset (Dice 0.69/0.27), and proposes instead a semi-automatic training scheme (OV2ASSION) where experts annotate only sparse slices. With expert input at expert-equivalent gaps (1 in ~5 slices manual), Dice reaches inter-expert level (0.95 tumor / 0.91 kidney) while cutting expert time by ~80%. The main value for the field is a negative result plus a realistic human-in-the-loop fallback and an explicit call for a shared international pediatric Wilms' tumor CT database (KiTS19-style), rather than a deployable automatic method.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Clinical evaluation cohort is only 10 mCRPC patients (<50). The segmentation model was trained on large public datasets (TotalSegmentator, HaN-Seg), but training set sizes are not stated in this paper.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources clearly described: two cited public datasets for training ([10] TotalSegmentator, [21] HaN-Seg); 10 consecutive retrospective patients from a single centre with explicit eligibility (mCRPC, [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617, VERITON-CT 200), IRB approval 2405B and informed consent.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No train/validation/test split reported; paper only states the nnU-Net was 'trained and validated on two public datasets' without any split methodology.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process for the training data is not described; the paper relies on existing public dataset labels. Bone marrow vs cortical bone separation is a rule-based HU threshold, not an annotation.

Q5_external_validation.justification: The pretrained model was applied to an in-house cohort disjoint from training data (a form of external application), but no quantitative segmentation accuracy (Dice/HD/volumes) is reported on it — validation is only indirect, via dose-rate agreement with MIRDcalc.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture not described in the paper; identified only by citation to nnU-Net V2 [20] (a self-configuring framework). No task-specific configuration details for the 22-structure model.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: DL training details (hyperparameters, splits, augmentation) absent; reproducible in principle since datasets and framework are public and the 23 structures are listed. In contrast, SPECT/CT acquisition/reconstruction and dosimetry parameters are thoroughly reported (OSEM 4 subsets/8 iterations, TEW scatter correction, 2.46 mm voxels, NIST-traceable calibration).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never mentioned; the implicit nnU-Net default is assumed.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Key post-processing clearly defined: bone voxels with HU 0–200 assigned to bone marrow, >200 to cortical bone/osteocondensing tumour. Reconstruction, scatter correction, CT-to-density conversion (Schneider et al. [23]) and activity unit conversion all fully specified.

Q10_code_availability.justification: SimpleDose is freely accessible as a SaaS demo (oncometer3d.com), but no source code, training scripts or model weights are released.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: No segmentation metrics whatsoever (no Dice, HD, or volumetric similarity). Reported metrics are dosimetric: % deviation vs MIRDcalc/LDM, organ masses, activity concentrations, dose rates, runtimes.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only (median and IQR per organ across 10 patients); no confidence intervals, p-values or significance tests.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Benchmarked against two established dosimetry methods (MIRDcalc organ-S-values as reference; EANM-recommended LDM) and contextualized against prior studies (Carter et al., Dewaraja et al., Brosch-Lenz et al.). Segmentation itself uses nnU-Net, the de facto SOTA baseline.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-organ results for all 7 organs of interest (bone marrow, kidneys, liver, lungs, pancreas, salivary glands, spleen) in Tables 3–4, covering masses, concentrations, dose rates, deviations and absorbed doses; no organ-averaged reporting.

Q15_limitations.justification: Discrepancies analyzed with plausible causes (lungs 21%, pancreas 11%, bone-marrow IQR 61% attributed to phantom-based cross-organ S-values; LDM photon-crossfire neglect) and current limits stated (organ-only, tumour model and Monte Carlo comparison underway, single case not generalizable). No dedicated limitations section; segmentation errors never assessed.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low concern: 10 consecutive retrospectively included patients with explicit eligibility criteria, single scanner, IRB approval and consent. Caveat: small single-centre cohort, anatomy limited to head-to-mid-thigh coverage.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate concern: the dosimetry protocol was applied identically across patients and compared against a consistent reference (MIRDcalc), but segmentation output was never checked against ground truth, so segmentation errors propagate unquantified into every dose endpoint.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate: all planned dose comparisons, timings and per-organ tables are reported; however, no segmentation quality metrics are reported at all, and the multi-time-point illustration uses a single patient.

detailed_extraction: SCOPE NOTE FOR REVIEW: this is a dosimetry pipeline paper; deep-learning segmentation is an embedded, inherited component (pretrained nnU-Net V2 on public data), with no new segmentation method, training experiment, or accuracy evaluation. Segmentation: nnU-Net V2 [20] trained/validated on TotalSegmentator [10] and HaN-Seg [21], simplified to 22 structures; custom rule-based post-processing splits bone into bone marrow (HU 0–200) and cortical bone (>200), yielding 23 structures (Table 1: adrenal glands, aorta, bone marrow, cortical bone, brain, colon, duodenum, esophagus, gallbladder, heart, kidneys L/R, lacrimal glands, liver, lungs L/R, pancreas, salivary glands, small bowel, spleen, stomach, trachea, urinary bladder). Imaging: VERITON-CT 200 360° CZT SPECT/CT, 72–96 h post-injection (median 92 h), 5 min/bed × 4 beds head-to-mid-thigh, OSEM 4 subsets/8 iterations, triple-energy-window scatter correction (primary 101.6–124.2 keV), 2.46×2.46×2.46 mm³ voxels, Bq/mL calibration via phantom + NIST-traceable dose calibrator; median injected activity 7025 MBq. Dosimetry: collapsed-cone superposition (CCS) with scaled dose-point kernels for patient-specific density (authors' prior work [13,14], previously validated vs Monte Carlo on phantoms); comparators LDM (EANM, mean β+e = 147 keV for 177Lu) and MIRDcalc (ICRP adult male phantom scaled to CT-derived organ masses). Results: median runtime 161 s (IQR 23) whole-body on 20-core Intel Xeon CPU; median |Δ| vs MIRDcalc <5% for kidneys (2.4%), liver (2.9%), salivary glands (1.1%), spleen (4.0%); higher for lungs (21%), pancreas (11%); bone marrow −1.8% but IQR 61% (phantom micro-structure modelling). LDM systematically underestimated (kidneys −3.1%, liver −9.2%, marrow −16%, spleen −10%), consistent with Carter et al. Clinical example: 4 time points (5.4 h, 21.4 h, 69.8 h, 165 h; 7043 MBq); bi-exponential integration vs Hänscheid single-time-point; 14 min multi-time-point vs 3.3–3.5 min single-time-point; day-1 STP best matched for liver/lungs/salivary glands, day-3 for other organs (n=1). DATA INCONSISTENCIES (relevant to extraction): abstract reports kidneys LDM deviation as −93.1% while Results/Table 3 report −3.1% (apparent typo); abstract gives bone marrow SD deviation as +1.8% while Results/Table 3 give −1.8%; Results text labels the 67 (13) g mass as spleen while Table 3 assigns it to pancreas (spleen 193 (182) g). Availability/ethics: SaaS at oncometer3d.com; data on reasonable request; IRB 2405B; funding Région Normandie/Centre Henri Becquerel; tumour segmentation for PSMA lesions and Monte Carlo comparison announced as future work.
contribution_summary: Proof-of-concept of SimpleDose, a fully automated whole-body [177Lu]Lu-PSMA dosimetry pipeline for 360° CZT SPECT/CT that combines nnU-Net-based 23-structure segmentation (public-data-trained model plus an HU-threshold bone marrow/cortical bone split) with collapsed-cone superposition to compute patient-specific voxel-level dose rates. In 10 patients it matched the MIRDcalc reference within ~5% median deviation for most soft-tissue organs in ~161 s, and demonstrated 14-min multi-time-point and ~3.5-min single-time-point dosimetry. For this segmentation-focused review, the paper evidences off-the-shelf deep-learning segmentation deployed reliably enough for clinical dosimetry, but contributes no segmentation accuracy evaluation of its own.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Six independent cohorts totaling ~222 scans (~147 train / 75 test), but each task trains a separate model with only 3-40 training subjects (skeletal 3-40, orbita 21, mandible 19, cardiac 32, fetal 20, pulmonary 15) — below the >50-per-task threshold for every individual model. The authors explicitly frame this as a feature, and their ablation (Dice 0.92 at n=3 vs 0.94 at n=40) argues small sets suffice for their high-contrast targets; however, adequacy for soft-tissue organs is untested.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources thoroughly documented: Skåne University Hospital 3D Centre clinical referrals (5 cohorts), 8 TCIA cases (skeletal), and the published fetal MRI cohort of Ryd et al. 2022 (42 fetuses, GA 36 [29-39] wks, 1.5T Siemens Aera bSSFP). Table 3 details modality, train/test sizes, clinical application, and anatomy per cohort; CT vendors (Siemens, Philips, GE, Toshiba/Canon) listed; supplemental files give per-case age, sex, pathology, resolution, and volume size; ethics approvals reported (Dnr 2021-03583, Dnr 2013/551).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Train/test sizes explicitly stated per cohort, with an explicit statement of no train/test overlap and that anatomic/pathologic/resolution diversity was preserved when splitting; knees were deliberately excluded from skeletal training for a zero-shot test case. However, the split mechanism (randomization, stratification) is not described, and no dedicated validation set is reported for five of six tasks (only fetal used 5-fold CV), leaving model-selection/early-stopping practice unclear.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process well described: semi-automatic segmentation (thresholding + morphological operations) in Segment 3DPrint v4.0 followed by extensive slice-by-slice manual correction and 3D pen tool editing; every dataset reviewed by a second observer; same annotations used for both training and evaluation. Note this introduces circularity with the authors' own commercial software, but the process itself is clearly reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external test validation. The 8 external TCIA cases were added to the training set (to include older scans), not held out for independent testing. The zero-shot knee experiment is illustrative but remains an internal test case from the same single-center pipeline. All evaluation is on in-house single-center data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture fully specified: Mathworks 2D U-Net (3x3 convolutions, 'same' padding, encoder depth 4) applied to 128x128 patches of transversal, sagittal, and coronal 2D stacks with voxel-wise probability averaging across the three orientations (tri-planar consensus); patch-based (rather than full-volume) inference for memory efficiency, with workflow figure. Task-specific deviations are also documented (mandible uses only sagittal+coronal planes).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Reproducibility is strong on paper: complete hyperparameter table (patch 128 [256 fetal], Adam, lr 0.001 [0.005 fetal], lr drop period 4-6, drop factor 0.8-0.9, encoder depth 4, epochs 100, batch 30-100, L2 1e-4, gradient threshold L2 norm) plus a detailed augmentation table with per-augmentation probabilities and uniform-distribution ranges. Caveats: some values are given as ranges per task, the code is proprietary (Matlab/Segment 3DPrint), and the loss/optimizer mapping to Matlab defaults requires assumptions.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Cross-entropy loss is stated but never justified. Notably, the paper itself highlights severe class imbalance (trachea = 1.8%±0.7% of lung volume) — precisely the scenario where the CE-vs-Dice/compound-loss choice matters — yet no rationale, alternative comparison, or discussion of loss selection is provided.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre- and post-processing exhaustively described. Preprocessing: isotropic resampling to the highest of in-plane/through-plane DICOM resolution; tri-planar stacking; 128x128 patch extraction with specified overlap ensuring multiple coverage. Postprocessing: object filling; removal of objects <0.1 ml; class-specific probability thresholds (50%/25%/12.5%, Table 4) selected on training data only; n-largest connected components (26-connectivity); anatomical touch constraint (trachea must contact parenchyma).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No public code, models, or weights. Implemented in Matlab R2022a and embedded in the commercial Segment 3DPrint software (Medviso AB); the senior author owns Medviso AB (declared COI). Data cannot be shared due to privacy regulations. Combined with no public benchmarks, independent reproduction is essentially impossible.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Four complementary metrics reported with SDs: Dice, Jaccard, 95th-percentile surface distance (signed and absolute, via surface triangulation), and median surface distance. The authors also thoughtfully discuss metric interpretation pitfalls (citing Reinke et al.), e.g., the inflated cardiac 95th-percentile distance (11.07 mm) caused by clinically insignificant missed small vessels.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± SD reported for all metrics and per-patient distributions shown as bar plots; however, no confidence intervals, no p-values, no significance testing (e.g., for the n=3 vs n=40 ablation differences of ~2%), and the authors acknowledge results reflect a single training run per task (except fetal 5-fold CV), which they admit can produce statistically different models.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: No baseline comparisons whatsoever. nnU-Net is cited and acknowledged as the challenge-winning framework but is neither implemented nor compared; comparison_methods list is empty. Claims of 'high performance' rest on absolute metric values on private data without external reference points.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure results given in Table 5 (e.g., mandible 0.96 vs eyes 0.88 vs trachea 0.82 Dice) plus full per-patient Dice/Jaccard breakdowns for every task (Figs. 10, 14-18), enabling identification of outlier cases (e.g., dissociated failures between orbita and eyes within the same patients).

Q15_limitations.justification: Exemplary failure analysis: dedicated failure-mode section with figures of the lowest-scoring case per task and specific causes (poor bone quality, cropped volume missing an eye, skull misclassified as mandible, contrast-filled liver included in cardiac segmentation, fetal head motion artifacts, out-of-range HU in newborn with esophageal catheter), plus an explicit limitations section (fixed hyperparameters, single training runs, untested soft-tissue organs, metric sensitivity to cropping/post-processing, undeleteable data).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate risk. Single-center convenience sample of patients referred to a hospital 3D printing centre; explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and the randomization/stratification procedure for train-test assignment are not reported. The authors did deliberately preserve diversity (age, pathology, scanner, resolution) and engineered a zero-shot knee case, but generalizability beyond one Swedish tertiary centre (and one vendor mix) is unverified; only 8 public (TCIA) cases, used in training.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate risk. Consistent evaluation pipeline and identical metric suite applied to all test cases; ground truths reviewed by a second observer; post-processing thresholds selected on training data only with an explicit statement of no test-based adjustment. Residual concerns: per-task post-processing configurations (Table 4) carry tuning discretion; ground truth generated in the same commercial software as deployment (annotation-evaluation circularity); models trained only once per task (except fetal), so training stochasticity is unquantified by the authors' own admission.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low risk overall, with caveats. All per-structure and per-patient results, failure cases, and limitations are transparently reported, and the authors actively caution against over-reading Dice/Jaccard. However, the lung 'vessels' class was trained but not included in reported test metrics, no negative baseline comparisons exist to selectively report against, and hyperparameter/augmentation settings were fixed 'by consensus' without documented tuning trails.

detailed_extraction: TASK-SPECIFIC CONFIGURATIONS: Mandible model used only sagittal+coronal planes (transversal excluded because mandible vs. maxilla/teeth is indistinguishable in axial 2D patches of identical bone intensity) and disabled mirroring/transpose augmentation since left-right position relative to the skull is the only discriminating cue. Fetal model (the original application, from Ryd et al. 2022) used patch 256, lr 0.005, 5-fold CV, and 0% mirroring/transpose/streak-noise augmentation. All other tasks shared one hyperparameter set fixed by consensus without post-hoc tuning. AUGMENTATION (Table 1): global 3D volume rotation U(-20,20) deg at 0-50% probability; 2D rotation U(-20,20)-U(-45,45); scaling U(0.7,1.3)-U(0.6,1.4); mirroring H/V + transpose 50% (0% mandible/fetal); white noise U(0,15%) and streak noise U(0,50%)-U(0,70%) of intensity range; brightness U(-30,30)-U(-100,100) HU; contrast U(0.95,1.05)-U(0.7,1.3)-U(0.65,1.5); Gaussian blur (kernel 3); sharpening U(0.7,1.3) (fetal-only); augmentations re-drawn per epoch so no identical patch recurs. CLASS DEFINITIONS: skeletal = single filled-bone class; oculo-cranial = bone incl. thin orbital floor + eyes; mandibulo-cranial = mandible + cranium (all other bone); cardiac = contrast blood pool (chambers + connected vessels) + bone; fetal = fetus/placenta/umbilical cord/amniotic fluid (only fetus evaluated); pulmonary = parenchyma + vessels + trachea, but ONLY parenchyma and trachea appear in test metrics (vessels class trained yet never evaluated). COHORT DETAILS: cardiac cases aged 1 day-18 y with broad CHD spectrum (ToF, univentricle, hypoplastic/double-outlet ventricles, VSDs), all IV-contrast, with contrast intensity noted as highly variable; fetal = 42 fetuses (only 20 train/22 test used here); pulmonary with 11/15 train and 7/10 test contrast-positive, trachea = 1.8%±0.7% of lung volume (explicit severe class-imbalance stress test). EVALUATION METHOD: 95th-percentile signed AND absolute surface distances from ground-truth surface normals via triangulation; median distances very low across tasks (0.12-1.17 mm). KEY ABLATION FINDINGS: skeletal Dice essentially plateaus (0.92 at n=3, 0.92 at n=5, 0.94 at n=10, 0.93 at n=20, 0.94 at n=40; ~2% spread); performance gains from added data concentrate on the initially hardest patients (#6,10,12,13) while n=3 beat n=40 on 3 easier patients (incl. #2) — an explicit generalizability-vs-performance trade-off; adding many easy cases may degrade hard-case performance. ZERO-SHOT: knee excluded from training achieved Dice 0.95/Jaccard 0.91; authors argue models learn local tissue texture/intensity rather than anatomy — advantageous for grossly abnormal 3D-printing anatomy (severe scoliosis, heterotaxy). FAILURE MODES: poor image/bone quality (skeletal); cropped volume not covering left eye (orbita); skull misclassified as mandible + unsegmented bony condyle mass + skull support segmented (mandible); unusually contrast-filled liver wrongly included + missed small vessels (cardiac — explaining the 11.07 mm 95th-pct distance); fetal head motion artifacts; out-of-range HU in hours-old newborn + contrast-filled esophageal catheter (lung). EFFICIENCY: 10.10 s inference for 256x256x256 on consumer Alienware laptop (NVIDIA Ti 3080), supporting the resource-constrained adoption claim. ADMINISTRATIVE: funded by Swedish Research Council (2021-04855), Region of Scania ALF, Swedish Heart & Lung Foundation (20230720); COI — Heiberg is founder/owner of Medviso AB whose Segment 3DPrint was used for annotation, evaluation, AND deployment; data non-shareable (privacy); article CC BY 4.0. REVIEW-RELEVANCE CAVEATS: despite the title, no 3D convolutions are used — it is a 2D U-Net producing 3D output via tri-planar consensus; only five of six tasks are CT (fetal is MRI); only 8/147 training scans are from a public source; no comparison to nnU-Net despite citation; results should be treated as single-center, no-baseline evidence for a deployment-oriented framework rather than as SOTA segmentation evidence.
contribution_summary: The paper introduces a generalizable, resource-light clinical segmentation framework: a single fixed-hyperparameter 2D U-Net applied tri-planarly with probability-averaging consensus fusion and standardized augmentation/post-processing, integrated into the commercial Segment 3DPrint software, achieving average Dice 0.92±0.06 across six 3D-printing tasks using only 3-40 training subjects per task and ~10 s inference on a consumer GPU. A training-set-size ablation (Dice plateau from n=3) and a zero-shot knee experiment (Dice 0.95) support the central claim that local texture/intensity learning suffices for data-efficient, anatomy-agnostic segmentation of bone and high-contrast structures. For systematic review purposes, the contribution is strongest as clinical-translation and data-efficiency evidence, but is weakened by the absence of SOTA comparisons (e.g., nnU-Net), lack of external test validation, proprietary code, and untested soft-tissue organs.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 82 NIH scans, 4-fold CV -> ~61 training subjects per fold, exceeding the >50 threshold; still small by pancreas-segmentation standards and adequate only marginally.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public NIH Pancreas dataset (Roth et al.) explicitly cited with acquisition details (82 contrast-enhanced abdominal CT, 512x512xL, L in [181,466], slice thickness 0.5-1.0 mm) and a data availability link.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 4 fixed folds, 3 train / 1 test, plus 10% of training slices held out for overfitting monitoring; standard NIH protocol. Minor caveat: the 10% validation split is at slice level, so slices from the same scan can appear in both training and validation (test folds remain scan-level).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground-truth masks inherited from the NIH dataset; no annotation process (annotators, protocol, inter-rater agreement) described in this paper — only the source citation.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort; single public dataset with internal 4-fold cross-validation only.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Conceptually well described with figures and equations (2.5D U-like, 4 encoder/decoder blocks, first two encoder layers 3D conv + rest 2D, dense blocks of 6 conv layers, hybrid spatial+channel attention in skips). However, filter counts, kernel sizes, and decoder channel configuration are not specified, so exact reimplementation is not possible from the text.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Good coverage: Keras, GTX 1060, Adam, lr=1e-5, batch size 1, 30 epochs per model, slice-selection rule (>100 pancreas pixels), 10% validation slices. Missing: any data augmentation, per-layer hyperparameters, and whether the fixed folds match Roth et al.'s exact splits; no code released to close gaps.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Soft-Dice reformulated as loss (Eq 3), defined and cited to V-Net, but never justified — notably no discussion of class imbalance, the standard motivation for Dice loss on an organ occupying <2% of volume.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described: HU clip [-100,240], rescale to [0,255], resize to 224x224, 3 adjacent slices as channels with edge-slice replication (Si,Si,Si) at volume boundaries, coarse-stage slice filtering, margin frame added before fine-stage cropping, majority-vote multi-view fusion.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; data availability statement covers the dataset only.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC only. Mean/max/min/std are statistics of the same metric; no HD95/ASSD, sensitivity, specificity, or VOE.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only (mean±std, max, min over test cases); no confidence intervals, no significance tests — despite the claim of a 'significant improvement' over Zhang et al. (86.61 vs 84.61) with no test to support it.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive Table 2 comparison against 6 published pancreas methods (Zhou, Roth, Yu, Asaturyan, Zhang, Li) plus ablations vs Attention U-Net, DANet, 2D U-Net, and 3D U-Net. Caveat: comparison numbers taken from original papers, not re-run under identical conditions.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (pancreas), so all reported results are organ-specific; additionally reports per-view coarse DSC, fusion DSC, and slice-level DSC distribution (DSC<0.5: 9.42% -> 3.09%).

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section or failure-case analysis; a single sentence in the Fig 7 discussion admits poor boundary prediction. Dataset-size and 2.5D limitations are never acknowledged by the authors.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-unclear. Uses the full public NIH dataset (82 scans) with fixed 4-fold CV and no apparent case cherry-picking; however, patient inclusion/exclusion criteria are inherited from Roth et al. and not restated, and no patient demographics/clinical characteristics are reported.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate/unclear. The proposed pipeline is evaluated consistently (3D DSC after multi-view fusion, same preprocessing for all stages/folds), but all 6 SOTA baselines are quoted from their original publications rather than re-implemented under identical folds and preprocessing; outcome claims are not supported by significance testing.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate. Unfavorable results are disclosed (coarse-stage DSC 78.79, >20-point max-min gap per view, poor boundary prediction), suggesting limited selective reporting; but reporting is confined to DSC, with no inference time, no per-fold breakdown, and no failure-case analysis.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Majority-vote fusion is formalized as Y = (Y_s + Y_a + Y_c)/3 (Eq 4), i.e., an average of binary masks — the binarization threshold (>0.5, i.e., >=2 of 3 views) is implied but never stated. (2) Channel attention differs from CBAM: global average AND max pooling are applied after CONCATENATING two encoder feature maps X and Y from different dense blocks (not pooling a single map), then shared conv -> fusion -> sigmoid; spatial attention upsamples Y by 2, fuses with X, applies 1x1 convs + sigmoid (Eq 6). (3) Notation overload: Y denotes both ground-truth mask (Eq 1) and an encoder feature map in the attention section. (4) Volume boundaries handled by replicating the edge slice (Si,Si,Si). (5) Two stages x 3 views = 6 models trained per fold (24 models total across 4 folds), an inference-cost consideration not discussed; inference time not reported. (6) Training constrained to a consumer GTX 1060, which motivates the 2.5D design; parameters 7.3M for the fine model. (7) No data augmentation is mentioned. (8) Comparisons to Zhou/Roth/Yu/Asaturyan/Zhang/Li use figures from original publications (same dataset, standard 4-fold protocol assumed but not verified). (9) Slice-level analysis: fraction of slices with DSC<0.5 drops from 9.42% (2D U-Net) to 3.09% (proposed). (10) The provided full text is truncated mid-Table 3 (ablation table), so the numeric ablation values for 2D/3D U-Net and the attention variants are not extractable from the supplied text; only the prose claims (proposed attention > Attention U-Net > DANet ordering; 30 vs ~70 min/epoch training time) are available. (11) No funding, no competing interests; open-access CC-BY.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a 2.5D U-shaped network that mixes 3D convolutions (first two encoder layers) with 2D convolutions, dense convolution blocks, and a hybrid spatial+channel attention module in the skip connections, embedded in a Zhou-style cascaded coarse-to-fine, three-view framework with majority-vote fusion. It achieves 86.61±3.47 mean DSC (max 92.03, min 73.89) on the NIH pancreas benchmark with 4-fold CV, outperforming prior methods with modest compute (7.3M parameters, trainable on a GTX 1060) and improved stability (higher minimum DSC, fewer low-DSC slices). The contribution is an accuracy/compute trade-off for small-organ segmentation, but the evidence base is a single small public dataset, Dice-only evaluation, no statistical testing, and no code release.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 80 training scans exceeds the >50 threshold, though modest for 3D DL; total corpus is 110 (131 LiTS minus 21 excluded).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: LiTS public benchmark explicitly named with access link in data availability statement; version/year of LiTS subset not pinned.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split sizes given (80/10/20) but randomization method, stratification, or seed not described; no cross-validation.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Uses LiTS public annotations without describing the annotation protocol; partial credit for actively excluding 21 cases deemed inaccurately annotated.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single dataset (LiTS) only; test set is an internal split, no independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Generator (4-down/4-up U-Net, 3x3 convs, BN, ReLU, multi-axis attention in skips, axis-projection FP with learnable fusion weights) and discriminator (3 conv layers + FC + sigmoid, dropout 0.5, conditional CT+label input) fully specified with figures.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: PyTorch 1.8.0, AdamW (lr 2e-4), batch size 2, RTX 3090, plus public code repo compensate for missing epoch count/training duration in the text.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Both components explicitly motivated: Tversky loss for tumor class imbalance, Wasserstein distance for GAN stability/mode collapse.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (depth cropping to label range, HU windowing level 70/width 100, range -30 to 170, resize 256x256) and postprocessing (connected components, drop <0.3x largest) fully specified.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Source code with model publicly released at https://github.com/jhliao0525/MA-cGAN.git.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice, Hausdorff distance (HD95), average surface distance (ASD), and Jaccard all reported per structure.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests visible in provided text; single-point results only.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Seven baselines spanning CNN, attention, and Transformer families: 3D-UNet, AttnUNet, TransUNet, UTNet, TransBTS, UNETR, SwinUNETR. Whether baselines were retrained under identical settings is unstated.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver (Dice 96.95) and tumor (Dice 78.53) reported separately with full metric sets for each.

Q15_limitations.justification: Slower adversarial-training convergence acknowledged in results discussion; general GAN instability discussed in background, but a dedicated limitations treatment could not be fully verified from truncated text.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Single public dataset; authors excluded 21/131 LiTS cases (~16%) post hoc for annotation inaccuracy — reason stated but exclusion criteria not formalized; no patient-level inclusion/exclusion criteria.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. All models evaluated on the same internal test split with consistent metrics; unclear whether the 7 baselines were retrained under identical preprocessing/hyperparameters or numbers cited from prior work.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Four complementary metrics reported per target structure; missing uncertainty estimates and unverifiable ablation/limitation completeness due to text truncation are the main gaps.

detailed_extraction: Methodological details not in prior extraction: (1) The multi-axis FP mechanism projects 3D volumes onto axial, sagittal, and coronal planes, raising target-pixel proportion from O(1/n^3) to O(1/n^2); the three axis features are fused via three learnable scalar weights. (2) Discriminator is conditional: receives CT volume concatenated with either real or generated label map, output via FC + sigmoid; dropout 0.5. (3) Adversarial loss is log-free Wasserstein form combined with Tversky loss for the generator; stated purpose is balancing generator/discriminator during adversarial training. (4) Reported efficiency: 4.99M parameters, 41.93 GFLOPs — notably lightweight versus Transformer baselines. (5) Qualitative claims: fewer false positives and clearer tumor boundaries (ITK-SNAP used for visualization). (6) Stated clinical motivation: manual annotation takes >30 min/case. (7) Missing/never reported in visible text: epoch count, training wall-clock, inference latency, ablation results for MA/FP/cGAN components (likely present but truncated), whether comparisons used retrained or cited baselines, license of released code, exact LiTS subset version. (8) Funding: multiple Chinese national/provincial grants; no competing interests declared.
contribution_summary: Proposes MA-cGAN, a conditional GAN whose generator is a 3D U-Net augmented with multi-axis attention that projects volumes onto all three anatomical planes and fuses them via learnable weights, paired with a conditional convolutional discriminator and a Tversky + Wasserstein loss to handle tumor class imbalance and GAN instability. Achieves Dice 96.95 (liver) / 78.53 (tumor) with HD95 2.15 / 12.12 on a LiTS subset, outperforming seven CNN/Transformer baselines at only 4.99M parameters. Key caveats: single-dataset internal validation, no statistical significance testing, and slower convergence than purely supervised models.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 422 chest CT scans (303 with expert lung annotations) exceed the >50 subject threshold. Note: this is an evaluation-only cohort; the wrapped models were pretrained externally and no training was performed in this study.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source clearly described and cited: NSCLC-Radiomics (Aerts et al., TCIA), downloaded as DICOM from NCI Imaging Data Commons via the idc-index Python package. Publicly accessible.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No train/validation/test split exists — the platform is inference-only and all 422 scans serve as an evaluation set. No split methodology is (or needs to be) described, but the criterion is not met.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Expert annotations of left/right lungs for 303 patients are used as reference, but the annotation process (annotator expertise, protocol, inter-rater agreement) is not described in this paper — deferred to the original dataset publication.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single-dataset evaluation (NSCLC-Radiomics only). No held-out external cohort. The authors explicitly argue for recurring local validation over external validation (Youssef et al.), but no independent dataset is used here.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: No network architecture is described in-text; the 30 wrapped models (incl. nnU-Net-based TotalSegmentator, LungMask, MONAI models) defer to their original publications. Partial credit because the actual contribution — the platform/deployment architecture (containers, IO modules, workflows, metadata schema, CI/CD) — is fully and precisely described, and per-model architecture is captured in the structured metadata schema.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Reproducibility of execution is the paper's core contribution and is handled rigorously: verbatim docker run commands for all models, per-model sample input + reference output (Zenodo) with automated Dice<0.99 deviation checks, JSON-schema-validated metadata, CI/CD with PR-triggered test reports published on GitHub. Training hyperparameters are N/A (no training). Caveat: Docker Hub images are tagged :latest with no version pinning.

Q8_loss_function.justification: N/A — inference-only platform; no training or loss functions are discussed. Models are used with pretrained weights.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described: automated DICOM sorting (dicomsort), format conversion (plastimatch, dcm2niix, dcmqi; NIFTI/MHA/TIFF/DICOMSEG/RTStruct), 18 core IO modules (importers/filters/converters/exporters/organizers), YAML workflow orchestration, and explicit postprocessing (lobe-level outputs aggregated into composite left/right lung masks to match expert annotation format).

Q10_code_availability.justification: Fully open: code/containers on GitHub (https://github.com/MHubAI), Docker Hub images (mhubai/<model>), web platform (https://mhub.ai/), 3D Slicer plugin (MHubRunner), and public interactive result dashboards (Looker Studio). Specific software license for the code not stated in-text.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice is the only accuracy metric used (in the use case and in the reproducibility test engine). No surface-distance or volumetric metrics (e.g., Hausdorff distance, ASSD). Paired t-tests and Spearman correlations are statistical analyses of Dice, not additional metrics.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired t-tests with effect estimates and p-values for left/right lung differences (e.g., LungLobes estimate −0.0115, p<.001) and Spearman rank correlations for age vs Dice (n=590). No confidence intervals reported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Side-by-side comparison of three independently developed state-of-the-art lung segmentation models (TotalSegmentator v1, LungMask, LungLobes) on identical data under identical execution, against expert reference — enabled by the platform itself. Weakness: headline Dice values appear only in Figure 4d and public dashboards, not numerically in the text.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Left and right lung results reported separately per model, both graphically (Fig 4d) and statistically in-text (per-organ paired t-tests). Per-case Dice available via public dashboard. Limited to two structures, consistent with the use-case scope.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated limitations discussion: Docker admin privileges, contributor overhead for metadata/reproducibility compliance, incomplete modality coverage (e.g., WSI beyond TIFF), single-sample reproducibility tests cannot cover edge cases, GPU requirements limit deployment.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Case selection is clearly defined (all 422 NSCLC-Radiomics chest CTs; 303 with expert labels; 14 excluded from age analysis for missing age data). However, the cohort is narrow (NSCLC patients only), limiting generalizability of the benchmark to other populations/pathologies; this is acknowledged indirectly via the authors' local-validation argument.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All three models were executed with identical docker commands, identical input data, the same expert reference standard, and a single Dice computation pipeline; no model-specific tuning was applied. Assessment conditions are consistent by construction.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate. All outcomes, including unfavorable findings (LungLobes left-lung deficit; small negative age correlations for LungMask and TotalSegmentator), are reported, and case-level results are publicly released, minimizing selective reporting. However, absolute Dice scores are not reported numerically in the text (relegated to a figure and external dashboards), and the standardization scoring rubric (0-2 per characteristic) is author-defined without independent validation.

detailed_extraction: Study type: infrastructure/framework paper with a lung segmentation benchmark as demonstration; published as a non-peer-reviewed Research Square preprint (posted June 9, 2026) — findings should be weighted accordingly. Model repository composition at publication: 30 models = 22 segmentation, 8 prediction, 2 feature extraction; modalities CT (18), MRI (10), PET (3), X-ray (1), pathology (2). 17/30 models (56.7%) share at least one segmentation label with another model, enabling pairwise comparison without relabeling. Standardization quantification: four characteristics (input format, output format, inference interface, user documentation) scored 0-2 each across 30 models (240 points max); original distributions 36% (86/240), MHub.ai deployments 99% (237/240), reported as +275% (151 points). Scoring rubric explicitly defined (e.g., output standardized = DICOMSEG with semantic annotations; CLI standardized = identical command across models). Reproducibility testing: per-model real-world sample input + reference output on Zenodo; test engine (mhub.test entry point) checks directory-, file-, and content-level differences; Dice<0.99 vs reference flagged as deviation; independent reproducibility check per model during contribution with reports public on GitHub; framework updates gated by these tests. Framework internals: Python runtime (mhub.run) with semantic descriptors/queries resolving IO via a local metadata graph; extension API for third-party IO modules; custom model-wrapper modules; keyword lookup table mapping ROIs to DICOMSEG identifiers (e.g., HEART, LEFT_UPPER_LUNG_LOBE; composite findings like LEFT_LUNG+TUMOR). Evaluation details: 422 NSCLC-Radiomics CTs from IDC (idc-index package); 303 with expert left/right lung annotations; models run via default CLI with zero model-specific adjustment; LungLobes lobe outputs aggregated to composite lungs; age analysis excluded 14 patients without age (n=590 Dice observations reported; note 303−14=289 patients would imply n=578 — minor inconsistency in the text). Statistical results: left-vs-right lung — LungLobes estimate −0.0115, p<.001 (left lower); LungMask estimate −0.000435, p=.828; TotalSegmentator estimate −0.00123, p=.539. Age correlations — LungLobes ρ=.013, p=.756 (ns); LungMask ρ=−.132, p=.001; TotalSegmentator ρ=−.116, p=.005 (small negative). Dashboard infrastructure: Google Cloud Storage → Google Cloud Healthcare API DICOM Store → BigQuery (metadata queries) → OHIF viewer via DICOMweb through unauthenticated proxy → Looker Studio dashboard. Ecosystem positioning: authors argue no equivalent inference-time standardization exists (MONAI Model Zoo, Hugging Face, BioImage Model Zoo aid discovery but do not enforce execution interfaces); TotalSegmentator cited as rare successful single-model example. Technical preprint with implementation details: Nürnberg et al., arXiv:2601.10154. Conflicts of interest: Aerts reports consulting/stock from multiple companies; NIH- and ERC-funded. Relevance to the present review: this paper contributes no new segmentation method or accuracy result for 3D organ segmentation; its value is as enabling infrastructure (DICOM-native packaging of existing organ-segmentation models incl. TotalSegmentator, lung/lobe segmentation) and as a template for reproducible multi-model benchmarking. Include only if the review covers reproducibility/deployment as a secondary outcome.
contribution_summary: MHub.ai is an open-source, container-based platform that standardizes inference-time distribution of 30 peer-reviewed medical imaging AI models via a unified DICOM-native application interface, structured metadata, and built-in reproducibility tests (sample input/reference output with Dice<0.99 deviation gating), raising deployment standardization from 36% to 99% on the authors' rubric. Its utility is demonstrated by benchmarking three lung segmentation models (TotalSegmentator v1, LungMask, LungLobes) on 422 NSCLC-Radiomics chest CTs using identical one-line docker commands, with per-organ Dice, paired t-tests, age correlations, and full case-level public dashboards. The key contribution to 3D organ segmentation research is not a new model but reproducible benchmarking infrastructure that removes setup friction and enables side-by-side comparison of existing organ segmentation models on clinical DICOM data.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 160 patients / 12,640 slices; 128 training patients exceeds the >50 threshold. Test set small (16 patients) but training size adequate.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single center (Peking Union Medical College Hospital), dates (Jan–Dec 2019), scanner (Philips Brilliance Big Bore), acquisition parameters (512×512, 5mm, 1.1543mm spacing), and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria all stated.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Patient-level random 8:1:1 split (128/16/16) clearly stated; model selected on validation loss; all slices of the 16 test patients evaluated. No random seed given (minor).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual delineation by trained radiation oncologists per ESTRO and RTOG protocols; CTV delineation rules tabulated; all contours reviewed/approved by two oncologists with >10 years experience.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort. Single-center data only; generalization to other centers explicitly listed as a limitation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: U-ResNet fully described: ResNet34 encoder fully replacing U-Net encoder, decoder with nearest-neighbor upsampling + conv + residual block, four skip connections, 2.5D three-slice input, Xavier init, batch norm; architecture figure provided.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Framework (PyTorch 1.0/Python 3.6), optimizer (Adam, lr=0.001), 50 epochs, GPU (GTX 1080) reported. Missing: batch size, data augmentation, and the exact formulation of the loss weighting. Not reproducible without these.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Self-adaptive weighted cross-entropy proposed with a rationale (joint one-pass multi-class prediction of CTV+OARs), but no equation for the adaptive weights and no ablation vs. plain CE — the core novelty is not fully specified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: 2.5D input formation (three adjacent slices as channels) described, but no intensity normalization/windowing, resampling, or augmentation described; no post-processing reported.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no URL or repository mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC + 95HD (both with mean±STD) plus blinded clinical scoring by two oncologists and time-cost evaluation.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Wilcoxon matched-pairs tests with p-values for model comparison, McNemar and weighted kappa for inter-observer consistency, significance threshold stated. No confidence intervals, but p-values present.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Only one experimental baseline (U-Net, fairly trained with identical configuration). Comparison to DD-ResNet/DDCNN/DDNN uses literature numbers from a different dataset (Men et al.), so indirect.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-structure DSC and 95HD tables with STDs and p-values for CTV, contralateral breast, spinal cord, heart, and both lungs.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated limitations section: single center, GT approved by only two oncologists, 2.5D vs 3D, exclusion of pacemaker artifacts and contrast CT, slice-thickness dependence, poor inter-observer kappa (0.282), and honest reporting that U-Net beat U-ResNet on right-lung 95HD.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Inclusion/exclusion criteria explicit (early-stage BC post-BCS, whole-breast irradiation; axillary/supraclavicular RT excluded; pacemaker-artifact and contrast CT excluded), but single center and no statement of consecutive enrollment.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Same held-out test patients for both models; U-Net trained with identical configuration; clinical evaluation blinded (AI and GT contours randomly distributed to two independent oncologists with a fixed grading rubric).
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Unfavorable results reported (U-Net superior right-lung 95HD, P=0.041; poor inter-oncologist consistency kappa=0.282), and limitations proactively discussed.

detailed_extraction: RELEVANCE FLAG FOR REVIEW SCOPE: this is a 2.5D method (three stacked slices as 2D input channels), not true volumetric 3D segmentation — classify accordingly. Cohort: median age 49 [42,58]; 79/160 left-sided BC; mean CTV volume 494.41±198.51 cm³. Clinical evaluation subsets are separate from the 16-patient test set: 20 additional cases for OAR scoring (rubric: 3=no edit, 2=≤4 slices edited, 1=≥4 slices edited, 0=unacceptable) and 10 patients/650 slices for CTV scoring (3=acceptable, 2=minor, 1=major, 0=not acceptable; ≥2 = clinically usable); 99.4% of AI CTV contours judged acceptable by oncologist A vs 98.1% of GT. Time: 10.03 s auto-segmentation vs 20–30 min manual; AI-assisted correction reduces contouring to ~10 min (CTV) / 5 min (OARs). Internal inconsistencies to note: abstract reports contralateral breast DSC 0.95 while Table 2 reports 0.94; text reports U-Net right-lung 95HD as 2.98 mm while Table 2 reports 2.89±1.26 mm. Reference 23 (diffGrad) is cited for the Adam optimizer — citation error. Industry involvement: three co-authors are employees of MedMind Technology (model likely co-developed commercially); funded by National Foundation for Education Sciences Planning (BLA200216); IRB approval and Declaration of Helsinki compliance stated. No data augmentation or class-imbalance analysis reported; per-class Dice for small structures (spinal cord 0.93) suggests the weighted CE mitigated but did not eliminate class imbalance. Self-declared future work: multi-center data, true 3D U-Net, improved right-lung delineation.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes U-ResNet, a 2.5D U-Net variant whose encoder is fully replaced by ResNet34, with a self-adaptive weighted cross-entropy loss enabling one-pass joint segmentation of breast CTV and five OARs for breast-conserving radiotherapy planning. On 160 single-center patients it modestly but significantly outperforms a same-configuration U-Net (CTV DSC 0.94 vs 0.93, P=0.001), achieves CTV 95HD (4.31 mm) better than prior deep-learning reports, and is the first study to clinically validate combined CTV+OAR auto-contouring for this setting — blinded oncologist scoring showed AI contours equivalent to ground truth (10 s vs 20–30 min). Its main value to the review is clinical-translation evidence (blinded expert evaluation, time savings) rather than architectural novelty, with generalizability limited by the single-center, non-3D design and no code release.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Evaluation cohort is large (n=1204 adults, far above threshold), but this is an application of a pretrained model; training set size is not reported here (deferred to refs 19/20, 'separate patient sample').

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Clearly described: 1250 consecutive adults undergoing multiphasic renal-donor CT at a single academic center, Feb 2010-Jan 2017; 46 exclusions itemized (39 missing/corrupted data, 7 splenic absence); demographics given (mean age 45.2±12.4; 726 women, 478 men).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No split methodology described in this paper. The entire 1204-case cohort is used for evaluation of a model trained on a separate sample (so the evaluation set is independent of training data), but no formal train/val/test protocol is reported.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Reference standard for the downstream task is clearly defined (PDFF = -0.58×CT_HU + 38.2 from unenhanced volumetric liver attenuation; thresholds 5/10/15%), but no segmentation ground truth or annotation process is described; segmentation accuracy vs manual contours is never evaluated.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single institution, single CT vendor (GE). Authors explicitly state external validation is warranted. No external/independent-site testing.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Only 'modified 3D U-Net' is stated; full architecture details are in prior publications (refs 19, 20), not this paper.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: data augmentation listed (3D rotation, crop, elastic deformation, CycleGAN for non-contrast, random flips) and NIH Biowulf HPC named; no hyperparameters, optimizer, epochs, or training details. Attenuation computation (volumetric mean over all liver/spleen voxels incl. intrahepatic vessels) is described.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never mentioned.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: CT acquisition and reconstruction described in detail (120 kVp, modulated mA, noise index 17-27.5, 5mm/3mm-interval slices reformatted to 3mm contiguous; split-bolus contrast timing). Segmentation pre/post-processing steps are not described.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No statement of code or model availability.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and ROC-AUC at three PDFF thresholds (5%, 10%, 15%). Dice not applicable (no segmentation GT).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Formal analysis: trapezoidal AUC over all 1204 elemental areas; Hanley & McNeil test for AUC differences with p-values (p=0.66/0.54/0.19). Confidence intervals not reported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Discussion compares against prior manual-ROI contrast-enhanced studies, DECT/VNC approaches, and the group's prior unenhanced-CT tool, but no head-to-head quantitative comparison in results.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver attenuation alone and liver-spleen difference reported separately (both organs of the 2-organ model used), but no per-organ segmentation performance (e.g., liver vs spleen Dice) is reported.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations section: single center/vendor, non-pure portal venous phase, derived reference standard, potential impact of intrahepatic vessel inclusion, poor discrimination at the 5% PDFF threshold.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low concern within scope: consecutive sampling with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria; however, cohort limited to healthy renal-donor candidates at one academic center, restricting generalizability (steatosis prevalence may differ in clinical populations).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate concern: fully automated pipeline applied uniformly to all 1204 cases with 100% success, but the reference standard is itself derived (unenhanced CT attenuation converted to PDFF via formula), not a direct measurement; no manual segmentation quality check reported in this paper.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low concern: multiple thresholds reported including unfavorable results (e.g., sensitivity only 34.0% for any steatosis at <100 HU; 29.5% for L-S difference <10 HU); limitations candid. Minor issue: AUC values for liver-spleen difference differ between abstract (0.662/0.866/0.986) and Results text (0.669/0.854/0.962) in this accepted manuscript.

detailed_extraction: IMPORTANT FOR REVIEW SCOPE: This is an application/outcome study using a previously published segmentation model (modified 3D U-Net, trained on a separate sample per refs 19/20), not a segmentation methodology paper. Segmentation accuracy (e.g., Dice) is never evaluated; the contribution is clinical validation of a downstream quantitative task (steatosis categorization). Extraction details: (1) Cohort: 1204/1250 consecutive renal-donor adults retained after exclusions; single center; GE scanners; unenhanced + parenchymal (split-bolus) phases analyzed; arterial phase excluded (insufficient hepatic coverage). (2) Pipeline: automated 3D U-Net liver+spleen segmentation -> volumetric mean HU (intrahepatic vasculature included) -> contrast-enhanced HU (or liver-spleen difference) vs reference PDFF from unenhanced HU via Fat% = -0.58×HU + 38.2 (formula validated cross-vendor, ref 12). (3) Reference prevalence: PDFF>=5% 50.1% (603/1204), >=10% 12.5% (151), >=15% 4.8% (58), >=20% 1.4% (17). (4) Key results: AUC (liver attenuation) 0.669/0.854/0.962 at 5%/10%/15% PDFF; <90 HU gives 75.9% sens/95.7% spec/47.3% PPV/98.7% NPV for moderate steatosis; 96.8% (90/93) of patients <90 HU had PDFF>=5%. Liver-spleen difference: <5 HU gives 91.4% sens/95.0% spec for moderate; 93.8% (30/32) with <-10 HU had PDFF>=15%. AUCs of liver-only vs liver-spleen not significantly different (p=0.66/0.54/0.19) -> splenic segmentation adds no value here. (5) Tool succeeded in 100% of cases (1204/1204). (6) Analysis in Excel; trapezoid AUC; Hanley & McNeil comparison. (7) Manuscript inconsistencies to note: abstract vs Results AUC discrepancy for liver-spleen difference; title typo ('Heathy'). (8) Authors' stated future work: external validation across vendors, true portal venous phase, diverse populations.
contribution_summary: This study applies a previously developed fully-automated 3D U-Net hepatosplenic segmentation tool to categorize hepatic steatosis on contrast-enhanced CT in 1204 healthy adults, using unenhanced-CT-derived PDFF as the reference standard. It demonstrates that categorical steatosis assessment is feasible on contrast-enhanced CT (AUC up to 0.962-0.986 for moderate steatosis, e.g., <90 HU threshold: 75.9% sensitivity/95.7% specificity), performs substantially worse for mild (5%) steatosis, and finds no added value from splenic attenuation. For this review, it counts as evidence that deep-learning liver/spleen segmentation runs fully autonomously at scale (100% success on 1204 scans) to enable opportunistic NAFLD screening, though it provides no segmentation accuracy metrics itself.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 210 kidney cancer patients / 45,424 CT frames, well above the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: KiTS19 challenge data clearly identified and cited (Heller et al.); frame/organ counts given; authors note 90 further challenge cases pending release.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 80:10:10 split stated per model, but the unit of splitting (patient vs. frame) is unspecified; frame-level random splits appear likely, which would leak same-patient slices across train/test and inflate metrics.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth is the challenge-provided semantic segmentations (cited), but the annotation process itself (annotators, protocol, inter-observer handling) is not described in this paper; metrics computed on preprocessed GT labels.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort; evaluation confined to internal 10% test split of KiTS19; official held-out challenge evaluation not reported.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Full layer-level detail: encoder 9 conv / 4 pooling / 2 dropout (50%), decoder 13 conv / 4 up-sampling, 4 skip connections, ReLU/sigmoid activations, plus ensemble fusion logic (bitwise AND of three binary U-Nets) with block diagram.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam (lr 1e-4, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.99), batch size 12, ~10 epochs, per-model sampling strategies, augmentation, all software versions, and public code repo; minor ambiguity only ('ten iterations' wording, split unit).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted BCE motivated in one clause (class imbalance) with supporting selective sampling; no discussion of segmentation-standard alternatives (e.g., Dice/compound loss).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Exceptionally explicit: full preprocessing chain with exact kernel sizes and thresholds, and post-hoc volumetric validation with all numeric acceptance criteria (kidney vol >19,000, COM 20-80% depth; tumor vol >350, axes >10/>3, sphericity >0.29).

Q10_code_availability.justification: Code publicly available at https://github.com/Aj-Jamie/KiTS_Code, linked in a dedicated Code Availability section.
