Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Precision, recall, and per-class F1 (pixel-wise F1 is Dice-equivalent) reported before and after volumetric validation; note standard volumetric Dice on original-resolution images is not computed.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or variance estimates; per-case F1 plotted descriptively (Fig. 4) but no statistical testing.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: No baseline or SOTA comparison; explicitly acknowledged ('It remains to be seen how this compares to other solutions').

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-class results (background/kidney/tumor) in Table 1 plus per-case F1 and volume plots identifying outlier cases 15, 30, 88.

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid and specific: below clinical standard, tumor over-segmentation (precision 0.40), 2D lack of depth context, preprocessing failures (case 88 artifacts), and absence of method comparison.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. All 210 available challenge cases used; frame inclusion criteria per model stated (e.g., random quarter of kidney-free frames). Residual concern: likely frame-level rather than patient-level splitting, and 90 pending challenge cases excluded.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. Authors evaluated their own model on preprocessed ground truth; no blinded or independent assessment; probable same-patient frame overlap across splits; non-standard metric (2D F1 on preprocessed labels instead of 3D Dice on original geometry) hinders cross-study comparability.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Unfavorable outcomes reported transparently (tumor precision 0.40, degraded F1 when restored to original image format); main gap is missing leaderboard/SOTA context rather than selective outcome reporting.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Per-model data sampling — strict kidney+tumor model: 19,479 frames (all kidney/tumor frames plus a random quarter of kidney-free frames, ~4:1 containing:not ratio); lax model: 16,356 kidney-containing frames; tumor model: tumor frames doubled via horizontal-flip augmentation plus a small sample of tumor-free frames. (2) Ensemble fusion: lax kidney+tumor output ANDed bitwise with strict and tumor-only outputs; masks summed to labels {0,1,2}; each U-Net is binary with sigmoid output (no softmax multi-class head). (3) Training: mini-batches of 12 at 256x256, Adam, ~10 epochs ('ten iterations' — wording ambiguous). (4) Evaluation caveat: metrics computed on 2D preprocessed frames against preprocessed ground truth; authors state F1 decreased when predictions were restored to original image format but do not quantify this; no 3D Dice on original-resolution volumes; results are NOT from the official KiTS19 held-out test phase. (5) Volumetric validation ablation (Table 1): kidney F1 0.8013->0.8497; tumor F1 0.4510->0.5019, achieved partly by trading tumor recall (0.8990->0.8623) for precision (0.3449->0.3964). (6) Tumor relabeling rule: tumor bounding cube intersecting kidney bounding cube -> relabeled kidney, else background. (7) Implementation built on the public zhixuhao Keras U-Net repo; trained on a Tesla K80 (12 GB) via Google Colaboratory. (8) Funded by Rangsit Research Institute grant 90/2561.
contribution_summary: A challenge-entry method fusing three standard 2D U-Nets (lax kidney+tumor, strict kidney+tumor, tumor-only) via logical bitwise AND, followed by a rule-based 3D volumetric validation step (volume, position, morphology, sphericity, and cross-frame consistency thresholds) applied to stacked 2D predictions. The main contribution is demonstrating that cheap anatomically-informed post-hoc 3D filtering of 2D outputs improves per-class F1 (kidney 0.80->0.85, tumor 0.45->0.50) without the cost of a 3D network. Performance remains below clinical utility — tumor precision is poor (0.40) from over-segmentation — and no external or SOTA comparison is provided.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 130 LiTS training scans (70 test) plus 20 3DIRCADb scans; well above the >50 subject threshold, supplemented by 4,077/14,160 liver/tumor training patches.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public LiTS MICCAI 2017 challenge dataset (multi-site clinical data) and 3DIRCADb (European hospitals) both identified with scan counts, resolution, and a data availability statement.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Official LiTS 130/70 split with test GT held by challenge; 5-fold cross-training on training set with explicit patch counts (4,077/1,019 liver; 14,160/3,540 tumor). Minor gap: fold composition not specified.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth used as provided by LiTS/3DIRCADb ('manually segmented tumors'); no annotation protocol, rater expertise, inter-rater agreement, or QC process described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: LiTS-trained weights applied unchanged to 3DIRCADb as an independent external test set (Section 4.5).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Layer-by-layer spec in Table 2, residual block (Eq. 1), attention residual module (Eq. 2) with trunk/soft-mask branch and depths D=0..3, ~4M parameter count, patch sizes all given.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam (LR 1e-3, β1=0.9, β2=0.999, ×0.1 plateau decay after 20 epochs), 50 epochs × 5 folds, 150 patches/volume, GPU and framework given; batch size, data augmentation, and random seeds not reported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: V-Net-style Dice loss cited with equation, but choice asserted ('measures similarity directly') rather than justified against alternatives (e.g., cross-entropy, class imbalance rationale).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Fully specified: HU window [-100,200] with tissue-HU table, zero-mean/min-max normalization, downsampling to 256×256 for stage 1, patch extraction, 3D connected-component labeling, 5-model voting ensemble, filtering of tumor voxels outside liver.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Public GitHub repo (RanSuLab/RAUNet-tumor-segmentation.git); no release version or license stated.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Six metrics per Heimann et al. 2009: Dice global + per-case, Jaccard, VOE, RVD, ASSD, MSD — on both datasets.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or variance across the 5 folds; only single point estimates.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Tables 5–6 compare against ~13 methods (H-DenseUNet, Kaluva, Bi, Christ CFCN, challenge entries) on both LiTS and 3DIRCADb.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver and tumor reported separately per dataset and per metric; no averaged cross-structure result hiding performance.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations: FP/FN on tiny low-contrast tumors (visualized in Figure 10), 3D training cost, empirically chosen tumor patch size due to GPU limits.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-unclear: public challenge data with an externally defined split reduces author-driven selection, but patient-level inclusion criteria and site composition are not reported; 3DIRCADb (n=20) is an opportunistic external set.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: standardized challenge metrics (Heimann 2009) on LiTS test with held-out ground truth limit assessor discretion; however, 3DIRCADb comparison rows reuse numbers quoted from prior papers rather than re-running baselines.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate: all headline outcomes for both datasets and both structures reported, including the weak tumor per-case Dice (0.595); but no per-fold variance, CIs, or inference time reported.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not in the primary extraction: (1) Stage-1 (RA-UNet-I, 2D localization) trained on 32,746 liver-containing slices (23,283 train / 9,463 val) plus 1/3 of randomly sampled non-liver slices, at 256×256 downsampled resolution; 5-fold CV not used at this stage; final boundary box padded 10 pixels in coronal/sagittal/axial directions. (2) Tumor patch-size ablation performed: 32×32×32, 64×64×32, 128×128×32 compared; 128×128×32 selected as the largest feasible on a 1080Ti; 150 patches sampled per liver VOI; no interpolation/resizing in the tumor stage to preserve small lesions. (3) Evaluation framework follows Heimann et al. 2009 (SLIVER-style); final predictions = voting ensemble over the 5 fold models; model trained fully from scratch — no pretrained backbone, no CRF postprocessing. (4) Authors claim first application of attention residual learning (Wang et al. 2017) in 3D medical volumetric segmentation; journal version follows arXiv preprint 1811.01328. (5) 3DIRCADb tumor Dice (0.830) is computed only on livers containing tumors; high tumor RVD (0.740) and MSD (53.3) on 3DIRCADb indicate instability on small/outlier lesions. (6) Not reported anywhere: batch size, data augmentation policy, inference time, per-fold results, code release version or license. (7) LiTS test evaluation appears to be via official challenge metrics/leaderboard (Table 5 includes other LiTS submissions MEDDIIR and Summer).
contribution_summary: RA-UNet couples a 2D coarse liver-localization stage (RA-UNet-I) with a 3D residual attention-aware U-Net (RA-UNet-II) that sequentially segments liver then tumor in a cascade, claiming the first application of attention residual learning to 3D medical volume segmentation via a compact ~4M-parameter from-scratch model. It reaches 0.961 per-case liver / 0.595 tumor Dice on the LiTS test set and transfers to 3DIRCADb at 0.977 / 0.830, outperforming listed 2D baselines on liver and beating Christ et al.'s CFCN (0.56) on 3DIRCADb tumors. The advance is architectural (attention residual modules inside a 3D U-Net plus voting ensembling) rather than a new training paradigm; tumor segmentation — not organ segmentation — remains the weak point.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Exceeds threshold: LiTS-2017 with 60 training scans (50 labeled/10 unlabeled) and KiTS19 with 200 CT scans; both well above 50 subjects.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source clearly identified as two established public benchmarks (LiTS-2017, KiTS19). No patient demographics, scanner, or acquisition-protocol details given, but source itself is unambiguous.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split numbers stated (LiTS: 60/20/20; KiTS19: patch-level 900/100 labeled, 210/210 val/test), but the split methodology (random vs. official split, stratification) is not described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth relies on standard public benchmark annotations; the annotation process (who, how, inter-rater) is never described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Partial only: two public datasets are used, but each model is trained and tested within the same dataset (no cross-dataset or independent-center external validation).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture thoroughly described: 3D U-Net discriminator with SE modules in every conv block, pyramid pooling (avg-pool sizes 1/2/5) at encoder end, 4 encoder + 3 decoder SE module groups, transposed convolutions, feature-restoration generator, ~150M parameters, with figures.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partial: epochs (100), GPU (GTX 1080Ti), patch size, and preprocessing given; but optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and data augmentation are not reported. Framework unspecified. No code.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Losses are defined (summed CE over labeled/unlabeled/fake images with fake=label 2; L2 feature-matching for generator) and the feature-restoration design is motivated, but the loss choices themselves are not formally justified or ablated against alternatives.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing is fully and explicitly described (HU clipping to [-200,200], normalization, gray-value mapping to [0,255], liver crop/resize to 256x256xN, 256x256x16 patching) including rationale. Post-processing explicitly absent.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository URL provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice plus Hausdorff Distance and ASSD. Caveat: HD/ASSD reported only for 2 qualitative example cases, not dataset-level statistics.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, standard deviations, or significance testing anywhere; single-point Dice values only.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Compared against 3D U-Net, its own ablation (SE+pyramid pooling), DenseNet, 3D DenseUNet-65, FCN+ACM, and GIU-Net, including honest reporting of cases where it loses (FCN+ACM, GIU-Net).

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Organ-specific Dice reported separately per dataset (liver LiTS val/test, kidney KiTS19 val/test). No per-case distribution though (HD/ASSD for only 2 cases).

Q15_limitations.justification: Extensive, candid limitations: ~150M params, ~50h training, GPU memory demands, weaker HD/ASSD (model selected on Dice), underperformance vs. FCN+ACM/GIU-Net, and lack of quantitative metrics for GAN-generated images.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/moderate. Public benchmarks reduce single-center bias, but how the 100 LiTS scans and 200 KiTS19 scans were selected from the full cohorts is unstated; no inclusion/exclusion criteria; LiTS subset (100 of 131) selection method not explained.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. Evaluation used held-out test splits, but metric reporting is inconsistent (dataset-level Dice vs. only 2 example cases for HD/ASSD), and the authors admit model selection was based on Dice, which favors Dice over boundary metrics. Comparisons with FCN+ACM/GIU-Net appear partly drawn from literature rather than retrained under identical conditions.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate. Limitations and negative comparisons are reported transparently; however, no uncertainty quantification, no failed-run reporting, incomplete hyperparameters, and no code release limit independent verification.

detailed_extraction: Semi-supervised GAN mechanics: the improved 3D U-Net acts as discriminator performing liver segmentation while jointly classifying voxels/patches as real, unlabeled, or fake (fake = class 2); discriminator loss = sum of cross-entropies over the three image types. The generator is a DCNN that synthesizes fake 3D volumes by restoring them from randomly selected feature maps of real images (deliberately NOT random noise), trained to minimize L2 difference between real and fake feature maps; motivation: noise-input DCGANs on 3D CT converge too slowly vs. the fast-converging 3D U-Net discriminator, causing gradient dispersion, and noise-generated CT lacks realistic contours/internal texture. Architecture details: SE module = channel attention (global pooling -> bottleneck -> sigmoid weights -> scale) combined with 2 conv layers (first adjusts resolution/channel count); encoder = 4 SE module groups (2 SE modules each), first conv stride 2 with channel expansion; pyramid pooling module = 3 parallel 3D avg-pools (sizes 1, 2, 5), 1x1 conv fusion per scale, upsample, concat, then 1x1 conv channel reduction; decoder = 3 SE module groups with transposed conv (stride 2, channels halved) + skip concat; final transposed conv restores resolution and concatenates with original input image. Preprocessing pipeline: HU clip [-200, +200] (justified: liver contrast range, removes bone interference, faster convergence) -> normalize to [0,1] -> scale by 255 to gray [0,255] -> liver-region crop + resize to 256x256xN -> cut into 256x256x16 patches (LiTS: 500 training patches). Compute: single NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti (11 GB), 100 epochs at ~30 min/epoch (~50 h total); deep-learning framework not reported. Evaluation caveats for reviewers: best headline Dice 0.9424 is LiTS test; LiTS validation is higher (0.9638); kidney KiTS19 experiments (Dice 0.959) included despite liver-focused title; HD/ASSD given only as 2 paired example cases vs. baseline 3D U-Net (e.g., case 1 HD 15.33 vs 18.68 mm). Note: supplied full text is truncated mid-Methods; experiment-section details supplemented from previously extracted data.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a semi-supervised 3D DCGAN framework for liver CT segmentation in which the discriminator is an improved 3D U-Net (SE channel attention + pyramid pooling) and the generator produces realistic fake 3D volumes by restoring them from real feature maps instead of random noise, addressing labeled-data scarcity in 3D medical segmentation. It achieves Dice 0.9424 on LiTS-2017 test and 0.959 on KiTS19, outperforming baseline 3D U-Net and several published methods, while candidly reporting efficiency limitations (~150M parameters, ~50 h training on one GPU).

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 131 LiTS scans re-split into train/val/test; training subset comfortably exceeds 50 subjects, though modest by current standards.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: LiTS public benchmark explicitly named; however, no patient demographics, scanner, or acquisition protocol details are provided.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Authors report re-splitting the 131 LiTS training scans because official test labels are withheld, but split ratios, randomization, and stratification are not described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Relies on standard publicly documented LiTS expert annotations; no description of annotation protocol, annotator expertise, or inter-observer variability.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single-dataset validation (LiTS only); external multi-center validation is explicitly listed as future work.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully described with figures and equations: 3D U-Net backbone, three-branch multi-scale encoder, codebook (K=64, C=64, straight-through estimator), Mamba module (state size 16, d=64) at bottleneck, decoder with center-crop/padding alignment.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (Adam, lr=1e-4), epochs (160), batch size (1), framework (PyTorch/MONAI), and GPU reported; but no data augmentation details, no split ratios, no training time, and no code to compensate.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Composite loss justified component-wise (VQ commitment for representation stability, inclusion loss for tumor-within-liver anatomical prior) with weights selected via ablation (alpha=0.4, beta=0.6); base segmentation loss type not explicit.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing thorough (HU clipping -200..200, B-spline/nearest-neighbor resampling, z=1mm, 48-slice sampling, min-max normalization); post-processing 'not reported' rather than explicitly stated as none.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model weights publicly released.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five metrics: Dice, VOE, RVD, ASD, 95HD, reported separately for liver and tumor.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests reported anywhere.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Eight baselines compared (3D U-Net, VNet, Att-UNet, SegResNet, ResUnet, UNETR, CodeBookUNet, VAEUNet) plus ablation studies; caveat: all re-implemented/evaluated on the authors' internal split, not LiTS leaderboard.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full metric set reported per structure: liver (Dice 0.94, VOE 0.06, ASD 1.92mm, 95HD 8.79mm) and tumor (Dice 0.47, VOE 0.53, ASD 12.76mm, 95HD 34.81mm).

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid limitations: single dataset, near-zero Dice (<0.05) for tumors <10 voxels, encoder not optimized for ultra-small lesions, limited codebook interpretability.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate: patient selection is defined by public LiTS benchmark inclusion (clear), but the authors' internal re-split procedure (ratios, randomization) is undescribed and no external cohort is used, limiting generalizability.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: all compared methods (including MONAI re-implementations) evaluated on the same internal split with identical metrics; absence of statistical testing means reported superiority may not be significant.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate: per-structure results, ablations, efficiency, and failure cases (tiny tumors) are transparently reported; however, no uncertainty quantification, post-processing and training time unreported, and no code release prevents independent verification.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Training config: 160 epochs, batch size 1, Adam lr=1e-4, PyTorch with MONAI baseline implementations, NVIDIA RTX 4080 Super 16GB; inference ~0.04 s/sample (efficiency comparison, Fig. 8). (2) VQ mechanism (Eqs. 1-5): squared Euclidean distance assignment, one-hot nearest-neighbor selection, straight-through estimator for gradient flow, commitment loss weight lambda=0.25, codebook K=64 x C=64. (3) Mamba module placed at bottleneck specifically to model cross-slice z-axis dependencies; authors claim linear-complexity long-range modeling vs quadratic Transformer attention. (4) Minor internal inconsistency: Section 3.1 describes encoder kernels as 3x3x3/5x5x5/7x7x7 with continuous max-pooling, while Section 3.2 describes 1x1x1+3x3x3, dilated 3x3x3 (simulating 5x5x5), and average-pooling branches. (5) Evaluation caveat: 'state-of-the-art' claim is relative to eight re-implemented baselines on the authors' own LiTS re-split, not the withheld LiTS test leaderboard; tumor Dice of 0.47 is below typical LiTS leaderboard tumor performance, and 95HD of 34.81mm for tumors indicates substantial boundary failures. (6) No data augmentation strategy reported; loss weights alpha=0.4, beta=0.6 selected empirically. (7) Paper motivates work via three challenges (tumor scale variation/anisotropy/attention cost, DOF-redundancy trade-off, missing anatomical priors). (8) Note: supplied full text is truncated at Section 3.4; experiment-section assessments rely on the prior extraction record. (9) Timeline: received 2025-09-18, published 2026-03-18, CC BY license; no code URL or release version available.
contribution_summary: Proposes a hierarchical 3D U-Net for liver and tumor segmentation in CT that couples a multi-scale context encoder with a Mamba-based module at the bottleneck for linear-complexity cross-slice dependency modeling, plus a vector-quantization codebook (K=64) that enforces compact, discriminative feature representations. An inclusion loss embeds the anatomical prior that tumors must reside within the liver, regularizing outputs and reducing false positives. On an internal re-split of LiTS, the method outperforms eight baselines with liver Dice 0.94 / tumor Dice 0.47 at ~0.04 s per sample, with ablations confirming each module's individual contribution.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 490 patients / 610 CT series total; 487 series for training — well above the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single-center institutional data (Peking University First Hospital) with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, full CT acquisition protocol (scanner range, contrast agent/dose/injection rate, 4 phases with timing, kV, slice thickness), plus 81-patient external institutional set and 300-scan KiTS21. Minor internal inconsistency: enrollment window stated as Aug 2009–Jul 2022 in Methods but Aug 2009–Aug 2021 in Results.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 8:1:1 split into train/validation/test (487/58/65), with all series from the same patient kept in the same set to prevent leakage.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotated in ITK-SNAP 3.6.0 by a 15-year fellowship-trained radiologist with a junior radiologist, blinded to clinical/pathological information; explicit labeling rules (kidney includes cortex/medulla/sinus, excludes retroperitoneal fat and hilar structures; masses include necrosis/hemorrhage, exclude venous/collecting-system extension). KiTS21 kidney labels harmonized to local conventions. Weakness: no consensus mechanism or inter-rater agreement statistic reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Two independent external evaluations: 81-patient external institutional set (segmentation + classification chained end-to-end) and 300-scan public KiTS21 challenge dataset.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Cascaded 3D U-Net (filters=16) + 10-layer 3D ResNet (hidden=128, dropout=0.1, GAP+FC) with schematic diagrams in supplementary figures; but 'pretrained=1' never specifies the pretraining source, and per-layer specifications are not given.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Batch size (4), epochs (400), learning rate (0.0001), input size (128³), windowing, and augmentation all reported — but optimizer, loss, framework, and hardware are missing; no code released. Full reproduction not possible.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function not reported for either the segmentation or classification model, and no justification is given.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing fully specified: DICOM→NIFTI, 30 HU/300 HU window, resize to 128×128×128, augmentation (rotation ±10°, noise, translation ±0.1). Post-processing described: kidney-crop ROI between cascade stages; radiodensity-threshold removal of sinus fat for KiTS21 label harmonization.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC plus Hausdorff Distance for segmentation; connected-domain TP/FP/FN with precision/recall/F1 for detection; accuracy/precision/recall/F1 and ROC-AUC for classification.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post-hoc tests comparing DSC across mass types (P values reported per comparison); demographic comparability tested (P>0.05); boxplots show score distributions. No confidence intervals on mean DSC.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Fair internal ablation against a one-stage 3D U-Net (same data/hyperparameters), plus literature-level comparisons (Chen, He, Houshyar, Türk). No head-to-head with a current SOTA baseline such as nnU-Net on the same data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: DSC reported separately for left/right kidney and left/right renal mass across all five datasets; further stratified by mass type (AML/cystic/solid) and by size (<5 mm vs ≥5 mm).

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicitly discusses retrospective design, missing pathological confirmation (imaging-based labels), worse DSC on cystic/AML vs solid, five iso-density solid masses with DSC 0 in external set, and poor classification of sub-5-mm lesions.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-to-moderate. Inclusion/exclusion criteria are explicit (contrast-enhanced CMP+NP CT, excluded severe artifacts and prior biopsy/surgery). Mitigating concerns: retrospective single-center design; whether recruitment was consecutive is not stated; mass type distribution (1296 cystic vs 198 AML) is imbalanced with no handling discussed.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. Reference standard created by radiologists blinded to clinical/pathological data, and identical metrics/thresholds applied across internal, external, and KiTS21 sets. Concerns: reference standard is imaging- not pathology-based for many masses; the same local team modified KiTS21 kidney labels, which could favor agreement; end-to-end chain (segmentation feeding classification) only fully exercised in external validation.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Per-organ, per-mass-type, and per-size-stratum results reported for all datasets; failure cases (DSC=0 masses), FP/FN counts, and misclassification patterns disclosed. Gaps are methodological (loss, optimizer, framework unspecified) rather than selective outcome reporting. Commercial co-author affiliation (medical technology company) with no conflict-of-interest statement visible in the provided text.

detailed_extraction: Acquisition: 4-phase CT (plain, CMP 30–35 s, NP 60–70 s, delayed 190–200 s), 80–120 kV, 1–1.5 mm reconstruction, 1 mm interval; contrast iopromide 370 or iohexol 320 mgI/ml at 2 ml/kg, 2.5 ml/s. Ethics: IRB-approved, consent waived, HIPAA deidentification. Lesion counts: 198 AML / 1296 cystic / 397 solid across 610 internal series; 42 AML / 352 cystic / 33 solid in the 81 external series. Demographics: internal 263 M / 227 F, mean age 49.75±18.72 (2–86 y); external 42 M / 39 F, 51.01±12.93 (23–77 y); no significant demographic difference. Training detail: classifier is trained on masses cropped via MANUAL labels (not segmentation output), then resized to 128³ with identical augmentation to segmentation; ResNet pretrained flag set but pretraining corpus unspecified. Detection evaluated at connected-domain level: test set left TP=82/FP=39/FN=15, right TP=63/FP=41/FN=20; external left TP=177/FP=53/FN=67, right TP=123/FP=47/FN=60. External protocol: classification run only on true-positive detections ≥5 mm. KiTS21: 300 labeled series, kidney labels edited by local radiologists for convention consistency (sinus fat removed by radiodensity threshold), mass labels untouched. Ablation: one-stage single 3D U-Net (same architecture/hyperparameters) underperformed the two-stage cascade. Misclassification patterns: solid masses with cystoid degeneration/necrosis most often misclassified; sub-5 mm AML/cystic masses dominate errors. Interpretability via Grad-CAM (supplementary). Unreported: loss function, optimizer, framework, GPU, training/inference time, parameter counts. Data note: enrollment end-date inconsistency (Jul 2022 in Methods §2.1 vs Aug 2021 in Results §3.1); phase selection from 4-phase scans (CMP+NP used) may introduce correlation between series of one patient, partially mitigated by patient-level splitting.
contribution_summary: This paper presents a fully automated cascaded pipeline for renal mass characterization: a 3D U-Net segments bilateral kidneys as ROI, an ensemble 3D U-Net segments masses on the cropped volume, and a 10-layer 3D ResNet classifies masses as AML, cystic, or solid, with Grad-CAM for interpretability. Trained on 610 contrast-enhanced CT series (490 patients), it achieves near-perfect kidney DSC (0.99 test) and moderate mass DSC (0.75/0.83 test, degrading to 0.68/0.64 on KiTS21 and ~0.70–0.72 externally), with 90.56% classification accuracy (91.97% for ≥5 mm masses). The main contributions are the two-stage ROI-cropping design (shown superior to a one-stage ablation) and demonstration of cross-dataset generalization, though clinical utility is bounded by moderate mass-segmentation accuracy, detection precision near 60–68%, and absent pathology-based confirmation.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 135 patients / 15,398 manually annotated slices; 108 patients (11,932 slices) for training — well above the >50-subject threshold. Balanced across normal (15), ARDS (100), and COVID-19 (20).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Three named centers (Policlinico Milan 2003–2018 trials, San Paolo Milan COVID-19, University Medical Center Göttingen); scanner models, kV, slice thickness (2.0–5.0 mm), kernels, and filters tabulated (Table 2); ethics approval stated (Göttingen 14/12/12); ARDS CTs acquired at defined airway pressures (5/15/45 cmH2O).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 80/20 split at patient level (108/27 patients), preventing slice-level leakage; exact patient/slice counts per class provided (Table 1, Figure 1). Caveat: two-way split only — no dedicated validation set described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth created manually and/or semi-automatically by experienced intensive care physicians using proprietary Maluna 3.14 software, stored as .xroi coordinates. However: number of annotators, blinding, semi-automatic vs purely manual proportion, and inter-observer agreement are not reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation. Test set drawn from the same pooled multi-center collection and same distribution as training data; no independent cohort, public benchmark, or other-center evaluation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Modified 2D U-Net fully specified: 32 filters at first level (halved from original 64 due to GPU memory), 3×3 kernels, SAME padding, strided-conv downsampling, LReLU (α=0.1), batch norm on all conv layers, dropout 0.4 at bottleneck, Xavier initialization, 1×1 conv output; architecture diagram provided (Figure 3).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Minibatch size (12), iterations (113,784), training time (44.2 h), and hardware fully specified. Missing: learning rate, momentum, weight decay, epoch count. Optimizer not explicitly named (inferable as SGD from toolkit limitations section). Critically, the entire stack (LabVIEW, NI-Vision, DeepLTK, Maluna) is commercial and license-protected, impeding independent reproduction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Mean Squared Error used for binary segmentation with no justification — an unconventional choice versus Dice/cross-entropy; the limitations section reveals MSE was chosen because cross-entropy was not supported for the data type in the toolkit, i.e., a constraint, not a design decision.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing exceptionally well documented (Figure 2): DICOM-to-HU conversion via Rescale attributes, rescaling to −1024/+100 HU, 8-bit conversion, binary thorax mask (threshold + particle filter), masking, normalization to [−1,+1], prone-image rotation via DICOM Patient Position tag. Full train/test pipelines diagrammed (Figures 6–7). No post-processing applied or described (predictions used directly).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No public code or model. Explicitly commercial/license-protected software (LabVIEW, DeepLTK, Maluna). Data only 'available from authors upon reasonable request' — not deposited.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: No Dice (toolkit limitation), but exceeds criterion intent: slice- and volume-level IoU, linear regression (R²), Bland-Altman with 95% CIs, and — notably — downstream clinical validation of CT-qa variables (lung volume, tissue-fraction classes, lung weight consistency, recruitability agreement).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Bland-Altman biases with 95% CIs (e.g., −9.8 ml [−75.7/+56.0]), R² per tissue class (0.99/0.99/0.98/0.91), paired t-test/Wilcoxon with p-values, performed in R 4.1. Minor gap: no CIs on IoU itself (only mean ± SD).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Qualitative comparison only: results situated against Hofmanninger et al. U-Net231 (85% vs 80–87% ARDS/trauma; 91% vs 94% normal) and narrative review of U-Net variants (U-Net++, Res-U-Net, 3D U-Net, 3DSegNet). No head-to-head quantitative benchmark on the same data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (lungs), so adapted appropriately: results broken down per lung condition (normal 91.3%, ARDS 85.2%, COVID-19 84.7% slice IoU), per ARDS severity (mild/moderate/severe), per anatomical region (cranio-caudal U-shape analysis), with best/worst case figures (IoU 99% to 43%).

Q15_limitations.justification: Extensive, honest failure analysis: dedicated 'Inaccuracies' and 'Limitations' sections; worst cases visualized (Figure 9, IoU down to 43%); apex/base and pleural-effusion failure modes explained; overfitting acknowledged (train vs test gap); hardware constraints; DeepLTK functional gaps itemized.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low-moderate. Multi-center, multi-pathology recruitment across 2003–2018 with no slices excluded; however, underlying ARDS patients came from prior convenience trial cohorts, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria for this study are not stated, and COVID-19 (20 patients) is under-represented relative to ARDS (100).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. Outcome assessment consistent across groups and benchmarked against expert ground truth; but ground truth was produced with the same proprietary Maluna toolchain the authors operate, is partly semi-automatic, has no inter-observer reliability data, and there is a stated train-vs-test performance gap suggesting possible overfitting to annotation style. Reference standard itself is imperfect in severe ARDS (lung weight varied up to 336 g across pressure levels), which the authors acknowledge cuts both ways.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All pre-specified outcomes reported including unfavorable ones (worst-case figures, train/test gap, per-severity failures); limitations unusually candid. Minor concerns: some agreement analyses relegated to supplementary material, and runtime advantage (5–10 s vs 1–2 h) is emphasized more than the IoU gap versus Python-based state of the art.

detailed_extraction: TASK/ORGAN: Fully automatic binary segmentation of lungs (single organ) from chest CT for quantitative CT analysis (CT-qa) in ARDS/COVID-19. APPROACH CLASS: 2D U-Net applied slice-by-slice — NOT true 3D volumetric segmentation (review-relevant: authors state 3D semantic segmentation is not possible in their DeepLTK toolkit). ARCHITECTURE: 2D U-Net, contraction/expansion paths, first level 32 filters (halved from Ronneberger's 64 due to 16 GB Quadro P5000 limit), depth to 1024 channels at 16×16, strided 3×3 conv downsampling, up-conv + skip concatenation, LReLU (α=0.1), batch norm, dropout 0.4 at bottleneck, Xavier init, 1×1 conv single-filter output. IMPLEMENTATION STACK (unusual): LabVIEW + NI-Vision + commercial DeepLTK (Ngene) on CUDA/CUDNN, Windows 10, Xeon W-2135. DATA: 135 patients / 15,398 slices from 4 scanners (GE LightSpeed Qx/i, GE LightSpeed VCT, Siemens Somatom Definition Flash, Siemens Sensation 16); slice thickness 2.0–5.0 mm; kernels STANDARD/B30f/B31f/B40f/LUNG/B41f/B75f; ARDS CTs at end-inspiratory 45 cmH2O and end-expiratory 5/15 cmH2O, taken 4.1±2.6 days post-admission. SPLIT: random patient-level 80/20 → 108 train (11,932 slices) / 27 test (3,466). TRAINING: MSE loss, SGD (implied), minibatch 12, 113,784 iterations (~114 epochs), 44.2 h. RESULTS (test set): slice IoU — normal 91.3±10.1%, ARDS 85.2±13.9%, COVID-19 84.7±14.0%, overall 87.3±10.0%; volume IoU — 96.3±0.6 / 88.9±3.1 / 86.3±6.5 / 89.6±5.1%; error is U-shaped along cranio-caudal axis (worst at apex/base/pleural recesses, which hold only 4.1±2.0% of parenchyma); total lung volume R²=0.99, bias −9.8 ml [−75.7/+56.0]; tissue-class R² 0.99 (over-inflated), 0.99 (well-aerated), 0.98 (poorly aerated), 0.91 (non-aerated); recruitability bias +0.3% [−5.5/+6.2] as non-aerated fraction change, −0.5% [−3.3/+2.3] as well-aerated change. EFFICIENCY: 0.041±0.007 s/slice, ~5 s per 100-slice scan vs 1–2 h manual. VALIDATION NOVELTY: clinical-variable-level agreement (recruitability, 'baby lung'/well-aerated tissue) rather than mask overlap alone; lung-weight pressure-invariance used as an indirect inaccuracy probe (max 336 g discrepancy, partially attributable to blood shift and genuine annotation difficulty at 5 cmH2O with pleural effusion). NOT REPORTED: Dice, ASSD/HD boundary metrics, learning rate, number of annotators, inter-observer variability, validation set, inference-time augmentation/post-processing. FUNDING/COI: departmental funds + unrestricted Sartorius AG grant.
contribution_summary: This paper demonstrates a fully automatic 2D U-Net (implemented in the non-standard commercial LabVIEW/DeepLTK stack) trained on 135 multi-center patients with normal, ARDS, and COVID-19 lungs, segmenting a complete CT scan in ~5 seconds versus 1–2 hours of manual work, with test IoU of 87.3% overall and clinically acceptable agreement on downstream CT-qa variables (lung volume bias −9.8 ml, R²=0.99; recruitability bias ≤0.5%). Its key strengths for the review are validation at the level of clinically actionable variables (recruitability, tissue fractions) rather than mask overlap alone, and unusually transparent failure analysis (apex/base errors, pleural effusion confusion, overfitting signs). It is limited by a 2D slice-wise (non-3D) approach, MSE loss, absence of external validation, no Dice or boundary metrics, and zero code/data availability due to proprietary tooling.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 221 post-contrast CT scans from 206 dogs; training sets of 115 scans (Exp 1) and 160 scans (Exp 2) clearly exceed the >50 subject threshold. Authors note this is large relative to prior veterinary DL studies (40 and 76 dogs) though modest vs. human datasets.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single institution (Hokkaido University Veterinary Teaching Hospital, Japan) clearly identified with full imaging protocol details: 80-row MDCT (Aquillion PRIME), 80-120 kVp, 0.5 mm slices, standardized contrast protocol (600 mgI/kg, portal venous phase), anesthesia protocol, breed distribution, body weight, and liver volume statistics for all subsets.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split procedure explicitly described (random shuffle, 80:20 train/test, 10% of training for validation; exact counts 115/12/32 and 160/16/45; stratification by mass status in Exp 2). However, evaluation was performed at image level rather than dog level — scans from the same dog were not guaranteed to be separated across splits, creating acknowledged intra-patient leakage risk that compromises split validity (scored partial).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process well described: single veterinary radiology technologist (15 years experience) performed all segmentations on Synapse Vincent 3D workstation with defined protocol (intrahepatic vessels included in ROI), then reviewed by a veterinary radiology specialist (>10 years experience). Minor gap: no inter-observer variability or reliability assessment reported.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation. All data from a single institution; test sets are internal random splits of the same cohort. Multi-institutional validation explicitly listed as future work.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: 3D U-Net described at the conceptual level (encoder-decoder, skip connections, 3D convolutions, 3D max-pooling, trilinear upsampling, 2-channel output) with an architecture figure. However, implementation specifics are missing: number of encoder/decoder levels, filter counts per level, and depth are not specified (referred only to 'original U-Net adapted to 3D').

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Training highly specified: 100 epochs, SGD (batch size 4, lr 0.01, momentum 0.9, weight decay 1e-4, constant LR), patch-based training (96×96×96, 8-voxel overlap via TorchIO GridSampler/GridAggregator), checkpointing on validation accuracy (top 10 epochs), single GPU (RTX 4090), PyTorch + TorchIO framework. Notably, no data augmentation was used (explicitly stated as a limitation), which actually aids reproducibility.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Cross-entropy loss chosen and minimally justified as a 'standard and widely adopted choice for multiclass segmentation tasks in medical imaging.' No discussion of alternatives (Dice loss, combined losses), class imbalance handling, or empirical motivation; authors themselves suggest focal loss as future work.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Full pipeline documented: binary mask generation (liver=1/background=0), intensity rescaling to [-1,1] (RescaleIntensity), resizing to 256×256×200 with interpolation type specified per data type (linear for images, nearest-neighbor for masks), patch extraction details, and GridAggregator reconstruction at inference. Absence of further postprocessing is explicitly stated.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or public repository mentioned. Only a data availability statement (raw data available on request).

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Comprehensive metric suite: DSC, IoU, sensitivity, specificity, precision, voxel accuracy, volume ratio, plus Pearson r and R² for volumetric agreement — all formally defined with equations and computed voxel-wise on full-volume aggregated predictions.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Partial: Pearson correlations reported with p < 0.001. However, no confidence intervals or standard deviations for DSC/IoU/other segmentation metrics, no statistical tests comparing the two experiments or the with/without-mass subsets, and no significance testing against comparator methods. Results reported as means only.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: No head-to-head experimental comparison. Contextual discussion-only comparisons: LiTS challenge top algorithms (DSC 0.93–0.96), TotalSegmentator, and prior veterinary DL studies (kidney, adrenal, lymph node). No baseline ablation (e.g., 2D U-Net, nnU-Net) or alternative architecture benchmarked on their data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver), so per-organ reporting is inherently complete. Goes further with subset-level reporting: separate DSC for Exp 2 test cases with hepatic masses (0.924) vs. without (0.931), and full metric tables per experiment (Table 2).

Q15_limitations.justification: Thorough, candid limitations section: single-institution data, modest dataset size vs. human studies, limited breed/clinical condition representation, image-level evaluation with potential dog-level leakage, uncontrolled breed-size distribution across subsets, reduced performance/increased variability on livers with masses, and absence of data augmentation. Concrete future directions provided.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Retrospective single-center cohort with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (excluded cirrhosis, PSS, marked ascites due to rarity/protocol inconsistency), but convenience sampling from one hospital, no control of breed/size distribution across subsets, and multi-scan dogs not tracked at patient level during splitting.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. Outcomes assessed consistently via a uniform, pre-specified metric pipeline across both experiments, with GT from an experienced annotator reviewed by a specialist. However: single-annotator ground truth without inter-observer reliability assessment, and potential train/test leakage (image-level rather than dog-level splits) could inflate apparent performance.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate. All planned metrics reported for both experiments plus pathological subset breakdown; volume correlations reported with p-values; limitations transparently disclosed. Concerns: no dispersion measures (SD/CI) for primary metrics, no per-case failure analysis or qualitative failure enumeration beyond one illustrative figure, inference/training wall-clock times not reported, and no code release to enable verification.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Imaging: Aquillion PRIME 80-row MDCT; 512×512 matrix, 0.5 mm slice thickness, helical pitch 0.813, 0.5 s rotation, Auto Exposure Control (Sure Exposure 3D); contrast agents iohexol (Omnipaque 300) or iopamidol (Iopamidol 150) at 600 mgI/kg via power injector (20 s injection, cephalic vein); portal venous phase with variable acquisition timing; dogs anesthetized (propofol induction, isoflurane maintenance), dorsal or sternal recumbency. (2) Dataset characterization: median body weight 8.4 kg [IQR 5.53–14.88], median liver volume 318 mL [IQR 204–563]; 29–34 breeds represented (most common: Mixed n=33, Miniature Dachshund n=32, Toy Poodle n=21); mass subgroup had smaller median body weight (7.55 kg) but larger median liver volume (427.5 mL). (3) Exclusions: cirrhosis, portosystemic shunts (non-standard imaging timing), and large-volume ascites. (4) Training/loss curves: Exp 1 mean train/val loss 0.124/0.125; Exp 2 0.170/0.132 with higher training fluctuation attributed to morphological diversity; test losses 0.05 and 0.057 respectively; checkpoint selection by validation accuracy (top-10 epochs). (5) Ethical/regulatory: retrospective study, institutional Animal Care and Use Committee approval not required; records fully anonymized. (6) Transparency notes: use of ChatGPT-4.5 for proofreading disclosed; funded by JSPS KAKENHI (23K1407403) and JST SPRING (JPMJSP2119); no industry conflicts. (7) Key interpretive caveat: volume ratio near 1.0 does not guarantee spatial accuracy (acknowledged by authors); DSC performance on mass cases (0.924) vs. non-mass (0.931) attributed to distribution shift and small mass subgroup (62 scans).
contribution_summary: This is the first deep learning model for automated liver segmentation in canine abdominal CT, addressing an unmet need in veterinary medicine. Using a 3D U-Net trained on 221 single-institution CT scans, the authors achieved mean DSC of 0.926–0.929 and volume correlations of r ≥ 0.995, matching top human LiTS benchmark performance despite inter-breed anatomical variability and modest data. The two-experiment design (normal livers vs. combined with/without hepatic masses) establishes a baseline for interpreting performance degradation on morphologically complex, mass-containing livers and demonstrates feasibility of clinical veterinary liver volumetry for diagnosing hepatomegaly/microhepatica and monitoring postoperative regeneration.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Primary experiments use LiTS with 130 training CT volumes, well above the >50 subject threshold. However, secondary 3DIRCADb experiments are very small (15/5 liver, 12/3 tumor splits), so size adequacy holds only for the LiTS experiments.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Both public datasets are clearly characterized: LiTS (131 train/70 test volumes from six clinical sites with differing scanners/protocols; inter-slice 0.55-1.0 mm, intra-slice 0.45-6.0 mm) and 3DIRCADb (20 IV contrast-enhanced CTs, 15 with tumors).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Splits are stated (LiTS 130/70; 3DIRCADb 15/5 liver and 12/3 tumor with 'cross-validation performed concurrently'), but no validation set is mentioned (risk of hyperparameter tuning on test data), the cross-validation scheme is described only vaguely, and LiTS test labels are not publicly available, leaving unexplained how test-set Dice was computed.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: The annotation process is not described at all (annotator expertise, number of observers, inter-observer agreement); the paper implicitly relies on the datasets' published reference masks.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Partial only: the method is evaluated on two distinct public datasets (LiTS and 3DIRCADb), but separate models are trained and tested within each dataset; there is no true external validation (no cross-dataset testing, no independent/institutional cohort).

Q6_architecture_description.justification: The U-shaped 2.5D encoder-decoder with residual blocks (2-3 conv layers + shortcut, 3x3 kernels, BN, ReLU; 5-slice input HxWx5, middle-slice output) is described and illustrated (Figure 4), but the number of encoder levels, filter counts per stage, and parameter count are omitted, preventing exact reimplementation.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Learning rates (0.001 combined-loss phase; 0.00005 boundary-loss phase), loss weights (w1=w2=1; alpha=5, beta=1), LR decay rule (x0.5 when improvement < 0.002), augmentation (0.8-1.2x scaling), input resolution (5x320x320), and hardware (3x Tesla K80, PyTorch) are given; but the optimizer, batch size, number of epochs/iterations, and patch-sampling strategy are not reported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss design is the central contribution and is well justified: the paper taxonomizes distribution/region/boundary/compound losses, explains why CE and Dice neglect fuzzy boundaries, and supports the boundary loss with ablations (tumor Dice Per Case +6.3% over combined loss; ordering boundary > contour > combined losses).

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described for both cascade stages: HU truncation [-150,300] + [0,1] normalization (liver); [-135,265] truncation, [0,255] scaling, grayscale inversion, [0,1] rescaling (tumor). Post-processing (3D connected components + per-slice dilation for liver; 3D dense CRF + HU-based FP/FN removal for tumor) is quantified (+5.1% liver Dice, +4.1% tumor Dice; FP reduced 0.7%/0.1%).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository link provided; the data availability statement covers only the public datasets.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice Per Case, Dice Global, IoU, VOE, RVD, ASD, RMSD are reported, plus accuracy/recall and FP/FN rates for the post-processing analysis.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Only descriptive statistics (mean +/- SD on 3DIRCADb: liver 0.961+/-0.08, tumor 0.68+/-0.15); no confidence intervals, significance tests, or correction for multiple comparisons.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive comparison against 10+ methods (2D UNet, Christ cascaded FCN, Chlebus, 3D V-Net, Han 2.5D ResNet, H-DenseUNet, Yuan, 3D AH-Net, Med3D, 3D-DenseUNet, Wang) on both datasets. Caveat: baseline numbers are quoted from prior publications rather than re-implemented under identical conditions, and no comparison with then-current top-performing methods such as nnU-Net.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Results are reported separately for liver and tumor on each dataset, with per-structure Dice, IoU, VOE, RVD, ASD, and RMSD rather than a single pooled average.

Q15_limitations.justification: Limitations are discussed (2.5D still trails some fully 3D models such as H-DenseUNet/Yuan on liver Dice; boundary loss fails on staggered/overly complex boundaries), but there is no dedicated failure-case analysis with illustrative examples.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/unclear. Data are unselected public benchmarks used as-is with no patient-level inclusion/exclusion criteria; one LiTS training case is dropped (130 of 131) without explanation; the feasibility of computing Dice on the 70 LiTS test volumes (whose reference labels are private) is not explained.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Moderate. The same metric suite is nominally applied to all methods, but competing results are taken from original papers rather than re-run, so training data, preprocessing, and post-processing differ across compared rows; the authors' internal ablations are consistent and fairly conducted.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate. Unfavorable results are reported (liver Dice below H-DenseUNet/Yuan; tumor Dice only 74.5%), ablations and per-structure metrics are included; however, several comparison tables (Tables 3-5) contain misaligned/garbled or inconsistently formatted values (e.g., proportions mixed with percentages), reducing transparency. No protocol registration or pre-specified outcomes.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details: (1) Two-phase staged training applied identically to both cascade stages: network first optimized with combined CE+Dice loss (LR 0.001, w1=w2=1); once loss plateaus (accuracy improvement threshold 0.002 triggers LR halving), optimization switches to the boundary loss (LR 0.00005, alpha=5, beta=1). (2) Boundary loss construction: distance term = sum over pixels of gradient magnitude sqrt(du_x^2 + du_y^2); area term = symmetric-difference/Dice-like term; boundary term defined morphologically - ground truth A is dilated 4 iterations (B) and eroded 4 iterations (C); extraboundary Om = A XOR B, intraboundary Im = A XOR C; boundary error e = sum(O_pred) + sum(1 - I_pred). Sensitivity to beta analyzed (Figure 6): beta=1 yields lowest converged loss. (3) Ablation specifics (LiTS): 2D -> 2.5D gains are tumor Dice Per Case 73.7 -> 74.5 (+0.8%) and IoU 58.3 -> 59.4 (+1.1%); liver Dice 93.9 -> 94.3 (+0.4%) and IoU 88.5 -> 89.3 (+0.8%). Loss ablation (2.5D): tumor Dice Per Case CE 62.4 < Dice 65.7 < combined 68.2 < contour 73.8 < boundary 74.5; liver Dice Global 92.6 (CE) -> 96.1 (boundary). (4) Cascade mechanics: liver mask dilated 5 pixels/iterations to define the tumor-stage ROI in both training and testing; final output is merged liver+tumor masks. (5) Resource/efficiency claims: input 5x320x320 with batch size 1, ~4 GB VRAM vs 24 GB reported for H-DenseUNet; total inference 30-100 s per volume depending on slice count; trained on 3x NVIDIA Tesla K80 in PyTorch. (6) 3DIRCADb protocol: liver 15 train/5 test, tumor 12 train/3 test (only 15 of 20 volumes contain tumors), with cross-validation mentioned but the fold scheme unspecified. (7) Baseline provenance: comparison figures appear compiled from original publications rather than re-implemented; Table 5 contains formatting inconsistencies (values such as '0.680'/'0.796' mixed with percentage-scale Dice), and Tables 3-4 alignments are partially garbled in the source. (8) Reporting gaps: optimizer, batch size, epoch count, patching, deep supervision, and validation strategy unreported; single excluded LiTS case unexplained. (9) Scope note for this review: this is a liver(+tumor)-specific 2.5D slice-based method, not true volumetric 3D segmentation and not multi-organ; its review-relevant value lies in (a) the boundary-aware compound loss (+6.3% tumor Dice Per Case over combined loss in ablation) and (b) the memory-efficiency argument for resource-constrained clinical deployment. Claimed superiority should be interpreted only against 2017-2018 baselines, as no comparison with 2019-2021 SOTA (e.g., nnU-Net) is provided.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a cascaded 2.5D residual FCN framework with a novel boundary loss (distance + area + boundary terms, applied after initial combined CE+Dice optimization) and structure-specific post-processing (3D connected components for liver; dense CRF + HU-based FP/FN filtering for tumor) for liver and tumor segmentation in contrast-enhanced CT. It reports LiTS Dice Per Case of 94.3% (liver) and 74.5% (tumor) using only ~4 GB VRAM (~6x less than H-DenseUNet), positioning boundary-aware supervision as an effective, memory-efficient alternative to fully 3D networks, though liver Dice still trails the best 3D baselines. Reproducibility and generalizability are limited by the absence of released code, incomplete training details, no true external validation, and comparisons restricted to older baseline methods.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 62 patients from three centers exceeds the >50 threshold, but no training was performed — all subjects are a retrospective evaluation cohort for a pre-trained commercial model, and comparison subgroups are modest (n=42 manual-era vs n=20 AI-adjusted-era). Partial credit only.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Sources well described: three Italian centers (UPMC Hillman San Pietro Rome, UPMC Hillman Villa Maria Mirabella Eclano, Marrelli Hospital Crotone), treatment period Jan 2020–Jul 2025, CT acquisition parameters (1.25 mm slices, 512×512 matrix), patient preparation (full bladder/empty rectum), linac models, and hypofractionation protocol (62 Gy/20 fx, dual-arc VMAT).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No train/validation/test split exists. The C_AI vs C_man (n=42) and C_AI vs C_adj (n=20) grouping is a temporal cohort division for workflow comparison, not an ML data split. Authors explicitly acknowledge the resulting temporal bias and non-comparability of cohorts.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual contouring followed international guidelines (ESTRO ACROP, QUANTEC, AAPM TG-101), but no consensus committee, physician count, or experience level is described. Critically, the AI contour itself (C_AI) was designated the 'gold standard' reference — a circular design that the authors acknowledge as a limitation.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No formal external/independent test set. Partial credit for multi-institutional retrospective data (3 centers) and evaluation of an external pre-trained model on local data; however, both cohorts originate from the same institutions and differ only by time window.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture described only as '3D U-net models' within the proprietary ART-Plan v2.3.1 (TheraPanacea) Class IIb medical device. No depth, width, input dimensions, or model design details; treated as a commercial black box.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No training or fine-tuning was performed ('no fine-tuning was performed using institutional data'), and no model internals or hyperparameters exist to report. Only the inference workflow (cloud export, import to Eclipse v15.6/MiM v7.2.8/Monaco v6.2.2.0) is reproducible.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Not applicable/not reported — authors did not train the model and the commercial loss function is undisclosed.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Patient preparation, CT simulation parameters, image export to the ART-Plan cloud server, and 'rule-based post-processing techniques' are mentioned. However, preprocessing specifics (resampling, normalization, cropping) and the exact post-processing rules are not described.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Proprietary commercial software (ART-Plan); data explicitly unavailable due to privacy/ethical restrictions per the Data Availability Statement.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Two complementary metrics used: Dice Similarity Coefficient (volumetric overlap) and maximum Hausdorff Distance (boundary deviation), computed in Velocity v4.0. Authors note that surface DSC/95th-percentile HD were unavailable in the software.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Formal statistics: one-sided Welch's t-test (all p<0.0001), Cohen's d effect sizes (all |d|>0.8, 'large/very large'), full descriptive statistics (median, min, max, mean, SD), and Welch–Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. Confidence intervals not reported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: No quantitative benchmarking against other auto-segmentation tools, published baselines, or literature values. Comparisons are strictly internal (C_man vs C_AI vs C_adj); literature is discussed only narratively.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-structure results (both metrics, complete statistics) reported separately for CTV, anorectum, and bladder. Minor caveat: bowel bag and femoral heads were segmented but excluded from analysis without quantitative results.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated and candid limitations section: small sample, hip-implant artifact cases with degraded metrics, circular AI-as-ground-truth problem, HDmax outlier sensitivity, temporal cohort bias, absence of standardized DSC/HD thresholds, no causal inference possible, exploratory nature stated.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate-High. Retrospective, non-randomized design. Mitigating: no exclusion criteria applied (consecutive clinical cases, including 2 hip-implant patients). Aggravating: cohorts are non-concurrent and defined by treatment era (manual 2020–2024 vs AI-adjusted 2025), so group membership is confounded with time and workflow evolution — acknowledged by authors.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: High. The reference standard is the AI output itself (C_AI), which structurally guarantees superior agreement for the AI-adjusted workflow (C_adj); the C_adj metrics effectively measure the magnitude of clinician modification rather than segmentation accuracy, making the comparison asymmetric and potentially self-fulfilling. Outcome measurement (DSC/HDmax in Velocity) was at least applied consistently across groups.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Only 3 of 5 segmented structures analyzed (bowel bag, femoral heads omitted); no confidence intervals; no dosimetric or clinical endpoints; numerical inconsistency between abstract/text (CTV median HDmax 9.22 mm) and Table 1 (9.52 mm); hip-implant failures described only qualitatively; exploratory framing is transparent, reducing but not eliminating this risk.

detailed_extraction: STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective, multicenter (3 Italian centers), non-interventional observational technical note; ethics approval waived under Italian regulatory framework (Ministry of Health DM 30 Nov 2021, AIFA 425/2024, EU Reg. 536/2014); informed consent obtained; no external funding; no declared conflicts. POPULATION/TREATMENT: 62 prostate cancer patients, moderate hypofractionation (62 Gy/20 fx), 2 coplanar VMAT arcs, PTV = CTV + 7 mm (5 mm posteriorly); knee-fix immobilization; CTV = prostate + seminal vesicles. AI SYSTEM: ART-Plan v2.3.1 (TheraPanacea, Paris), CE Class IIb commercial auto-contouring device; deep learning based on 3D U-Net with rule-based post-processing; cloud-based inference (minutes); no institutional fine-tuning. WORKFLOWS: C_man = manual delineation in Eclipse/Monaco with MRI/PET available; C_AI = automatic contour from planning CT only; C_adj = clinician-reviewed/corrected AI contours ('digital expert' paradigm) with MRI/PET available. STRUCTURES: CTV, bowel bag, anorectum, bladder, femoral heads segmented; only CTV, bladder, anorectum analyzed. EVALUATION: Geometric analysis in Velocity v4.0; DSC and HDmax; one-sided Welch's t-tests with directional hypotheses and Cohen's d. KEY RESULTS — DSC (C_AI vs C_man → C_AI vs C_adj, median): CTV 0.80 (0.49–0.90) → 0.92 (0.82–0.97); anorectum 0.86 (0.58–0.91) → 0.99 (0.86–0.99); bladder 0.94 (0.78–0.97) → 0.99 (0.97–0.998). HDmax (median): CTV 12.33 mm (8.07–26.67) → 9.52 mm per table / 9.22 mm per text (internal inconsistency; range 5.5–19.13); anorectum 17.50 (5.00–30.00) → 1.42 (0.94–18.00); bladder 7.50 (3.52–18.45) → 3.75 (0.97–6.69). All p ≤ 0.0006 (reported as <0.0001); Cohen's d: DSC +1.34/+2.39/+1.96, HDmax −0.91/−2.15/−1.43 (CTV/anorectum/bladder). CONTEXTUAL FINDINGS: median DSC 0.84 in cases where physicians approved AI CTV without modification despite MRI/PET availability; 2 hip-implant patients showed lower DSC/higher HDmax from CT metal artifacts. CONCEPTUAL CONTRIBUTION: 'predictive peer review' — AI contours as a standardized visual reference preceding formal peer review, positioned explicitly as assistive rather than a replacement for clinical judgment. METHODOLOGICAL CAVEATS FOR REVIEWERS: (1) ground-truth circularity (AI as reference); (2) temporal confound between cohorts; (3) evaluation of a pre-trained commercial system, not a novel or reproducible model; (4) no dosimetric endpoint; (5) single CT modality for AI vs multimodal input for manual workflows (unequal information conditions); (6) maximum HD used despite acknowledged outlier sensitivity. RELEVANCE TO REVIEW SCOPE: relevant as multicenter clinical-deployment evidence for 3D U-Net-based CT segmentation of pelvic OARs/targets in prostate radiotherapy, but NOT a methodological DL segmentation contribution (no training, architecture detail, or code).
contribution_summary: This multicenter technical note retrospectively evaluates a commercial 3D U-Net auto-contouring system (ART-Plan/TheraPanacea) as a 'predictive peer review' tool across three Italian radiotherapy centers, comparing manual, AI, and AI-adjusted contours in 62 hypofractionated prostate cancer patients. It reports that AI-adjusted contours agree significantly more with the AI reference than manual contours do (CTV median DSC 0.80→0.92; HDmax 12.33→9.52 mm; all p<0.0001, large effect sizes), supporting reduced interobserver variability and workflow standardization via a physician-as-reviewer paradigm. Its contribution is a clinical workflow/validation paradigm rather than a novel segmentation algorithm, with the central methodological weakness of using the AI output itself as the ground truth reference.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Partial. 380 CT volumes total across three datasets, but per-task training sizes after the 5:1 split are ~108 (LiTS), ~175 (KiTS), and only ~33 (segTHOR) — the heart task falls below the 50-subject threshold. Official test sets (LiTS 70, KiTS 90, segTHOR 20) were never used.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Good. Three well-established public challenge datasets (MICCAI 2017 LiTS, MICCAI 2019 KiTS, ISBI 2019 segTHOR) are cited with references, training/test volume counts, class composition, and providers summarized in Table 1.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Partial. A 5:1 train:test ratio on the official training sets is stated, but no random seed, stratification, or patient-level split procedure is described, and no separate validation set exists. Evaluation is on internal splits rather than official challenge test servers, so results are not comparable to published leaderboard figures.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: No description of the annotation process for any dataset (annotator expertise, inter-rater agreement, protocol). The paper only generically notes that annotation is time-consuming and subjective; it relies implicitly on challenge-provided labels.

Q5_external_validation.justification: None. Each model is trained and tested on internal splits of the same single dataset per task; no independent external cohort or cross-dataset generalization experiment (e.g., train LiTS → test KiTS) was performed.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Partial. The architecture is well illustrated (3D ANU-Net nested encoder-decoder, attention-gated dense skip connections, deep supervision on X0_1..X0_4, layer-by-layer FPC module, 7-step point-sampling pipeline with figures), but key numeric details are missing: channel widths per stage, kernel sizes, MLP configuration, and the point-sampling hyperparameters K (overgeneration factor), β (importance ratio), and the smoothing constant s.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Poor. Optimizer, learning rate, learning-rate schedule, batch size, number of epochs/iterations, data augmentation, patch-sampling strategy, and even the deep learning framework are all unreported. Only the GPU (single GTX 1080Ti) and patch size (256×256×32) are given. Training from the paper alone would be impossible.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Good. Section 2.2 systematically reviews distribution-based (CE, WCE, focal) vs. area-based (Dice) losses, and Section 3.4 justifies the hybrid loss (soft Dice + 0.1 × squared-error × HD-weighted boundary term, averaged over 4 deep-supervision outputs) with explicit rationale and citation (Karimi & Salcudean 2020) for boundary learning; BCE for the FPC binary module is justified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Partial. Volumes were unified to 256×256×32 patches (Table 1; apparent typo '256×56×32' for heart), and the FPC gating (dot product with {0,1}) is described as an integrated post-hoc mechanism. However, intensity normalization, resampling vs. cropping procedure, number of patches per volume, and sliding-window inference details are absent.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or availability statement; no repository URL or license for released artifacts.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Good. Four segmentation metrics (mIoU, Dice, Recall, Hausdorff Distance) plus per-volume inference time, all with formulas provided in Section 4.2.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: None. All results are single point estimates with no confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests, or repeated runs; test sets are small (e.g., ~7 volumes for segTHOR), making uncertainty quantification especially important.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Seven baselines compared under identical splits/metrics (3D UNet, 3D R2UNet, 3D UNet++, Point 3D UNet++, 3D UNet3+, Attention 3D UNet, Attention 3D R2UNet) plus two ablation axes (deep supervision, FPC) — a broad comparison set. Caveats: nnU-Net (cited by the authors as the key adaptive framework) is absent, and comparisons on private 5:1 splits prevent calibration against published challenge results.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Good. Separate results tables per task (Tables 2–4: liver, kidney, heart) each reporting the full metric set, with ablation rows per organ. Note each task is single-organ binary rather than multi-organ.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations section, no failure-case analysis, and no future-work statement. Missed regions are only visually flagged with red arrows in qualitative Figures 8–10 without any discussion.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/moderate concern. Patients come from established public challenge cohorts (clear provenance, mitigating overt selection bias), but the authors constructed their own 5:1 internal splits without describing randomization or stratification, excluded the official test sets, and collapsed each dataset to a single binary organ class (discarding tumors/other OARs), which may favor the proposed single-organ pipeline.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate concern. The same splits, metrics, hardware, and protocol were applied uniformly to all seven baselines and ablations, supporting internal fairness; however, baseline re-implementation details are unreported, and the absence of any validation set raises the possibility of test-informed hyperparameter/tuning choices.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate concern. Ablation results are transparently reported, including unfavorable intermediate configurations (e.g., base Render 3D U-Net without DS/FPC underperforms Point 3D UNet++ and 3D UNet3+ on liver IoU). However, there is no limitations section, no uncertainty quantification, no official-test-server results, and no failure-case discussion.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not captured in prior extraction: (1) DATA HANDLING — Only official training sets used; official test sets (LiTS 70, KiTS 90, segTHOR 20) never evaluated, so no challenge-server leaderboard comparison. Each dataset reduced to one binary class: liver-only (LiTS), kidney-only (KiTS), heart-only (segTHOR); tumors, aorta, trachea, esophagus treated as background — explaining multi_organ=false despite three organs overall. Table 1 lists heart patch size as '256×56×32' (apparent typo for 256×256×32). (2) LOSS DETAILS — Hybrid loss = mean over 4 deep-supervision outputs of [1 − soft Dice + 0.1 × (Yi − Y)² ∘ weighted HD boundary term]; smoothing constant s value unspecified; HD-weighted boundary formulation follows Karimi & Salcudean (IEEE TMI 2020); FPC trained separately with BCE. (3) POINT-SAMPLING — Explicitly adapted from PointRend (Kirillov et al., arXiv:1912.08193): overgeneration of KN candidates (K>1, value unreported), importance sampling of top-βN most-uncertain points, (1−β)N uniform unimportant points (β unreported); coarse decoder upsamples via bilinear interpolation; a lightweight MLP independently predicts labels of selected uncertain points; resulting point features REPLACE upsampled features before attention-gated concatenation with encoder features. (4) FPC MODULE — Operates on deepest encoder block X4_0; pipeline: dropout(0.5) → conv → adaptive maxpool(2) → sigmoid → argmax ∈ {0,1}; output mask dot-multiplied with the binary decision, zeroing predictions when organ absence is detected. (5) EVALUATION INCONSISTENCIES — Section 4.2 (Eq. 11) states d() is Manhattan distance, while Section 3.4 (Eqs. 6–7) defines Euclidean distance for HD — an internal inconsistency; HD units (mm vs. voxels) unspecified; surface metrics like ASSD/NSD not reported. (6) ABLATION STRUCTURE — Three Render variants per task (base; +DS; +DS+FPC) plus Point 3D UNet++ isolating the point-sampling contribution; point-sampling consistently improves UNet++ across all three tasks, and DS+FPC gives the best results. (7) COMPUTE — Single NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti; inference 1.6–2.0 s per 3D volume; model parameter count, training time, and memory footprint unreported. (8) CLAIMED NOVELTY — Authors claim first transfer of computer-graphics rendering/PointRend ideas to 3D medical CT segmentation; built on the authors' own prior ANU-Net (Li et al., Computers & Graphics 2020). (9) ADMINISTRATIVE — Funding: National Key R&D Program of China (2018YFB0204301); open access CC BY 4.0; no conflicts declared. Baseline implementation details (how the seven competitors were configured/trained) are not reported.
contribution_summary: Render 3D U-Net reframes 3D CT organ segmentation as a rendering problem, replacing standard decoder upsampling with a PointRend-inspired subdivision-based point-sampling scheme inside a 3D attention-gated nested U-Net (3D ANU-Net) trained under deep supervision with a hybrid Dice + Hausdorff-distance boundary loss, and adds a False Positive Classification (FPC) module that zeroes out predictions when organ presence is not detected. On internal 5:1 splits of LiTS (liver), KiTS (kidney), and segTHOR (heart) as single-organ binary tasks, it reported Dice of 96.08/95.89/96.12 with reduced Hausdorff distance versus seven U-Net-family baselines, with ablations attributing gains to point-sampling and FPC. The methodological novelty (boundary-focused rendering and explicit false-positive suppression) is notable, but evaluation rigor is limited by missing reproducibility details, no external validation, and no statistical analysis.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 20 subjects (10 female, 10 male with liver tumors) from 3D-IRCADb01; well below the >50-subject threshold. Slice-level data augmentation (flip, 90° rotation) inflates image count but not subject count.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Public 3D-IRCADb01 from IRCAD Digestive Cancer Institute clearly identified; DICOM format; 20 tumor-bearing cases out of 75; masks for liver, tumor, bone, arteries, kidneys, lungs.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No train/validation/test split described anywhere. Reported metrics are 'averaged over all test images' but the test set is never defined — unclear if evaluation includes training/augmented slices.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Reference masks ship with the public 3D-IRCADb01 dataset, but the paper does not describe the annotation process (raters, protocol, inter-rater agreement).

Q5_external_validation.justification: Single dataset only. Claim of testing on 'synthetic and real-world images' is not substantiated with any results.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: ResU-Net described conceptually with figure (pre-activated residual blocks replacing U-Net's 3×3 conv+ReLU in encoder/decoder/bridge), but no layer depth, filter counts, or parameter details.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Adam, lr=0.0001, batch size 16, NVIDIA Tesla T4 (Google Colab), TensorFlow/Keras, Python 3.9.1 reported. Missing: epochs, early stopping, split, and exact augmentation quantities.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Weighted cross-entropy explicitly chosen and justified for class imbalance, with equation and median-frequency class weighting given.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Pre-processing thoroughly described (HU windowing [-100,400], histogram equalization, [0,1] normalization, reflection + 90° rotation augmentation). No post-processing described at all.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model repository mentioned.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Six metrics: DSC, accuracy, precision, specificity, VOE, RVD — all with formulas (though the specificity/precision equations are both mislabeled 'Accuracy').

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, significance tests, or per-patient variance. All results are single point estimates.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Comparison tables vs. Christ (CFCN), Rafiei (3D-2D-FCN), Li, Jin (RA-UNet, 0.971), Almotairi (SegNet), but authors themselves call it 'rough comparability' — different datasets, not re-run on a common split.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver (Table 2) and tumor (Table 3) reported separately across all six metrics. No per-patient breakdown, but per-structure reporting is satisfied for this two-target study.

Q15_limitations.justification: No limitations or failure-case discussion; no qualitative examples of segmentation errors.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High — convenience sample of 20 public 3D-IRCADb01 cases; no eligibility criteria; small, single-source dataset from 2000s-era scanner technology.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: High — evaluation protocol undefined (no stated test split), raising concern metrics include training data; single reference standard; no blinding or independent assessment.
