risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: High — favorable-only reporting with no failure cases; internal inconsistency (abstract reports tumor DSC '0.83%' vs. Table 3 = 0.893); DSC values mislabeled as percentages; VOE formula as written computes 100×(1−Dice), not 1−Jaccard as claimed.

detailed_extraction: SCOPE NOTE FOR REVIEW: despite the review topic (3D organ segmentation), this is a 2D slice-wise method — CT volumes are converted to 2D slices and processed independently; no 3D context or volumetric post-processing. May be excluded or flagged under 3D-inclusion criteria. PIPELINE: (1) HU windowing at [-100, 400]; (2) histogram equalization; (3) normalization to [0,1]; (4) augmentation by x/y-axis reflection and 90° rotation (slice+mask jointly); (5) 2D ResU-Net with pre-activated residual blocks; (6) weighted cross-entropy loss with median-frequency class weights. TRAINING: Adam, lr 1e-4, batch 16, Google Colab Tesla T4, TF/Keras. RESULTS: liver DSC 0.9781, accuracy 0.991, precision 0.982, specificity 0.961, VOE 0.13, RVD 0.018; tumor DSC 0.893, accuracy 0.97, precision 0.950, specificity 0.957, VOE 13.15, RVD 7.23. ANNOTATION ERRORS IN PAPER: abstract states 0.97/0.83 DSC (as '%') vs. tables' 0.9781/0.893; specificity and precision equations both labeled 'Accuracy'; VOE equation is actually 100×(1−DSC); 'each has 2800 slices' phrasing ambiguous (likely total slices across 20 scans). Baselines cited: Christ CFCN 0.943/0.56 (liver/tumor), Rafiei 3D-2D-FCN 0.935, Li patch-CNN 0.80, Jin RA-UNet 0.971 — claimed best score (0.9781) exceeds RA-UNet by only 0.007 on a 20-patient dataset with no significance testing.
contribution_summary: Applies a 2D ResU-Net (U-Net with pre-activated residual blocks) plus a standard pre-processing pipeline (HU windowing, histogram equalization, flip/rotation augmentation, weighted cross-entropy) to liver and liver-tumor segmentation on 3D-IRCADb01, reporting DSC 0.978 (liver) and 0.893 (tumor). The contribution is incremental — an established architecture with conventional pre-processing and no novel methodological component. Evidence strength is limited by 20 subjects, an undefined train/test split, no external validation, and internal inconsistencies between abstract and reported tables.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 91 training scans (LiTS subset) exceeds the >50 threshold; 171 scans total across three datasets, though modest by current standards.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Three standard public benchmarks (LiTS, 3D-IRCADb, Sliver07) clearly identified with per-dataset splits; patient demographics/slice-thickness details not reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Explicit 91/20/20 split on LiTS plus five-fold cross-validation; 3D-IRCADb and Sliver07 held out as independent test sets.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Relies on publicly provided expert annotations; no description of annotation protocol, annotator expertise, or inter-rater agreement.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Evaluated on two datasets (3D-IRCADb, Sliver07) fully independent of the training data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Fully specified: 4-stage hierarchical encoder-decoder, EPA blocks, (4,4,2) patch embedding, skip connections, Hessian-based gradient encoder equations (∂²f/∂x∂z, ∂²f/∂y∂z), decoder fusion and final 3×3×3 + 1×1×1 convolutions.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Optimizer (Adam), initial LR 5e-4, batch 64, 1000 epochs, augmentations, and loss weights (α=β=γ=1) reported; LR schedule, 3D volume sampling strategy, and code not provided, limiting exact reproduction.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Rationale stated: Dice+CE for class imbalance, HD loss for boundary/challenging cases. Caveat: no loss ablation shown and the Dice+CE+HD combination is established, not novel as claimed.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing (HU clipping [-200,200], resize 512×512→256×256, augmentation list) and postprocessing (largest connected component + median filter) both explicitly described.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release; no repository URL provided.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice plus VOE, RAVD, ASSD, MSSD, and AUC/precision/recall (Sliver07).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Point estimates only; no confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests despite using five-fold cross-validation.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: 18 baselines compared including UNETR++, TransUNet, Swin-UNETR, nnFormer. Caveat: some baseline numbers are cross-referenced from Synapse (Table 1) or literature, and only 131/201 LiTS scans were used, limiting direct comparability.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver); Dice reported separately per dataset rather than only as an average.

Q15_limitations.justification: False positives near stomach/spleen/heart from HU overlap, false negatives near tumor boundaries, and 2.3× parameter overhead vs UNETR++ all explicitly acknowledged.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/unclear — public datasets reduce selection bias, but only 131 of the 201 official LiTS scans were used with no stated rationale for the subset choice, and the 91/20/20 split justification is not given.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate — standardized metrics on public ground truth applied uniformly across datasets; however, it is unclear whether the proposed postprocessing (connected components + median filter) was also applied to baseline methods, which could inflate relative gains.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low — all five metrics across three datasets reported, complexity overhead and failure modes disclosed; minor concerns: no variance or statistical testing, and uniformly favorable comparisons rely partly on cited literature numbers rather than re-runs.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details not in prior extraction: (1) Gradient inputs are ∂²f/∂x∂z and ∂²f/∂y∂z (first two off-diagonal elements of the last Hessian column), computed per-slice — first-order gradients along x/y per 2D slice, then second-order differencing along z — and stacked into 3D volumes; this captures boundary curvature along the z-axis. (2) Outputs of the three parallel encoders' EPA blocks are element-wise summed at each of the four stages; patch size (4,4,2) inherited from UNETR++. (3) Decoder: 4 stages, ×2 deconvolution upsampling, EPA blocks at all but the final stage, channels halved between stages, final fusion with encoder features then 3×3×3 and 1×1×1 convolutions. (4) Hybrid loss uses equal weights (α=β=γ=1) with deep supervision. (5) Baseline complexity in Table 1 (params/FLOPs: TransUNet 96.07M/88.91G, UNETR 92.49M/75.76G, Swin-UNETR 62.83M/384.2G, nnFormer 150.5M/213.4G, UNETR++ 42.96M/47.98G) was measured on Synapse, not directly comparable to G-UNETR++'s 97.73M/73.12G measured in the liver setup — an apples-to-oranges comparison in the paper. (6) No training time or inference time reported. (7) No ablation isolating the gradient encoders' contribution was found in the provided text; the loss combination is presented as novel but is established in the literature. (8) PyTorch on 2× RTX 3090; Ubuntu 18.04.
contribution_summary: G-UNETR++ extends UNETR++ with two parallel gradient-based encoders consuming second-order partial derivatives (∂²f/∂x∂z, ∂²f/∂y∂z from the CT Hessian matrix) to explicitly learn 3D organ-boundary geometry, paired with a Dice+CE+Hausdorff hybrid loss. It reports liver Dice of 97.38% (LiTS), 97.50% (3D-IRCADb), and 97.32% (Sliver07), outperforming 18 compared methods, but at 97.73M parameters (~2.3× the UNETR++ baseline) — 'moderate' only relative to nnFormer. The contribution is single-organ (liver) with external validation on two independent public datasets; no code is released, which limits verification and reuse.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 260 CT volumes (220 train / 40 test), well above the >50 subject threshold; multi-organ tasks (liver, kidney, spleen).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Described only as collected from 'different scanners of different medical institutions' — no institution names, patient demographics, acquisition protocol, inclusion criteria, or ethics statement.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 220/40 train/test split stated, but no validation set described for hyperparameter/tuning decisions; split performed once, no cross-validation.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation process never described — no mention of who segmented the ground truth, how many raters, inter-rater agreement, or reference standard.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort; all evaluation on 40 internal test cases from the same collection.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Uses standard 2D FCN (VGG-16 backbone) and 2D U-Net with architecture diagrams in Appendix A (Figures A1, A2), but no implementation specifics (input patch size, channel configs beyond figures) and no modifications detailed.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Hyperparameters given (SGD, batch 16, poly LR schedule init 0.001/power 0.9, 10x10^5 iterations, flip/mirror augmentation, TensorFlow), but the core A/B subset division 'based on simple statistics information' is vague and the dataset is unavailable, limiting true reproducibility.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice coefficient as loss is explicitly justified for voxel-level background/foreground imbalance, and the authors argue why focal loss alone is insufficient for dataset-level hard/easy sample imbalance.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing described (HU truncation to [-150, 250], flip/mirror augmentation), but no post-processing steps mentioned (unclear if none used or omitted from reporting).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model release mentioned anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice coefficient is the only metric reported; no Volumetric Similarity, Hausdorff distance, ASSD, sensitivity/specificity, etc.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Descriptive statistics only (mean ± SD, per-case min and max Dice); no confidence intervals, significance tests, or p-values despite small improvements (~0.8 Dice points).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: No comparison against published state-of-the-art methods (e.g., H-DenseUNet cited but not compared); only internal ablations against their own baseline and selection-ratio variants.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Results reported separately for liver (Table 1, A3), kidney (A1, A4), and spleen (A2, A5) with mean, min, and max per-case Dice for both architectures.

Q15_limitations.justification: Discussion offers interpretation (slice redundancy, shallow network capacity) and notes when the method helps most (hard cases), but no explicit limitations section, no failure-case analysis, and no acknowledgment of 2D-only or single-test-set constraints.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: HIGH — the 260 scans' origin and patient selection process are undefined; no inclusion/exclusion criteria, no consecutive or random sampling description, no demographics; results may not generalize.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: UNCLEAR/MODERATE — the same Dice metric was applied consistently to all cases on a fixed test set, but with unknown ground-truth provenance (annotator count, expertise, consensus process) and no blinding, assessment consistency cannot be verified.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: LOW/MODERATE — all planned experiments and tables are reported, including worst-case (min) Dice values where the method does not improve the maximum, and all three organs for both architectures; however, only one metric is reported and no pre-registered protocol or significance testing exists.

detailed_extraction: TASK: 2D slice-wise liver, kidney, and spleen segmentation from CT. DATA: 260 CT volumes from multiple institutions/scanners, slice spacing 0.45-5 mm; 220 random volumes for training, 40 for testing; intensities clipped to [-150, 250] HU. METHOD PIPELINE: (1) Divide training volumes into subsets A and B using simple volume statistics (slice count, positive/negative slice ratio) so both subsets preserve the dataset's positive/negative slice ratio; (2) train a pre-training model on B (slices augmented by flipping/mirroring) for 5x10^5 iterations; (3) use the pre-training model to score every slice in A and binarize into hard/easy by a Dice threshold set to the baseline model's min Dice (0.923 for liver/FCN — 6,268 hard vs 35,984 easy slices, ~1:6 ratio); (4) flip-augment hard slices and add them to B; (5) continue training to 10x10^5 total iterations (same architecture in pre-training and final stages, so no restart needed). Baseline ablation: reducing training set to selection ratios 0.8/0.5 barely changes mean Dice; performance drops sharply at ratios 0.3 and 0.2 (liver FCN mean 0.9512 and 0.9475 vs 0.9705 baseline), supporting slice redundancy in CT volumes. RESULTS (test set, mean ± SD / min / max Dice): FCN liver 0.9789±0.012/0.947/0.9854 (baseline 0.9705); FCN kidney 0.9258±0.067/0.8547/0.9693 (baseline 0.9167); FCN spleen 0.9801±0.007/0.9563/0.9975 (baseline 0.9773); U-Net liver 0.9604±0.022/0.912/0.987 (baseline 0.9532); U-Net kidney 0.9287±0.028/0.8591/0.9708 (baseline 0.9206); U-Net spleen 0.9857±0.005/0.9579/0.9969 (baseline 0.9795). Gains concentrate in the min (hardest-case) Dice, e.g., liver FCN min 0.923→0.947; max Dice is essentially unchanged. IMPLEMENTATION: TensorFlow; SGD, mini-batch 16; 'poly' LR schedule (initial 0.001, power 0.9); Dice loss; random mirror/flip augmentation. FUNDING: NSFC (61876026, 61672120) and CSTC project CSTC2015shmszx120002. NOT REPORTED: code/model availability, ground-truth annotation protocol, ethics approval, annotation inter-rater data, 3D context (purely 2D slice-based inference), tumor segmentation, runtime, and any external-cohort validation.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes an online hard-example enhancement strategy for CT organ segmentation: a pre-training model trained on one half of the training set acts as a task-specific hard/easy slice classifier (thresholded at the baseline's worst-case Dice), and flip-augmented hard slices are then added back to the training data to rebalance dataset-level hard/easy sample imbalance — something the authors argue Dice loss or focal loss alone cannot fix. Across FCN and U-Net on liver, kidney, and spleen segmentation, the method yields small mean Dice gains (~0.8-1.5 points) with consistent improvement on worst-case (min) Dice. A secondary empirical finding is substantial slice redundancy in CT training sets: reducing training volumes to 50% barely affects performance, while reductions below 30% degrade it sharply.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Large datasets used: private NPC cohort of 356 patients (>40,000 CT slices; 285 train / 71 test) and public LiTS dataset (130 labeled volumes, re-split 100 train / 30 test). Both far exceed the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: NPC dataset clearly attributed to Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center with ethics approval number (RDDA2020001435) and clinical trial registration (NCT01762514). LiTS is a well-known public MICCAI 2017 challenge benchmark, properly cited.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random division with exact patient counts (285/71 for NPC; 100/30 for LiTS) and five-fold cross-validation applied to all comparative and ablation experiments, with metrics reported as mean ± standard deviation over 10 runs. Minor weakness: no explicitly separate validation set described within folds.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground-truth masks for 13 labels (8 organ types with left/right pairs) are mentioned, but the annotation process is not described: number of annotators, level of expertise (e.g., radiation oncologists), annotation tools, or inter-rater agreement are all unreported. LiTS ground truth is provided by the challenge.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Partial only. The public LiTS dataset demonstrates generalizability across a second task (liver/tumor), but there is no external validation on an independent institution's NPC cohort. The NPC dataset is single-center and unavailable due to privacy restrictions.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture well described with figures: SEC module (cross-level feature fusion via 3×3 conv + upsampling, concatenation, followed by SE channel-attention block) placed at skip connections; stage-wise pyramid structure for multi-scale/global context; bilinear interpolation instead of deconvolution (checkerboard artifact avoidance); auto-context cascaded secondary U-Net. Missing fine-grained detail such as channel counts per stage, but conceptual completeness is good.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Thorough training details: multi-class cross-entropy loss (formula given), SGD (momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0001), initial LR 0.01 with polynomial decay (power 0.9), 100 epochs, batch size 16, PyTorch, RTX 2080 Ti 12GB, two-stage cascade training scheme explicitly described.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Multi-class cross-entropy is simply stated with its formula; no justification is provided and no alternatives (e.g., Dice loss, compound losses common for small-structure segmentation) are discussed or compared.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Partial. Image resizing to 256×256 (aspect-ratio preserved) is described; however, CT-specific preprocessing (HU windowing, intensity normalization) and any post-processing (e.g., connected-component filtering, CRF) are entirely absent from the paper.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Authors state 'We will release our codes on GitHub' but no URL or repository link is provided at publication time; the claim is unverifiable. The NPC dataset is explicitly unavailable.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice (per-organ, average, plus Dice-per-case and Dice-global for LiTS), precision, and recall (Table 4) are reported with formulas. Note: Jaccard similarity is claimed as a metric in the abstract but no Jaccard results appear in the paper.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired-sample t-tests at 95% confidence level comparing SECP-Net against all seven baselines (Table 3), with mean ± std over 10 experimental runs. Caveat: the reported threshold 'p < 0.5' is almost certainly a typographical error for 'p < 0.05', and no confidence intervals or effect sizes are given.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Comprehensive comparison against seven established U-shape methods (U-Net, Attention U-Net, CE-Net, UNet++, CPF-Net, Res-U-Net, Dense-U-Net) plus a 2.5D SOTA attempt (H-DenseUNet), on both datasets, with a dedicated ablation study (5 configurations) isolating each component's contribution.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Full per-organ Dice with standard deviations for all 13 labels reported in Tables 2 and 7, with specific analysis of small-organ improvements (eyes, submandibular glands, thyroid) rather than only averages.

Q15_limitations.justification: Partial. Authors acknowledge higher computational cost of the cascaded design and note that local/region-level attention needs further research. However, there is no systematic failure-case analysis of their own method (visualization section highlights competitor errors; SECP-Net residual failures are not analyzed), and the 2D limitation is not framed as a drawback.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/Unclear — single-center cohort (Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center); no explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, scanner, or slice-thickness details; random split mitigates within-cohort bias but generalizability to other centers/populations is unknown; dataset cannot be shared for verification.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-Moderate — standardized training settings across all compared methods, five-fold cross-validation, 10 repetitions, and identical preprocessing; however, GPU memory constraints forced batch size 1 for the 2.5D H-DenseUNet baseline, which the authors themselves admit degraded its performance, potentially disadvantaging volumetric competitor architectures.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-Moderate — per-organ Dice fully reported with mean ± std for all methods; however, Jaccard is claimed as an evaluation metric in the abstract but never reported, precision/recall are reported only as averages (not per-organ), and the statistical threshold appears misreported (p < 0.5 vs. p < 0.05).

detailed_extraction: TASK & SCOPE: Segmentation of 13 OAR labels in head-and-neck CT for NPC radiotherapy planning — left/right eyes, temporal lobes, mandible, parotids, submandibular glands, brainstem, spinal cord, thyroid gland. IMPORTANT FOR REVIEW SCOPE: despite the review topic (3D segmentation), this method is 2D slice-by-slice; the authors explicitly rejected 2.5D/3D (tested H-DenseUNet, batch size 1 due to 12GB GPU limit) arguing small effective training-set size and memory constraints. Should be flagged as a 2D method on volumetric CT data. ARCHITECTURE: (1) Primary network: U-shape encoder-decoder with SEC modules at each skip connection — SEC fuses feature maps between adjacent levels (deeper level convolved 3×3 stride 1, upsampled to shallower resolution, concatenated and fused via 3×3 conv, then passed through Squeeze-and-Excitation channel-attention block); pyramid structure propagates multi-scale + global context bottom-to-top across stages; SE block also at deepest pyramid level. (2) Secondary network: original U-Net taking concatenation of original image and primary network's probability map (auto-context cascade). Upsampling via bilinear interpolation (deconvolution rejected to avoid checkerboard artifacts). Training scheme: Step 1 train backbone U-Net to convergence; Step 2 add SEC+pyramid, initialize from Step 1 weights; then freeze primary, train secondary; finally fine-tune whole network. DATA: NPC: 356 patients, >40,000 slices, 512×512, resized to 256×256; organ volumes reported (smallest: left submandibular 8.9 cm³, left eye 8.4 cm³; largest: left temporal lobe 134.3 cm³). LiTS: 130 labeled volumes re-split 100/30 because official test server unavailable. KEY RESULTS (NPC, mean Dice ± std over 10 runs of 5-fold CV): SECP-Net 83.28% vs UNet++ 82.68%, Attention U-Net 81.80%, CPF-Net 81.19%, Dense-U-Net 80.23%, Res-U-Net 80.09%, U-Net 79.83%, CE-Net 78.52%. Largest gains on small organs: thyroid 74.81%, submandibular_L 77.38%, submandibular_R 79.19%, eye_L 81.19%, eye_R 80.81%. UNet++ slightly outperformed SECP-Net on temporal lobes and left mandible/parotid. Precision 0.908 / recall 0.902 (best of all methods). LiTS: Dice-per-case liver 85.47%, tumor 71.62%; Dice-global liver 87.82%, tumor 78.89% (all best). ABLATION: U-Net 79.83% → cascade-concat 81.75% → auto-context 82.13% → SEC 83.09% → SEC+concat 83.10% → full SECP-Net 83.28%. STATISTICS: paired t-test vs each baseline, reported as p < 0.5 (apparent typo for p < 0.05). FUNDING: Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation (2021A1515220140, 2022A1515011549, 2023A1515011104). FUTURE WORK: transformer integration; local-region attention modeling. NOTABLE ISSUES: abstract claims Jaccard metric but results absent; code release promised without link; no intensity normalization described; single GPU (RTX 2080 Ti, 12GB) constrained design choices.
contribution_summary: This paper proposes SECP-Net, a 2D cascaded U-shape network for CT organs-at-risk segmentation in nasopharyngeal carcinoma that introduces (1) SE-Connection (SEC) modules — channel-attention-gated cross-level feature fusion replacing naive U-Net skip connections — and (2) a stage-wise pyramid structure for multi-scale and global context propagation, combined with auto-context cascading of a secondary U-Net for refinement. On a 356-patient private NPC cohort it achieves the best mean Dice (83.28%) versus seven baselines, with the largest gains on small organs (eyes, submandibular glands, thyroid), and confirms generalizability on the public LiTS liver/tumor benchmark. The main value for the review lies in its evidence that attention-based multi-scale feature fusion plus cascading improves small-OAR segmentation, though its explicitly 2D design, single-center private data, and re-implemented baselines under constrained hardware limit stronger conclusions.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 4300 CT images (3900 LiTS + 400 KCGMH), 4000 for training. Subject count never stated (data counted in slices, not volumes), but LiTS benchmark source implies >50 patients. Adequate for training either way.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Two sources clearly described: public LiTS benchmark plus 400 clinical images from Kaohsiung Chang Gung Memorial Hospital with IRB approval (201801581B0).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split stated (4000 train / 300 test, 20% of train for validation), but randomization appears to be at image/slice level, risking same-patient slices in both train and test (leakage). No per-patient split or stratification described.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: KCGMH masks annotated by 3 radiologists with lesion-section discussion; LiTS uses public challenge ground truth. No inter-rater agreement statistics reported (minor gap).

Q5_external_validation.justification: Test set drawn from the same 4300-image pool as training. Paper itself notes only 'slight difference between testing and validation datasets'. No independent external cohort.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Full layer-by-layer tables for both networks: SED-1 (U-Net, 5 levels, 32→512 filters) and SED-2 (FC-DenseNet, DB/TD/TU modules with layer counts and channel dimensions), including skip connections and concatenate operations.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: ADAM optimizer, epochs (50/100), batch sizes (16/4), and learning-rate schedules (10^-4 with step decay for SED-1, exponential e^-0.9 decay for SED-2) all given. Missing: DL framework, hardware, random seeds, early-stopping criterion (text truncated), and no code release.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice Loss adopted for both networks over cross entropy, with qualitative rationale (similarity measure). No empirical justification or loss ablation.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly described: HU truncation to [-100, 200] and downsampling to 256×256. Post-processing (3D reconstruction of predicted lesions) stated as a goal but method details not provided in available text.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model availability statement anywhere in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Only Dice evidenced (liver 0.92, tumor 0.75) in available text. No second metric (IoU/Jaccard, HD, sensitivity) visible; text truncates before full results section.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, or variance measures reported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Extensive narrative positioning against prior 2D CNN/ED methods (FCN, Mask-RCNN, U-Net variants) in the introduction, but no clear quantitative comparison table against SOTA methods in available text.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Liver and tumor segmentation reported separately (0.92 vs 0.75 Dice), not averaged.

Q15_limitations.justification: No failure-case analysis or limitations discussion present in available text; section 4.1 truncates mid-sentence, so if a limitations section exists it was not verifiable.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Random split appears slice-level rather than patient-level (risk of leakage inflating results); KCGMH patient inclusion criteria not defined; test set from same pool as training.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. Fully automated, uniform pipeline and metric for all images; but no human-reader comparison and no independent test cohort; truncated results section prevents full verification.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Dice-only reporting without uncertainty estimates; no failure cases or per-case analysis; results that don't flatter the method (e.g., small tumors) not discussed.

detailed_extraction: Method: Two-stage cascade called Successive Encoder-Decoder (SED). Stage 1 (SED-1): standard U-Net (256×256 input, 5 encoder levels, filters 32→512, skip connections) localizes liver and masks out other organs/tissue. Stage 2 input = raw CT × liver mask (element-wise multiply); Stage 2 (SED-2): FC-DenseNet (Dense U-Net; dense blocks with 4/5/7/10/12/15 layers encoder, up to 880 channels at bottleneck) segments tumors within the masked liver ROI. Networks trained independently, both with Dice Loss and ADAM. SED-1: 50 epochs, batch 16, lr 10^-4 reduced 10% every 2 epochs. SED-2: 100 epochs, batch 4, lr 10^-4 multiplied by e^-0.9 every 2 epochs. Data: 3900 LiTS slices (HU-truncated to [-100, 200] HU, per ref [10]) + 400 KCGMH slices = 4300 total, all resized 256×256; 4000 train (80/20 train/validation) / 300 test. IRB: 201801581B0. Reported results: liver Dice 0.92, tumor Dice 0.75; 3D lesion reconstruction from adjacent slices for surgical planning. Clinical context: hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) diagnosis support. Note for the review: (1) this is liver+lesion segmentation, adjacent to but not strictly multi-organ segmentation; (2) data unit is slices, not patient volumes — Dice scores are not directly comparable to volume-level benchmarks like standard LiTS results; (3) paper text was truncated mid-Section 4.1 in the provided source, so remaining results, environment details, and any ablations/comparisons/limitations could not be assessed and may raise Q11/Q12/Q13/Q15 scores if present in the full text.
contribution_summary: Proposes SED, a two-stage series of encoder-decoder networks — U-Net for liver localization followed by FC-DenseNet for tumor segmentation within the masked liver region — motivated by reducing per-network task difficulty versus a single end-to-end model. On a mixed dataset of 4300 CT slices (LiTS + 400 institutional KCGMH images), it reports Dice scores of 0.92 (liver) and 0.75 (tumor), with 3D reconstruction of predicted lesions to support HCC surgical planning. Main limitations for review purposes: slice-level random split (possible patient leakage), single Dice metric, no external validation, and no code release.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: No subject/slice count reported anywhere in available text; dataset augmented with GAN-generated synthetic images, making effective real dataset size unknown.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Dataset source not identified in available text (no public dataset named, no institution, no scanner/ acquisition details).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No train/validation/test split methodology described in available text.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground-truth masks are referenced and shown (Fig. 5) but annotation process (who, how, inter-rater agreement) is not described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external/independent cohort validation reported.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Layer-level detail for all three components: GAN (13-layer generator + 13-layer discriminator), YOLOv3-RESNet-50 (181 layers, dual detection heads 7x7x2048 and 28x28x1048, 7 anchors), DeepLabv3+InceptionResNetV2 (853 layers); architecture figures provided.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Full hyperparameter tables: GAN (Table 1: lr 0.0002, batch 128, 3000 epochs), YOLOv3-RES (Table 3: batch 8, lr 0.001, 100 epochs, warmup 1000, L2 0.0005), segmentation (Table 4: SGDM, batch 8, 100 epochs, 512x512x3). Learning-rate ablation in Table 2.

Q8_loss_function.justification: GAN adversarial generator/discriminator losses defined mathematically; YOLOv3 detection loss and segmentation loss (softmax/pixel classification implied, not stated) are neither specified nor justified.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: No preprocessing described (no HU windowing, resampling, or normalization); input size 512x512x3 for CT is unexplained (3-channel conversion not documented); no post-processing described.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code or model availability statement in available text.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: mAP (0.99) for localization and accuracy (>95%) for segmentation reported; no region-overlap (Dice/IoU) or boundary metrics (HD/ASSD) evident in available text — accuracy alone is inadequate for segmentation.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: No confidence intervals, p-values, standard deviations, or cross-validation reported.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Abstract claims superiority over 'recently published work' and introduction reviews prior methods, but the comparison tables fall in the unavailable results section; claims not verifiable in provided text.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Results section truncated; per-structure (liver vs. tumor) breakdown not verifiable. Single-organ study regardless — no multi-organ evaluation relevant to the review scope.

Q15_limitations.justification: Discussion/limitations section not present in available text.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: High/Unclear — patient selection criteria, cohort size, and inclusion/exclusion rules not reported; mixing of synthetic GAN images with real data further obscures case provenance.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: High — all evaluation performed by authors on data that includes their own synthetic images; no independent/blinded reference-standard assessment; ground-truth annotation process undocumented.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: High — headline metrics (0.99 mAP, >95% accuracy) reported without variance or per-case results; key results/comparison section unavailable in provided text; paper subsequently retracted (Diagnostics 2026, 16, 2728), raising integrity concerns.

detailed_extraction: RETRACTED 2026-08-26 (notice: doi 10.3390/diagnostics16172728). Three-stage pipeline: (1) modified GAN generates synthetic liver CT slices (64x64x3 input, 5x5 filters, leakyReLU 0.2, dropout 0.5, label-flip factor 0.3/0.5, 3000 epochs, batch 128, lr 0.0002, Adam-style decay 0.5/0.999) — generator: input+reshape+4 transposed-conv+batchnorm+ReLU+Tanh; discriminator: 5 conv + 4 LeakyReLU + 3 batchnorm; (2) YOLOv3-RESNet-50 localization: ResNet-50 feature extractor feeding YOLOv3, two detection heads (activation-37: 7x7x2048 for small objects; activation-49: 28x28x1048), 7 anchors, confidence/IoU thresholds 0.5, batch 8, lr 0.001 (selected via Table 2 ablation: errors 0.2354/0.2014/0.1354/0.1989 at lr 0.0001/0.0005/0.001/0.002), warmup 1000 iters, L2 0.0005, penalty threshold 0.5, reported mAP 0.99; (3) DeepLabv3 with pretrained InceptionResNetV2 backbone (853 layers) for '3D-semantic segmentation', trained with SGDM, batch 8, 100 epochs, input 512x512x3, reported >95% test accuracy. CAVEATS: (a) '3D' claim unsupported — all components process 2D slices; (b) liver+tumor only (single organ), not multi-organ; (c) dataset identity, size, split, and Dice/IoU results not recoverable from available text; (d) citation [45] for DeepLabv3 and [50] for YOLOv3 appear inconsistent in numbering (likely editorial error, consistent with retraction).
contribution_summary: Proposes a three-stage liver cancer CAD pipeline: a modified GAN for synthetic CT slice generation, a YOLOv3 detector with ResNet-50 backbone (dual-scale detection heads) for liver/tumor localization (0.99 mAP), and DeepLabv3 with an InceptionResNetV2 backbone for tumor segmentation (>95% accuracy). The main novelty claim is synthetic data augmentation to address small-lesion segmentation with limited training data. Note: the paper was retracted in 2026 and its '3D' segmentation claim is not supported by the 2D slice-based architecture.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 260 unenhanced abdominal CT scans (209 stone-positive, 51 stone-negative) with 7:3 train/test split and 5-fold cross-validation, yielding ~182 training cases per fold—well above the 50-subject threshold. Adequate for a 2-structure task, though modest by modern multi-organ standards.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single-center retrospective collection (First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, 2018–2020) thoroughly described: screening of ~500 scans, deduplication via SeriesID, de-identification, DICOM→NIfTI conversion, full acquisition parameters (slice thickness distribution: 119@2.5mm, 101@1.25mm, 31@2.0mm, 7@0.62mm, 2@0.42mm; XY spacing 0.371–0.977mm), ethics waiver, and public release on Zenodo.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: A 7:3 train/test ratio with 5-fold cross-validation is stated, but the precise relationship between the CV folds, the validation set used for model selection ('best models selected based on validation loss'), and the test set is ambiguous. No explicit statement of patient-level splitting or leakage prevention.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Rigorous three-stage annotation pipeline: (1) 30 trained students from biomedical engineering/CS annotated in 3D Slicer, (2) experienced instructors reviewed and corrected, (3) ten professional urological radiologists inspected and required iterative revisions until approval. Two labels (kidney, kidney stone). No inter-rater reliability statistics reported, which prevents a perfect score.

Q5_external_validation.justification: All training and evaluation performed exclusively on the in-house dataset from a single institution. No external or independent cohort (e.g., KiTS19, public stone CT cohorts) used for validation.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Five architectures (3D U-Net, Res U-Net, SegNet, DeepLabV3+, UNETR) are described at a conceptual level with citations to original papers; the two-stage coarse-to-fine scheme is well specified (cube shapes (1,96,192,192) stage 1 and (1,64,160,160) stage 2, strides, regionprops-based cropping). However, architecture-level implementation details (depth, filter counts, modifications from original implementations) are omitted.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Training protocol fully reported: 200 epochs, AdamW (weight decay 0.001), initial LR 0.001 with ReduceLROnPlateau, batch size 8, Dice+CE loss, model selection by validation loss, augmentation specifics (random affine 0±10°, horizontal inversion p=1, applied only to labeled cubes; 10,874 stage-1 and 3,492 stage-2 augmented cubes), PyTorch 1.9.0, and hardware (NVIDIA Tesla A100 40GB, AMD EPYC 7742, 64GB RAM).

Q8_loss_function.justification: Combined Dice + cross-entropy loss used, which is a standard and sensible choice for class-imbalanced segmentation, but no explicit justification is provided for the combination; only the AdamW optimizer choice is briefly rationalized ('better optimizing effects than conventional Adam').

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing extensively documented: HU clipping [-135, 215], z-axis resampling to 1.25mm (native 0.42–2.5mm), min-max normalization, x/y center-cropping (256×256 stage 1; 512×512 stage 2), regionprops-based 3D cube clipping with explicit lengths/strides. Post-processing described: coarse mask resampling to native resolution, per-kidney cube cropping from stage-1 predictions, mask overlay on output.

Q10_code_availability.justification: The annotated dataset is commendably public (Zenodo, https://zenodo.org/record/6042410), but no source code, trained model weights, or inference pipeline is released, limiting reproducibility of the reported results.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Four complementary metrics (Dice, specificity, sensitivity, accuracy) with formal TP/FP/TN/FN definitions, plus a case-level 'success rate' analysis and 2D/3D qualitative visual comparisons—exceeding the Dice-plus-one requirement.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean ± standard deviation across ten training repetitions reported for the dependent-training experiments (Table 1) and 5-fold CV design stated. However, no confidence intervals, no p-values, and no statistical significance testing between architectures or between dependent/independent training.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Head-to-head benchmarking of five well-established architectures plus an ablation of the two-stage dependent vs. independent one-step training, and stone-size-stratified analysis. However, no comparison against published results on shared public benchmarks (e.g., KiTS19 kidney Dice ~0.969 referenced only narratively via Zhao et al.), and all baselines are the authors' own re-implementations.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Per-structure results reported separately for kidney (best: Res U-Net 96.54±1.06%) and kidney stone (best: 80.59±1.28%), further stratified by stone size (small 60.11±0.84%, middle 76.08±3.46%, large 83.39±2.33%), with per-network breakdowns for all five models.

Q15_limitations.justification: Candid discussion of limitations: heavy computational cost of the two-stage scheme, cascading failure risk (stage-1 false positives corrupting stage-2 kidney cropping), difficulty of stone segmentation (size variability, appearance diversity, small shapes, class imbalance), and poor DeepLabV3+/UNETR stone performance. Future work (single-network design, inner-structure segmentation on enhanced CT, PCNL planning) outlined.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Retrospective single-center cohort; ~500 scans collected but the criteria for excluding ~240 scans during 'data cleaning' are not specified; no patient demographics (age, sex, comorbidities) reported; marked class imbalance (209 stone-positive vs. 51 stone-negative). Consecutive sampling is not explicitly claimed.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate. All five networks trained and evaluated under an identical protocol with 10 repetitions, and ground truth was consensus-reviewed by ten urological radiologists, supporting consistent outcome assessment. However, the 'success rate' metric lacks a defined threshold and is reported only graphically, introducing subjective assessment risk.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate. Main metrics reported in full tables with mean±std, including unfavorable results (e.g., DeepLabV3+ stone Dice 33.36%). Gaps include: no CIs/p-values, success rates shown only as figures without numeric values, a missing table cell (DeepLabV3+ small-stone Dice '\'), no per-fold CV results, and undeclared training/inference runtimes.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details: (1) Annotation economics: 30 students trained for first-pass labeling in 3D Slicer, instructor review, then final approval by 10 urological radiologists with iterative revisions—relevant for transferability of annotation protocols in a systematic review. (2) Data curation: SeriesID-based deduplication, Python-based PHI removal, DICOM→NIfTI conversion, case renaming ('wd0001' style) following Heller et al. (3) Stone size stratification definitions: small 0–6mm (volume 0–28mm³), medium 6–20mm (28–315mm³), large >20mm (>315mm³). (4) Augmentation applied only to labeled cubes to balance positive/negative samples: random affine (0±10°), horizontal inversion (p=1), and their combination; yielded 10,874 stage-1 cubes (96×96×196, likely typographical ordering of (1,96,192,192)) and 3,492 stage-2 cubes (160×160×64). (5) Stage 1 merges kidney+stone into a single 'kidney' class for coarse localization; stage 2 performs fine 2-class segmentation. (6) Model selection by minimum validation loss; losses visualized in Figs. 6–9. (7) Notable nuance for meta-analysis: the independently trained 3D U-Net achieved kidney Dice 96.70%, marginally exceeding the best proposed-scheme result (Res U-Net 96.54%), so the claimed benefit of two-stage dependent training is clearest for stone segmentation (80.59% vs. 79.83%) rather than kidney Dice. (8) Related-work anchor: positions against Parakh et al.'s cascading CNN for urinary stone detection (external sensitivity 0.88/specificity 0.91 at patient level). (9) Funding: NSFC Grant 8210031051 and Shenzhen Technology University school-enterprise fund. (10) Conflict of interest: three authors affiliated with Wuerzburg Dynamics Inc. (founder + two employees). (11) Ethics: retrospective design with waiver; patient consent waived. (12) Licensing and code release version: not stated.
contribution_summary: This study contributes (1) the first open-access, radiologist-approved annotated dataset of 260 unenhanced abdominal CT scans with kidney and kidney-stone masks (Zenodo), addressing data scarcity for renal stone AI research, and (2) a two-stage coarse-to-fine training scheme with interchangeable backbones (3D U-Net, Res U-Net, SegNet, DeepLabV3+, UNETR) that improves segmentation over independent one-step training, achieving 96.54% kidney Dice and 80.59% stone Dice with Res U-Net. It further provides a systematic architecture benchmark and stone-size-stratified error analysis showing small stones (<6mm) remain the principal failure mode (Dice 60.11%).

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Training set N=20, below the >50 threshold, though by design (label-efficiency is the paper's thesis). Total cohort N=120 with a large N=100 hold-out test set partially mitigates; adequacy hinges on DOKEN auto-labeling quality.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Source clearly described: single-center Stanford Health Care AF ablation cohort (Oct 2014–Jul 2019), written informed consent, IRB approval (NCT02997254). Gap: CT acquisition parameters (scanner, slice thickness, contrast phase) not reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Random 20/100 train/test split explicitly stated. However, the validation set implied by Figure 4 (validation loss/Dice curves) is never described, and no external split exists.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Test-set GT process described (expert panel manual segmentation via EnSite Verismo v2.0.1 + 3D Slicer substructure parsing). Missing: number of experts, experience level, inter-rater reliability, adjudication. Training labels are algorithmic (DOKEN), not human-verified per case.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation performed. Single-center internal hold-out only; external generalizability is cited via the authors' prior work (ref 36) but not demonstrated here.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: nnU-Net cited (Isensee et al. 2021) and shown in Fig 3, but the specific configuration (2D vs 3D variant, folds, patch size, depth) is not reported; relies on self-configuration and the external reference.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Largely specified: SGD Nesterov momentum 0.99, initial LR 0.01, batch size 2, 1000 epochs, CE+Dice loss, full augmentation list, z-score normalization, spline resampling. Missing: GPU hardware, nnU-Net version/config, validation split construction, random seeds; code not released at publication.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Sum of cross-entropy and Dice loss stated; this is the nnU-Net default but no explicit justification is given in the text.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thorough: complete DOKEN pipeline (erosion/dilation index formulas, Savitzky-Golay + polynomial fitting, Voronoi centerline boundary refinement, SVM iteration prediction), z-score normalization, third-order spline resampling to median spacing, on-the-fly augmentation; optional Taubin smoothing in supplement.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Not publicly available: 'code and networks with trained weights will be released upon acceptance' — a promise, not a release. Only the pre-existing public digital heart models (Zenodo 4309958) are linked.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice + average surface distance + novel centroid-boundary distance + IoU success rate + Pearson correlation of LA volume/sphericity + Bland-Altman analyses.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Medians/IQR, 95% CIs, Pearson correlations with p-values, Bland-Altman plots, McNemar's test (p=0.034 for seed tuning), t-test/chi-square as appropriate. Minor gaps: no CI on headline Dice, no multiplicity correction.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Literature-level comparison only (prior LA works: Dice 91–97%, 93.4%). No head-to-head baseline (e.g., nnU-Net trained on manually labeled data), and commercial tools (CARTO, SimVascular) discussed but not benchmarked.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Only pooled mean Dice across all six substructures and aggregate PV/LAA boundary distances. No per-structure breakdown (LA body, LSPV, LIPV, RSPV, RIPV, LAA) anywhere in the paper.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations section: single center, no multi-expert label fusion, DOKEN's four-PV geometric assumption (6/34 variants misparsed), CT data not releasable. Dedicated failure analysis of anatomical variants (Fig 8).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate/Unclear. Whether patients were consecutive or consecutively enrolled is not stated; inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond 'AF ablation with cardiac CT' undefined; single-center AF-only cohort narrows the anatomy/image-quality spectrum. Random 20/100 split mitigates within-cohort allocation bias but not cohort selection bias.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. All N=100 test cases evaluated against the same expert-panel reference with identical metrics; however, the reference standard is a single annotation without adjudication or inter-rater reporting, and DOKEN-generated training labels are not independently verified per case, risking correlated label bias.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Primary outcomes reported with IQR/CI and negative variant-parsing cases shown (Fig 8); but per-structure Dice, per-case failure Dice distributions, hardware/runtime figures, and baseline comparisons are omitted, and code is promised rather than released, limiting independent verification.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details: (1) DOKEN mechanics — structuring element is a 3×3×3 cross (center + 6 neighbors); Erosion Index = (V(Convex(Ei))−V(Ei))/V(Ei), global minimum of Savitzky-Golay-filtered polynomial fit gives erosion iterations; Dilation Index = (V(Di+1)−V(Di))/V(Di), first stationary point gives dilation iterations; LA-PV/LAA boundaries replaced by planes orthogonal to centerlines derived from maximal inscribed spheres (Voronoi) connecting substructure centroids to LA centroid. (2) Two SVMs predict erosion/dilation iteration counts for clinical CT; trained on N=5 manually segmented seed shells (LA volumes 71–140 mL); parsing success (IoU>0.5 vs experts) rose 67%→94% with N=5 seeds, plateauing at 92–94% for 10–30 seeds (McNemar p=0.034). (3) Ground truth: EnSite Verismo Segmentation Tool v2.0.1 (Abbott) for LA+4PV+LAA shell, then manual parsing into 6 substructures in 3D Slicer. (4) Variant analysis: four-PV configuration (N=66) parsed at 100% success, boundary agreement 1.26 mm (95% CI −5.15 to 7.68); common left PV ostium (N=12) and LAA-occluded cases (N=3) parsed despite no variant training; supplemental/branch PVs 19/25 parsed; total 28/34 variants at 1.95 mm agreement (95% CI −6.34 to 10.25). (5) Centroid-boundary distance is a newly proposed metric: mean distance from heart centroid to LA-PV/LAA boundary points. (6) Claimed >10-fold relative reduction in train:test ratio (<1:5 vs typical >3:1). (7) Funding: NIH R01 HL149134, R01 HL83359; IRB Stanford, NCT02997254 (2016); CC BY license. (8) Taubin 3D smoothing for 3D printing shown in Supplemental Figure S1. (9) Training loss convergence and validation Dice curves in Figure 4; qualitative examples at 25th/50th/75th percentile accuracy in Figure 6.
contribution_summary: The paper introduces DOKEN, a domain-knowledge-encoding algorithm that automatically labels six left atrial substructures by morphological erosion-dilation parsing of cardiac geometry (tuned via SVMs on only 5 seed cases), enabling nnU-Net training on just 20 patients while validating on 100 hold-out cases — an inverted ~1:5 train:test ratio. It achieves Dice 96.7%, 1.51 mm median surface distance, and expert-level correlation (r=0.99), parsing 28/34 anatomical variants. The contribution is label-efficiency rather than accuracy superiority over SOTA: it lacks external validation, per-structure results, head-to-head baselines, and released code.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Training cohort of 2594 patients (multi-center coronary CTA, described from prior work [9]) far exceeds threshold; however, the present validation cohort is only 53 patients (52 measurable), marginally above the >50 cutoff, and authors acknowledge underrepresentation of cardiac pathologies.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single-center retrospective PACS query (04/2020-04/2023) with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, patient flow diagram, full demographics table (age 64±16, 36% female, BMI 25.7±5.3), and detailed scan parameters (kV distribution, CTDIvol, kernels, slice thickness).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: No train/val/test split performed in this study — the entire cohort serves as an independent external test set for a pre-trained commercial model, with explicit statement that training data contained no data from the validating institution. Original training split methodology is deferred to reference [9] and not described here.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Reference standard well described: CMR segmentations in cvi42 v5.14 auto-contoured then manually corrected in consensus by two blinded experts (6-yr radiologist, 3-yr cardiology resident). Model training GT (auto-masks from contrast CT deformably registered to non-contrast, human-verified) also described.

Q5_external_validation.justification: The entire study is an external/intermodal validation: model developed by Siemens Healthineers on multi-center coronary CTA data, validated here against CMR (clinical gold standard) on an institutionally independent cohort — the exact gap the paper identifies in prior work [9].

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Described only at high level: 'image-to-image segmentation network combined with a conditional variational autoencoder' plus a heart isolation model; full architecture deferred to Jacob et al. [9]. No layer/feature details in this paper.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No training hyperparameters, optimizer, augmentation, or inference settings provided; model is proprietary (Siemens AI-Rad Companion Research), so the pipeline cannot be reproduced from this paper or its reference.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never mentioned, neither here nor summarized from the underlying technical report [9].

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Clinical-level preprocessing described (axial soft-tissue kernel, thin slices, supine, full craniocaudal chest coverage; heart isolation model; mass computed via myocardial density 1.05 g/mL; schematic in Supplementary Figure S1). Technical preprocessing (resampling, normalization, post-processing of masks) not specified.

Q10_code_availability.justification: Explicitly not public: algorithm 'available for research only' (proprietary); measurement data available only on request; imaging data unavailable for ethical/legal reasons.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Multiple metrics used (ICC, Bland-Altman limits of agreement, within-subject coefficient of variation, mean differences with 95% CI, confusion-matrix classification metrics, 3-point qualitative Likert rating) — but no direct segmentation overlap metric (Dice/IoU) against reference masks; agreement assessed only at the derived-volume level.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Thorough: 95% CIs and p-values throughout, Wilcoxon/paired t-tests, Mann-Whitney U for subgroup comparisons (ECG-gated vs non-gated), ICC with published classification bands, univariable linear regression for error predictors, SAS 9.4.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Narrative comparison only: situates ICCs against the same model's intramodal results (Jacob et al., ICC 0.92-0.98) and discusses alternatives (Naghavi, Miller, radiotherapy planning tools); no head-to-head benchmarking of competing methods on the same data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Fully stratified per structure: separate ICC, Bland-Altman, and difference values for LVEDV (0.85), LVESV (0.84), LVM (0.91), RVEDV (0.79), RVESV (0.78), LA (0.74), RA (0.61), plus per-chamber qualitative failure analysis.

Q15_limitations.justification: Systematic failure analysis (3/52 major failures with specific causes: missed caudal slices, rib leakage, pericardial effusion leakage) plus a candid limitations section: small sample, pathology underrepresentation, no phase-matching, single scanner model (SOMATOM Force), approximate density ROI measurements.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low risk: consecutive retrospective inclusion with predefined criteria and a STROBE-style flowchart; residual concern is single-center recruitment and exclusion of situs inversus/non-supine scans limiting spectrum generalizability.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-to-moderate: CT measurements fully automated (no operator variability) and CMR reference by two consensus readers blinded to diagnoses; however, the qualitative segmentation quality rating is not stated as blinded, and absence of CT/CMR phase-matching (acknowledged) may bias agreement estimates downward.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate: unfavorable results fully reported (systematic RV/atrial overestimation, RA ICC 0.61, RV dilatation false positives 6/7, 6% major failures); mitigating concerns are heavy industry involvement (three Siemens employees as authors, speaker honoraria to others) and no data/code sharing enabling independent verification.

detailed_extraction: Task framing: clinical validation (not development) of a pre-existing commercial DL model (Siemens AI-Rad Companion Research) for fully automated 4-chamber + LV myocardium segmentation on NON-CONTRAST chest CT, validated against CMR. Cohort: 53 consecutive patients (19F/34M, age 64±16) with paired non-contrast chest CT and CMR ≤3 weeks apart (mean interval 3±4 days, range 0-16); exclusions: situs inversus (n=1), incomplete CT coverage (n=2), unavailable/unassessable cine (n=8). CT: SOMATOM Force dual-source dual-energy; 43 non-ECG-gated, 10 prospectively gated (target 65% R-R, measured 47-79%); tube voltage mostly 100 kV. CMR: Siemens 1.5T/3T scanners, bSSFP cine, short-axis (ventricles) and 4/2-chamber long-axis (atria) at ED/ES; BSA-normalized EACVI thresholds used for dilatation/hypertrophy classification; Mosteller formula for BSA. Model provenance: trained on 2594 multi-center coronary CTA patients (mean age 60.2±11.4, 45% female) with paired non-contrast/contrast series; GT masks generated on contrast series via automated segmentation + deformable registration to non-contrast, human-verified; architecture = image-to-image segmentation network + conditional VAE (details in Jacob et al. 2023); combined at inference with a heart isolation model. Key results (52/53 = 98% success): ICC — LVEDV 0.85, LVESV 0.84, LVM 0.91, RVEDV 0.79, RVESV 0.78, LA 0.74, RA 0.61 (all p<0.001); systematic overestimation of RV volume (+18 mL, relative +27.5%), LVM (+30 g), LA (+48 mL), RA (+38 mL); CTLV fell within MR ED-ES range in 71%; classification: LV dilatation 7/15 sensitivity with 1 false positive; RV dilatation 1/1 true positive but 6 false positives; LV hypertrophy 1/5 sensitivity, 0 false positives. ECG-gating showed no significant effect on any agreement measure. Quality rating: 73% no issues, 21% minor, 6% major failures; cardiac implants (LV patch, CRT leads) did not degrade segmentations. Regression found no significant predictors of myocardial volume error (density delta, hematocrit, BMI, mAs, CTDIvol, gating — all p>0.05). Notable methodological caveats: authors argue CT 3D atrial volumetry may be MORE accurate than the biplane/monoplane CMR reference (geometric assumptions underestimate atria), i.e., reference-standard imperfection partially explains poor atrial ICCs. Ethics: University of Freiburg approval 22-1270-S1-retro; consent waived. Funding: university Open Access fund (no direct industry funding declared); COI: Siemens employees/honoraria as noted.
contribution_summary: This paper provides the first intermodal (CT vs CMR) clinical validation of a commercial deep learning model for fully automated quantification of all four cardiac chamber volumes and LV myocardial mass on routine non-contrast chest CT, addressing the gap left by prior intramodal-only validation. In 53 paired patients, ventricular volumes and LV mass correlated well-to-excellently with CMR (ICC 0.78-0.91) with ~98% processing success and no significant dependence on ECG-gating, while atrial volumes performed only moderately (ICC 0.61-0.74) with systematic overestimation. The work supports using opportunistic non-gated chest CT as a screening adjunct for incidentally detecting cardiac dilation/hypertrophy, though the proprietary, non-reproducible model limits scientific transparency.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 86 subjects (>50), adequate for a paired-method validation study; note: no training set exists — evaluation-only design.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Single institution, acquisition dates (Jan–May 2025), scanner model (GE Optima CT660), full CT/contrast protocol, and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria all reported.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Not applicable — no model training; all 86 cases used as a single evaluation set.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Manual reference by two blinded observers, slice-by-slice paint, with intra-observer ICC 0.996–0.997 and inter-observer ICC 0.991; authors correctly note manual is not absolute ground truth.

Q5_external_validation.justification: None — single center, single scanner, healthy-adult cohort only.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Underlying DL architectures never described; RVX and TotalSegmentator used as black-box 3D Slicer plugins with only citations to original works.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: No training details (pretrained models used as-is), but the operational workflow is highly reproducible: software versions, module commands, thresholds, ROI settings all specified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Not applicable — no training performed, no loss function discussed.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Thoroughly described: DICOM import, thresholding, ROI bounding boxes, error corrections limited to distinct errors (8/86 quantified), nii.gz export, SliverR metric computation.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No custom code, but all tools are publicly available/open-source: 3D Slicer 5.8.1, TotalSegmentator, RVX Liver Segmentation extension.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Dice, Hausdorff Distance, Bland–Altman bias + 95% LoA, absolute/relative volume error, ICC, processing time.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Repeated-measures ANOVA with Greenhouse–Geisser correction and Bonferroni post-hoc, 95% CIs, ICCs, normality testing, effect size (η²=0.179).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: The study's core design is a head-to-head comparison including SOTA TotalSegmentator; discussion benchmarks against published limits of agreement.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ (liver) study — criterion only partially applicable; no subgroup or per-case breakdown reported.

Q15_limitations.justification: DL overestimation quantified, 8/86 (9.3%) failure cases reported with figures and correction time; generalizability limits discussed in visible text.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (low ambiguity), but moderate spectrum bias: healthy controls only, single center — excludes the diseased/hepatomegaly livers where volumetry is clinically most needed and where DL errors are known to increase.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low: all methods run in the same software by trained observers; manual reference by two blinded observers with ICC verification; identical automated metric pipeline (SliverR). Caveats: RVX methods received manual corrections of distinct errors while TotalSegmentator was uncorrected; reference standard is itself manual and not absolute truth.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate: all metrics and failure cases reported. However, the Abstract claims 'TotalSegmentator showed the closest agreement' while the Results/Discussion show RVX Semi-Automatic had the lowest bias (8.63 vs 14.37 cm³) and lowest HD (22.74 vs 31.33 mm) — an internal inconsistency favoring the fully automatic tool.

detailed_extraction: Design: single-center retrospective comparison study; 86 contrast-enhanced abdominal CTs (41 M / 45 F; mean age 60.02±17.32 M vs 54.44±18.29 F, p=0.151), Tokat Gaziosmanpasa University Hospital, Jan–May 2025; healthy control CTs only (excluded: abdominal pathology, hepatomegaly, liver disease history, imaging artifacts). Imaging: GE Optima CT660, 120 kVp, 150 mAs, 64×0.5 mm collimation, 2.5 mm slices / 1.25 mm reconstruction, 512×512 matrix, portal venous phase ~60 s post 1.5 mL/kg iodinated contrast. Reference: manual slice-by-slice Paint in 3D Slicer 5.8.1 Segment Editor, two observers experienced in abdominal imaging, blinded; mean of the two observers' volumes used. Compared methods (all within 3D Slicer): (1) RVX Liver semi-automatic (Paint liver/non-liver + Grow from Seeds + manual correction); (2) RVX Deep Learning (threshold preprocessing + Segment CT + manually adjusted volume-rendering ROI + Apply); (3) TotalSegmentator (Fast option, fully automatic). Manual corrections limited to distinct errors; required in 8/86 (9.3%) RVX DL cases, +5.2±1.6 min, excluded from reported algorithm time. Reliability (10-case subset, ≥2-week interval): intra-observer ICC 0.997/0.996; inter-observer ICC 0.991 (manual), 0.889 (semi-automatic). Metrics via SliverR extension / Segment Comparison module, manual as reference; masks exported as nii.gz. Statistics: SPSS 28; Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality; repeated-measures ANOVA, sphericity violated (Mauchly p<0.001), Greenhouse–Geisser corrected F(2.348, 199.618)=18.501, p<0.001, η²=0.179; Bonferroni: RVX DL significantly higher than all other methods (p<0.001), all other pairs NS. Bland–Altman bias (New−Manual): semi-auto +8.63 cm³ (95% LoA −141.30 to 158.56), RVX DL +45.83 cm³ (−72.40 to 164.86), TotalSegmentator +14.37 cm³ (−84.76 to 113.51). Dice: 0.911±0.032 / 0.946±0.018 / 0.938±0.021 (semi-auto / RVX DL / TS). HD: 22.74±6.24 / 40.26±10.11 / 31.33±9.78 mm. Times: manual 40.42±5.86, semi-auto 10.42±1.72, TS 2.04±0.47, RVX DL 0.64±0.09 min. Ethics: approved (No: E-15235480-050.04-564671), Declaration of Helsinki, anonymized. No model training/fine-tuning — all models used off-the-shelf as pretrained. Note: supplied full text ends mid-Discussion; limitations section, funding, and conflicts declarations not visible.
contribution_summary: A head-to-head clinical validation of two RVX Liver Segmentation workflows and TotalSegmentator against manual segmentation on 86 healthy-adult CTs, showing clinically acceptable volumetric agreement (Dice 0.911–0.946) with 4–60× time reductions (0.64–10.42 min vs 40.42 min manual). TotalSegmentator offered the best speed/accuracy trade-off with no significant volume bias (+14.4 cm³), while the RVX deep-learning mode was fastest but systematically overestimated volume (+45.8 cm³ bias, highest HD, 9.3% over-segmentation rate). This is an application/evaluation study of pretrained tools, not a model-development paper — the rubric's architecture, training, and split criteria are largely inapplicable.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Adequate for liver (LiTS 131 train; MSD liver 131) and pancreas (MSD 282), but cardiac has only 20 volumes and SLIVER07 size is never specified; 70/20/10 split further shrinks per-subset counts.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: LiTS and MSD well described with citations, sizes, resolutions, slice spacing. However SLIVER07 (used for VGG-16 per Section 3.7) has no size or composition given, and the paper contradicts itself: abstract and Table 4 say VGG-16 used LiTS, Section 3.7 says SLIVER07.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split ratio stated (70/20/10 train/val/test; LiTS 131/70 also cited), but no description of randomization, patient-level splitting, stratification, or whether the official challenge splits were used.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Ground truth is inherited from public challenge annotations (not re-annotated); label binarization to organ-only is described, but the original annotation process (raters, protocol, inter-rater agreement) is not discussed.

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external or independent cohort. All training and testing occur within LiTS/MSD/SLIVER07; no inference on outside data.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Standard 3D U-Net (Chainer) with 64x64x64 patches and VGG-16 (TensorFlow) referenced rather than specified; no layer-by-layer detail, filter counts, or description of how VGG-16 was adapted from classification to segmentation (decoder/FCN head unexplained).

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Learning rate (1e-4), weight decay (2e-4, VGG-16), optimizers, losses, initializers, framework, and hardware reported; but epochs, batch size, data augmentation, and convergence criteria are missing, so full reproduction is not possible.

Q8_loss_function.justification: CE and Dice loss are experimental variables of the study itself and outcomes are analyzed (CE > Dice for liver; Dice loss failed entirely on pancreas), but a priori justification for the candidate set is thin and rationale is mostly post-hoc empirical.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing clearly specified: isotropic 1x1x1 mm resampling, zero-mean/unit-variance normalization, label binarization, 64x64x64 patch extraction. Postprocessing explicitly none.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, model weights, or repository link provided in the paper.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Eight metrics: Dice, Hausdorff Distance, Average Hausdorff Distance, Mahalanobis Distance, Mutual Information, Variation of Information, AUC, Volumetric Similarity — computed with the VISCERAL evaluation package.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Paired t-tests (p <= 0.05) of each configuration against the best configuration per dataset, per metric (Tables 5-7), with explicit p-values for VGG-16 comparisons. cardiac data excluded from testing due to small n (disclosed). No confidence intervals.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: No external state-of-the-art baseline (e.g., nnU-Net, other published liver/pancreas methods). All comparisons are internal between the paper's own 12 hyperparameter configurations.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Fully separated per-organ results: Tables 1 (liver), 2 (heart), 3 (pancreas), 4 (LiTS/VGG-16), with mean and standard deviation for every metric and configuration.

Q15_limitations.justification: Failures reported openly: Dice loss produced no results for any pancreas configuration and some liver configurations; cardiac test set too small for statistics; cardiac data is MRI not CT; authors concede quality-metric values are hard to interpret concisely. Best-vs-worst qualitative examples shown. No dedicated limitations section, but discussion is substantive.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Unclear/moderate. All data from public challenges (LiTS, MSD, SLIVER07), but the 70/20/10 split procedure is unexplained (randomization, patient-level independence unverified) and SLIVER07 composition is unreported. Contradictory statements on which dataset the VGG-16 experiments used (Section 3.7: SLIVER07; abstract/Table 4: LiTS) make the evaluated cohort uncertain.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. All configurations were evaluated identically with eight standardized metrics via the VISCERAL package, and statistical testing supports config comparisons. Mitigating gaps: no external validation, cardiac statistical analysis omitted, and one architecture (VGG-16) evaluated only on a single-organ 2D slice setup.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Moderate. Failed runs are excluded from results tables (GloDC-Adam for liver; all Dice-loss pancreas configurations), though exclusions are disclosed. Only 3 of the 9 possible weight-init x activation combinations appear in Table 4 for VGG-16, with no explanation of the missing six. Best-case Dice values are highlighted per organ while overall configuration tables show the margin between best and worst configs is small (liver 3D U-Net Dice range ~0.858-0.897).

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Evaluation implemented with the VISCERAL evaluation software package; metric recommendations taken from its reference paper. (2) VGG-16 operates slice-by-slice on 2D axial CT slices with a softmax final layer; 3D U-Net consumes 64x64x64 volumetric patches. (3) ReLU was fixed for all 3D U-Net runs, justified by literature and ~6x speed advantage over tanh/sigmoid for the multi-dataset workload; cross-entropy was fixed for all VGG-16 runs. (4) Statistical testing design: paired t-test of each configuration against the best per dataset per metric; heart database excluded due to limited test data; second-best configs (LecCE-Adam liver, HeCE-Rms pancreas) mostly indistinguishable from best, indicating small effect sizes between parameter choices. (5) Excluded/failed runs: GloDC-Adam (liver) and every Dice-loss pancreas configuration produced no usable segmentation. (6) No tumor/lesion segmentation evaluated despite labels existing — labels binarized to organ parenchyma only. (7) Training details not reported for either experiment: epochs, batch size, augmentation, early stopping. (8) Hardware: NVIDIA Tesla V100 (VGG-16) and DGX2/Volta (3D U-Net). (9) Scope flag for this CT-focused review: the cardiac/left-atrium results (best Dice 0.892) are from MSD cardiac MRI, NOT CT — only liver and pancreas results are applicable to a CT segmentation review; the VGG-16 liver Dice of 0.921 is 2D slice-based, not volumetric 3D. (10) Funding: H2020-MSCA-ITN Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions. (11) No code, license, or versioned benchmark release.
contribution_summary: An empirical ablation study evaluating how weight initialization, activation function, loss function, and optimizer choices affect CNN segmentation performance, using 3D U-Net on MSD (liver, pancreas, cardiac) and VGG-16 on LiTS liver data, scored with eight metrics plus paired t-tests. Best combinations identified: Glorot+Adam+CE for 3D U-Net (liver Dice 0.897, pancreas 0.691) and Glorot+tanh+CE for VGG-16 (liver Dice 0.921). The contribution is practical guidance on hyperparameter selection rather than a new architecture; notably, Dice-loss configurations failed outright on pancreas, differences between configurations were small, and no external state-of-the-art comparison was performed.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 100 T2-weighted MRI subjects (50 healthy, 50 CKD) exceed the >50 threshold, with 10 subjects scanned 5x for measurement-precision assessment. However, size is still modest for deep learning: after subject-wise splitting, the training subset is likely ~60-70 subjects, and the authors themselves acknowledge the 'limited number of MRI subjects' as motivation for heavy augmentation.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Two public datasets explicitly cited ([20] MRI, [21] CT) with composition tabulated (Table 2): MRI = 100 abdominal T2-weighted scans with manual kidney masks, healthy/CKD halves, subject metadata CSV, separate archives per group; CT = ~12,446 colorized images (5077 normal, 3709 cyst, 2283 tumor, 1379 stone) from hospitals in Dhaka, Bangladesh (per reference [9]). Minor weakness: CT dataset provenance is reported 'according to literature' rather than first-hand.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split strategy type is stated (subject-wise split for MRI to prevent slice-level information leakage; image-wise split for CT to balance classes), but the actual train/validation/test ratios or per-subset subject counts are never reported, preventing exact reproduction of the data partition.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: MRI masks described only as 'manually defined' and supplied with the public dataset; annotator expertise, annotation protocol, inter-/intra-rater agreement, and correction procedures are not described. GT masks were cleaned of small isolated components during preprocessing. The CT dataset has no segmentation masks at all.

Q5_external_validation.justification: External evaluation is explicitly claimed — the colorized CT dataset was 'used solely as an external evaluation set' for cross-modality structural robustness, with no CT used in training. However, this is contradicted in Section 3.2, which states CT images 'were used primarily to enrich the anatomical variability available to the encoder' (i.e., training). Moreover, the CT set contains no ground-truth masks, so how Dice/HD95-class segmentation evaluation on CT was performed is unclear. External validation is claimed but not verifiable as described.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Architecture described in depth: 4-stage residual encoder (two 3x3 convs + InstanceNorm + ReLU + residual shortcuts per stage, max-pool downsampling), U-Net decoder with transposed-conv/learned upsampling, skip concatenation, 1x1 conv + Softmax over 4 classes (background/cortex/medulla/pelvis), GAP+MLP functional head, and a differentiable morphological biomarker module (Euclidean distance transform thickness, volumetric sums, cortex-medulla ratio). Formalized via Eqs. 1-23 and Algorithms 1-3. Only minor omissions: exact channel widths per stage and explicit values for depth parameters.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Exceptionally detailed training specification: AdamW (lr 1e-4 -> 2e-6, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, weight decay=0.01), cosine annealing with warm restarts and 5-epoch warm-up, batch sizes 8 (MRI)/16 (CT), 120 epochs, gradient clipping 5.0, dropout 0.15 (functional head only), FP16 mixed precision, full software/hardware/container stack (Table 3: PyTorch 2.2.1, CUDA 12.2, Docker 24.0, RTX 4090), 3 random seeds with mean reporting, ~14.7 h training time. Minor gaps: final values of consistency-loss weights alpha and beta are not reported.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Losses are motivated: Dice + cross-entropy for segmentation (standard), a 70% MAE / 30% MSE hybrid justified as balancing large-deviation penalty and smoothness, and the novel structure-function consistency loss (L_sf = alpha|y_morph - y| + beta|y_hat - y_morph|) extensively motivated on physiological grounds. Total weights lambda1=1.0, lambda2=0.75, lambda3=0.25 justified via empirical tuning plus ablation evidence. Only alpha/beta numeric values missing.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing is thorough for both modalities: corrupted-slice removal, uniform resampling, z-score intensity normalization, abdominal cropping, mask cleaning/alignment (MRI); resize to 150x150, [0,1] scaling, per-channel mean-variance normalization (CT); extensive on-the-fly augmentation (rotations, flips, affine, zoom, elastic deformation, brightness/Gaussian noise/contrast jitter). However, post-processing of network outputs (e.g., connected-component filtering) is not addressed anywhere.

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code repository, model weights release, or public availability statement appears anywhere in the provided text; only Docker containerization of the private environment is described.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Comprehensive multi-metric suite, all formally defined (Eqs. 24-32): Dice, IoU, Pixel Accuracy, HD95 for segmentation; MAE, RMSE, Pearson r, R2 for eGFR regression; plus a custom Consistency Error (CE = |y_morph - y|) for structure-function alignment.
