Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Means +/- SD throughout; p-values reported (kidney Dice comparison p=0.0498; tumor comparisons with significance stars in Figure 3 boxplots); statistical test types not named and no confidence intervals (minor gap).

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Systematic 4-way baseline comparison (SS/DS x SwinUNETR/nnUNet-3D) functioning as an ablation of both the dual-stage design and backbone choice, all trained with standard parameters for fairness; positioned against KiTS challenge winners.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study; kidney Dice/precision reported separately from tumors, with tumor results stratified by size (small/medium/large; further binned <=2cm, >2-3cm, >3-4cm) and by histological subtype (supplementary Figures S4-S6).

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations section: cyst FPs from missing benign annotations, ccRCC-only private set limiting generalization, plus honest reporting that sensitivity drops to 0.63 for <=2cm tumors and 'other' subtypes perform worst.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate concern. Public KiTS23 training cohort has reported subtype distribution, but the private external cohort is single-institution (MSKCC), nephrogenic-phase-only, and ccRCC-only, narrowing the case spectrum; the randomization method for the 80/20 split is unstated.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. All models evaluated against the same manual reference standard with a predefined detection threshold (3D IoU 0.25), formally defined metrics, and baselines trained with standardized parameters for fair comparison.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low-moderate. Detection and segmentation outcomes comprehensively reported per dataset, tumor size, and subtype (extensive supplementary material); however, training/inference runtimes are unreported and no code release permits independent verification.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary methodological details: (1) Stage-1 selection was empirically justified - SwinUNETR beat nnUNet-3D on kidney Dice (0.97+/-0.02 vs 0.95+/-0.05, p=0.0498), motivating ViT for large organs + CNN for localized tumor search. (2) SwinUNETR initialized with pretrained weights from ref [42] (transfer learning). (3) Augmentation (rotations, scaling, mirroring, axis transposition, gamma correction) yielded +5.5% Dice and improved size-class balance. (4) VOI from stage 1 expanded 25% to balance context vs search space; authors argue stage-1 localization quality is as important as stage-2 segmentation (poor localization inflates FPs). (5) Detection threshold: 3D object-wise IoU >= 0.25. (6) KiTS23 training subtype composition: ccRCC 247 (63.49%), papillary 39 (10.03%), chromophobe 33 (8.48%), oncocytoma 19 (4.88%), TCC 17 (4.37%), other 34 (8.74%). (7) Sub-4cm analysis on private data (607 tumors): <=2cm n=44 (sens 0.63, Dice 0.81), >2-3cm n=97 (0.93, 0.83), >3-4cm n=110 (0.97, 0.86); <=2cm sensitivity attributed to unreliable CECT attenuation. (8) SS->DS gains largest for nnUNet-3D small-tumor sensitivity (KiTS23 0.59->0.74, +25.42%; private 0.62->0.84, +35.48%); DS benefit on large tumors is primarily FP reduction rather than Dice. (9) ccRCC-only comparison (Fig S4) showed consistent performance across datasets; 'other' subtype lowest Dice (Fig S6). (10) Private kidney organ annotations unavailable, so organ results are KiTS23-only. (11) Funding: NIH/NCI Cancer Center Support Grant P30 CA008748; no conflicts declared; IRB statement 'not applicable'. (12) For review scope: kidney-only (single organ + tumors, 3D CECT); not multi-organ, so limited contribution to multi-organ benchmarks like TotalSegmentator/AMOS but strong for renal-specific pipelines.
contribution_summary: The paper proposes a dual-stage pipeline pairing a ViT-based SwinUNETR for kidney localization with a residual-block and attention-gate-enhanced 3D UNet for tumor segmentation, arguing that investment in stage-1 localization quality is critical to reduce false positives in stage 2. Its key empirical claim, supported by an ablation over SS/DS variants of nnUNet-3D and SwinUNETR on 1081 CECT scans with external validation, is that this design substantially raises small-tumor (<=4cm) detection sensitivity (0.90/0.89) while cutting false positives per patient (0.23/0.15) versus single-stage SOTA. Notably, training uses only public KiTS23 data, with a 592-scan private ccRCC cohort reserved entirely for external validation; main gaps are missing code, incompletely specified training schedules, and generalizability limited by the ccRCC-only external set.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Each model trained on only ~20 scans (32.52% of n=61); total curated corpus is 122 scans but no single model sees >50 training subjects. Authors explicitly acknowledge this (250-450 scans in comparable works).

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Thoroughly described: in-house Charité PACS pull (Oct 2020-Mar 2021) with scanner models/counts (Canon Aquilion One/PRIME, GE Revolution HD/EVO/LightSpeed VCT), contrast agents and volumes, 70-80s portal venous timing, 5 mm slices; MSD Spleen task referenced with provenance (MSKCC chemotherapy patients).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split proportions and sizes given (41 train+val / 20 test per dataset) but the split method (random vs. stratified, by patient) is never described; reported percentages (32.52%/9.15%/20.33%) sum to ~62% and are internally inconsistent with the 41/20 split (~67%/33%), suggesting a reporting error.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Semi-automatic 3D Slicer segmentation with manual correction by two radiologists (9 and 5 years experience); inter-rater ICC >0.9 (95% CI 0.914-0.998); designated single annotator (R2) as GT. MSD test GT (not public) re-annotated by same radiologists.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Full cross-dataset evaluation in both directions: in-house U-Net tested on MSD test set and open U-Net tested on in-house test set - the core experimental design and the paper's main strength.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: Residual U-Net per Kerfoot et al. with strided conv encoding, strided transpose-conv decoding, skip connections, implemented in MONAI - but no channel counts, depth, or filter numbers given; reader must consult Kerfoot et al.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: 500 epochs, batch size 2, Adam lr=1e-4, Dice loss, deterministic training enabled, validation every 2 epochs, complete augmentation pipeline, exact framework versions (PyTorch 1.8.1, MONAI 0.5.0, PyTorch Lightning 0.9.0, Python 3.7). Only GPU hardware unspecified.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Dice loss stated without any rationale or comparison to alternatives.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Both pipelines fully specified: pre (DICOM->NIfTI, resample 1.5x1.5x2.0 mm with correct mask interpolation, windowing -57 to 164 HU, balanced positive/negative 96^3 patch sampling) and post (sigmoid, stitching, 0.5 threshold, resample back, largest connected component).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, weights, or repository released; only the MSD input data is public. In-house data explicitly not shareable.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Four metrics: DSC, relative absolute volume difference, average symmetric surface distance, maximum Hausdorff distance - overlap, volume, and surface-based all covered.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Mean +/- SD and 95% CIs per metric per model/dataset; Mann-Whitney U test comparing models (p=0.526 and p<0.001); statsmodels/scikit-learn versions given.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Table 3 compares against 6 prior methods (Gauriau, Wood, Gloger, Gibson, Linguraru, plus their two internal models) with abnormality-inclusion noted; discussion adds Ahn and Humpire-Mamani. Caveat: literature-based numbers, not reimplemented on common data.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ (spleen) study, so all results are organ-specific by construction; per-case distributions shown as boxplots (Fig. 2) and qualitative per-patient examples (Fig. 3). No pathology-subgroup breakdown (e.g., splenomegaly vs. normal) is given, which would have been more informative here.

Q15_limitations.justification: Dedicated limitations paragraph: small dataset, no cross-validation, portal-venous-phase-only training, preselection bias from excluding intrasplenic distortions (infarctions, focal lesions); failure cases visualized qualitatively (open U-Net on splenomegaly, Fig. 3).

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate. Consecutive PACS sampling over a defined period mitigates cherry-picking, but scans were curated for image quality, complex intrasplenic distortions were excluded (acknowledged preselection bias), and the cohort is enriched for pathology (51% splenomegaly in train+val). MSD cohort is a specific population (liver-metastases chemotherapy patients).
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low. Identical architecture, training protocol, and metrics applied to both models; GT annotation consistent (single radiologist with inter-rater ICC check); outcomes measured the same way across all four model/dataset combinations.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. All four metrics reported with CIs for all model/dataset combinations; limitations and failure cases disclosed. Minor issues: internal split percentages are inconsistent/uninterpretable, per-case results not released, and no code to verify results.

detailed_extraction: Study design: retrospective, IRB-approved (Charité EA4/136/21, 5 July 2021), consent waived; no external funding; departmental grant disclosures for one author (B.H.); no competing interests declared. Annotation: 3D Slicer v4.11.20210226; two radiologists (R1: 9y, R2: 5y experience); R2's contours = ground truth; ICC(2,?) >0.9 (95% CI 0.914-0.998) used as reliability evidence rather than a Dice-based inter-observer agreement. In-house cohort (n=61): portal venous phase abdominal CT, 5 mm axial reconstructions, contrast 100-140 mL (iomeprol/iobitridol/iopromide), injected 70-80 s before imaging; train+val (n=41): 56% female, age 62.6+/-16.2, 51.2% splenomegaly, 26.8% cirrhosis, 15.6% lymphoma, 9.8% no pathology, remainder other cancers (lung, pancreas, liver, prostate, colorectal); test (n=20): 25% female, 35% splenomegaly, 15% cirrhosis, 10% lymphoma, 5% no pathology. MSD spleen (n=61): MSKCC liver-metastases chemotherapy patients; official test GT not public so authors annotated all 20 test cases themselves - note this makes 'open test set' GT author-produced, slightly weakening the external-validation claim. Training: deterministic mode enabled for reproducibility; 500 epochs, validation every 2; Dice loss only (no BCE/CE combination); RAVD reported without SD (zero-centered metric, absolute value taken). Statistical comparison via Mann-Whitney U on DSC (scikit-learn 0.23.1, statsmodels 0.11.1). Key quantitative result: the open (normal-spleen) U-Net collapses on pathological spleens (DSC 0.648+/-0.289, RAVD 42.3%, HD 30.1 mm) while the pathology-trained model is near-symmetric (0.941 in-house / 0.906 open). Reporting anomalies to flag: split percentages (32.52/9.15/20.33%) do not sum to 100 and conflict with the stated 41/20 split; GPU hardware, per-split integer counts, and per-patient results not reported; patch sampling ratio described only qualitatively ('balanced'). No code/weights released; data availability statement covers MSD only. Corrections/additions to prior extraction: cross-dataset result naming clarified (rows = training set, columns = test set); in-house test-set demographics now available; ICC CI and full scanner/contrast inventory newly captured.
contribution_summary: This is a controlled cross-dataset generalizability study showing that a 3D residual U-Net trained on normal spleens (MSD) fails on pathological abdomens (DSC 0.648 vs 0.941; RAVD 42% vs 4%), while a model trained on a pathology-enriched in-house cohort performs well on both distributions. The actionable finding for the field is that spleen segmentation models built on normal-anatomy datasets (including most MSD-trained models) cannot be assumed safe for clinical populations with splenomegaly, ascites, or perisplenic disease. The contribution is evidentiary rather than architectural - no new method is proposed.

Q1_dataset_size.justification: Only 20 donors total; 8 for training (597 slices). Far below the >50-subject threshold. Partially mitigated by ITU_U-Net adding SLIVER07 data and augmentation, but the in-house training set is inadequate by itself.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Thoroughly described: 20 contrast-enhanced abdominal CTs from living liver donors, 2 scanners (Philips Brilliance 16/64), pixel spacing 0.7–0.8 mm, slice thickness 3–3.2 mm, ~90 slices/patient, 15% atypical liver shapes, IRB approval and informed consent obtained.

Q3_train_test_split.justification: Split clearly stated (8 train / 12 test; 597/1325 slices, 30/70%) with test ground truth withheld from participants. However, no validation set is described, and there is an internal inconsistency: Methods state 12 test datasets while Table 2 reports results on '14 patients'.

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Well described: manual segmentation by image specialists and radiologists, revised by an independent expert radiologist, final masks by consensus. Intra-user repeatability quantified (grade 95.14; VO 97.21%; liver volumes 1491 vs 1496 mL).

Q5_external_validation.justification: No external validation. All test data come from the same 20-donor single-center cohort. SLIVER07 data were used only to augment training, not as an independent test set.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: ITU_U-Net and METU_U-Net (with adversarial CAN) are described in detail with architecture figures, kernel sizes, strides, and channel counts. DEU_DeepMedic and DEU_Nifty-Net ran on defaults (referenced). X_U-Net and Y_U-Net are only vaguely described ('different configurations/tuning'), leaving 2 of 6 DL methods opaque.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: ITU_U-Net training is specified (SGD, momentum 0.9, lr 0.0002, 300 epochs, 4x4 kernels/stride 2), and METU pre/post-processing is given. But hyperparameters for METU, X, and Y U-Nets are unreported; DeepMedic/NiftyNet rely on undocumented 'slight parameter changes for adaptation'; no code released.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss functions for the U-Net variants are not explicitly stated. Partial credit: METU_U-Net introduces a CAN adversarial loss during training with an explicit rationale (regularization for sharper edge responses). No justification of segmentation loss choice for the other methods.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Per-method preprocessing/postprocessing clearly reported, including negative results: ITU (HU clipping -1500 to 1500, DICOM window level/width; histogram equalization and morphological cleanup explored but excluded), METU (per-image normalization; 3D connected components).

Q10_code_availability.justification: No participant code or trained models released. NiftyNet is open-source as a platform, but the adapted implementations and challenge data pipeline are not publicly available.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: Five complementary metrics (VO, RVD, ASSD, RMSD, MSSD) with defined grade-conversion thresholds, plus volumetric regression analysis, Bland-Altman plots, and intra-user variability. Exceeds the Dice+1 minimum.

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: 95% confidence intervals reported for all Table 2 metrics; Bland-Altman and regression analyses for volumes; intra-user variability quantified. However, no significance testing (p-values) between methods.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: Head-to-head comparison is the study design: 6 DL methods vs 6 well-established semi-automatic baselines (active contours, super-pixels, watershed, fast marching, region growing, RSS) on identical hidden test data, contextualized against SLIVER07 challenge findings.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ (liver) study with complete reporting: per-method mean ± 95% CI for all five metrics, per-patient score distributions (Fig. 4), and volume agreement analyses. No aggregation hiding.

Q15_limitations.justification: Extensive, specific limitations: 3 mm slice thickness causing partial-volume errors at oblique interfaces (heart, stomach), small cohort (20 donors, 2 scanners), grading-strategy assumptions (unit density, vessels ignored), MSSD sensitivity, and complete DL failures on some cases.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Moderate risk. Selection is clearly defined (living liver transplant donors, IRB-approved, 2 scanners) but narrow: only healthy donor livers from a single center. Generalizability to disease-bearing livers (tumors, lesions — deliberately excluded from this cohort unlike SLIVER07) and other centers/scanners is limited. Spectrum bias toward healthy, contrast-enhanced livers.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low risk. All 12 methods evaluated on the same withheld test set with identical metrics and expert-consensus ground truth never shown to participants. Caveat: semi-automatic method parameters were set 'by educated guess' by engineers rather than optimized per-case, which could disadvantage the interactive baseline; this is acknowledged but not controlled.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low risk. All 12 submitted results reported, including poor performers (Y_U-Net 37.6, 3D-FM 23.7), failure modes discussed, and post-hoc ensemble analyses with multiple selection orderings (random, best-to-worst, worst-to-best). Minor gap: numeric per-patient results are shown graphically (Fig. 4) rather than tabulated, and the 12-vs-14 test patient discrepancy is unexplained.

detailed_extraction: Supplementary details: (1) Study was structured as a challenge with 14 registered teams, 12 submitting results; training data + ground truth released to teams, test images only released, test ground truth withheld (grades returned to participants). (2) Grading system: metric values below threshold scores get 0 and are linearly mapped to 50–100 otherwise — VO <50%→0, RVD >10%→0, ASSD >10 mm→0, RMSD >15 mm→0, MSSD >50 mm→0; final score = unweighted average of five metric grades. (3) Intra-user variability (same expert, same case, two sessions): volumes 1491/1496 mL, VO 97.21%, RVD 0.347%, ASSD 0.611 mm, RMSD 1.04 mm, MSSD 13.038 mm → grade 95.14, establishing the human ceiling; MSSD was the weakest human metric (grade 86), so algorithmic MSSD grades should be interpreted cautiously. (4) METU_U-Net specifics: 2D U-Net generator with BN before convolution, PReLU, discriminator taking 256x256x2 label/image input; 3D context via concatenation of neighboring slices; CAN active only during training. (5) Heatmap analysis: automatic methods have FN voxels <0.3% of liver (interactive methods leave small undetected regions); interactive methods err regionally at isodense borders (gastric wall, diaphragm, IVC), automatic methods distribute FPs more diffusely — motivating ensembles since FPs are correctable and FNs are not. (6) Fusion analysis: MV tested under three orderings (random, best-to-worst, worst-to-best); all-method MV 86.70, automatic-only MV 83.87; STAPLE max 88.74 (all methods, best-to-worst), automatic-only 86.02; STAPLE needs ≥2/3 of results in worst-to-best order; STAPLE superior but slow to converge (EM iterations), MV fast with near-zero parallel overhead. (7) Discrepancy flag for review: Methods section states 12 test datasets; Table 2 caption and Fig. 4 report 14 test patients — unresolved in text. (8) Ethics/funding: IRB approval, informed consent, TUBITAK grant 116E133; no conflicts declared. (9) All DL methods were CNN-based; none used transformer or vision-language approaches (consistent with 2019 submission date). (10) Baseline context: prior to DL, interactive methods had historically outperformed automatic ones in liver segmentation challenges (per SLIVER07-era literature cited); this paper documents the crossover point.
contribution_summary: This challenge-style study provides the first head-to-head comparison of deep learning automatic methods against six well-established semi-automatic methods for liver segmentation and volumetry in living liver transplant donors, demonstrating that DL methods now dominate (top 4 ranks all DL; best VO 90.4% METU_U-Net, best final score 79.6 ITU_U-Net) with higher accuracy and lower volume-estimation variability than interactive techniques. It further shows that ensemble fusion of DL outputs via STAPLE/MV raises performance to 86.0–88.7 at near-zero time cost when models run in parallel, and it contributes an expert-consensus-annotated donor CT dataset with a five-metric graded evaluation protocol and quantified intra-user ceiling (95.14).

Q1_dataset_size.justification: 3,089 CT scans total; 2,840 for training (56-2,840 per model) and 249 held-out test scans — far above the >50 subject threshold.

Q2_dataset_source.justification: Four sources enumerated with counts and provenance: COVER-ALL trial (NCT04083378), Anderson et al. (2021), public BTCV challenge (Synapse link provided), and MD Anderson internal research database with stated inclusion criterion (any CT with an available liver contour).

Q3_train_test_split.justification: 249 scans withheld before training with explicit no-patient-overlap statement; BTCV (n=30) reserved purely for external validation; sub-datasets randomly sampled at fixed sizes with curated-scan proportions reported per subset (e.g., 2/56, 244/2840).

Q4_ground_truth.justification: Annotation hierarchy explicitly defined: highly curated = generated/validated by a board-certified interventional radiologist; minimally curated = unvalidated sources (early AI models, trainees) with a defined QC step — 5-fold cross-validation DSC screen, radiologist review and correction of the 65 scans with DSC < 0.90.

Q5_external_validation.justification: Dedicated external test set: 30 BTCV challenge scans never seen in training, reported separately from the 219 internal test scans across all metrics.

Q6_architecture_description.justification: nnU-Net 3d_fullres with automated per-dataset configuration; deviation from default (batches/epoch 250→1000) documented; use of auto-configuration is a deliberate, stated design choice to avoid tuning bias; official repository cited.

Q7_reproducibility.justification: Partially reproducible: batches/epoch modification, GPU hardware (5x A100), ~18 h/model, and 3d_fullres config reported. Missing: nnU-Net version (v1 vs v2 differ), epoch count, random seeds, fold strategy for final models; most training data is private and not released.

Q8_loss_function.justification: Loss function never stated; only inferable as the nnU-Net default (compound Dice + cross-entropy). No justification provided.

Q9_preprocessing.justification: Preprocessing delegated entirely to nnU-Net's automated pipeline (by reference, not described in-paper: no resampling, normalization, or patch details); postprocessing not explicitly addressed ('none reported').

Q10_code_availability.justification: No code, trained models, or configs released; institutional data available only upon request. Only the public nnU-Net repository is cited.

Q11_multiple_metrics.justification: DSC, surface DSC (2 mm), HD95, and 2D axial Slice DSC, plus slice-level failure analysis (counts/proportions of slices with DSC = 0, <0.80, <0.90) and distribution statistics (mean, median, Q1, 5th percentile).

Q12_statistical_analysis.justification: Friedman test across models with Dunn's multiple-comparisons post-hoc (alpha = 0.05), p-values reported in supplementary tables; sampling variance of small datasets quantified via eight independently resampled 56-scan models. No confidence intervals, but nonparametric testing is appropriate and thorough.

Q13_comparison_sota.justification: nnU-Net is justified as SOTA and serves as the backbone, but all comparisons are internal ablations of dataset composition; no benchmarking against external published methods or BTCV leaderboard results despite testing on BTCV.

Q14_per_organ_results.justification: Single-organ study (liver); the one target's results are exhaustively reported — 3D and slice-level metrics, internal vs. external split, per-model breakdowns.

Q15_limitations.justification: Explicit limitations: liver-only (may not transfer to small, high-variability structures like tumors), dataset still an order of magnitude smaller than natural-image corpora, findings possibly architecture-specific (untested on Swin UNETR/MedNeXt), and restricted data access.

risk_of_bias.selection_bias: Low. Sources, counts, and inclusion criteria predefined; random sampling of sub-datasets; explicit no-patient-overlap between training and testing. Residual concern: data dominated by a single institution (MD Anderson); minimally curated scans admitted solely on presence of a contour (no clinical criteria), though this mirrors the research question.
risk_of_bias.performance_bias: Low-moderate. All ~17 models evaluated identically on the same withheld test sets with the same metric suite; automated nnU-Net configuration explicitly used to prevent tuning bias. Concerns: no separate validation set — the same 249-scan test set was reused for all model comparisons; 'Model 1' (best of eight 56-scan runs, DSC 0.964 vs. 0.955 worst) was selected post-hoc as the small-dataset comparison anchor, favoring favorable comparisons.
risk_of_bias.reporting_bias: Low. Full metric distributions reported including worst-slice failure rates; p-values in supplements; limitations section candid. Minor concerns: best-of-8 anchor selection; medRxiv preprint not peer reviewed; no protocol or analysis plan pre-registered.

detailed_extraction: Dataset arithmetic — 493-scan highly curated pool (258 COVER-ALL + 205 Anderson + 30 BTCV) split into 244 training (76 COVER-ALL + 168 Anderson) and 249 test (182 COVER-ALL + 37 Anderson + 30 BTCV); test set includes 54 intraoperative scans with ablation-probe artifacts; plus 2,596 minimally curated internal scans (unvalidated contours from early AI models/trainees) with QC via 5-fold CV of a 2,840-scan model and radiologist correction of the 65 scans scoring DSC < 0.90. Mixed sub-dataset curated fractions: 56:2 (4%), 142:15 (11%), 284:21 (7%), 710:59 (8%), 1420:119 (8%), 2130:182 (9%), 2840:244 (9%). Variance protocol — eight resampled 56-scan mixed-curation models (Models 1-8, default 250 batches/epoch) averaged DSC 0.960 (range 0.955-0.964); Models 4 and 8 showed one-tailed distributions attributed to missing metal-artifact outlier scans; Model 1 chosen as anchor and retrained at 1000 batches/epoch. Key results — full test set: DSC plateau 0.970-0.971 above 710 scans; 56→142 mixed-curation gains significant (DSC 0.961→0.967, HD95 4.56→3.18 mm, SD 2mm 0.936→0.950, all p<.001); highly curated 244-scan statistically indistinguishable (p>.999) from all mixed models ≥1,420 scans on 3D metrics; Slice DSC full test: mixed 710-scan (0.957) significantly beats curated 244-scan (0.954, p<.001). BTCV external: all models degrade; curated 244-scan significantly worse on Slice DSC than all mixed models ≥284 scans (p<.02) except 2840 (p>.999); mixed 710-scan peaks (Slice DSC 0.929, 5th pct 0.821, 0-DSC slices 2.04%, HD95 6.8 mm, SD 2mm 0.94). Statistics — Friedman + Dunn's, alpha=0.05, p-values in Supplementary Tables 1-3. Compute — 5x NVIDIA A100, ~18 h/model, 3d_fullres only (no 2D/3D ensembling). Availability — BTCV public via Synapse (syn3193805); institutional data on request; no code/model release; nnU-Net version unstated. Internal discrepancy — abstract reports HD95 2.98 mm for the curated 244-scan model vs. 2.87 mm for the best (2,840-scan) model; both consistent with results text. Total trained models ≈ 17-18.
contribution_summary: First comprehensive controlled comparison of the annotation-quality vs. dataset-quantity tradeoff for AI-based whole-liver CT segmentation, training 3D nnU-Net models on 56-2,840 scans spanning highly curated and mixed-curation compositions. A 244-scan highly curated dataset matched a 2,840-scan mixed-curation dataset (10x larger) on 3D metrics (DSC 0.971, p>.999), while larger mixed-curation datasets improved generalizability on external BTCV data (Slice DSC 0.929 at 710 scans) and reduced worst-slice failures. The authors conclude the quality/quantity tradeoff is nuanced and goal-dependent: quality suffices when data are scarce and inference is in-distribution; quantity buys robustness out-of-distribution.
